intro.heading: Six ways IGCSE support is sold, and only one of them is a tutor
paragraphs: A search for a nearby IGCSE tutor returns a mixed set that looks homogeneous. Some of those results are agencies that will match you to a freelancer. Some are international marketplaces where the tutor may be in another country and quote in another currency. Some are individual freelancers advertising directly. Some are licensed tuition centres with premises, selling scheduled classes rather than one-to-one hours. Some are school-run clinics that are already included in your fees. They are five different products with five different cost structures, and the search engine ranks them as though they were one.

That matters more at IGCSE than at any other stage, because IGCSE is a nine-subject problem. A parent is not buying one tutor; they are deciding how to allocate a finite budget across nine subjects, two years and one external series. Picking a provider model badly costs more than picking a tutor badly, because the model determines whether you can concentrate hours where the evidence says they belong or whether you are locked into a class timetable that treats every subject as equal.

Dubai Hills Estate is a good place to run that comparison, because every model is available within a short radius. The British campuses in the Al Khail corridor have produced a genuine local market in mainstream IGCSE subjects, which is more than can be said for Diploma specialisms. Licensed centres sit a short drive away. Freelancers advertise in community groups. So the question here is not availability. It is which model gives you the ability to move hours between subjects in February, when the marked evidence finally tells you where they should go.

The second half of this page covers ground this market leaves empty. The regulator map for all seven emirates, including ADEK, which is named by none of the competitor pages audited. The mandatory UAE subjects that run alongside the licensed curriculum, with the KHDA class-organisation rules in full, because no competitor in any cluster has a section on them. What a KHDA inspection band actually implies and what it does not. And the private-candidate route, for students who need to sit a subject their school does not enter them for.

On delivery, the position is stated once and plainly. IB Gram delivers tutoring to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. The in-home market in Dubai is real and its published rates appear in the comparison below, so you can weigh it properly rather than take our word for anything. If physical presence in the room is what your child needs, that market is the right answer and this page will tell you what it charges and what to ask before you hire into it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-hills.programmesIntro: IGCSE in Dubai sits inside a longer route with two possible exits, and the tutoring decision changes at each stage. These are the four stages families in this corridor ask about and what each one actually needs.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the option block
programmes.description: The year subjects are chosen and tiers are provisionally decided, which makes it the highest-leverage year in the whole route and the one nobody buys tutoring for. A student placed on a lower tier on Year 9 evidence can carry a capped grade ceiling into a series two years later. Useful work here is narrow: algebraic fluency, written explanation in science, and reading speed, because those three underpin nine subjects rather than one.
programmes.countryNote: Campuses in the Al Khail corridor set option deadlines in the spring of Year 9, so a Dubai Hills Estate family waiting for the first Year 10 report has already passed the point where the subject list and the tier were set. Asking the school in writing which tier each subject is provisionally set at is the single most useful Year 9 email.

programmes.name: Year 10
programmes.description: Content is taught and nothing external is examined, which makes it the cheapest year in which to fix something and the year families skip. A gap closed in Year 10 compounds across two years and can still support an argument for a tier change while entries remain open. The same gap closed in the spring of Year 11 costs roughly twice the hours against eight competing subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 enquiries from Dubai Hills Estate cluster in January, after the first full internal assessment round. That is reasonable timing and the evidence it produces is genuinely useful, which is why it is worth asking for the marked papers rather than the grade summary when the report arrives.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the series
programmes.description: Nine or ten subjects reaching an external series simultaneously, which turns tutoring into triage. The question stops being what to teach and becomes where the hours go: which subjects sit within one grade of a threshold, which marks are lost to timing rather than knowledge, and which practical or alternative-to-practical component has never been sat under conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Most students in this corridor sit the June series, with November used for resits and early entries. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's risk, so the only timetable worth planning against is the one the school confirms for its own centre.

programmes.name: The fork after IGCSE
programmes.description: A Level or the IB Diploma, and in Dubai Hills Estate both are reachable within minutes, which makes the choice genuinely open. IGCSE grades are the entry evidence for both and the thresholds differ by subject and by school. A student intending Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, or A Level Mathematics, generally needs a strong higher-tier grade rather than a comfortable one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private sector is still expanding: seven new private schools arrive for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Next year's post-16 shortlist in this corridor will not be this year's.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-hills.subjectsIntro: At IGCSE the allocation question is as important as the teaching question, so each subject below carries a note on where its marks are typically lost and when intervening actually pays.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Method marks lost to unshown working in multi-step questions, so one arithmetic slip costs a whole question. It is the subject where a tier decision bites hardest and the one most often worth starting in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, graph gradients and any question asking for a relationship rather than a value. The practical route differs by board, and students sitting a written alternative-to-practical paper usually have the least practice in the component carrying it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations learned as a recipe and ionic equations unbalanced for charge. Organic families are memorised rather than understood, which shows up the moment a question asks about an unfamiliar member of a known family.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision rather than knowledge breadth. Approximately correct biology written in imprecise words earns nothing, and students find that loss the hardest to accept because they genuinely knew the answer.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: A strong answer to a slightly different task than the one set. Directed writing specifies audience, purpose and form, and structural marks lost to the wrong form cannot be recovered by the quality of the prose.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading comprehension precision and the specific summary conventions, which reward selecting and compressing rather than paraphrasing. Students strong in spoken English often underperform here because the paper tests reading discipline.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Definition recall is the floor and application to the case in the question is where the marks are. Diagram accuracy carries a meaningful share, and students who revise terminology without drawing plateau at a predictable level.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Marks follow applying a tool to the specific organisation rather than describing the tool. Case-study questions reward judgement with justification, which is a different skill from the content recall students revise for.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Split between theory and problem solving in syllabus pseudocode, which is marked strictly to its own conventions. Students fluent in a programming language often score below their ability because they write in that language instead.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside or after higher-tier mathematics by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. It front-loads calculus and trigonometry and exposes weak algebra immediately rather than gradually.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: A mandatory subject in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Support has to respect the rule that different or additional content needs prior Ministry permission.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: A double award covering biology, chemistry and physics in two grades rather than three subjects. A legitimate route rather than an easier one, and a tutor has to know which parts of each single-subject syllabus fall outside its scope.

sections.heading: What a search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Hills Estate actually returns
paragraphs: The direct answer: a mixed list of five different products ranked by proximity. Agencies that will match you to a freelancer and take a margin. International marketplaces where the tutor may sit in another time zone and the price may be quoted in dollars. Individual freelancers advertising directly. Licensed tuition centres selling scheduled classes at premises. And, usually absent from the list entirely, the school-run clinics you have already paid for inside the fees. Proximity tells you nothing about which of those you are looking at.

The stronger filters are all answerable in one phone call and almost nobody asks them. Which syllabus code has this person taught, and in which years. Have they marked that board's papers against its published scheme, or only taught the content. Which tier. If the subject has a practical component, which route did their students sit. For an agency, who actually teaches and who sets the price. For a marketplace, where is the tutor and in what currency is the rate. Those five questions eliminate most of a search result list faster than any amount of reading reviews.

Dubai Hills Estate has an unusual advantage here, which is that the local market in mainstream IGCSE subjects is genuinely real. The concentration of British campuses in the Al Khail corridor has produced freelance supply in mathematics, the three sciences and English that does not exist for Diploma specialisms. So for a Year 10 student needing mainstream maths help, hiring locally can work. It falls over at the specific end: Additional Mathematics, Computer Science pseudocode and alternative-to-practical technique are the three requests that regularly exceed local supply.

The allocation point is the one that justifies this whole page. At IGCSE you are not buying a tutor, you are deciding how to spend a fixed budget across nine subjects. The model you choose determines whether you can move hours in February when the marked evidence finally shows where they belong. A scheduled class at a centre cannot be reallocated. A weekly freelance commitment usually cannot either, without an awkward conversation. One-to-one hours bought against a written allocation can be, and that flexibility is worth more than any hourly saving.

sections.heading: Six provider models compared on what they actually give you
paragraphs: Every competitor page in this market compares itself against an unnamed other platforms straw man, which is unfalsifiable and therefore useless to a parent. A model-level comparison is a different thing: it compares how support is structured and priced rather than making claims about named rivals. The table below does that for the six ways IGCSE help is bought in Dubai, including the two we do not sell and the one that is already inside your school fees.

The rates in it are market figures with their sources. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. BartyED's premium named tier reaches AED 650. Independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 once travel is inside the price.

Two columns in the table deserve attention because they are where this market is weakest. The first is whether the rate is published at all: three of the six competitor pages audited publish no price, and one of its own frequently asked questions asks the price and then declines to answer it. The second is whether a permit is verified. Only one competitor page in the entire audited set touches tutor licensing, in a single subheading, and it ranks partly on that alone, which tells you how low the bar currently sits.

The licensed centre row carries a distinction worth spelling out. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific licence for a specific kind of business. IB Gram does not hold it and does not describe itself as holding it, because we have no UAE premises. A platform implying that status is making a claim you can check.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, one budget: how the hours should actually distribute
paragraphs: The single most expensive habit in IGCSE tutoring is fairness. A parent with nine subjects and a budget divides it evenly, or close to it, because that feels balanced. The result is a thin layer of support across nine subjects, none of which receives enough contact to change anything, at the same total cost as a concentrated plan that would have moved two or three grades. Allocation is the decision, and it should be made from marked evidence rather than from which subject the student complains about most.

The method is unglamorous. Sit full papers under timing in the two or three subjects that feel weakest, from the correct board and tier, and mark them against the published scheme question by question. Then rank the subjects by two things: how close the current mark sits to a grade threshold, and how much of the loss is recoverable in the weeks available. A subject losing marks to unshown working is highly recoverable. A subject losing marks to two years of missing content, eight weeks out, is not, and spending there is a decision to feel better rather than to score better.

The ranking produces uncomfortable output, which is why most families never produce it. It usually says that one subject the student finds unpleasant should receive no hours at all, because the marks are not recoverable in time, and that a subject the student feels fine about should receive several, because it sits one mark below a threshold. Both of those conclusions are correct and neither is intuitive. The written allocation exists so you can challenge it before anything starts rather than discover it later.

The table sets out the subject-level reality that feeds the ranking. The intervention timing column is the most useful: it names when work in that subject is cheap and when it is expensive, which is information nobody publishes and every parent needs. Mathematics in Year 10 is the cheapest useful hour in the whole route. Computer Science pseudocode in the last month of Year 11 is one of the most expensive, because it is a convention-learning problem that cannot be compressed.

sections.heading: Distance or evidence: what each filter actually tells you
paragraphs: It is worth being fair to the proximity instinct, because it is not irrational. A parent searching for someone nearby is buying reliability, lower cancellation risk, and the belief that a local tutor understands the school. Two of those three are genuine wants and the third is a misunderstanding. Understanding a school means knowing its assessment calendar, which board it enters each subject with and which practical route it uses, and all three of those are documents rather than postcodes. A tutor in another emirate with the calendar in front of them knows your school better than a neighbour without it.

Reliability is the strongest argument for local and it is weaker than it looks in this specific city. A visiting tutor crossing Dubai at 17:00 is in the same traffic as the school buses, and in-home sessions in this corridor are lost to road conditions more often than families expect when they book. Cancellation risk is not lower for a local in-home tutor; it is differently distributed, concentrated on exactly the evenings when traffic is worst, which tend to be the evenings a student most needs a routine.

What the evidence filter gives you instead is specific and testable. Ask a prospective tutor to mark one of your child's recent papers against the published scheme and return it with the loss pattern named. That costs them an hour and tells you more than any interview: whether they know the scheme, whether they can diagnose rather than describe, and whether their written feedback is usable by a fifteen-year-old. A tutor who will not do it has told you something. A tutor who does it well has demonstrated the only skill that matters.

The comparison is not symmetrical, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. There are students for whom physical presence is the intervention: younger children, students who will not engage with a screen, households where an adult in the room is the point of the arrangement. For those students the in-home market is the right answer and its published rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is priced in. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so for those families we are the wrong provider and this page should say so rather than argue.

sections.heading: The sixth-form fork, and how IGCSE grades decide it
paragraphs: In most of Dubai the post-16 decision is partly geographic. In this corridor it is not: A Level campuses and IB continuum schools sit within minutes of each other, so the choice turns on the student's grade profile and intentions rather than on what is reachable. That makes IGCSE grades the deciding evidence, and it makes the tier decision taken in Year 9 relevant to a conversation two years later that nobody connects to it at the time.

The two routes reward different profiles, which is the part families most often get wrong. A student with a few very strong grades and several moderate ones is often better served by A Level, which lets them specialise and drop the moderate subjects. A student with a broad, even profile and no clear subject direction is usually better served by the Diploma, which requires six subjects across groups and rewards consistency. Choosing the Diploma to keep options open is reasonable; choosing it with three weak grades across required groups is a harder two years than families anticipate.

Specific thresholds matter more in mathematics than anywhere else. A student intending A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches generally needs a strong higher-tier IGCSE grade rather than a comfortable one, because the next course assumes content and fluency the lower tier does not develop to the same depth. Where a student is one grade short, Additional Mathematics 0606 is sometimes used as bridging evidence, and that decision has to be made early enough to be taught properly rather than crammed.

On universities, the honest position is that published entry requirements differ by institution and by intake, and they change. Some engineering and science programmes name Analysis and Approaches specifically rather than accepting either mathematics route. The correct research method is to read the current page for the specific programme at the specific institution rather than relying on what an older sibling needed three years ago. Tutoring is not required for university admission, and any suggestion otherwise is false urgency about an admissions process.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside IGCSE, and the rules that govern them
paragraphs: No competitor page in any of the ten query clusters audited has a section on this, and Arabic appears across the whole corpus only as a subject chip on a list. That is a strange omission, because these subjects occupy real hours in every Dubai private school week and they shape what else a timetable can hold. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April.

The class-organisation rule is the one most parents have never been told. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. KHDA also sets the language of instruction: Standard Arabic for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

There are two further rules that affect how support for these subjects can honestly be described. KHDA requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete and checkable credential point rather than a marketing line. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which means a tutoring service cannot offer its own alternative syllabus for them.

The practical consequence for an IGCSE plan is about hours rather than content. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. Add that to nine IGCSE subjects, a sport and a commute, and the number of genuinely usable weekday evening slots in a Dubai Hills Estate household is one or two rather than five. Build the allocation around the real week.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what an inspection band means
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai learn the KHDA band and assume it is the whole picture. It is not, and the regulator map matters for families who move between emirates, which in the UAE is common. Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages audited in this market.

The other four regulators complete a map almost nobody publishes. Sharjah's private education is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval, not only inspection, sits with the emirate regulator there.

On what a band means, the useful reading is narrower than parents assume. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the judgement is about the school as a whole. It is not a subject-level statement, and it is not a statement about your child's cohort, teacher or option block. An Outstanding school can have a weak year in one subject, and a Good school can have an exceptional department. The band tells you about institutional quality; it tells you nothing diagnostic about one student's physics marks.

Scale gives the band its context. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and International Baccalaureate at 7. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

sections.heading: Sitting IGCSE as a private candidate
paragraphs: Some students need a subject their school does not enter them for: a language the family speaks at home, an extra science, Additional Mathematics where the school does not offer it, or a resit after a disappointing series. The route exists and it is routine, but it sits outside the school's administration, which is where families get caught. The entry is made through an examination centre that accepts private candidates, the family handles the registration and the fee, and the deadlines are the board's rather than the school's.

The deadline arithmetic is the part to internalise, and it is cleanest to see as a choice between two sittings rather than a single countdown. A UAE candidate has exactly two Cambridge series available, June and November, because the February and March series is offered in India only. Entries for June close in the spring and entries for November close over the summer, so at any point in the year the next usable deadline is already only a few months out. Pearson's published calendar shows the same geometry from the other side: its November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from a November series do not reach students until the new year, with November 2025 results landing on 22 January 2026. A family deciding in December that a private entry would be useful is not deciding about this winter. They are choosing between June and the November after it, and the honest version of that conversation starts with which of the two the candidate can actually be ready for.

Two board-level facts change a private-candidate plan. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable, so the centre's own confirmed timetable is the only one to plan against. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

The practical constraint most often missed is practical assessment. A private candidate in a Cambridge science has to be entered for a route the centre can actually deliver, which in practice usually means the written alternative to practical rather than a laboratory practical test. That changes the preparation substantially, because the alternative paper is a reasoning paper about experimental method rather than a manual-skills test. Confirm the component route with the centre before the teaching plan is written, not after. IB Gram teaches the syllabus and the papers; we do not register candidates and we are not an examination centre.

sections.heading: How lessons reach Dubai Hills Estate, and what we will not promise
paragraphs: Stated once, plainly: IB Gram delivers tutoring to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and the same statement appears on every country page on this site. The phrase in this page's address is what parents type, and the right response is to answer it rather than to dodge it, which is what the comparison tables above are for.

For a mainstream IGCSE subject in this community, the online argument is weaker than it is for Diploma specialisms, and it would be dishonest to overstate it. The Al Khail corridor has real local supply in mathematics, the three sciences and English. Where online wins here is at the specific end and on flexibility: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode, alternative-to-practical technique, and the ability to move hours between subjects in February when the marked evidence says they should move.

Session timing favours this community whichever model you choose. Bus runs from the Al Khail campuses often land before 15:40, so 16:00 is a genuine start rather than an optimistic one, which is earlier than almost anywhere else in the corridor. Where two children attend different campuses on different buses, one weekday evening will usually not hold two sessions, and a weekend morning is the realistic second slot rather than a later weekday one. Ramadan moves the productive window after Iftar for many households, and agreeing that shift in advance works far better than renegotiating weekly.

What video delivery requires is small and decisive. A stable connection, a device with a camera, and a way to show handwritten working: a document camera, or a phone on a stand pointing at the desk. IGCSE marks in mathematics and the sciences live in the working, so a student who cannot show their page loses most of the value of the session. That takes twenty minutes to set up and is worth doing in the first week rather than tolerating for a term.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the subjects we cannot always cover
paragraphs: Four details make a first message useful: year group, subject, syllabus code and tier. Without the code a match is a guess, because Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are three different mathematics assessments. Without the tier the past papers come from the wrong set. Without the year group the right structure is unknown, since single-subject teaching and multi-subject triage are different services. If you do not have the code and tier, the most useful email you will send this term is the one asking the school for them, subject by subject.

A free trial lesson follows with the tutor who would actually teach, and no card details are taken beforehand. In the first fortnight a full paper from the correct board and tier is marked against the published scheme, question by question. For a Year 11 student that marking is also the allocation tool, producing a written ranking of which subjects should receive hours and which should not. You get that ranking before the second paid session so you can argue with it while nothing is committed.

The limits, stated before you pay rather than after. Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode and alternative-to-practical technique are the three requests that most often exceed available specialist supply in a specific weekday evening window. When that happens we say so, and the options we offer are a different slot, a weekend morning, a short wait for a calendar to open, or a bounded block rather than a weekly commitment. We will not put a generalist into a specialist slot and leave you to find out.

Two things we do not do at all, to be clear rather than coy. We do not register examination candidates or act as an examination centre; that administration sits with the family and the centre. And we do not write coursework. A tutor teaches technique, explains what a mark scheme rewards and marks practice against published criteria; no tutor should write the coursework, draft the assignment or complete work a student submits as their own, and we decline those requests when they are made.

faqs.question: Is a nearby IGCSE tutor better than an online one for a Dubai Hills Estate family?
faqs.answer: For a mainstream subject, local can genuinely work here, which is not true everywhere in Dubai. The Al Khail corridor's concentration of British campuses has produced real freelance supply in mathematics, the three sciences and English. Where local fails is at the specific end: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode and alternative-to-practical technique regularly exceed what is available nearby. The better filter either way is evidence rather than distance. Ask a prospective tutor to mark one recent paper against the published scheme and return it with the loss pattern named.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a tutoring agency and an online platform in Dubai?
faqs.answer: An agency matches you to a freelancer and takes a margin, so the person teaching is usually not the person who set the price, and rates in this market run from around AED 150 to AED 450 and above an hour depending on level. An online platform matches and schedules directly, which generally means the tutor is named before you pay and hours can be moved between subjects against a written allocation. The practical test is to ask who teaches, who sets the rate, and whether you can reallocate hours mid-term without renegotiating.

faqs.question: How should I split a tutoring budget across nine IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Unevenly, and from marked evidence. Sit full papers in the two or three weakest subjects, from the correct board and tier, and mark them against the published scheme question by question. Then rank by how close the mark sits to a grade threshold and how much of the loss is recoverable in the time left. The output usually says one unpleasant subject should get nothing, because the marks are not recoverable, and a subject the student feels fine about should get several. Spreading evenly across nine typically moves none of them.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to fix in the last two months?
faqs.answer: Computer Science pseudocode and Additional Mathematics, for the same underlying reason: both are convention and fluency problems that need repetition rather than explanation, and repetition cannot be compressed. Mathematics method-mark habits, by contrast, are highly recoverable late because they are a habit rather than a gap, and biology terminology responds within a handful of sessions. Knowing which category a subject falls into is what makes a late allocation sensible rather than hopeful, and it is why the marked paper matters more than the student's own sense of which subject feels worst.

faqs.question: Does a licensed tuition centre in Dubai need a specific permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a different thing from an individual tutor's permit. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Individual private tutors instead need the MoHRE private tuition work permit. IB Gram holds no UAE premises and therefore no training-institute permit, and does not describe itself as holding one. Ask any centre to show theirs.

faqs.question: Which emirate regulator inspects my child's school if we move out of Dubai?
faqs.answer: It changes with the emirate. Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That map is published on the u.ae private schools page.

faqs.question: Does a KHDA Outstanding rating tell me anything about my child's IGCSE physics teaching?
faqs.answer: Very little. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the judgement is about the institution as a whole. It is not a subject-level statement and it says nothing about your child's cohort, teacher or option block. An Outstanding school can have a weak year in one department and a Good school can have an exceptional one. For a diagnostic answer about physics marks you need the marked papers, not the inspection report, and the two are answering completely different questions.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education lessons reduce the time available for IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: Yes, measurably, and almost no tutoring page mentions it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA calculates the required instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length if the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. Add nine IGCSE subjects, a sport and a commute, and most households in this community have one or two genuinely usable weekday evening slots rather than five.

faqs.question: Why are Arabic and Islamic Education classes separated for Arab and non-Arab students?
faqs.answer: Because KHDA requires it. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. KHDA also sets the language: Standard Arabic for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

faqs.question: Can my son sit an extra IGCSE subject his school does not offer?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a private candidate through an examination centre that accepts them, with the family handling registration and the fee. The deadline arithmetic is what catches people. The two series open to a UAE candidate are June and November, and the entry list for each closes months ahead of the papers, June in the spring and November over the preceding summer, so the decision has to be made a term early rather than a fortnight early. Ask the centre for its own cut-off in writing, because a centre usually sets an internal deadline earlier than the board's. Confirm the practical component route with the centre first, because laboratory practical tests are often unavailable to private candidates and the written alternative needs different preparation.

faqs.question: How many students and schools are actually in Dubai's private sector?
faqs.answer: In 2024-25 Dubai's private schools served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and International Baccalaureate at 7. Seven new private schools arrive for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. That scale is why mainstream IGCSE tutor supply in this corridor is reasonable while specialist supply is not.

faqs.question: Should I ask a tutor to mark one of my child's papers before booking?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most informative hour you can buy or ask for. Marking a recent paper against the published scheme tests three things no interview reveals: whether the tutor knows that board's scheme, whether they can diagnose a loss pattern rather than describe the content, and whether their written feedback is usable by a fifteen-year-old. A tutor who declines has told you something useful. A tutor who returns it with the pattern named has demonstrated the only skill that actually determines whether the hours will be worth anything.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram arrange a tutor to come to a house in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market here is real, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour from Bestimate's 2026 table and independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is included. If you hire into it, ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and takes two working days to issue.

faqs.question: What time can IGCSE sessions realistically start from the Al Khail campuses?
faqs.answer: Around 16:00, which is earlier than almost anywhere else in this corridor and the clearest practical advantage this community has. Bus runs often land before 15:40, and twenty minutes to change and eat makes 16:00 genuine. Where two children attend different campuses on different buses, one weekday evening will usually not hold two sessions, and a weekend morning is the realistic second slot rather than a later weekday one. During Ramadan the productive window moves after Iftar for many households, and that shift works best agreed in advance.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is available for the subject and slot we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you before you pay anything. Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode and alternative-to-practical technique are the three requests that most often exceed available specialist supply in a particular weekday evening window. The options we offer are a different slot, a weekend morning, a short wait for a specialist's calendar to open, or a bounded block rather than a weekly commitment. What we will not do is fill a specialist slot with a generalist. No competitor page audited in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: The search says "near me". The grade is decided by a syllabus code
paragraphs: Dubai Internet City is a free-zone office district with residential towers folded into it, sitting between Knowledge Park, Al Sufouh and the Marina. Families here live within a tram ride of a dense British-curriculum school cluster, and that is exactly why the phrase "IGCSE tutor near me" is such a misleading way to shop. Proximity is easy to supply in this part of Dubai. Syllabus accuracy is not.

Here is the thing that search cannot tell you. Two children in neighbouring towers can both be "doing IGCSE Maths" and be sitting entirely different qualifications. One is entered for Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 on the Extended tier, two papers, no coursework, calculator allowed on both. The other is entered for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, Higher tier, also two papers, but with a different formula sheet convention and a different style of command-term wording in the mark scheme. A tutor who has taught one and not the other will prepare your child for the wrong traps.

The same split runs through the sciences. Cambridge IGCSE Physics is 0625; Pearson's is 4PH1. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry is 0620; Pearson's is 4CH1. Cambridge Biology is 0610. Cambridge separates Core and Extended tiers and sets an alternative-to-practical paper as well as a practical option; Pearson International GCSE science does not tier the same way and assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Both are respectable routes. They are not interchangeable in a revision plan.

So this page is written from the syllabus up. It names the codes, sets out how each paper is weighted, lists the places the mark schemes punish students who know the content but answer the wrong question, and explains what past-paper work actually looks like when it is done properly rather than as a pile of downloaded PDFs. The cost section publishes what the Dubai market charges in AED, with the sources attributed, because three of the six pages ranking for this query publish no price at all, and two of the remaining three quote in US dollars, which is not a currency any Dubai family settles a tuition invoice in.

One point to settle early, because it affects every other decision. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service offered only in India. Lessons for a family in Dubai Internet City are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen and a tablet the tutor writes on. That is a deliberate trade. It widens the pool from the handful of qualified 0620 teachers who happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Sufouh to every specialist available on Gulf Standard Time, and it removes travel cost from the hourly rate.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined subject by subject, each with its own four-digit syllabus code. Most subjects offer Core and Extended tiers; Core caps at grade C or 5, Extended runs the full A* to G or 9 to 1 range. Papers are sat in the June and November series. Coursework exists in some subjects and not others, and most Dubai schools choose the non-coursework route, which pushes every mark onto timed written papers.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable per zone. The guidance is blunt: use the correct version for your zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after reading the wrong one. Families near Dubai Internet City should take the window from their own school's exams officer rather than from a UK-facing revision site.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE uses specification codes beginning with a 4 — 4MA1 Maths A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Maths Specification A tiers into Foundation and Higher. Exams run in the May/June and November windows each year. Some subjects are modular, meaning units can be sat across sittings and the best result carried, which changes how a two-year plan is sequenced compared with Cambridge.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's published history gives families a reliable sense of the lag between paper and result. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the next day. Check the live official timetable, because provisional versions are revised.

programmes.name: What comes after IGCSE in this cluster
programmes.description: Schools in the Al Sufouh and Emirates Hills belt split at 16. Some continue to A Level, some into the IB Diploma Programme, and a few offer both. The IGCSE grades a child earns in Year 11 are the entry currency for either route: a school will usually want a 7 or above in Extended Maths before letting a student into Maths AA Higher Level or A Level Further Maths.
programmes.countryNote: This matters locally because the cluster around Dubai Internet City contains both kinds of sixth form within a few kilometres. A family can genuinely choose, and the choice is easier to make in Year 10 than in the week results arrive. A tutor who knows both post-16 routes can tell you which IGCSE subjects to protect and which can safely be allowed to land a grade lower.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-inter.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects most often requested by families in the Dubai Internet City, Knowledge Park and Al Sufouh cluster, with the syllabus code and the specific place marks go missing in each one.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Two papers, both calculator-permitted on the current syllabus. Extended candidates lose most marks on functions, transformations of graphs and the harder end of probability. The recurring error is method shown too thinly to earn method marks when the final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight. Higher-tier candidates come unstuck on surds, iterative methods and vector proof. Pearson's mark schemes are generous to correct working and unforgiving to answers with no supporting line, so the fix is almost always presentation rather than content.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Extended candidates sit a theory paper, a multiple-choice paper and either a practical or the alternative-to-practical paper. Marks drain away on electrical circuit reasoning, moments and the difference between describing and explaining a graph gradient.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations carry a large share of the Extended grade and are where weaker candidates stop writing. Organic chemistry nomenclature and the electrolysis of molten versus aqueous compounds are the other two reliable sources of lost marks.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The content is wide and the papers reward precision of vocabulary over volume. Candidates who write "the plant makes food" instead of naming photosynthesis, the reactants and the site of the reaction lose marks they believe they have earned.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: Many schools in this cluster enter mid-ability candidates for a combined science award rather than three separate sciences. The content is reduced but the paper structure differs, so revising from separate-science past papers wastes time on topics that will not appear.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510/0511)
subjects.description: Common in this school cluster, where many pupils are strong speakers but score below their ability on the reading-and-writing paper. The summary task and the register of the directed-writing task are the two components a tutor can lift quickly.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition reward control of structure and a deliberate register. Candidates who treat the extended-response question as a chance to write beautifully, rather than to answer the question asked, cap themselves at the middle bands.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: The case-study paper is where grades are decided. Students who define terms correctly but never apply them to the named business in the insert lose the application and evaluation marks, which together outweigh the knowledge marks.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Internet City search actually returns
paragraphs: Type the phrase and you get three kinds of result. The first is a marketplace listing freelance tutors by distance, with no indication of which exam board any of them has taught. The second is an agency page that names the area in an H1 and then says nothing about it again. The third is a tuition centre in another part of Dubai hoping the area name is close enough. None of the three answers the question a parent is really asking, which is: can this person teach the specific paper my child is entered for?

The reason distance ranks so highly is historical. These queries were built for a market where a tutor drove to the villa, so proximity was a hard constraint and the search engine learned to treat it as the main signal. That constraint has gone for anything taught at a desk with a shared screen. What remains is the signal that was always the real one: does the tutor know the code, the papers and the mark scheme.

The table below sets out what each result type actually gives you and where it falls short, using only things a parent can check before paying anybody. Every row is a test you can run in a ten-minute phone call.

Our honest position: for a family in Dubai Internet City, the right question is not who is nearest. It is who has marked enough 0580 Paper 4 scripts to know that the functions question is where your child's two grades are hiding.

sections.heading: The syllabus codes behind every IGCSE grade in this cluster
paragraphs: A code is not administrative trivia. It determines how many papers your child sits, how long each one is, what proportion of the grade each carries, whether a calculator is allowed, and whether practical skills are assessed in a separate paper or inside the theory. Two children revising the same topic from the same textbook can need completely different practice because they are entered for different codes.

Find the code first. It is printed on the statement of entry the school issues, usually in the term before the series. If you cannot find that, the exams officer can tell you in a sentence, and most will also confirm the tier in the same reply. Any tutor who does not ask for both in the first conversation is guessing, and guessing in this market is expensive, because the wrong practice feels like progress right up until the paper.

The table maps the codes most used by schools around Al Sufouh and Internet City. Paper structures are summarised; the official syllabus document on the board's own site is the authority and should be the thing you check against, because specifications are revised and a page like this one can only be a signpost.

The practical consequence for revision is simple. A Cambridge 0625 candidate needs the alternative-to-practical paper drilled as its own discipline, because it tests experimental reasoning in a style no theory paper replicates. A Pearson 4PH1 candidate does not sit that paper and should spend the same hours on extended-calculation questions instead.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost, by paper and by habit
paragraphs: Marks leave a script in patterns, and the patterns repeat across cohorts. After enough marked papers the list becomes short and predictable, which is good news: a predictable loss is a fixable one. Almost none of it is about content the student has never met. Most of it is about answering a different question from the one printed.

The largest single cause is command-term misreading. State wants a bare fact and no justification. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants why, with a mechanism. Calculate wants a numerical answer with units and working. Evaluate wants a judgement supported by both sides. A student who explains when asked to state wastes time; one who describes when asked to explain loses the mark entirely. This is a reading habit, and it is trainable in about four sessions.

The second cause is method economy. Children who are good at mental arithmetic write less down, and then a slip in the final line costs them every mark on the question rather than one. The mark scheme is built to reward visible steps. Writing more is not a style preference here; it is the mechanism by which partial credit exists.

The third is time allocation. A paper marked out of 80 over 90 minutes gives you a little over a minute per mark. Students routinely spend fifteen minutes on a four-mark question they find interesting and then leave eleven marks blank at the end. A tutor can fix this with a stopwatch and two papers, and it is often worth more than another month of content revision.
bullets: Maths: method not shown, so a final-answer slip takes the whole question down
Chemistry: moles calculations abandoned rather than attempted in parts
Physics: graph gradients described instead of explained with a physical cause
Biology: everyday vocabulary used where the mark scheme needs a named term
Business and Economics: definitions correct but never applied to the named case
All papers: last page blank because minutes were spent unevenly

sections.heading: Past-paper work done properly, not just downloaded
paragraphs: Most families already have past papers. Very few are getting much from them. A paper sat without timing, marked against an answer key rather than a mark scheme, and then filed away, produces a score and no information. Done properly, the same paper produces a list of specific, repairable errors, which is the only output worth the three hours it takes.

The method that works is unglamorous and has four steps. Sit the paper to the real clock. Mark it against the official mark scheme, awarding each mark exactly as written, including the method marks the student thinks they do not deserve. Classify every lost mark by cause — content gap, command-term misread, method not shown, arithmetic slip, ran out of time. Then attack only the largest category in the next session.

That classification step is the one families skip and the one that carries all the value. A student losing 18 marks to timing and 4 to content does not need more content. Treating every low score as a knowledge problem is the most common waste of money in this market, and it feels productive, which is why it persists.

One boundary matters here as well. The boards hold copyright in their papers and in their mark schemes. A tutor should work from the official source on the board's own site, or through the school's own access, and should not be distributing packs of reproduced material to families. Reference it, link to it, mark against it — but do not supply it as a download.
bullets: Sit to the real clock, including reading time, in one sitting
Mark against the official mark scheme, not a model answer
Classify each lost mark by cause, then count the causes

That is the test this market mostly fails: three of the six pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays tuition in.

Read from the cheapest row upward. Budget online tuition, typically delivered by a university student, is quoted from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's Dubai rate table, with independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors run AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650.

Monthly packages circulating in this market include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are the market, published so you can judge any quote against it. For what a match actually costs in your child's subject and tier, the honest route is the free trial lesson and the consultation that follows, because the answer depends on the subject, the tier and how many weeks are left before the series.

sections.heading: Online versus a tutor driving to Al Sufouh: the arithmetic
paragraphs: This is the comparison most families in Dubai Internet City are actually making, so it deserves numbers rather than adjectives. An in-home tutor prices travel into the hourly rate whether or not the invoice says so. On the Dubai figures above, the in-home band starts about AED 30 an hour above the qualified online band and tops out considerably higher. Over a two-year IGCSE course at one session a week, that gap is real money.

Travel also shapes the timetable. A tutor crossing from Mirdif or Al Qusais to Al Sufouh at 17:00 is committing an hour and a half to deliver sixty minutes. That tutor will reasonably take the booking that minimises driving, which means the slots available to you are the ones nobody nearer wanted. An online tutor on Gulf Standard Time has no travel to recover and can hold a 19:30 Tuesday slot indefinitely.

Then there is the pool. The number of people within a twenty-minute drive of Internet City who have taught Cambridge 0620 Extended to a high standard is small. The number available on Gulf Standard Time is not. For a mainstream subject the difference is modest; for a specific tier of a specific code in a specific board, it is the whole decision.

The honest case against online is also worth stating. A child who will not sit still at a screen, or who has no quiet corner in a shared tower apartment, will do better with a person in the room. IB Gram does not offer that in the UAE, and if that is your child, a local in-home tutor is the right answer and we will say so.

sections.heading: The IGCSE exam calendar counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Nobody competing for this search publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the single most useful thing a parent can know is how early the decisions get made. Entries close months before the paper. Tier choices are made before that. By the time revision feels urgent, several options have already closed.

The fixed points for UAE candidates are the June series and the November series for Cambridge, and the May/June and November windows for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not available to candidates sitting in Dubai, which is worth knowing because a great deal of online revision content is written for it.

Work backwards from the paper. The exam window itself is published per Cambridge administrative zone, and your school's exams officer holds the correct one — Cambridge is explicit that using the wrong zone timetable is the candidate's risk. Before that come internal mocks, usually a full term ahead. Before those, the final entry deadline, which is where tier changes stop being possible. And before everything, the tier decision itself.

The dates that can be stated with confidence are the ones already past, because they are checkable. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. For the series ahead, read the live official timetable on the board's own site; provisional versions get revised, which is why no page should restate them.

sections.heading: KHDA, the school report and what an inspection band means
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band for each school. Reading that report properly tells you more about your child's chances than any league table.

The bands run from Outstanding down through Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak and Very Weak. What matters for tutoring decisions is not the overall label but the subject-level and phase-level detail inside the report. A school rated Very Good overall can carry an Acceptable judgement for secondary mathematics attainment, and that is precisely the signal a Year 10 parent should act on.

Scale context helps too. KHDA figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in Dubai, offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places.

One line for clarity, because competitors blur it. KHDA regulates schools and issues educational services permits to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no claim to KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval or accreditation. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is useful; implying it endorses a tutoring platform would not be true.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an IGCSE tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: This matters more in this market than most parents realise, because there are operators in this SERP selling completed assessed work. One sells finished Internal Assessments outright. That is an integrity breach that puts the student, not the seller, at risk of losing a qualification, and no reputable tutor goes anywhere near it.

The boundary is clear and easy to police. A tutor may teach the content, model a technique on a different example, explain a mark scheme, discuss a plan the student has drafted, and give feedback on work the student has written. A tutor may not write, redraft to completion, or supply text for anything that will be submitted as the student's own. Coursework in IGCSE subjects that still carry it falls squarely inside that rule.

In practice the honest version is also the more useful one. A student who is talked through why their conclusion does not follow from their data learns something that transfers to the next piece of work. A student handed a better conclusion learns nothing and cannot reproduce it under exam conditions, which is where most of the grade actually sits.

The same restraint applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards. They should be referenced and linked from the board's own site, used with the school's permission, and never redistributed as downloads. Any tutor offering you a pack of reproduced board material is telling you something about how they operate.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule that decides UAE university entry
paragraphs: Families in this cluster often plan on a UK or North American university and then find a UAE option is attractive after all. At that point the Ministry of Education equivalency rules become the thing that matters, and they are badly covered across this market — one ranking competitor publishes the wrong subject count.

For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A competitor page stating that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects is simply wrong.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by an IELTS Academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published in that source, so no figure for the IB route is stated here — check moe.gov.ae or the attestation authority directly.

Two cautions. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation; it is a Ministry process and parents should use the official channel. And tutoring is not required for equivalency — it helps a child reach the grades, nothing more. Anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Hardly anyone in this market mentions this, and parents should ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone who tells you the permit carries a fee is wrong.

The eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two working day completion time.

Two consequences for a Dubai Internet City family. First, individuals providing private lessons without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure you see quoted should be treated with suspicion. Second, there are conduct limits — Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Marketing your child's own teacher as a private tutor is not a service anyone should be offering.

An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again: that needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram is an online matching platform and holds no such permit, which is why it does not describe itself as KHDA approved.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The useful first conversation takes about fifteen minutes and covers four things: the exam board and syllabus code, the tier, the series your child is entered for, and the most recent marked paper with its actual score. With those four, a sensible recommendation is possible. Without them, anybody who quotes you a programme is guessing.

Then a free trial lesson, which should open with a past-paper question rather than a conversation about goals. Fifteen minutes of watching a child attempt a real question tells a tutor more than half an hour of discussion, and it tells you whether the two of them can work together. If the answer is no, the match changes and nothing has been lost.

Availability is where this market is least honest, so here is the position plainly. For mainstream IGCSE subjects at both tiers, a specialist is usually available on Gulf Standard Time within a few days. For a narrow combination — a specific tier of a less common code, in a crowded evening slot, during the weeks before a series — there may be a wait, or the only available specialist may be working from outside the UAE on the same time zone. We say which, before you book, rather than filling the slot with whoever is free.

And if the honest answer is that your child does not need a programme, that gets said too. Two sessions on moles, a re-test, and a stop is sometimes the whole intervention. A platform that cannot recommend less is not advising you.
