faqs.answer: It is online, and deliberately so. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — home visits are an India-only service. Lessons for a Dubai Internet City family run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen and a writing tablet, on Gulf Standard Time. The reason is the pool: the number of people within a twenty-minute drive of the free zone who have taught Cambridge 0620 Extended well is small, while the number available on your time zone is not. You also stop paying travel inside the hourly rate, which the Dubai in-home band prices in whether or not the invoice says so.

faqs.question: Where is the four-digit syllabus code written down, and who at school knows it?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the statement of entry the school issues, usually in the term before the series, and the exams officer can confirm it in one message. Cambridge codes are four digits — 0580 Maths, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0450 Business. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specification codes begin with a 4, such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Get the tier as well: Core or Extended for Cambridge, Foundation or Higher for Pearson Maths A. Any tutor who does not ask for both the code and the tier in the first conversation is working from assumptions, and in this market those assumptions get expensive.

faqs.question: Does it really matter whether my child sits Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: For revision planning, yes. Both are two-paper maths qualifications of comparable standing, but the papers differ in formula-sheet convention, in command-term phrasing, and in how the mark schemes reward partial work. Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended; Pearson Maths A tiers into Foundation and Higher. A tutor who has taught only one will drill the wrong traps. For a university application the difference is slight. For the eight weeks before the paper, when every session should be aimed at a specific question type, it is the whole plan.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams run for candidates sitting in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and those are the two available to UAE candidates. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a great deal of online revision content aimed at that window does not apply to your child. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable for each, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one. Take your window from your school's exams officer rather than a revision blog.

faqs.question: What does a qualified IGCSE tutor cost per hour in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Working up from the cheapest: EdFlik publishes budget online tuition from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, typically delivered by university students. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 for a qualified online tutor, and the band for that tier runs to about AED 300. In-home one-to-one with travel priced in is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, with independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. TutorChase publishes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Those are market figures from the providers named, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but scores two grades below their mocks. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always technique rather than knowledge, and it is the most fixable problem in this subject area. Three causes account for most of it. Command terms misread, so the student explains when asked to state or describes when asked to explain. Method not shown, so a slip in the final line costs every mark instead of one. Minutes allocated unevenly, so eleven marks sit blank on the last page. Mark two full papers and classify every lost mark by cause, and the pattern names itself. A block of timed paper work usually moves more grade than another month of content revision.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do families around Al Sufouh and Knowledge Park ask for most?
faqs.answer: Extended Mathematics first, by a wide margin, followed by Chemistry and Physics at Extended tier. English as a Second Language comes next and is often underestimated: many pupils in this cluster speak fluently and still score below their ability on the reading and writing paper, where the summary task and the register of the directed writing are the recoverable marks. Business Studies and Economics arrive later, usually when a case-study paper has gone badly. Computer Science is more common here than across Dubai generally, which is unsurprising given who works in the free zone.

faqs.question: Should my child sit Core or Extended, and when is that decided?
faqs.answer: Usually during Year 10, by the school with parents consulted, and it is the single most consequential academic decision of the course. Core caps at grade C or 5; Extended runs the full range. Entering a struggling candidate for Extended in hope produces a low grade rather than a high one, while entering a capable candidate for Core removes the grades a competitive sixth form wants to see. The decision should rest on marked papers at both tiers, not on optimism. Once the final entry deadline passes, changing tier stops being straightforward.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does UAE Ministry of Education equivalency actually require?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside that, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking for these searches states six subjects, which is wrong. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency; verify through the Ministry's own channel before acting.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework where the subject still has it?
faqs.answer: Up to a clear line, yes. A tutor can teach the skill the coursework assesses, model the technique on a different example, explain the criteria, discuss a plan the student has drafted, and give feedback on text the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, redraft it to completion, or supply wording for submission. That boundary is not a formality: an operator in this market sells completed assessed work, and the student is the one who loses the qualification. The honest version is also more useful, because feedback on your own reasoning transfers to the next task.

faqs.question: Is the person teaching my child from Internet City legally permitted to tutor here?
faqs.answer: They do, and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated two working day turnaround. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: What should I read in my school's KHDA inspection report before booking tuition?
faqs.answer: Skip the overall band and go to the subject and phase detail. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes judgements from Outstanding down to Very Weak, but the overall label averages across phases. A school rated Very Good can carry an Acceptable judgement for secondary mathematics attainment, and that specific line is what should drive a Year 10 tutoring decision. For context on the market, KHDA recorded 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment.

faqs.question: How long before the exams is too late to start IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: Six weeks still changes a grade if the work is aimed correctly, because at that range the available gains are in technique rather than content. Timed papers, command-term drills and minute-per-mark discipline all move marks quickly. What six weeks cannot do is build two years of missing foundations, and anyone promising that is selling you something. The honest assessment comes from one marked paper: if the losses are mostly technique and timing, there is real ground to recover. If they are mostly content gaps across every topic, the conversation should be about the November series instead.

faqs.question: Can lessons fit around a free-zone working day and Dubai evening traffic?
faqs.answer: That is one of the clearer advantages of the online format here. Parents working on the Internet City or Knowledge Park campuses often finish between 18:00 and 19:00, which makes a 19:30 weekday start the most requested slot in this cluster. Because no tutor is driving to Al Sufouh, that slot can be held week after week rather than surrendered to whoever lives closer. Weekend mornings work well for families in JBR and the Marina during the run-up to the June series, and sessions can shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan.

faqs.question: Suppose nobody is free for 0620 Extended in our evening slot — then what?
faqs.answer: You are told, before you book. For mainstream IGCSE subjects at either tier, a specialist on Gulf Standard Time is usually available within a few days. For a narrow combination — an uncommon code at a specific tier, in a crowded evening slot, in the weeks before a series — there may be a wait, or the only available specialist may be working from outside the UAE on the same time zone. Which of those applies is stated in advance rather than hidden. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is a choice they have made.

faqs.question: Will a tutor supply past papers and mark schemes for us to work from?
faqs.answer: A tutor will point you to the official source and work from it, but will not hand over reproduced packs. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the exam boards' copyright, and they should be accessed through the board's own site or through your school. A tutor offering a bundle of reproduced board material is telling you something about how they operate. What a tutor does add is the marking: a paper scored against the real mark scheme, with every lost mark classified by cause, is worth far more than the PDF itself.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-inter.closingHeading: Start with the code, not the postcode
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-inter.closingBody: If you remember one thing from this page, make it the four facts: board, syllabus code, tier, and the most recent marked paper with its real score. With those, a sensible recommendation takes fifteen minutes. Without them, every quote you receive is a guess dressed up as a plan. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the exact code your child is entered for rather than to the distance between two addresses in New Dubai. The first lesson is free, it opens with a past-paper question, and if the honest answer turns out to be four sessions and a stop, that is what you will be told.

intro.heading: A mock script tells you more than any tutor directory
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park sits in the southern corridor, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2, with industrial and commercial plots alongside residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj, served by Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Emirates Road and its own Metro station towards Expo City. A British-curriculum school and two IB schools sit inside the district, with the wider cluster in Jebel Ali, Al Furjan and Dubai South taking most of its secondary students.

Parents here search for an IGCSE tutor near me and get a list sorted by distance. That list cannot answer the question they are actually asking, which is whether anyone can fix the problem their child has. And in IGCSE the problem is usually much more specific than the grade suggests, because four quite different failures produce identical grades: thin content knowledge, method marks forfeited by unshown working, one catastrophic topic, and simply running out of time.

Three of those four are short fixes of three to five sessions. One is a term of work. No report card distinguishes them and no tutor directory helps, but a marked mock script distinguishes them in about ten minutes, and a parent can do a surprising amount of that reading themselves. This page shows how, because a family that arrives at a first conversation already knowing which of the four they have cannot be sold the wrong thing.

The second thing worth establishing is the board. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers with different codes, different tier vocabulary and different mark allocation conventions, and departments choose independently, so one student can sit Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Edexcel 4CH1 Chemistry in the same year. A tutor working from the wrong board's past papers teaches diligently and wastes the term, and nobody notices until a paper looks unfamiliar.

The third thing to settle is when a session can realistically happen, because in this corridor that is a harder question than it looks. Children travel to schools inside DIP, to Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, Dubai South or further north, so arrival home ranges from under four o'clock to past six. A session should start twenty to thirty minutes after arrival rather than immediately, which means the workable slot for one household can be an hour later than for a neighbour two streets away.

One premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. In a corridor where school runs are long and local specialist supply is thin relative to the district's footprint, that is the arrangement that puts the right teacher in front of your child rather than the nearest available one.

sections.heading: Reading a marked mock script yourself
paragraphs: This is the most valuable twenty minutes available to a family in this situation, and it needs no expertise. Sit down with the marked script, ignore the grade entirely, and look for patterns rather than for individual mistakes. Four patterns account for most of what you will find, and each points to a different plan of a different length.

Pattern one: answers that are correct but score low. A final answer the teacher has ticked, with a mark well below the total available for the question, almost always means method marks were forfeited because the working was not shown. This is the most common and most fixable problem in IGCSE mathematics and the sciences, and it typically takes four sessions of the student marking their own scripts against the scheme.

Pattern two: long answers with few marks. Where your child has written three or four sentences and collected one mark, the command term was almost certainly mismatched: a description offered where an explanation was required. Pattern three: marks lost in one concentrated region of the paper, with the rest intact. That is a single topic failure, and three to five sessions on that topic closes it. Pattern four: the back of the paper blank or rushed. That is timing, not knowledge, and the plan is a per-question time budget rather than more teaching.

The table below sets out what each pattern means and what it costs to fix, so you can arrive at any conversation with a provider already knowing roughly what you need. That changes the conversation entirely, because a family that can name the pattern cannot be sold a term of general revision for a four-session problem.

sections.heading: Matching the board, and why it is checked per subject
paragraphs: Across the competitor pages researched for this market, exactly one syllabus code appeared in an entire seven-page cluster. The consequence is predictable: families do not know the boards differ in ways that matter, so they do not check, and a tutor ends up building practice from the wrong papers with everybody acting in good faith.

The content overlaps heavily, which is what makes the error survive. A student revising Cambridge 0625 Physics material for an Edexcel 4PH1 paper will recognise most of the physics and still meet an unfamiliar paper. Tier vocabulary differs outright, with Cambridge setting Core and Extended and Edexcel Mathematics setting Foundation and Higher, which creates a specific hazard: a parent translating between those terms on a phone call can agree to the wrong entry.

Departments choose independently, which is the part most often missed. A student at a school in DIP or Jebel Ali can sit Cambridge for one subject and Edexcel for another in the same examination season, with two sets of conventions and two timetables. So the check is per subject, it takes one email to each subject teacher, and it is the highest-value administrative task a parent can do this term.

Then tell the tutor in writing which codes they are working from, and ask which series their practice papers come from. A tutor who answers immediately has an organised set; one who cannot is improvising, and improvised practice in Year 11 is how a term disappears without any identifiable mistake having been made.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, and what to do if you have four
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the planning unit that works for one component, with six to twelve focused sessions inside it and the student's own timed practice between them. Families in this corridor frequently have less, partly because mock results arrive late in a term and partly because a long school run compresses the week. So it is worth saying what shorter windows can and cannot do.

With eight weeks, week one is diagnosis rather than teaching, weeks two to six teach and then test the identified failure, week seven is a second full paper under timing, and week eight is a review at which stopping is a legitimate outcome. With four weeks, the diagnosis has to come from the script before the first session rather than during it, and the target narrows to one component with no second attempt at choosing.

With two weeks, the honest advice is to stop trying to move the grade and start protecting it. Drill the things that are pure technique and lose nothing: showing working, carrying full precision, reading the command term, and a per-question time budget. Those four cost no new learning and are worth real marks. Attempting new content in the final fortnight produces a tired student and an unchanged outcome.

And if the time has genuinely run out, the November series exists. Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run one, and for a candidate in Dubai that is the resit route, since the February and March series is offered to India only. Planning a November attempt is easier than a first attempt because you have the real script and the real grade, so the two or three topics that cost it can be identified precisely. Entry is arranged by the school's exams officer.

sections.heading: The tier decision in a corridor where families move
paragraphs: The tier entry caps or opens the grade available, and it is confirmed by the school to a school deadline. In the southern corridor it carries an extra complication, because this is a growing area where families change schools more often than in established districts, and post-16 provision varies between the long-standing schools in Jebel Ali and the newer ones towards Dubai South and Expo City.

The consequence is specific. A capped mathematics or science entry removes a prerequisite whatever grade is achieved inside it, so a Core or Foundation mathematics candidate is not positioned for A Level Mathematics or for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in the IB Diploma. If the family then moves to a school with a different post-16 offer, a Year 10 administrative decision constrains a choice nobody was considering at the time.

The honest test is a timed paper from the harder tier, taken now, with no notes and marked properly. Mid-range or above and the conversation is over. Near the bottom of that tier's range and there is a genuine question about whether a block of work closes the gap in the weeks available. What should not decide it is which tier feels more comfortable in class, because comfort and capability separate sharply under examination timing.

Ask the subject teacher when the tier must be confirmed and work backwards from that date rather than from the examination date. Ask explicitly what the entry means for post-16 options, since it is usually presented as a form rather than as the pathway decision it is. And if a school move is even possible, weight the decision towards keeping the fuller tier open where the student can genuinely cope.

sections.heading: What it costs, and what to verify before paying
paragraphs: Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all, two quote in US dollars and one publishes a star rating it awarded itself. So the useful approach is to publish the market, let any quote be judged against it, and compare providers on what can actually be verified.

The market, attributed and dated October 2026. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 per hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, BartyED at AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table, and in this corridor the travel component is doing more work than it would centrally. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

The verifiable items are these. Whether a rate is published at all and in a currency you transact in. Whether the provider states a position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit that individuals offering private lessons need under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Whether a free trial exists and what condition is attached to it on the same page. Whether the tutor can name the board, code and tier. And whether any approval is claimed from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, which an independent tutoring platform does not hold, and which we do not hold either.

For wider context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the variable line in an education budget, which is the argument for a short diagnosed block rather than the cheapest available hour attached to no plan.
bullets: A published rate, in a currency you actually pay in
A stated position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit
A free trial with any condition disclosed on the same page
A tutor who can name the board, code and tier
No claimed approval from any regulator or examination board

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: Send five things: the board and code for each subject of concern, the tier, the school, the last two marked papers, and the time your child actually gets home on a normal weekday. In this corridor that last item decides whether the plan survives contact with the week, and it is the one most providers never ask for.

The free trial lesson comes before any payment and does two jobs. It produces the diagnosis, confirming or correcting whatever you read in the script yourself, and it tests the proposed slot in practice. If the agreed time turns out to be fifteen minutes too early for a student coming off a long bus journey, that is far better discovered before a term is built around it.

Four things this page will not do, set against the eight-week plan in section four. It will not promise a grade, because the plan's worth lies in what it closes, and no honest provider controls the outcome well enough to promise it. It will not suggest that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression, which would be a false claim about a regulatory process; those processes examine your child's certificate, not who helped them revise for it. It will not borrow a regulator's standing either: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch, in this corridor or anywhere else. And it will not quote satisfaction statistics, because a figure published without its sample, its date and its method is decoration rather than evidence.

Two final notes. Enquiry forms collect information about a child, so we ask only for what the plan needs, say why, and keep a privacy link on every page; we do not ask for a child's photograph and you can ask for the record to be deleted. And we do not publish or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads, because that material is the boards' copyright. We cite it and link to it, and work from what your child's school legitimately provides.

faqs.question: What should I look for in my child's marked IGCSE mock script?
faqs.answer: Patterns rather than individual mistakes, and ignore the grade. Correct answers scoring well below the question total mean method marks lost to unshown working. Long answers collecting one mark mean a command term mismatch. Losses concentrated in one region mean a single weak topic. A rushed or blank back page means timing. Those four need plans of three to five sessions, three to four, three to five and four respectively, so identifying which you have is worth more than any amount of general revision.

faqs.question: Does a tutor travel to our address in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: No. We teach IGCSE one-to-one into DIP homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. In this corridor that is a practical advantage, since an in-home tutor would be driving towards your address in the same afternoon traffic your child's school bus is sitting in.

faqs.question: Why is local tutor supply thin in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Structural reasons rather than anything about the community. Dubai Investments Park is substantially industrial, commercial and warehousing land with residential enclaves inside a large footprint, so the resident population is low relative to the district's size and the number of resident qualified teachers is low in absolute terms. It also sits far enough south that in-home tutors ration evening slots by drive time. Narrow the request to a specific board and code and the local list can be empty on the evening you need it.

faqs.question: How do I know the tutor is using the right past papers?
faqs.answer: Ask two questions and expect immediate answers. Which board and code are you building practice from, and which series do these papers come from? A tutor with an organised set answers both without pausing. One who cannot is improvising, and improvised practice in Year 11 is how a term disappears with nobody making an identifiable mistake. Confirm the code yourself first from the school's assessment paperwork, then state it to the tutor in writing.

faqs.question: We only have four weeks before the exams. What can be done?
faqs.answer: One narrow component, chosen before the first session rather than during it, which means doing the script reading yourself first. Four weeks has no margin for choosing the wrong target. What four weeks cannot do is broad coverage, so the honest plan picks the component carrying the most recoverable marks and leaves the rest. If you have two weeks, stop chasing the grade and protect it: drill shown working, full precision, command terms and a per-question time budget.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting if the mock grade was very low?
faqs.answer: It depends what the script shows rather than what the grade says. A very low grade produced by unshown working, a command term habit and a timing collapse is three technique problems and recoverable faster than families expect. A very low grade with scattered small losses and no pattern is a genuine content gap, which is a term of weekly work rather than a short block. The script distinguishes them, and we would rather tell you the second answer than sell the first.

faqs.question: What if you cannot cover our board and subject at the time we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the nearest workable alternative and a realistic date for when the slot or the specialism opens. Core subjects on both boards are usually matched within a few days; the tight points are early evenings in the weeks before a series and narrower board and code combinations. What will not happen is a general tutor being presented as the board specialist you asked for, which is the standard failure in this market and the reason many families give up.

faqs.question: Could our tutor be outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is stated rather than hidden if so. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a particular board and code, the match may be a teacher working from outside the country on Gulf Standard Time. Several providers conceal this behind a non-UAE contact number, which is a trust failure rather than a delivery problem. The question that matters does not change: has this person taught this board and code, and can they name the failure from a marked script?

faqs.question: Our child is at school in Jebel Ali. What time can sessions start?
faqs.answer: Usually around 6pm. The return journey from Jebel Ali in afternoon traffic typically puts a secondary student home between 4.45pm and 5.30pm, and the session should begin twenty to thirty minutes after arrival, because a student who sits down immediately is present without being available. For a Dubai South run the floor is later again. Write down the real arrival times for a week rather than estimating, and build the plan on that number.

faqs.question: Can a full past paper be done on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and attempting it is one of the commonest ways a plan goes wrong in this corridor. A full paper needs unbroken time and a reasonably fresh student, which a weekday evening after a long bus journey does not provide. Put complete timed papers at the weekend and use weekday evenings for narrow technique work such as marking a script against the scheme, command term drills or precision rules. That split also happens to put the highest-value work in the best slot.

faqs.question: Does the tier entry matter if we might change schools?
faqs.answer: It matters more. A capped mathematics or science entry removes a prerequisite regardless of the grade achieved inside it, and post-16 provision varies across this corridor between established Jebel Ali schools and newer ones near Dubai South and Expo City. Since families here move schools more often than in older districts, a Year 10 form can constrain a Year 12 choice at a school you have not yet joined. Weight the decision towards keeping the fuller tier open where the student can cope.

faqs.question: How do I compare tutoring providers when nobody publishes prices?
faqs.answer: Compare on what can be verified rather than on tone. Whether a rate is published at all and in dirhams. Whether the provider states a position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which individuals offering private lessons need and which is free for two years. Whether a free trial exists with its conditions on the same page. Whether the tutor can name the board, code and tier. And whether any regulator or board approval is claimed, which no independent platform holds.

faqs.question: Should we book help for all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: Usually not in a long-commute household, because each subject needs independent practice between sessions and the journey has already taken those hours. Send marked scripts from two different sciences: if the same pattern appears in both, such as command term mismatches or unshown working, one block improves all three. If the patterns differ, start with the subject where the script shows the clearest recoverable component, verify the fix on a timed paper, then move to the next.

faqs.question: Is the November series a realistic plan rather than a defeat?
faqs.answer: It is a realistic plan, and in some cases the better one. Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run a November series, and for a candidate sitting in Dubai that is the resit route; the February and March series is offered to India only. A November attempt is easier to plan than a first attempt because you hold the real script and the real grade, so the two or three topics that cost it can be identified precisely rather than guessed. Entry is arranged by the school's exams officer.

Every match starts with the syllabus code on your child's exam entry, the tier the school has entered them for, and the slot in the week that survives the Marina traffic.

intro.heading: Searching for a tutor near the Marina is really a scheduling question
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai Marina who searches for an IGCSE tutor near me is rarely asking about geography for its own sake. The question underneath is narrower: can somebody competent sit with my child between the end of the school day and the point where the evening collapses? Marina households run on a long commute at both ends. Children board a bus at the tower at 6:40am, are taught until early afternoon, and are back in the building somewhere between 3:30pm and 4:30pm depending on which school and which route. Bolt a tutor's own drive onto that and the hour that was meant to help becomes the thing everyone is late for.

That is the problem this page is built around. Everything below starts from the Marina timetable and works outwards: which schools the Marina, JBR, JLT and the Greens actually feed, what time each of those schools releases, and what a workable session looks like on a Sunday, a Tuesday and a Thursday. The syllabus content matters too, and it is covered further down, but a tutor your child cannot reliably meet is not a tutor.

The honest answer to the literal search is that IB Gram does not send anybody to a Marina address. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India. That is not a workaround. It is the reason a Marina family can be matched with somebody who has taught Extended Chemistry 0620 for years rather than with whoever is free in Jumeirah on a Tuesday. Removing the drive removes the single biggest constraint on who is available at 5pm.

Dubai is the densest private-school market in the UAE. KHDA counted 227 private schools in the emirate for 2024-25, teaching 387,441 pupils across 17 different curricula, with 37 per cent of those pupils on a UK curriculum. That means IGCSE is the single largest Year 10 and Year 11 route in the city, and that a Marina family has real choice. It also means that two children living in the same tower may be sitting different boards, different tiers and different papers in the same subject, which is exactly why a generic weekly hour so often disappoints.

What follows is the practical version. Finish times for the schools this neighbourhood feeds. The board and syllabus codes you will see on an exam entry slip. What the Dubai market charges, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. Where the Extended tier quietly caps a grade. How Ramadan and the long Gulf summer move a revision plan. And what a tutor is allowed to do with a piece of coursework, which matters more than most families realise until a school raises it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-marin.programmesIntro: A Marina teenager is almost always on one of four tracks at 14 to 16. Knowing which one tells you what the next two years contain, which certificate the UAE Ministry of Education will later look at, and whether tutoring should be aimed at papers or at criteria.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses ending in externally marked papers, usually eight to ten subjects. Most subjects are tiered: Core papers lead to a restricted grade range, Extended papers open the full range. Syllabus codes are four digits and they matter. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for younger year groups.
programmes.countryNote: Several British-curriculum schools serving the Marina and Al Barsha corridor enter Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson for mathematics, or split by subject department. Ask the examinations officer for the entry codes rather than assuming; two pupils in the same Year 11 class at the same school can sit different boards in different subjects, and the past papers you practise on need to match.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes begin with a digit and a subject prefix, such as 4MA1 for mathematics or 4PH1 for physics. Mathematics is tiered as Foundation and Higher. Pearson International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so a Marina family planning a revision block should work from the live official timetable PDF on qualifications.pearson.com rather than from a date copied onto a tutoring website. Dates get revised. A plan built on a stale date is the most avoidable mistake in this market.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The alternative route at the same age in IB-continuum schools near the Marina. There are no tiered papers. Work is assessed against four criteria per subject group, each scored 1-8, converted at the end of the year into a 1-7 grade. MYP 5 carries the Personal Project, which is supervised in school.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Emirates Hills and the Meadows often have one child in MYP and one sitting IGCSE, because the two systems coexist within a short drive of each other here. Support for an MYP child looks different: the target is the criterion descriptor, not a past paper, and a tutor who only knows exam boards will aim at the wrong thing.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the main curriculum
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes for both groups are prohibited.
programmes.countryNote: This is the part of a Marina report card that surprises families who have arrived recently from the UK. These subjects sit on the timetable in addition to the IGCSE block, and they carry their own language-of-instruction rules: Standard Arabic for Islamic Education for Arab pupils and for Arabic first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-marin.subjectsIntro: Requests from Marina and JBR households concentrate in a predictable handful of subjects. Below is what each one actually assesses at IGCSE and the point in the course where marks usually start leaking, which is the thing a parent needs in order to judge whether an hour a week is aimed at the right place.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are the two most common entries around the Marina. Extended and Higher tier add algebraic fraction manipulation, functions, calculus-adjacent gradient work, histograms with unequal class widths and vectors. Most lost marks are method marks surrendered by jumping straight to an answer.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1. The repeated failure points are unit conversion inside a multi-step calculation, describing an experiment in enough detail to be repeatable, and the difference between what a graph gradient means and what its intercept means. Electricity circuits reward practice more than reading.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1. Extended adds mole calculations with limiting reagents, electrolysis products at both electrodes and organic series naming. Students who can recite definitions still lose marks on the six-mark extended-response questions because they list facts instead of building a chain of reasoning.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1. The marks sit in precise terminology and in data questions on unfamiliar experiments. Osmosis, enzyme-rate graphs and the difference between a control variable and a control experiment account for a large share of avoidable losses at Extended tier.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Cambridge 0500 and 0510 are both widely entered around the Marina, and the choice between them has a real effect on the grade ceiling and on what a university later accepts. Directed writing and summary tasks are marked against reading criteria as well as writing criteria, which catches confident writers out.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts vary by school, so a tutor has to work from your child's actual text list rather than a generic one. Marks are awarded for close analysis of specific language choices; retelling the plot of a set play scores very little however fluently it is written.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0450 and 0455. These reward application to the stimulus case rather than textbook definitions. The analysis and evaluation marks at the top of each question are where most Marina students stop short, usually because nobody has shown them what a developed evaluation paragraph looks like.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Cambridge 0478. Pseudocode and trace tables are mechanical skills that improve quickly with supervised practice. The theory half, covering data representation, networks and security, is usually where a strong programmer loses the grade.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by a minority of Marina students heading for A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level. It introduces differentiation, integration and trigonometric identities a year early, and it is the single best preparation for the jump into Diploma mathematics.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools and examinable as an IGCSE subject in its own right. KHDA requires schools to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential point a parent can reasonably ask about.

schoolClusters.note: The schools most often named on enquiries from this cluster. Several run IGCSE at 16 and then split into A Level or the IB Diploma, which is why a Year 11 decision often has a Year 12 consequence attached to it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-marin.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request from this cluster. All of them are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and all of them start with a free trial lesson so the match can be judged before anything is paid.

modes.title: The weekday evening hour
modes.description: A single fixed slot each week, placed after the bus returns and before the household's own dinner routine. For most Marina addresses that lands between 5pm and 7pm. The slot is held in the tutor's diary for the term, which matters more than it sounds: a floating session is the one that quietly stops happening by week six.

modes.description: Longer sessions placed where the weekday squeeze does not reach. Families in Al Furjan and on Bluewaters, where the journey home is the binding constraint, often prefer two hours on a Saturday morning to two scattered weekday hours. It also suits paper practice, which needs an uninterrupted run rather than forty minutes before a swim squad.

This is the right purchase when a mock paper has already identified where the marks went, and the wrong one when nobody yet knows what the problem is.

sections.heading: What a Marina parent is actually buying when they search for a tutor nearby
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Marina, in practice, means an hour that reliably happens. Proximity is a proxy for that and nothing more. The reason distance ever mattered is that a tutor who had to drive from Mirdif to a Marina tower at 5pm on a Tuesday would either arrive late, charge for the journey, or decline the slot. Remove the journey and the proxy stops being useful, because the pool of people who can teach your child at 5pm on a Tuesday is suddenly everyone who is free at 5pm on a Tuesday rather than everyone who is free and within a twenty-minute drive.

This matters most in exactly the subjects Marina families ask about. A Year 11 child sitting Extended Chemistry 0620 with a weak grasp of electrolysis needs somebody who has marked that question type repeatedly. Within a short radius of a given tower there may be nobody who fits that description and is free in the slot. Across the UAE and our wider panel there will be several. The trade is a specialist you can reach against a generalist you can see, and for a tiered, code-specific qualification the specialist usually wins.

There is a second, less obvious benefit. A session with no journey attached can be forty-five minutes rather than ninety, because nobody is amortising a drive. That changes how support can be shaped. A child who needs frequent short contact before a series of mocks can have three half-hours in a week instead of one long session they are too tired to use. Families paying by the hour for a visiting tutor almost never get that option offered, because it does not work economically for the person doing the driving.

To state the delivery plainly, since the phrase in the search suggests otherwise: IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Marina address, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. Everything else on this page assumes that, including the scheduling table below.

sections.heading: The Marina school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: The finish time of the school day is the single piece of information that determines whether a tutoring slot is realistic, and it is the one no tutoring website publishes. Below is an indicative picture for the schools most often named by families in this cluster. Treat it as a starting point and check it against your own school's current timetable, because finish times shift with year group, with activity days and with the academic calendar.

Two patterns emerge from it. The first is that nothing before 4:30pm is dependable for a Marina household, and nothing before 5pm is dependable for a JLT or Al Furjan one, because the inbound leg of the bus route is the variable part. The second is that activity days are the real enemy of a weekly slot. A child in a school squad or a Model United Nations team will finish on site at 5pm one or two days a week, and a session placed on one of those days is the session that gets cancelled until it stops being booked at all.

The practical answer is to pick the quietest day in the week rather than the most convenient one, and then protect it. Sunday is often the best candidate in Dubai because it sits at the start of the school week, before fixtures and deadlines accumulate. Thursday is usually the worst, for the same reason in reverse. Where a household has two children in the same school, a back-to-back pair on one evening protects one evening rather than spoiling two.

sections.heading: Which board your child is actually entered for, and why the codes matter
paragraphs: Parents in this cluster frequently discover in Year 11 that the past papers their child has been working through belong to the wrong board. It is an easy mistake. Schools around the Marina mix boards by department, and the certificate at the end says International GCSE either way. The difference shows up in the paper structure, in the formula sheet provided, in the tiering, and in whether a topic is examined at all.

The fix takes one email. Ask the examinations officer for the board and the syllabus code for each subject your child is entered for. You will get back a list like 0580, 0620, 4PH1, 0500. Those codes are the key to everything else: the correct specification, the correct past papers, the correct mark scheme wording, and the correct timetable. A tutor who starts by asking for that list is telling you something useful about how they work.

The table below sets out the boards a Marina family will encounter and where each one's authoritative material lives. None of these documents should be supplied to you by a tutoring company. Specifications, past papers and mark schemes are the boards' copyright and they are published on the boards' own sites; a provider offering to hand over a bundle of them is doing something it is not entitled to do. Reference them, and download them from the source.

One further wrinkle catches families who move mid-course. A child arriving in Year 11 from a UK school may have begun a domestic GCSE specification rather than an international one, and the content lists are not identical even where the subject name is. The same applies in reverse to a family leaving Dubai partway through. In both cases the first hour of tutoring is better spent mapping what has and has not been taught against the specification the child will actually be examined on, rather than beginning revision on an assumption. That mapping exercise is unglamorous and it saves whole weeks later.

sections.heading: The twenty-minute radius problem, subject by subject
paragraphs: The reason a nearby tutor is harder to find than it looks is that IGCSE is not one subject. It is thirty or forty of them, each tiered, each on one of three boards. A parent searching within a short drive of a Marina tower is looking for the intersection of four conditions: the right subject, the right tier, the right board, and free at 5pm on a specific weekday. Each condition cuts the pool. Together they can cut it to nobody.

This is where the online format earns its place rather than being a compromise. The table below is an honest account of what changes per subject when the radius constraint is dropped. For mathematics the gain is modest, because competent IGCSE mathematics tutors are relatively plentiful in Dubai. For Extended Chemistry with an electrolysis problem, or for Computer Science theory, or for Arabic as a first language to 0508 standard, the gain is the difference between a specialist and a willing generalist.

It is worth being equally honest about the ceiling. Dropping the radius does not conjure a specialist for every niche at every hour. Some combinations, particularly minority-language subjects and the less commonly entered creative subjects, take longer to match, and occasionally the honest answer is that the best available slot is a weekend one rather than a Tuesday evening. Where that applies we say so before anything is booked rather than filling the slot with somebody who does not know the specification.

sections.heading: What a Marina family will be quoted, and what the monthly figure looks like
paragraphs: Most families think in months rather than in hours, so start there. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged offers in the market sit alongside those numbers: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Seeing the monthly figure first is useful, because it is the number that has to survive a family budget for two academic years rather than for one week.

Translated back into hourly rates, the published bands look like this. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is the university-student and group end of the market. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200 to 450 or more, with home tutors reaching AED 500. BartyED quotes AED 650 at the named-examiner end. Those are each provider's own published figures as recorded in October 2026, not ours, and they will move.

Three things follow for a Marina household. First, the spread is roughly fifteenfold from bottom to top, so a quoted rate tells you almost nothing on its own; what matters is whether the person has taught the specific syllabus code at the specific tier. Second, the in-home premium is real and it is mostly travel: the same qualified tutor appears in the AED 150 to 300 band online and the AED 180 to 500 band at an address. Third, the useful question to ask a provider is not the rate but what the rate includes, because marking, session notes and a replacement if the match fails are either in the price or they are not.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages, and no figure above is ours. The honest route is a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many sessions the situation actually needs, which is frequently fewer than a family expects and occasionally more. Ask, too, whether a quote includes VAT, because the published figures above are not consistent on that point and the difference compounds over a two-year course.

Qualified subject tutor, online: roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour

IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists: roughly AED 200 to 450 and above

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the entry decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: In most Cambridge subjects a school enters a candidate for either Core or Extended papers, and in Pearson mathematics for Foundation or Higher. The decision is usually taken by the department during Year 11, often on the evidence of a mock. It has consequences a parent should understand before it is made rather than after, because the Core route restricts the grade range available and the restriction cannot be undone once the entry closes.

The right question is not always 'how do we get onto Extended'. A child placed on Extended who cannot access the harder half of the paper may score worse than the same child on Core, and a school that recommends Core is often reading the evidence correctly. Where tutoring genuinely changes the picture is earlier: in Year 10 and the first term of Year 11, when the gap being described is a gap in the foundations rather than a gap in ambition. By March of Year 11 the entry is usually fixed and the useful work is maximising the grade within the tier that was chosen.

So the timing of the hour matters as much as the hour. A Marina family deciding in September of Year 10 whether to start has a different question in front of them from one deciding in February of Year 11. In the first case the work is foundational and the entry decision is still open. In the second the work is paper technique inside a fixed tier, and the honest advice is sometimes to buy fewer sessions aimed at a shorter list of topics rather than a general weekly hour that tries to cover everything and lands nowhere.

Ask the department two questions at the first parents' evening of Year 11: which tier are you minded to enter, and what would change your mind. The answers tell you what the next six months of support should be aimed at, and they are far more useful than any generic revision plan.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the Gulf summer and the shape of a Dubai revision year
paragraphs: A revision plan written for a UK school year does not survive contact with the Dubai calendar. Three features of the local year reshape it. The school day shortens during Ramadan and the household rhythm changes with it, so afternoon tutoring frequently moves to a post-Iftar slot for that period. The long summer break is longer and hotter than a UK one, which makes it the best available window for closing a foundational gap and the worst for sustaining momentum if nothing is scheduled. And a substantial number of Marina families travel for extended periods during breaks, often across time zones.

Each of those is manageif it is planned for. Ramadan sessions can be moved later in the evening rather than cancelled, and the subjects that suit a shorter, quieter session are the content-heavy ones rather than timed paper practice. Summer is where a Year 10 student who has fallen behind in algebra can realistically catch up, because there are no competing deadlines; a fortnightly session across July and August costs little and prevents the September restart from being a reset. Travel is simply easier to accommodate when the lesson follows the laptop rather than the postcode.

The dates that genuinely bind are the board ones, and they sit further out than families expect. Start with Pearson, because Pearson publishes the window precisely: the November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the results from that series do not reach students until the new year, the way November 2025 results landed with students on 22 January 2026. Entries for a November series close over the preceding summer, so a Dubai Marina family looking at an autumn sitting in September is already looking at the series after it. Cambridge has the same shape across its own two series, June and November, with entries closing months in front of the papers; the February and March series that appears in some online calendars is offered in India only and is not available here. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Confirm your school's zone with the examinations officer.

For the IB side of the local picture, note that no IB session or results date on this site is confirmed from the IB itself, because ibo.org blocks automated checking. UAE schools sit the main May session; for any specific date, ask your child's IB coordinator or read it on ibo.org directly.
bullets: Ramadan: move the slot later rather than pausing, and favour content over timed papers
Summer: the only window where a foundational gap closes without competing deadlines
Entry deadlines sit months before the papers; the Pearson November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026 with entries closed since the summer
Confirm your centre's Cambridge administrative zone before using any timetable

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Two things in this market are routinely offered that should not be. The first is a bundle of specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables supplied as downloads. Those documents belong to Cambridge, Pearson and OxfordAQA, and reproducing or redistributing them is not a provider's to do. The correct behaviour is to name the document, cite where it lives on the board's own site, and work from the copy you download yourself. If a provider's selling point is a vault of material, ask who owns it.

The second is help with work that has to be the student's own. IGCSE carries less internally assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but where it exists, and in every piece of assessed work a school submits, the boundary is the same: a tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria, reviews a draft the student wrote, and gives feedback the student then acts on. A tutor does not write, redraft or complete the work. One provider in this market sells completed IB Internal Assessments outright. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, and it is the clearest possible reason to ask a direct question about process before booking anybody.

There is a third boundary worth knowing because it affects who you can legally hire. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted with suspicion. The official application route is MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'.

In Abu Dhabi there is an additional rule Marina families sometimes encounter through relatives there: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against the current ADEK publication before relying on it. Either way, 'your child's own teacher, privately' is not a request anybody should be making.

process.title: Send the subject, the board and the code
process.description: One line is enough to start: the subject, the exam board, the syllabus code and the tier, plus the year group. If you do not have the codes yet, the examinations officer at your child's school will send them on request. Having them before the first session is what stops a tutor working from the wrong specification.

process.title: Name the two slots that genuinely work
process.description: Pick the quietest weekday in your household's week, not the most convenient one, and give a second option. Tell us the bus return time for your address and whether there are activity days. Slots placed around a real timetable survive the term; slots placed around good intentions do not.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session with no commitment. It is a diagnostic as much as an introduction: the tutor works through a question your child has recently got wrong and finds out whether the problem is the topic, the method, the exam technique or the reading of the question. You get a written note of what was found.

process.title: Agree a short plan, not a subscription
process.description: After the trial you should get a topic list and a rough number of sessions, with a point at which the plan is reviewed. If the honest answer is six sessions on three topics rather than a weekly hour for a year, that is what we say. Open-ended commitments suit the provider more than the student.

process.title: Review against mock papers
process.description: Progress is judged on marked papers, not on how the sessions felt. After each school mock the topic list is rewritten against the actual mark breakdown. Where a subject has stabilised, the sessions stop or move to another subject rather than continuing out of habit.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code comes first
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the board and code on the entry, not from the subject name. A Cambridge 0580 Extended student and a Pearson 4MA1 Higher student need different papers, different formula sheets and different mark scheme wording, and a tutor who does not ask which one you are sitting has told you something.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price or the evening
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for a comparably qualified tutor. Most of that gap is the journey. Removing it also removes the lateness, the cancellations in bad weather and the pressure to book ninety minutes because sixty does not justify the drive.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the Marina week
whyPoints.description: Sessions are placed after the bus returns and away from activity days, in Gulf Standard Time, and held in the diary for the term. Where a household has two children, consecutive slots protect one evening instead of spoiling two.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what a tutor may do
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains the criteria, reviews a draft your child has written and gives feedback. A tutor does not write or complete assessed work, and does not redistribute board-owned papers or mark schemes. Both boundaries are stated before anyone starts.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before booking
whyPoints.description: Some subject, tier and time-slot combinations are thin, particularly minority languages and some creative subjects. Where the best available match is a weekend slot or a longer wait, we say so rather than filling the hour with somebody who has not taught the specification.

whyPoints.title: A free trial before anything is agreed
whyPoints.description: One full diagnostic session at no cost, with a written note of what it found. If the match is wrong, say so and the next one is arranged. Judging a tutor from a profile page is guesswork; judging one from an hour with your own child is not.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Marina who will come to the apartment?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. Visiting tutors do exist in this market and published rates for them run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for comparable qualifications, with most of that gap being travel. The practical trade is between somebody you can see who may be a generalist and somebody matched to your child's exact syllabus code and tier. For a tiered, code-specific qualification the second usually produces more marks.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start for a child on a Marina school bus?
faqs.answer: For most Marina and JBR addresses the bus returns between about 3:30pm and 4:30pm, so 5pm is the first dependable start and 4:30pm works only on non-activity days for the closest schools. JLT, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens households should plan for 5:30pm because the inbound leg is longer. Activity days matter more than the average finish time: a child in a school squad or a Model United Nations team will be on site until about 5pm once or twice a week. Pick the quietest day in the week rather than the most convenient one and the slot survives the term.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Email the examinations officer at the school and ask for the board and syllabus code for each subject. You should get back a list such as 0580, 0620, 4PH1, 0500. Schools around the Marina mix boards by department, so a child can be sitting Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in mathematics in the same year. The codes determine which specification, past papers, mark scheme wording and timetable apply. Working through the wrong board's papers is one of the most common and most avoidable problems we see in Year 11, and the email that prevents it takes two minutes to send.

faqs.question: My child is on Core tier. Can tutoring move them onto Extended?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the conversation happens early enough. The entry decision is usually taken by the department during Year 11 on the evidence of a mock, and once entries close it is fixed. Tutoring changes the picture most in Year 10 and the first term of Year 11, when the gap is foundational rather than one of ambition. By February of Year 11 the useful work is maximising the grade inside the chosen tier. Ask the department which tier they are minded to enter and what would change their mind; those two answers tell you what the next six months of support should target.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost per month for a family in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged offers in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures published by other providers, not IB Gram prices. Ask any provider what the rate includes, and whether it includes VAT, because the published figures are inconsistent on both points.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IGCSE subjects for the same child?
faqs.answer: For closely related subjects, often yes. Physics and mathematics pair well because the algebra and graph work overlap. Chemistry and biology pair less well than parents expect, because the mark schemes reward quite different things. Where one tutor covers two subjects, a 90-minute session split across both is usually better than two separate hours, since the handover time disappears. Where the two subjects need genuinely different specialists, two tutors is the right answer even though it is less convenient, and we would rather say so than stretch one person across both.

faqs.question: Do sessions have to stop during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: No. The usual adjustment is to move the slot later into the evening, often after Iftar, and to use that period for content-heavy work rather than timed paper practice, which needs an alert start. The school day shortens during Ramadan and the household rhythm changes with it, so a 5pm slot that worked in January frequently does not work in the Ramadan weeks. Tell us before the period starts rather than during it, so the tutor's diary can be rearranged once instead of cancelled repeatedly. Families who plan this in advance lose no continuity at all.

faqs.question: Is the long Dubai summer a good time to start IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: For a foundational gap it is the best window in the year, because there are no school deadlines competing for attention. A Year 10 student who has fallen behind in algebra or in chemical calculations can realistically close that gap across July and August, and a fortnightly session is usually enough to stop September being a restart from zero. For paper technique it is a weaker window, because the techniques fade without the pressure of assessment. Many Marina families travel for long stretches of the summer, which online delivery accommodates without rescheduling around a tutor's own holiday.

faqs.question: Should I ask a Dubai Marina tutor whether they hold the MoHRE tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat specific amounts you see quoted as unverified. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold the permit; the official route is MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' page.

faqs.question: Will a tutor give us past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: They should not, and nor should any provider. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the property of Cambridge, Pearson and OxfordAQA, and redistributing them is not a tutoring company's to do. The right behaviour is to name the document, point you to the board's own site, and work from the copy you download there. If a provider's main selling point is a private library of board material, that is a question to ask rather than a benefit to accept. Working from official sources also guarantees you have the current version.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with a piece of assessed schoolwork?
faqs.answer: Teach the underlying skill, explain what the assessment criteria reward, look at a draft your child has written, and give feedback your child then acts on. What a tutor must not do is write, redraft or complete the work. One provider in this market sells completed IB Internal Assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger for the student and a straightforward reason to ask any prospective tutor how they handle drafts before booking. A tutor who answers that question clearly and without hedging is usually the one worth hiring.

faqs.question: Which subjects around the Marina are hardest to find a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Arabic as a first language to 0508 standard, Computer Science 0478 theory rather than programming, Extended Chemistry at the electrolysis and mole-calculation end, and English Literature where the school has chosen less commonly taught set texts. Inside a short drive of a Marina tower there may be nobody who covers one of those and is free at 5pm on a weekday. Across the UAE and our wider panel there usually is. Where the honest answer is a weekend slot or a longer wait, we say that before anything is booked rather than filling the hour with a willing generalist.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education really compulsory if my child is on a British curriculum?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited. Language of instruction is set too: Standard Arabic for Islamic Education for Arab pupils and Arabic first language, and the school's curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 11 student in the Marina start with?
faqs.answer: One, in one subject, for most students. Two subjects at once is reasonable where both are genuinely weak and the household can protect two slots. Three is almost always a mistake in Year 11 because the homework attached to each session stops being done and the sessions become a substitute for independent work rather than a prompt for it. The better lever is specificity: one hour aimed at a three-topic list drawn from a marked mock paper does more than three hours of general revision. Review it after the next mock and change the list, not the number of hours.

faqs.question: The first IGCSE tutor was not right for my daughter. What then?
faqs.answer: Say so and a different one is arranged. The free trial exists precisely so that this decision gets made in week one rather than in week eight, and a written note of what the trial found travels to the next tutor so your child does not repeat the diagnostic. Mismatches are usually about pace and manner rather than subject knowledge; a child who needs to be asked questions does badly with a tutor who prefers to explain, and that is visible within an hour. It is a normal part of the process, not a complaint.

faqs.question: Do I need to be in the room while the lesson is happening?
faqs.answer: No, and most Marina parents are not. What you should get instead is a note after each session saying what was covered, what was set, and what the tutor thinks the next priority is. That is more useful than overhearing an hour, because it is written in terms you can act on. Younger students sometimes benefit from a parent settling them for the first few minutes, and a shared living space in a Marina apartment works fine with headphones. Ask for the session note as a standing arrangement rather than requesting it each time.
