intro.heading: The real constraint is the bus, not the tutor
paragraphs: Dubai Media City sits in Al Sufouh, a free zone of offices and studios between Sheikh Zayed Road and the sea, with Dubai Internet City inland and Dubai Knowledge Park along the tram line. It has residential towers and no school. Every secondary-age child living here travels out in the morning, most commonly to the Al Barsha cluster, to Emirates Hills and the villa belt, or along the coast. The journey home is the thing that decides when tutoring can happen, and it is almost never discussed before a slot is booked.

Most British-curriculum secondary schools in Dubai finish in the middle of the afternoon, and the roads immediately around the larger gates stall for the best part of an hour afterwards. Add a bus route that collects several communities and a Year 10 or Year 11 student living in a Media City tower is realistically through the door somewhere between four and five o'clock, later if there is an after-school activity. That child then has school homework, which on a British secondary timetable in an examination year is not trivial.

Which means a tutoring slot has to fit into a narrow window and survive it for a whole term. A 4pm booking looks efficient on paper and gets missed one week in three. A 7pm booking with a fed, changed student who has already done thirty minutes of homework holds for fifteen weeks. The difference between those two decisions is worth more than the difference between a mid-tier and a premium tutor, and it costs nothing.

The UK curriculum is the largest in this city, with KHDA's 2024-25 figures showing 37 per cent of private school enrolment on it, against 26 per cent Indian, 14 per cent American and 7 per cent International Baccalaureate, across 387,441 students in 227 schools. So there is no shortage of people who can teach IGCSE content around here. The shortage is of slots that work, matched to the right board, held consistently. This page is about both.

On delivery, the position is simple. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm on school nights. Nobody has to add a drive to the end of your child's commute, which is precisely what makes the later slots available in the first place.

There is a second reason to start with the timetable rather than the tutor. Progress in an examination year comes from a sequence: a paper attempted, marked against the official scheme, logged, and then attacked again a fortnight later. A sequence with a hole in it every third week is not a sequence, it is a series of unconnected hours, and the student ends the term having been taught plenty and having changed nothing. Protecting one hour properly is therefore an academic decision rather than an administrative one, which is why it occupies the first half of this page.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0500 First Language English, with several subjects tiered into Core and Extended. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June with November as the resit route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the correct zone timetable is essential.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics Specification A, 4PH1 Physics and 4BI1 Biology, with Mathematics Specification A tiered into Foundation and Higher. Practical skills in the sciences are assessed through the written papers, so experiment description and data handling have to be drilled inside paper practice rather than at a bench.

June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so work from the live official version.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · MYP 4 and MYP 5 at this age
programmes.description: The non-examined alternative at IB continuum schools. Eight subject groups, four criteria each marked out of eight, grade accumulated from coursework across the year. A student here needs criterion literacy rather than past-paper technique, which is a different tutoring job and a different kind of specialist.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai IB schools run the MYP for all five years and others stop at 14 and enter students for IGCSE anyway, so neighbours in the same tower can be on different tracks. The school's examinations officer can confirm which, and it is worth confirming before buying anything, because the wrong assumption wastes a term.

programmes.name: What follows: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide sixth-form entry. A Level courses usually ask for a grade 6 or B in the subject, and Higher Level IB choices rest on the same evidence. Mathematics is the pinch point: a student who sat Core or Foundation has a visible algebra gap before either route, and Year 11 is the cheap time to close it.
programmes.countryNote: Both routes exist within a short bus ride of Media City, with GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh offering British and IB Diploma pathways and Dubai College running the British route. Because the decision is usually made late in Year 11, a tier decision taken quietly in Year 10 has already narrowed it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-media.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects families in this corridor actually ask for, with codes and the specific places marks disappear in an examination year.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Most losses are method marks on multi-step questions where working was not written down, plus misread command words. Extended and Higher carry the algebraic manipulation, trigonometry and functions that the lower tiers omit. A timed paper every week, marked line by line, moves this faster than reteaching topics does.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are the usual complaints; unit handling and equation rearrangement under time pressure are the actual problems. Graph questions want a gradient with the triangle shown and units stated, and students routinely leave both implicit. Explanation questions reward reasoning written out, not reasoning held in the head.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and qualitative analysis. Students memorise reactions and then stall on an unfamiliar substance. The fix is pattern work from the periodic table and deliberate practice on multi-step mole problems where the limiting reagent is not signposted.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy content tested through exact command terms. Writing everything known about a process scores below answering the question asked. Data interpretation and experiment-description questions are the cheapest marks in the paper and the ones most students never practise on purpose.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: All three sciences in a compressed award, which students expect to be easier and find denser per mark. Support works best as triage across the three, targeting whichever discipline is dragging the overall grade rather than splitting the hour evenly between them.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. Capable writers lose marks by ignoring the audience and purpose instructions and by overrunning the first task. The work is reading the question properly and planning to a fixed structure that can be executed inside the time allowance.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Exercise-by-exercise technique: locating specific information, note-taking and summary writing to a word limit. Fluent speakers often underperform because the paper tests reading precision rather than conversation. Progress is usually fast once the exercise types are practised separately.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Definitions, diagram accuracy and applied response to the stimulus. The common loss is answering from general knowledge instead of the case material. Marks come from naming the concept, applying it to the given situation and judging where the command word asks for judgement.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and theory for Computer Science; practical application skills for ICT. Students who code confidently still drop marks on the required pseudocode style, which is mechanical and responds quickly to short repeated practice.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: School-set streams alongside the licensed curriculum
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever the curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Support reinforces the school's own material rather than importing another syllabus.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source handling and named case studies. History candidates describe sources instead of using them as evidence; Geography candidates omit the named example that the mark scheme wants. Both are structural, and both improve once the student knows what each command word is asking for.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor near me search means from this address
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Media City, in practical terms, means one-to-one teaching for a Year 10 or Year 11 student on a named board, in a slot that fits after the school bus gets back to Al Sufouh, delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time. There is no school in the free zone, so there is no local staff room to draw on, and the nearest tuition centres are a cluster inland in Al Barsha.

Most families searching this phrase are not short of options. The UK curriculum is the biggest in Dubai, so plenty of nearby adults can teach the content. What they are short of is a workable hour. The evening in a Media City household with a Year 11 student contains a commute, homework set by a school that is also preparing for the same examinations, a sport or a music commitment, and often a younger sibling on a different schedule.

That is why this page is organised around the school run rather than around teaching philosophy. Get the hour right and an average tutor produces results. Get the hour wrong and the best tutor in the emirate produces a cancellation pattern. Families consistently underestimate this, partly because tutoring is sold on the tutor and partly because nobody asks what time the bus gets in before proposing a slot.

Removing travel is what makes the right hour available. A tutor who has to reach Al Sufouh by six is choosing between your household and the traffic; a tutor teaching over live video is simply there at six. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and for this corridor that constraint is the thing that makes the schedule work rather than a limitation on it.

sections.heading: The Media City school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Here is the afternoon as it actually runs. Most British-curriculum secondary schools in Dubai finish in the middle of the afternoon. The roads immediately around the larger gates in Al Barsha and the villa belt stall for roughly an hour afterwards, and a bus serving several communities adds collection stops. A student from a Media City tower on an Al Barsha route is usually home between four and five; one on an Emirates Hills or Jebel Ali route is often later.

Then the evening has to absorb four things: changing and eating, school homework, any activity, and the tutoring hour. In an examination year the homework is not optional and not short, and a student who does tutoring before homework will do homework badly at nine o'clock. The sequence that works is arrival, food, a short burst of homework, then the session, then the rest.

The table below sets out the pattern by school cluster so you can find your own household in it. Finish times vary by school and by year group and change between terms, so treat the columns as the shape of the afternoon and confirm the detail with your school. What does not vary is the conclusion: in this corridor, 6pm and 7pm are the slots that survive, and 4pm is the slot that gets rescheduled.

One further point for households with more than one child. Two siblings on different bus routes produce two different arrival times and often two different sports schedules, and the temptation is to book back-to-back sessions to contain the disruption. That works if the second child is the one who arrives later. Booked the other way round, it reliably collapses by week four.

sections.heading: Building a Year 11 week the household can actually keep
paragraphs: A Year 11 week has more fixed content than most families realise, and tutoring has to be fitted around it rather than declared into it. School homework, at least one activity, a mock or assessment most weeks in the spring, and a weekend that has to contain both rest and revision. Planning the tutoring hour without writing that week down is how families end up rescheduling every fortnight.

The template below is the one that works most often in this corridor: one tutored hour, two protected independent study blocks, one timed paper done at home, and a weekend that is deliberately not full. The point of the independent blocks is that tutoring does not create progress on its own. The student has to attempt things alone and get them wrong somewhere other than in the lesson, or the lesson becomes a performance.

Notice what is not in the template. There is no second tutored subject unless a second subject is genuinely failing, no daily revision schedule that will be abandoned by week three, and no study on the evening of the activity. Plans fail by being too full, and a plan that fails in February is worse than a modest plan that survives to June, because the student concludes that planning does not work.

Use the template as a starting shape and cut it rather than add to it. The households that get the most out of a term are the ones that protect one hour of tutoring, two hours of independent work and one timed paper, and leave the rest of the week alone.

sections.heading: Ramadan, mock weeks and the parts of the year that break the schedule
paragraphs: Three things reliably disrupt a tutoring plan in a Dubai school year, and all three are predictable. Ramadan shortens the school day and moves the productive study window to the evening. Mock weeks displace normal teaching and set homework aside, which feels like relief and usually costs a fortnight of momentum. Residential trips and national holidays remove individual weeks without warning.

Ramadan is the easiest to handle well and the most often handled badly. Families who pause for the month lose four weeks from a term that frequently contains coursework deadlines and mock preparation. Families who shift sessions later keep continuity at almost no cost, and because lessons are delivered over live video there is no travel to rearrange around the shorter day or around iftar timing. Deciding in advance is what matters; drifting through the month is what costs the term.

Mock weeks are worth planning for differently. The useful move is to treat the mock itself as the week's timed paper, then spend the following session marking it properly against the official scheme rather than discussing how it felt. Most students come out of mocks with a strong opinion about a paper and no idea which marks they actually lost, and the gap between those two things is where the next eight weeks of work should come from.

Trips and holidays are absorbed by recording lessons and by writing the plan down. A written plan means a missed week can be caught by the student alone; an undocumented plan means a missed week becomes a lost month because nobody remembers what the target was. That is unglamorous administration and it is the difference between a term that produces a grade change and one that produces a feeling of having tried.

sections.heading: What a weekly slot costs, and what adding a car would add
paragraphs: The published market makes the comparison easy. Qualified subject tutors working online in Dubai are quoted from AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget online tutoring runs from AED 45 to AED 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Specialists in IB, IGCSE and A Level run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

In-home one-to-one visits are published between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's band at AED 180 to AED 350. Read against the online figures, the premium is the car. For a Media City household that premium buys something actively unhelpful: it ties the lesson to a tutor's drive through Al Sufouh at exactly the hour the roads are worst, which is the thing you were trying to avoid by booking late in the first place.

Monthly packages tell the same story more bluntly. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. For weekly paper practice, eight contacts is a better structure than four, and the four-visit package costs roughly double. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Those are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram prices, and they are the sort of thing worth checking before you accept any quote. What a parent can verify is short: the rate, whether it is per hour or per lesson, whether travel is inside the number, the cancellation terms, and the remedy if the match is wrong. Three of the six strongest-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no rate at all, which is why this table exists.

sections.heading: Entries, series and the deadline the school handles quietly
paragraphs: Families plan tutoring around the examination and forget the entry. Final entries and tier confirmations are submitted months before the papers, by the school, usually without much announcement. By the time a parent decides in March that a tier was wrong, the entry has long been made, which is why the useful conversation about tier happens in Year 10.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to a Dubai candidate. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states in its exams officers' guide that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any page restating future dates should be treated with caution and the live official timetable used instead.

The practical reading for a Media City family is about when to buy. If a grade matters for a sixth-form place, the June series is the target and the work has to begin in the autumn, because a March start gives eight or nine usable weeks. November is the recovery route, with Pearson results arriving in January. Deciding on a November entry in August is calm; deciding in October is not.

sections.heading: Not making the week worse: homework, deadlines and what a tutor should leave alone
paragraphs: There is a failure mode in which tutoring makes a Year 11 student worse off. It happens when the tutor sets their own homework on top of the school's, teaches a method that contradicts the one the class uses, and schedules extra sessions in the week of a mock. The student ends up busier, more confused and no closer to a grade, and the family concludes that their child cannot be helped.

The avoidable version is simple. The tutor works from the school's own scheme of work, uses the school's notation and method where there is a choice, and sets at most one piece of work a week, usually a timed paper that replaces rather than adds to the student's own revision. Where the school's method is genuinely weaker, the tutor teaches both and says which one to use in the examination, rather than quietly overwriting what the class teacher said.

Deadlines belong to the school, and a tutor should know them without owning them. Mock dates, coursework submission dates where a subject has them, and the school's internal assessment calendar all shape what the next four sessions should do. A tutor who has never asked for those dates is working blind, and a parent can test this in one question on the first call.

The final piece is restraint. The right number of tutored subjects is the number that are actually failing, which is usually one. A parent buying three subjects in February is often buying reassurance, and the hours come out of the student's own study time, which is where most of the improvement actually has to happen. Saying that out loud costs us revenue and is still the correct advice.

sections.heading: When the slot you need is not available
paragraphs: The late slots are the contested ones. Between 6pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time, on a weekday, in a popular subject, in the spring, is the single hardest booking in the UAE market, because every family in this corridor has worked out the same thing about the school run. Being honest about that is more useful than pretending otherwise.

If no suitable specialist is free in the slot you want, you are told so, with the earliest realistic alternative, rather than matched to whoever is available at the wrong level. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a subject, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and that is stated before you book. Two providers ranking for Dubai searches route parents to numbers in another country without saying so; the delivery works, and concealing it does not.

There are two practical workarounds. The first is the weekend double, which frees the contested weekday evening entirely and suits households with heavy activity schedules. The second is booking in September for a slot you will need in February, which sounds excessive and is simply how the market works. Families who start in the autumn get the hour they want; families who start in March take what is left.

If a match turns out wrong after the first paid session, you are matched again. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and in a market where one provider sells completed coursework outright, a provider that offers a re-match instead of a promise is making the only commitment that can actually be tested.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start if my child buses to Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Plan for 6pm. Most British-curriculum secondary schools in Dubai finish in the middle of the afternoon, the roads around the larger Al Barsha gates stall for roughly an hour afterwards, and a bus serving several communities adds collection stops. A student from a Media City tower is usually home between four and five, and then needs to change, eat and make a start on school homework. A 4pm booking looks efficient and gets rescheduled; a 6pm booking holds for fifteen weeks.

faqs.question: Should tutoring come before or after school homework?
faqs.answer: After a short burst of it, not before. In an examination year the school's own homework is substantial and not optional, and a student who does the tutored hour first ends up attempting homework badly at nine o'clock. The sequence that works in this corridor is arrival, food, thirty minutes of homework to clear the urgent part, then the session, then whatever is left. It sounds minor and it is the difference between a term that runs and a term that unravels.

faqs.question: We have two children on different bus routes. How do we schedule both?
faqs.answer: Back-to-back sessions work, but only in the right order: the child who gets home later takes the later slot. Booked the other way round the arrangement collapses by about week four, because the first session starts while the second child is still in traffic and the household spends the evening managing the overlap. Where weekday evenings cannot absorb two sessions, a weekend double for one child and a weekday hour for the other is usually the cleaner split.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session as good as a weekday one?
faqs.answer: Slightly less effective in theory, considerably better in practice if the weekday evening is genuinely full. Two separated hours beat one two-hour block because the student attempts work alone in between, which is where the real learning happens. But a weekend double that happens every week beats a Tuesday hour that is missed every third week. For households with heavy sport commitments or several children, the weekend block is the honest choice rather than the compromise.

faqs.question: How should we use a mock result rather than just worry about it?
faqs.answer: Treat the mock as the week's timed paper and spend the next session marking it against the official scheme with the tutor, question by question. Most students come out of mocks with a firm opinion about the paper and no idea which marks they actually lost, and the difference between those two things is the syllabus for the next eight weeks. An error log built from a marked mock is the most useful revision document a Year 11 student can own.

faqs.question: Does tutoring stop for Ramadan or move?
faqs.answer: It moves, for most families in this corridor. School days shorten and the productive study window shifts to the evening, so the weekly slot moves later rather than being suspended. Because lessons are delivered over live video, there is no travel to rearrange around the shorter day or around iftar timing. The decision matters because a four-week pause in a term that contains coursework deadlines and mock preparation is expensive, and drifting through the month without deciding is the costliest option.

faqs.question: How much of the week should be tutoring and how much independent study?
faqs.answer: One tutored hour, two independent blocks of about 45 minutes, and one timed paper done alone is the shape that works in a Year 11 week here. Tutoring does not create progress by itself: the student has to attempt things alone, get them wrong somewhere other than the lesson, and bring the evidence back. Plans fail by being too full, and a plan that collapses in February teaches a student that planning does not work, which is worse than no plan.

faqs.question: Can a tutor set extra homework on top of what the school gives?
faqs.answer: One piece a week at most, and ideally it replaces rather than adds. The usual sensible choice is a timed paper that takes the place of the student's own unstructured revision. Tutoring that adds load without removing any is how a Year 11 term goes backwards: the student becomes busier, more confused if the tutor's method contradicts the class method, and no nearer a grade. A tutor should use the school's notation where a choice exists, and say so if a method differs.

faqs.question: Which slot is hardest to book in Dubai, and when should I ask for it?
faqs.answer: A weekday evening between 6pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time in a popular subject in the spring is the hardest booking in this market, because every family in the corridor has worked out the same thing about the school run. Ask in September for the hour you will want in February. Families who book in the autumn get their preferred slot; families who start in March take what is left, which is often an awkward hour or a weekend block.

faqs.question: Would an in-home tutor solve the timetable problem instead?
faqs.answer: It usually makes it worse. An in-home arrangement ties the lesson to a tutor's drive through Al Sufouh at the hour the roads are at their worst, which is exactly the constraint a later slot was meant to avoid, and it costs more: published in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should we tutor in an examination year?
faqs.answer: Usually one, occasionally two, rarely more. Buying three or four in the spring is generally buying reassurance, and those hours come out of the student's own study time, which is where most of the improvement actually has to happen. If three subjects are genuinely failing, the problem is more likely to be the week, the sleep or the tier than the teaching, and a timetable conversation will do more than three tutors. Reassess from marked work after four sessions.

faqs.question: When do schools submit IGCSE entries, and can a tier still change?
faqs.answer: Final entries and tier confirmations go in months before the papers, submitted by the school, usually without an announcement. That is why a tier conversation in Year 10 is useful and the same conversation in March of Year 11 mostly is not. If you want a tier reviewed, bring evidence rather than an opinion: one lower-tier paper and one higher-tier paper from the same series, both sat to time, settles the argument faster than any discussion of potential.

faqs.question: Which exam series does a Dubai Media City candidate actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always check the live official timetable through the school.

faqs.question: What does the first session actually involve if we have no marked work to hand?
faqs.answer: A question or two from your child's own syllabus, attempted live, with the tutor watching how they set out the work rather than only whether the answer is right. That reveals more than a marked paper in many cases, because most lost marks come from unwritten working, misread command words and abandoned multi-step questions. You get a written note afterwards naming the largest single loss and what the first four sessions would target, before anything is paid.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is good but the hour never works?
faqs.answer: Change the hour before you change the tutor, and change it once rather than renegotiating weekly. A slot that has been missed twice in four weeks is not going to settle, and the usual fix is moving half an hour later or moving to a weekend block. If after that the arrangement still does not hold, the honest conclusion is about the week rather than the teaching, and a frank conversation about what else is in the evening is more useful than a new match.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-media.closingHeading: Fix the hour, then book the tutor
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-media.closingBody: If you are searching for an IGCSE tutor near me from Dubai Media City, start with the afternoon rather than the shortlist. That hour is usually 6pm or later in this corridor, and it is bookable precisely because nobody has to drive to it. Then confirm the board and syllabus code with the school, take a free trial lesson on a real question, and judge the arrangement at session four on a timed paper marked against the official scheme.

intro.heading: The report card arrives in a particular week, and the week decides the plan
paragraphs: Dubai Production City has no secondary school inside it. Students bus out to Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Jebel Ali, and most of them are on the standard Dubai academic year: late August or early September to late June or early July, in three terms with a long winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break in the second half of the year. That calendar, far more than the neighbourhood, determines what a tutor should be doing with a student in any given month.

Search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Production City and the results are ranked by distance. What they cannot tell you is whether now is the right moment to start, what the next eight to twelve weeks should achieve, or whether the problem your child has is one that a particular term can fix. A family arriving in October has the whole of Year 11 available. A family arriving after the spring break has weeks, and the right plan is narrower and more selective.

We write plans to that structure. First term of Year 10 is foundation work: tiering decisions, study habits, and closing the gaps that followed a student up from Year 9. Second and third terms of Year 10 are content consolidation while it is still being taught, which is the cheapest marks available in the whole qualification. First term of Year 11 is mock preparation. Second term is paper technique and entry confirmation. Third term, where it exists before the series, is pure past-paper volume.

Two local factors change the shape of that. Ramadan moves earlier by roughly eleven days each Gregorian year, so the weeks it overlaps with mock season shift annually, bringing shortened school days and post-Iftar study with them. And the Production City bus day is long, which compresses weekday evenings and makes long single sessions a poor investment compared with shorter, more frequent ones. Both get planned in rather than discovered.

One more thing a distance-sorted search cannot show you. The two IGCSE boards running in Dubai schools set different papers, different tiers and different grading scales, and in a school entering candidates with both, the pattern differs subject by subject. A term plan written without that information is a term plan written for the wrong exam, so the first thing we ask any Production City family for is the board and the syllabus code, straight from the exams officer, in writing.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. Everything on this page was reviewed in October 2026, and where an exam timetable is involved, read the board's own live PDF rather than any restatement, including ours. Where we quote a date it is a past one, because a past date is checkable and a future one eventually stops being true without anybody editing the page.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-produ.programmesIntro: Three routes cover almost every enquiry from this cluster, and the differences between the two IGCSE boards change what a term's work should look like. Get the board and tier in writing from the exams officer before any plan is written.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Mostly tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. Syllabus codes are worth knowing: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Assessment is linear and sat at the end of the course, with practical or alternative-to-practical routes in the sciences decided by the school.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your Production City child's exams officer which zone the school sits in, in writing, before planning a single revision week.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Uses 4-prefix codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4EA1 English Language, graded 9-1. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher; the International GCSE sciences are untiered. Some subjects are available in a modular pattern, which spreads assessment across sessions rather than concentrating it in one terminal run.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables for sessions a year ahead and revises them, so the live official PDF is the only version to plan a term against. January results matter locally too: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is what makes the second half of the winter term a decision point for Dubai families.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Most Dubai British-curriculum schools move students into AS and A Level at sixteen, with subject-specific IGCSE grade requirements for entry. Mathematics and the sciences typically need a grade 6 or B. The step in abstraction from IGCSE Extended to AS is steeper than anything a student has met, particularly in Mathematics where early calculus arrives immediately.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Verify on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-produ.subjectsIntro: Eight subjects, with the term in which work on each usually pays best. The pattern is that content-heavy subjects reward early consolidation and technique-led subjects respond late, which is the single most useful planning fact at this level.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1. Responds quickly at any point in the year because a large share of lost marks are method marks the student earned mentally and never wrote down. Bounds, algebraic manipulation and vectors are the recurring content gaps.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1. Best worked on in the second and third terms of Year 10, while electricity and moments are being taught. Late work on Physics is possible but selective, and should target two topics rather than the syllabus.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1. Moles and stoichiometry are the gate: a student who cannot do mole calculations reliably will lose marks across every paper. Fix that early, because everything downstream assumes it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cambridge 0610 or Pearson 4BI1. The highest content volume of the three sciences, so it rewards steady work across both years and punishes a late sprint. Transport in plants, homeostasis and genetics are the usual trouble spots.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Cambridge 0500 and 0510, or Pearson 4EA1. The fastest-moving subject in a short block, because directed writing and the summary task are governed by a structure a student can learn once and apply in every paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Additional
subjects.description: Cambridge 0606. Taken by a small, strong cohort as a bridge to AS Level, covering early calculus, trigonometric identities and series. The best preparation available at sixteen for A Level Mathematics, and the subject where local specialist tutors are genuinely scarce.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0455 or Pearson 4EC1. Diagram accuracy decides the grade, and data response questions need figures quoted from the extract rather than paraphrased. Both are technique rather than content, so late work is effective here.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Cambridge 0450 or Pearson 4BS1. Students reliably reach the analysis band and stop short of the evaluation band, which is where the top marks sit. Teaching a justified judgement is a few sessions of work and it transfers to every extended answer.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Cambridge 0508 or 0544. For Dubai students this runs alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic requirement, which is a different syllabus from the examined IGCSE. Families here often need support on both streams in the same term.

sections.heading: The Dubai school year, term by term, for a Year 10 and Year 11 student
paragraphs: The standard Dubai academic year opens in late August or early September and closes in late June or early July, split into three terms with a long winter break and a spring break. Within that, a British-curriculum student's two IGCSE years have a predictable rhythm, and it is a rhythm that most tutoring arrangements ignore entirely in favour of a flat weekly hour that means the same thing in October as in April.

First term of Year 10 is the only moment when tiering is genuinely open. Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: that decision should be made on evidence from timed work rather than on optimism or anxiety, and a student who is moved to Extended in the second term of Year 11 has a very hard year. Work in this term should be diagnostic and habit-forming rather than exam-focused.

The middle of the two-year course, from the second term of Year 10 to the first term of Year 11, is where the cheapest marks live. Consolidating a topic in the fortnight after the school teaches it takes a fraction of the time it takes to reconstruct it eighteen months later. Almost no family starts here, which is why almost every family pays more than they needed to.

The last two terms are technique. Mocks arrive in the first or second term of Year 11 depending on the school, and they are the first honest signal of where a student actually is. Everything after that should be chosen from the mock script rather than from a syllabus checklist.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the weeks a plan actually loses
paragraphs: Any plan written across a Dubai school year has to survive Ramadan, and the complication is that Ramadan moves. It shifts earlier by roughly eleven days each Gregorian year, which means the school weeks it overlaps with change annually. A plan copied from a previous year's calendar will be wrong about which term is affected, and that is not a small error when it lands on a mock window.

During Ramadan, school hours in Dubai are shortened and family routines move substantially later. Study happens after Iftar for many households, which is workable and in some ways better: a student studying at nine in the evening with the household awake around them is more focused than one studying at five while fasting. Sessions move to post-Iftar slots as a normal request, and the slot is held rather than quietly dropped.

The other calendar losses are more predictable and more often mishandled. The long winter break tempts families into booking a full intensive programme, which usually produces a tired January. One or two targeted sessions on a single weak topic achieves more. The spring break typically sits uncomfortably close to the series, and the right use of it is timed paper work rather than new content.

The practical step is to put the dates on the table at the first conversation. Your school's term dates, your travel plans, and the Ramadan window for the year ahead. A plan built around those is a plan that still exists in week nine, which is more than can be said for most weekly arrangements.

sections.heading: What the distance-sorted search result cannot tell you
paragraphs: A near-me search ranks by proximity and then by whoever has invested most in local listings. Neither signal correlates with the thing you need, which is a tutor who teaches your child's board at your child's tier and is free in a slot your child is actually awake for. In Production City, where no secondary campus sits inside the community, those three conditions rarely coincide in the same person locally.

The structural reason is simple. IGCSE teachers cluster at the campuses that teach IGCSE, in Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha and Jebel Ali. A teacher finishing at four in Al Barsha does not reach IMPZ before five, and between five and seven the drive is closer to forty minutes. The Dubai travel premium of roughly AED 50-150 an hour, visible in the difference between published online and in-home bands, is that journey priced into your invoice.

It gets worse for the specific requirements that matter. Additional Mathematics 0606, a Pearson modular entry pattern, Arabic as a first language: these have small cohorts in any one community, so the number of local specialists is small, and the number free at half past five on a Tuesday in the mock term is smaller still. Online, the only filter left is subject and board knowledge.

We are explicit about this rather than coy, because IB Gram does not offer UAE home visits at all. Independent home tutors operate here and for a younger child needing physical supervision they can be the right choice. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student working to a term plan, what you want protected is the hours, and the journey is what spends them.

sections.heading: Mock results read at component level
paragraphs: A mock grade is almost useless on its own. A mock script is the most valuable document a Year 11 family will see all year. The grade tells you there is a problem; the script tells you which of three completely different problems it is, and the three need completely different plans.

The first is content: whole topics the student cannot attempt. These show as blank or abandoned questions clustered in particular areas, and they need teaching, in a fixed order, starting with whatever the other topics depend on. In Chemistry that is almost always moles. In Mathematics it is usually algebraic manipulation.

The second is technique: questions attempted and marked low despite the student knowing the material. These show as answers that describe when the command term said explain, or that stop at analysis when the band needed a judgement. This is the fastest thing to fix, often within a handful of sessions, and it is where most of the recoverable marks in a mock script sit.

The third is pacing: a script that is strong at the start and thin at the end, or whole final questions untouched. That is a timing problem and it is solved by practising question allocation by mark value, not by learning more content. Ask the school for the component breakdown, bring it to the first session, and let it choose the plan rather than deciding in advance. Schools provide component marks on request and are usually glad to be asked, because it is the conversation they would rather have than one about grades.

sections.heading: What a term of tuition costs in Dubai, and when the spend works hardest
paragraphs: Think in terms rather than hours. A term is roughly twelve weeks, so one weekly session is twelve hours and a twice-weekly mock-term pattern is twenty-four. At the Dubai market band for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor online, roughly AED 150-300 an hour, a single term at one session a week is AED 1,800 to AED 3,600. The twice-weekly mock term runs double that.

The return on that spend is not constant through the year, which is the part no package page tells you. Twelve hours spent in the second term of Year 10 consolidating content as it is taught recovers more marks than twenty-four hours spent in the final weeks of Year 11 trying to reconstruct the same material. The same money does different amounts of work depending on when it is spent.

The Dubai market bands, read in October 2026: budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270; premium or examiner-led at AED 500-650 or more, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages seen include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Worth adding as context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. These are market figures and not IB Gram prices. We start with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many hours the goal actually needs.

sections.heading: Boards, codes and the email to send this week
paragraphs: A term plan written without knowing the board is a term plan written for the wrong exam. In a Dubai school running both Cambridge and Pearson, entries genuinely differ by subject, which is why a report card can show 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades with nothing wrong. Parents routinely do not know, and nobody tells them unless they ask.

The differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics is tiered Core and Extended with Core capped at grade C; Pearson 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher on a 9-1 scale. Cambridge sciences offer a practical paper or an alternative-to-practical route and the school chooses; Pearson International GCSE sciences are untiered. Pearson offers some subjects modularly, which changes the shape of a revision term entirely.

So send one email to the exams officer and ask for four things per subject: the board, the syllabus code, the tier, and the series the student is entered for. Ask also which Cambridge administrative zone the school sits in, because Cambridge states that using the correct zone timetable is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one.

Bring that list to the first tutoring conversation. We match on board and tier as well as subject, and the reason is practical: a student revising from the wrong board's past papers is practising for an exam nobody is sitting, and that is a term lost rather than a session lost.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the honesty boundary
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspections published on a six-band scale. Those reports are public and free, and the single most useful document available to a family considering a school move at the end of Year 9.

Individual tutors need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services system, and u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

On the academic side, the boundary is the same at IGCSE as at Diploma level. A tutor teaches the skills an assessment examines, explains what the criteria reward, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete assessed work. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material; we reference and link the official source.

IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and has no UAE office. Ask any provider describing itself as approved which permit it means, because the phrase is used loosely in this market and the precise answer is informative.

sections.heading: Starting this term rather than next
paragraphs: The sequence is short and the first step is the one families skip. Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier, the next assessment date and, if there is one, a recent marked script. Those five things let us match a specialist precisely and write a plan that fits where you are in the year rather than a generic programme.

Then take the free trial lesson, which is a real teaching hour on the current sticking point rather than a consultation. Afterwards you get a short written note on what the tutor found. No card is held, nothing renews, and if the match is wrong we rematch once at no charge. For Production City households the slot usually lands at 5:30pm or later on weekdays, and weekend mornings work well for anything demanding.

On availability we give dates rather than substitutes. In the four weeks around mocks, early evening slots go first, and some subjects are thin year-round: Additional Mathematics, Arabic as a first language, and board-specific modular entries. If the specialist is a week away we say the date. If they are based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say that before you book.

What we will not do, in Production City or anywhere else in the UAE, is send a tutor to your address. Home visiting is an India-only service for us. For a plan that has to survive a full term, the online format is what keeps the sessions happening when the bus is late, the road is closed or the family is away for half-term.

faqs.question: When in the Dubai school year should we actually start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: The second term of Year 10, if the choice is free. Consolidating a topic in the fortnight after the school teaches it takes a fraction of the hours needed to reconstruct it eighteen months later, so the same money recovers more marks. Almost no family starts there, because nothing feels urgent yet. The next best moment is the first term of Year 11, before mocks, when there is still time to repair content as well as technique. Starting after the spring break is possible but the plan has to be narrow and selective rather than comprehensive.

faqs.question: How do we keep a tutoring plan running through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Move the sessions after Iftar and agree it in advance. School hours shorten and household routines move later, so a nine o'clock session with the family awake is usually more productive than a five o'clock one while fasting. The planning trap is that Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so the school weeks it overlaps with change, and a schedule copied from last year will be wrong about which term is affected. We hold the slot rather than dropping it, and we put the window into the plan at the first conversation.

faqs.question: Why does a near-me search not find the right IGCSE tutor here?
faqs.answer: Because it ranks by distance and local listing spend, and neither predicts whether somebody teaches your child's board at your child's tier in a slot your child is awake for. Dubai Production City has no secondary campus inside it, so IGCSE teachers cluster at the campuses in Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha and Jebel Ali. One finishing at four in Al Barsha does not reach IMPZ before five, and the published travel premium of roughly AED 50-150 an hour is that journey priced into your invoice.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school's exams officer, and when?
faqs.answer: This week, in one email, for four things per subject: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series your child is entered for. Also ask which Cambridge administrative zone the school sits in, because Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct zone timetable and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. In a school running both boards, entries differ by subject, which is why a report card can carry 9-1 grades beside A*-G grades without any error in it.

faqs.question: Our child's mock grade was a 4. What do we do with that?
faqs.answer: Ask for the component marks, because the grade alone cannot tell you which of three problems you have. Blank or abandoned questions mean content gaps and need teaching in dependency order. Attempted questions marked low usually mean command-term misreads, which is the fastest thing to fix and where most recoverable marks sit. A script that thins towards the end is a pacing problem solved by allocating time against mark value. Those three need different plans and different numbers of hours, and only the script distinguishes them.

faqs.question: Is a winter-break intensive programme worth booking?
faqs.answer: Usually not as a full programme. Families book ten to twenty hours across the long break with good intentions and produce a tired January, which costs more than it gains in a term where mocks are often close. One or two targeted sessions on a single weak topic, with real rest around them, achieves more. The spring break is different: by then content teaching has limited returns and timed paper work has high ones, so a short burst of papers over that break is usually a sound use of the time.

faqs.question: What does one term of weekly tuition cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A Dubai term is roughly twelve weeks, so one weekly session is twelve hours. At the market band for a qualified IGCSE subject tutor online, roughly AED 150-300 an hour, that is AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 for the term. A twice-weekly mock-term pattern doubles it. Specialists sit higher at AED 200-450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those figures were read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table, and they describe the market rather than our price list, which is why we start with a free trial lesson instead.

faqs.question: Can my child still move from Core to Extended partway through?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it gets harder every term. The tiering decision is genuinely open in the first term of Year 10 and should be made on evidence from timed work rather than on optimism or anxiety. A student moved up in the second term of Year 11 faces a very hard year, because Extended content they never met has to be learned alongside revision of everything else. If a move is being considered, ask the school for a timed Extended paper first and decide from the script, not from classwork.

faqs.question: What time do sessions start for a Year 11 student commuting from IMPZ?
faqs.answer: Realistically 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time or later on weekdays. With no secondary campus inside Dubai Production City, students bus to Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Jebel Ali and are typically home between four and half past, needing food and a break first. Students in Dubai South and Emaar South often need six o'clock or later. Because the lesson is online it starts at the booked minute rather than when somebody arrives, and weekend mornings work well for anything that demands concentration.

faqs.question: Does a Pearson modular entry change how we plan the year?
faqs.answer: Considerably. Where a subject is offered modularly, units can be sat across sessions rather than in a single terminal run, so revision is sequenced unit by unit instead of building to one peak. That suits a student who struggles to hold a whole syllabus in view and disadvantages one who needs a single deadline to work. Pearson publishes provisional timetables a year ahead and revises them, so plan against the live official PDF and confirm the entry pattern with the exams officer before writing any term schedule around it.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject gives the quickest improvement late in the year?
faqs.answer: English Language, usually, because the directed writing and summary tasks are governed by a structure a student can learn once and then apply in every paper. Mathematics is close behind, since a large share of lost marks are method marks the student earned mentally and never wrote down. Economics and Business Studies move on the evaluation band, which most students never reach despite knowing the content. The sciences are slower and should be targeted at two or three specific topics rather than attempted whole.

Independent home tutors do work in this area, with market in-home rates of roughly AED 180-350 an hour, and for a younger child who needs physical supervision they can genuinely be the better choice.

faqs.answer: A tutor will teach the skills the task assesses, explain what the criteria actually reward, question the approach before weeks go into something unworkable, and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor will not write, rewrite or complete any part of it, because the line is authorship and it is not negotiable. We also do not reproduce or distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material. We reference the official source and work from papers the school or student legitimately holds.

faqs.answer: Usually two to four days for mainstream subjects, and we give a date rather than a substitute when it is longer. Early evening slots go first in the four weeks around mocks, and some subjects are thin all year: Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language, and board-specific modular entries. intro.heading: When you start matters more than where the tutor lives
paragraphs: Two families in Silicon Oasis hire the same tutor for the same subject at the same rate. One starts in September of Year 10, the other in March of Year 11. The first spends less in total and ends with a better grade, and the reason has nothing to do with the tutor. Algebraic fluency, precision in written explanation and close reading all take months of repetition, and March does not contain months. September of Year 10 contains eighteen of them.

That is why a search built around proximity solves the wrong problem. A tutor five minutes away who starts in March is worse than one on a video link who starts in September, by a margin that is not close. Distance affects convenience and the reliability of a start time. Timing affects which gaps can be addressed at all, which is a difference of category rather than degree.

There is also a supply argument that cuts the same way. Dubai Silicon Oasis is well served at the budget end of the tutoring market, partly because Academic City's university campuses sit next door, and thinly served for specific board and tier combinations. The published budget band in this emirate runs AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, which is genuinely useful for content revision and genuinely unsuited to Extended-tier structural work.

So the honest version of the near-me question is this. Can you find somebody nearby? Almost certainly, for one subject at a reasonable level. Will proximity be the thing that determines the grade? No. The term you begin in, the board and tier you are matched to, and whether anybody has read a marked paper before buying hours will determine it, and all three are independent of where the tutor sleeps.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis, Cedre Villas, Academic City and the surrounding communities, lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical consequence for a two-year plan is scheduling durability: the same slot can hold through a term, move for a mock week in a single message, and survive a family trip without being lost.

What follows is both years laid out term by term, with what each block can realistically achieve, what the summer between them is worth, how sixth-form applications overlay the autumn of Year 11, and what to do in the ten days after results. Use it to decide when to spend, which is the decision that actually moves the outcome.

None of this makes a nearby tutor a bad choice. For a Year 10 student who will not engage over a screen, somebody in the room is worth the travel premium and the narrower selection that comes with it. The argument is only about which variable to optimise first. Decide the term and the board, then decide the delivery, rather than the other way round, because reversing that order is how families end up with a convenient arrangement aimed at something the calendar will not allow.

programmes.description: Two years to externally marked papers in a June or November series. Cambridge splits many syllabuses into Core and Extended routes with a grade ceiling attached to the lower one; Pearson sets Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics. The tier decision is made during Year 10 on the basis of classwork.

A student whose autumn performance improves gets a better prediction and therefore a better set of options, regardless of what happens in June. Almost no family plans tuition around that fact.

programmes.name: Equivalency and mandatory UAE subjects
programmes.description: Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade.
programmes.countryNote: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies occupy timetable space in every Dubai private school regardless of curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. That is school-day time unavailable for IGCSE content, which is worth factoring in when judging what a term can cover.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-silic.subjectsIntro: This grid is sorted by how early each subject needs to be addressed, because that is the timing question. Subjects at the top of the list cannot be rescued late; those at the bottom genuinely respond to a short block in the final term.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: The slowest subject in the set to move. Quotation selection and close analysis need repeated marked practice across months, so this is the first subject to address in Year 10 and the worst one to leave until spring of Year 11.

subjects.name: Mathematics, algebraic fluency
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, simplifying and rearranging appear in every paper and underpin physics and chemistry calculations too. Built by repetition rather than explanation, which means two terms rather than a block, and it cannot be acquired between March and June.

subjects.name: Biology, written precision
subjects.description: Naming the structure, the process and the consequence is a habit, not a fact, and biology mark schemes award nothing for general sense. Months of marked practice rather than weeks, so Year 10 is the right place for it.

subjects.name: Physics, extended written answers
subjects.description: Six-mark questions want a causal chain that names a mechanism. Students write three restatements of the first sentence instead, which earns one mark. A habit that forms over a term or two, so addressing it in Year 11 spring is already late.

subjects.name: English Language, directed writing
subjects.description: Answering the specified audience and form is a readable rule, so this half of the paper responds inside six to eight weeks. Reading-response depth takes longer, which means a late plan will lift one half of the subject and not the other.

subjects.name: Mathematics, procedural topics
subjects.description: Reverse percentages, similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, cumulative frequency, circle theorems. Finite sets of steps that close in two or three sessions at any point in the year, which makes them the right late purchase.

subjects.name: Chemistry, calculations and analysis tables
subjects.description: Moles calculations and the Cambridge qualitative analysis tables are learnable procedures rather than habits, so chemistry tolerates a late start better than physics or biology do. Four to six focused sessions produce visible movement.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Among the fastest to respond. Data-response technique and stating an explicit judgement in evaluation questions are both teachable rules, so a short block in the final term is a defensible purchase in these subjects.

subjects.name: Computer Science theory
subjects.description: Finite content with repeating question styles, so structured revision inside eight weeks works for most students. Practical coding confidence takes longer and belongs in Year 10, which is a distinction worth making before booking.

subjects.name: Command words and exam technique
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, calculate and compare demand different amounts, and answering the wrong amount costs marks or time. One session with a past paper improves every subject at once, and it works at any point in the two years.

sections.heading: Year 10, term by term
paragraphs: Year 10 is the year with everything to gain and no pressure to act, which is why it passes unused in most households. Autumn term is when the new content starts and when a Key Stage 3 gap becomes visible for the first time against real IGCSE demands. This is the moment to find out whether the student can rearrange a formula, add algebraic fractions and write a four-sentence causal explanation, because all three will be assumed from here on.

Spring term of Year 10 is when the tier decision begins to form. Schools set Core or Extended entries on Cambridge syllabuses, and Foundation or Higher in Pearson mathematics, on the basis of classwork and internal assessment. If there is any ambition towards a sixth-form course with a specific grade requirement, this is the term in which a diagnostic assessment has leverage, because the entry can still be discussed with the school.

Summer term of Year 10 carries end-of-year examinations at most schools, and those papers are the second-best diagnostic in the two years after the Year 11 mocks. They are marked, they are free, and almost nobody reads them properly. Sorting the lost marks by cause at that point sets up the summer and the whole of Year 11, and it takes an hour.

The spend in Year 10 should be modest and specific. One named weakness, addressed weekly for a term, at the qualified band rather than the specialist band. That is a far smaller commitment than the exam-year equivalent, which Bestimate puts at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month for one weekly hour, and it addresses the thing that would otherwise consume the spring of Year 11 without resolving.

sections.heading: Year 11, term by term
paragraphs: Year 11 autumn is the term families underestimate most, because it is the term in which predicted grades are formed. Sixth-form and foundation applications are generally made on predictions, so a student whose autumn performance improves gets a better set of options regardless of what June eventually produces. That is a concrete consequence available in October and almost nobody buys tuition for it.

The mock window, at many schools in late autumn or early in the spring term, is the hinge of the whole year. Mocks are marked by the school at no cost and contain more usable information than any paid assessment. The grade is the least useful part; the distribution of lost marks by cause is the plan for the rest of the year, and reading it properly takes under an hour and no subject expertise.

Spring term is technique. Marked timed papers, command words, working conventions, question selection, and the finite procedural topics that are still closable. This is where the market sells most heavily and where it also over-promises, because a plan that quietly includes building algebraic fluency from scratch cannot succeed and the family will conclude that tutoring does not work.

The final six to eight weeks should taper rather than intensify. Heavier early, lighter late, and the last week on an error tally rather than new material. A student revising at maximum intensity into the papers arrives depleted, and the marginal topic learned in that fortnight is worth less than the alertness it costs. That is unglamorous advice and it is consistently the difference between a predicted grade met and missed.

sections.heading: The summer between, which is the cheapest window
paragraphs: Between the end of Year 10 and the start of Year 11 sits the longest break in the two years, with no school, no homework and no deadline. It is the only block where longer sessions are possible without competing against a school day, and it is also the period of lowest demand in the after-school window across the whole UAE, which makes it the easiest time to secure a good tutor at a good hour.

What it is for is the one weakness Year 10 exposed. Not general revision, not getting ahead on next year's content, and not a broad programme across three subjects. One named thing, four to six sessions, with marked practice between them. A student who arrives in September with formula rearrangement already automatic has changed what the Year 11 autumn block can be used for, which is the whole point.

The second thing it is for is reading the Year 10 end-of-year papers properly. Those papers are marked, free, and almost always filed unread. Sorting the lost marks into causes before the summer sessions begin means the sessions are aimed rather than general, and it also tells you whether the problem is content, technique, or capability, which determines whether four sessions is the right number or four months is.

The reason almost nobody uses this window is psychological rather than financial. In July nothing is failing, there is no report in the house, and the examinations are eleven months away. By the time urgency arrives the window has closed and the same work costs more and achieves less. Writing it down in a page like this one is the only intervention available, since no provider has an incentive to market a quiet July.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, and why autumn of Year 11 is the hinge
paragraphs: Sixth-form places, whether A Level, IB Diploma or BTEC, are generally offered on predicted grades during Year 11. Those predictions are formed from classwork, internal assessments and the mock papers, which means they are largely settled before the spring term even begins. A family focused entirely on June is optimising for the wrong date, because the doors open or close on the prediction months earlier.

This produces a specific and under-exploited opportunity. A student who improves measurably in the autumn of Year 11 gets a better prediction, a better set of offers and more room to negotiate, and the improvement needed is often technique rather than knowledge. Command-word reading, working layout and timing all move quickly, and they move the internal assessment marks that feed the prediction.

It also produces a risk worth naming. A student whose autumn is weak receives a low prediction, applies accordingly, and then outperforms it in June with no obvious route back to the course they wanted. Schools and colleges handle that case with varying flexibility, and the honest position is that it is far better prevented than remedied. Ask your school when predictions are issued, and work backwards from that date.

The practical plan is simple. Treat the autumn of Year 11 as a term with a deadline at its end, because it has one even though nobody calls it that. Buy technique work in September and October rather than in March, and aim it at whatever the Year 10 end-of-year papers identified. The cost is identical and the consequence is larger, which is as close to free as tuition planning gets.

sections.heading: Results day and the ten days after it
paragraphs: Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Decisions that follow results have short deadlines: a remark has to be requested quickly, a November entry has to be made, and a sixth-form place may need confirming or renegotiating. Families who have not thought about any of this in advance make expensive decisions in a fortnight that includes travel and school closures.

The useful preparation is a decision tree written in advance. What grade in each subject would be acceptable. What grade would trigger a remark request, which is appropriate when a mark sits close to a boundary and the school agrees. What grade would trigger a November entry. And what the fallback sixth-form option is, with the requirement for it written down rather than remembered.

The November route is genuinely workable and deserves to be framed as a route rather than a failure. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is early enough for most sixth-form and foundation conversations, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Entry fees are set by the examination centre rather than by a tutor, so the reserve has to exist before the whole budget goes into term-time lessons.

Preparation for a November entry is a focused eight to ten week block rather than a repeat of the year. The content has already been met, so the work is the specific topics that failed, the technique that cost marks, and a different approach to timing. That is a narrower and cheaper piece of work than Year 11 was, provided the diagnosis from the June paper is done honestly rather than hopefully.
