sections.heading: What a nearby tutor can and cannot do
paragraphs: Having answered the timing question, the proximity question deserves a fair answer rather than a dismissal. A tutor who lives nearby offers two real advantages: a physical presence, which changes behaviour for some younger students, and a device that cannot be scrolled under the table. For a Year 10 student who will not engage over a screen, those are not small things and they are worth paying the travel premium for.

What a nearby tutor cannot offer is a choice. In-home tuition requires somebody willing to drive to your address inside the narrow usable window, which means the pool is defined by geography rather than by board and tier. Along this corridor, where journeys run twenty-five to forty minutes in the late afternoon, that pool is small for Extended-tier combinations and smaller again for a specific Pearson code.

The market prices the difference openly. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with travel inside the figure, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor and from AED 150 for IGCSE at Unitors. Monthly packages run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

So the fair conclusion is this. If your constraint is a student who needs someone in the room, hire nearby and accept the narrower choice and the later start. If your constraint is matching a specific board and tier, or holding a durable slot across two years, the distance filter is the one to drop. Neither answer is universal, and a provider telling you otherwise is describing its own business model rather than your situation.

sections.heading: Confirm the board and tier before any of this applies
paragraphs: A timing plan built on the wrong examination is a well-sequenced waste. Ask the school in writing for the board and the syllabus code for each subject, plus the tier where Cambridge applies. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics with Core and Extended routes; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses forms like 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 with Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics.

The differences change the plan rather than just the content. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade available, which makes the Year 10 diagnostic a tier conversation rather than a revision one. A modular structure on some Pearson qualifications changes when a paper can be sat and how a resit works. And Cambridge's alternative-to-practical written paper on several science syllabuses changes what practical preparation should consist of.

The series matter too, and they are frequently misstated to UAE families. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no Dubai student sits it. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's own risk.

Get all of this in the first week of September rather than in October. The autumn block is the one with runway, and three weeks of it spent discovering which board and tier the student is on is three weeks that cannot be recovered later. One message to the school, answered subject by subject, protects every hour that follows it.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Silicon Oasis, and what we will not pretend
paragraphs: Send four things: which year and term you are in, the syllabus codes and tiers, the last set of marked papers, and the hour your child is realistically at a desk. The marked papers matter most, because sorting the lost marks by cause costs nothing and determines whether you need four sessions or four months. We then match a tutor to the code and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost.

Afterwards you receive a written note setting out which gaps are closable in the block you are in and which needed an earlier one. If you are in March of Year 11 with an algebraic fluency problem, the note will say that the remaining weeks cannot deliver it and will propose what they can deliver instead. That is a worse sales message than the alternative and it is the one that produces a result in June.

The limits. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch and we claim none. We hold no board or regulator approval, so nobody here is KHDA approved or Cambridge accredited. We do not supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; we reference them and link to the official source.

And no dates presented as our own authority. Every Cambridge and Pearson date on this page is attributed and backward-looking, and forward-looking series are named by month only, because a series named by month stays true and one named by month and year is wrong a year later with nobody having touched the page. Take your actual dates from the school's exams officer or the board's live timetable.

whyPoints.description: A gap addressed in Year 10 costs a fraction of the same gap in spring of Year 11, and some gaps cannot be closed late at any rate. Most pages in this market optimise for proximity because proximity is what people type. Timing is what changes the grade.

whyPoints.title: An honest list of what closes late
whyPoints.description: Command words, timing, working layout and finite procedural topics all move in weeks. Algebraic fluency, biological precision and close literary analysis do not. Naming which side each of your gaps sits on is the difference between a plan that works and one that disappoints.

whyPoints.title: The summer window written down
whyPoints.description: The longest break, the lowest demand, the only block where two-hour sessions do not compete with a school day. Nobody markets a quiet July because there is no urgency to sell, which is exactly why it appears on this page instead.

whyPoints.title: A fair answer on proximity
whyPoints.description: A nearby tutor genuinely helps a student who will not engage over a screen, and the in-home band is AED 180 to 500 with travel inside it. Where board, tier or slot durability is the binding constraint, distance is the filter to drop. Neither answer is universal.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether an IGCSE tutor is actually near Dubai Silicon Oasis?
faqs.answer: Far less than when you start. A tutor five minutes away who begins in March of Year 11 will achieve less than one on a video link who begins in September of Year 10, because algebraic fluency and precision in written explanation take months of repetition and March does not contain months. Proximity affects convenience and start-time reliability. Timing affects which gaps can be addressed at all, which is a difference of category rather than degree.

faqs.question: Which term should a Silicon Oasis family start IGCSE tuition in?
faqs.answer: Autumn of Year 10 for anything structural, because that is the only block with real runway and the tier decision is also forming then. Spring of Year 10 if the aim is to influence a Core or Extended entry, with a written diagnostic to take to the school. Autumn of Year 11 if the aim is a better predicted grade, which drives sixth-form applications. Spring of Year 11 for technique only, which is real but bounded.

faqs.question: What can we achieve in the summer between Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: Quite a lot, because nothing competes. It is the longest break in the two years, the only block where two-hour sessions do not follow a school day, and the period of lowest demand in the after-school window across the UAE. Four to six sessions aimed at the one weakness Year 10 exposed, with marked practice between them. A student who arrives in September with formula rearrangement already automatic has changed what the autumn can be used for.

faqs.question: Why is autumn of Year 11 more important than parents think?
faqs.answer: Because predicted grades are formed then, from classwork, internal assessments and mock papers, and sixth-form and foundation applications are generally made on those predictions. A student who improves measurably in October gets a better prediction and a better set of offers regardless of what June produces. Technique moves quickly and feeds exactly the internal marks a prediction is built from, so the opportunity is both real and cheap.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects cannot be rescued in the spring of Year 11?
faqs.answer: English Literature first, because quotation selection and close analysis need repeated marked practice across months. Then anything resting on algebraic fluency, and the written precision that biology and physics mark schemes demand. By contrast, chemistry's moles calculations and qualitative analysis tables, economics data-response technique and computer science theory all respond reasonably to a short late block, so a spring start in those is defensible.

faqs.question: Do your tutors travel to homes in Cedre Villas or Academic City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Across the market, in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors with travel inside the figure, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor. Our lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, which also makes a slot durable across two years rather than one term.

faqs.question: Is budget tutoring near Academic City worth using for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For the right job, yes. The published budget band in this emirate runs AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, sustained partly by the undergraduate population next door, and it is genuinely effective for content revision, homework supervision and repetitive marked practice. Pointed at Extended-tier structural work it tends to produce a term of reassurance and no grade movement, after which a specialist is hired anyway with less time left.

faqs.question: How do we use my child's Year 10 end-of-year papers?
faqs.answer: They are the second-best diagnostic in the two years and they are almost always filed unread. Sort every lost mark into causes: did not know it, ran out of time, misread the command word, or knew it and wrote an answer that did not earn the marks. Count them. The largest cause tells you what the summer sessions should be aimed at, and whether the problem is content, technique or capability, which determines the number of hours.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE results arrive, and what happens next?
faqs.answer: Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The decisions that follow have short deadlines: a remark request, a November entry, or confirming a sixth-form place. Write the decision tree in advance, agree with the school what grade would trigger each branch, and hold an entry-fee reserve from the start of the year.

faqs.question: Is a November IGCSE entry a sensible route from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and framing it as a failure causes real harm. It is simply the other series. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, early enough for most sixth-form and foundation conversations, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Preparation is a focused eight to ten week block rather than a repeat of the year, because the content has been met and the work is the specific topics and technique that failed.

faqs.question: Can the Core or Extended entry still be changed in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes very early in Year 11, and realistically the window is Year 10. The school makes the entry decision from classwork and internal assessment, and Core on Cambridge syllabuses does not reach the top grades. If a sixth-form course requires a grade above that ceiling, the conversation needs evidence rather than conviction: a written assessment showing the student handles Extended content once an earlier gap is secure is what schools respond to.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board my child's school enters?
faqs.answer: Ask in writing, subject by subject, because many Dubai schools split boards across subjects for staffing or historical reasons. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580, 0620 and 0625 with Core and Extended routes; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses forms like 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 with Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics. Do it in the first week of September, because the autumn block is the one with runway and discovering this in October shortens it.

faqs.question: Does a tutor near Silicon Oasis need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a reasonable question to ask directly. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published.

faqs.question: Should a tutor help with IGCSE coursework or assignments?
faqs.answer: With teaching and feedback, yes; with producing the work, never. A tutor may explain what a task is assessing, work through a comparable example on a different topic, read what your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write, complete or edit the piece to a finished state. Work submitted as a student's own that is not theirs is a malpractice matter and the consequence lands on your child.

faqs.question: What should the first month of a timing-led plan produce?
faqs.answer: A written statement of which gaps the block you are in can close and which needed an earlier one, which is the single most useful thing to hold and the thing nobody supplies. Plus the syllabus codes and tiers confirmed in writing, and one measurable technique change, usually in timing or in how much working is shown. No grade prediction, because nobody can honestly offer one.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-silic.closingHeading: Optimise the term, not the postcode
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-silic.closingBody: The near-me search is understandable and it answers the wrong question. Distance decides how convenient the lesson is; the term you begin in decides what the lesson can achieve. So tell us which year and term you are in, the syllabus codes and tiers, and send the last marked papers. Sorting those marks by cause costs nothing, the free trial lesson costs nothing, and the written note that follows will tell you plainly whether this block can close your child's gap or whether the honest answer is to aim at what it can.

intro.heading: The question behind a near-me search is almost always how long is left
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai South rarely start searching for a tutor at a calm moment. The search happens after a mock paper comes back two grades below expectation, or when a Year 11 parent counts the weeks to the June series and finds there are fewer than they assumed. The word in the query is near me, but the actual question is how much can be fixed in the time remaining, and by whom. Distance is a proxy for urgency: something close feels like it can start sooner.

It cannot, in any meaningful sense. A local tutor still has to have a free slot, still has to be matched to the right board and tier, and still has to spend the first session diagnosing. The only variable proximity genuinely changes is whether somebody can drive to your villa, and for a Year 11 candidate working through marked past papers that is the least important variable in the list. What matters is whether the plan is placed correctly in the year.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, which means a session can usually start within days rather than waiting for somebody's route to clear. That speed is the practical benefit of the model when the constraint is time, and it is worth more than presence to a candidate eight weeks from a paper.

So this page is a calendar. It sets out the Dubai academic year term by term and what each term is actually for. It sets out the two series a UAE candidate can sit, counted backwards from the papers to the entry deadline. It gives a worked eight-week plan, week by week, for a student holding a disappointing mock. It explains how to read a mock result rather than react to it, what the 9 to 1 grades mean, and how Ramadan and the long breaks change where the work can go. And it gives the cost per term rather than per hour, because a term is the unit a plan is actually bought in.

Two facts to fix before the detail. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, and planning a revision block towards it is a wasted term. Second, Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Confirm the zone and the final timetable with the school, every year.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-south.programmesIntro: Dubai South students reach IGCSE through a British-curriculum route that starts in Key Stage 3, and some take the IB Middle Years Programme instead to the same age. All three stages appear in requests from this cluster.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course begins, with no external examinations and therefore no early warning. Algebraic fluency, scientific notation, structured written explanation and reading speed are what transfer into Year 10. A weakness in any of them is invisible until the first IGCSE mock returns a grade nobody expected, by which point two years of the fix window have gone.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai South the Key Stage 3 years are also when the school decides which board and which science route a cohort takes. Whether triple or double award science is offered, and whether the school enters Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, is set at school level and varies between the Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park schools. Ask in Year 9, not Year 10.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, usually eight to ten subjects, externally examined at the end. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings in many subjects; Pearson Edexcel tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Grading runs 9 to 1 on Edexcel and on reformed Cambridge subjects, with A*-G still in use for some. The entry tier caps the grade before revision begins, which makes it the highest-stakes decision of Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai South candidates sit the June series, with November available as a resit route. Entry is handled by the school as the examination centre and the deadline falls months before the papers. Mock examinations typically land a term earlier, and the mock is the fixed point a tutoring plan should be built around because it is the next real evidence anyone will have.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB route for the same age band, marked on four criteria per subject from A to D on a 0-8 scale and converted to a 1-7 grade, with the Personal Project in the final year carrying the heaviest time load. There are no public examinations in most schools, which changes the shape of the year completely: the deadlines are internal and continuous rather than external and terminal.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Dubai South run the Middle Years Programme instead of IGCSE, so two children of the same age in neighbouring villas can face entirely different assessment. Families moving between the systems mid-secondary need gap mapping across a holiday rather than weekly tutoring, because the content overlaps while the assessment calendar does not.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Dubai South families request most, with the syllabus code and the part of the course that becomes urgent late. Codes are worth checking on your child's own timetable because boards vary between schools here.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended covers the full grade range and Core caps lower, so the tier decision has to be settled before any plan is written. Late in the course the recurring losses are bearings, vectors, transformations and the compound questions at the end of Paper 4. The formula list is provided and most candidates meet it for the first time in the examination hall.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted calculator papers with Higher tiering needed for the top grades. Pearson favours longer multi-step contextual questions, so a student arriving from Cambridge mid-course stumbles on phrasing rather than content. Ratio, proportional reasoning and the final multi-mark questions are the late-stage priorities.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is the component most reliably neglected until the final weeks, and it carries real marks for identifying variables, reading instruments and suggesting improvements. On the theory papers, unit prefixes and gradient interpretation account for a disproportionate share of late losses.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables are where the spread sits, and both are learnable in a compressed block because they are procedural. Ionic equations attempted without balancing charge score nothing. Organic chemistry at this level is nomenclature and reaction type, which makes it one of the most recoverable topics late in the year.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: High recall volume means late-stage gains come from structured note compression rather than rereading. Command-term discipline is the other lever: describe, explain and suggest demand different answers, and over-writing a two-mark question costs time the last question needs. Diagram-based topics reward a short block of focused drill.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response are marked on structure as much as expression, and the summary question is where reading marks leak because candidates copy the passage instead of condensing it. Both are improvable in eight weeks because they are technique rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study based, with marks for applying a concept to the business in the stimulus rather than defining it. Analysis and evaluation command words carry the highest tariff and are where candidates stop short. Break-even, cash flow and ratio calculations are reliable marks and reliably under-practised in the final term.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked and an unlabelled axis loses the mark whatever the prose says. The data-response paper rewards reading the figures before writing. Elasticity calculations and the distinction between a movement along a curve and a shift of it are both short, high-yield topics for a compressed block.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers theory including data representation; Paper 2 is algorithms and programming in pseudocode rather than a real language. Trace tables are dependable marks that almost nobody drills. A student who has coded only in Python needs pseudocode conventions taught explicitly, and that is a two-session job rather than a term.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: The alternative to three separate sciences, with reduced content and a different paper structure. Families should confirm which route the school has entered their child for before any plan is written, because the papers are not interchangeable and past papers from the wrong route waste the weeks that are left.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students because Arabic is mandatory in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules. Listening, reading, writing and speaking are all assessed. The writing component responds quickly to a small bank of accurately drilled structures, which makes it one of the better late-stage targets in the timetable.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Offered by some schools as a bridge towards A Level or the IB Diploma, covering calculus, trigonometry and vectors beyond 0580. It sits alongside the main mathematics entry and the overlap is smaller than students expect, so it needs its own slot in a revision timetable rather than being folded into maths.

sections.heading: The Dubai school year, term by term, and what each term is for
paragraphs: A tutoring plan written without the year in it is a plan to do the same thing in September as in April, which wastes both. The Dubai academic year runs from late August or early September to the start of July, with a long winter break in December, a spring break, and a shortened school day during Ramadan. Each of those periods suits different work, and matching the work to the period is most of what good planning consists of.

The first term is coverage. There is no examination pressure, the school is still teaching new content, and this is the only window in which a genuine gap can be closed slowly. It is also the only time a tier decision can realistically be revisited with evidence. Families who start in September rather than February get a different service for the same money, and in this cluster they are a minority.

The second term is mocks and repair. The mock result is the single most useful piece of information anyone will have before the real papers, and the weeks after it are when a plan should be rewritten rather than continued. The third term is pacing and consolidation, with no new content, and the two long breaks are where the work that needs uninterrupted hours should sit. The table below sets that out against the actions that belong in each period. Read it against your own child's school calendar rather than in the abstract, because mock windows in this cluster differ by several weeks between the Al Furjan schools and the Dubai Investments Park ones, and a plan aimed at the wrong mock date loses a fortnight it cannot replace.

sections.heading: Eight weeks after a disappointing mock: the worked plan
paragraphs: This is the most common situation behind a near-me search in Dubai South in the spring term. A mock has returned a grade two below expectation, there are roughly eight weeks to the series, and the instinct is to revise everything again. That instinct is wrong, because the mock has already told you which parts do not need revisiting. The plan below treats the mock as a diagnostic document rather than a verdict.

The structure is four fortnights, each with one job, and a timed assessment at the end of each. Week one is diagnosis only: going through the mock script answer by answer, separating losses that are content from losses that are technique, and writing the list down in priority order. Nothing is taught in that first session, which surprises parents and is the reason the remaining fourteen sessions are aimed correctly.

Fortnights two and three take the list in order, highest-cost topic first, with one timed section at the end of each to check the repair held. The final fortnight is whole papers and pacing with no new material, because a student two weeks from an examination gains more from writing three papers under conditions than from meeting a new topic. The table gives the shape; the content of each fortnight comes from the student's own script, which is why no two of these plans are the same. It also explains why the block is quoted as sixteen sessions rather than as an open arrangement: the structure only works if the checkpoints are fixed in advance and the fortnight repeats when a checkpoint shows the repair did not hold.

sections.heading: How to read a mock result instead of reacting to it
paragraphs: A mock grade is a number and a number invites a reaction. The useful information is underneath it, in the distribution of the losses. Three students can score the same grade for completely different reasons: one ran out of time and left the last twelve marks blank, one answered every question and lost two or three marks across the whole paper, and one knew four topics well and two not at all. Those three need three different plans, and the grade alone does not distinguish them.

The questions worth asking of a script, in order. Did the paper get finished? If not, the problem is pacing and the fix is timing drill, not content. Are the losses concentrated in a few topics or spread evenly? Concentrated losses are a coverage problem and respond to teaching. Evenly spread small losses are a technique problem and respond to command-word and presentation work. Did the student lose marks on questions they could answer in conversation? That is examination-writing rather than knowledge.

It is also worth checking what the mock actually was. Some schools set a full past paper under real conditions; others set a shortened or adapted version, and a few mark generously to keep morale up. A grade produced by a non-standard paper or a lenient scheme is not comparable to a real one, and a plan built on it will be aimed at the wrong target. Asking the school which paper and which mark scheme were used takes one email and occasionally changes the entire diagnosis.
bullets: An unfinished paper is a pacing problem, whatever the grade says
Concentrated losses respond to teaching; spread losses respond to technique
Marks lost on content the student can explain aloud are a writing problem

sections.heading: Results, remarks and the resit decision, with dates that can be checked
paragraphs: Results arrive at the examination centre before they reach students, and both the gap and the dates are published. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The pattern holds year to year: a June series produces results in August and a November series produces results in January. Those are the windows in which a remark or a resit decision has to be made.

The remark route runs through the school as the examination centre, not through the family. A remark can move a grade down as well as up, which schools explain and families often do not absorb. It is worth requesting when a grade sits just below a boundary that matters for a sixth-form place or an equivalency requirement, and it is usually not worth requesting on a grade several marks clear of one. The decision has a deadline, which is why the days immediately after results matter more than the weeks after them.

The resit route is the other November use. For Dubai South students who miss a required grade in June, the November series is the straightforward second attempt, and the entry is made through the school months before the papers. A resit decided in September and prepared across the autumn is a different proposition from one decided in October with six weeks left. The table sets out the sequence so the decisions can be made in order rather than all at once.

sections.heading: What the 9 to 1 grades mean, and why boundaries move
paragraphs: Grading runs 9 to 1 on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE and on reformed Cambridge subjects, with A* to G still in use on some Cambridge syllabuses. A grade 9 is above the old A*, and the grades are not a simple relabelling of the letters, which is why comparing a sibling's A from several years ago to a 7 today is not informative. Schools in this cluster use both scales depending on the subject, so a Year 11 report can contain two different grading systems at once.

Grade boundaries are set after each series rather than published in advance, because they are adjusted to the difficulty of that series' papers. That has a direct planning consequence: the percentage that reached a grade 7 last June is not a target this June. What does transfer between series is the structure of the papers and the relative weight of each component, and that is what a plan should be built on.

The tier interacts with all of this. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade available, so a candidate on the lower tier cannot reach the top grades however well they perform. That makes the entry decision the highest-leverage thing in Year 10 and a sunk cost by the spring of Year 11. A family discovering the cap late has one remaining question worth asking: whether the November series with a different entry is a better route than pushing at a ceiling in June.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the breaks and where the hours actually are
paragraphs: The UAE calendar supplies two kinds of time, and most tutoring plans use the wrong one. Term weeks give an hour here and there against a full school workload. The winter and spring breaks give consecutive days with nothing competing. For work that needs uninterrupted stretches — a full timed paper, a coursework write-up, a complete topic rebuilt from scratch — the break is worth more than the month of term weeks around it.

Ramadan changes the shape of the day. School hours shorten, afternoon concentration drops, and the useful window moves into the evening after iftar. The practical adjustments are to shorten sessions from ninety minutes to sixty, to move them later, and to switch from content teaching to timed question practice, which costs less concentration per mark gained. Families who want to keep momentum without adding fatigue usually drop from two sessions a week to one for the month and move the heavy work into the spring break instead.

For a Year 11 candidate the arithmetic is worth doing explicitly. Count the weeks to the series. Subtract the final fortnight, which is pacing only. Identify which of the remaining weeks fall in a break and which fall in Ramadan. What is left is the real working window, and it is almost always smaller than the raw week count suggests. Doing that calculation in January rather than April is the difference between a plan with slack in it and a plan that runs out of time.
bullets: Breaks hold consecutive days; term weeks hold fragments
During Ramadan: shorter sessions, later start, timed practice over new content
Drop from two sessions a week to one rather than abandoning the plan
Count the real working weeks in January, not in April

sections.heading: Cost per term, which is the unit a plan is actually bought in
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how this market quotes and terms are how families budget, so here is the translation. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget provision at AED 240-600 a month, mid-market at AED 600-1,200, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more. Published monthly packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Behind those monthly figures, the hourly bands are published by the providers that charge them. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the budget end, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is in the price.

The useful comparison for a calendar-led plan is what each format costs across a block rather than an hour. An eight-week block of two sessions a week is sixteen sessions, which at a qualified online rate of AED 150-300 is a very different commitment from the same block in-home at AED 180-500. The table does that arithmetic. Every figure is attributed to the provider that published it; these are market bands, not an IB Gram price list, and our own conversation begins with a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Why a calendar-led plan suits online delivery in Dubai South
paragraphs: When time is the binding constraint, two things matter: how quickly a plan can start, and how many sessions a week it can hold. Both favour online delivery from a community like Dubai South. A session can usually begin within days because no route has to be cleared, and three sessions a week in the final fortnight is schedulable because nobody is driving. An in-home tutor fits one visit an evening and has to be willing to make it to the southern corridor at the hour your child is free.

The second advantage is the mark scheme. A calendar-led plan runs on marked scripts, timed sections and the official scheme, and those are documents. Two documents side by side on a shared screen, annotated live, is a better arrangement than paper passed across a table. It also leaves a record: what was annotated in week three is still there in week seven, which matters in a plan whose whole structure is checking whether a repair held.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so there is no comparison to soften here. For a Dubai South family eight weeks from a series, the question is whether presence is worth more than speed, frequency and specialist matching. For a seven-year-old, presence usually wins. For a Year 11 candidate with a disappointing mock and a fixed date, it usually does not, and the table sets out why in terms that can be checked against your own week.

faqs.question: How many weeks do we really have before the IGCSE series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the raw count suggests. Start from the examination date, subtract the final fortnight, which should be pacing and whole papers rather than new work, then mark off any weeks that fall in the winter or spring break and any that fall during Ramadan, when sessions shorten and move after iftar. What remains is the real working window. For most Dubai South families counting in January, that calculation removes three or four weeks they had assumed were available, which is precisely why it is worth doing before the first session rather than in April.

faqs.question: Can eight weeks of tutoring change an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Often, when the eight weeks are aimed. They cannot cover a syllabus, and attempting it produces panic rather than marks. What they can do is attack the specific topics and techniques a marked mock script exposes, in priority order, with a timed checkpoint at the end of each fortnight. Students regularly gain marks in that window from pacing, command-word reading and mark-scheme vocabulary alone, none of which requires new knowledge. The deciding factor is whether week one is spent diagnosing or spent teaching, and it should be spent diagnosing.

faqs.question: What should the first session after a bad mock actually do?
faqs.answer: Nothing but read the script. Answer by answer, the session establishes whether the paper was finished, whether the losses sit in a few topics or spread thinly across all of them, and whether marks went on content the student does not know or on content they could explain aloud but wrote badly. Those three findings produce three different plans from the same grade. Teaching in that first hour feels more productive and makes the remaining fifteen sessions less accurate, which is an expensive way to feel better.

faqs.question: Does my child's school decide which exam series they sit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The school acts as the examination centre, makes the entry and sets the internal deadline for confirming it, which falls months before the papers. Families do not enter candidates directly in the normal course. For a UAE candidate the available options are the June series and the November series, with November commonly used as a resit route. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones, so the school is also the place to confirm which zone timetable applies before anyone plans a revision schedule around dates.

faqs.question: Is it worth requesting a remark on an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: It depends on the margin and on what the grade is needed for. A remark runs through the school as the examination centre, has a published deadline shortly after results, and can move a grade down as well as up. It is usually worth requesting when a grade sits a mark or two below a boundary that matters for a sixth-form place or an equivalency requirement, and usually not when the grade is several marks clear. Decide in the days after results rather than the weeks, because the window is short.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai South student plan a November resit?
faqs.answer: In the days after August results, not in October. A resit entry goes through the school months before the November papers, and the autumn term is long enough for a properly aimed block if the decision is made early. The preparation should start from the June script rather than from a blank revision plan, because the script says which topics and which techniques cost the grade. A resit decided in October with six weeks left is a different and much weaker proposition than one decided in August with a term to work in.

faqs.question: How do winter and spring breaks change a revision plan?
faqs.answer: They supply consecutive days with no competing school workload, which is a different resource from a weekly hour. Work that needs uninterrupted time belongs there: a full timed paper marked and reviewed within forty-eight hours while the student still remembers their reasoning, a coursework write-up, or a topic rebuilt from the beginning. Four to six sessions placed on consecutive days in a fortnight achieve more than the same number spread across six weeks of term. Most families in this cluster underuse the breaks and then run short in the spring.

faqs.question: What changes during Ramadan for a Year 11 student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, afternoon concentration drops, and the usable window moves to the evening after iftar. The practical adjustments are shorter sessions, usually sixty minutes rather than ninety, moved later, with content teaching replaced by timed question practice because that costs less concentration per mark gained. Families who want momentum without added fatigue generally drop from two sessions a week to one for the month and move the heavy work into the spring break. Planning that in advance works considerably better than improvising it in the second week.

faqs.question: Are grade boundaries the same every year for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No. They are set after each series and adjusted to the difficulty of that series' papers, which means the percentage that reached a grade 7 last June is not a target this June. What does carry across series is the structure of the papers and the relative weight of each component, and that is what a revision plan should be built on. It also means aiming a clear band above the target rather than exactly at it is the sensible response to a system that will not tell you the threshold in advance.

faqs.question: How quickly can tutoring start for a student in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Usually within days for the common subjects, because online delivery means no route has to clear and no tutor has to be willing to drive to the southern corridor at a particular hour. Mathematics, the three Cambridge sciences and English Language are the deep end of the pool. Less common entries such as Computer Science 0478 or Arabic 0544 can take a week or more, and we say so with a date rather than seating a generalist. For a student eight weeks from a series, that speed is worth more than physical presence.

faqs.question: Should a Year 10 student start tutoring now or wait?
faqs.answer: Now is the better answer, and it buys a different service. In Year 10 the school is still teaching new content, there is no examination pressure, and a real gap can be closed slowly rather than patched. It is also the only window in which a tier decision can be revisited with evidence, because a term of work ending in a full timed paper at the higher tier produces something a school will actually consider. By the spring of Year 11 the entry is settled and the ceiling is fixed, whatever the revision achieves.

faqs.question: What does an eight-week block cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Two sessions a week for eight weeks is sixteen sessions, so the hourly band decides it. Using published Dubai figures, qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180-350 on Bestimate's 2026 table, with independent tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Bestimate's monthly estimate for specialist examination-year support is AED 1,000-2,000 or more. These are market bands from the providers named, not IB Gram prices; our own conversation starts with a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script and the official mark scheme shared on screen. We state it plainly because a time-pressured family deserves to know what they are buying before the first session rather than after it. Independent in-home tutors do work in this part of Dubai if physical presence is the priority for your household.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should the final fortnight have?
faqs.answer: Three or four short ones rather than two long ones. In the last two weeks nothing new should be attempted, so the work is timing, question order, mark-scheme vocabulary and the handful of topics a student can still secure. Sixty-minute sessions three or four times a week keep that work frequent while respecting the fact that concentration, not time, is the scarce resource at that point. A ninety-minute session in the final week tends to end with twenty minutes of nothing useful happening.

faqs.question: My child finished the paper but still lost marks everywhere. What now?
faqs.answer: That pattern points at technique rather than coverage. Small losses spread evenly across a paper usually mean command words are being misread, answers are the wrong length for the marks available, or working is not being shown where a question requires it. None of that improves with more content teaching. The work is short timed answers, marked against the official scheme, with the wording of the band compared against what the student wrote. It is unglamorous, it takes about four sessions, and it is the fastest available gain for a competent candidate.

faqs.question: Which schools near Dubai South do IGCSE candidates attend?
faqs.answer: Most come from the British-curriculum arc around Al Furjan, Jebel Ali and Discovery Gardens, or from the mixed cluster in Dubai Investments Park and Green Community where British, IB continuum and SABIS provision sit close together. Mock windows and exam boards differ between these schools, which is why a plan starts by asking when the next mock is and which syllabus code appears on the timetable. KHDA publishes annual inspection ratings for each of them. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named here.

intro.heading: What a syllabus-literate tutor does differently
paragraphs: There is a particular kind of tutoring session that feels productive and changes nothing. The tutor explains a topic clearly, the student follows, both leave satisfied, and the next paper comes back at the same mark. It happens because the session addressed the subject rather than the assessment, and at IGCSE those are different things. The subject is chemistry. The assessment is Cambridge 0620 Extended, which asks for chemistry in a specific set of forms and pays for it against a published scheme.

A syllabus-literate tutor starts from the specification. Every Cambridge and Pearson syllabus publishes its content list, its assessment objectives and its paper structure, and every past paper comes with a mark scheme that states what earns a mark and what does not. Read together, those documents answer most of the questions a parent in Dubai Sports City is actually asking: why a bright student keeps scoring in the middle, and what would have to change.

The answer is usually mechanical. Across a full IGCSE paper, a student who loses a single mark per question to presentation habits loses more than one who does not understand a whole topic. Working held in a calculator instead of written down. A rounded intermediate value carried into the next step. A unit omitted from a final answer. An ionic equation without charges balanced. 'Describe' answered with an explanation, or 'explain' answered with a description. None of those is a knowledge problem, and all of them are teachable in weeks.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a Sports City address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. The practical gain is that a student entered for a specific code can be matched to someone who has taught that code, instead of to the nearest available subject graduate — and for a Year 11 student eight weeks out, that distinction decides whether the block recovers marks or revisits content.

The speed matters too. Because matching does not depend on who can reach Victory Heights on a Tuesday evening, a specialist can usually be proposed within a day and a trial lesson held the same week. Families searching after a mock result are spending calendar they cannot get back, and the days lost to arranging a visit come straight off the block.

Everything below is organised by syllabus: what each paper asks, where the marks go, the nine habits that cost one mark at a time, and a past-paper routine that uses five years of material properly rather than working through them front to back until the term ends. programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE

Cambridge offers the February/March series to India alone, so any revision schedule a Sports City family finds that references a February window belongs to a different country's calendar and should be discarded.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The years in which algebraic manipulation, scientific explanation and extended writing are built, assessed internally and in many schools through Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which run in March, May and October. A student who leaves Year 9 unable to rearrange a formula meets that gap again in mathematics, physics and chemistry simultaneously.
programmes.countryNote: Enquiries at this stage from Town Square, Mudon and Remraam are usually prompted by a Year 9 report. The high-value work is narrow: rearrangement, ratio, standard form and writing a cause-and-effect sentence. Six to eight sessions is often the whole intervention.

programmes.name: Additional Mathematics and the step to 16-plus
programmes.description: Cambridge 0606 sits alongside 0580 for students heading towards A Level or Higher Level mathematics, and covers calculus, functions and trigonometry at a level closer to AS. It is the single best preparation for the jump at 16, and it is also the course where the gap between a comfortable 0580 Extended student and a struggling one becomes visible.
programmes.countryNote: Requests for 0606 from Sports City and Arabian Ranches concentrate in the second half of Year 11, often after a student has been advised to take it and found the first topics harder than expected. A short block on differentiation and function notation usually settles it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-sport.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names the syllabus code and the specific place marks are lost on that paper. The codes are what appear on a school's subject information sheet and at the top of every past paper, and they are worth checking before any tutoring is booked.

subjects.name: Mathematics — Cambridge 0580
subjects.description: Number, algebra, coordinate geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors, probability and statistics. Extended reaches further into algebraic fractions, functions and advanced trigonometry. Marks go missing in unwritten method, premature rounding carried through a multi-step answer, and solutions given without units or without the context the question asked for.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics — Cambridge 0606
subjects.description: Functions, calculus, series, trigonometric identities and vectors at a level approaching AS. Differentiation of composite functions and the use of correct notation are where the spread opens. Students who treat it as harder 0580 rather than as a different course lose marks to presentation conventions they have never been taught.

subjects.name: Chemistry — Cambridge 0620
subjects.description: Particles, atoms and bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, the periodic table, electrochemistry, energetics, organic chemistry and chemical analysis. Three calculation types carry most of the available marks: moles from mass, moles from concentration and volume, and percentage yield or purity. Setting the calculation out is where the method marks are.

subjects.name: Physics — Cambridge 0625
subjects.description: Motion, forces and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear physics and space physics. Reliable losses are unit conversion before substitution, direction dropped from a vector quantity, and explanation questions answered by quoting a formula when the scheme wants a causal chain in words.

subjects.name: Biology — Cambridge 0610
subjects.description: Cells, movement into and out of cells, biological molecules, enzymes, nutrition, transport, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. The paper rewards precise terminology and penalises near-misses: osmosis described without a partially permeable membrane, or diffusion described without a concentration gradient.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science — Cambridge 0653 and 0654
subjects.description: The two-award and double-award routes for students not entered for three separate sciences. Papers mix disciplines, so revision organised by science rather than by paper leaves a student unprepared for the order in which questions arrive. Progression to an A Level or Higher Level science from this route should be checked with the receiving school.

subjects.name: English Language — Cambridge 0500 and 0990
subjects.description: Reading response, summary and directed writing. Form, audience and register carry marks independently of content, so a well-written article where a letter was specified loses more than a plainer letter. Summary questions reward selection and compression, and are the component most often lost to writing too much.

subjects.name: English Literature — Cambridge 0475 and 0992
subjects.description: Set texts, passage-based questions and extended essays. The most common failure is narrating the plot instead of analysing the writing. A single quoted phrase with a comment on its effect earns more than a paragraph of accurate summary, and that trade is the whole technique.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics — Cambridge 0450 and 0455
subjects.description: Case-study papers requiring application to the business or economy given in the stimulus. Definitions earn a fraction of what applied analysis earns, and Economics diagrams lose marks mostly through unlabelled axes and shifts that are drawn but never referred to in the written answer.

subjects.name: Computer Science — Cambridge 0478
subjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, security, algorithms and programming. Pseudocode answers are marked on logic rather than on the syntax of any one language, which students who have only written in Python routinely misread. Trace tables are a technique worth two sessions and recur every series.

sections.heading: The four science and maths syllabuses, and where each one bleeds marks
paragraphs: Four codes account for most of the enquiry volume from this part of Dubai: 0580 mathematics, 0620 chemistry, 0625 physics and 0610 biology. Each has a characteristic failure mode, and a tutor who knows it can usually identify a student's position from a single marked paper rather than from a term of observation.

In 0580 the characteristic loss is method. The answer is often right and the marks are not available because nothing was written down, or because an intermediate value was rounded and carried forward. In 0620 it is calculation layout: moles from mass, moles from concentration and volume, and yield or purity are the three types that recur, and the scheme pays for the structure of the working as much as for the number at the end.

In 0625 it is unit and direction discipline, plus explanation questions answered with algebra. A question that says 'explain why the lamp becomes dimmer' is asking for a chain — resistance rises, current falls, power falls — and a correct formula earns nothing. In 0610 it is terminology precision, because the scheme accepts specific words and rejects near-synonyms, which is why biology feels arbitrary to students who have never read a mark scheme.

The table below sets this out by code. It is written as a diagnostic aid: a parent can hold their child's last paper against it and recognise the pattern before any tutor is involved. Content lists, paper structures and tiering details should be read from the current official specification, which is published by the board and changes between cohorts.

sections.heading: Nine habits that each cost one mark at a time
paragraphs: The largest single category of recoverable marks on an IGCSE paper is not a topic. It is a set of habits, each worth one or two marks, repeated across every question in every subject. Because each instance is small, none of them appears in a school report, and because they appear everywhere, together they are frequently worth a grade boundary across a full entry of eight or nine subjects.

They are also the fastest thing to fix, which is why a good first block targets them before content. Three to four weeks of deliberate practice changes a habit. Three to four weeks does not teach a missing term's worth of organic chemistry. A family with eight weeks and a mixed problem should spend the first half on habits and the second half on the two most examinable missing topics.

The list below is drawn from mark-scheme wording rather than from general advice, and each item corresponds to a specific reason a scheme withholds a mark. The useful exercise is to take a marked paper and count how many lost marks fall into each row, because the count decides the order of work rather than the teacher's instinct.

What makes this teachable online is that it is entirely visible on a shared screen. The student writes, the tutor reads the working as it appears, and the moment a line is skipped it can be stopped and named. That is harder to do across a table than it sounds, and it is the one activity where the screen is a genuinely better surface than paper.

sections.heading: A past-paper routine that uses five years properly
paragraphs: Most students use past papers badly, and the pattern is identical everywhere: start with the oldest paper, work forwards, mark it roughly, feel vaguely encouraged, repeat. By the end of term they have attempted eight papers and learned almost nothing transferable, because nothing was logged and nothing was repeated at the right interval.

The working set is about five recent years, and it should be used in three modes rather than one. Mode one is by topic: pull every question on electrolysis from five years and do them consecutively, which shows how narrow the question variation actually is. Mode two is by paper, to time, to build pacing and question-order decisions. Mode three is re-attempting the questions previously lost, two or three weeks later, which is the mode almost nobody uses and the one that produces durable change.

Marking is where the value sits. The student should mark their own work against the official scheme with the tutor present, saying out loud why each mark was awarded or withheld. That exercise teaches the examiner's logic, which is the thing being examined. Having work marked silently by someone else teaches nothing except the score.

An error log makes the whole routine compound. One line per lost mark: the paper, the question, the category from the habits table, and the fix. After four weeks the log shows that three categories account for most of the losses, and the revision plan writes itself. Sports City families can run this with no tutor at all; what a tutor adds is the marking judgement and the discipline of re-attempting.

sections.heading: Practical science when the lessons are on a screen
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how practical science works if tuition is online. The answer separates two things. The laboratory itself is the school's job and cannot be replaced: handling apparatus, following a method under supervision, and seeing a reaction behave unexpectedly are school experiences. What is examined, though, is largely the written skill around practical work, and that is teachable on screen using real past-paper data.

Cambridge sciences carry a practical component with an alternative-to-practical route, and the question style on that paper is distinctive. It asks which variable should be controlled and why, which apparatus is appropriate and to what precision, how to tabulate results with units in the heading, how to identify an anomalous point, and what is wrong with a method as described. Each of those is a technique with a correct form that can be drilled.

Pearson handles the same skills within its own paper structure, which is one more reason the code matters. A student drilled on one board's practical question style and entered for the other will recognise the science and misread the task, and in a mock report that looks like carelessness rather than mismatch.

The honest division of labour is worth stating to a Year 10 student directly: the school supplies the bench, the tutor supplies the written technique, and the marks for practical work are awarded for the second of those. Students who believe practical marks reward being good with apparatus are often surprised by how much of the paper is about tables and anomalies.

sections.heading: What the money buys, band by band
paragraphs: The most useful way to read tutoring rates is to ask what each band actually does, rather than to sort them by price. At the bottom, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. That band buys supervision and company: homework completed, a Year 8 student kept moving, questions answered. It does not buy mark-scheme judgement, and a Year 11 Extended paper is a mark-scheme problem.

The working band is qualified subject teaching delivered online, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. That is the money that buys someone who can read a marked paper and name the pattern. Above it, specialist rates run AED 200 to 450 and beyond — TutorChase quotes AED 270, Bestimate puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more — which buys code-level familiarity and tiering judgement.

In-home visiting is published at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted, and the premium over the online band is a journey. The premium end of the market reaches AED 650, which is BartyED's published figure for named tutors, and it buys scarcity rather than a different kind of teaching. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Every figure here is published by the provider named and was read in October 2026. None is IB Gram's price list. They appear because most pages ranking for this search publish no price, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not what a Sports City family pays in. The practical conclusion is that the gap between the budget band and the working band buys judgement, and the gap between online and in-home buys transport.

sections.heading: Entries, tiers and the June series
paragraphs: Two administrative facts shape every IGCSE revision plan in Dubai, and both sit with the school rather than the family. The first is the entry itself: which board, which syllabus code, and which tier. The second is the entry deadline, which closes months before the papers and after which the tier is fixed for that series.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate works to June with November as the resit route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. In the most recent completed cycles, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning against.

The practical instruction for a Sports City family is to find out two dates and one entry. When do the school's entries close, which tier has the student been entered for, and what grade does that tier cap? A tiering conversation held before the deadline is a decision. Held afterwards it is a complaint, and the grade ceiling stands for that series regardless of how the revision goes.
bullets: UAE candidates sit June and November; February/March is India-only
Cambridge centres sit in one of six zones with separate timetables
