sections.heading: The regulator, the mandatory subjects and honest limits
paragraphs: A near-me search run from Dubai Sports City returns tutors advertising out of Sharjah, Ajman and Abu Dhabi, so it helps to know that the school regulator changes with the emirate even when the drive does not feel like a border. Your own school is overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. The powers differ as well as the names: in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A tutor citing a regulator relationship in one emirate has told you nothing about a school in another.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. Using different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. For a Year 11 student, the effect is that the examined timetable is not the whole timetable.

On the tutoring side, the UAE regulates private tuition by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval or accreditation, and claims none. It operates no office or centre in the UAE. The regulators and boards named on this page are described because a parent needs to know who does what — which authority inspects the school, which board sets the paper, and which ministry issues the tutoring permit. None of them endorses this service, and any provider implying otherwise is making a claim worth testing before paying.

process.title: Send the code and the tier
process.description: An enquiry naming the syllabus code, the tier and the year group can be answered precisely. 'Cambridge 0625 Extended, Year 11, last mock 5' is enough to decide whether a genuine specialist is free. The code is printed on the school's subject sheet and at the top of every past paper.

process.title: Trial lesson on the student's own paper
process.description: A full online session with the proposed tutor, spent reading the student's most recent marked script. Lost marks are sorted into the habit categories and the two or three missing topics are named. The written summary afterwards is useful whether or not a block follows.

process.title: Habits first, then content
process.description: Where the diagnosis is mixed, the first half of a block targets the mechanical losses and the second half the most examinable gaps. Doing it in that order means the student sees a score move early, which matters more for a Year 11 student's willingness to work than any other factor.

process.title: Weekly past-paper work, self-marked
process.description: Questions are set from the five-year working set and marked by the student against the official scheme in the session, with every withheld mark named. The error log is kept across weeks rather than restarted, so a repeated category becomes visible instead of being forgotten.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The target set in session one is measured in writing. If the error log shows the same categories recurring, the block changes: a different diagnosis, a different tutor or a different frequency. A block nobody reviews tends to run to its end regardless of whether anything moved.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 Extended and Pearson 4CH1 overlap in content and differ in question style, tiering and practical arrangement. A tutor matched to 'chemistry' rather than to the code will teach correct chemistry against the wrong paper, which is the most common reason a Year 11 block produces no movement.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes used as teaching material
whyPoints.description: Students mark their own work against the official scheme with the tutor asking why each mark was awarded. That teaches the examiner's logic, which is what is being assessed. Having work marked silently by somebody else teaches the score and nothing else, which is why it changes so little.

whyPoints.title: Habits counted before content is taught
whyPoints.description: A single mark lost per question to presentation habits outweighs a whole missing topic across a full paper. Counting the categories on a marked script decides the order of work, and that order is what makes an eight-week block produce a visible change rather than a vague improvement.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. A family should be able to see where a quote sits in the market before agreeing to it.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits stated up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live, one-to-one and online in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, and in-home visiting runs only in India. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and operates no UAE office. Saying this in the first paragraph removes the conversation that otherwise happens after a deposit.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria and techniques and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not write, complete or produce coursework of any kind. That is a board rule, not a preference, and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the candidate.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor from IB Gram travel to Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson is delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Visiting tutors do operate in this part of Dubai and published market rates for in-home one-to-one sessions run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The premium pays for the journey. The online format is offered instead because it allows matching to a syllabus code.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge syllabus codes do Sports City students most often need?
faqs.answer: Mathematics 0580 by a wide margin, then Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and Biology 0610. Additional Mathematics 0606 appears in the second half of Year 11 for students heading towards A Level or Higher Level mathematics. Students not entered for three separate sciences sit Combined 0653 or Coordinated 0654, where papers mix disciplines and revision has to be organised by paper rather than by science. English Language 0500 or 0990 and Business Studies 0450 make up most of the rest.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand the topic but still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer is not in the form the mark scheme pays for. Method held in a calculator earns no method marks. A rounded intermediate value loses the accuracy mark. 'Explain' answered with a formula earns nothing because the scheme wants a causal chain in words. In biology, a near-synonym is rejected outright. Take the marked paper and count how many lost marks are mechanical rather than knowledge-based; for most Year 11 students in this belt the mechanical count is the larger one.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used in the months before the June series?
faqs.answer: In three modes rather than one. By topic, pulling every question on a single topic from five years so the narrow variation becomes visible. By paper, sat to time, to build pacing and question-order decisions. And by re-attempting the specific questions previously lost, two or three weeks later, which is the mode almost nobody uses and the one that makes the change durable. Keep a one-line error log per lost mark, with the category and the fix, and review it rather than restarting it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's work for them each week?
faqs.answer: A tutor can, but it is the weaker option. The higher-value exercise is for the student to mark their own work against the official scheme while the tutor asks why each mark was awarded or withheld. That teaches the examiner's logic, which is the thing being assessed, and it transfers to papers nobody has marked. Work marked silently by an adult teaches the score only, which is why students who are heavily marked often plateau at the same grade for a year.

faqs.question: How are practical skills examined if we never set up an experiment?
faqs.answer: The examined skill is mostly written: choosing and controlling variables, selecting apparatus and precision, tabulating results with units in the heading, identifying anomalous points and criticising a method as described. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical route in several sciences, and all of those techniques can be drilled on screen with real past-paper data. What online lessons cannot replace is handling apparatus in a school laboratory, which remains the school's part of the work.

faqs.question: What are the three chemistry calculations that matter most in 0620?
faqs.answer: Moles from mass using relative formula mass, moles from concentration and volume for solutions, and percentage yield or percentage purity. Between them they account for a large share of the calculation marks across the Extended papers, and each has a layout the scheme rewards. Students who learn them as three templates — write the known quantities, write the relationship, substitute, then evaluate — recover marks within about three weeks, because the arithmetic was rarely the problem in the first place.

faqs.question: Should a Sports City student in Year 11 add 0606 to a full subject load?
faqs.answer: For a student heading towards A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, usually yes, because it covers calculus, functions and trigonometric identities at a level closer to AS and removes most of the step up at 16. For a student who finds 0580 Extended genuinely hard, it adds load without a clear return. The honest test is current performance on algebraic manipulation rather than enthusiasm, and that can be assessed from one marked 0580 paper.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist for a specific code be found?
faqs.answer: Usually within a day, with a trial lesson in the same week, because matching does not depend on who is free within driving distance of Sports City on a given evening. The exception is the weeks around mock results, when demand across every Dubai cohort rises at once and the scarcer codes — 0606 Additional Mathematics, 0478 Computer Science — can involve a short wait. Where that happens you are told, rather than being matched to a general tutor described as a specialist.

faqs.question: Does my child's school decide the Core or Extended entry?
faqs.answer: Yes. Where a Cambridge syllabus is tiered, the school makes the entry, usually during Year 10 and on the basis of attainment to that point, and Core caps the grade available however well the student performs in the series. Pearson's Foundation and Higher structure behaves similarly. The useful question at a parents' evening is specific: which tier, what grade does it cap, and what would have to change for that to be revisited before entries close?

faqs.question: Which English Language component causes the most lost marks?
faqs.answer: Directed writing, because form, audience and register carry marks of their own. A well-written article scores poorly if the task asked for a letter, and no amount of content rescues it. The summary question is the second, lost mainly to writing too much: the marks are for selection and compression, so a longer answer is often a weaker one. Both are technique rather than ability, and both respond to three or four weeks of deliberate practice against the scheme.

faqs.question: Do tutors teaching Dubai students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are unverified.

faqs.question: What is the smallest useful block of IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four sessions, if the target is a single habit or a single calculation family. That is enough to change written-method discipline, to install the three chemistry calculation templates, or to fix unit and direction handling in physics. It is not enough to rebuild a topic nobody taught properly. Booking four with a stated target and reviewing them honestly is better practice than booking a term and hoping, because the review is what tells you whether to continue.

faqs.question: Why do mock results differ so much from predicted grades?
faqs.answer: Because mocks are the first time many students meet the full paper under time, and timing is a separate skill from content. A student who knows the material but has never sat the paper to length will leave questions unattempted, and unattempted questions score nothing regardless of knowledge. Sort the mock losses by cause: if 'question not attempted' or 'content not retrieved under time' is a large category, the next block is pacing work, not more teaching.

intro.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs around Dubailand, and where the money leaks
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible pages competing for this search publish no price at all. One of them asks the price question in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. Two of the three that do quote give figures in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. That is the state of the market a parent in Arabian Ranches or Motor City is trying to budget against, which is why this page starts with numbers rather than reassurance.

The published spread is wide. At the bottom, online generalists and university students work from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. In the middle, qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at AED 150 to 300, and Unitors publishes International GCSE from AED 150. Above that sits specialist International GCSE and A Level provision at AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

Hourly rates mislead, though, because nobody buys an hour. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget provision at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward. Packages in circulation include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Read those two together and the in-home option costs roughly twice as much for half the number of contacts.

The waste is rarely in the rate. It is in buying the wrong thing. A family pays for twenty cheap hours when six specialist hours would have moved more marks. A family pays a travel premium for a Year 10 student who works perfectly well on a screen. A family pays for months of tuition in a subject where the real problem is that the entry tier caps the grade, which no number of hours can fix once entries close. And a family pays for a generalist because the specialist was further away, which in this belt is a distance problem rather than a quality problem.

IB Gram's position on price is simple and it is not a rate card. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video to UAE families; home visits are a service we run only in India, so nobody is sent to a Dubailand address and no travel is being billed. The first session is a free trial with no card, because the only figure worth comparing is whether this particular specialist moves this particular student. Everything below is the detail a parent needs to interrogate any quote, ours included.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.programmesIntro: Cost behaves differently across the stages a Dubailand family passes through. The notes below set out what each stage usually needs, because buying examination-year intensity for a Year 8 student is one of the commonest overspends in this market.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, pre-International GCSE
programmes.description: No certificating examinations, so the purpose is trajectory rather than grades. Cambridge Checkpoint tests in March, May and October indicate whether a student is heading for Core or Extended. The skills that decide that are algebraic fluency, writing explanations rather than descriptions, and sustaining a structured paragraph. The budget band that suits this stage is the lower one, and paying specialist rates here is usually premature.
programmes.countryNote: The newer Dubailand communities skew young, so a large share of enquiries from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon and Town Square concern these years. Work done here at AED 240 to 600 a month is materially cheaper than remediation in Year 11 at AED 1,000 to 2,000, which is the strongest cost argument on this page.

programmes.name: Year 10, first International GCSE year
programmes.description: The year the tier is decided and the year most content is delivered. Consolidating topics while they are still being taught is cheaper than revisiting them a year later, and it is the stage where mid-range qualified provision at AED 150 to 300 an hour does the most per dirham. A diagnostic against the real syllabus code early in the year prevents the most expensive mistake available.
programmes.countryNote: For Dubailand families this is also the year the journey lengthens, since secondary students travel out of the belt. Sessions in Year 10 should be sized for a school night rather than a free afternoon, which argues for shorter frequent slots rather than long ones at a premium rate.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the examination series
programmes.description: The expensive year, and the one where specialist rates are genuinely justified. Work shifts from content to board-specific technique: command terms, timing, the structure a markscheme pays for. Bestimate puts specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward per month for a weekly session, and the intensity usually rises above weekly in the final stretch.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit June and November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. A November resit is a real second chance but results reach students in January, which is after many sixth-form conversations, and that timing should be priced into the plan rather than discovered.

programmes.name: Post-16 and the equivalency question
programmes.description: A Levels or the IB Diploma, with International GCSE tier and grade constraining the options. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited International GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Getting the five-subject count right in Year 9 costs nothing. Getting it wrong can cost a resit series and a year. dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: Not every International GCSE subject costs the same to support, because the scarcity of specialists and the amount of technique involved differ. These notes are about where hours convert into marks most efficiently.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The best-supplied subject in the market, so rates sit mid-band rather than at a scarcity premium. Hours convert efficiently because the failure is usually method presentation rather than understanding, and that is teachable in a defined number of sessions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fewer specialists than maths, so expect the upper half of the qualified band. Electricity and mechanics are taught early and compound, which means money spent in Year 10 goes considerably further than the same money in the spring of Year 11.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry concentrate the difficulty into identifiable blocks, which makes short targeted runs unusually cost-effective. A diagnostic that locates the block is worth more than a term of general revision.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume makes this the subject where families most often buy too many hours. The marks are lost in answer structure on longer questions, so a small number of sessions on technique usually beats extended content coverage.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Reduced content across all three sciences, and the classic overspend: families buy separate-science support and pay for topics that have been removed from the award. Confirming the award before booking saves weeks of fees.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Well supplied and mid-band. Progress depends on repeated marked writing, so the cost driver is how much the tutor reads between sessions rather than the session length itself. Ask what marking is included before comparing quotes.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate specification with its own components. Families who book first-language support for a second-language entry pay for material of limited use, which is among the cheapest errors to avoid and the most common to make.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Application and evaluation carry the top band, not definitions. Hours spent on definitions are close to wasted at this level, so a tutor who starts with past-paper evaluation questions is using the budget correctly.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Thinner specialist supply, so rates run higher. The frequent and expensive mistake is booking support for one when the student is entered for the other, since the two specifications share almost nothing in content.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: First language and additional language routes
subjects.description: Compulsory in Dubai private schools, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. Support works from the school's own material, because for the mandatory subjects any different or additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.regionsIntro: What a family in this belt pays depends partly on where they live, because distance determines whether a travel premium applies at all. These notes are about cost rather than character.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Established and relatively accessible, so in-home quotes here sit nearer the middle of the AED 180 to 500 band than the top. Secondary journeys out of the belt still push session times later, which narrows the pool willing to visit.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2 and 3
regions.note: Further along Al Qudra Road and younger in profile. In-home quotes rise with the distance, while the lower demand band suited to Years 7 to 9 makes the premium harder to justify financially.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: Closer to the Al Khail corridor and denser, so visiting tutors quote more competitively here than anywhere else in the belt. The constraint is the evening sports calendar rather than the fee.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Training occupies the hours a visiting tutor would otherwise fill, which pushes requests to weekend mornings. A weekend visit commands the top of the in-home band, where an online weekend session does not.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills and Town Square
regions.note: The longest journeys and therefore the highest travel loading in the belt. This is where the gap between the online and in-home bands is widest, and where it is most clearly paying for a car.

regions.name: Mudon and Remraam
regions.note: Two-sibling evenings are requested from here more than anywhere else. In-home that means either one tutor stretched across two levels or two visit fees; online it means two consecutive slots and no travel loading at all.

sections.heading: The sourced rate card nobody else publishes
paragraphs: Start with the full spread, because a parent cannot judge a quote without it. The figures below come from competitor pages that published them and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table. They are market rates and not IB Gram's prices, and each row names who published it so the claim can be checked rather than taken on trust.

Reading the table from the bottom up is more instructive than from the top down. The cheapest band exists and it is legitimate for the right job. A university student at AED 50 an hour working through number bonds with a Year 7 in Mudon is good value. The same person preparing a Year 11 for an Extended chemistry paper is not, because they have never read the markscheme that decides the grade, and the twenty hours bought at that rate produce less movement than six hours at three times the price.

The in-home row is the one to read most carefully. AED 180 to 500 an hour, travel included, is what the market quotes for a visit. The teaching inside that hour is not systematically better than the teaching in an online hour at AED 150 to 300. The difference is the journey, and in a belt that runs from Arabian Ranches to Town Square the journey is long. That is why the monthly comparison matters more: roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against roughly AED 799 for eight online ones.

One more figure deserves stating because it should be zero. The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Any tutor presenting a licensing or registration cost as a line item in a quote is charging for something that is free.

sections.heading: Four places Dubailand families waste the money
paragraphs: Overspending on tuition in this belt follows a pattern, and all four versions of it are avoidable with information a parent already has or can get in one email. None of them is about being charged too much per hour. All four are about buying the wrong product.

The first is buying volume instead of expertise. Twenty hours at AED 60 feels prudent against six hours at AED 270, and for a Year 8 it probably is. For a Year 11 sitting an Extended paper in eight weeks it is not, because the work at that point is board-specific technique and the cheap tutor is reconstructing the specification from memory. The second is paying the travel premium for a student who does not need physical presence. Below roughly Year 5, and for students with significant attention difficulties, presence does real work. For a fifteen-year-old working on 0580 past papers, the premium buys a drive.

The third is the expensive one. Paying for months of tuition when the problem is the entry tier. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C, and once entries are submitted no quantity of hours changes that. A family spending AED 1,200 a month on a subject where the ceiling is already below the grade they need has bought nothing. The fix costs three or four diagnostic sessions and one conversation with the school, in time.

The fourth is buying support for the wrong specification. Cambridge 0500 First Language English and 0510 Second Language English are different qualifications. Computer Science 0478 and ICT 0417 share almost nothing. Combined and Coordinated Science awards have content removed that separate-science material still covers. Each of those errors costs a term of fees and produces revision that does not match the paper. One email to the examinations officer asking for the board, code and tier prevents all four.

sections.heading: The hourly rate is the wrong unit, so ask what the quote includes
paragraphs: Two tutors quoting AED 250 an hour can be offering substantially different products, and the difference is invisible in the number. The variable is what happens outside the session. One tutor marks a past paper between sessions and arrives with a diagnosis. Another arrives and asks what the student would like to look at. The second is cheaper to deliver and costs the same.

So the questions to ask are specific. Is written work marked between sessions, and how much of it? Is the session length sixty minutes of teaching or fifty-five with setup? Are materials written for the correct syllabus code, or generic? Does the fee cover a short written note to the parent, and does anyone review progress against a starting diagnostic? Is the rate per hour or per lesson, and are those the same thing? Does the quoted figure include VAT, and if the provider cannot say, that is itself informative.

Ask also what happens when a session is missed, because this is where unadvertised costs appear. A cancellation window, a policy on make-up sessions, and whether a package expires are all things a parent should know before paying for a month. Market packages circulate at roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and in both cases the question of what happens to an unused session is worth asking in writing.

On our side the answers are stated rather than implied. The trial lesson is free, requires no card, and is a full session rather than a fifteen-minute introduction. We do not publish an IB Gram rate card on these pages because the right number depends on subject, level and frequency, and a figure quoted before anyone has met the student is marketing rather than information. What we will not do is attach a condition to the word free without saying so on the same screen.

sections.heading: Group classes, tuition centres and the per-student illusion
paragraphs: A group class looks like straightforward arithmetic: divide the tutor's rate by four and the price per student falls. For some purposes that arithmetic holds. For the problem most Dubailand families are actually trying to solve, it does not, and understanding why saves a wasted term.

A group moves at the group's pace. If four Year 11 students share a class and one of them is losing marks on moles while another is losing them on organic mechanisms, the hour addresses at best one of those and the other student is sitting through content they already have. Group teaching is efficient for delivering a syllabus and inefficient for closing a specific deficit, which is precisely what examination-year tutoring is for. Used earlier, in Years 8 and 9, a group class covering breadth is often good value.

Tuition centres with premises in Dubai are a different legal and commercial animal from an individual tutor. A centre needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit is worth asking about, and it is also the reason the phrase approved tutor is used loosely in this market: the permit belongs to the institution, not to a person, and it is not a judgement about teaching quality.

IB Gram does not operate a centre, an office or a branch in the UAE, and holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval or accreditation. We explain what each body does and link to it. A provider claiming an approval it cannot evidence is telling a parent something useful about the reliability of its other claims, including its prices.

sections.heading: Budgeting a full Year 10 to Year 11 run
paragraphs: Most families in this belt do not want a rate, they want a total. The honest way to produce one is to multiply a monthly band by the months, then add the examination-year intensity separately, because the final stretch is where frequency rises. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give the base: AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support.

A two-subject plan running from the start of Year 10 to the June series is roughly eighteen school months, allowing for breaks. At the mid band that is a substantial commitment, and it is worth asking whether both subjects need the whole period. Frequently they do not. One subject may need a diagnostic and a ten-week block in Year 10, with the budget concentrated on the second subject in Year 11. Spreading an identical amount evenly across both for eighteen months is the default and it is rarely optimal.

Context helps a parent judge whether the total is reasonable. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the following academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tuition is therefore the variable cost in a household education budget while fees are not, which argues for deciding the tutoring total deliberately rather than letting it accumulate monthly.

sections.heading: What tuition cannot buy at any price
paragraphs: This section exists because the alternative is a page that implies money solves everything, and that is both untrue and the thing that makes parents distrust tutoring generally. There are outcomes no fee purchases, and saying so is the most useful thing a provider can do for a family deciding how much to spend.

No tutor can guarantee a grade. Not at AED 50 an hour and not at AED 650. Grades depend on the student's work between sessions, on what the papers ask in a particular series, and on where boundaries fall. No provider can promise a grade, a fixed improvement or a refund tied to an outcome, because none of them has a mechanism to keep that promise, and the UAE treats commercial representations seriously. Equally, no statistic should be quoted at a parent without the number of students behind it, the date and the method, which rules out most of the satisfaction and improvement figures displayed in this market.

No tutor may produce assessed work, whatever the fee. One page ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum. That is an academic malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A tutor may teach content, explain what criteria reward, test an approach, read a draft the student wrote and show where it loses marks, and teach referencing properly. A tutor must never draft or rewrite the submission.

And no tutor can undo a closed entry. If a tier caps the grade, the money is better spent on the tier conversation than on hours. Nor is tutoring required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for a UAE university place or for school progression, and any page suggesting otherwise is manufacturing pressure around a regulatory process. The published equivalency requirements are a matter of record, and checking them on moe.gov.ae costs nothing at all.

sections.heading: Why the near-me search produces the wrong price in this belt
paragraphs: Return to the search phrase, because distance and price are the same conversation here. Dubailand is a development zone rather than a neighbourhood, stretching south-east along Al Ain Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and absorbing Arabian Ranches and its successors, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills, Town Square, Mudon and Remraam. Two families both searching from Dubailand addresses can be twenty-five minutes apart.

A tutor pricing a visit to Town Square is pricing eighty minutes of driving attached to a sixty-minute lesson, plus the risk that Al Qudra Road is slow. They have two options: charge the top of the AED 180 to 500 band, or widen their subject range so that the diary fills with whoever is nearby regardless of subject. Most do some of both. The parent therefore pays more and chooses from less, which is the opposite of what a proximity search is supposed to deliver.

Remove the journey and both problems dissolve at once. The rate loses its travel component, so the comparison is with the AED 150 to 300 online band rather than the AED 180 to 500 in-home one. And the match is made on board, syllabus code and tier rather than on who is free and close, which is the variable that actually determines whether the hours convert into marks.

That is the whole of the argument for how IB Gram serves this belt, and it should be stated without overselling it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced Cambridge and Pearson teachers outside the Emirates, which is how a Town Square family reaches a 0620 Extended specialist at all. A parent deserves to know that before paying rather than after.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor near Dubailand actually charge per hour?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai spread runs from AED 45 to AED 650. Budget online provision is AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150. Specialist provision runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. In-home visits are AED 180 to 500 including travel. None of these are IB Gram prices; they are the market, cited so a quote can be checked.

faqs.question: What should I budget per month for Year 11 in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session put specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward per month, against AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 240 to 600 for budget provision. Most Year 11 plans rise above weekly in the final stretch, so the realistic figure sits at the top of that band for a subject that matters. Packages of roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions exist and are worth comparing against the in-home equivalent of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use an online platform than a home tutor around Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: On published figures, yes, and the gap is the journey rather than the teaching. Online qualified provision is quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour against AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel included. Monthly, four two-hour in-home sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 while roughly AED 799 buys eight online sessions. For a young child or a student with significant attention difficulties the in-home premium buys something real. For a Year 10 or 11 student working on past papers, it mostly buys a drive.

faqs.question: Why do tutors quote more to visit Town Square than Motor City?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is longer and the risk of delay is higher. Dubailand stretches south-east along Al Ain Road and Al Qudra Road, so a tutor visiting the far communities is attaching up to eighty minutes of travel to a sixty-minute lesson. They either charge the top of the AED 180 to 500 band or widen their subject range to fill a diary with nearby families regardless of subject. The parent ends up paying more and choosing from less, which is the opposite of what a proximity search is meant to achieve.

faqs.question: Does the tutoring price include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a general fact on these pages because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation, and a tutoring page is not the right source for a tax position. What a provider can and should tell you is whether the figure they have quoted you is inclusive or exclusive, and whether they hold a tax registration number. A provider who cannot answer either question clearly has told you something useful about their invoicing.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor false economy for an Extended tier paper?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and the reason is specific rather than snobbish. At AED 45 to 65 an hour the tutor is typically a generalist or a student who has not read the markscheme that decides the grade. For a Year 8 building number fluency that is fine and good value. For a Year 11 eight weeks from an Extended paper the work is board-specific technique, and twenty hours of general revision moves fewer marks than six hours aimed at measured gaps. Buy the diagnostic first, then decide which band the actual problem needs.

faqs.question: Can group classes save money for my Dubailand Year 10?
faqs.answer: For breadth, yes. For a specific deficit, rarely. A group moves at the group's pace, so if four students are each losing marks somewhere different, the hour addresses at most one of them. Group teaching is efficient at delivering a syllabus and inefficient at closing a gap, which is what examination-year tutoring is for. Used in Years 8 and 9 for coverage it can be good value, and tuition centres running them in Dubai need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is worth asking about.

faqs.question: How much does the tutor's UAE permit add to the price?
faqs.answer: Nothing, and any quote with a licensing line item deserves a question. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no amounts are published.

faqs.question: What is the most expensive mistake families in this belt make?
faqs.answer: Paying for months of tuition in a subject where the entry tier already caps the grade below what the family needs. A Cambridge Core entry leads to grades C to G, and once entries are submitted no quantity of hours changes that. A household spending AED 600 to 1,200 a month against a capped ceiling has bought nothing. Three or four diagnostic sessions and one timely conversation with the school cost a fraction of that and are the only intervention that works, provided they happen before entries close.

faqs.question: Do rates in Dubai rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: Demand does, and availability tightens, which has the same effect on a family's options even where a published rate does not change. The specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and upward is the one that fills first, and the half past five to seven weekday window fills across the whole city at once. Booking a specialist in the autumn for a June series costs the same per hour as booking in March and secures an hour that actually suits the household. That is a scheduling saving rather than a discount, but it is a real one.

faqs.question: What should a quote include besides the teaching hour?
faqs.answer: Marking of written work between sessions and how much of it, whether the session is sixty minutes of teaching or fifty-five with setup, whether materials are written for the correct syllabus code or generic, whether a note to the parent is included, the cancellation window, whether unused sessions in a package expire, and whether VAT is inside the figure. Two tutors quoting the same hourly rate often sell different products, and the difference lives entirely in that list rather than in the number.

faqs.question: Can anybody guarantee my child a grade for the money?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering one is making a promise with no mechanism behind it. Grades depend on work between sessions, on what a particular series asks and on where boundaries fall. We publish no grade guarantee, no improvement guarantee and no refund tied to an outcome. We also publish no satisfaction or results statistic, because any such figure needs the number of students, the date and the method stated alongside it, and most of the figures displayed in this market carry none of those three.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should we actually pay to support?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with, and concentrated rather than spread. A common pattern that wastes money is weekly support in four subjects at a mid rate for eighteen months. A better pattern is a diagnostic across all four, then a ten-week block in whichever one or two are actually losing marks, with the budget held back for the examination year in the subject that matters most. Note separately that Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education.

faqs.question: Is the free trial lesson really free in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Yes: a full session, no card, no condition attached and nothing to cancel afterwards. We are deliberate about this because the word free is used loosely in this market, and attaching an unstated condition to it is a consumer-protection problem as well as a trust one. Where any condition does apply to something described as free, it belongs on the same screen as the word. Use the trial as a diagnostic rather than a sales meeting: the test is whether the tutor can name the skill costing marks by the end of the hour.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.closingHeading: Decide what you are buying before you compare rates
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.closingBody: An IGCSE tutor near me in Dubailand is a question about distance, and distance is the part of the price that does the least for your child. intro.heading: The syllabus code decides everything a tutor should be doing
paragraphs: Two Year 11 students in neighbouring Emaar Beachfront towers can both be studying "IGCSE Chemistry" and be sitting different examinations. One is entered for Cambridge 0620 at Extended tier with the Alternative to Practical paper. The other is on Pearson 4CH1, where practical skills are assessed inside the written papers. They need different past papers, different formula familiarity, different practical write-up conventions and different revision order. A tutor who works from the subject name instead of the code will teach one of them for the other's examination.

This matters more than it should because almost nothing in the market names a code. Across the seven competitor area pages researched for this project, exactly one syllabus code appeared anywhere. Parents are therefore sold "IGCSE Maths tutoring" and reasonably assume it is a single thing. It is not. Cambridge 0580 is tiered into Core and Extended with different paper pairs and different grade ceilings. Edexcel 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher. Additional Mathematics 0606 is a separate qualification taken alongside, and a student insecure on 0580 algebra will drown in it.

The second thing a proximity search cannot give you is command-term literacy. Every IGCSE question opens with an instruction that sets the ceiling for the answer. State, describe, explain, calculate, suggest and evaluate each demand something specific, and the commonest avoidable loss at this level is a student answering a cheaper instruction than the one printed. That is a habit, not a knowledge gap, and it is repaired in two or three sessions once someone names it. No amount of re-teaching the topic fixes it.

Emaar Beachfront's geography makes the local-tutor route harder than the search results suggest. The peninsula has one road link, no school and no tuition centre inside it, and visitor parking that needs a resident to clear basement access. A tutor travelling here spends roughly two and a quarter hours to deliver one, in the window when the whole cluster is moving. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

The rest of this page is the subject detail. Which papers each tier produces, by code. Where marks actually leak in 0580 Maths and in the three separate sciences. The difference between the separate-science route and the Combined and Coordinated awards, which is not simply a matter of less content. Which English syllabus your child is sitting, since that changes the paper entirely. The command terms with what each one requires. And the way past papers should be used, which is not the way most students use them.

One caution before the detail. Boards revise syllabuses on a cycle, and a page written once is not a substitute for the current specification. Everything here should be checked against the syllabus document your child's school is working from, which the exams officer can name in a sentence. What this page can do is tell you which questions to ask and what the answers mean, which is more than a list of tutors sorted by how close they live to the causeway.

sections.heading: Why "IGCSE tutor near me" is not specific enough to buy
paragraphs: The search assumes IGCSE is one thing. It is a family of separately coded qualifications from at least two major boards, tiered, with different paper structures and different practical arrangements. The first question any competent tutor asks is which code and which tier, and the first question a proximity-ranked list cannot answer is whether anyone on it has taught that code. For a widely entered subject at the lower tier, the distinction is survivable. For 0620 Extended, 0625 Extended or 0606, it is the whole job.

The second assumption is that the problem is the subject. Usually it is a component or a habit. A student scoring 58 on a Cambridge Extended paper may be losing twelve marks to unshown method, eight to misread command terms, six to rounding instructions ignored, and only four to content they genuinely do not know. Those four marks are the only ones that need teaching. The other twenty-six need a fortnight of disciplined answer construction, which is cheaper and faster and almost never what is sold.

That diagnosis needs a marked script, which is why we ask for one before matching anyone. A reported grade tells you the student is at a 5. The script tells you which of the four problems above produced the 5, and therefore how many sessions it will take and what kind of tutor it needs. Families who send scripts get a breakdown in the trial lesson; families who send grades spend the first hour reconstructing what the script would have shown in ten minutes.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: different papers, different ceilings
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers most of its IGCSE subjects. Core candidates sit one pair of papers and the highest grade available to them is a C. Extended candidates sit a different pair and can reach A*. Edexcel tiers as Foundation and Higher on the same principle. This is not a difficulty setting applied to one examination; the papers are different documents, and a Core candidate practising Extended papers is working above the ceiling they will be marked against while missing the question styles they will actually face.

The tier decision is taken by the school, usually in Year 10, on evidence it already holds. Once final entries are filed it stops being a live decision. That timing has a consequence families rarely appreciate: tutoring started after the entry deadline cannot change the ceiling, and for a student entered at Core who is capable of Extended, the ceiling is the single largest improvement available. Starting in Year 10, while the decision is still open and can be supported with real evidence, is worth more per dirham than any amount of Year 11 rescue work.

There is an honest case for Core as well. A student who will not reach a C on Extended papers is better served by a tier where the questions are accessible and the grade is secure, because a bare pass on the harder tier and a comfortable grade on the easier one are not equivalent on a transcript. The error is not choosing Core; it is choosing it on thin evidence, early, and never revisiting it. Ask the school what evidence the decision rests on, and ask in Year 10.

sections.heading: Mathematics 0580 and 4MA1: where the marks actually go
paragraphs: At Extended tier the losses cluster in four places and none of them is the hardest topic on the syllabus. First, unshown method: a correct final answer with no intermediate line collects a fraction of the marks allocated, and students who do the algebra mentally are penalised for competence. Second, rounding and accuracy instructions printed in the question and then ignored. Third, units, particularly in area, volume, speed and compound measure questions. Fourth, the structured multi-part question where part (a) is wrong and every subsequent part inherits the error.

The fourth is the most expensive and the most fixable. Examiners allow follow-through credit in many schemes, but only when the method is visible. A student who shows the working carries marks forward from a wrong start; a student who does not loses the whole question to one arithmetic slip in part (a). Teaching a student to show method is not teaching them mathematics, which is why class teachers often cannot prioritise it and why a fortnight of focused work on it moves a grade.

The board difference matters here too. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 ask similar mathematics in different phrasing, with different formula support and different conventions about how much working a mark scheme expects. A student practising the wrong board's papers for six months arrives in the exam reading unfamiliar question structures under time pressure, and loses minutes before losing marks. Confirm the code with the school, then practise only from that board.

sections.heading: Separate sciences, Coordinated or Combined: choosing the route
paragraphs: Cambridge offers the sciences three ways and the choice has consequences beyond workload. Separate Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and Biology 0610 produce three grades and the deepest preparation for A Level or Diploma sciences. Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award covering all three in reduced depth and producing two grades. Combined Science 0653 is a single award producing one. For a student intending to take a science at Higher Level or A Level, the separate route is usually the better preparation; for a student who needs the science requirement and has stronger subjects elsewhere, it is a poor use of two years.

The trap is assuming the combined routes are a subset of the separate ones. They are a distinct selection of content, chosen for coherence across the three disciplines, and some separate-syllabus topics are absent while some combined-syllabus treatments differ. A student on 0654 revising from 0620 resources covers material they will not be examined on and misses material they will. This happens constantly, because separate-science resources are more plentiful online and nobody checks the code.

The practical arrangement differs by route as well, and within Cambridge by school choice: a practical test paper or the alternative-to-practical paper, decided by the centre. The alternative paper is still a practical examination; it tests apparatus choice, sources of error, how to read a scale and what a results table needs, from a written stimulus. That is entirely teachable online, which is worth saying because families assume a practical component rules out remote preparation.

sections.heading: Which English examination is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: English causes more confusion than any other IGCSE subject because the codes describe genuinely different examinations. First Language English, coded 0500 or 0990 depending on the grading scale, assesses reading response, directed writing and composition for students using English as their primary academic language. English as a Second Language, coded 0510 or 0511 depending on how speaking is treated, assesses reading, writing and listening for students for whom English is an additional language. A student can be moved between them mid-course, and their past-paper practice must move with them.

The losses differ by syllabus. On First Language reading, students retell the passage instead of selecting from it, and lose marks for summarising what was asked to be analysed. On directed writing, register drift is the main cost: a student writes a letter that becomes an essay halfway through. On Second Language papers, the listening component rewards a specific discipline about reading the question before the audio plays, which is practised rather than known.

Composition is the component families most often believe is unteachable, and it is the most teachable of all. Structure, paragraph purpose, controlled variation in sentence length and a planned ending are mechanical and improvable. Students who produce fluent but shapeless writing gain more from four sessions on structure than from a term of reading. Confirm which code your child sits before buying any resource, because a 0500 workbook will not prepare a 0510 candidate for the paper they face.

sections.heading: Command terms at IGCSE: the ceiling on every answer
paragraphs: Every question opens with an instruction and that instruction sets the maximum. State and name want recall. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants why, with a mechanism. Suggest wants a plausible answer applied to an unfamiliar context and is where strong students stall, because they want the certainty the word does not require. Calculate wants working. Evaluate wants a judgement with both sides. A student answering describe when explain was printed has written a correct answer to a question that was not asked.

The repair is fast because it is procedural. Take a dozen past questions from the right board, underline the command term in each, write what that term demands before writing any content, then compare the answer against the structure of the mark scheme rather than its exact wording. Three sessions of this changes the shape of every answer a student writes for the rest of the course. It is the highest-return work available at IGCSE and it is rarely requested, because it looks like technique rather than teaching.

It matters particularly for students arriving from a different system. A student who came from a curriculum that rewarded complete, thorough answers will write complete, thorough answers to state and lose nothing but time, then write the same thorough answer to evaluate and lose the judgement marks. Families in this cluster include many mid-course arrivals, and the first term's disappointing results are usually command-term losses rather than content gaps.

sections.heading: Past papers, grade boundaries and honest self-marking
paragraphs: Most students treat past papers as a quiz: work through, check answers, feel reassured. That produces familiarity and little mark movement, because the step that creates improvement is marking against the official scheme and understanding why it awarded what it did. A student who can predict their own total to within a few marks has internalised the examiner's logic. A student who cannot is guessing, and will guess in the exam too.

Grade boundaries are the other thing families misread. Boundaries move between series and between tiers, because they are set after the papers are marked to reflect their difficulty. A student aiming at a specific grade should be working to a comfortable margin above last series' boundary rather than to the boundary itself, and should understand that a mark two below a boundary is not a near miss in any sense that affects the certificate. We explain how boundaries work in principle; we do not reproduce or publish boundary tables, and nor should any tutoring site.

Official papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents should come from your child's school or the board's own channels. We reference and explain them in sessions. We do not supply them as downloads, because board material is copyrighted and, for unreleased material, redistributing it exposes a student to a malpractice finding. Ask the subject teacher first; most schools release recent papers and schemes on request for exactly this purpose.

One practical note on logistics. Keep the marked scripts. Parents throw them away after a parents' evening, and they are the only record of how a particular student loses marks rather than how many. A folder of four marked papers across a year is the most useful document any new tutor can be handed, and it is the difference between a first session spent diagnosing and a first session spent asking questions whose answers were already written down.

sections.heading: Booking a code-matched tutor from the peninsula
paragraphs: Send four things: the subject list with board and syllabus code, the tier for each, the marked mock script where the school will release it, and the hours that genuinely exist after a school run that starts before 07:00. Of those, the code and the script do the most work. The code determines which tutor and which question style; the script determines how many sessions and what kind of work. Everything else is scheduling.

We match one tutor per subject and propose slots in Gulf Standard Time. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, used to produce a breakdown of lost marks by type rather than a sales conversation. If the match is wrong after the trial or in week two, we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist with it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with a shared working page the student keeps, and we do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE.

The limits, stated plainly. We cannot promise a grade and no tutor who has marked a paper would. An Extended-tier specialist at a popular twice-weekly evening hour is sometimes unavailable that week, and we will say so and offer the realistic alternatives rather than fill the slot with a generalist. And code-level work needs the student writing between sessions: an hour a week can direct the other six, and cannot replace them.

Finally, a word on expectations between sessions. The student does the writing. An hour a week can tell them which six hours to spend and how to spend them, and it cannot be those six hours. Families who treat the weekly slot as the whole of the work see the smallest movement, and families who treat it as the steering see the most. That is true of every tutor in this market, ours included, and it is worth saying before you pay anybody.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE syllabus code my child in Emaar Beachfront is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer rather than the subject teacher, and ask in writing. The entry confirmation lists the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, which is the only document that settles it. Report cards show subject names and tell you nothing about the examination. Families in this cluster regularly discover in the spring that months of revision used another board's papers, and that is an administrative failure rather than a student one. Keep the list somewhere the whole household can see it.

faqs.question: What is the highest grade available on the Cambridge Core tier?
faqs.answer: A C. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above a C however well they perform. Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach A*. Edexcel applies the same principle through Foundation and Higher tiers. This is why the tier decision is more consequential than any individual topic: it sets the ceiling before any revision begins. The decision sits with the school, usually made in Year 10 on evidence it already holds, and it closes when final entries are filed.

faqs.question: Can we move our child from Core to Extended in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Only before final entries are filed, and only with the school's agreement. After the entry deadline the tier is fixed for that series. If you believe your child is capable of Extended, the conversation to have is in Year 10 and it should be evidence-led: ask what the decision rests on, and offer a full Extended paper sat under timed conditions as additional evidence. That is the single largest improvement available to a capable student placed on the lower tier, and it expires on a date.

faqs.question: Is Coordinated Sciences 0654 just a shorter version of the three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: No, and the assumption costs marks. 0654 is a distinct selection of content chosen for coherence across chemistry, physics and biology, so some separate-syllabus topics are absent and some treatments differ. A student on 0654 revising from 0620 or 0625 resources covers material they will not be examined on and misses material they will. It happens often because separate-science resources are easier to find online. Revise from resources matched to the code on the entry confirmation.

faqs.question: Is 0606 worth adding for a Beachfront student heading to A Level Maths?
faqs.answer: Only if the 0580 Extended algebra is already secure. 0606 front-loads calculus and trigonometry and assumes complete fluency in everything 0580 covers, so a student still consolidating algebraic manipulation is being asked to learn two things at once under exam pressure. For a student heading to A Level Maths or Maths AA at Higher Level it is excellent preparation. For a student at a borderline Extended grade it is the commonest overreach we see in this cluster.

faqs.question: How is the practical component assessed if my child studies with an online tutor?
faqs.answer: The practical component happens at school, under conditions the centre sets within the board's rules. Cambridge sciences use either a practical test paper or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the centre chooses. The alternative paper is still a practical examination: it tests apparatus choice, sources of error, reading a scale, and what a results table needs, all from written stimulus. That is entirely teachable over video, so a practical component does not rule out remote preparation the way families assume.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when the final answer is correct?
faqs.answer: Because method marks are awarded for visible working, and follow-through credit on a multi-part question only applies when the examiner can see the route. A student who does the algebra mentally and writes one line is penalised for competence: one arithmetic slip in part (a) then loses the whole question instead of one mark. Teaching a student to show method is not teaching mathematics, which is why class teachers rarely prioritise it, and why a fortnight on it reliably moves a grade.

faqs.question: Which command term causes the most trouble at this level?
faqs.answer: Suggest, followed by explain. Suggest asks for a plausible answer applied to an unfamiliar context, and strong students stall on it because they want a certainty the word does not require, so they restate a textbook fact and collect nothing for application. Explain asks for a mechanism, and students substitute a fuller description, which caps the answer below the top band. Three sessions spent sorting past questions by command term changes the shape of every answer written afterwards.

faqs.question: What is the difference between First Language English and English as a Second Language?
faqs.answer: They are different examinations, not difficulty levels. First Language English, coded 0500 or 0990 depending on grading scale, assesses reading response, directed writing and composition for students using English as their main academic language. English as a Second Language, 0510 or 0511 depending on the speaking element, assesses reading, writing and listening for additional-language learners. A student moved between them mid-course needs their practice material changed with them, which is frequently overlooked.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us what grade boundary to aim for?
faqs.answer: A tutor can explain how boundaries work and why aiming at one is a mistake. Boundaries are set after each series is marked, to reflect how the papers performed, so they move. A student targeting a grade should be working to a comfortable margin above the previous series' boundary rather than to the boundary itself. We explain the mechanism and we do not reproduce boundary tables; those come from the board or the school, and a tutoring site republishing them is not a reliable source.

faqs.question: Where should we get past papers from?
faqs.answer: From your child's school or the board's own channels. Most schools will release recent papers and mark schemes on request because that is what they are for. We reference and explain them in sessions and do not supply them as downloads: board material is copyrighted, and redistributing unreleased material creates a malpractice exposure for the student rather than for the site hosting it. Any service offering a complete archive as free downloads should make you ask where it came from.

faqs.question: My child is strong in class and weak on paper. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always answer construction rather than knowledge. The pattern is recognisable in a marked script: content present, command term misread, method invisible, rounding instruction ignored, last question unattempted because of timing. None of that is addressed by re-teaching topics, which is what gets sold. Four sessions on command terms and method discipline, plus two paper audits, usually moves this student more than a term of subject revision, and costs considerably less.

faqs.question: How soon can an online session start from a Beachfront tower?
faqs.answer: For a widely entered subject at the lower tier, usually within a few days, because the only variable is matching a free hour. For an Extended-tier science specialist at a popular 17:30 slot it takes longer, and occasionally a particular code and tier combination has nobody free that week. We would rather give you a date we can hold. The first fixed point is the trial lesson; the weekly slot is agreed immediately after it, in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to apartments on this peninsula?
faqs.answer: Not ours. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Independent tutors in Dubai do travel to Beachfront addresses, and market sources quote AED 180 to 500 an hour for in-home one-to-one with travel included. On a peninsula with one road link and escorted basement parking, that premium buys presence and costs reliability across a sixteen-session Year 11 block.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emaar-beach.closingHeading: Send us the code, the tier and the script
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emaar-beach.closingBody: IGCSE is not one qualification and a tutor who works from the subject name is guessing at which examination your child sits. We will match a tutor to the code, propose a slot in Gulf Standard Time, and open with a written breakdown of where the marks are going. One free trial lesson per student, no card required.

intro.heading: Nearby is a purchase, and from Emaar South it is a dear one
paragraphs: A near-me search feels like a search for convenience. From Emaar South it is a search for somebody willing to drive twenty-five to forty-five minutes each way, through end-of-working-day traffic, to the southern edge of Dubai, for one lesson. Nobody does that for free. It is priced into the hour, and the published bands show how much: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is included, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online.

That is the first cost this page puts a number on. The second is less visible and usually larger: the cost of a wrong diagnosis. A family who buys a term of weekly sessions without anybody reading a marked script has spent twelve to fifteen hours at whatever rate they agreed, and the script at the end of it looks like the script at the start. That is not a cheap mistake disguised as an expensive one. It is the single most expensive thing in this market, and it is free to avoid.

The third is the set of costs nobody budgets for at the beginning of Year 10. Examination entry where a candidate sits privately. A remark request after results. A November resit entry, which means paying twice for one grade. Materials, where a provider offers to supply them, which raises a separate question this page answers directly. None of these is large on its own and together they change what a two-year plan actually costs.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, so the travel premium in those published in-home bands is not part of what you pay here. Emaar South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script and the official mark scheme shared on screen. Saying so plainly belongs on a cost page, because what is not on offer is part of the price comparison.

What this page does not contain is an IB Gram rate. That is deliberate rather than evasive, and it is a different position from the three of six most visible providers in this market who publish no price at all while also declining to explain why. Our conversation starts with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis, because a number quoted before anybody has looked at a marked script is an answer to a question nobody has asked yet.

One regulatory note that is also a cost note. Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, which means no legitimate tutor can present it as a cost passed on to you. KHDA oversees Dubai's private schools and does not accredit tutors; IB Gram holds no KHDA approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre.
