dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emaar-south.programmesIntro: Three stages, three very different cost profiles, and Emaar South households are usually buying at one of them without having compared the three.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: Nothing is externally examined, which makes this the cheapest point at which anything can be fixed. A gap in algebraic fluency or structured writing closed in Year 8 takes a term of weekly sessions with no deadline pressure. The same gap in Year 11 takes an intensive block at a specialist rate and still leaves the student behind on content arriving at the same time.
programmes.countryNote: Emaar South's age profile skews young, so a large share of households here are at exactly the stage where the cheap intervention exists. Almost none take it, because nothing is visibly wrong yet. That is the clearest available arbitrage in this market and it goes unexercised every year.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, externally examined, with an entry tier that caps the achievable grade. Most of the money in this market is spent here and most of the waste happens here too, because families buy parallel arrangements in two or three subjects without a diagnosis in any of them.
programmes.countryNote: An Emaar South candidate carries a long daily journey alongside this workload, which limits how many weekly sessions a plan can hold. That constraint is useful rather than unfortunate: it forces the question of which subject genuinely repays the money instead of permitting three half-funded arrangements.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma
programmes.description: Where the money gets more expensive. Bestimate's monthly estimates put specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more against AED 600-1,200 mid-market, so a decision at sixteen that forces remedial work at eighteen is costly twice over. Tier and award choices at IGCSE can do exactly that.
programmes.countryNote: For a family budgeting across both stages from Emaar South, money spent correctly at IGCSE reduces what has to be spent after sixteen rather than sitting alongside it. A combined science award or a Core tier entry that fails a sixth-form requirement is the clearest example of a saving that turns into a larger bill.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB route for the same ages, marked against four criteria per subject from A to D and converted to a 1-7 grade. The cost logic differs completely: the best-value purchase is a short block teaching the criteria explicitly, which improves every subject at once instead of one.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools Emaar South families travel to run the Middle Years Programme rather than IGCSE, so a parent comparing what a neighbour spends should first check whether the neighbour's child is in the same system at all. The sensible spend is not merely different in size but different in shape.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emaar-south.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Emaar South families pay for, annotated by what a session in each one is actually buying.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: The best return per hour in this market, because the faults are specific, visible on a script and improvable within a term. What caps the return is the entry tier, so a Year 10 pound spent producing timed higher-tier evidence is worth more than a Year 11 pound spent revising inside a fixed ceiling.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The same return, with one way to lose all of it: a tutor working from Cambridge past papers. The syllabuses differ in structure and question style, so the money buys correct mathematics aimed at a paper the student will not sit. Checking the code costs nothing.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Good value, and the cheapest gains sit in Paper 6, the alternative to practical, whose question types repeat across series and which almost nobody drills. Four sessions of technique there frequently beats a term of content sessions for a student who already understands the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, qualitative analysis and charge balancing are procedural, which makes them cheap to repair in a compressed block once a script has named them. Broad content revision in chemistry is among the least efficient purchases on this list.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The dominant task is compressing a large recall load into usable notes, and that is work the student does alone. The efficient purchase is a short block teaching the method, then independent work, rather than a standing weekly session paying somebody to witness revision.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the summary question are structural and improve fast, which makes a narrow block good value. General reading practice is the classic expensive non-purchase here: it feels productive, costs the same per hour, and moves nothing measurable.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Analysis and evaluation command words carry the highest tariff and are reliably where candidates stop short, and the break-even, cash flow and ratio calculations are available marks. A block aimed at those two things beats working through the textbook at the same hourly rate.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram drill and elasticity calculation are short, cheap and high-yield, and an unlabelled axis loses the mark whatever the prose says. Paying for wider reading in economics is paying for something the student can do with a library card.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are procedural and under-practised, so a short block is excellent value. The specialist pool is thinner than for the sciences, which means booking early matters more here than price comparison does.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: Confirm the route before paying anything. Past papers from the separate sciences are not usable for a combined candidate, so a tutor given the wrong one sets content that is not on the syllabus. That is a full term of fees for no gain and it happens regularly.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules, and often the grade a family worries about most. The writing component responds quickly to a small bank of drilled structures, which makes it unusually good value per session.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A separate syllabus covering calculus and further trigonometry beyond 0580, which needs its own slot rather than being folded into a maths hour. Budget it as an additional subject, because treating it as a free extension of one is how a plan quietly runs short of time.

sections.heading: The proximity premium, quantified from this address
paragraphs: Begin with what nearby costs, since that is what the search asked for. The published Dubai bands separate cleanly by whether anybody drives. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced into the hour.

From Emaar South the premium sits at the upper end of that spread rather than the middle, for a reason that is purely geographical. A tutor reaching this community is making the same journey the child made, in the same traffic, and committing roughly ninety minutes of unpaid travel around a sixty-minute lesson. A provider who does not price that in does not come, and a provider who does is charging for it whether or not the invoice itemises it.

The monthly packages published in this market express the same thing more starkly than the hourly rates do. AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions. AED 1,599-1,799 a month buys four in-home sessions of two hours. That is roughly double the money for half the number of sessions, and the difference is not teaching. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give the wider frame: AED 240-600 for budget provision, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

The premium also buys a constraint that never appears on a rate card. A tutor who has allocated ninety minutes of travel to your address can fit one session that evening, which means you take the slot their route allows rather than the slot your child can work in, a sibling pair becomes awkward, a two-subject plan becomes impractical, and a cancellation is hard to rearrange because the whole evening was yours. sections.heading: What a wrong diagnosis costs, priced out
paragraphs: This is the largest number on the page and no provider puts it on one. Take a family who buys a standing weekly session in mathematics at the mid-market band, Bestimate's AED 600-1,200 a month, for a full term. Nobody read a marked script before it started, so the tutor began where tutors begin, at the top of the syllabus, and worked forward. Twelve to fifteen hours later something feels calmer and the next mock returns the same grade.

The money is gone and so is the term, which is the part that cannot be bought back. An IGCSE candidate has roughly six usable terms between the start of Year 10 and the June series of Year 11, and one of them has now been spent confirming that the student can follow an explanation. Meanwhile the actual fault, which might have been pacing, or command words, or a results table convention on Paper 6, has gone unnamed and will reappear in the examination.

The variant that costs even more is a board mismatch. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are separate syllabuses with different paper structures; 0625 and 4PH1 likewise; and separate-science past papers are unusable for a combined-award candidate. A tutor set to work on the wrong one teaches accurate material towards a paper the student will never sit, at full rate, for as long as nobody checks. The check is a glance at the timetable and takes under a minute.

Both failures are prevented by the same free action: send a marked script and ask what the first session will target. If the answer names a component and a technique, a diagnosis has happened. If it names a topic or describes an approach, it has not. That one question is worth more than any amount of price comparison, because it distinguishes between buying hours and buying a result.

sections.heading: Cost per mark instead of cost per hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how this market quotes and they are the wrong unit for a decision. The useful question is what a block of sessions is likely to move, and that varies enormously by what the block is aimed at. Four sessions on Paper 6 technique for a Cambridge science candidate addresses a component whose question types repeat across series and which the student has almost certainly never drilled. Four sessions re-explaining the particle model addresses something they already know.

The same logic sorts the rest of the timetable. A block on command-word discipline pays into every science and maths subject at once, because the fault appears in all of them simultaneously, so four sessions can affect three grades. A block on the supplied formula list costs one session and prevents a candidate deriving something that was printed on page two of their own examination paper. A block on reverse percentage and ratio addresses topics examined reliably on both boards and practised far below their mark value.

Against those, consider what broad content revision buys. It is the default purchase, it is comfortable for everyone involved, and for a student whose content is broadly present it moves very little, because the marks are not being lost where the hours are being spent. The hourly rate for those two blocks is identical. The cost per mark is not comparable.

This framing also answers the question of when to stop, which an hourly framing never does. A block aimed at a named component ends when a timed section shows the component is no longer losing marks. A standing weekly arrangement aimed at a subject has no natural end, which is why it continues, and continuing past a closed diagnosis is the quietest way several thousand dirhams leave a family's account in this market.

sections.heading: The costs nobody budgets for in Year 10
paragraphs: A two-year IGCSE plan has costs beyond sessions, and they arrive at moments when a family has no appetite for another decision. The first is examination entry. Where a school enters a candidate, entry is handled through the school as the examination centre and sits inside the fee structure. Where a student sits as a private candidate, which happens for a resit or an extra subject, entry is a separate arrangement with its own cost and its own earlier deadline.

The second is a remark. A remark request runs through the school after results, has a published deadline shortly afterwards, and can move a grade down as well as up. It is reasonable to request where a grade sits a mark or two below a boundary that matters for a sixth-form place or an equivalency requirement, and it is a cost with no refund if the grade holds. The decision window is days rather than weeks, which is why it belongs in a plan rather than in a panic.

The third is the November resit, which means paying twice for one grade: the original entry, the original preparation, then a fresh entry and an autumn block. It is often the right call, particularly where a Core tier ceiling was discovered in June, but it should be entered as a deliberate purchase. A resit decided in August with a term ahead costs the same entry fee and buys far more preparation than one decided in October with six weeks left.

The fourth is materials, and it deserves a direct answer because providers offer them. Nobody should sell you IGCSE past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables or syllabus documents. Those are copyright material belonging to Cambridge or Pearson, and a legitimate tutor references and links to the official sources rather than reselling them. If a provider's package includes a fee for supplied papers, that is worth questioning rather than valuing.

sections.heading: Why no provider should be selling you past papers
paragraphs: This is a small point with a large signal attached. IGCSE past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables and syllabus documents are published by Cambridge and Pearson and are their copyright material. A tutoring provider that reproduces them in a bundle, hosts them behind a paywall or includes a materials fee for supplying them is distributing somebody else's work, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well.

The legitimate practice is straightforward. A tutor references the official document, links to the board's own page, and works from what the student has lawfully received through their school. Mark schemes for released papers are published by the boards and a tutor can show a student where to find them. That is both the correct position and the more useful one, because a student who knows where the official mark scheme lives can use it after the sessions end.

For a family pricing providers, the practical use of this point is as a filter. A package quote that itemises supplied materials is telling you something about how the provider treats rules generally, which is relevant information when the same provider will later be giving advice about internal assessment boundaries and academic honesty. The same instinct that bundles copyright papers tends to produce other shortcuts.

The adjacent version of this is worth naming too, because it is the most serious thing in this market. One page ranking in this cluster sells completed Internal Assessments. That is malpractice under the rules of the relevant programme, the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller, and no price makes it a reasonable purchase. A provider offering finished coursework should be declined on that basis alone, whatever their session rate looks like.

sections.heading: Allocating a two-year budget rather than spreading it
paragraphs: A family with a fixed amount to spend across Years 10 and 11 does better allocating it deliberately than committing to a flat weekly arrangement. The shape that works puts money early where it changes a ceiling, concentrates it around the mock, and holds some back for the autumn after results in case a resit is the right call.

Year 10 is where a pound moves a ceiling. A term of weekly work ending in a timed higher-tier paper, marked against the official scheme, produces evidence a subject lead can act on while the entry deadline is still open. After the entry closes, the same term of work buys revision inside a fixed cap, which is worth having and worth less. Very few families in this market spend in Year 10, and the ones who do get a different product for the same money.

The middle of the budget belongs to the eight-week block after the mock, which is sixteen sessions aimed by the mock script rather than by the syllabus. That is the honest unit for comparing providers, and it is also the point at which a family has the most information and the least time, which is exactly when a defined block with fortnightly checkpoints outperforms an open arrangement.

The reserve matters and almost nobody holds one. If a June grade lands below what a sixth-form place or an equivalency requirement needs, the decision has to be made in the days after August results, the resit entry goes through the school months before the November papers, and the autumn block has to be paid for. A family who has spent everything by May has no capacity for the one purchase that can still change the outcome. The table sets out the allocation.

sections.heading: What free has to mean, and what to ask before paying
paragraphs: The word free appears across this market with conditions attached somewhere out of sight: a card required, a minimum commitment triggered, a trial that is really a sales call with a student in the room. If free is used, the condition belongs on the same screen as the word. Ours has none: one full session, no card, taught by the tutor who would take the block, and no obligation at the end of it.

The test of whether a trial is genuine is whether you receive something in writing afterwards that you could hand to a different tutor and have it be useful. A written diagnosis naming the component faults in priority order passes that test. Enthusiasm does not. Sometimes our honest output is that four sessions will do rather than a term, which costs us money and is the correct answer.

Then there is a short list of questions worth asking any provider before money moves, and each has a definite answer in one sentence. Which syllabus code have you taught, and at what tier. What will the first session target, where a component is the right answer and a topic is the wrong one. Is the quoted number the number I will pay, including any tax treatment. What happens if the match is wrong in week two. What do I receive in writing after each session. Is the price per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson.

Two more belong on the list from this community specifically. What weekday slots exist after 17:00, because a provider with nothing late cannot serve an Emaar South school run, and an early slot agreed in optimism is the commonest reason an arrangement here quietly stops. And does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, so there is no legitimate reason not to hold one and no basis for it appearing as a cost.

sections.heading: Where this leaves a household at the southern edge of Dubai
paragraphs: Pulling the numbers together, the position for an Emaar South family is reasonably clear. Insisting on proximity costs the top of the in-home band, roughly AED 180-500 an hour on published figures against AED 150-300 online, plus a one-session-per-evening constraint that makes a sibling pair or a two-subject plan awkward. What it buys is physical presence, which is worth paying for at primary age and worth considerably less for a Year 11 candidate working through a marked script.

Buying without a diagnosis costs a term, and a term is the scarce resource rather than the money. Buying at the budget band for a technique fault costs the same term with a smaller invoice attached. Buying three parallel subjects in a household with a forty-minute school run costs three subjects' worth of fees and generally collapses around half term, which is why sequencing is both cheaper and better.

What works, on the published numbers and on the structure of the qualification, is a small number of defined purchases placed deliberately. Four diagnostic sessions first. A technique block that pays into several subjects. Year 10 money spent producing timed higher-tier evidence while a ceiling can still move. Sixteen sessions after the mock, aimed by the script. A reserve held for the autumn in case a resit is the right call. And nothing bought open-ended.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the travel premium is not part of what you pay here, and there is no rate on this page because the diagnosis comes first. Every AED figure above is published by the provider named and can be checked, which in a cluster where three of six visible providers publish no price at all is a low bar that most of this market does not clear. That is the honest summary, and it is the one we would want if we were the ones paying.

faqs.question: Does living in Emaar South make a tutor more expensive?
faqs.answer: If the tutor travels, yes, and measurably. Published Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. From the southern edge of the emirate the quote sits at the upper end of that spread, because a tutor is absorbing a twenty-five to forty-five minute journey each way. Online delivery removes the premium entirely, since nobody drives.

faqs.question: What is the most expensive mistake an Emaar South family can make?
faqs.answer: Buying a term of sessions before anybody has read a marked script. The money matters less than the term: an IGCSE candidate has roughly six usable terms between the start of Year 10 and the June series, and one spent confirming that a student can follow an explanation is one that cannot be recovered. The actual fault, which might be pacing, command words or a Paper 6 convention, goes unnamed and reappears in the examination. Sending a script first costs nothing.

faqs.question: How do I compare providers when nobody quotes the same way?
faqs.answer: Compare blocks rather than hours. Two sessions a week for eight weeks is sixteen sessions, and that is a unit every provider can price, which makes it the honest basis for comparison. An hourly rate tells you nothing about what a plan costs end to end, nor about what it is aimed at. Then ask what the first session will target: a component and a technique is a real answer, a topic or an approach is not, and that distinction matters more than a few dirhams either way.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 6 cheaper to fix than a whole science syllabus?
faqs.answer: Because its question types repeat across series and almost no candidate has drilled them. The alternative to practical paper asks students to identify variables, read instruments, complete results tables with correct headings and units, plot and interpret graphs, and suggest improvements addressing a named error. Those are learnable conventions, marked independently of whether the student understands the experiment. Four sessions can affect three science grades at once, at the same hourly rate as four sessions of broad revision that affect none.

faqs.question: Should I pay for a remark after IGCSE results?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the margin and on what the grade is needed for. A remark runs through the school as the examination centre, has a published deadline shortly after results, costs a fee with no refund if the grade holds, and can move a grade down as well as up. It is reasonable where a grade sits a mark or two below a boundary that matters for a sixth-form place or an equivalency requirement, and generally not worth it where the grade is several marks clear of one. Decide within days, not weeks.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth paying for twice?
faqs.answer: Often, and it should be a deliberate purchase rather than a reaction. The resit means a fresh entry through the school plus an autumn preparation block, on top of what the first attempt cost. Where a Core or Foundation tier ceiling was discovered in June, or where a grade misses a sixth-form requirement, it is usually the right call. The timing decides the value: a resit chosen in August with a full term ahead buys far more preparation than the same entry chosen in October with six weeks left.

faqs.question: Should a tutoring package include past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and a fee for them is worth questioning rather than valuing. IGCSE past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables and syllabus documents are Cambridge and Pearson copyright material. A legitimate tutor references the official document, links to the board's own page and works from what the student lawfully has through school. Released mark schemes are published by the boards, and a student who learns where to find them can use them long after the sessions end, which is more useful than a bundle.

faqs.question: How should a two-year IGCSE budget be split?
faqs.answer: Early money in Year 10 where it can still move an entry tier, because a term of work ending in a timed higher-tier paper produces evidence a subject lead can act on while the deadline is open. A small share on a technique block that pays into several subjects. The largest single share on the sixteen-session block after the mock, when a family has the most information and the least time. And a reserve held for the autumn, because a resit decision arrives days after August results.

faqs.question: Does a cheap online tutor ever make sense for an IGCSE candidate?
faqs.answer: For a supervision problem, yes. At AED 33-65 an hour, which is what Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, a family buys somebody who keeps a student at the desk, answers direct questions and checks arithmetic. For a student who will not sit down alone that is the correct purchase and the specialist bands would be waste. What it generally cannot do is read a marked script and identify that the results table headings are losing marks, which is a different problem and needs a different band.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram charge for travel to Emaar South?
faqs.answer: No, because no tutor travels. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script and the official mark scheme shared on screen. On a cost page that is the relevant point: the travel element of the published in-home bands, which runs from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once driving is priced in, is simply not part of what you pay.

faqs.question: Is the private tutor permit a cost that gets passed on?
faqs.answer: It cannot legitimately be. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee with a two working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A provider presenting licensing as a cost to the family is misdescribing something that is free, which is worth noting.

faqs.question: Can three subjects be funded at once from this community?
faqs.answer: Funded, often. Sustained, rarely. A household with a twenty-five to forty-five minute school run each way cannot support three weekly sessions plus the independent practice that makes sessions work, and arrangements like that generally collapse around half term having spent three subjects' worth of fees. Sequencing costs less and produces more: a technique block that pays into all three first, then four to six weeks on the weakest subject, then the next, with a clearer diagnosis in each.

faqs.question: When should a block of sessions stop?
faqs.answer: When the timed evidence shows the named faults are no longer costing marks, which is why blocks should be bought with end points and fortnightly checkpoints. Compare each checkpoint against the original written diagnosis. If the losses that were named have gone, the block has done its job. Continuing by default past that moment is extremely common, because nobody involved has an incentive to raise it, and it is the quietest way a few thousand dirhams become reassurance rather than marks.

faqs.question: What should the free trial lesson leave me holding?
faqs.answer: Something in writing you could hand to a different tutor: which component is losing marks, whether the losses are content or technique, what the first four sessions would target and in what order, and an honest view of how much support is needed. If what you are left with is enthusiasm, the hour was a sales call with your child in the room. Ours requires no card, carries no condition behind the word free, and sometimes concludes that four sessions will do rather than a term.

faqs.question: Why does an early tutoring slot cost an Emaar South family money?
faqs.answer: Because it is the slot most likely to be abandoned. A student walking in at 16:30 after a long journey and sitting down five minutes later spends the first twenty settling, so a ninety-minute session delivers about sixty-five of what was paid for. Over a term that is several sessions of value lost, and the arrangement is usually dropped around half term with motivation blamed. Booking at least forty-five minutes after the door opens recovers the difference at no additional cost.

faqs.question: Do group sessions reduce the cost usefully?
faqs.answer: They reduce the hourly cost and change the product. In a group of two to four, a tutor cannot aim the hour at one student's specific faults from their marked script, so what a group does well is cover content and hold pace. That suits a student genuinely behind on coverage. For a student losing marks to technique it is the wrong purchase, and buying it saves money per hour while wasting the whole spend, which is the worst of the available outcomes.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emirates-hi.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IGCSE subjects Emirates Hills families ask for most heavily between January and May: maths, the three separate sciences, English and economics. Each works to one named specification and one exam series, not a general idea of Year 11.

intro.heading: An IGCSE term has deadlines long before it has exams
paragraphs: Emirates Hills parents rarely begin looking for a tutor at the start of the academic year. The search tends to arrive after a progress report, a disappointing mock, or a conversation at the school gate about who is already getting help. By then the exam calendar has a shape of its own, and that shape decides what tutoring can and cannot achieve. A family starting in October has the whole syllabus available to work through. A family starting in late February has one window left, and the only sensible plan is triage.

That is why this page is organised by date rather than by subject. Your child's school has already taken decisions on your behalf: which board, which series, Core or Extended, which optional components. Those decisions were locked in months before the first paper. A UAE candidate sits either the Cambridge June series or the Cambridge November series, and Cambridge closes final entries for each of them well ahead of the papers, June in the spring and November over the preceding summer, with the centre's forecast grades following on its own published deadline. An entry made in the spring cannot be rewritten in May because a tutor has since found a weakness in Paper 4.

Dubai gives the calendar an extra layer. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate, and the schools serving Emirates Hills, The Springs, The Meadows and The Lakes run on at least two different exam boards between them, sometimes within one family. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit alongside the international curriculum as mandatory subjects in every Dubai private school, which means a Year 11 timetable is already fuller than the equivalent timetable in the UK. Revision time is not a free resource here; it has to be found.

The honest answer to the search behind this page is that proximity is the least useful thing to optimise for. A tutor who lives ten minutes from the Montgomerie does not thereby know where candidates lose marks on Cambridge 0625 Paper 5. IB Gram matches your child to a tutor chosen for the specification and the component, then delivers the lesson one-to-one over live video at a Gulf Standard Time slot that fits around school, prep and the drive home. Home visits are an India-only service; nobody is dispatched to a UAE address.

What follows is the term as a tutor sees it: the Cambridge and Pearson milestones with their published dates, a realistic eight-week plan, the market rate for this kind of help expressed by the month rather than the hour, how Ramadan reshapes the revision calendar, the equivalency check worth making before results day, and the line a tutor must not cross on coursework. Every figure is attributed. Where a date belongs to the exam board, the board is named so you can check it yourself, on its own site, before you build a revision plan around it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emirates-hi.programmesIntro: Emirates Hills households are rarely on one programme. A Year 9 child may be finishing Cambridge Lower Secondary while a sibling sits IGCSE and the eldest chooses between A Level and the IB Diploma. These are the four stages the tutoring has to join up.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses examined at the end, usually across eight to ten subjects. Cambridge splits most sciences and maths into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings; Pearson runs a single tier on most specifications. The grade a student can reach is therefore partly a function of a tiering decision taken in Year 10, which is why the first useful question a tutor asks is which paper numbers appear on the entry.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is the densest IGCSE market in the Gulf. UK-curriculum schools account for 37 per cent of private enrolment in the emirate, and the schools around Emirates Hills, Springs 3 and The Meadows feed both Cambridge and Pearson entries. Ask the exams officer which board and which administrative zone the centre sits in before buying any revision material, because the timetable version differs.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years that decide the IGCSE tier a child is offered. Cambridge Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October and report against a published scale rather than a grade. They are diagnostic, not certificated, and the schools that use them well treat the feedback as a map of what to fix before Year 10 begins. Algebraic fluency and the handling of graphs are the two areas that most often decide Core or Extended.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving into the Emirates Hills and Springs communities mid-year often arrive from a different curriculum entirely. A Year 8 transferring from a CBSE or American school meets Checkpoint-style assessment for the first time, and the gap is usually in written explanation rather than in content. Two terms of weekly work on command terms normally closes it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-16 route most British-curriculum schools in this part of Dubai offer. Three or four subjects, examined in AS and A2 halves or linearly depending on the board and the school's policy. The jump from IGCSE Extended maths to AS Pure is the single steepest transition in the British system, and it is felt in October of Year 12 rather than at the exam.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement includes one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, in addition to the IGCSE requirement. Check the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it for a university application.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, offered by several IB World Schools within a short drive of Emirates Hills. Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Students arriving from IGCSE find the internal assessment load and the independent research expectations unfamiliar rather than the content.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. That changes the post-16 choice available to Emirates Hills families within the same catchment, and it is worth asking a prospective school which programme its Year 11 cohort actually moves into.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emirates-hi.subjectsIntro: Subject requests from this cluster concentrate heavily in the quantitative papers and in the sciences with a practical component. Each entry below names the specification code, because the code is what decides which past papers are worth sitting.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended Paper 2 and Paper 4 reward algebraic fluency above everything else. The marks that go missing are usually in rearrangement, surds and the harder trigonometry in non-right-angled triangles, plus method marks lost because working stops at the answer.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for AS Pure. Calculus, logarithms and kinematics appear here first, and students who take it find the Year 12 transition far less abrupt. The common failure is treating it as harder 0580 rather than as an early A Level course.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical component account for most of the lost marks. Paper 5 asks for a recorded method, a table with consistent significant figures and a stated improvement; Paper 6 asks the same thinking in writing. Both are drillable in a way that content revision is not.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles calculations, the reactivity series and organic nomenclature. Extended candidates lose marks on limiting-reagent questions and on explanations that describe what happens without naming the particles involved. State symbols and balanced equations are cheap marks that disappear under time pressure.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: A content-heavy specification where the marks turn on precision of language. Osmosis, transport in plants and the control of blood glucose are the recurring weak points, and the examiner expects named structures and directional statements rather than general description.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two IGCSE grades. The content per science is lighter than the separate specifications, but the papers move between disciplines without warning, so students who revise in silos are caught by the switching rather than the difficulty.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, both calculator. Higher tier candidates lose marks in vectors, transformation of graphs and the longer multi-step problems where the first line of working is the whole battle. The tier decision matters more here than on 0580.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Assessed by two written papers with no separate practical exam, so experimental skills are tested in writing inside the theory papers. Students moving from a Cambridge school mid-course need the formula sheet differences pointed out in the first lesson.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Two written papers covering principles, inorganic, physical and organic chemistry. The organic section goes slightly further than its Cambridge counterpart, and the quantitative questions reward candidates who set out moles work in a visible table rather than on a calculator.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Chosen by a large share of Dubai candidates. Reading comprehension marks hinge on quoting precisely and not over-answering; the writing papers are marked against register and audience as much as accuracy. Timed practice with a marked script beats any amount of grammar drill.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: A popular option in the British-curriculum schools near Emirates Hills. Structured questions reward definition, diagram and application in that order, and candidates who skip the definition lose a mark they had already earned in their head.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a Foreign Language 0544
subjects.description: Sat by many non-Arab students in Dubai alongside the KHDA mandatory Arabic requirement. Progress depends on scripted speaking practice and on learning the set vocabulary lists properly, since the reading papers reuse them heavily.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emirates-hi.modesIntro: Three patterns of work cover almost every request from this cluster. The right one depends entirely on how many weeks are left, which is the argument this page keeps returning to.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the year
modes.description: One or two sessions a week on a fixed slot, running with the school's scheme of work rather than ahead of it. This is the pattern that changes a grade, because it gives time for a topic to be taught, practised, marked and revisited. Started in Year 10, it also puts the tiering decision on firmer ground.
bullets: Fixed Gulf Standard Time slot held for the term
Work sequenced against the school's own order of topics
Marked written work between sessions, not just talked-through examples
A half-term review that compares paper performance, not effort

modes.title: The eight-week exam sprint
modes.description: Two sessions a week for the last stretch before a mock or a live series. The plan is deliberately narrow: identify the three topics costing the most marks, drill them with past-paper questions by component, and spend the final fortnight on timing and the mark scheme rather than on new content.
bullets: Diagnostic paper in week one, sat under exam timing
Three topics only, chosen by marks lost rather than by difficulty

modes.title: Practical and past-paper clinics
modes.description: Short blocks aimed at one component. The commonest requests from Emirates Hills families are Cambridge 0625 Paper 5 and 0620 Paper 6 technique, and the longer structured questions on 0580 Paper 4. These are skills rather than knowledge, which is why they respond to a handful of focused sessions.

Significant figures, units and axis choice marked as an examiner would

sections.heading: What the search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Emirates Hills gets you this term
paragraphs: The literal answer first. A search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Emirates Hills returns three kinds of result: agencies that will send someone to a villa, tuition centres in Al Barsha or the Marina that expect your child to travel, and online platforms. IB Gram is the third kind. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and a tutor is never dispatched to a UAE address. Home visits exist as a service only in India.

That is not a hedge, it is the reason the matching works. Emirates Hills is a low-density villa community. The pool of tutors who can physically reach it inside a school-night window and who also specialise in, say, Cambridge 0620 Extended organic chemistry is extremely small. Remove the travel constraint and the pool becomes every subject specialist available at that hour. The parent is no longer choosing between the right subject and the right postcode.

The second thing a term-time search gets you is a decision about timing, and this is where most families lose weeks. If your child's school has already submitted Cambridge final entries, the tier and the components are set. A tutor can change how well your child performs on Paper 4; a tutor cannot move them from Core to Extended in March. Knowing which of those conversations you are in changes what you should ask for in the first lesson.

So the first session with IB Gram is diagnostic and free. The tutor asks for the last mock paper, the entry details, and the specification code. Those three things decide the plan. If the answer is that eight weeks is not enough to reach the grade you were hoping for, you will be told in the first lesson rather than in April.
bullets: Bring the last mock paper, not the report card: the paper shows where the marks went
Ask the school for the specification code and the paper numbers on the entry
Check whether entries have already closed for the series your child is sitting
Expect the first lesson to end with a week-by-week plan, not a package

sections.heading: The Cambridge IGCSE year counted backwards from the exam hall
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for these queries publishes an exam calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is the thing that makes a tutoring decision urgent or not. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and for a candidate sitting in the UAE those are the only two options. The February and March series that turns up in search results is offered in India only, so it has no bearing on a plan made in Emirates Hills. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests do run in March, May and October, but they are a lower-secondary diagnostic rather than an IGCSE sitting, and reading them as an extra exam window is the most common way a family miscounts the year.

Read the table from the bottom up and the logic becomes obvious. Certificates arrive once results are confirmed. Results reach the centre on Cambridge Direct after the June papers are marked. The school's forecast grades go in on the deadline Cambridge publishes for the series, which means they are assembled from mock evidence gathered earlier in the year. The written papers themselves fall in the June window set by your centre's zone timetable. And final entries close in the spring, months before the first paper, which is the part that matters: the decision that caps your child's grade is taken a term or two before anybody sits an exam, and no amount of revision afterwards can lift a Core entry above its ceiling.

There is one administrative trap worth more than any revision tip. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam. Dubai parents who download a timetable from a UK forum are reading a different zone's document. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre is in and work from the official timetable only.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: find out which timetable your child is actually on
paragraphs: Two boards dominate International GCSE in Dubai, and families in the Springs and Meadows schools are frequently on different ones without realising it. The difference matters for three practical reasons: the series available each year, the way the practical component is assessed, and when results land. Buying revision guides for the wrong board is the cheapest avoidable mistake in a Year 11 budget.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November series a long way ahead of the papers, which is why any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a date copied from a page like this one.

The assessment difference is the one that changes lesson content. Cambridge separate sciences carry a practical component sat as either a laboratory paper or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Several Pearson specifications assess experimental skills inside the theory papers instead. A student who transfers school mid-course from one board to the other has not merely changed syllabus order; they have changed what the exam asks them to be able to do, and the first tutoring session should establish which it is. Ask the school for the specification number on the entry form, since 0625 and 4PH1 are the same subject assessed two different ways.

sections.heading: The next eight weeks, as a tutor would actually spend them
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window most Emirates Hills families arrive with. It is enough to move performance meaningfully and not enough to re-teach two years, so the plan has to be ruthless about what gets left out. The structure below is what a subject specialist does with sixteen sessions, and it starts with measurement rather than teaching.

Week one is a full past paper per component, sat under real timing, marked against the published scheme by the tutor rather than by the student. The output is not a percentage; it is a list of marks lost grouped by cause. In a typical Cambridge 0580 Extended script those causes fall into four buckets: content not known, method known but stopped too early, arithmetic under pressure, and question not read. Only the first bucket needs teaching. The other three need different interventions entirely.

Weeks two to five take the three topics that cost the most marks and work them properly: taught explanation, worked example, independent question set, then past-paper questions on that topic only, drawn from several series. Three topics in four weeks sounds slow until you watch a student try to cover nine and retain none. Weeks six and seven move to whole papers again, two per week, with the mark scheme read aloud afterwards so the student learns what the examiner is counting.

The final week is deliberately light. Timing practice, the formula sheet, the command terms, and a short written list of the five things to check before handing a paper in. No new content. Families who push new material into the last week usually lose more marks to anxiety than they gain in knowledge.
bullets: Week 1: diagnostic paper per component, marked and grouped by cause of loss
Weeks 2-5: three topics only, taught then drilled with topic-filtered past questions
Weeks 6-7: two full papers a week, with the mark scheme read against the script
Week 8: timing, command terms and a checklist; no new material

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs an Emirates Hills family by the month
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family budgets in. The figures below are market rates in AED, attributed to where they were published, and they are presented monthly because that is how a tutoring decision is actually taken. An hourly rate tells you nothing about a term.

Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, is advertised in Dubai from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, which on one session a week lands at around AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's own estimate. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, so AED 600 to 1,200 a month. An IGCSE specialist in an exam year runs AED 200 to 450 and above, which is AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more. The spread is wide because the market is not pricing hours; it is pricing how well the tutor knows the mark scheme.

The in-home premium is the figure worth examining closely. Published in-home rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to 500 an hour, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Set against an online package advertised at AED 799 a month for eight sessions, the premium buys travel, not teaching. In a community like Emirates Hills, where internal distances are long and the evening traffic along Umm Suqeim Road and Al Khail Road is unforgiving, a meaningful share of that premium is paid for a car being somewhere. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so the comparison is not a sales device; it is the arithmetic that explains why the model is online.

Two cautions. First, these are market rates from named sources, not IB Gram's price list; ask for a current quote and take the free first lesson before committing. Second, the context matters: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees being held does not mean tutoring rates are, and a family planning a two-year IGCSE run should budget for the full period rather than the term in front of them.

sections.heading: Why the search says near me and the lesson still happens online
paragraphs: There is an honest version of this argument and a dishonest one. The dishonest version claims online is always better. The honest version is that online removes a constraint which, in this specific neighbourhood, costs a family more than it gains them, and that for a small number of students the constraint was worth paying for.

Take the geography seriously. A tutor driving to an Emirates Hills villa for a 5pm session leaves wherever they live by four, clears security at the gate, finds the plot, and leaves again at six into the Al Khail Road evening. That is two hours of a working evening for one hour of teaching, and the rate reflects it. More importantly, it caps how many evenings that tutor can work, which caps how specialised they can afford to be. Subject specialists in small fields cannot build a viable week out of villa visits.

Online lessons invert that. The same hour is taught by whoever is genuinely strongest on Cambridge 0625 Paper 5 technique at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, screen-sharing a past paper, annotating it live, with the recording and the written notes available afterwards. A sibling in a different year group can be taught back-to-back without a second journey. A family that moves from The Springs to Dubai Marina keeps the tutor and the slot. And when the family travels in the summer, the sessions travel with them.

Where the in-person format genuinely wins is with younger children who will not sit still in front of a screen, and with students whose difficulty is organisational rather than academic and who need somebody physically moving the paper in front of them. If that is your child, say so in the first lesson. It is a better conversation than six weeks of a format that is not working.
bullets: Tutor pool is chosen by specification knowledge rather than driving distance
No travel premium inside the hourly rate, and no cancelled session because of traffic
Past papers annotated on a shared screen, with the notes kept after the lesson
Siblings taught back-to-back on the same evening without a second journey
A move between Dubai communities does not break the arrangement

sections.heading: Ramadan, half-terms and the revision weeks that actually exist
paragraphs: Revision plans drawn up in the UK and reused in Dubai almost always overcount the available weeks. The UAE academic calendar has its own shape, and the single largest factor is Ramadan, which moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar and sits squarely across the spring exam run-up. School days shorten. Energy in the late afternoon drops. Families keep different hours.

The practical adjustment is to move sessions rather than cancel them. Post-iftar slots work well for teenagers who are fasting and badly for younger children. Early-morning sessions before school, which almost nobody books in a normal term, suddenly become the most productive hour of the day. A tutor who has worked with Gulf families through several Ramadans will suggest the shift before the first week rather than after the third missed lesson.

The second factor is the way mandatory subjects fill a Dubai timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Those hours are real and they come out of the same week as IGCSE revision.

Count the weeks honestly before booking anything. Take the exam date, subtract the school's own mock window, subtract the two weeks around Eid, subtract the half-term the family has already booked flights for, and subtract the final light week. What is left is the plan. Most families discover they have two-thirds of the weeks they assumed, which is usually the moment the decision about how many subjects to target gets made properly.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E: the equivalency check to make before results day
paragraphs: This is the section nobody else writes, and it matters more than most of the revision advice above. If your child intends to apply to a UAE university, or to have their certificate recognised locally, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules decide which grades count. Families discover the rule after results day far too often, when the subject that would have made the set has already been dropped.

On the British track, the published requirement is that a student passes five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The detail that catches people is which subjects count: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule.

For the American track, the same source sets out English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold has been verified from the Ministry's own pages, so no figure is published here. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate rather than trusting any tutoring site, including this one.

Equivalency is not something a tutoring platform performs, guarantees or speeds up, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. What a tutor can do is point out in Year 10, while the choice is still live, that the subject your child is about to drop may be the fifth one that counts. That single conversation has saved families a resit series.
bullets: Five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3
Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the count of five
Plus one A Level at E, or two AS Levels at E, on the British track
American track: SAT Math 450+, and IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading-writing 450
No verified IB points figure: confirm on moe.gov.ae before relying on one

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch in the final term
paragraphs: The last term is when the pressure to cross a line is highest, and the UAE market contains providers who will cross it for a fee. One site found during research sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Any family tempted by that should understand what they are buying: a malpractice finding against their own child, with the certificate at risk, and no recourse.

The boundary itself is not complicated. A tutor teaches the content, explains the assessment criteria, models the technique on a different question, reads the student's own draft and gives feedback on it, and asks the questions that make the student find their own weak paragraph. A tutor never writes, completes or produces the coursework, the exploration or the essay, and never edits it to the point where the words stop being the student's. Work submitted must be the student's own, and a tutor whose feedback has been honest leaves a visible trail of the student's own improvement.

There is a UAE-specific layer too. Private tutoring here is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. The official application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listed with a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

One related rule is worth knowing before you ask a teacher at your child's school for private lessons. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify the current policy document before acting on it, but do not assume the arrangement is uncomplicated.

process.title: Tell us the paper, not just the subject
process.description: The useful first message names the board, the specification code, the tier and the paper numbers on the entry, plus the exam series. Cambridge 0620 Extended sitting in June is a different brief from Pearson 4CH1 sitting in November, and the match changes accordingly.

process.title: Free first lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: The matched tutor spends the first session on the last mock paper rather than on introductions, grouping lost marks by cause. It costs nothing and you decide afterwards whether to continue. If eight weeks is not enough for the grade you want, that is said in this lesson.

process.title: A written plan with dates on it
process.description: You receive the week-by-week sequence, counted back from the exam or mock date, naming the three topics being targeted and the components being drilled. The plan is a document you can take to the school, not a verbal promise.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked work between them
process.description: Lessons run on a held Gulf Standard Time slot over live video, with written notes afterwards and a set of questions to complete before the next one. Work done between sessions is marked by the tutor, because unmarked practice rehearses the mistake.

process.title: A half-term review against paper performance
process.description: At the midpoint the plan is checked against a fresh timed paper rather than against how the lessons felt. Topics that have closed are dropped and the next-costliest ones replace them. If the tutor is not the right fit, the match is changed without an argument.

process.title: An honest answer when cover is thin
process.description: Some subject and tier combinations have few UAE-hours specialists. When that happens you are told before booking, offered the nearest available specialist and the slot that works, and told plainly if the right person is not free.

whyPoints.title: The specification, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched to a named specification and component: 0580 Extended Paper 4, 0625 Paper 5, 4MA1 Higher. A general maths tutor and a 0580 Paper 4 tutor do different jobs, and the second is what moves a grade in the final term.

whyPoints.title: Dates from the board, with the board named
whyPoints.description: Every exam date on this page is attributed to Cambridge International or Pearson so you can verify it on their own site. Where a date is not verifiable, including IB session dates, no figure is published at all.

whyPoints.description: The rate table quotes what named providers publish, in the currency a Dubai family budgets in, with the month the figures were read. Nothing on this page is presented as a statistic about IB Gram's own students.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria, model technique and give feedback on the student's own draft. They do not produce assessed work. Said plainly because this SERP contains providers who sell exactly that.

whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run a UAE office or send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are an India-only service. You will not discover that after paying.

whyPoints.title: Siblings and moves handled without friction
whyPoints.description: Two children in different year groups can be taught back-to-back on one evening, and a move between Emirates Hills, The Springs and the Marina does not change the tutor or the slot.

faqs.question: How late in the IGCSE year can an Emirates Hills family still start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Usefully late, as long as the goal changes with the date. With eight weeks before a paper, a specialist can measure where marks are being lost, fix the three costliest topics and drill timing and command terms. That moves performance. With three weeks, the honest target is protecting the marks your child already has: timing, question selection and the mark scheme. What cannot be done late is a tier change, because Cambridge entries close months earlier, nor re-teaching two years of content. Ask for a diagnostic paper in the first session so the plan matches the weeks that actually remain rather than the ones you hoped for.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam series will my child in Emirates Hills actually sit?
faqs.answer: Your child's school decides, and it is written on the entry. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and those are the two available here, since the February and March series is offered in India only. Checkpoint tests in March, May and October exist for lower secondary and are not an IGCSE sitting. Most British-curriculum schools around Emirates Hills, Springs 3 and The Meadows enter candidates for June. Ask the exams officer for the series, the paper numbers and the centre's administrative zone, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and each zone has its own timetable version. Working from the wrong zone's timetable is a genuine risk, not a technicality.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the papers does a Cambridge entry deadline close for an Emirates Hills candidate?
faqs.answer: Months, not weeks. Cambridge closes final entries for a June series during the preceding spring, and for a November series over the preceding summer, and the centre's forecast grades follow on a separate published deadline. Results then reach schools on Cambridge Direct after the papers are marked, with certificates later again. The gap between the entry deadline and the first paper is the point worth absorbing: board, tier and component choices are locked in long before the exam feels close. If you are weighing Core against Extended for a science, that conversation belongs in the autumn term, not in the spring. Ask the exams officer for your centre's own cut-off, which is usually earlier than the board's, and confirm the series dates on cambridgeinternational.org.

faqs.question: Why does my child's school need forecast grades before the results arrive?
faqs.answer: Forecast grades are the centre's own prediction of what each candidate will achieve, submitted to Cambridge on a deadline the board publishes for each series, June and November alike. They exist for administrative and quality purposes and sit entirely with the school. For a parent in Emirates Hills they matter for a different reason: the forecast is often the number a sixth form or university sees first, so a weak mock in January can shape a prediction that outlives it. That is a strong argument for starting focused work before the mock rather than after it, when there is still something for the teacher to revise upward.

faqs.question: How do Cambridge administrative zones change the timetable we should follow?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes a separate version of each series timetable per zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The practical effect in Dubai is that a timetable shared in a UK parents' group may show different days or sessions from the one your child's centre is working to. Ask the exams officer which zone the school sits in and download the timetable from cambridgeinternational.org rather than from a revision site.

faqs.question: What can eight weeks of IGCSE tutoring realistically change before a mock?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order of return. Technique on a specific component, which is the fastest: recording a method properly for Cambridge 0625 Paper 5, or setting out moles work visibly on 0620, can recover marks within two sessions. Then the two or three topics where the loss is concentrated, which take about four weeks to teach, practise and retest. Then timing and question order in the final fortnight. What eight weeks does not do is cover a syllabus. A tutor who promises a grade jump without first marking a paper is selling a feeling, and no honest plan starts before the diagnostic.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a villa in Emirates Hills?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. There is no UAE office or centre. The reason is practical as well as commercial: a tutor who has to reach an Emirates Hills plot by 5pm can teach very few evenings a week, which limits how specialised they can be. Online delivery means your child is matched to the strongest available specialist for their specification and paper rather than to whoever can drive to the gate.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost a Dubai family per month rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market estimates for one 60-minute session a week put a budget online tutor at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month, a qualified subject tutor at AED 600 to 1,200, and a specialist working with an exam-year candidate at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above, based on Bestimate's Dubai rate tables. Monthly packages advertised in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. These are market figures from named sources, not IB Gram's prices. Take the free first lesson and ask for a current quote before budgeting.

faqs.question: When do Pearson Edexcel International GCSE results reach students in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Pearson runs May/June and November series each year. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November series many months in advance, and those dates can be revised. Use qualifications.pearson.com as the source rather than a date quoted on a tutoring page, and ask your child's exams officer to confirm what the centre is working to.

faqs.question: How should IGCSE revision be planned around Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Move the sessions rather than cancelling them. School days shorten during Ramadan and late-afternoon concentration drops noticeably, so the slots that work change: post-iftar sessions suit fasting teenagers well, and early-morning sessions before school become the most productive hour of the day for many students. The planning error is counting Ramadan and the Eid break as ordinary revision weeks. Take the exam date, subtract the mock window, the Eid period, any family travel and a light final week, and build the plan from the weeks that remain. Most families find they have fewer available weeks than they assumed.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE grades count for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. That is in addition to proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority; no tutoring provider performs or guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework in the final term without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, model the technique on a different question, read your child's own draft and give feedback on it. A tutor must never write, complete or produce the work itself, and must not edit it to the point where the words stop being your child's. The distinction matters because the UAE market contains sites selling completed Internal Assessments outright, which puts the student's own certificate at risk. Work submitted for assessment has to be the student's own, and honest feedback leaves a visible trail of their own improvement.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with Dubai students need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. The official route is MoHRE's service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listed with a two-working-day completion time via the MoHRE app, website and e-services.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for an Emirates Hills student mid-term?
faqs.answer: For the common combinations, usually within a few working days, because the pool is not limited to people who can drive to the gate. The variable is the component rather than the subject: Cambridge 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher is straightforward to cover, while a narrow pairing at an awkward hour takes longer. You will be told before booking if the specialist you need is not free, together with the nearest alternative and the realistic slot. An honest wait is better than a fast match with somebody who has not taught that specification.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody covers my child's IGCSE subject combination?
faqs.answer: You are told, before any payment, and given the options plainly. For a thin subject the usual outcome is a specialist working from outside the UAE on a Gulf Standard Time slot, which works well for written subjects and for maths. Where even that is unavailable, the honest answer is no, with a suggestion of what else would help: a general science tutor to stabilise the fundamentals, or focused work on examination technique that transfers across papers. No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why it is written here rather than discovered later.
