intro.heading: Four different problems that all sound like "my child is struggling"
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry from this catchment starts the same way: a subject is named, a grade is mentioned, and a tutor is requested. Underneath that sentence sit four quite different problems, and they need four different kinds of help. Buying the wrong one is the usual reason a term of conscientious tutoring leaves a grade where it started.

The first is a content gap: material that was taught and not learned, or was missed through absence or a change of school. It needs teaching, it takes a term, and it is the only one of the four that more lessons reliably fixes. The second is a technique habit: method lines never written, command terms answered at one depth, rounding applied too early, multi-part questions abandoned. The content is there and the marks are not. This needs drilling and it moves in weeks.

The third is comprehension. The mathematics or the science is sound and the student has answered a slightly different question from the one on the page, which in a catchment with this many home languages is common and frequently misdiagnosed as subject weakness. The fourth is organisation: work handed in late or not at all, revision that never starts, a mock arriving unprepared. That is a self-management problem and a subject tutor is a poor instrument for it.

A radius search cannot distinguish between those four, and nor can a price comparison. What distinguishes them is one marked paper read by somebody who knows the mark scheme. That hour is the single highest-value thing available to a family here, and it is why our first request is for a photograph rather than a phone call.

Two of those four diagnoses are not best solved by weekly subject tuition at all, which is worth saying on a page whose purpose is to sell weekly subject tuition. A technique habit is gone in four to six focused sessions, so an open-ended term costs more and removes the deadline pressure that makes the change hold. An organisation problem needs self-management work, and a subject tutor booked for it tends to become another appointment the student is unprepared for. Knowing which of the four you have is worth more than any comparison of hourly rates in this catchment.

Green Community makes this worth saying because proximity usually works here. The school run is short, often walkable, and most services a family needs sit inside Dubai Investments Park. The habit of choosing the nearest option is reasonable and well earned. It just does not sort tutors by anything that matters, and for the narrower syllabus codes it sorts the list down to nobody.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What follows: the four diagnoses compared, one-to-one set against group classes, school support and self-study, what Year 10 buys that Year 11 cannot, the AED bands with their sources, and the series calendar counted backwards.

sections.heading: The four diagnoses, and what each one actually needs
paragraphs: Separating these four is most of the work, and it is work a radius search cannot do. A content gap means material was taught and not learned. It shows on a script as questions the student cannot begin, and as answers that stop after the first recall step. It needs teaching, it needs a term, and it is the only one of the four where buying more weekly lessons is straightforwardly the right response.

A technique habit shows differently. The student can explain the question verbally, the method is broadly right, and the marks are missing anyway: no working written, rounding applied at an intermediate step, a command term answered at the wrong depth, a multi-part question abandoned after the part that did not resolve cleanly. Those are behaviours. They move in four to six focused sessions and then they are gone, which means an open-ended weekly slot is the wrong product.

A comprehension problem is the one most often missed. The signature is correct work applied to a slightly different question from the one printed, or a competently written piece aimed at the wrong audience. In a catchment where home languages are as varied as they are here, this is common, and treating it as a subject weakness wastes a term. The fix is a reading discipline: underline what is asked, restate it, then answer.

An organisation problem is the fourth, and a subject tutor is a poor instrument for it. Work handed in late, revision that never starts, a mock arriving unprepared. What helps is self-management work - mapping a real task backwards from its deadline, repeatedly, until the student does it unprompted - and it is better bought as a short block than as a term of subject lessons that will also be missed.

sections.heading: One-to-one, group class, school support or self-study
paragraphs: Having identified the problem, the next comparison is the format, and one-to-one is not automatically the answer. It is the most expensive option per hour and the only one that diagnoses, which means it earns its price for a technique habit or a comprehension problem and is sometimes overkill for a content gap that a group class covers adequately.

A group class at a tuition centre is the cheapest supervised option per hour, because the teacher's time is shared. For a student who is broadly on track and needs structured practice with someone present, it is good value. It cannot identify one student's specific habits, and for a Green Community family it also costs two journeys a week, which is a real price in time even over short distances.

School support is the option families consistently under-use, and it is free. Most schools in this catchment run subject clinics, catch-up sessions or departmental drop-ins, and the teacher running them already knows the student, the scheme of work and the internal assessment calendar. Asking what exists before buying anything is sensible, and the answer sometimes removes the need to buy at all.

Self-study with past papers is free and works for exactly one thing: building familiarity with question shapes in a student who is already accurate. Its weakness is marking. Self-marking systematically over-rewards, because the student knows what they intended to write and reads their own shorthand generously, so a missing unit or an absent method line passes unnoticed. Self-study plus occasional external marking is a genuinely economical combination that very few families use.

sections.heading: What Year 10 buys that Year 11 cannot
paragraphs: The timing comparison matters more than the price comparison, because one decision taken in Year 10 constrains everything afterwards. Core and Foundation entries cap the maximum attainable grade. That is their function, and for a student who cannot access the higher paper at all it is the right call. Used as a confidence measure after a bad term, it trades a few comfortable months for a permanent ceiling.

Year 10 therefore buys evidence for a decision that is still open. Sit a timed paper at each route, have both marked externally against the official scheme, and read what the marks say rather than how the hour felt. A student losing Extended or Higher marks to unwritten method, early rounding and abandoned questions is a higher-route candidate with three fixable habits. A student who cannot begin most questions is a genuinely different case, and the marking makes that clear inside an hour.

Year 10 also buys habits at their cheapest. Writing method lines, holding full precision until the final step, underlining what a question asks before answering: these cost a term to install when nothing else is competing, and they pay on every paper in every subject afterwards. Installed in Year 11, they are being built during the mock cycle, which is the worst possible time to be changing how a student writes.

Year 11 buys something narrower but still real: habit repair and timed practice. What it cannot buy is a year of unmet content, and an honest tutor says so in the first session rather than in April. It also cannot reopen the tier decision in most schools, because the entry deadline has passed, and that is the one loss no amount of later effort recovers.

sections.heading: Reading three quotes from this catchment
paragraphs: Sort the published figures by what the hour contains rather than by what it costs, and the three quotes in your inbox stop looking like one market. At the bottom sit the online budget providers - Tutopiya advertising from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 - where the hour contains supervision and practice. In the middle sits online subject teaching, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Above that the figures split by what is being paid for: Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, where part of the fee is a car arriving in your street, while specialist exam-year work is published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270 and BartyED publishes AED 650, where the fee is syllabus-code depth instead. All were read in October 2026 and attributed to whoever published them. A near-me shortlist mixes those two upper bands constantly, because from a Green Community address both of them simply look like the expensive option.

Put three quotes side by side and the variation usually has three sources, only one of which is about teaching. The first is the format: a group seat, a one-to-one hour online, or a one-to-one hour with a journey attached. The second is the drive, which from Green Community is modest and from Emaar South is not. The third is specialism, and that is the one worth paying for.

The trap is that the in-home band and the specialist band overlap almost completely. A family can pay AED 350 an hour and receive a generalist whose premium is covering a commute, or pay AED 250 an hour online and receive someone who has taught that syllabus code for years. Price alone cannot tell those apart, and neither can proximity.

What can tell them apart is asking. Which syllabus code have you taught, and what papers are in it? Do you mark against the official scheme, and can you show a marked example? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which the UAE government states is granted free of charge for two years? Three questions, three sentences each, and more informative than any rate comparison. None of the figures above are IB Gram prices; our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: The series calendar counted backwards from the papers
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline to a Dubai family is giving them another country's dates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window.

Counted backwards, the sequence is unforgiving. Final entries close months before the papers, and the route or tier is fixed at that point. Mocks sit about a term ahead and exist to generate diagnostic data. A timed-paper cycle needs the final eight to ten weeks, which presupposes the syllabus has been covered once. Where a science subject uses a practical test rather than an alternative-to-practical paper, that component has its own earlier date.

Most enquiries arrive after the mocks, which is precisely when the content window has shut. That is a workable starting point for recovering habit marks and a poor one for teaching a year of unmet material, and the first session should say which applies rather than promising both.

Two standing rules. Plan from the live official timetable on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from any date restated on a tutoring page, this one included. And ask your centre in writing which of Cambridge's six administrative zones it sits in, because the zone determines which timetable version applies and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility if the wrong one is used.

paragraphs: For code-matched IGCSE work the format fits the task, because most sessions are a marked paper on a shared screen with both people annotating the same question. A lesson can start at 4pm rather than 5.30pm because nobody is driving, and it does not cancel when the port roads or Sheikh Zayed Road seize up.

The selection effect is where it matters most, and it is sharpest for the narrow codes. For Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 the local pool here is reasonable. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1, a Cambridge 0511 speaking component or a first-language Arabic stream, a radius search from Dubai Investments Park can return nobody usable at all. Those are the cases where delivery model changes the outcome rather than the price.

A search with 'near me' in it deserves the blunt answer before anything else on this page: IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. Nobody drives to Green Community West, Green Community Motor City or anywhere else in Dubai Investments Park, because in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That belongs near the top of a near-me page rather than somewhere a parent finds it after booking, and it is stated here for a specific reason - two providers ranking for these UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote. Proximity is the thing this search asks for and the one thing we cannot sell you.

The honest limits: a student who will not begin work without an adult physically present does better in person, and that is also the student most likely to have an organisation diagnosis rather than a subject one. A weak connection shortens the hour whatever the clock says. A shared study space, more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas, undermines any lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room. If one of those applies, hire locally and ask the three questions above.

sections.heading: Permits, copyright and the claims we do not make
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the UAE government states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, publishes no fee, lists a two-working-day completion time and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. The government states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so we quote no amount and nor should anyone else. Never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher.

On copyright: we do not host or distribute Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or specifications. They are the boards' material, and circulating unreleased content is a malpractice exposure for the student. We reference and link the official sources and work from the copies the school is licensed to provide.

What we do not claim: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation or partnership, publish no self-asserted star rating or review count, promise no grade or improvement figure, and quote no statistic without its source and date.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child needs a tutor or something else?
faqs.answer: Read one marked paper against the mark scheme before buying anything. If marks are missing on questions the student can explain to you verbally, the problem is technique and a short block of four to six sessions will do more than a term. If questions were not begun at all, it is content and it needs teaching over a term. If the work is correct but answers a slightly different question, it is comprehension. If sections are blank and work is going in late, it is organisation, and a subject tutor is the wrong instrument.

faqs.question: Is one-to-one tuition always better than a group class in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: No. One-to-one is the most expensive option per hour and the only one that diagnoses, so it earns its price for a technique habit or a comprehension problem and is sometimes more than a content gap requires. A group class is the cheapest supervised option because the teacher's time is shared, and for a student broadly on track who needs structured practice it is good value. It cannot identify one student's specific habits, and it costs your household two journeys a week even over short distances.

faqs.question: Should we ask the school for help before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families consistently skip this step. Most schools in this catchment run subject clinics, catch-up sessions or departmental drop-ins, and the teacher running them already knows your child, the scheme of work and the internal assessment calendar. It is free and it is better informed than any external tutor on day one. Ask what exists, for which subjects and on which days, before buying anything. Sometimes the answer removes the need entirely, and sometimes it tells you exactly which gap an external tutor should fill.

faqs.question: Why does self-marking past papers not improve my child's grade?
faqs.answer: Because self-marking systematically over-rewards. The student knows what they intended to write, reads their own shorthand generously, and does not notice a missing unit, an unwritten method line or a command term answered too shallowly. So the paper is completed, filed, and nothing changes. Self-study plus periodic external marking is a genuinely economical arrangement that very few families use: the student sits papers alone, and someone who is not the student marks one in three against the official scheme and names the habits.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start IGCSE tutoring here?
faqs.answer: Year 10, clearly, and the reason is the tier decision rather than the content. Core and Foundation entries cap the attainable grade, they are frequently chosen as a confidence measure after a bad term, and the ceiling only becomes visible when a sixth form publishes its entry requirement. Two timed papers marked externally give a family evidence while the entry is still open. Year 10 also installs habits at their cheapest, before they would otherwise have to be built during the mock cycle.

faqs.question: My child's maths is correct but the marks are low. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly method lines not written down. A student works part of a question mentally, writes only the answer, and when the answer is right nothing is lost. On the next question a sign error creeps in, the answer is wrong, and with no working on the page every method mark available is lost as well. Over a full paper this routinely accounts for a whole grade. It is a discipline rather than a concept, and three or four sessions of strict enforcement usually installs it permanently.

faqs.question: Could my child's problem be reading the question rather than the subject?
faqs.answer: It is more common than families expect, particularly where English is an additional language, and it is the diagnosis most often missed in this catchment. The signature is correct work applied to a slightly different problem from the one printed, or a competently written English piece aimed at the wrong audience or form. Treating it as subject weakness wastes a term. The fix is a reading discipline: underline what is actually asked, restate the question in the student's own words, then answer. Two to four sessions usually does it.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor near Green Community before the first paid lesson?
faqs.answer: Three questions. Which syllabus code have you taught, and what papers are in it? Do you mark against the official scheme, and can you show me a marked example? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which the UAE government states is granted free of charge for two years? A tutor who answers the first two precisely and the third without hesitation is usually worth a trial. Price is the easiest thing to compare and tells you the least about any of this.

faqs.question: Why would a tutor recommend we do not hire them?
faqs.answer: Because two of the four common diagnoses are not best solved by weekly subject tuition, and saying so costs us one booking and buys a family a plan that works. An organisation problem needs self-management work, not a subject tutor who will also be missed. A content gap in a well-staffed department may be better served by a free school clinic run by someone who already knows the student. The written diagnosis from the free first session says which, including when the answer is to buy nothing.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find an Additional Mathematics 0606 tutor here?
faqs.answer: Two to three days rather than one, and we say so at the enquiry. Cambridge 0606 and Pearson's Further Pure 4PM1 have the thinnest specialist supply of any code in this catchment, because few students take them and fewer tutors cover the calculus and trigonometric identity content properly. A radius search from Dubai Investments Park or Dubai South commonly returns nobody usable, which is the clearest case in this cluster where the delivery model changes the outcome rather than merely the price.

faqs.question: Do group classes exist for IGCSE subjects in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, at tuition centres, and they are the cheapest supervised option per hour because the teacher's time is shared across the room. The honest trade is that a group class cannot diagnose one student's specific habits, which is exactly what a technique or comprehension problem requires, and it commits your household to two journeys a week. For a student who is broadly accurate and simply needs structured practice with an adult present, it is a reasonable purchase and often the right one.

faqs.question: Can a technique habit really be fixed in four sessions?
faqs.answer: Habits move faster than content does, and four to six focused sessions with external marking is usually enough to change one. The mechanism is unglamorous: the student sees two marks withheld for a missing unit, three times, and the behaviour changes. What does not work is discussing the habit, or adding it as advice at the end of a content lesson. It needs to be the whole purpose of the session, with the marking done by someone who is not the student and the losses named explicitly each time.

faqs.question: Does the science practical component affect when we should start?
faqs.answer: It can, and it catches families out. Where a centre uses a practical test rather than an alternative-to-practical paper, that component has its own date and is frequently earlier than the written papers, so a student planning to revise practical skills last may find the component already behind them. Ask the exams officer which arrangement applies and when it falls, and confirm the centre's Cambridge administrative zone at the same time, since the zone determines which timetable version applies to your child.

faqs.question: How do sessions work around Ramadan in Green Community?
faqs.answer: The hour moves and the plan usually does not. School hours shorten during Ramadan and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a weekday 5pm slot typically becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. Where a series is close, keep the frequency and change only the time, which holds up better than lengthening fewer sessions. Because no tutor is travelling to your address, moving a slot is a shared-diary adjustment rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute, and it moves back just as easily afterwards.

intro.heading: In this part of Dubai the problem is not finding a tutor, it is telling them apart
paragraphs: Hor Al Anz sits in Deira, next to Abu Hail and Al Muteena, inland from Al Mamzar, with the Green Line of the Metro running through it. It has one of the most active private tuition markets in the emirate: group classes at centres in Al Qusais and Al Nahda, informal home tuition advertised locally, and a wide spread of prices. A near me search here does not return an empty list. It returns too long a list, with nothing in it that lets a parent choose.

What is missing from that list is the only information that matters: which syllabus has this person actually taught, to which tier, and through to examination. Every option in the results describes itself as an IGCSE tutor. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations with different calculator rules and different past papers, and Core and Extended are different content with different grade ceilings. Someone who has taught one of those competently may have no useful experience of the others.

So this page gives you the things a map cannot. It explains the command words that determine how an answer is marked, which is where most capable students lose marks. It sets out which papers each subject sits and what each paper rewards. It explains what a tier caps and when that decision closes. And it gives five questions that work on any provider in this district, including us, with the warning signs written out.

The reason that matters more than proximity is simple arithmetic. Marks in IGCSE are awarded against a published scheme, not deducted from a perfect answer. A student who writes a thorough paragraph for a two-mark question and a thin answer for a six-mark question has misread two instructions, not misunderstood two topics, and the repair is a fortnight of technique work rather than a term of content. Most families in this district have been sold the term.

It is worth saying plainly that the local market has a genuine advantage over the one in New Dubai. Group classes within walking or Metro distance cost a fraction of private one-to-one work, published Dubai bands start at roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end, and for a student who is simply behind on material that is a sensible purchase. What those classes cannot do is read one student's script against a mark scheme and tell you which of six different things is costing the marks. Knowing which of those two situations you are in is most of the decision, and it takes one marked paper rather than a consultation.

On delivery, the position is plain. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. Where a group class at a local centre is the right purchase for your situation, we will say so on this page rather than pretend otherwise, because in a market this crowded the useful thing is a straight comparison rather than another claim.

sections.heading: Command words: the vocabulary that decides how an answer is marked
paragraphs: The most common reason a capable IGCSE student underperforms is that they answer the wrong kind of question. Each paper uses a controlled vocabulary of command words, each with an agreed requirement, and examiners apply them literally. State wants a fact. Describe wants an account of what happens. Explain wants reasons, with a chain of reasoning in which each link can earn a mark. Calculate wants working and a value. Suggest wants an applied answer to an unfamiliar situation, where several responses may be acceptable.

Students lose marks in both directions and the second direction is less obvious. Writing an explanation for a question that asked for a description earns nothing extra and consumes minutes that the back of the paper needed. Writing a description where an explanation was wanted earns nothing at all. A student who does both across a paper can lose a noticeable number of marks without a single gap in subject knowledge, which is the most frustrating way to lose a grade and the quickest to fix.

The method is narrow and repetitive. Take the student's own answers, set the published mark scheme beside them, and identify what the scheme awarded that the answer did not supply. Within three or four sessions a student can predict the required answer shape from the command word and the mark allocation alone. That skill transfers to every question in every subject, which is why a technique block is better value than subject teaching for students whose content is actually sound.

One further habit belongs here: counting. A six-mark question wants six distinct scoring points, and depth does not substitute for coverage. Reading the allocation first, planning that many separate points in the margin, and then writing them is mechanical, learnable in two sessions, and pays out on every long-answer question in every paper the student sits.

sections.heading: Which paper is which, subject by subject
paragraphs: Parents are often surprised to learn how differently the papers are structured across subjects their child sits in the same fortnight. Knowing the structure is not trivia: it determines what revision should look like in the final month, because a multiple-choice paper rewards elimination and speed while an extended-response paper rewards planning, and preparing for both in the same way under-serves each.

The pattern across Cambridge separate sciences is a theory paper set alongside a practical-skills component, with most international centres sitting that as a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory test. Mathematics sits two papers, with Cambridge taking one of them without a calculator and Pearson allowing a calculator throughout. English qualifications differ according to which of the two English syllabuses the student is entered for, which is the first thing to confirm. Business, economics and accounting typically pair a structured paper with a case or data-based one.

The durations, weightings and exact paper numbers differ by syllabus and by tier, and they are revised from time to time, so the specification on the board's own site is the document to check rather than any summary including this one. What is stable is the type of demand each paper makes, and that is what the table below sets out. Use it to decide what final-month revision should consist of in each subject.

One Cambridge administrative point belongs here because it has caught families out. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school for the version that applies to your centre and keep it.

sections.heading: Tiers, grade scales and what a capped grade actually closes
paragraphs: Two things confuse families here and both are worth five minutes. The first is tiering. Cambridge mathematics and the separate sciences are entered at Core or Extended, and Pearson mathematics at Foundation or Higher. The lower tier covers less content and its grade ceiling is capped, which means the top grades are unavailable regardless of how well the paper goes. The department usually decides from set performance in Year 10, and many parents learn the tier when a mock timetable appears in Year 11.

The second is the grade scale. Many current IGCSE syllabuses report on a nine-to-one scale while some still report A* to G, and students may hold a mixture across their subjects. That is normal and it causes anxiety mostly because nobody explains it. What matters practically is not the scale but the ceiling: a capped tier can quietly remove a post-16 route the family assumed was available, and that is a decision taken by default rather than by discussion.

If a science or mathematics route after sixteen is intended, raise the tier question early in Year 10 and ask one specific thing: what would need to improve for a higher tier entry to be considered? That answer is a work plan, and it is far cheaper to act on than a capped grade is to live with. By the spring of Year 11 the entry is lodged and the question has changed to how to get the best out of the tier taken.

sections.heading: What a group class can do, and what only a marked script can
paragraphs: This district has a genuine advantage that families in New Dubai do not: plenty of affordable group tuition within walking or Metro distance. It would be dishonest to pretend that is worthless. A group class is a reasonable and cheap way to cover content for a student who is simply behind on material, to add structure to a week, and to keep a reluctant student working alongside peers.

What a group cannot do is diagnose. In a class of ten, nobody reads one student's script closely enough to notice that they lose marks to command words in biology and to abandoned method in physics, and that those two findings would change what the next month should contain. Diagnosis requires someone to sit with one student's answers and the published mark scheme, which is a one-to-one activity by nature rather than by preference.

The sensible conclusion for a budget-conscious family is therefore not either-or. It is content coverage in a group plus periodic one-to-one marking, which is cheaper than weekly private teaching and better targeted than more group hours. We say this knowing it recommends less of our own service than a weekly booking would, because it is what the marked evidence usually supports.

Where one-to-one teaching is genuinely the right purchase is a real content gap that the group pace will not close, a narrow technical problem that needs somebody watching the working appear, or a student whose confidence has gone and who needs to be unobserved by peers while it is rebuilt. Those are specific situations and they are worth paying for. General reassurance is not, and in a crowded market it is the thing most often sold.

sections.heading: Five questions worth asking any tutor in this district
paragraphs: In a market with this many options, the useful filter is a short list of questions whose answers are verifiable. These five work on any provider, including this one, and the willingness to answer is as informative as the answer itself. We would encourage families here to ask them in the same words of everybody they are considering.

Which syllabus codes and tiers have you taught, and have you taken students through to examination in them? How will you mark my child's work, and against what? What will the first session actually consist of? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? And what will you tell me at week four if it is not working? That last question is the one that separates providers who expect to be measured from those who do not.

The permit question is ordinary rather than confrontational. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

One further piece of advice specific to a dense local market: do not pursue an arrangement with your child's own schoolteacher. Reported regulatory rules in Abu Dhabi bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct points the same way. Beyond the rules, it puts a teacher in an awkward position with respect to assessing your child.

sections.heading: Study conditions, the Metro and the shape of a Deira evening
paragraphs: Students in this district travel mostly by school bus or on the Green Line, which gives a more predictable arrival than a car in New Dubai traffic without making it early. Those attending the Al Qusais, Al Nahda or Abu Hail cluster are typically home between 15:30 and 16:30; those crossing the Creek arrive later. After food and a change of clothes, the slot that holds across a term is 17:00 to 17:30 at the earliest, and later for the longer commutes.

Apartment study conditions deserve a few minutes of setup. A hard surface rather than a sofa, squared paper and a ruler for graph work, the student's own calculator rather than a phone, and headphones so a busy household is not part of the lesson. The camera is angled at the page rather than the face, because in every one of these subjects the diagnostic value comes from watching the working appear line by line.

Where siblings share a room, which is common here, staggered evenings work and a shared session does not. Two students at different levels in one hour means one is supervised while the other is taught. If a budget covers one child, making that choice deliberately and using a marking clinic for the other is better than splitting the hour and halving the value for both.

Ramadan shifts the pattern for several weeks and Dubai schools adjust their hours. The arrangement that works is fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work set between them, agreed before the month begins. For a Year 11 student those weeks often sit close to a mock series, which is exactly why the shift is worth planning rather than improvising.

sections.heading: The series, the timetable and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE runs in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Those are the windows open to a UAE candidate, and the Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. That last point is worth stating clearly in a district where many families have direct experience of the Indian system and could reasonably assume the same calendar applies here.

Pearson's published pattern shows the real shape of a year: its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why the live official timetable is the document to use rather than a restatement on any page.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will suggest otherwise. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE, we do not enter candidates for examinations, and we do not perform Ministry equivalency. A tutoring operation with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; we hold none because we have no premises.

We also reference and link official syllabus, specimen and timetable documents rather than reproducing them, and we do not supply board-owned papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Your child's school has legitimate access through its own subscriptions. Every figure on this page carries a source, and we publish no success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we could not produce the data behind any of them and a number without a method is decoration.

process.title: Ask the school for codes and tiers
process.description: One email to the examinations officer requesting the syllabus code and tier for each subject on the entry, plus the zone-correct Cambridge timetable where it applies. In a district where both boards are in use, this is the single most valuable piece of administration a parent can do, and it costs nothing.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: The script rather than the grade. We categorise every lost mark into command word, answer length, abandoned method, content gap, arithmetic or timing, and the tally decides what to buy. It frequently shows that a technique block of four sessions would do what a term of teaching was being considered for.

process.title: Free trial lesson on the student's own answers
process.description: The first session is free and is spent with the mark scheme open beside your child's own work, not on a conversation about services. A short written note follows naming the two priority items and what order to address them in, and that note is yours whether you book anything or not.

process.title: Choose the cheapest option that fits the diagnosis
process.description: If the problem is technique, a short block. If it is a real content gap, weekly teaching. If the student works well alone, marking only. If a group class at a local centre plus periodic marking covers it, we will say so, even though it means recommending less of our own service than a weekly booking would.

process.title: Review at week four and stop when it is done
process.description: A second marked paper at week four, with the error tally compared against week one. If the pattern has moved and the problem is solved, we say so and finish. If it has not, we change the approach or the tutor. Open-ended monthly renewal suits a provider more than a family.

whyPoints.description: In a district with this many options, every provider describes itself identically. Tutors here are listed by the codes and tiers they have taught to examination, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations and the past papers do not transfer.

whyPoints.description: For most students who attend a reasonable school and do the work, command words and answer length are the largest recoverable category. It is also the one nobody sells, because it looks less like teaching than content revision. A four-session block often does what a term was being bought for.

whyPoints.description: Nothing is lost to a cross-Creek commute or to cross-emirate traffic from Al Nahda, because nobody travels to the lesson. Over an eight-week block the number of sessions that actually happen matters more than any plausible difference between two competent tutors.

whyPoints.description: No board or regulator approval, no UAE premises, no home visits in the Emirates, no candidate entries and no equivalency service. Where a regulator is named on this page it is explained and linked rather than used as a credential.

faqs.question: There are dozens of IGCSE tutors near Hor Al Anz. How do we choose?
faqs.answer: By asking which syllabus codes and tiers they have taught through to examination, because that is the only answer that distinguishes them. Every option in a local search describes itself as an IGCSE tutor, and Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607, Pearson 4MA1 and Pearson 4MB1 are four different examinations with different calculator rules and separate past-paper libraries. Add three more questions: how will you mark my child's work and against what, what happens in the first session, and what will you tell me at week four if it is not working?

faqs.question: Does IB Gram provide tutors who come to homes in Deira?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Sessions here are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. In this district that mainly buys reliability and choice: nothing is lost to cross-Creek or cross-emirate traffic, and you select from everyone who has taught your child's syllabus code rather than from those willing to travel to Abu Hail on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe and explain in an IGCSE answer?
faqs.answer: Describe asks for an account of what happens, with roughly one point per mark available and no reasoning required. Explain asks for reasons or causes in a linked chain, where each link can earn a mark. Supplying reasons to a describe question earns nothing extra and consumes time the back of the paper needed; supplying a description where an explanation was wanted earns nothing at all. Across a full paper a student who confuses the two loses a noticeable number of marks with no gap in subject knowledge, which is the fastest loss to repair.

faqs.question: How many points does a six-mark question need?
faqs.answer: Six distinct scoring points, which is not the same as six sentences or a thorough paragraph. Marks are awarded against a published scheme rather than deducted from a perfect answer, so three strong points score three. The mechanical fix is to read the allocation first, plan that number of separate points in the margin, then write them using precise terminology rather than an approximation. Two sessions working on the student's own answers usually establishes the habit, and the gain shows up on every long-answer question in every subject.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a local centre enough?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, often yes. A group class is a cheap and reasonable way to work through material a student is simply behind on, and to keep a week structured. What it cannot do is diagnose: in a class of ten, nobody reads one student's script closely enough to notice that marks are going to command words in biology and abandoned method in physics. The best value for many families here is group content coverage plus periodic one-to-one marking, which is cheaper than weekly private teaching and better targeted than more group hours.

faqs.question: What does Core tier actually cap, and when is it decided?
faqs.answer: Core covers less content than Extended and its grade ceiling is capped, so the top grades are unavailable regardless of performance on the day. The decision is usually made by the department from set performance during Year 10, and many parents discover the tier when a Year 11 mock timetable arrives. If a science or mathematics route after sixteen is intended, raise it early in Year 10 and ask what specifically would need to improve for an Extended entry to be considered. That answer is a work plan with a real deadline on it.

faqs.question: Why do grades appear as nine to one in some subjects and letters in others?
faqs.answer: Because syllabuses have moved to the numeric scale at different times, so a student can legitimately hold a mixture across their subjects. It causes more anxiety than it should, largely because nobody explains it. What matters practically is not the scale but the ceiling imposed by the tier, since a capped tier can quietly close a post-16 route. If you are unsure which scale applies to a given subject, the syllabus page on the board's own site states it, and the school's examinations officer can confirm what appears on the entry.

faqs.question: How are practical science skills assessed if lessons happen on a screen?
faqs.answer: Laboratory work for school purposes happens at school under the school's supervision, and no tutor takes part in it. What tutoring affects is the written assessment of practical skills, which most international centres sit as an alternative-to-practical paper. The question types are predictable: reading an instrument to the correct precision, identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, spotting the flaw in a described method, completing a results table with headings and units, plotting and interpreting a graph, and suggesting a specific improvement rather than a generic one.

faqs.question: Can four sessions really make a difference?
faqs.answer: Where the problem is technique rather than content, yes, and that is more often the case than the market admits. A student who attends a reasonable school, does the homework and still lands in the same grade band is usually losing marks to command words, answer length, abandoned method and rounding instructions. Those are mechanical and they respond quickly. Where a marked script shows a genuine content gap in three topics, four sessions will not fix it and we will say so rather than selling a block that cannot deliver.

faqs.question: What should the first session with any tutor consist of?
faqs.answer: Looking at the student's own marked work with the published mark scheme open, and categorising where the marks went. Not a diagnostic test the provider has written, not a conversation about goals, and not the first topic of the syllabus. A tutor who starts teaching before seeing a script is working blind, and in a crowded market the answer to what happens in session one is one of the quickest ways to tell providers apart. Ask it before you pay for anything.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE candidates in Dubai actually sit their papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Dubai centres normally enter the main Year 11 cohort for the summer window and use November as the resit route. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, which matters here because many families have direct experience of the Indian system. Ask the school for the zone-correct Cambridge timetable, since every centre sits in one of six administrative zones and the wrong version is the school's problem to prevent and yours to check.

faqs.question: Can we get a copy of our child's marked examination script?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer, because access runs through the centre rather than directly to a family, and the process and deadlines differ by board. It is worth asking in the spring rather than in August, so the route is known before results arrive. A script is genuinely useful if a resit is being considered, because it shows whether marks were lost to technique or to content, and those two point to very different plans and very different amounts of work.

faqs.question: Do tutors working in Deira need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any amount you read as unverified, and treat irritation at the question as informative.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same family share a session?
faqs.answer: We would advise against it. Two students at different levels in one hour means one is supervised while the other is taught, and neither gets the diagnostic value that comes from a tutor watching one student's working appear. Where a budget covers one child's tuition, it is better to choose deliberately, fund the subject that gives the widest benefit, and use a marking clinic for the second child. Splitting an hour halves the value for both rather than doubling it.

intro.heading: Three things to do before you pay anyone
paragraphs: Most families in these clusters search for a tutor at the point where a report has gone wrong, and most of them buy before checking two cheaper options and one piece of arithmetic. This page is written in that order deliberately, because a tutoring arrangement bought on top of an already full week tends to displace the work the school set rather than adding to it, and then nobody can say what changed.

The first thing to check is free. Most schools in Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Silicon Oasis and Academic City run some form of after-school subject support - a clinic, a revision session, a departmental drop-in - and almost none of them advertise it to parents. For a student already on a school bus, staying forty minutes after the bell is sometimes simpler than a session at home, and it is taught by the person who will mark their coursework. Ask the head of year what exists before you look anywhere else.

The second is the subject teacher. A short, specific email - which topics is my child not secure on, and what would you have them do about it - produces better targeting than any external diagnosis, because the teacher has seen a year of work. It also tells you whether the problem is understanding, effort or organisation, and only the first of those is a tutoring problem.

The third is arithmetic rather than enquiry. A Year 11 student carrying eight or nine IGCSE subjects has school homework most evenings, and from International City they have already spent an hour or more travelling. Count the hours honestly before agreeing a slot. If there is no room in the week for a session and the work it generates, the honest answer is to change something else first.

Having done all three, the proximity search itself is worth understanding. International City has no international school inside any of its clusters, and the people who teach named international specifications in Dubai mostly live near the schools that employ them. So 'near me' returns availability rather than expertise, and for a specific syllabus code at a specific tier it frequently returns nothing usable.

IB Gram answers that by removing distance from the matching decision: one-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the specification. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are an India-only service for us. What follows compares the four support options honestly, including the ones we do not sell: the school's own clinic, a tuition centre in another district, a freelance tutor who travels, and one-to-one online. Each suits a different household, and the comparison is made on cost, who teaches, whether a journey is involved and what tends to go wrong, rather than against an unnamed competitor nobody can check.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-internation.subjectsIntro: Where the recoverable marks are in each subject, and roughly how much homework each generates in a Year 11 week.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / 0980)
subjects.description: Two papers with a non-calculator component in common variants. Short, frequent practice beats long sessions, which suits a commuting student. The quickest gains are working shown, rounding controlled and the final long question attempted.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers with a calculator permitted throughout, so hand-arithmetic drilling is wasted here. The recoverable marks sit in the extended problems at the end of each paper, which reward a partial attempt far more than students believe.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism carry the heaviest load and generate steady homework. Confirm whether the school entered a practical paper, the alternative-to-practical, or neither, because Pearson sciences have no practical examination at all.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and electrolysis repay targeted drilling more than any other topic. Practical questions reward exact vocabulary for separation techniques and gas tests, which is learnable in a fortnight of short sessions rather than a term.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The heaviest content volume of the three sciences and therefore the heaviest homework. Command terms decide the grade, and data and graph questions reward reading the axes before writing. Suits short frequent work rather than long sessions.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences in two subjects, with papers moving between biology, chemistry and physics. The specific skill is switching without losing time, which is best practised by paper section in a weekend slot rather than on a weekday evening.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Form errors cost whole mark bands: a competent essay written when a letter or article was specified scores badly. Needs the weekend slot, because a complete timed response cannot be produced properly after a long commute.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Accuracy beats ambition in the mark scheme. Note-taking and summary tasks are the most teachable components and produce the fastest visible movement in a short run of evening sessions.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450) and Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Both punish generic answers. Economics diagrams must be titled, labelled and referenced in the prose to score at all; Business Studies top bands require a justified judgement. Light homework load, which makes them easy to fit.

subjects.name: Geography (0460) and History (0470)
subjects.description: Geography marks go on case-study specificity - named place, figure, date. History marks go on source answers that address provenance rather than content. Both are techniques, both move quickly, and both generate substantial reading.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Computer Science loses marks on trace tables and algorithms that ignore edge cases. ICT is practical-assessment heavy and the loss is procedural - steps omitted, evidence not captured, file naming ignored - which needs access to the software.

subjects.name: Bridging into A Level or the Diploma
subjects.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation, basic differentiation and timed essay structure, all assumed from the first week of Year 12. Six to eight summer sessions, when the commute has gone and nothing competes.

sections.heading: The free options at school, which nobody mentions
paragraphs: Before any money moves, there are usually two forms of support available at no cost, and in this district both are more convenient than they sound. The first is after-school subject support. Many schools in Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Silicon Oasis and Academic City run clinics, revision sessions or departmental drop-ins, and they are rarely advertised to parents. For a student already waiting for a bus, staying forty minutes is often easier than arranging an evening at home.

It also has an advantage no private tutor can match: it is taught by the person who sets and marks the work, who knows the school's assessment calendar and who is accountable for the outcome. If your child's school offers it in the subject that worries you, try it for a month before buying anything. Ask the head of year rather than the subject teacher, because the head of year knows what runs across the department.

The second free option is a specific email to the subject teacher. Not 'how is my child doing', which produces a reassuring non-answer, but 'which topics is my child not secure on, and what would you have them do about it over the next six weeks'. A teacher who has seen a year of work can target better than any external diagnosis, and the reply usually tells you whether the problem is understanding, effort or organisation.

That distinction matters, because only the first is a tutoring problem. A student who is not completing the work already set will not be rescued by more teaching, and a student whose difficulty is organisational needs a different intervention entirely. We would rather say that before a booking than after one, which is why the free trial lesson ends with a written note rather than a package quote.

sections.heading: The four kinds of after-school support, compared
paragraphs: Having exhausted the free options, a family in these clusters has four realistic choices, and the differences between them are practical rather than philosophical. School-run support is free and taught by the marker but runs on the school's schedule and in a group. A tuition centre is cheaper per hour because the cost is shared, and it means a third journey into a different district.

An independent freelance tutor who travels is the traditional option and in this district the hardest to arrange well, because the pool within reach is thin and the journey is long. Online one-to-one removes the journey and widens the choice of specialist, at the cost of needing a quiet room and a working setup at home. Each of those four fits a different household, and none of them is best for everyone.

The table below compares them on the dimensions that actually decide the outcome: cost, who teaches, whether a journey is involved, how individual the attention is, and what can go wrong. The rates are market figures attributed to the providers publishing them and read in October 2026. None is an IB Gram rate; ours is quoted after the free trial.

The honest summary for a family here is that school support should be tried first, a tuition centre makes sense for content revision where a third journey is tolerable, and one-to-one online makes sense where a named specification specialist is needed - which is most of the time at Extended or Higher tier.

sections.heading: The homework arithmetic for nine subjects
paragraphs: This is the calculation that should precede any booking and almost never does. A Year 11 student with nine IGCSE subjects receives work from most of them in a given week. From International City they also spend an hour or more a day travelling. The week has a fixed number of usable evening hours, and adding a tutoring session plus its homework into a week with no spare capacity removes something else.

What gets removed is usually the school's own homework, because that has no external advocate. The result is a family paying for tuition that displaces the work the tuition is meant to support, which is the most self-defeating pattern in this market. It is entirely avoidable by counting first.

The table below sets out a working estimate for a commuting Year 11 week. The numbers are illustrative rather than authoritative - your child's school sets its own load - but the shape is the point. In most cases there is room for one session and one homework slot, and no room at all for two sessions. That is why we ask about the week before quoting rather than afterwards.

If the arithmetic says there is no room, the honest options are to reduce something, to move the session to the weekend where it competes with nothing, or to wait for a holiday block. All three are better than a session that crowds out the work it was bought to reinforce.

sections.heading: What the proximity search returns, and why
paragraphs: International City was not built around schools. It is a dense residential and commercial district, its secondary students travel out in several directions, and the adults who teach named international specifications in Dubai mostly live near the schools that employ them. A search for a tutor nearby therefore returns people who are available rather than people who teach Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher routinely.

That distinction is not snobbery about qualifications. A tutor who taught a national GCSE in another country ten years ago may be an excellent teacher and still not know that Cambridge 0625 carries a practical or alternative-to-practical component while Pearson 4PH1 has no practical examination at all, or that one mathematics specification includes a non-calculator paper and the other does not. Those facts change what a student should spend eight weeks doing.

There is also a rule worth knowing before somebody offers you a convenient arrangement. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An offer of your child's own teacher privately is one to decline.

So the practical approach from this district is to stop optimising distance and start optimising specification knowledge, then solve the logistics by removing the journey. That is what online one-to-one does. It is not magic and it does not suit every student, but for a named syllabus at a named tier it widens the pool from almost nothing to a real choice.

sections.heading: The tier ceiling, and why it matters more than the tutor
paragraphs: Before buying tutoring it is worth checking whether the constraint is teaching at all. Cambridge Core caps the achievable grade at C or grade 5 and Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5, while Extended and Higher run the full range. A student entered for Core who needs grade 6 for a sixth-form course cannot reach it however good the tutor is, and no amount of technique work changes that.

The same applies in the sciences. A single combined science frequently permits no science at A Level or Diploma Higher Level, and a double award often permits only one or two depending on the receiving school's rules. Those rules belong to the sixth form rather than to the board, and they vary between schools a few kilometres apart in this part of Dubai.

So ask two questions in Year 10. First, which tier and route is my child entered for, from the examinations officer, in writing. Second, what tier and grade does your sixth form require for the courses they are likely to want, from two sixth forms, also in writing. If the answers are incompatible, that is the problem to solve, and tutoring is a tool for solving it rather than a substitute.

Where a tier change is worth arguing for, the work is specific. The higher tier adds a named list of topics - function notation, circle theorems, vector ratio, histograms with unequal intervals, the sine and cosine rules - rather than a generally higher standard, and a term of targeted sessions can produce marked evidence at that tier. Schools respond to marked papers. By the second term of Year 11 the window has closed almost everywhere.

sections.heading: From the mocks to the June series, for a commuting student
paragraphs: Mock results in Dubai schools usually arrive in the second term, which leaves a defined run to the June papers. For a family that does not pass the school gate daily, those results often arrive as a number with no context, and the number is the least useful part. Ask for the marked script and the question-level breakdown explicitly.

Read the script for pattern rather than for the worst score. Marks lost evenly across a paper usually mean timing or technique. Marks lost in clusters usually mean a topic. Marks lost heavily in the final third almost always mean pacing, which responds fastest to timed practice. A gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 is a question-style problem rather than a knowledge gap, and that is a fortnight of work.

The plan from there, for a bus-dependent household, is one weekday evening session on mark-scheme walkthrough and error-log work, and one weekend morning on a full timed paper. The weekend slot carries the heavier half, because a complete paper cannot be sat properly at seven in the evening after an hour on a bus. Starting that weekend habit in the first term of Year 11 rather than after the mocks is what makes it establish at all.

On dates: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November - its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six timetable zones, and says using the wrong zone's version is the candidate's own risk.

sections.heading: What it costs, and where the bands stop being useful
paragraphs: Every figure here was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram rate. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For Core-tier content support and for Key Stage 3 catch-up, that band contains genuinely usable help.

Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and this is where most useful IGCSE tutoring in Dubai actually happens. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and advertised home-tutor rates at 200 to 500, with published monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions.

Monthly, Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Published online packages include AED 799 a month for eight sessions. For context on the wider education budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year.

The band that stops being useful is the lowest one, once the work is Extended or Higher tier technique or an alternative-to-practical paper. Paying AED 60 an hour for that is not a saving; it is a different purchase. Equally, paying AED 400 an hour for Core-tier content revision is buying something the student does not need. Matching the band to the work is most of the value available in this market.

sections.heading: Checking the tutor, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: The nearest tutor to an International City address is not the same thing as a lawful one, and a proximity search cannot tell those two apart. So start with one request rather than a question about experience: ask to see the permit, in the first conversation, before any money moves. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a licence. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was created by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it runs for two years, and it is granted free of charge. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has ever been published, any specific dirham figure quoted at you should be disregarded on sight.

The breadth of the eligible list is why nobody tutoring in this neighbourhood has a credible excuse for working without one. The filing route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, submitted through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. The categories it accepts are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. A graduate renting a studio in one of the Clusters and teaching Year 11 maths at weekends falls inside that list, which means an unpermitted tutor has skipped two working days of free paperwork rather than failed any kind of test.

On coursework, the boundary is firm. Several IGCSE subjects carry internally assessed components, and wherever a mark is awarded for work submitted as the student's own, a tutor may teach the skill, explain the criteria, question a draft and give written feedback - and may not supply text, rewrite paragraphs, choose topics or generate data. The search results this page sits in include an operator selling completed coursework, and a malpractice finding from that falls on the candidate.

What we do not claim: no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE; no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson; no guaranteed grades; no star ratings we cannot evidence; and no supplied board papers or mark schemes, since we cite and link the official sources instead.
