faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in International City?
faqs.answer: There is one-to-one IGCSE tutoring available for a student living in International City, delivered live online rather than by a tutor coming to your flat. IB Gram offers home visits in India only. For a named syllabus at a named tier the proximity search is the wrong tool here: no international school sits inside the district, the people who teach these specifications live near the schools that employ them, and the search returns availability rather than specification knowledge.

faqs.question: What should we try before paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Two free things. Ask the head of year what after-school subject support the school runs - many schools in Al Warqa, Al Qusais, Silicon Oasis and Academic City hold clinics or departmental drop-ins and never advertise them, taught by the person who marks the work. Then email the subject teacher asking which specific topics are not secure and what your child should do about it. The reply usually reveals whether the problem is understanding, effort or organisation.

faqs.question: How do we know whether there is room in the week for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Count it. A Year 11 week here contains about thirty hours of school, eight to ten hours of travel from these clusters, and eight to twelve hours of homework across nine subjects. In most commuting households that leaves room for one session and its homework, and no room for two. If the arithmetic says there is no room, the honest answers are to move the session to a weekend morning, which competes with nothing, or to wait for a holiday block.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre cheaper than a private tutor?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, because the cost is shared across a small group, and for content revision that can be good value. The trade-offs are a group pace, little individual diagnosis, and a third journey into another district on top of the school run - which from these clusters is a real cost in time rather than a minor inconvenience. For Extended or Higher tier technique work, where the need is specific, one-to-one usually does more per dirham spent.

faqs.question: Why is the weekend morning better than a weekday evening here?
faqs.answer: Three reasons. It competes with no school homework, so nothing is displaced. The student is rested rather than an hour off a bus. And it is long enough for a full timed paper plus the mark-scheme walkthrough, which takes two to three hours and simply cannot be done at seven in the evening. For many Year 11 students in these clusters the weekend session should be the main one, with a weekday evening as the supplement if at all.

faqs.question: Should we check the tier before looking for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, because it may be the actual constraint. Cambridge Core caps the grade at C or grade 5 and Pearson Foundation at grade 5, while Extended and Higher run the full range. A student entered for Core who needs grade 6 for a sixth-form course cannot reach it however good the teaching. Get the entry list from the examinations officer in writing, and ask two sixth forms what tier and grade they require. If those answers conflict, that is the problem to solve.

faqs.question: Can we still change tier in Year 10?
faqs.answer: Often yes, with evidence, and the work is specific rather than general. The higher tier adds a named list - function notation, circle theorems, vector geometry with ratio, histograms with unequal intervals, the sine and cosine rules - rather than a vaguely higher standard. A term of targeted sessions can produce marked papers at that tier, which is what schools respond to. By the second term of Year 11 entries are made and the window has closed almost everywhere.

faqs.question: What do we ask for when the mock results arrive?
faqs.answer: The marked script and the question-level breakdown, not the grade. Read it for pattern: marks lost evenly across the paper mean timing or technique, marks lost in clusters mean a topic, and marks lost heavily in the final third mean pacing, which responds fastest to timed practice. A gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 is a question-style problem rather than a knowledge gap, which is a fortnight of work rather than a term.

faqs.question: Does the board my child sits change the revision plan?
faqs.answer: Substantially, which is why the entry list matters. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 includes a non-calculator component in common variants while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, so hand-arithmetic drilling is essential for one and wasted for the other. Cambridge sciences offer a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical depending on the school's choice; Pearson's 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 have no practical examination at all. A tutor who does not ask will teach a generic course.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE papers sat, and what is the zone issue?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable having run from late October to 19 November 2026. On zones: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a different timetable each, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one.

faqs.question: Would an AED 60 an hour tutor be enough for Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right work. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52, and that band contains perfectly usable help for Key Stage 3 catch-up and Core-tier content. It stops being useful for Extended or Higher tier technique and for alternative-to-practical preparation. Equally, paying AED 400 an hour for Core content revision is buying something the student does not need.

faqs.question: What does a travelling tutor cost from these clusters?
faqs.answer: Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and advertised home-tutor rates at 200 to 500, with monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Against the online qualified band of AED 150 to 300, the travel premium is roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour. From International City that premium buys a journey through the worst traffic of the day.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with internally assessed coursework?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor may teach the skill the task depends on, explain what the assessment criteria reward, question a draft and give written feedback the student then acts on. A tutor may not supply sentences that end up in the submission, rewrite a paragraph, choose the topic or generate data. The test is whether your child could explain, without notes, why each sentence says what it says. One operator in these search results sells completed coursework outright.

faqs.question: Does the person teaching my child need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted at you as unverified. Ask to see it; somebody who holds one shows it without hesitation.

faqs.question: What if tutoring turns out not to be what we need?
faqs.answer: Then we say so after the trial lesson rather than taking the booking. A student who is not completing the work the school already sets will not be rescued by more teaching, and a difficulty that is organisational rather than academic usually needs a conversation with the school instead. The written note after the free trial says which of those situations we think you are in, and it is more useful than a package quote.

Each one names the board, the code and the papers they have taught, and each keeps a slot inside the window a JBR school run leaves open on a weekday.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near JBR who actually knows this syllabus?
paragraphs: That is the question, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a map pin. The honest answer is that proximity to JBR has almost no bearing on whether a tutor knows your child's examination. IGCSE is not one qualification. It is a family of specifications issued by different awarding bodies, each with its own code, its own paper structure, its own grading scale and its own tiering decision. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is graded A* to G and now includes a non-calculator paper. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is graded 9 to 1, permits a calculator in every paper and supplies a formula sheet. A tutor fluent in one and guessing at the other will teach the wrong exam technique with complete confidence.

JBR sharpens the point because there is no school inside the towers. Families here send children outward to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, the villa belt around Emirates Hills and The Meadows, Jumeirah Village and sometimes further. Those schools do not all use the same board. Within a single school, different departments frequently use different boards: mathematics with Cambridge, sciences with Pearson, English with one and Arabic with another. So the twenty-minute radius around a JBR address does not contain a coherent local market for your child's specification. It contains whoever lives nearby.

The second reason proximity misleads is tiering. Most IGCSE subjects are entered at one of two tiers, and the tier carries a grade ceiling. A Cambridge Core entry cannot be awarded above a C. A Pearson Foundation entry cannot be awarded above a 5. That decision is usually taken by a department in Year 10, sometimes provisionally, and parents often find out months later from a statement of entry they did not read closely. No tutor, however good, can lift a result past the ceiling of the tier the child is entered for. Knowing the tier before you buy hours is worth more than any amount of local convenience.

Third, the calendar sits a long way from the paper. Cambridge runs its International GCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with each centre allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which means the useful tutoring decisions are made in the autumn, not in the spring.

So this page is built to answer the real question rather than the typed one. It sets out how to establish which board and code your child is sitting, what separates the three boards you are likely to meet, what each tier ceiling is, what to ask a prospective tutor and what a vague answer means, how the entry calendar runs backwards from a paper, what Dubai providers publish for IGCSE tuition with every figure attributed, and where five IGCSE passes take a student next. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.programmesIntro: A JBR child meets IGCSE in the middle of a longer route, and tutoring decisions at 14 are really decisions about what happens at 16 and 18. These are the four stages in the order families here encounter them.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE entry, assessed internally and in many schools with Cambridge Checkpoint tests, which Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Checkpoint results carry no certificate weight but schools use them to stream and to recommend tiers. This is the cheapest moment to intervene in a subject that is drifting, because nothing is yet locked and no entry has been made.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Year 9 option choice is where a lot of later difficulty originates. A JBR family choosing between triple science and a co-ordinated award, or between Cambridge International Mathematics and the standard syllabus, is choosing the two years that follow and often the post-16 route as well. Schools here publish options booklets in the spring term; reading one properly is worth more than a term of tutoring.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, each entered at a specified tier with its own papers and its own grade range. Cambridge issues codes in the 0xxx range such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0620 for Chemistry and 0500 for English First Language. Pearson Edexcel issues 4-prefixed codes such as 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4EA1. OxfordAQA operates a third set of specifications used by a smaller number of Dubai schools.
programmes.countryNote: For the Ministry of Education, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 form the base of British-track equivalency, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. That single rule should shape the subject block a JBR family plans at 14, and it is also the rule one currently ranking competitor publishes incorrectly as six subjects.

programmes.name: A Level and International A Level
programmes.description: The commonest post-IGCSE route in the British-curriculum schools around JBR. Three or four subjects taken in depth, with AS and A2 structures varying by board. Cambridge runs International A Level in its June and November series alongside IGCSE. Entry is usually conditional on IGCSE grades in the same or a related subject, which is why a Year 11 grade matters beyond the certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry equivalency on the British track requires one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, sitting on top of the five IGCSE passes. Families who drop to two A Levels for workload reasons should check that arithmetic before the decision rather than after, and confirm it on the Ministry's own guidance.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, taken by a significant minority of students from British-curriculum schools in this part of Dubai. Six subjects across six groups, three Higher and three Standard, graded one to seven, with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge adding up to three further points. A strong IGCSE grade in a subject is the usual gatekeeper for taking it at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools around Al Barsha and the villa belt run IGCSE to 16 and then offer both the Diploma and A Level, so JBR families frequently face that choice inside their existing school. The relevant IGCSE signal differs by route: A Level selectors look at depth in the subject, Diploma coordinators look at breadth across six groups, including whichever language and humanities subject the student would rather have dropped.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects JBR families ask about most, listed with the specification codes you are likely to see on a statement of entry. If the code beside your child's subject is not the one listed here, that is the detail to tell a prospective tutor first.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core or Extended; Foundation or Higher
subjects.description: Two very different examinations. Cambridge 0580 Extended now sets a non-calculator paper alongside a calculator paper and grades A* to E at that tier. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout, supplies a formula sheet and grades 9 to 4 at Higher. Teaching the wrong one costs marks on mental method, on formula recall and on timing.

subjects.name: Cambridge International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: A separate Cambridge syllabus chosen by schools whose students are heading into the IB Diploma, with graphical-calculator work embedded and a different balance between method and investigation. Students moving between 0580 and 0607 mid-course find the question style unfamiliar even where the content overlaps, which is a tutoring problem rather than a knowledge problem.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Cambridge 0610 carries a practical component as either a Practical Test or the Alternative to Practical paper. Pearson 4BI1 has no practical examination and assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead. Marks leave on terminology precision: a named process earns the mark where a description of something increasing earns nothing.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables are the recurring difficulties, and the balance differs by board. Cambridge rewards the specific observations in the analysis section; Pearson's longer first paper rewards sustained multi-step calculation. Students who learn one board's expected phrasing and sit the other lose marks on wording alone.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves cause more lost marks than any other topics, usually through circuit reasoning rather than arithmetic. Units and significant figures cost marks across every paper. Cambridge's Alternative to Practical paper has its own question grammar about variables, control and precision that is learnable in a handful of focused sessions.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.description: A compressed route covering all three sciences for two certificate grades, or one. It is not an easier syllabus so much as a shallower one, and students moving to IB sciences or A Level from a combined award meet a wider content gap in the first term. Knowing which award a child is entered for changes the revision plan completely.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response, with marks awarded for structure and register rather than for fluency. Confident speakers routinely underperform because the assessment rewards a controlled argument about a text, not an opinion about it. Timing is the second recurring fault: strong candidates leave the final question underwritten.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: A distinct specification from First Language English, with separate speaking arrangements, and the two are sometimes confused when families describe what their child is taking. For equivalency and for post-16 entry the distinction matters, so check the code before buying English tuition pitched at the wrong specification.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455)
subjects.description: Both reward application to a named context rather than definition recall. Students lose marks by explaining a concept correctly without applying it to the case in the question, and by ignoring the command term: analyse, evaluate and discuss carry different mark structures. Data-response questions are the most reliably under-practised part of both courses.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 First Language, 0544 Foreign Language)
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic regardless of licensed curriculum, and the IGCSE entry may be as a first or foreign language. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, and requires teachers of Arabic to hold appropriate KHDA approval, so the school route and the tutoring route need to be aligned rather than parallel.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.regionsTitle: Where JBR students sit their IGCSEs, and what varies between those areas
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.regionsIntro: The useful difference between these neighbourhoods, for an IGCSE family, is not distance. It is which boards their schools use, where the examination centre is, and how the Year 9 option structure is built. Those three vary considerably across a short stretch of New Dubai.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The closest school district to JBR, with a mix of British-curriculum schools running Cambridge and Pearson specifications in different departments. Short commutes here mean a weekday session is straightforward, and students usually sit their papers at their own school as the registered centre.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: The largest destination for JBR secondary students and the most mixed in board terms, with several schools running IGCSE to 16 before splitting into A Level and the IB Diploma. Families here most often cannot say which board a subject uses without checking, because the answer differs department by department.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Immediate neighbours sharing tram stops and school buses with JBR. The practical difference for an IGCSE family is the highway crossing from JLT, which pushes an evening session later, and the slightly wider spread of schools reachable from the Marina side.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Springs
regions.note: The villa belt, where several long-established British schools sit. Option structures here tend to be broader, with triple science and separate humanities more commonly available, which changes what a Year 10 student is carrying and therefore what tutoring is for.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Triangle and Circle
regions.note: Newer schools that have absorbed much of the New Dubai demand, several of them running Pearson specifications across the sciences. A JBR student travelling here has a return leg that runs against the afternoon flow, which makes weekday timings more predictable than the morning run.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Al Safa
regions.note: Established British-curriculum schools with long IGCSE histories and settled departmental board choices. A family moving here from another emirate or another country sometimes finds a mid-course board change, which is the single most disruptive thing that can happen to a Year 11 student.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Reached from JBR by one bridge, so school routes are identical to the towers plus the crossing. Worth noting only because the crossing is the variable that breaks an otherwise reliable 16:45 start on a busy afternoon.

regions.name: Jebel Ali and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: The longest commutes in this set and the most likely to make a weekend session the better purchase. Several schools in these areas run large IGCSE cohorts, which means mock timetables and internal deadlines are published early and can be planned around.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and Al Barsha: the main IGCSE destinations
schoolClusters.note: This is where most JBR students sit Years 10 and 11. The board mix is the thing to check rather than the school's reputation: within one of these schools, mathematics may run Cambridge while the sciences run Pearson, and that affects which tutor is the right hire for each subject.

schoolClusters.city: The villa belt and Jumeirah Village
schoolClusters.note: Broader option structures, larger cohorts and earlier-published mock timetables. Families here are more likely to be offered triple science and separate humanities, which is a heavier Year 10 load and the main reason a JBR student in this group asks for help in two subjects rather than one.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and the older British schools
schoolClusters.note: Settled departments with long-standing board choices, which makes the specification easy to confirm once you ask. Students joining mid-course from a different board are the group that most reliably needs a term of focused work on question style rather than content.

sections.heading: The question under the search, answered without a map
paragraphs: Does anyone near JBR know my child's syllabus? Almost certainly somebody does, and almost certainly not within a twenty-minute drive of the towers, because that radius was never selected for specification knowledge. It was selected for who happens to live on this stretch of coast. The specification is the variable that matters, and it is national and international in supply.

Here is the thing most families have not been told: IGCSE is a brand, not a syllabus. Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel and OxfordAQA each publish their own specifications for the same subject names. They differ in grading scale, in tiering, in whether a calculator is permitted, in whether a formula sheet is supplied, in whether there is a practical examination, and in the exact phrasing a mark scheme rewards. A tutor who has taught one board for ten years and is meeting the other for the first time will teach competent content with the wrong examination technique.

The table below sets out the codes a JBR-area student is most likely to be entered for, by subject, across the boards in common use in Dubai. Use it as a checklist against your child's statement of entry rather than as a reading exercise. The code in the left column is the single most useful thing you can give a prospective tutor, and the fact that most parents cannot produce it is precisely why tutoring in this market is so often mismatched. Read down the right-hand column too, because that is where the teaching consequence sits rather than the administrative detail.

sections.heading: How to find out which board and code your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: This takes about fifteen minutes and it is the highest-value quarter hour available to an IGCSE parent in Dubai. The most reliable source is the statement of entry, issued by the school once entries are made. It lists the awarding body, the syllabus code, the components and the tier, and it is the document a tutor should be matched against. If the entries have not yet been made, the school's options booklet or the head of department will tell you what the cohort is being entered for.

Failing that, three quick checks usually settle it. The front of the exercise book or the revision guide the department issued often carries the code. The textbook the school uses is normally endorsed by one board and says so on the cover. And the school's examinations officer, who exists in every IGCSE centre in Dubai, can confirm both the board and the centre's timetable zone, which matters more than parents realise.

Why the zone matters: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination because the wrong zone's timetable was used. A revision plan built from a timetable downloaded off the internet rather than confirmed with the centre is a plan with a date error waiting in it.

Once you have board, code, tier and zone, the tutoring conversation changes completely. Instead of asking for a maths tutor, you are asking for someone who has taught 0580 Extended, knows the non-calculator paper, and can work backwards from a June series. That request can be met precisely. The vaguer request cannot.

sections.heading: Three boards, one name: what actually differs
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Grading runs A* to G, with tiered subjects entered as Core, capped at C, or Extended. Several Cambridge sciences carry a practical component sat either as a Practical Test or as the Alternative to Practical paper, and the 0580 mathematics syllabus now sets a non-calculator paper alongside the calculator one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Grading runs 9 to 1. Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher, with the Foundation ceiling at grade 5, a calculator permitted in both papers and a formula sheet provided. The international sciences have no separate practical examination; practical skills are assessed within the written papers, which changes what a tutor needs to drill. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for future November sittings, so a plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate a date.

OxfordAQA operates a third set of international specifications used by a smaller number of Dubai schools, and a handful of centres in the emirate are approved to enter private candidates for examinations they do not teach. That last point matters for a student who has been home-educated, has moved mid-year, or wants to add a subject their school does not offer. It is a conversation to have with a centre directly, well before an entry deadline, because the private-candidate route has its own paperwork.

None of this makes one board better. It makes them different, and the difference is the whole argument for matching a tutor to a code rather than to a subject name. The table sets the three side by side on the points that change teaching.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the ceiling nobody mentions at the parents' evening
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential decision in an IGCSE and the one families understand least. In Cambridge subjects a Core entry is capped at grade C; in Pearson mathematics a Foundation entry is capped at grade 5. The entry is made by the school, often on the basis of Year 10 performance, and it can usually be changed up to the final entry deadline but not after. A parent who discovers in April that the child is on a capped tier has discovered it too late to do anything about it.

The decision is not simply ambition. A student entered for Extended who cannot access the harder material can finish with a lower grade than the same student would have achieved at Core, because the Core paper rewards secure performance on the foundation content. The right question is not which tier is better, it is which tier this child can perform across in eight months, given the hours available. That is a judgement about the specific student, and it needs the mock script in front of you rather than a general view.

Where tutoring genuinely changes the tiering outcome is the window between a disappointing Year 10 result and the final entry deadline. Eight to twelve focused hours on the topics that separate the tiers, finished before entries close, is the intervention that keeps the higher ceiling available. The same hours spent in the spring, after entries are locked, cannot buy back a capped grade.

One further UAE-specific consideration. Ministry equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A capped tier that still delivers a comfortable pass does not jeopardise the equivalency arithmetic. What it does affect is post-16 entry into A Level or Higher Level Diploma study in the same subject, where departments set their own thresholds. Check those before accepting a tier recommendation.

sections.heading: What to ask a prospective tutor, and what a vague answer means
paragraphs: A tutor who knows your child's specification answers these questions in one sentence each. A tutor who does not will answer in generalities, and the generality is the signal. This is not a test of politeness; it is the fastest available way to establish whether the hour you are about to buy will be useful.

Ask which board and code they have taught, and how recently. Ask how the papers are weighted for that code and what the tier ceiling is. Ask which topics the mark schemes treat most harshly. Ask whether they will work from the school's scheme of work or their own sequence. Ask what happens between sessions, because marking a student's written attempt is the part of tutoring that produces most of the improvement and the part most often left out of a low rate. Ask whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. Ask what they will not do on coursework.

The last one deserves spelling out. A tutor may teach, explain, model, set practice and give written feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may not write any part of an assessed submission, supply text to be inserted, or edit a draft until the words are no longer the student's. In this market completed coursework is openly sold, and it is a malpractice trigger that falls on the student. Any provider who treats that boundary as negotiable is a risk to your child's certificate, not a shortcut to it.

And ask about availability honestly. Common subjects can usually be matched inside a week. A narrow combination, a less-taught board, or a slot that only works at 16:15 on a Tuesday may take longer or may not be coverable at all. A provider who always says yes to the slot is either very large or not telling you the truth, and the second is more common.

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the paper
paragraphs: This is the gap nobody fills on a Dubai tutoring page, and it is the most practically useful thing an IGCSE parent can be told. The examination is not the first date that matters. Final entries, forecast grades, mock windows and coursework deadlines all sit in front of it, and several of them sit in the previous calendar year. Planning tutoring from the paper date backwards produces a different and better spend than planning it forwards from whenever the panic starts.

The two series a JBR candidate can actually enter are Cambridge's June series and its November series; the February and March series belongs to India and should be ignored on any UAE plan. Lay a June year out and one date does all the work. The examination period falls in the June window on your centre's zone timetable. Final entries close in the spring, months earlier, and that entry is the last moment a tier can be changed. Forecast grades follow on Cambridge's own published deadline for the series, results reach the centre on Cambridge Direct once the papers are marked, and certificates come later again. The lag at the far end is longer than parents expect, and Pearson's calendar shows how long: its November 2025 International GCSE results did not reach students until 22 January 2026. Every one of those is a date a family should have in a calendar, but the entry date is the only one still open to influence.

Pearson's recent sequence shows the same shape at the other end. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and can revise them, the right habit is to link the official timetable page rather than to trust a date copied onto a tutoring site, including this one.

The planning consequence for a JBR family is simple. Decide the tier and the subject block in the autumn term of Year 11, buy the specification-matched weekly hour from then, and reserve the pre-series block for the eight to ten weeks before the papers. Hours bought in the final fortnight are the most expensive and least effective hours in the whole two years.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs around JBR, starting from the cheapest option
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families begin and where most of the disappointment lives. The cheapest published rates in Dubai sit at AED 33 to AED 52 an hour on Tutopiya's comparison panel, although that panel carries a revision date around twenty-one months old, so treat it as historic rather than current. EdFlik publishes an entry tier from AED 45 to AED 65. At that level you are buying an hour of company and explanation, usually from a university student, with little or no marking between sessions.

The next step up is where specification knowledge starts to appear. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. At the top, BartyED quotes AED 650. Every figure here was read in October 2026 from the provider's own page, which means you can confirm each one before treating it as a benchmark. That matters because three of the six pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars.

In-home visiting carries its own band: Bestimate puts it at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500, with monthly in-home packages seen at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. The difference between those two columns is travel, parking and lift time, not teaching. For a Year 11 student working through 0580 Extended past papers, the money buys more when it is spent on who is teaching rather than on getting them to the building.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page. The honest sequence is a free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, then a quote once the board, code, tier and component are known, because an hour of Alternative to Practical technique and an hour of general science revision are not the same product and should not carry the same number.

sections.heading: Where five IGCSE passes take a JBR student next
paragraphs: The certificate is not the destination and treating it as one distorts the tutoring decision. Three routes open at 16 for a student in this part of Dubai: A Level or International A Level, the IB Diploma, and the Ministry equivalency pathway that sits underneath both for families planning on a UAE university. Each reads an IGCSE transcript differently, and the differences should shape which subjects you put hours into in Year 10.

A Level departments look for depth in the same or a closely related subject, and most publish a minimum IGCSE grade for entry. Diploma coordinators look for breadth across six groups, which means the language or humanities subject a student would rather drop is often the one that decides whether a Diploma place is offered. For Ministry equivalency on the British track the requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count of five.

That last rule is published and specific, and one page currently ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. It is worth reading the Ministry guidance yourself rather than inheriting a competitor's error, because a family that drops a subject on a wrong assumption cannot get the year back. IB Gram does not perform, submit, expedite or guarantee equivalency or attestation. It is a Ministry process, the official channel is the one to use, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

The practical upshot for a Year 10 JBR family is to decide the post-16 route provisionally before the spring of Year 10, then spend tutoring money on the subjects that route actually needs. A student heading for Higher Level sciences in the Diploma needs the sciences secure. A student heading for A Level economics needs the mathematics secure. Spreading the same budget thinly across every subject on the timetable is the commonest way this money is wasted in Dubai.

process.title: Bring the statement of entry, not just the subject
process.description: The board, the syllabus code, the components and the tier are all on that document, and together they turn an unanswerable request into a precise one. If entries have not been made yet, the department head or the options booklet will tell you what the cohort is being entered for. Fifteen minutes finding this out saves a term of mismatched teaching.

process.title: A free trial lesson in the real slot
process.description: One trial per student, no card details taken, held at the weekday time you intend to keep rather than a convenient demonstration hour. A 16:45 Tuesday after an Al Barsha bus and a 16:45 Tuesday in theory are different things, and the trial is the cheap way to find out which one you have.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from the series
process.description: The tutor writes down the sequence before the second session, built from the entry deadline, the school's mock window and the examination period rather than from today. For a Year 11 student that usually means content consolidation first, question style second, and timed full papers in the final eight to ten weeks.

process.title: Written notes, and a change of tutor if the match is wrong
process.description: A short record after each session names what was covered, what the student managed unaided and what remains open. Those notes are what you use to decide whether to continue, and they can be shared with the school if asked. If the match is wrong, change it after two sessions rather than after ten.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject heading
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations with different calculator rules, different grading scales and different tier ceilings. Matching on the code is the difference between an hour that sharpens examination technique and an hour that teaches the right content the wrong way.

whyPoints.title: The tier ceiling explained before you spend
whyPoints.description: A Core entry caps at C and a Foundation entry caps at 5, and no number of hours changes that after the entry deadline. We tell you where the ceiling is and when it can still be moved, because the most valuable eight hours in a tiered subject are the ones bought before entries close.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the awarding body
whyPoints.description: The calendar on this page comes from Cambridge's and Pearson's own published key dates and timetables, with the caution that provisional timetables are revised and that Cambridge's six zone timetables are not interchangeable. A plan built on a date copied from a tutoring site is a plan with an error in it.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on assessed work, stated out loud
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, model, set practice and give written feedback on the student's own work. They do not write, co-write or edit to completion any assessed submission. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, naming that boundary is the point rather than the small print.

whyPoints.title: Availability told straight
whyPoints.description: Common subjects are usually matched within the week. A narrow board and component combination in a single weekday slot sometimes cannot be staffed, and when that is the case we say so and offer the nearest workable alternative rather than filling the hour with somebody who does not know the paper.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near JBR who has actually taught my child's specification?
faqs.answer: Somebody has, and the odds of them living within a twenty-minute drive of the towers are poor, because that radius was never chosen for specification knowledge. The variable that decides whether an hour helps is the code: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ on calculator policy, grading scale and tier ceilings. Matching nationally and internationally on the code produces a shorter list than a map does, and a far more useful one. Bring the statement of entry and the request becomes answerable in a single sentence.

faqs.question: Where do I look to find my child's syllabus code and tier?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry is the authoritative document. The school issues it once entries are made and it lists the awarding body, the syllabus code, the components and the tier. If entries have not been made, ask the head of department or read the options booklet. Three faster checks usually work too: the front of a department-issued revision guide, the endorsement printed on the school's textbook, and the examinations officer, who can also confirm the centre's Cambridge timetable zone.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 in practice?
faqs.answer: Enough to change how a tutor teaches. Cambridge 0580 grades A* to G, tiers as Core, capped at C, or Extended, and now sets a non-calculator paper alongside a calculator paper. Pearson 4MA1 grades 9 to 1, tiers as Foundation, capped at 5, or Higher, permits a calculator in both papers and supplies a formula sheet. A student drilled for one and sitting the other loses marks on mental method, on formula recall and on timing, before any question of content arises.

faqs.question: Why does my child's school use different exam boards for different subjects?
faqs.answer: Because the choice is usually departmental rather than institutional. A head of mathematics may prefer one specification's paper structure while the science team prefers another's practical arrangements, and both decisions are legitimate. The consequence for a parent is that you cannot answer which board my child sits with one word, and that any tutoring enquiry needs to be made subject by subject. Ask each department separately, or read the codes off the statement of entry, which lists them all.

faqs.question: Can my child's tier be changed after the school has made the entry?
faqs.answer: Up to the final entry deadline, usually yes, and after it, no. Cambridge closes final entries for a June series during the preceding spring, months before the examination period opens, and for a November series over the preceding summer. That closing date is the last point at which a Core entry can become Extended. A parent who discovers a capped tier once revision has started has discovered it too late, which is why the conversation with the department belongs in the term before the entry rather than the term before the exam. Ask the exams officer for the centre's internal cut-off as well, because it is usually set earlier than the board's.

faqs.question: Does a Core or Foundation entry limit what my child can do at 16?
faqs.answer: It limits the grade and therefore sometimes the route. A Cambridge Core entry cannot be awarded above a C; a Pearson Foundation entry cannot be awarded above a 5. Post-16 departments set their own minimum IGCSE grades for A Level and for Higher Level Diploma study, and a capped grade can fall below those thresholds even when it is a perfectly respectable pass. For Ministry equivalency, which asks for five accredited passes at no less than E or grade 3, a capped tier that passes is not a problem.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should my child take for a UAE university route?
faqs.answer: The published Ministry requirement on the British track is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Most Dubai schools enter eight to ten subjects, which gives comfortable headroom. One page currently ranking for these queries states six subjects, which is worth checking against the Ministry's own guidance rather than accepting.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor to find out whether they know the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Six questions, answerable in a sentence each. Which board and code have you taught, and how recently. How are the papers weighted for that code. Where is the tier ceiling. Which topics do the mark schemes treat most harshly. Will you follow my child's school scheme of work or your own. What happens between sessions, and is marking included. A tutor who answers in generalities is telling you something, and the generality itself is the answer you needed.

faqs.question: My child moved school mid-course and the board changed. How bad is that?
faqs.answer: Disruptive but fixable, and it is a question-style problem more than a content one. The topics overlap heavily; what differs is the paper structure, the calculator policy, the formula provision and the exact phrasing a mark scheme credits. Six to ten focused hours comparing the two boards' question grammar, reading mark schemes side by side and sitting timed practice under the new paper length usually settles it. Doing that early in the transition is far cheaper than discovering the mismatch in a mock.

faqs.question: Does the Alternative to Practical paper mean my child can skip laboratory work?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it that way costs marks. Cambridge sciences assess practical skills either as a Practical Test or through the Alternative to Practical paper, and the latter asks about variables, control, precision, sources of error and the presentation of results. Those questions have their own grammar and they assume real bench experience, which the school provides. A tutor can teach the question technique and the expected phrasing over video; the laboratory work itself stays with the school.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubai students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the separate sciences dominate the requests from this part of the city, followed by English first language and then the Group 3 subjects, business and economics. The pattern is driven by tiering and by post-16 thresholds rather than by difficulty alone: these are the subjects where a grade decides whether an A Level or Higher Level place is offered. Arabic appears steadily too, because it is mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum.

faqs.question: When should a Year 11 student in JBR start paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Autumn term, counted backwards from the series rather than forwards from the panic. Decide the tier and the subject block before the entry deadline, run a specification-matched weekly hour from then through the mock window, and reserve a fixed pre-series block for the eight to ten weeks before the papers. Hours bought in the final fortnight are the most expensive and least effective of the two years, because there is no longer time to change anything a mock script reveals.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tutors working with students in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor visit our apartment in JBR?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. UAE lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing for annotating a past-paper script and saved worked solutions. The published in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour appears on this page so you can compare the formats on cost and tutor pool, not because the visit is on offer.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework or a controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes. A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain what the criteria reward, model an approach on a different example, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor cannot write any part of the submission, supply text to be inserted, or edit a draft until the words are no longer the student's. That is a malpractice matter and the consequence falls on the student. Any provider selling completed work is a risk to the certificate.

faqs.question: What if no tutor covers my child's board and code in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We say so before anything is paid. Common subjects on the main boards are usually matched inside a week. A narrow combination, a less commonly taught specification, or a single fixed weekday slot can take longer or occasionally cannot be covered at all. In that case we offer the nearest workable time or tell you plainly that we cannot staff it. Putting a student with a tutor who does not know the paper costs more than leaving the hour unbooked.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.closingHeading: Bring the code, and the rest of the conversation is short
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.closingBody: Find the statement of entry, read off the board, the syllabus code and the tier, and note the weekday window your school run actually leaves. With those four facts a match takes minutes instead of guesswork, and you will know before you pay whether we can staff it. We will also tell you where the tier ceiling sits and when it can still be moved. Lessons run one to one on live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the first one free, one per student, and no card details taken.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jebel-ali.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects for Year 9 to Year 11 students across Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens and Dubai South. Every match starts with the syllabus code, because the code determines the papers and the papers determine the work.

intro.heading: Start from the code on the exam entry, not the subject on the report card
paragraphs: There is a small piece of paper that makes most IGCSE tutoring decisions straightforward, and almost no parent reads it before hiring. It is the exam entry statement, and it carries a syllabus code against each subject. 0580 is Cambridge Mathematics. 4MA1 is Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A. 0620 is Cambridge Chemistry, 4CH1 the Edexcel equivalent. Those are different qualifications with different papers.

Hire a tutor on the subject name alone and you may get three months of excellent teaching aimed at the wrong specification. It happens most often in the sciences, where topic coverage genuinely diverges between boards, and in mathematics, where the paper structures differ: Cambridge Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 while Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4, and Edexcel runs two equally weighted papers across Foundation and Higher tiers.

This page is built around that detail. It maps the subjects a Jebel Ali Year 11 actually sits onto their codes, sets out where the marks live inside each paper, and names the topics that consistently cost marks in this catchment. The UK curriculum accounts for 37% of Dubai's private school enrolment, so IGCSE is the single largest qualification in the emirate by student numbers, and the tutoring market around it is wide but shallow.

Geography is the other half of the problem. Jebel Ali sits at the industrial western edge of Dubai, with its residential communities spread out through Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Green Community, Dubai South and Emaar South. A "near me" search from here returns tutors who will drive, priced for the drive, and the further south you live the shorter that list gets. For a subject like Additional Mathematics 0606 or Further Pure 4PM1, the list is often empty.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and that is stated here rather than discovered later. The practical effect is that the code on the exam entry decides the tutor, instead of the driving distance deciding it.

One more reason to lead with the code: it tells you how many papers there are, and therefore how the available weeks should be divided. A Cambridge science candidate has theory papers and a practical paper assessed in writing, and the practical paper is the one nobody revises separately even though it is the cheapest set of marks on the table. A Cambridge Extended maths candidate has a short paper and a long paper that reward different habits. Dividing eight weeks of preparation evenly across a subject, without knowing its paper structure, is how a conscientious student ends up with the same mark they started with.

What follows is the code map, the paper anatomy, the topics that recur as weaknesses in this catchment, the AED market bands with their sources, and the questions to ask any tutor before the first lesson. Read it with your child's exam entry statement and most recent marked paper in front of you.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core and Extended
programmes.description: Subjects carry four-digit codes: Mathematics 0580, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Biology 0610, English as a First Language 0500, Economics 0455. Most run a Core route and an Extended route, with Core candidates sitting one pair of papers and Extended candidates another. The Core route carries a lower maximum grade, which is the whole point of it.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your Jebel Ali centre which zone it sits in; the answer changes which PDF applies to your child.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1 and Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1. Tiered subjects run Foundation and Higher papers. Mathematics A sits as two equally weighted papers rather than a short-and-long pair.

Pearson revises provisional timetables, so work from the live PDF rather than any restated date.

programmes.description: Both routes are available inside this catchment without moving house. A Levels take three or four subjects in depth with published entry grades. The IB Diploma takes six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, graded out of 45. The decision is made during Year 11 on predicted grades, before results arrive.

Entry grades matter here because some of them are not reachable from a Core or Foundation entry, which is why the tier decision in Year 10 deserves evidence.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, the two years that decide Year 10
programmes.description: Nothing in these years appears on a certificate, with optional Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. That invisibility is the hazard: algebraic fluency, equation rearrangement and reading stamina formed here determine how Year 10 feels.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Al Furjan and Green Community often begin tutoring in Year 9 after a Checkpoint report, and it is the cheapest intervention point in the school career. Rebuilding algebra at 13 costs a term of weekly sessions. Rebuilding it in Year 11 costs marks on every paper that uses it, which is most of them.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: Each subject below carries its codes and the specific place marks go missing in this catchment. These are the patterns our tutors see repeatedly in marked papers from the Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park schools.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge Core sits Papers 1 and 3, Extended sits Papers 2 and 4; Edexcel 4MA1 runs two equally weighted papers. Marks go on unwritten method lines, rounding applied at an intermediate step, and multi-part questions abandoned after part (a).

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main course by students heading for A Level Maths, Further Maths or IB Higher Level. Calculus and trigonometric identities dominate. The local tutor pool for these codes is the thinnest of any subject in this catchment.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits is the recurring weakness, followed by moments, pressure and the equations that need rearranging before they can be used. Students who recognise a formula but cannot transpose it under time pressure lose the back half of every multi-part question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry, then organic chemistry. The practical paper rewards precision about apparatus choice and about why a step controls a variable, which is rarely taught as explicitly as it is examined.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-term sensitive. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance generate most questions, and six-mark answers written as unlinked bullet lists cap the mark regardless of how much the student knows.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Reading passages and directed writing. The audience and form specified in the question carry marks, so a strong piece written in the wrong register scores below a competent one in the right register.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an assessed speaking component. Very common in Discovery Gardens and Jebel Ali given the mix of home languages, and writing marks rise fastest with structured paragraph planning rather than vocabulary drills.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Economics turns on labelled, correctly shifted diagrams; Business Studies turns on using the case-study data provided. The top-tariff questions ask for evaluation, and candidates listing advantages against disadvantages without reaching a judgement cap themselves.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data representation, networks and the practical ICT tasks. Confident Python coders still lose theory marks on binary and hexadecimal conversion and on network concepts, because those are examined in prose rather than in code.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Arabic is required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA mandates separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language. Identify the stream before the first lesson; the streams are not interchangeable.

sections.heading: The code map: what your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Every IGCSE subject has a code and the code is the specification. Two children in the same Al Furjan street can both be sitting "IGCSE Chemistry" and be preparing for different topic lists, different paper counts and different question styles. Until the code is confirmed, tutoring is guesswork dressed up as teaching.

The codes also decide how many papers there are and how they are weighted. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 splits by route: Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3, Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 sits two papers of equal weight across Foundation and Higher tiers. In the sciences, Cambridge 0620, 0625 and 0610 each include an assessed practical paper examined in writing, which is a distinct skill from the theory papers and is rarely revised separately.

Where to find the code: the exam entry statement the school issues, the subject pages in the school's curriculum section, and the top of any past paper your child has been given. If all three are unavailable, the subject teacher will tell you in one email. It is a thirty-second question that prevents a term of misdirected work.

Our first message to a Jebel Ali family always asks for the code rather than the subject. When a parent does not have it, we ask for a photograph of a marked paper instead, because the code is printed on the front of it.

One practical warning about codes and timetables together. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. So the code tells you what will be asked, and the zone tells you when. Both come from the centre rather than from a tutoring page, and both are worth confirming in writing.

sections.heading: Where the marks sit inside a paper, and why revision misses them
paragraphs: Students revise content because content is what a textbook is organised around. Papers are not organised around content; they are organised around question types. A Physics paper will ask about electricity by giving a circuit and asking for a calculation, then a rearrangement, then an explanation of what happens when one component changes. Rereading the electricity chapter prepares a student for none of those three moves.

This is why a student can revise conscientiously for a fortnight and score the same mark. The content was already mostly there. What was missing was fluency in the question shapes, and the only way to build that is to attempt the shapes and have someone mark them against the official scheme.

The marking is the part students cannot do for themselves. Self-marking systematically over-rewards, because the student knows what they meant to write and reads their own shorthand generously. An examiner-literate reader marks what is on the page: no unit, no mark; no method line, no method mark; "it gets bigger" where "explain" was asked, part marks at best. Seeing that applied three times changes the habit.

In this catchment the most common recoverable blocks are the same every year: method lines in maths, rearrangement in physics, moles set-up in chemistry, command-term depth in biology, and diagram labelling in economics. None of them are content problems and all of them respond to drilling inside eight weeks.

The practical consequence for a Jebel Ali family is that the first session should be spent marking rather than teaching. An hour of external marking against the official scheme produces a ranked list of habits, and that list is what the following six weeks attack. Teaching before the marking is teaching in the dark.

sections.heading: The science practical paper, which almost nobody revises for separately
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson both assess practical skills in writing, and that paper is where science candidates in this catchment shed the most marks per hour of effort available. Students treat it as the easy paper because there is no content to learn. The mark scheme treats it as a test of precision, and precision is a trained habit.

What it actually asks: choose apparatus and justify the choice; identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables in the scenario given; state how a variable is controlled in operational terms rather than in principle; tabulate results with correct headings and units; plot a graph with sensible scales and a line that respects the data; and describe a procedure another person could follow without guessing.

Each of those has a conventional form the examiner expects. "Keep the temperature the same" earns less than "keep the water bath at 30 degrees Celsius, measured with a thermometer, for every run". A results table with units in the cells instead of the headings loses marks that nothing in the student's understanding justifies losing. These are rules, and rules can be taught in four sessions.

To be explicit about the division of labour: the hands-on practical work happens in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision, as the specification requires. A tutor prepares the written skills the paper examines and reviews the student's own write-ups. We do not distribute board papers or mark schemes, which are copyright material; we link the official sources and work from the school's licensed copies.

sections.heading: The grade scale, the tier ceiling, and what a boundary really means
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects now report on a 9 to 1 scale, with some still using A* to G depending on the subject and the centre's choice. Parents who grew up with letters often misread the numbers in both directions: a 7 sounds worse than an A and is broadly comparable, while a 4 sounds like a pass and sits at the lower boundary of what many sixth forms will accept for a subject they intend to continue.

More important than the scale is the tier ceiling. A Cambridge Core entry or a Pearson Foundation entry caps the maximum attainable grade. That is the function of the route, and it is the right choice for a student who cannot access the higher paper at all. It becomes a problem when it is chosen as a confidence measure in Year 10 and discovered as a constraint in Year 11, after the sixth-form entry requirement has been read.

Grade boundaries themselves move between series, because they are set after the papers are marked to keep standards comparable. That has two consequences for tutoring. First, a raw mark from a past paper cannot be converted confidently into a grade, so anyone quoting you a precise conversion is guessing. Second, the marginal marks matter more than they feel: the gap between two grades is often a handful of marks spread across habits rather than a chunk of missing content.

We do not publish or distribute grade-boundary tables, since they are the boards' copyright material. What we do is tell a family plainly whether the marks lost on the paper in front of us are habit marks or content marks, because those have different prognoses and different costs.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs around Jebel Ali, cheapest first
paragraphs: Read the market from the bottom and the structure becomes clear. The cheapest published online tuition in Dubai starts at about AED 33-52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik, as advertised in October 2026. That band buys supervision: someone capable, usually early-career, who will keep a Year 9 working through a worksheet and answer questions as they arise. For a confident student who simply does not sit down, it can be enough.

The next band up, AED 150-300 an hour online, is where a trained subject teacher appears. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is the band in which someone knows that 0580 Paper 4 is a different animal from 0580 Paper 2, and plans accordingly. For most Year 10 and 11 work this is the right place to be.

Above that, specialists are published at AED 200-450 and beyond, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270 and one premium provider, BartyED, at AED 650. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 per Dubai rate guidance, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, and the travel is inside those figures. Monthly packages seen in the market: around AED 799 for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

None of these are IB Gram prices and this page carries no rate card, because the fee depends on subject and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. The bands are published so that a quote can be judged. A family in Emaar South offered AED 450 an hour for Cambridge 0580 is paying specialist money in the subject with the deepest supply in the market, and is entitled to ask what the premium covers.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one from Jebel Ali, with the drawbacks stated
paragraphs: For code-matched IGCSE work the online format is a good fit, because most of the work is a marked paper on a shared screen. The tutor and the student annotate the same question at the same moment, which is better than one paper copy passed across a table. Sessions can start at 4pm rather than 5.30pm, and they do not cancel when the port roads or Sheikh Zayed Road seize up.

The selection effect is the larger benefit and it is strongest for the narrow codes. For Cambridge 0580 the local pool is reasonable. For 0606 Additional Mathematics, 4PM1 Further Pure, Cambridge 0511 speaking components or a first-language Arabic stream, a radius search from Dubai South can return nothing at all. Online, those codes are coverable.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We state it at the top of the page because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote, and the disclosure is the minimum a family is owed before booking.

The real drawbacks: a student who will not start work without an adult present does better with one in the room; children under about ten lose focus faster on screen; a shared study space in a Discovery Gardens apartment undermines the hour; and a weak connection shortens the lesson regardless of the invoice. If that is your household, hire locally and ask two questions first - the MoHRE permit, and whether they have taught that exact syllabus code.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and the claims to check before you pay anyone
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the UAE government states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, publishes no fee, lists a two-working-day completion time and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. The government states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is quoting something unverified.

One thing never to arrange: paid private tuition from your own child's class teacher. The permit carries a code of conduct and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff are reported as barring paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. The principle is the same in Dubai even where the regulator differs.

Finally, the claims to discount. IB Gram is not KHDA approved; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with physical premises, we hold none and operate no UAE office. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation or partnership, publish no self-asserted star rating, and quote no statistic without its source. Ask any tutoring service for the same.

sections.heading: How to start, and what we do when we cannot help
paragraphs: Send the syllabus code, the subject, the year group and a photograph of the most recent marked paper. If you do not have the code, the marked paper carries it on the front cover. That one photograph is worth more than a long conversation about the term, because it shows where the marks actually went rather than where the student felt uncertain.

We match a specialist to that code. Mathematics and the separate sciences on either board usually match within a day. Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1, first-language Arabic streams and the speaking components can take two or three days, and we tell you which case you are in before you start waiting rather than afterwards.

The trial lesson is free and taught by the matched specialist, not by a salesperson. It is built on the paper you sent: the tutor works through the lost marks with your child writing rather than watching, and finishes with a short written note of what the paper showed and what the first month should target. There is no card required to book it and nothing to commit to beforehand.

When no suitable specialist has a slot at the hour you need, we say so. The options we offer are real ones: a different weekday with the right tutor, a short block until a regular slot frees up, or a recommendation to hire locally with the permit and code questions in hand. No competitor in this market publishes what happens when they cannot help, which is precisely why it is written here.
