faqs.question: Where is the syllabus code printed for a Jebel Ali IGCSE candidate?
faqs.answer: Three places carry it. The exam entry statement the school issues lists a code against each subject. The school's curriculum pages usually state the board and often the code. And the front cover of any past paper your child has been set prints it. Codes beginning 0 are Cambridge - 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology - while codes like 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 are Pearson Edexcel. If none of those are to hand, one email to the subject teacher settles it in a sentence.

faqs.question: Does it really matter whether we hire a 0580 tutor or a 4MA1 tutor?
faqs.answer: It matters enough to ask before the first lesson. The paper structures differ: Cambridge 0580 Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4, while Pearson 4MA1 runs two equally weighted papers across Foundation and Higher tiers. Question styles and the weighting of topics differ with them. A capable tutor can teach either, but one preparing a student on the wrong specification spends weeks on question shapes the paper will not use. The code takes thirty seconds to confirm and saves a term.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE topics cause most trouble in the Jebel Ali schools?
faqs.answer: The pattern is consistent across the marked papers we see from this catchment. In Physics, electricity and circuits, then anything requiring a formula to be rearranged before use. In Chemistry, moles and stoichiometry, then organic. In Mathematics, algebraic manipulation buried inside geometry and statistics questions, plus rounding applied too early. In Biology, command-term depth rather than content: six-mark answers written as unlinked lists. None of these are knowledge gaps in the ordinary sense, and all of them respond to drilling the specific question shape inside eight weeks.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on the science practical paper?
faqs.answer: Because it is marked on precision rather than knowledge, and precision has conventions nobody teaches explicitly. "Keep the temperature the same" scores less than "hold the water bath at 30 degrees Celsius, checked with a thermometer, for every run". Units belong in table headings, not in the cells. Graph scales must use most of the grid, and the line must respect the data rather than the expectation. A described procedure has to be followable by a stranger. These are rules, and four focused sessions typically fix them.

faqs.question: Is a grade 4 at IGCSE good enough for sixth form here?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject and the destination. A 4 sits at the lower edge of what many sixth forms accept, and for a subject the student intends to continue - maths into A Level or IB Higher Level, a science into either - the stated entry grade is often higher. Within this catchment both A Level and IB Diploma routes are available, and each school publishes its own entry requirements. Read the requirement for the subjects your child wants to continue before deciding whether a grade needs work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us what grade my child's past-paper mark converts to?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and anyone offering a precise conversion is guessing. Grade boundaries are set after each series is marked, to keep standards comparable between sittings, so the same raw mark can fall either side of a boundary in different years. We also do not publish or distribute boundary tables, which are the boards' copyright material. What a tutor can tell you honestly is whether the marks lost on the paper in front of them are habit marks or content marks, because those two have very different prognoses.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find an Additional Mathematics 0606 tutor for Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Usually two to three days rather than one, because 0606 and Pearson's Further Pure 4PM1 have the narrowest specialist pool of any code in this catchment. A radius search from Dubai South for either often returns nothing usable, which is exactly the case where online delivery changes the outcome rather than merely the price. We tell you the expected wait at the enquiry rather than after you have waited, and if nobody suitable has a slot at your hour we say so and offer alternatives.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel science papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we treat them as separate jobs rather than one. Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each include an assessed practical paper examined in writing; the Pearson equivalents 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 handle practical skills differently and their topic coverage diverges from Cambridge in places. A tutor is assigned to the code your child is entered for. If your school enters different subjects with different boards, which happens, each subject gets a tutor matched to its own specification.

faqs.question: Can tutoring happen online if we live in Emaar South with a long school run?
faqs.answer: That is the case where the format helps most. Because no tutor is travelling, a session can start as soon as your child is home rather than after someone has crossed the city, and families here commonly take a 4.30pm or 5pm slot that no in-home tutor would offer at any rate. Lessons also do not cancel for traffic or road closures. The practical requirements are a reliable connection and a quiet space for the hour, which in a villa is usually easier than in a shared apartment.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10. Is it too early to start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest useful point, and the reason is the tier decision. Core and Foundation entries cap the attainable grade, and they are frequently chosen in Year 10 as a confidence measure then discovered in Year 11 as a constraint on sixth-form entry. Sitting a timed paper at each route and having it marked externally gives the family evidence rather than impressions. Beyond that, habits formed in Year 10 - writing method lines, rounding at the end - are much cheaper to build than to repair.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers, mark schemes or revision notes?
faqs.answer: We do not host or distribute board material. Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and specifications are copyright, and circulating unreleased material is a malpractice exposure for the student. We reference and link the official sources on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, and we work from the copies your child's school is licensed to provide. A service offering you a complete paper library, or material not yet released, is worth declining on those grounds alone.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Jebel Ali tutor before the first paid lesson?
faqs.answer: Three things. Which syllabus code have they taught, and can they name the papers in it? Do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which the UAE government states is granted free of charge for two years? And how will they mark your child's work - against the official scheme, or by impression? A tutor who answers the first two without hesitation and has a clear answer to the third is usually worth a trial.

faqs.question: Will our weekly lesson time survive Ramadan and the mock period?
faqs.answer: It will move, and the move is planned rather than improvised. School hours shorten during Ramadan and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a weekday 5pm slot usually shifts to early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. Mock and examination weeks need the opposite: sessions clustered ahead of papers and paused after them. Because nobody is driving to your address, changing a slot is a calendar adjustment rather than a renegotiation of a commute, and it shifts back just as easily afterwards.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at once in Year 11?
faqs.answer: One to start with, two at most. A Year 11 is already carrying eight or nine subjects and a mock cycle, and adding three tutors adds three sets of homework to a timetable that has no space in it. The first month is diagnostic in any case, and a marked paper in one subject usually reveals habits - method lines, command-term depth, rounding - that transfer to the others once corrected. Families who begin with three subjects most often reduce to one or two by half term.

intro.heading: What you can verify about an IGCSE tutor near me, before paying
paragraphs: A distance search is a sorting tool that answers a question nobody actually has. The question a JLT parent has is whether this person can move their child's grade in Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4PH1, and proximity is silent on that. Worse, the radius filter is actively harmful at IGCSE level, because it eliminates the people most likely to know the answer and keeps the people most likely to be available at 17:00 on a Tuesday.

The useful reframing is verification. There are exactly five things about a tutor that a parent can check independently, without specialist knowledge and before any money moves: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, the syllabus codes they have actually taught, whether they can read a mock script and tell you where the marks went, whether they will put the boundary on coursework in writing, and whether the first lesson is genuinely free of condition. Everything else on a tutoring profile is assertion.

Price sits inside that frame rather than above it. Market rates in Dubai run from AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online on Unitors' published figures, to AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit on Bestimate's and independent home tutors' rates, and AED 650 at the premium end with BartyED. The honest way to read that ladder is by how much becomes verifiable as you climb it. At the bottom you can verify the permit and little else. In the middle you can verify code experience and mark-scheme fluency. At the top you are frequently paying for a reputation that cannot be checked at all.

Several things in this market are asserted and should not be believed without evidence. Self-published star ratings are one: competitors in this cluster show 4.92 out of 5 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 on the same page, and one shows 5.0 from 20 reviews alongside a claim about a far larger student body. Examiner status is another, and a tutor's current examiner role is not something a platform can usually evidence, nor does it grant any access to marking or boundaries. Regulator approval is the third and most dangerous: no tutoring platform in this market is approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, and any page implying otherwise has told you something important about itself.

IB Gram delivers to JLT as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We hold no UAE office and do not offer home visits in Dubai, since those run only in India. Removing distance from the equation is the point rather than a limitation: the shortlist for your child's subject and code is drawn from people who have taught it, and every claim on this page is one you can test in a fifteen-minute conversation before agreeing to anything.

That is precisely why a neighbour's recommendation is weaker evidence here than the code question.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: The stakes rise and so does the value of verifying the honesty boundary rather than the credentials. Internal assessment, the Extended Essay and coursework all create pressure to cross a line, and the only protection a family has is a tutor who stated the boundary before it was tested. Ask the question at IGCSE, because the habits form here and the consequences land later.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving JLT run both A Levels and the IB Diploma with different published entry thresholds. Ask the school for those thresholds before deciding how much IGCSE support to fund; the number tells you exactly how far your child needs to travel and in which subject, which is also what a tutor needs to know.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency
programmes.ageRange: At the end of the school route
programmes.description: For the British track a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. That rule is verifiable on the authority's own channels, which is where to read it.
programmes.countryNote: IB Gram does not perform, arrange or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it. A page implying that a family needs tutoring to achieve equivalency is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process, which is itself a reason to distrust the rest of the page.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the third column is what a competent tutor should be able to tell you in the first conversation without seeing any work. If they cannot, they have not taught the code, whatever the profile says.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: They should be able to say which papers your child's tier sits, which is calculator and which is not, and that method marks are forfeited by unshown working. A tutor who talks about mathematics in general and never mentions the tier has not taught the entry.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: They should name how practical skills are assessed on their board and should be unsurprised that electricity is the commonest reported weakness. Ask what they would do about circuit reasoning specifically; a general answer about more questions is not an answer.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: They should mention moles calculations and organic naming unprompted as the two places marks concentrate relative to teaching time, and should know that the expected style of working differs between the boards' mark schemes.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: They should talk about command terms before they talk about content, because that is what discriminates at this level. A tutor who proposes to re-teach the syllabus from the start is proposing the most expensive possible plan.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: They should distinguish retrieval from inference in the reading questions and should ask to see a marked writing response rather than a sample of free writing. Marks here are structural, so the diagnosis has to come from a marked script.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: They should confirm the code first, because this is a different paper set from first-language English with listening and speaking components. A tutor who treats the two interchangeably will teach the wrong paper well.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: They should name the evaluation marks at the end of extended answers as the usual loss, and should be able to describe what an evaluative sentence looks like. If the answer is about revision notes, the diagnosis is wrong.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: They should mention pseudocode conventions and trace tables, and should know that a confident programmer can still lose heavily on the written paper. Ask how they would mark a trace table; the answer is specific or it is nothing.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main course by students heading for A Level or Higher Level mathematics. A tutor should be able to say how it changes Year 12 readiness, because that is the only reason to take it.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: As organised by the school under KHDA requirements
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. Any tutor here should say that support follows the school's own material, since additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jlt.regionsIntro: These notes are about what a nearby search actually returns in each community, and what time a session can realistically start. Both matter more than the distance figure a map gives you.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Lettered clusters around four lakes with visitor registration at most towers. A distance search here returns people working across the whole Marina corridor rather than inside JLT, so the apparent locality is thinner than it looks.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Shares JLT's search radius almost entirely, which means a near-me search from either address returns substantially the same list. If a neighbour's recommendation is in that list, the code question still applies.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: The beachfront strip past the Marina. Distance searches from here return the same corridor, with the added friction that the drive in from Sheikh Zayed Road is the slowest leg of it at 17:00.

regions.name: The Greens
regions.note: Closer to the Al Barsha campuses, so a 16:30 start is realistic. Local searches return more school-adjacent tutors here, which is convenient and still says nothing about the syllabus code.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Adjacent to The Greens with lighter golf-course-side traffic. Weekend sessions are common here in Year 11, which widens the pool considerably compared with a weekday slot.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Immediately south of JLT with a large resident population and a different school mix. Demand concentrates on mathematics and the sciences, so those are the codes to verify most carefully.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: A school destination rather than a residential base for most JLT families. Tutors who market themselves as near a school here are near the campus, not near your home, which are different claims.

regions.name: Barsha South
regions.note: The longest school route from JLT. Students are home latest, so a near-me search filtered to an early slot excludes exactly the people who could have taught the subject.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Barsha South campuses
schoolClusters.note: The main destination cluster for JLT secondary students. Boards and codes vary by campus rather than by neighbourhood, which is why verification has to be per child rather than per area.

schoolClusters.city: Marina, Al Sufouh and Emirates Hills campuses
schoolClusters.note: The second cluster for JLT families, with several schools running IGCSE before a split into A Levels or the Diploma. Published post-16 thresholds differ between them and are worth collecting before funding Year 11 work.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim campuses
schoolClusters.note: A longer run chosen for curriculum rather than proximity. Families here most often verify against a weekend slot rather than a weekday one, which changes who is available.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jlt.modesIntro: Three ways to begin, ordered by how much you can verify before committing. The first is the one to use if you have never hired a tutor, because it produces evidence rather than a contract.

modes.title: The screening conversation, then a trial
modes.description: Fifteen minutes on the five checks, then one free trial lesson with no card details required. Nothing is agreed in either. The purpose is to collect evidence: did they ask for the code, could they read the mock, did they state the coursework boundary without being pushed. A tutor who passes that and then teaches a good trial lesson has been verified about as far as a parent can verify anyone.

It is the cheapest way to test whether a verified tutor also works for your particular child, and it has a hard stop, so the decision to continue is a decision rather than a default.

modes.description: Six to ten sessions on the specific component where marks are going, worked under timed conditions and marked against the published criteria for the right board. This is where most IGCSE value sits once the diagnosis is known, and it is the format a verified specialist should be proposing rather than an open weekly slot.

sections.heading: Why distance is the weakest filter you can apply
paragraphs: A near-me search ranks by a quantity that does not appear anywhere in your child's grade. It is a proxy, and proxies are fine when nothing better exists. Here something better exists and takes one message to obtain: the board, syllabus code and tier for every subject, which the school's examinations officer will confirm. Filter on that and the list changes completely.

The cost of filtering on distance is specific and measurable. You eliminate every specialist who cannot reach Jumeirah Lakes Towers by 17:00, which at IGCSE level is most of the people who have taught your child's code through several series. You retain people whose main qualification is geography. Then you pay the in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, for the privilege of having applied the weaker filter.

There is also a subtler cost. A tutor hired on proximity is in a weak position to be replaced, because the replacement has to satisfy the same radius. Families end up keeping an adequate local tutor through a year when they would have changed an online one in a fortnight. The table below sets out each filter a parent might apply, what it actually predicts, and what it costs to get wrong.

None of this argues that in-person teaching has no value. For a seven-year-old learning handwriting, presence is most of the lesson. For IGCSE, where the work is a marked script, a past paper and a shared screen, presence is the most expensive component of the invoice and the least load-bearing part of the lesson.

sections.heading: The five checks, and what good looks like on each
paragraphs: Verification only works if the checks are things a non-specialist can perform. These five are. None requires subject expertise, none requires a reference, and all five can be completed before money moves. They also work on any provider, not only on us, which is the point of publishing them.

The permit is the cleanest. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service called 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask to see it. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, treat any quoted amount with suspicion.

The code check is the one that cannot be bluffed. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 will say things about expected working in moles calculations that a tutor who has not cannot improvise. The mock-script check is the one that saves the most money, because it distinguishes a diagnostician from someone who will propose re-teaching the syllabus. And the coursework boundary check is the one that matters most later, when Year 12 arrives and the pressure to cross a line becomes real.

The fifth check is about the offer itself. A free trial should be free of condition, and if conditions exist they belong on the same screen as the word free: trial length, eligibility, and whether card details are required. Ours is one full lesson, with no card details required. Any provider unwilling to state the conditions plainly has answered a different question than the one you asked.

Ask what they would refuse to do

Ask what the free lesson requires

sections.heading: What the tutor permit proves, and what it does not
paragraphs: The permit is the only credential in this market that a parent can verify without specialist knowledge, which makes it valuable and also makes it over-read. It establishes that an individual is legally permitted to provide private tuition in the UAE. It says nothing whatsoever about subject knowledge, teaching ability or familiarity with your child's syllabus code, and a tutor who offers it as evidence of quality has misunderstood it.

Eligibility is deliberately broad. The permit covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. A permitted tutor may therefore be a head of department with twenty years of Cambridge experience or a seventeen-year-old. Both are lawful; only one can read your child's mock script.

Two boundaries sit alongside it. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific authorisation issued to organisations with premises, and no individual tutor permit confers it. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct pointing the same way, so an arrangement with your child's own teacher is not one to pursue.

The claim to watch for is the inverse of the permit: approval. No platform in this market, including this one, is approved, accredited, licensed or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Those bodies regulate and award; they do not endorse tutoring companies. A page claiming otherwise is either confused or misrepresenting, and both are reasons to stop reading it.

sections.heading: Price per verified credential, bottom to top
paragraphs: If verification is the frame, then the sensible way to read the price ladder is by what becomes checkable at each rung. At the bottom tier, AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, you can verify the permit and the subject background and little else, which is appropriate for Year 8 homework and inadequate for a Year 11 entry.

In the qualified band at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB, code experience and mark-scheme fluency become checkable, because a tutor at that level can discuss the specific paper and the specific loss. This is the band where the five checks all return real answers, and for Years 10 and 11 it is where the money belongs.

Above it the picture inverts. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, a band that overlaps the qualified online band entirely while adding nothing verifiable: travel is not a credential. Specialist exam-year rates at AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, do buy deeper board familiarity. The premium tier at AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650, is largely reputation, and reputation is the one thing on this page a parent cannot check.

These are market figures published by the providers named, with the dates and sources attributed, and none of them is an IB Gram price. Our own position is a free trial lesson and a consultation that sets the plan before a figure is agreed, which is itself a verifiable claim: you will know whether it was true by the end of the first conversation.

sections.heading: The fifteen-minute script for a first conversation
paragraphs: Verification is easier with a script, because the questions that produce evidence are not the questions that come naturally. The natural question is how a tutor would help, which invites a sales answer. The useful questions are narrow and factual, and a good tutor enjoys them because they are the questions a teacher would ask themselves.

Open with the code. 'My child sits Cambridge 0580 Extended. Which papers is that, and what do you see students lose marks on?' Then the mock. 'I can send you a marked script. Can you tell me which question types the marks went on?' Then the boundary. 'If my child sent you a finished piece of coursework and asked you to fix it, what would you do?' Then the permit. Then the trial conditions. Five questions, fifteen minutes, nothing bought.

What you are listening for is specificity and the willingness to say no. A tutor who says a subject is fine at both tiers, who proposes to start from the beginning of the syllabus, who treats the coursework question as a request for a service, or who cannot say how long the free lesson lasts has failed the screen. A tutor who says they have not taught that board and would rather you found someone who has, has passed it in the most useful way available.

Finish by asking what they would do if the first six sessions did not move anything. The honest answer involves changing the method or standing down, not adding hours. That question is the one most likely to produce an uncomfortable pause, and the pause is information.
bullets: Open with the syllabus code and tier, not with the grade you want
Offer a marked mock and ask where the marks went
Ask what they would refuse to do with a finished piece of coursework
Ask to see the permit and ask what the free lesson requires
Ask what happens if six sessions change nothing

sections.heading: What a marked mock tells you that a profile cannot
paragraphs: A mock script is the best diagnostic instrument a JLT parent owns and most families never use it for anything except reading the grade. Cover the grade and read only the places where marks were not awarded. The pattern is usually obvious within ten minutes and it points at one of two completely different purchases.

If the working is largely right and marks are still missing, the problem is technique: unshown method, a misread command word, an answer that explained where it should have evaluated, a unit left off. Technique is cheap to fix, moves fast, and needs six to ten sessions at most. If the working stops early or goes somewhere unrelated, the problem is content, which is slower, more expensive, and the one case where a standing weekly slot across Years 10 and 11 can be justified.

Hand the same script to a prospective tutor and the second diagnostic begins, this time of them. A tutor who has taught the code reads it the way you just did and says something specific within a minute. A tutor who has not asks for more context, talks about building confidence, and proposes a full syllabus review. That is not dishonesty; it is the honest output of someone who cannot see what is in front of them, and it will cost you a term to discover any other way.

Keep both outputs. The script, your own reading of it, and the tutor's reading form a record you can compare against the next marked assessment, which is the only review point worth using. A calendar date is not evidence. A second script is.
bullets: Cover the grade and read only the unawarded marks
Right working with missing marks means technique: six to ten sessions
Working that stops early means content: a longer, costlier plan

sections.heading: The regulator, the inspection band, and what a school report means
paragraphs: Parents verifying a tutor often want to verify the school too, and the published evidence there is real. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the Ministry of Education.

Dubai's market context is published too, and it is useful for calibration. In 2024-25 the emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37%, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7% of enrolment. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

A band is a judgement about a school, not about your child's subject. A Good school can have a weak department and an Outstanding one can have a difficult year group. The useful move is to read the inspection report's subject-level commentary rather than the headline band, and then ask the subject teacher the narrow question about papers and question types. Verification works the same way at school level as at tutor level: specific and checkable beats a summary judgement.

One thing not to read into a band: it has no bearing on tutoring. No inspection rating approves, recommends or validates any tutoring provider, and no tutoring provider can claim standing from one. The bands are a parent's tool for choosing and monitoring a school, and that is the whole of their use here.

sections.heading: Claims that should end a conversation
paragraphs: Some answers are disqualifying rather than merely weak, and knowing them in advance saves a term. An offer to produce assessed work is the clearest. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and buying one is an academic-integrity breach that triggers a malpractice process against the student, not the seller. Any provider who treats a finished draft as a job rather than as the student's own work should be left where you found them.

A claim of regulator approval is the second. No tutoring platform in this market is approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. The KHDA Educational Services Permit exists, but it is issued to training institutes with premises and a permit number, so a page claiming the status without the number is making it up.

A self-published star rating is the third. Rivals in this cluster publish 4.92 out of 5 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 on the same page, and one shows 5.0 from 20 reviews against a claim of a far larger student body. Self-serving review markup is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. A promised grade is the fourth, and no honest provider sells one. The fifth is a statistic with no sample size, date or method attached, which is simply a number someone liked.

The last is more subtle and worth naming because it is common here: a UAE page with a non-UAE conversion path. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, and one shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page. We hold no UAE office and say so; what we will not do is display one we do not occupy.
bullets: An offer to produce coursework: disqualifying, and the student carries the consequence
Regulator approval claimed without a permit number: made up

Any statistic with no sample size, date or method: ignore it

sections.heading: Starting from JLT, with everything we have claimed testable
paragraphs: Send three things: the school, the board and syllabus code with the tier, and a marked mock if you have one. We propose a tutor who has taught that code, with a slot set after the commute home to Jumeirah Lakes Towers rather than during it, and you take a free trial lesson that costs nothing and requires no card details. Matching takes two to four working days for mainstream IGCSE subjects.

Run your five checks on whoever we propose. Ask for the permit, ask which codes and how many series, send the script and ask what they see, ask what they would refuse to do with a finished piece of coursework, and ask what the trial involves. If an answer is weak, say so and we propose someone else. A provider that publishes a verification checklist and then fails it has published an unusually effective argument against itself.

Where we cannot help, we say so at the enquiry stage. Mathematics, the three sciences, English, Economics, Business and Computer Science are normally staffed in UAE evening hours. A less common language, a specialist art or design option or an unusual code sometimes is not, and we will tell you rather than placing a general tutor against a specialist brief. For Arabic and Islamic Education, support follows the school's own material, because additional content needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

The review point is the next marked school assessment, not a date. If the script has moved, the block is finished and we close it. If it has not, we change the method or the tutor and tell you which, rather than extending an approach that did not land. Everything in that sentence is checkable by you with a second mock script, which is the point.
bullets: Send the school, the code and tier, and a marked mock
Free trial lesson, no card details, before anything is agreed
Run the five checks on whoever is proposed, including ours

process.title: Get the code and tier in writing
process.description: From the examination entry statement or the examinations officer, for every subject. This replaces a distance filter with a filter that predicts something. It takes one message and it is the single highest-value action available to a parent in this market.

process.title: Find and photograph a marked mock
process.description: One script with the marks visible is worth more than any profile. You will read it yourself for technique against content, and you will use it to test whoever you speak to. Keep it; it becomes the baseline for the review later.

process.title: Run the fifteen-minute screen
process.description: Code, mock, coursework boundary, permit, trial conditions. Five questions, nothing bought. The willingness to say no is as informative as any answer, and a tutor who tells you they have not taught your board has given you the most useful reply available.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session at no cost with no card details required. Ask your child afterwards what the tutor did rather than whether they liked them. A session where something specific was fixed is a different signal from a session that went pleasantly.

process.title: Buy a block, then review against a second script
process.description: Four diagnostic sessions or a six to ten session paper block, with a stated end. The review is the next marked assessment compared with the baseline script, not a conversation at a month's end. If nothing moved, the method or the tutor changes.

whyPoints.title: We publish the checks that test us too
whyPoints.description: The five verification points on this page apply to any provider, including this one. A checklist that only flatters the publisher is marketing; one you can turn around and run on us is evidence. Run it on whoever we propose.

whyPoints.title: Proposed against a syllabus code
whyPoints.description: We ask for the board, code and tier before naming anybody, because Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different examinations. Exactly one syllabus code appeared across the whole area cluster researched for this project, which indicates how rarely that question gets asked here.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no self-published star rating, no examiner status we cannot stand behind, no statistic without its sample size, date and method. That list removes most of what this market's pages are made of, which is the reason to publish it.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and absence stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram holds no UAE office and runs no home visits in Dubai; those operate only in India. A UAE page should say where its conversion path leads rather than route you abroad quietly.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary in writing
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria, question approaches and give feedback on the student's own drafts. Nobody produces an assessed piece. A ranking competitor in this market sells completed coursework, so the boundary needs stating rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: Coverage disclosed before you commit
whyPoints.description: If we cannot staff your subject or code this term we say so at enquiry, rather than placing a general tutor and letting a mock reveal it in March. No competitor researched for this project publishes a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE tutors are realistically within reach of a JLT tower?
faqs.answer: Fewer than a map suggests, and the number is the wrong thing to count. A distance search from Jumeirah Lakes Towers returns people working across the whole Marina corridor, filtered to those who can arrive by about 17:00 on a school night. That filter removes most tutors who have taught your child's specific syllabus code through several series, and keeps those whose strongest qualification is geography. Filtering on the board, code and tier instead takes one message to the examinations officer and produces a shortlist that predicts something about the grade.

faqs.question: What can I actually verify about a tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Five things, none needing subject expertise. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, which you ask to see. The syllabus codes they have taught and for how many series. Whether they can read a marked mock and name the paper and question type where marks went. What they would refuse to do with a finished piece of coursework. And what the free trial actually requires, including length and whether card details are needed. Everything else on a tutoring profile is assertion, and in this market several of the common assertions contradict themselves on the same page.

faqs.question: Does a MoHRE permit mean the tutor knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating the two is the commonest misreading in this market. The permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, establishes that someone is legally permitted to provide private tuition in the UAE. Eligibility covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A permitted tutor may be a head of department or a seventeen-year-old. Both are lawful; only one can diagnose a Cambridge 0580 Extended script.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor in the first fifteen minutes?
faqs.answer: Five narrow questions and nothing about outcomes. Which papers does my child's code and tier sit, and what do students lose marks on. Can I send you a marked script, and what do you see in it. If my child sent you finished coursework and asked you to fix it, what would you do. May I see your MoHRE permit. What does the free lesson involve and require. Then one more: what happens if six sessions change nothing. The honest answer involves changing method or standing down, never adding hours.

faqs.question: Is a nearby tutor worth more than a specialist in another time zone?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE work, usually less. The lesson consists of a marked script, a past paper and a shared screen, all of which transfer to video without loss, so presence is the most expensive line on the invoice and the least load-bearing part of the teaching. In-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The practical constraint on a distant specialist is the clock, not the quality: the session has to land in a workable evening slot for both sides.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor has really taught our exam board?
faqs.answer: Ask for the codes and then listen for detail they could not improvise. Someone who has taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry will say specific things about expected working in moles calculations; someone who has not will talk about chemistry in general. Then send a marked mock from that board and ask what they see. A tutor who has taught the code reads it within a minute and names the question type. A tutor who has not asks for context and proposes a full syllabus review, which is the most expensive plan available.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection band actually tell me?
faqs.answer: It is a judgement about a school, not about a department or your child's subject. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. A Good school can carry a weak department and an Outstanding one can have a difficult year group. Read the subject-level commentary in the report rather than the headline band, then ask the subject teacher the narrow question about papers and question types. No band endorses any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Should I believe a tutor who says they are an examiner?
faqs.answer: Not without evidence, and be careful what the claim is being used to imply. Current examiner status is rarely something a platform can evidence for an individual, and it confers no access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. If someone offers examiner status as a reason to pay a premium, ask which board, which series and who appointed them. The useful version of that experience shows up as fluency in how answers are credited, which you can test directly by handing them a marked script.

faqs.question: What does a marked mock tell me that a tutor's CV does not?
faqs.answer: Everything that matters about the next purchase. Cover the grade and read only the unawarded marks. If the working is right and marks are missing, the problem is technique: six to ten sessions, fast movement, cheap. If the working stops early or wanders, the problem is content: a longer and costlier plan, and the one case where a standing weekly slot across Years 10 and 11 is justified. A CV cannot tell you which of those two you have, and the script tells you in ten minutes for nothing.

faqs.question: Which claims on a tutoring website should I simply ignore?
faqs.answer: Self-published star ratings, because rivals in this cluster show 4.92 out of 5 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 on one page. Any claim of regulator approval without a permit number, since the KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises. Any promise of a particular grade. Any statistic with no sample size, date or method. And any UAE page whose conversion path is a non-UAE phone number, which two ranking competitors in this market use. None of those are close calls.

faqs.question: How much should a verified subject specialist cost for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The band where all five checks return real answers is the qualified online tier at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. Below it, at AED 33 to 65, you can verify the permit and the subject background and little else. Above it, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 add travel rather than a credential, and the premium tier at AED 500 to 650 is largely reputation. IB Gram quotes after a free trial and a consultation rather than publishing a flat rate.

faqs.question: Can I speak to another JLT parent before committing?
faqs.answer: You can ask, and you should weigh the answer carefully, because a neighbour's recommendation is weaker evidence here than people expect. Campuses across Al Barsha, Barsha South, Al Sufouh and the Marina enter students against different boards, so two children in the same tower can sit different codes in the same subject. A tutor excellent for one may be teaching the other the wrong board's habits. Use a recommendation to shorten the list and then run the code check anyway; it is the step the recommendation cannot replace.

faqs.question: Is the free trial lesson genuinely free, with no conditions?
faqs.answer: Ours is one full lesson at no cost with no card details required, and the conditions belong on the same screen as the word free, which is why they are stated here. When any provider offers a free trial, ask three things: how long it is, who is eligible, and whether payment details are collected first. If those answers are not given plainly, the offer is not plainly free. A trial that ends with you deciding against the tutor has worked exactly as intended and should cost nothing.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we verified becomes unavailable?
faqs.answer: You get told, and you re-run the checks on the replacement rather than inheriting them. Continuity matters at IGCSE because a tutor who has read your child's scripts carries context that a new one does not, so a mid-block change is a real cost and we will say so rather than presenting it as routine. Where a replacement is necessary we propose someone who has taught the same code, hand over the session notes and the baseline script, and expect you to screen them the same way you screened the first.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor at all, or is this a conversation with the school?
faqs.answer: Start with the school, because it is free and better informed. Ask the subject teacher which paper and question type is losing marks and what should be practised, and ask what clinics, workshops and mock feedback already run; most Dubai secondary schools run several. Those fees, which KHDA confirmed will not rise for private schools in the emirate in 2026-27, already cover a good deal of support. If the answer is a specific technique gap the school cannot staff individually, that is the moment a short paid block earns its place.

intro.heading: Start from the syllabus code, because everything else follows from it
paragraphs: Most IGCSE tutoring goes wrong at the first question, and the first question is not about the student. It is: which syllabus is your child entered for? A family in Jumeirah 1 searching for an IGCSE tutor near me will be offered plenty of people who teach IGCSE maths. Far fewer will ask whether that means Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1, and the difference is not cosmetic. From 2025, Cambridge 0580 candidates sit a non-calculator paper; Edexcel 4MA1 candidates may use a calculator on both papers. A term of revision built on the wrong assumption wastes the term.

The same fork runs through every subject. Cambridge grades IGCSE on an A* to G scale; Pearson grades International GCSE on 9 to 1. Cambridge sciences carry a practical component, either a laboratory test or an alternative-to-practical written paper; Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical skills inside the theory papers instead. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in many subjects, which cap the available grade; Edexcel offers Foundation and Higher tiers in maths with different grade ranges. None of this is obscure, and all of it is published, but it decides what a tutor should spend ten weeks doing.

So this page is built around the content rather than around the neighbourhood. It names codes, sets out paper structures, works through the command words that mark schemes actually reward, explains how past-paper practice should be run so it produces diagnosis rather than reassurance, and covers the practical-skills question that online tutoring has to answer honestly. It also sets out the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides which five IGCSE subjects count when your child applies to a UAE university, because one competitor page currently publishes the wrong subject count.

On delivery, the position is plain. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a Jumeirah 1 household that is usually an advantage rather than a compromise, because the schools along this coastal corridor split between Cambridge and Pearson entries, and a tutor chosen from a board-specific pool rather than from whoever drives down Jumeirah Beach Road is more likely to have marked the paper your child is about to sit.

One more framing point before the detail. An IGCSE grade is not a measure of how much a student knows; it is a measure of how many marks they collected under timed conditions against a published scheme. Those are different things, and the gap between them is where tutoring earns its money. A student who understands electrolysis and writes four lines when the question says 'explain' has not been let down by their knowledge.

subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides the grade more than content does. sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: find out before you buy anything
paragraphs: Dubai schools entering students for an international GCSE choose between Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, and some split by subject, entering Cambridge sciences and Edexcel mathematics or the reverse. The school's exams officer knows; the student frequently does not. Ask for the board and the five-character syllabus code per subject, and write them down, because every sensible decision after this one depends on them.

The structural differences are real. Cambridge grades IGCSE A* to G and Pearson grades International GCSE 9 to 1, so comparing a cousin's result across boards is comparing two scales. Cambridge sciences carry a separate practical assessment, either a laboratory test or an alternative-to-practical written paper; Pearson International GCSE sciences assess practical understanding inside the theory papers. In mathematics, Cambridge 0580 candidates face a non-calculator paper from 2025 while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers, which changes what arithmetic fluency is worth.

Series availability differs too. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and in the UAE those are the only two a candidate can enter, because the February and March series is offered in India only. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests do run in March, May and October, but a Checkpoint is a lower-secondary diagnostic rather than an IGCSE sitting. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The practical consequence for a Jumeirah 1 family is that a retake window exists on either board within the same academic year, but the entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and missing one costs a whole series rather than a few weeks.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, and the grade ceiling nobody mentions
paragraphs: Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in a number of IGCSE subjects, and the tier a student is entered for sets the highest grade available before the exam is sat. This is the single most consequential administrative decision in Year 10, and it is frequently made on the basis of a mock result taken when half the syllabus had not been taught. A Core entry protects a student who would otherwise fail; it also removes the top grades from reach, which closes some A Level and Diploma doors.

The honest version of the decision is arithmetic rather than ambition. An Extended paper is longer, carries harder questions and demands more complete method. A student who can attempt eighty per cent of an Extended paper competently will usually do better there than on Core. A student who is still shaky on the Core content will produce an Extended script with large blank spaces, and blank spaces score nothing. The question to ask is not which tier sounds better but which paper the student can finish.

Pearson International GCSE handles this differently, with single-tier entry in the sciences and Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics carrying different grade ranges. So a family moving a child between a Cambridge school and a Pearson school mid-course is not only changing syllabus content but changing whether the tier question exists at all. That is a specific, checkable thing to raise with the new school's exams officer in the first week rather than the first term.

sections.heading: The command words that actually decide the mark
paragraphs: A mark scheme does not reward knowing things. It rewards producing the specific response the command word asks for, in the number of marks available. This is the most reliable source of recoverable marks in the whole IGCSE, and it is the part of the course least likely to be taught deliberately, because teachers under time pressure prioritise content coverage. A student who loses four marks a paper to command-word errors is losing most of a grade to something fixable in three weeks.

The pattern is consistent across subjects. State and give want a fact with no justification and no padding. Describe wants what happens, in order, without explanation. Explain wants a causal chain with because or therefore doing real work in it. Compare wants both items addressed in the same sentence rather than in separate paragraphs. Evaluate wants both sides and then a judgement, and the judgement is where the final marks sit. Calculate wants working, because method marks survive an arithmetic slip and a bare wrong answer does not.

The diagnostic habit worth building is counting. If a question offers four marks, four distinct scoring points are expected, and a student who has written two sentences has probably collected two marks regardless of how good the sentences are. Teaching a student to read the mark allocation as an instruction about length is a ten-minute intervention that pays for itself in the first mock.

sections.heading: Where marks go in each subject, specifically
paragraphs: In mathematics the recurring losses are premature rounding, method abandoned mid-question, and the non-calculator paper treated as a calculator paper without the calculator. Cambridge 0580 Extended candidates sitting a non-calculator paper from 2025 need genuine arithmetic fluency, including fraction and surd work, and students who have spent two years with a calculator in hand find that out late. Edexcel 4MA1 candidates face different pressure: a calculator on both papers raises the expectation of multi-step modelling questions.

In the sciences the losses cluster around units, significant figures and the gap between describing and explaining. A physics candidate who reads a gradient without stating its units has done the hard part and dropped the mark. A chemistry candidate who writes an unbalanced ionic equation or omits state symbols loses marks that have nothing to do with understanding the reaction. A biology candidate who writes a beautiful paragraph in answer to a two-mark 'state' question has spent five minutes buying nothing.

In English the losses are structural. Directed-writing tasks specify a form, an audience and a purpose, and a response in the wrong form is capped however well written it is. Reading-response questions want precise textual reference, which means short quotations used as evidence rather than long quotations used as decoration. In business and economics the ceiling is almost always the missing judgement: a student who sets out advantages and disadvantages and then stops has written the first two thirds of a full-mark answer.
These are patterns, not predictions. The point of marking real scripts against real schemes is to find out which of them applies to your child, because the remedy for one is useless against another.

sections.heading: How past-paper work should actually be run
paragraphs: Most past-paper practice is wasted because it is done in the wrong order. A student works through a paper with the mark scheme open, feels broadly fine about it, and learns nothing. The sequence that produces information is: sit the questions under time, close everything, mark against the published scheme, record the error type rather than the topic, and only then go back and teach the gap. Marking before teaching is what makes the practice diagnostic.

Timing deserves separate attention. Running out of time is not a content problem and cannot be fixed by revising content, but it is routinely treated that way. The fix is per-question pacing practice: give a student a four-mark question and five minutes, then three, then two, until the pace is internal. Students who have never been timed on single questions discover in the exam hall that their reading speed is the binding constraint.

The third element is the error log. A single sheet, one line per recurring mistake, revisited at the start of every session. It will contain five to eight entries, not fifty, and it will be remarkably stable. When the same entry stops appearing for three consecutive sessions it can be struck out, and that is a far better progress measure than a percentage on a paper, because the paper's difficulty varies and the error pattern does not.

One caution. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and the right way to use them is through the school or the board's own published materials. We reference and point to official sources rather than reproducing or supplying them, which is both a copyright matter and a reason to make sure your child is working from the version their series actually uses.

sections.heading: Practical science assessment when the tutoring is online
paragraphs: This is the honest difficulty with online science tutoring, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a reassurance. Cambridge IGCSE sciences carry a practical component: candidates sit either a laboratory practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which one depends on what the centre offers. Pearson International GCSE sciences assess practical understanding inside the written papers instead. In neither case does a tutor on video run an experiment with your child.

What the assessment actually tests, though, is largely written. The alternative-to-practical paper asks candidates to read instruments, tabulate results, plot and interpret graphs, identify variables, spot sources of error and suggest improvements. Every one of those is a paper skill, and every one of them is teachable over a shared screen using real data sets. Students who have done the experiments in school and never practised writing up the analysis lose marks in exactly this component.

Where the laboratory test applies, the school's own practical programme is the irreplaceable part, and a tutor's job is to make sure the student understands what they did and why, so that the write-up and the interpretation hold up. A tutor who claims to substitute for school laboratory work is overselling. A tutor who takes a student's own results table and shows them why their uncertainty treatment lost two marks is doing the part that is actually missing.

The practical question a parent should ask is therefore narrow: which component is my child entered for, and are we working on the skills that component measures? The answer is in the syllabus, and it changes what ten weeks of tutoring should contain.

sections.heading: The five subjects that count for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: Families in Dubai whose children may apply to a UAE university or need a certificate attested run into equivalency, and the British-track rule is specific. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That exclusion is the part most commonly got wrong. One ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five accredited subjects, with Arabic and Islamic education sitting outside that count. For a student choosing options in Year 9, the difference decides whether the timetable has room for an extra subject. Check it against the Ministry's own guidance before acting on any version of it, including this one.

For completeness, the American track works differently: English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold has been published on an official source we could read, so any page quoting one should be treated with scepticism until it is checked on the Ministry's own site.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation. It is a regulatory process run by the authorities, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. The reason it appears on this page at all is that the five-subject rule changes which IGCSE subjects a student should protect in Year 11, and that is a tutoring decision.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not do, and how a Jumeirah 1 week is actually scheduled
paragraphs: Two practical matters to close on. The first is boundaries. Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or controlled assessment, and where they do, the work is assessed as the student's own. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, question a weak argument and show a student how to reference properly. A tutor may not supply text that becomes part of a submitted piece. The test is whether every word on the page was generated by the student, and this market contains operators who fail that test for money.

Nor should any tutoring provider claim regulatory approval it does not hold. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises; individual private tutoring runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. IB Gram holds no regulator's approval and does not describe itself as approved, licensed or accredited by one. Ask any provider who does to show the number.

The second matter is the week itself. A Jumeirah 1 family's realistic constraint is the afternoon: the school-gate congestion on Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road runs well past 15:00, and students living on Pearl Jumeira or coming back from inland schools arrive home later than the map suggests. Because lessons are delivered over video, a slot at 18:30 or 19:30 starts at that minute and does not depend on anybody completing a journey. The slot holds through school holidays, shifts for travel, and moves to a post-Iftar time during Ramadan rather than being cancelled.

If you are weighing areas as part of a school decision, the companion pages for Dubai Marina, JBR, JLT, Emirates Hills, The Springs, The Meadows, The Lakes and The Greens cover the same ground for those catchments, and the Jumeirah 1 area page sets out the wider local picture.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the board and the syllabus code for each subject, and write them down. Students often do not know, and the two boards differ in ways that change revision entirely: Cambridge grades A* to G and Pearson grades 9 to 1, Cambridge 0580 includes a non-calculator paper from 2025 while Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers, and the sciences handle practical assessment differently. Some Dubai schools split by subject, entering Cambridge sciences and Edexcel mathematics, so one answer for the whole timetable may not exist.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor near me in Jumeirah 1 need to teach the same board as the school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this matters more than distance. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry knows the practical component and the question styles that go with it; a tutor who has taught Pearson 4CH1 knows a different paper structure. Preparing a student against the wrong specification produces confident revision and a disappointing result. Because IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, the pool is selected on specification experience rather than on who can reach a Jumeirah 1 address, which is what makes board-specific matching possible at all.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between a Core and an Extended entry?
faqs.answer: The tier sets the highest grade available before the paper is sat. Core covers the shared core content with shorter, more structured papers and makes only the lower part of the grade scale reachable. Extended adds the extended content, runs longer papers with more multi-step questions, and makes the top grades available. The decision should be arithmetic rather than aspirational: a student who can attempt most of an Extended paper competently will usually score better there, while one still shaky on core content will hand in a script with blank spaces.

faqs.question: Which command words cost my child the most marks?
faqs.answer: Usually explain, evaluate and compare. Explain wants a causal chain with each link stated, and students write a description with the word because attached. Evaluate wants both sides plus a supported judgement, and students stop before the judgement, which is where the final marks sit. Compare wants both items addressed against the same criterion in the same sentence, not two separate paragraphs. The diagnostic habit that fixes all three is reading the mark allocation as an instruction about how many distinct scoring points to produce.

faqs.question: Is the Cambridge non-calculator maths paper a real change for my child?
faqs.answer: It is, and it catches students who have had a calculator in hand since Year 7. From 2025, Cambridge 0580 candidates sit a non-calculator paper alongside the calculator one, which puts genuine weight on fraction work, indices, surds and mental estimation. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 candidates face the opposite pressure: a calculator on both papers raises the expectation of longer multi-step modelling questions. Either way, the first fortnight of useful tutoring is arithmetic fluency drills, which feels unglamorous and recovers marks faster than anything else available.

faqs.question: What is the right order of operations for working through a past paper?
faqs.answer: Sit the questions under time with everything closed, then mark against the published scheme, then record the type of error rather than the topic, and only then go back and teach the gap. Marking before teaching is what makes the practice diagnostic. Most students do the reverse, work through a paper with the scheme open, feel broadly fine and learn nothing. Pair that with per-question timing practice, because running out of time is not a content problem and cannot be fixed by revising more content.

faqs.question: Can practical science skills be taught if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer depends on the component. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper tests reading instruments, tabulating results, plotting and interpreting graphs, identifying variables and suggesting improvements, and all of that is paper work that transfers perfectly to a shared screen with real data sets. Where a laboratory practical test applies, the school's own practical programme is irreplaceable, and a tutor's job is to make sure the student can analyse and write up what they did. No tutor on video substitutes for a school laboratory.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects count towards UAE equivalency, and are Arabic and Islamic education included?
faqs.answer: The sourced rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited A Level subject at E or two AS Level subjects at E. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor page states that six subjects are needed, which does not match the published guidance. Check the current rule against the Ministry of Education's own material before acting on any version of it, including this one.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held, and how far ahead is the entry deadline?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for lower secondary. There is no spring IGCSE sitting here: the February and March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and its published November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in the new year. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers on both boards, Cambridge closing June entries in the spring and November entries over the summer. Always work from the live official timetable for your centre's zone, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones.

faqs.question: My child joined a Dubai school mid-year and the board changed. What now?
faqs.answer: Do a syllabus audit in the first fortnight, before anything else. A board change alters content coverage, tiering, grade scale and sometimes the practical component, and the topics taught in a different order elsewhere leave gaps that nobody has flagged. Map the new specification's content list against what your child has actually been taught, mark the unmatched items, and work through them in the order the new school's scheme of work will need them. Mid-year arrivals are common in Al Wasl and City Walk, and this audit is what makes the first term survivable.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring if the exams are three months away?
faqs.answer: Not too late to matter, but the plan has to change. Three months is enough to fix technique, command-word discipline, timing and a short list of high-frequency topics, and that can move a grade. It is not enough to teach two years of missing content, and any provider implying otherwise is selling something. The first lessons should therefore be spent identifying the few topics that appear most often in the paper and are most recoverable, and then drilling them under timed conditions rather than attempting full syllabus coverage.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with IGCSE coursework or a controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria ask for, question reasoning that does not hold and show the student how to reference properly. A tutor may not supply text that becomes part of a submitted piece, or return a draft rewritten into a finished state. The test is whether every word on the page was generated by the student. Providers in this market do sell finished work, and a student who submits it risks a malpractice finding, so the boundary is worth stating to any tutor before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Do you cover both tiers of maths, and can you help us decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the decision is settled with evidence rather than opinion. Two lessons with diagnostic questions drawn from both tiers show whether a student completes core-level questions reliably and can attempt harder ones, which is the real signal. We set out the grade range each tier makes available and the progression consequences for Year 12, then leave the entry decision to the family and the school, since the school submits it. We will not push a higher tier for its own sake.

Each profile names the syllabus codes that person teaches, because the code is what decides which papers your child sits and where the marks sit.

intro.heading: The cheapest decision you will make is the one you make before booking anybody
paragraphs: A search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Jumeirah 2 almost always starts after a mock paper comes back. The grade is lower than expected, there are eighteen months or eight weeks left depending on the year group, and the instinct is to find somebody fast and local. That instinct is reasonable and it is also the point at which most money gets committed in the wrong direction. Three decisions that sit on paperwork rather than in a lesson will move your child's final grade more than the choice between one competent tutor and another: the tier they are entered at, the number of subjects they are entered for, and the board whose papers they will actually open.

Those three decisions are made by the school, in consultation with you, and they are reversible only inside a window. A Core entry in Cambridge Mathematics 0580 caps the achievable grade at C. No amount of tuition raises a Core candidate above that ceiling, so AED 250 an hour spent pushing a Core candidate from a D to a C is money well used, and the same AED 250 spent hoping for an A is money spent on something the entry form has already ruled out. Parents in Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim regularly discover this in February of Year 11, when the entry has gone and the deadline has passed.

The subject count is the second one. The British-track equivalency rule the Ministry of Education applies counts five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. One competitor page ranking for this query tells UAE parents that six subjects are required. That is an error with a price attached: a family who funds tutoring across eight subjects to protect a six-subject rule has bought two subjects of support that the equivalency count never asked for, and has thinned the hours available for the subjects that decide a sixth-form offer.

The third is the board. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both run international GCSEs across Dubai, and in the same subject they set different papers, tier differently, and sit in different weeks. A tutor who knows Cambridge Physics 0625 inside out and is handed a child sitting Pearson 4PH1 will teach good physics and mis-time the practical component, because 0625 has a Paper 5 practical test or a Paper 6 alternative-to-practical and 4PH1 does not work that way. Most families in this neighbourhood do not know which board their child's school uses. It is printed on the statement of entry, and it takes one email to the exams officer to confirm.

What follows is written in that order, because that is the order in which the money is decided. The rate bands come in the middle of the page rather than at the top, with the provider who published each figure named, so you can check them yourself. IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Jumeirah 2 households as one-to-one lessons over live video; home visits are a service that exists only in our India operation, and this page does not pretend otherwise. The practical consequence of that is a wider pool: a Jumeirah 2 family gets a 0580 Extended specialist rather than whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive of Beach Road.
