dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Dubai families most often ask about, with the syllabus code and the specific place marks are lost. The code is worth knowing before you book anybody: it decides the paper structure your child will actually face.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Two papers at each tier, one without a calculator and one with, each worth half the grade. Extended candidates lose marks on functions, transformations of graphs and the harder probability work. Core candidates lose them on fraction arithmetic and multi-step percentage problems that the calculator paper assumes are automatic.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, both calculator-permitted, which changes revision priorities compared with Cambridge. Higher tier reaches grade 9; Foundation tops out at 5. The standard loss is in the long multi-mark questions at the end of each paper, where method marks are available and unclaimed because working is not written down.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Extended candidates sit a multiple-choice paper worth 30 per cent, a theory paper worth 50 per cent, and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper worth 20 per cent. The alternative-to-practical paper is where the most recoverable marks sit, because it tests apparatus description, tabulation and graph work rather than content recall.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Same three-component structure as physics. Marks leak in moles and stoichiometry, in writing ionic equations, and in the qualitative-analysis tests, which are memorisable and routinely not memorised. The practical component rewards precise language about controlling variables.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where the failure mode is not knowledge but command terms. A question that says describe is answered with explain, or the other way round, and the mark scheme awards neither. Diagram labelling and data interpretation from unfamiliar graphs make up a predictable slice of the theory paper.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences, Double Award (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics compressed into a double award, taken by students who want science breadth without three separate entries. The depth is lower than the single sciences but the volume is higher, so the tutoring problem is coverage and pacing rather than difficulty.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Widely taken across Dubai and widely underestimated. Reading and writing marks are lost to question-type confusion: summary tasks answered as commentary, and extended writing that ignores the register the task names. Speaking is separately endorsed in 0511.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition, plus reading responses on unseen passages. The single largest recoverable area is the directed-writing task, where form, audience and purpose carry marks that candidates lose by writing a good essay of the wrong kind.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks and are drawn badly under time pressure: unlabelled axes, shifted curves without a new equilibrium marked. The structured questions reward a definition, a diagram and an application in that order, and candidates who write prose without the diagram cap their own score.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study driven, which makes it look easier than it marks. Evaluation marks are only awarded for a judgement supported by the case material, so a generically correct answer that never quotes the business in front of it scores in the lower band.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Two papers, one on computer systems and one on algorithms and programming. Pseudocode questions are where marks concentrate and where practice is thinnest, because schools often teach a language and then examine a notation.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students in Dubai alongside the KHDA-mandated Arabic provision, which is a separate requirement with its own timetable hours. Marks are lost in the writing paper to tense control and to connectives, both of which respond quickly to short, frequent practice.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 2 search for an IGCSE tutor is really asking
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor near me in Jumeirah 2 is a proximity search for a problem that proximity does not solve. The question underneath it is usually one of three: my child's mock grade dropped and I do not know why; my child is entered at a tier I am not sure about; or exams are close and I want somebody who has seen these papers before. Only the first of those is improved by living nearby, and only marginally, because the diagnosis is done on a marked script rather than in a room.

Distance filters out the thing that matters. There are roughly 227 private schools in Dubai and the British curriculum accounts for the largest share of enrolment, so a subject specialist for a particular syllabus code exists somewhere in the city. Whether that person also lives within a twenty-minute drive of Jumeirah Beach Road is close to random. Filtering by postcode first and by syllabus second produces a tutor who is convenient and approximately right, which in a two-year qualification is an expensive combination.

IB Gram answers this search with online one-to-one tuition into Jumeirah 2 households. We do not operate home visits in Dubai; that format is available only through our India operation, and saying so plainly is more useful than implying a coverage we do not have. What a Jumeirah 2 family gains from the online format is selection: the tutor is chosen because they teach Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4PH1 Higher, not because of where they happen to live.

The rest of this page is ordered by where the money goes rather than by what reads well. Tier, subject count and board come first, because those three decisions are made on paperwork and are worth more than any single hour of teaching. The rate bands follow, with sources. The exam calendar comes after that, counted backwards from the series your child will actually sit, which in the UAE is June or November and never February or March.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: what the ministry's equivalency count actually says
paragraphs: The British-track equivalency requirement the Ministry of Education applies, as reported by Gulf Today in July 2026, asks for a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That single rule reorganises a tutoring budget. A Dubai school may enter a candidate for eight or nine IGCSEs for good educational reasons, and a competitive sixth form will look at the best of them. The ministry's count, however, is a floor expressed as five, not a tally of everything sat. Families who fund support across every entered subject are buying insurance against a requirement that does not exist, while the two or three subjects that will decide an A Level offer get a thinner share of the hours.

One ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. It is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that increases spending. Publishing the correct rule, with the source and date attached, is a better use of this page than another paragraph about commitment to excellence. Verify it yourself against the Ministry of Education's own channels before you act on it, because equivalency is administered by the ministry and not by any tutoring provider.

The practical instruction for a Jumeirah 2 household is to write down the five subjects the equivalency count will use, the two or three the intended sixth form actually requires, and the intersection. Tutoring money belongs in the intersection first. Nothing about equivalency requires tutoring at all, and any page that implies it does is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision that sets a ceiling on your spending
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE splits most sciences and mathematics into a Core route and an Extended route, and Pearson Edexcel splits its international GCSEs into Foundation and Higher tiers. The two routes sit different papers from the same syllabus, and the grade range differs. A Cambridge Core candidate in Mathematics 0580 works towards grades in the C to G range; an Extended candidate works in the A* to E range. A Pearson Foundation candidate in 4MA1 tops out at grade 5, where a Higher candidate reaches 9.

This is the single most consequential piece of paperwork in the two years, and most parents in Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim are not shown it directly. The school recommends a tier based on internal assessment, usually late in Year 10. The recommendation is sound more often than not, but it is a judgement made under timetable constraints, and it is not permanent until the entry deadline passes. A child two grades below their working level in January of Year 10 is a child whose tier is still negotiable in June.

The tutoring consequence runs in both directions. A Core candidate who is securely at C has nothing above them to buy, so additional hours should go to another subject, and a provider who keeps selling hours into that position is selling something the entry form has already closed. An Extended candidate sitting at E is in the opposite position: the ceiling is distant and the recoverable marks are concentrated in the papers they are already taking, which is the best possible place to spend.

Ask the exams officer two questions in writing. Which tier is my child currently entered for in each subject, and what is the last date on which that entry can be amended? The answers turn a vague worry into a dated decision, and they tell you exactly how many teaching weeks you have to influence it.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: the same subject, two different purchases
paragraphs: Dubai schools use both awarding bodies, sometimes within one school and occasionally within one subject department. The subject names look identical on a report card. The papers are not. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 assesses practical skills through a separate Paper 5 practical test or a Paper 6 alternative-to-practical paper worth twenty per cent of the grade. Pearson's International GCSE Physics 4PH1 distributes that assessment differently. A tutor who prepares a 4PH1 candidate for an alternative-to-practical paper is preparing them for an exam they will not sit.

Mathematics differs in a way that changes weekly practice. Cambridge 0580 carries a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper at each tier, each worth half the grade. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator in both written papers. A Jumeirah 2 student on 4MA1 who spends a term drilling mental arithmetic is doing something worthwhile and not something the examination rewards, while a 0580 candidate who never practises without a calculator walks into half their grade unprepared.

Grading notation is a third difference and a common source of confusion in Jumeirah households with children in different schools. Cambridge reports some syllabuses on A* to G and others on 9 to 1; Pearson International GCSE reports on 9 to 1. Two siblings can bring home incomparable numbers from the same academic year. The syllabus code on the statement of entry resolves it, and the current paper structure for that code is published on the awarding body's own site.

The instruction is short. Find the code, not the subject name. Send it to anyone you are considering paying, and ask them to describe the papers and weightings back to you before the first lesson. A specialist will answer in one sentence per paper. Anyone who answers in generalities about building confidence is telling you they will find out alongside your child.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in Dubai, read from the cheapest option upwards
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because the bottom is where most families start in practice and where the trade-off is clearest. Platform tuition delivered by university students is advertised in Dubai from around AED 45 to 65 an hour by EdFlik, and Tutopiya publishes rates from roughly AED 33 to 52. At those rates a weekly hour across a full academic year is a small line in a Dubai household budget. What it buys is supervised practice and company, which is genuinely valuable for a child who will not sit down alone, and is not the same thing as diagnosis.

The next band up is where a qualified subject teacher sits. Unitors publishes IGCSE rates from AED 150 an hour and IB rates from AED 200. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. The spread between the floor and the ceiling of this market is roughly fourteen-fold for one hour of a person's time.

In-home delivery sits across those bands with a travel premium attached. Bestimate reports in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors in Dubai are quoted between AED 200 and 500 once travel is priced in. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The premium is not a quality signal; it is a logistics charge, and it is the reason the same teaching hour costs more on Jumeirah Beach Road at five o'clock than it does at nine in the morning.

These are market figures published by the providers named, read in October 2026, and they are not IB Gram's price list. Our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a published hourly rate, because the right number of hours depends on the tier, the board and how far the mock sits from a boundary. What the table below is for is arithmetic: multiply the band you are considering by the weeks you actually have, and compare that against the decisions earlier on this page that cost nothing.

sections.heading: June or November: the two series a UAE candidate actually sits
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series that appears on some tutoring sites is offered to India only, and a UAE family who plans around it has planned around a date their child cannot sit. If you see a February or March exam window quoted for a Dubai school, that page is not written for your country.

Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes a separate timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. For a Jumeirah 2 parent this is a two-minute check with the exams officer, and it is the kind of detail no competitor page in this market mentions.

Pearson Edexcel runs its International GCSEs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results from the June 2026 series reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and results from the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates are published by Pearson and are the reason a November entry is a real option rather than a consolation: a January grade is still in time for most sixth-form processes.

Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November sitting a year or so out, and revises them before they become final. Every date in the table below should be checked against the live official timetable rather than taken from this page, and the table is built backwards from the examination so that a Jumeirah 2 family can see which decisions have already closed. Entry deadlines sit months before the paper, which is why the tier conversation belongs in Year 10 and not in the spring of Year 11.

sections.heading: The timetable hours you are already paying for: Arabic, Islamic education and social studies
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 applying to schools whose year begins in April. For a Jumeirah 2 family this is not a footnote. It is several periods a week that exist on your child's timetable whether or not they appear in any IGCSE entry.

KHDA sets the structure in detail. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic education and social studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

The language rules are specific too. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for social studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic education and in moral, social and cultural studies. KHDA also requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask about directly.

There is a real constraint on tutoring here, and it is worth stating rather than selling around. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support in these subjects therefore means working with the school's own material and the ministry's content, not importing a parallel course. Where a Jumeirah 2 family wants help with Arabic, the honest version is language practice and examination technique inside the framework the school is required to follow.

sections.heading: Four places Jumeirah 2 money goes and nothing comes back
paragraphs: The first is hours bought against a closed ceiling. A Core-tier candidate sitting comfortably at C has no headroom in that subject, and every additional hour there is an hour not spent on the Extended subject where a grade is actually moving. This is the most common waste in this market and the easiest to avoid, because it is visible on the entry form before a single session is booked.

The second is paying for content when the problem is technique. A child who knows the physics and loses twelve marks a paper to command-term confusion, unlabelled axes and unshown working does not need more physics. They need two hours with a mark scheme and somebody who will refuse to accept an unjustified answer. Content teaching is easier to sell and easier to deliver, so it is what gets sold; the diagnostic that distinguishes the two cases takes one marked script.

The third is the wrong board. Every hour spent on a paper structure your child will not sit is wasted at full price, and the failure is invisible until the examination. This is why the syllabus code matters more than the tutor's biography, and why a specialist should be able to recite the papers and weightings for that code before you pay anything.

The fourth is sessions bought and not used. Monthly packages in this market are priced on volume, and a package of eight sessions used four times is twice the advertised hourly rate. Ramadan, the long Dubai summer and the exam-leave period all interrupt a weekly rhythm, and a family paying monthly through those weeks is paying for availability rather than teaching. Ask what happens to an unused session before you commit to a month, and get the answer in writing.

sections.heading: Permits, and what a Jumeirah 2 parent can verify in two minutes
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official service is listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure is quoted here; a number circulating on other tutoring sites could not be verified against any official source. What a parent can do is ask the question, because a tutor operating properly will answer it without hesitation and the permit is free to obtain.

Two further points are worth knowing in Dubai. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not describe itself as KHDA approved, because it would not be true. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, which is reported rather than quoted here and should be checked against the current ADEK policy document.

The reason this sits on a page about cost is that permit status and legal structure are the two things in this market that are free to check and expensive to get wrong. A Jumeirah 2 family can ask about a MoHRE permit, read a school's KHDA inspection rating on KHDA's own site, and confirm a syllabus code with the exams officer, all in an afternoon and at no cost. Those three checks filter the market more effectively than any amount of comparison shopping on hourly rates.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, not the subject
process.description: Give us the code from your child's statement of entry, the tier, and one marked paper. That is enough to tell whether the problem is content, technique or tier, and it is the difference between a diagnosis and a guess. It takes a parent about ten minutes to assemble.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with no card taken
process.description: One full session with the matched specialist before any payment. The condition is simply that it is one lesson per student. You will get a short written note afterwards saying where the marks are being lost and roughly how many weeks it would take to recover them.

process.title: An hours estimate you can argue with
process.description: We put a number of weeks and a number of hours in writing, tied to the series your child is sitting and the distance between the mock mark and the boundary above it. If the honest answer is that the tier caps what is available, we say that instead of selling the hours.

process.title: Weekly sessions over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons run online, one to one, scheduled after the Jumeirah school-bus return rather than before it. Work is set between sessions and marked, because a session that reviews nothing written since the last one is a conversation rather than teaching.

process.title: A review point at six weeks
process.description: Six weeks is long enough for a trend and short enough to change course. If the marked work is not moving, we change the approach, the tutor or the subject allocation. Families who cancel usually do so because nobody offered them a checkpoint.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes rather than subject names
whyPoints.description: We match on 0580, 0625, 4MA1 and 4PH1 because those codes decide the papers. Exactly one syllabus code appeared across the whole seven-page area cluster we researched, which is why a tutor recommended on subject name alone is such a common and expensive mismatch.

whyPoints.title: The board and tier conversation first
whyPoints.description: Before an hour is sold, we ask which tier and which board. That conversation sometimes ends with us saying fewer hours are needed, or that the money belongs in a different subject. It is the part of the process that costs us revenue and saves you some.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the delivery format
whyPoints.description: Lessons into Jumeirah 2 are online and one to one. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, and this page does not use the search phrase to imply otherwise. The gain is a specialist chosen by syllabus rather than by driving distance.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on coursework help
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the student's own work. We will not produce a piece of assessed work, and we will say so to a student who asks. In a market where one competitor sells completed internal assessments, that boundary is worth naming out loud.

whyPoints.title: Regulatory facts, not regulatory decoration
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and MoHRE each do and link to their own pages. We hold no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them, and we never imply one. Naming a regulator is information; borrowing its authority is a misrepresentation.

faqs.question: In Jumeirah 2, how many IGCSE passes does a UAE equivalency file actually need?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement, as reported in July 2026, is a pass in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, paired with one A Level subject at E or two AS Level subjects at E. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A Dubai school may still enter your child for eight or nine subjects for sound educational reasons, and a competitive sixth form will look at more than five. Verify the rule against the ministry's own channels before acting on it, because equivalency is administered by the ministry and not by any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Does paying for tutoring in a sixth or seventh IGCSE subject buy anything?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but not for equivalency. The ministry counts five subjects, so a sixth entry is bought for a different reason: a sixth-form prerequisite, a university route, or a subject your child intends to continue. If the sixth subject is none of those, hours spent there are hours taken from the subjects that will appear on an A Level offer. One competitor page tells UAE parents six subjects are required; that is incorrect and it inflates spending. Write down the five the ministry counts and the two or three your intended sixth form requires, then fund the overlap first.

faqs.question: Is an IGCSE tutor near me in Jumeirah 2 worth paying extra for, and does anyone come to the house?
faqs.answer: Proximity adds very little to IGCSE support and IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Jumeirah 2 address; lessons run one to one over live video. Home visits are available only through our India operation. The Dubai in-home market is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors once travel is priced in, so the premium is a logistics charge rather than a teaching one. What the online format changes is selection: your child gets a specialist in their exact syllabus code instead of whoever is available within a short drive of Beach Road.

faqs.question: What is the real cost difference between a Core and an Extended entry?
faqs.answer: The entry itself is a school matter, but the tutoring consequence is large. Cambridge Core in Mathematics 0580 works towards grades C to G, so a candidate already secure at C has no headroom and additional hours in that subject buy nothing. Extended runs A* to E, which is a wide band with recoverable marks throughout, so hours there have somewhere to go. Pearson is the same shape: Foundation 4MA1 tops out at grade 5 and Higher reaches 9. Ask your exams officer which tier each subject is entered at and when that entry can still be amended.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's school in Jumeirah uses?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the statement of entry your child receives before a series, and the exams officer will confirm it in an email. Ask for the syllabus code, not just the board name, because the code identifies the paper structure: Cambridge Physics 0625 carries a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper worth twenty per cent, where Pearson 4PH1 assesses practical skills differently. Schools in Dubai sometimes use both awarding bodies across different departments, so one answer for maths does not settle science. Send the code to any tutor you are considering and ask them to describe the papers back to you.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor charge per hour in Dubai in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026 span roughly AED 45 to 650. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the platform end. Unitors publishes IGCSE rates from AED 150. Bestimate's Dubai table puts specialist IGCSE, IB and A Level tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium tutor. In-home delivery runs AED 180 to 500 once travel is included. These are market rates from the providers named, not IB Gram prices; our own process starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: How much should we budget across a full Year 10 and Year 11 for one subject?
faqs.answer: Work it as weeks multiplied by the band you are considering. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Two academic years is roughly eighteen teaching months once Dubai's summer and exam-leave weeks are removed. Run that arithmetic before you compare tutors, because the tier and board decisions earlier on this page change the answer more than a difference of AED 50 an hour does.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE examinations actually sat in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any Dubai page quoting a February exam window is not written for your country. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSEs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so confirm your school's zone with the exams officer.

faqs.question: Is the November series a resit or a first entry?
faqs.answer: It can be either, and treating it as a planned route rather than a failure changes how a family spends. Pearson publishes International GCSE examinations in May and June and again in November, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A January grade still arrives in time for most sixth-form processes. For Cambridge, June is the main series in the UAE and November functions as the resit route. The decision belongs with the school, so ask the exams officer what entering in November would mean for your child's timetable before you buy an intensive block.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic education count towards the five subjects the ministry needs?
faqs.answer: No. The July 2026 report of the ministry's equivalency requirements states explicitly that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required GCSE or IGCSE subjects. They remain compulsory on the school timetable: Arabic, Islamic education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. So they occupy real teaching hours and they sit outside the equivalency count, which is a distinction worth understanding before allocating a tutoring budget.

faqs.question: Who pays the examination entry fee, and where is it published?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set by the awarding body and administered by the examination centre, which for most Jumeirah 2 students is their own school. Schools recover them in different ways, so the figure for your child comes from the exams officer rather than from a tutoring page, and no amount is quoted here because it varies by centre, subject and series. Private candidates entering through a separate centre pay that centre directly. Ask for the fee per subject in writing at the same time as you ask about tier, because both conversations happen with the same person and in the same window.

faqs.question: Should we book group classes at a tuition centre instead?
faqs.answer: A group class is cheaper per hour and solves a different problem. It works when a child needs structure, pace and the company of others doing the same papers. It does not work when the lost marks are specific to that child, because a group tutor cannot mark one script closely enough to find them. A reasonable sequence for a Jumeirah 2 family is one diagnostic one-to-one session on a marked paper, then a group class if the finding is general and one-to-one hours if it is not. Ask any centre with premises in Dubai about its KHDA educational services permit.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is legally allowed to tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, the official service is listed as private tutor licensing with a two-working-day completion time, and it is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Because it costs nothing, there is no good reason for a working tutor not to hold one. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted with caution.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Dubai families most often ask for help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the separate sciences, by a wide margin, followed by English and economics. The pattern is less about difficulty than about visibility: a mathematics mock grade is unambiguous and arrives early, where a weakness in English extended writing shows up later and less sharply. Within mathematics, Cambridge 0580 Extended requests cluster around functions, transformations and probability. In the sciences, the recoverable marks sit disproportionately in the practical and alternative-to-practical components, which test apparatus description, tabulation and graph work rather than content recall.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skills a piece of work requires, explain the assessment criteria, and give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor may not write, redraft to completion or supply any part of assessed work, and IB Gram will decline a request to do so. One provider in this market advertises completed internal assessments; that is a malpractice trigger for the student and the consequences fall on them, not on the seller. If you are unsure where the line sits for a particular component, ask the school's examinations officer or subject coordinator for the written guidance.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if my child is halfway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan changes shape. With a term remaining, new content teaching rarely pays and paper technique usually does: timing, command terms, showing method for partial credit, and the practical or alternative-to-practical component where marks are most recoverable. The honest limits are that a tier ceiling cannot be lifted after the entry deadline passes, and a subject three grades adrift will not close that gap in eight weeks. We will say which of those applies after one marked script rather than after you have paid for a block of hours.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-2.closingHeading: Start with the paperwork, then buy the hours
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-2.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the order. Confirm the tier and the syllabus code with your child's exams officer, write down the five subjects the ministry's equivalency count will use, check the series your child is entered for, and only then compare what tutoring costs. Those four checks are free and they change the answer more than the gap between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour does. When you are ready, the next step from Jumeirah 2 is a free trial lesson with a specialist matched to that syllabus code, delivered one to one over live video, with a written note afterwards telling you where the marks are going and how many weeks it would take to get them back.

intro.heading: Start from the date on the timetable, not the distance to the tutor
paragraphs: The phrase typed into Google is about proximity, but the problem behind it rarely is. A parent in Jumeirah 3 searching for an IGCSE tutor near me is usually looking at a report, a mock mark or a teacher's comment, and working out how many weeks remain before something irreversible happens. The useful first question is not who lives nearby. It is which series your child is entered for, which board sets it, and how many teaching weeks sit between today and the first paper.

Those three answers change everything that follows. A Year 11 student entered for the June series has two full terms and a mock window; a candidate re-sitting in the November series has a compressed run with results arriving in January. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November each year. UAE candidates sit those two windows. There is no third option to plan around.

The dates that can be stated are worth stating, because no competitor page in this market names a session at all. Pearson's final November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes a provisional timetable more than a year ahead of each series and then revises it as centres confirm arrangements, which is why any plan should be checked against the live official timetable rather than against a date copied from a page like this one.

Once the date is fixed, the work divides cleanly. There are weeks for content, weeks for timed practice, and a final stretch that is almost entirely about paper technique and triage. Families who buy tutoring without that division tend to spend the whole period on content, arrive at the paper having never sat one under time, and lose marks that had nothing to do with knowledge. The eight-week plan further down this page exists to stop exactly that, and it carries a weekly test so a parent can see whether the money is doing anything. If the mark on a timed question has not moved after two consecutive sessions, the plan is wrong and should be changed rather than repeated.

Everything here is delivered one-to-one online over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time around the Jumeirah school run. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. In a term governed by deadlines that turns out to matter: a session scheduled for 5.15pm on a Tuesday in the week before a mock starts at 5.15pm, rather than whenever the traffic on Al Wasl Road allows.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: IGCSE tutoring only works if it is pinned to the exact syllabus code the school entered, because the mark scheme belongs to the board and not to the subject. These are the codes Dubai families ask for most, with the part of each that the final term decides.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decision caps the grade, so confirm it before planning anything. In the final weeks the marks sit in multi-step problems, correct use of a calculator, and showing method where the mark scheme awards it. Students who only practise topic exercises arrive unable to triage a full paper.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: A different syllabus from 0580 with a graphic-display-calculator expectation and an investigation element. Several Dubai IB continuum schools enter 0607 rather than 0580, and tutoring built for the wrong code wastes the term. Check the code on the entry confirmation, not the textbook cover.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where the final-term marks move most, along with the practical-skills paper where candidates lose marks for describing a method without naming the controlled variable. Formula recall is necessary but rarely the binding constraint by this point.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry, then organic chemistry and the qualitative-analysis tests. The common late-term failure is calculation presentation: the right answer with no working, or units dropped. A fortnight of marked calculation practice usually moves more marks than a fortnight of revision notes.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy, which tempts students into reading rather than writing. Marks are lost on command terms: describe against explain, and the difference between a trend and a reason. Practising answer length against the mark allocation is the single most transferable late fix.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into one or two grades, with a different balance of content from the separate sciences. Families frequently book three separate science tutors for a child entered for a co-ordinated award, which costs three times as much as it needs to and covers material not on the paper.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition, with reading responses marked for selection and inference rather than for summary. Timed practice with a marked response is the whole of the useful work in the last eight weeks; vocabulary building is a Year 10 activity, not a Year 11 one.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Different paper structure from First Language English and a different mark scheme, with a speaking component in 0511. Students moved into the UAE mid-course are sometimes entered for the wrong one of the two; the fix is a conversation with the school, not a tutor.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455, 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward structure over content in the extended-response questions: definition, explanation, application to the stimulus, evaluation. Dubai students typically arrive strong on definitions and weak on evaluation, which is the band where the available marks sit.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460, 0470)
subjects.description: Case-study recall plus source handling. In the last stretch the efficient work is building two or three reliable case studies to the standard the mark scheme wants, rather than a thin pass over every unit in the specification.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor near me in Jumeirah 3 can and cannot change in the time left
paragraphs: Start with the honest version. With two terms left, almost anything on the specification is reachable, including a tier change if the school agrees to it before entries close. With eight weeks left, content gaps can be closed selectively but not comprehensively, and the best return comes from paper technique, question triage and the three or four topics that appear on every paper. With two weeks left, the only things that move are timing, command-term discipline and not leaving questions blank.

That is a less comfortable message than the one most tutoring pages carry, and it is more useful. A family in Jumeirah 3 who understands which of those three situations they are in buys the right thing. A family who does not usually buys content revision in all three, which is the correct purchase in only the first.

The second question to settle is the board and the code. A Cambridge 0580 candidate and a Cambridge 0607 candidate are sitting different papers with different expectations about calculator use; a Pearson 4MA1 candidate sits a different structure again. The entry confirmation from the school's exams officer holds the authoritative answer. We ask for it before the first session because starting on the wrong code wastes a week nobody has to spare.

The third is the tier, where it applies. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, and the tier caps the grade available. A student working hard towards a grade that the entry does not permit is a specific and avoidable kind of waste, and it is discovered more often than it should be, usually in the final term.

sections.heading: The IGCSE calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: No page ranking for Dubai IGCSE tutoring names an examination series, an entry deadline or a results date. That is strange, because the calendar is the only part of the process with hard edges, and almost every decision a parent makes in Year 11 is really a decision about a date. The table below is built backwards from the paper, with each milestone attributed to whoever actually controls it.

Two things in it are worth reading twice. The first is that the entry deadline sits months before the examination, and the school's internal cut-off sits earlier still, so a decision about tier or board taken in the final term is usually too late to act on. The second is the gap between sitting a paper and being told the result: November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, which means a November candidate spends most of a term not knowing.

The verified Pearson dates are these. The final November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes a provisional timetable for every International GCSE series long before it runs, so dates can be revised at short notice and the live official timetable is the only version worth planning around.

For Cambridge, treat June as the main series and November as the resit route in the UAE. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong timetable. Ask your exams officer which zone your centre sits in and get that version in writing.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, week by week, with a test for each one
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the most common length of a late IGCSE booking in Dubai, usually because a mock mark arrived and somebody decided to act. Eight weeks is enough to change a grade, and it is not enough to cover a specification, so the plan has to decide what it is not doing. The version below allocates two weeks to diagnosis and high-frequency content, four to timed practice on the paper that is losing marks, and two to technique and triage.

Each week carries a test, because without one a block of eight sessions produces eight pleasant conversations and no evidence. The test is always a mark on a timed question, written by the student alone and marked against the board's scheme. If the number does not move across two consecutive weeks, something in the plan is wrong and it is better to know in week three than in week eight.

The plan assumes one hour a week of tuition plus two to three hours of the student's own timed work. That ratio matters more than the tutoring itself. A tutor who sets no independent timed work in the final eight weeks is not running an exam block; they are running a conversation, and a parent paying market rates for it is buying the wrong thing.

Jumeirah 3 families should build the school calendar into this before week one. Dubai half-term breaks and the Ramadan timetable both change what a week can hold, and a block that assumes eight uninterrupted weeks will usually get six. Plan for six and treat the other two as spare.

sections.heading: What the final stretch costs in Dubai, counted as a total
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for an exam block. What a family in Jumeirah 3 actually wants to know is the total: eight sessions, or sixteen, or thirty, and what that comes to. Setting it out that way also makes the trade-offs visible, because the difference between a generalist and a subject specialist across eight hours is a few hundred dirhams, while across a full year of weekly tuition it is several thousand.

The published market bands are these. EdFlik advertises budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes online rates from AED 150 for IGCSE. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and a subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with independent home tutors quoted as high as AED 500. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Those are market figures from each provider's own material, not an IB Gram price list.

Multiply them out and the picture changes. An eight-week block at one hour a week with a qualified subject teacher in the AED 150 to 300 band is roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400 in total, which is less than two months of the in-home monthly packages circulating in Dubai at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Measured against a grade that decides a post-16 subject choice, the eight-week total is usually the easier number for a family to justify than the hourly rate ever is.

One figure belongs in the context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A flat fee year is the natural moment to decide how much of the household education budget should go to a targeted exam block rather than to open-ended monthly tuition.

sections.heading: Zones, entries and the administrative mistakes that cost grades
paragraphs: A small number of IGCSE failures in the UAE have nothing to do with teaching. They are administrative, and they are entirely preventable by a parent who asks three questions in October rather than in May. The first concerns the timetable. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination because the wrong timetable was used. A timetable found through a general search may belong to a different zone.

The second concerns the entry itself. Parents are rarely given a copy of what the school submitted, and the details that matter are the ones that are easy to get wrong: the syllabus code, the tier where the subject is tiered, the components entered, and the candidate's name exactly as it will appear on the certificate. Asking the exams officer for the entry confirmation in writing takes one email and resolves disputes that otherwise surface after results.

The third concerns private candidates. A student not entered through their own school, which happens after a mid-year move or when a subject is dropped and later picked up, must find an approved centre and meet that centre's own earlier deadline. Centres also charge their own administrative fees on top of the board entry fee. None of this is difficult, and all of it takes longer than families expect.

A practical habit for Jumeirah 3 households: keep one folder with the entry confirmation, the zone-specific timetable, the coursework deadlines the school has set, and the results dates. Everything in that folder is free, and it prevents the category of problem that no amount of tutoring can fix after the fact.

sections.heading: Ramadan, half-terms and the Dubai school year against the exam window
paragraphs: Any plan drawn up in a Dubai October meets three interruptions before the papers arrive, and a block that ignores them loses a quarter of its sessions. School terms in the emirate carry their own break structure, the winter break removes a working fortnight from most revision plans, and Ramadan shortens school hours and moves the useful study window.

During Ramadan the practical tutoring slots move either to the early afternoon, once a shortened school day has ended, or to after Iftar. Both work over live video. Neither works reliably if somebody has to drive, because the roads either side of Iftar in Dubai are their own argument for online delivery. Families who plan a post-Iftar slot in advance generally keep the same tutor and the same weekday through the month, which preserves the rhythm a timed-practice block depends on.

The winter break is the other decision point, and it cuts both ways. For a June candidate it is the single best block of uninterrupted time available for timed papers, and two or three sessions across it are worth more than twice that number in a busy February. For a student who has just finished a November series it is a rest, and treating it as a revision window is usually counterproductive.

The last scheduling point is specific to this neighbourhood. Jumeirah 3 school runs put the first dependable weekday slot at around 4.45pm during term, with 5pm to 6pm the window that survives a whole block. In the fortnight before papers, families often move to two shorter sessions a week rather than one long one, which online scheduling makes trivial and a travelling tutor makes expensive.

sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the lines a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or a practical component, and in the final term those are the pieces most at risk of being over-helped. The rule is the same as it is in the IB: a tutor teaches, explains, models on a different example, and gives feedback on work the student has written. A tutor does not supply sentences to be copied, does not restructure a piece on the student's behalf and does not choose the investigation. The mark belongs to the student or it is worthless.

The same boundary applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and link to the boards' own pages rather than reproducing or supplying them, because redistributing them is copyright infringement and, for unreleased material, something considerably worse. Your school's exams officer and the boards' public sites are the right sources, and both are free.

This matters commercially as well as ethically. Research into this search market found a provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright. Any family offered finished work should treat it as a warning about everything else that provider says, because the risk sits entirely with the student, who is the one making a declaration about authorship.

The practical check a parent can run after any coursework session costs nothing. Ask your child what changed and why the mark scheme required it. A student who can answer has been taught. A student who cannot has been given something, and it will not survive a conversation with their teacher.

sections.heading: Booking this week, if the paper is close
paragraphs: If the examination is near, the sequence matters more than the deliberation. Get the mock script or the most recent marked paper, not the grade. Get the entry confirmation with the board, syllabus code and tier. Count the teaching weeks remaining, subtracting the breaks. Those three items take an evening to assemble and they turn a vague request for a tutor near Jumeirah 3 into a brief any competent subject teacher can act on immediately.

Then use the free trial lesson for diagnosis rather than for introductions. A good first session with a mock script in hand produces a ranked list of the topics costing the most marks and an honest statement of what is reachable in the time left. If a trial produces only encouragement, the tutor has not done the work, and you have the information you needed about whether to continue.

Expect us to be specific about availability. Matching is done on who can teach that board and code at the hour you want on Gulf Standard Time. For a narrow combination close to a paper date, the honest answer is sometimes a different weekday or a short wait, and we say so rather than putting a generalist into an exam block where the whole value depends on knowing the mark scheme.

Two sessions a week is often better than one in the last fortnight, and stopping entirely in the final two days is almost always right. The most common late mistake in this market is buying more hours in the last week, when the student needs sleep and a clear structure far more than they need another lesson.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series do Dubai candidates in Jumeirah 3 actually sit?
faqs.answer: Two. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November each year. UAE candidates sit those windows, with June as the main series and November commonly used for re-sits. Any plan should be checked against the live official timetable on the board's own site, because provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and dates can be revised before they are finalised.

faqs.question: When did the most recent November IGCSE papers and results actually fall?
faqs.answer: Pearson's final November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. For the previous series, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which shows the real gap between sitting a November paper and learning the outcome: most of a term. June results come faster, with June 2026 results going to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Those are Pearson's own published dates; confirm your own series against the live timetable rather than relying on a date reproduced elsewhere.

faqs.question: Why does my child's exam timetable differ from the one I found online?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A timetable found through a general search may belong to a different zone entirely. Ask your school's exams officer which zone your centre sits in and get that version in writing, then plan revision around it.

faqs.question: Can eight weeks of tutoring realistically change an IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Often yes, provided the eight weeks are spent on the right thing. Eight weeks is not enough to cover a specification, so the plan has to pick: usually two weeks of diagnosis and high-frequency content, four weeks of timed papers on the component losing marks, and two weeks of technique and triage. What moves a grade late is almost never new content; it is showing method, reading command terms correctly, managing time across a paper and not leaving questions blank. A block without independent timed work between sessions will not do it.

faqs.question: How much does an eight-week IGCSE block cost in Dubai in total?
faqs.answer: Counted as a total rather than an hourly rate, eight weekly hours with a qualified subject teacher in the published AED 150 to 300 band comes to roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400. Unitors publishes online IGCSE rates from AED 150; TutorChase publishes AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards. For comparison, in-home monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits circulate widely in the emirate. These are market rates from each provider's own material, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is there any point hiring a tutor who lives close to Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Proximity helps only if someone has to travel, and in our model nobody does. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. The cost of insisting on a nearby tutor is that the search narrows from subject expertise to driving distance, which matters most in the final term when the whole value of the session comes from knowing the board's mark scheme.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Cambridge 0607 rather than 0580. Does that change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a different syllabus from Mathematics 0580, with a graphic-display-calculator expectation and an investigation element that 0580 does not carry. Several Dubai IB continuum schools enter 0607. Working through 0580 material for a 0607 candidate covers some of the right content with the wrong technique and the wrong paper structure. Check the code on the school's entry confirmation rather than on the textbook, and tell any prospective tutor the code before the first session is booked.

faqs.question: What does Core and Extended mean for the grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: Cambridge tiers several IGCSE subjects into Core and Extended, and the tier caps the grade available: a Core entry cannot reach the top grades however well the paper is answered. The tier is decided at entry, which is usually a term or more before the papers, so a family who discovers it in the final weeks has limited options. If your child is working towards a grade the entry does not permit, that is worth resolving with the school immediately, and it is a conversation rather than a purchase.

faqs.question: Should we book a re-sit before or after the results arrive?
faqs.answer: Prepare the decision before, make it after. Both Cambridge and Pearson run June and November series, so the route exists, but entry deadlines sit well before the examination and sometimes close to the results date of the previous series. Read the mark breakdown rather than the overall grade: a grade missed by two marks on one paper is a different problem from a grade missed across every component. Identify the deadline for the next series first, then decide whether the gap is worth a term.

faqs.question: How do Dubai half-terms and Ramadan affect an exam revision plan?
faqs.answer: They remove weeks, and plans that ignore them lose roughly a quarter of their sessions. Build an eight-week block assuming six usable weeks. During Ramadan the workable slots move to the early afternoon after a shortened school day, or to after Iftar, and both run normally over live video while a travelling tutor becomes unreliable. The winter break is the single best uninterrupted window for timed papers if your child is a June candidate, and is better treated as rest if they have just sat the November series.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start from Jumeirah 3 during term?
faqs.answer: School days in this corridor end between roughly 2.30pm and 3.30pm and the run home adds twenty to fifty minutes, so around 4.45pm is the first dependable weekday start and 5pm to 6pm is the window that survives a whole block. Later slots at 7pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time are widely available and often better for households where both parents commute from Business Bay or DIFC. In the fortnight before papers, two shorter sessions a week usually beat one long one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework and practical write-ups?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits. A tutor may teach the technique, explain what the mark scheme rewards, model the method on a different example and give feedback on work the student has already written. A tutor may not supply sentences to be copied, restructure the piece or choose the investigation. We also do not reproduce or supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes, which belong to Cambridge and Pearson; we link to the boards' own pages instead. The mark has to be the student's or it is worth nothing.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a Dubai family need a licence or permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount quoted at you as unverified. This is a MoHRE permit, not a KHDA school licence.

faqs.question: My child has four weeks left and three weak subjects. What should we actually buy?
faqs.answer: One subject, properly, rather than three thinly. Four weeks split three ways gives roughly four sessions each, which is not enough to change a paper technique in any of them. Rank the three by how much the grade matters for the post-16 route, and by how many marks a mock script shows are recoverable. Then spend the four weeks on the one at the top and use free school support for the others. Spreading a short block across several subjects is the most reliable way to waste it.

faqs.question: What should I bring to the free trial lesson if the exam is close?
faqs.answer: The most recent marked script, not the grade; the school's entry confirmation showing board, syllabus code, tier and components; and a count of the real teaching weeks left once breaks are removed. With those three things a first session can produce a ranked list of the topics costing the most marks and an honest statement of what is reachable. The trial is free, needs no card details and carries no obligation, and if it produces only encouragement you have learned something useful about that tutor.

Confirm the series, get the zone-specific timetable and the entry confirmation from your school's exams officer, count the teaching weeks that are genuinely left once the breaks come out, and decide what the block is not going to cover. Then bring the marked mock script to a free trial lesson and ask for a ranked list of the marks that are recoverable. intro.heading: Nobody in this market will tell you what it costs, so here it is
paragraphs: The single strangest thing about searching for IGCSE tuition in Dubai is how hard it is to find a price. Research across sixty-odd competitor pages in October 2026 found that three of the six best-ranking pages publish no figure at all, and that the two which do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. One agency's own frequently-asked-questions section asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. That is not an accident; it is a negotiating position.

So this page starts with the numbers, cheapest first, and attributes each one. Budget online tuition in Dubai is advertised from around AED 45 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300. In-home visits including travel run from about AED 180 to AED 500. Specialist IGCSE and IB provision is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and the highest published figure found anywhere in the research was AED 650 an hour. The full table, with sources, is further down.

Knowing the bands is only half of it, because the useful question is not what an hour costs but what a grade move costs. A Jumeirah Golf Estates family paying AED 200 an hour for thirty weekly sessions has spent AED 6,000 to produce, often, no measurable change, because the sessions were general support rather than targeted at a diagnosed error. The same family spending AED 1,800 on nine sessions aimed at two specific topics and one technique habit frequently sees the grade move. Cost per hour and cost per outcome are different measurements and this market encourages you to confuse them.

The second half of this page is therefore about waste. Where it happens, why it happens, and the four or five decisions that cause most of it: tuition in too many subjects at once, tuition that starts before anybody has read a marked paper, tuition that continues through a second term without a review, the wrong board, and the wrong tier. None of those is about the tutor's hourly rate and all of them cost more than the rate does.

One thing worth saying before the numbers start. Comparing two quotes in this market is harder than it should be because the two providers are rarely selling the same unit. One is quoting an hour, another a ninety-minute lesson, a third a monthly package of eight sessions, and only one of them is including the time it takes to mark a full past paper properly between lessons. Put every quote into the same unit before you decide, and ask what happens to a prepaid block if the tutor changes.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Jumeirah Golf Estates families as one-to-one live video lessons at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Our own fee is quoted after a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on how many sessions the marked work shows you need.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-go.subjectsIntro: Price per subject varies less than families expect; what varies is the number of sessions each one needs to move. These are the IGCSE subjects most often requested from this part of New Dubai, with a note on what drives the session count.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The most requested subject and often the cheapest to fix, because the losses are habitual rather than conceptual: unrounded intermediate values carried forward, and method lines omitted on four and five-mark questions. Eight to ten sessions is a realistic block for a grade move.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken in Year 11 ahead of A Level or Diploma Higher Level mathematics. Tutor supply is thin, which lengthens the wait rather than raising the rate, and it introduces calculus and logarithms, so the session count is higher than for 0580.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity decides the grade, and it is where most of the session count goes. Circuit reasoning collapses on unfamiliar diagrams and formula rearrangement fails under time pressure. Expect ten to twelve sessions if electricity and waves are both weak.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations carry disproportionate weight and are rushed; the qualitative analysis ion tests are recall marks routinely left blank. Those two together are often six sessions and a visible grade change, which makes Chemistry one of the better-value blocks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content is manageable and the marks are lost on precision of language. Because the fix is linguistic rather than conceptual, Biology often needs fewer sessions than parents expect, and continuing past that point is a common waste.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Double or single award for students not taking three separate sciences. A student moved onto this route mid-Year 10 needs the specific gap identified, not the syllabus retaught, and paying for the latter is one of the larger avoidable costs in this market.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Writing marks hinge on text type and register. A student producing an essay where a report was asked for loses marks nobody has explained, and three or four sessions on text types is usually enough to recover them.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. The reading paper rewards short precise comment on selected evidence; long paraphrase scores badly. This is habit work, and the session count depends entirely on how entrenched the habit is.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams must be labelled and then used in the prose. A fully correct diagram the answer never refers to earns almost nothing, which makes this a cheap fix once identified and an expensive one if the tuition starts from the beginning of the syllabus.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Structured questions require application to the case organisation. Generic answers about customers and profit are why a confident student stalls at grade 6, and the correction is a technique block rather than a term of content coverage.

Budget online tuition, typically delivered by a university student, is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour; one platform lists from AED 33 to AED 52 and another from AED 45 to AED 65. Specialist IGCSE, IB and A-Level provision is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one UK-based agency publishing AED 270. The highest figure found anywhere in the research was AED 650 an hour for premium named or examiner-led tuition.

On monthly packages, one provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Every figure in this section was read from the provider's or survey's own published page in October 2026. They describe the market, not IB Gram; our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson, when the session count is actually knowable. If a provider quotes you a rate, ask whether it is per hour or per lesson, whether it includes VAT, and what the cancellation terms are, because those three answers change the real number more than the headline does.

sections.heading: What each band actually buys
paragraphs: A rate is not a quality score, and the bands are not simply better versions of each other. They buy different things, and matching the band to the problem is where most of the available saving sits.

The AED 45 to AED 150 band buys supervision, structure and company. The MoHRE permit is available to university students and to school students aged 15 to 18, so this band is entirely legitimate; it is just not the same product. For a Year 9 student who will not start homework unaided, it is excellent value. For a Year 11 Extended-tier Physics candidate eight weeks from the June series, it is money spent on the wrong thing, and the shortfall will not show up until results day.

The AED 150 to AED 300 band buys subject teaching at the right level from somebody who knows the syllabus and can mark against a scheme. For most IGCSE problems this is the correct band, and going above it rarely changes anything. The AED 200 to AED 450 and above specialist band buys paper-level fluency, which matters when a student is already at grade 6 or 7 and the remaining marks are precision rather than content.

The premium band, up to AED 650, buys reputation and scarcity. Sometimes that is justified by genuinely rare expertise. Often the claim attached to it is examiner status, and a claim of current examiner status for a named individual is worth asking for evidence of, since it cannot be verified from a website and nobody should be implying it gives access to marking or boundaries.

sections.heading: Where Jumeirah Golf Estates families waste money
paragraphs: None of the five big wastes is about the hourly rate, which is why focusing on the rate is itself a mistake. The first is buying tuition in three subjects at once. A student needs unaided practice between sessions and a Dubai timetable plus clubs leaves little room for it, so three weekly slots produce attendance without progress at three times the cost.

The second is starting before anyone has read a marked paper. A tutor given only a subject name begins at the start of the syllabus, which is almost always the wrong place, and the first four sessions get spent discovering what one marked mock would have shown in twenty minutes. The third is the unreviewed weekly slot. Tuition agreed in September is still running in March with nobody having asked whether the targeted errors have gone. That is the single largest avoidable spend in this community.

The fourth is the wrong board. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are different qualifications; a tutor working from a 0625 scheme of work with a 4PH1 candidate wastes time on topics that are not examined and misses ones that are. The fifth is the wrong tier, which is not a tuition problem at all: a student on Core cannot exceed grade 5, and no number of sessions changes that. If the post-16 plan needs a 7, the conversation is with the school, not with a tutor.

There is a sixth, smaller one worth naming: paying for a result that was going to happen anyway. A student already on an upward line after a bad term does not need a tutor to continue upwards, and nobody in this market will volunteer that. A short diagnostic block will tell you which situation you are in for a fraction of the price of a year.
