sections.heading: Cost per grade move, not cost per hour
paragraphs: The number that matters is the total spend attached to a change you can see in a school assessment. Run the arithmetic on a few realistic Jumeirah Golf Estates scenarios and the pattern is consistent: targeted short blocks beat open-ended weekly arrangements, and the gap is large.

Take a Year 11 Mathematics student losing marks on method lines and rounding. At a mid-band rate, nine focused sessions is in the region of AED 1,800 and usually produces a visible change at the next assessment, because the errors are habitual. Compare a general weekly arrangement running thirty weeks at the same rate: roughly AED 6,000, often with the same two habits intact in May because nobody ever named them.

Now take a harder case. A Year 11 Physics student weak on both electricity and waves is genuinely twelve sessions of content plus technique, around AED 2,400 at a mid-band rate, and it should be bought as a block with a review point rather than as an indefinite slot. And take the case where tuition is the wrong purchase altogether: a Core-tier student needing a grade 7. No spend fixes that; the tier conversation with the school is free.

sections.heading: Hidden extras that catch Dubai parents
paragraphs: The headline rate is the beginning of the price, not the end of it. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per lesson, because a ninety-minute lesson quoted as a session price is a different number. Ask whether it includes VAT; we limit ourselves to stating whether our own quoted prices include it, because the tax treatment of tuition fees is a Federal Tax Authority question and not something a tutoring page should assert.

Ask about cancellation and rescheduling. In a community where clubs in Dubai Sports City move without notice, a provider charging for a session cancelled with twenty-four hours' notice will cost a family several hundred dirhams a term that never appeared in the comparison. Ask whether marking between sessions is included or billed, because a tutor marking a full past paper properly spends real time on it.

Ask what the word free attaches to. A free trial with a card requirement, a minimum booking or an eligibility condition is a conditional offer, and the condition belongs on the same screen as the word. Ours is a single lesson with the proposed tutor, with no payment required to reach it, and we will say so in writing.

Finally, ask about replacement. If the match is wrong, is a different tutor provided, and at what cost? If a tutor leaves mid-term, what happens to a prepaid block? Those two answers tell you more about a provider than any rate does, and in this market they are rarely published.

sections.heading: Tuition cost in context: school fees and the rest of the budget
paragraphs: Tuition is rarely the biggest line in a Dubai education budget, and seeing it next to the others changes how families decide. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are therefore the stable line this year.

Around that sit costs families often forget when comparing tutors. Examination entry fees for a private candidate are paid to the centre, not the tutor. Transport to a tuition centre in Motor City or Al Barsha has a fuel and time cost that an in-home or online comparison usually omits. And a resit entry in the November series is a real budget item that is cheaper than a year of general support and almost never mentioned at the point of sale.

The context also matters for scale. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More supply tends to moderate prices over time, including in tuition.

The table puts the pieces in one place so you can see which parts you control. Read it before you compare two tutors, because the lines you cannot change should not be the ones absorbing your attention, and the two that you can change — the format you buy and the number of sessions you commit to — are both settled in a single conversation at the start.

sections.heading: Why the cheapest legal tutor is still legal
paragraphs: It is tempting to assume that a very low rate signals someone operating outside the rules. Usually it does not, and understanding why makes the rate card easier to read. Private tutoring in the UAE sits under a private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years.

The permit's eligible categories explicitly include university students and school students aged 15 to 18, alongside registered school teachers and government and private-sector employees. MoHRE's own service listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services. So a permitted eighteen-year-old charging AED 60 an hour is entirely within the rules. The question is not legality; it is fit.

What is not permitted is tutoring without the permit at all: individuals doing so are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure can be quoted honestly and we do not quote one. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tuition of students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction, which is press-reported and worth verifying against the current ADEK policy document.

One more thing to be clear about. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, runs no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB.

sections.heading: What we will not sell you
paragraphs: A page about cost should be explicit about what it refuses to charge for. We do not sell guaranteed outcomes, and we do not publish guaranteed grade improvements or money-back score promises. Nobody can honestly offer them, and in this market they are the clearest signal to look elsewhere.

We do not sell completed coursework. A tutor teaches the content, explains what each assessment criterion rewards, interrogates a plan, marks a draft against the criteria and teaches referencing. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete any part of the work. One operator in this market was found advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student.

We do not sell past paper and mark scheme bundles. Reproducing or redistributing IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is not ours to do; tutors reference them and link to the official source. And we do not sell a tutor's examiner status as a product, because current examiner status for an individual cannot be evidenced from a website and should never be implied to give access to marking or boundaries.

Finally, we do not publish a statistic we cannot support. No satisfaction percentage without a sample size, a date and a method; no self-asserted star rating; no median tutor score. Several providers in this market publish two different review figures on the same page, which is a good reason to treat all of them as decoration rather than data.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost for a family in Jumeirah Golf Estates?

The question is fit rather than legality: that band buys supervision and structure, which suits a Year 9 organisation problem and does not suit a Year 11 Extended-tier science.

faqs.question: What is the single biggest way families here waste tuition money?

faqs.question: How many sessions does an IGCSE grade move actually take?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the problem is habits or content. Habit errors — rounding intermediate values, omitting method lines, paraphrasing instead of selecting evidence — often move in eight to ten sessions. Two weak content topics, such as electricity and waves in Physics, is realistically twelve. Two high-weight topics in Chemistry, like moles and the ion tests, can be six. A good provider will name the number before you start and tie it to a review point. One who proposes an open-ended weekly slot has not diagnosed anything yet.

faqs.answer: Ask, and ask specifically. The wider point is that the headline rate is the start of the price. Also establish whether the figure is per hour or per lesson, whether marking a full past paper between sessions is included or billed, and what notice is required to cancel without charge.

faqs.question: Can tuition in two subjects at once ever make sense?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and three almost never. The constraint is not money but your child's week: a subject needs unaided practice between sessions, because the unassisted attempt is where the learning happens. With a full Dubai timetable plus clubs in Dubai Sports City, three weekly slots produce attendance without progress at three times the cost. It does not work for diagnosing an individual's recurring error, which is the thing most IGCSE students actually need. Scheduling also becomes the binding constraint for every family involved. We will advise against a group where one-to-one is clearly the right purchase.

faqs.answer: Frequently, yes, and almost nobody prices it in. Both Cambridge and Pearson run a November series, so a resit sits roughly five months after June rather than a year, and private candidate entry through an approved Dubai centre is possible. A focused block of eight to twelve sessions aimed at one paper is a smaller total than thirty weeks of general support. Two cautions: the November entry deadline falls well before the exam, often before results have settled, and the entry fee is paid to the centre rather than to a tutor.

What notice is required to cancel without charge; whether a rescheduled session can be moved within the same week; whether a prepaid block expires; and what happens if the tutor leaves mid-block. In a community where clubs move without warning, a provider charging for sessions cancelled with twenty-four hours' notice will cost several hundred dirhams a term that never appeared in your comparison. These answers tell you more about a provider than the hourly rate does, and they are rarely published.

Against that, a weekly mid-band tuition slot is published at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month. Tuition is the part of the budget you control, which is why a block total with a review date is a better purchase than an open-ended monthly commitment.

A tutor teaches the content, explains what the assessment criteria reward, interrogates a plan, points out where a method will not generate usable data, marks a draft against the criteria and teaches referencing. A tutor does not write, rewrite, complete or supply any part of the work. One operator in this market was found advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is academic malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not on the seller. Our tutors decline these requests.

intro.heading: What 'knows the syllabus' actually means
paragraphs: The honest version of this question is not whether a tutor knows the subject. Most candidates for the job do. It is whether they know your child's qualification, which is a narrower thing: a specific syllabus code, at a specific tier, with specific calculator rules, a specific practical assessment route, and a specific series that a UAE candidate can sit.

Those details are not cosmetic. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 cover similar content and assess it differently, including whether a calculator is permitted in a given component. Their past papers are not interchangeable. A tutor working from the wrong set will teach well, your child will work hard, and the grade will not move.

The tier is the second detail and the more consequential one. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher in some. The tier caps the available grade and removes content that post-16 courses assume. A tutor who has not confirmed the tier may spend a term teaching material your child will never be examined on.

The third is the exam calendar, where UAE-facing tutoring content is frequently wrong. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version.

The fourth, which nobody asks until it is late, is how practical skills are assessed on your child's entry. Some candidates sit a practical examination in a laboratory and others a written alternative-to-practical paper. Both test the same competences: writing a repeatable method, controlling variables, reading instruments, tabulating with units, plotting and criticising a method rather than reporting that it worked. The preparation differs, and the written route is routinely revised as theory, which it is not.

So the test for a tutor is not how long they have taught. It is whether they can tell you the paper structure for your child's code without looking it up, whether a non-calculator component applies, how practical skills are assessed on that entry, and which series your child will actually sit. That takes about ten minutes and it is the most useful ten minutes in this process, because every one of those answers can be checked against your school rather than taken on trust.

IB Gram matches your child to a tutor briefed on that exact entry, teaching live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and with no school and no tuition centre inside the Jumeirah Islands gates, online removes a journey rather than adding one.

sections.heading: Six things an IGCSE specialist can tell you about your child's entry
paragraphs: Use this as a checklist. A tutor who can answer all six has taught the qualification; one who can answer three has taught the subject. The difference is not detectable in the first fortnight and is obvious at the mock, which is why it is worth establishing before any money moves.

First, the syllabus code and what its paper structure is. Second, the tier your child is on and which topics the higher tier adds. Third, whether a non-calculator component applies, because that changes how algebra and arithmetic have to be trained. Fourth, how practical skills are assessed on that entry, in a laboratory or on a written alternative.

Fifth, which series your child will sit and which series exist for a UAE candidate, which is June and November for Cambridge and May/June and November for Pearson Edexcel. A tutor who mentions a February or March window has not taught UAE candidates, because that Cambridge series is offered to India only.

Sixth, what the school controls. Entry decisions, coursework and controlled-assessment deadlines, and the zone-specific Cambridge timetable all sit with the school rather than with the board or the tutor. A specialist asks for the school's internal calendar in the first conversation rather than working from the examination date.

The table sets each out with what a strong answer sounds like. It works on us as readily as on anyone else, and if a tutor we match cannot answer it, tell us and we will change the match rather than asking you to persist.

sections.heading: Why a strong GCSE teacher is not automatically an IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: This is the most common near-miss in Dubai. A tutor who has taught UK GCSE for a decade knows the subject thoroughly, and the International GCSE is a different qualification with different administration. The content overlaps substantially. The entry details, which are what a tutor needs to prepare a candidate properly, do not always.

The differences that matter in practice are administrative rather than intellectual. International GCSE subjects are frequently examined without the coursework components a UK course might carry, with practical science skills assessed through a laboratory examination or a written alternative instead. Which applies depends on your child's entry rather than on the subject.

The series pattern differs too. A UK teacher's instinct is a single summer examination with autumn resits in a couple of subjects. A UAE Cambridge candidate has June and November available as full series, and a Pearson candidate has May/June and November, with some Pearson subjects offering modular entry so a unit can be sat separately.

Then there is the zone system, which has no UK equivalent. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The school holds the right version.

None of this means a UK-trained teacher cannot be an excellent IGCSE tutor. Many are. It means the question to ask is about the entry rather than about the teaching, and that a tutor who has not thought about zones, series or practical routes needs to before your child's revision plan is built on their assumptions.

sections.heading: The ten-minute past-paper test
paragraphs: You do not need subject expertise to run this, and it is more informative than any CV. Take one marked paper for your child's actual syllabus code, give it to the tutor at the start of the trial session, and watch what they do with it. The useful signals are all behavioural rather than technical.

A specialist reads the paper before talking. They look at which questions lost marks rather than at the total, then ask the student what they were thinking on two or three of them. Within ten minutes they can tell you whether the losses are content gaps, method-selection failures, or exam conduct, and those three need different responses over different numbers of weeks.

A general tutor does something different and recognisable: they look at the grade, name the topics that appear in the paper, and propose revising them. That is not useless, and it is not diagnosis. It also leads to an open-ended programme rather than a defined piece of work, which is the commonest shape of wasted tutoring spend in this city.

The second signal is whether the tutor asks your child to write. A session in which the tutor explains for fifty minutes may be entirely accurate and will not change a mark. The student has to produce something while someone watches, because the failures are in production rather than in understanding.

The third is what they say about the next six weeks. A specialist names two or three specific targets with a rough number of sessions each. A general tutor describes covering the syllabus. Ask for the specific version, and if you cannot get it, that is your answer.

sections.heading: What we can honestly staff, and what we cannot
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is why most parents discover one after paying. Ours is on this page. Mathematics, the three sciences, English and the business subjects are well covered and usually matched within the same week. Computer Science is thinner at the specialist end. Additional Mathematics has a smaller pool and fills early.

The scarce resource is not the subject but the hour. Weekday slots between 17:00 and 19:00 in the spring term are what every Year 11 household in Dubai wants, and they fill from September onwards. A family booking a weekly slot in the autumn holds it; a family asking in February chooses from what is left, at the same hourly rate.

For the mandatory UAE subjects we are candid about the constraints. Support means working with the school's own material, because KHDA prohibits using different or additional content for those subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission, and the schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them.

The phrase that brought you here is near me, so the last limit to state is a geographic one about us rather than about supply. Two providers ranking for these Jumeirah Islands searches route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers and say nothing about it on the page. Our position: where a tutor covering a UAE family is based outside the UAE and teaches to Gulf Standard Time, you are told before you book, not after. A parent is entitled to know who is teaching their child and from where, and a search for someone nearby deserves a straight answer to that question even when the honest answer is that the lesson arrives over video.

If the combination you need is not free, you are told the position and offered a choice: an off-peak or weekend slot with the specialist, an interim tutor with a stated handover date, or a wait with a date attached. The table sets out where supply currently sits.

sections.heading: The practical question nobody asks until it is late
paragraphs: Every IGCSE science assesses practical skills, and how yours are assessed depends on the entry your school has made. Some candidates sit a practical examination in a laboratory. Others sit a written alternative-to-practical paper testing the same skills on paper. A tutor who does not establish which applies will prepare your child for the wrong thing.

Both routes test the same underlying competences: writing a method precise enough for someone else to repeat, identifying the variable changed and the ones controlled, reading an instrument to appropriate precision, tabulating with units in the headings, plotting with a sensible scale, drawing a line of best fit, and criticising a method rather than reporting that it worked.

The trap in the written route is that students revise it as theory because it is a written paper. It is not theory. It asks about apparatus, precision, anomalous results and improvements, and a student who has never been required to criticise a method on paper will perform poorly however well they know the content.

This is also the best-value block in science tutoring, because the skills transfer. Four to six sessions earn marks in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously, and again in whichever practical route applies. Almost no family buys it, because it does not look like a subject on an invoice.

Online delivery suits this work particularly well: the method is written, the table is drawn, the graph is plotted and then criticised, all on a shared screen. Hands-on laboratory work stays at school with the school's apparatus, where it belongs and where it would be in any case.

sections.heading: The series, the zones and counting backwards
paragraphs: A tutor who knows the calendar is more useful than one who knows an extra topic, because the calendar decides when anything can be done. For a UAE family the two Cambridge options are June and November, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October where schools use them. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only. It appears in Gulf-facing tutoring content regularly, and acting on it means building a revision plan around a window that does not exist for your child. That is the kind of error a parent cannot detect and pays for.

The November series is the resit route and its timing cost is worth knowing in advance. The Pearson precedent: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026.

So a November resit means a sixth-form application season carried out with a provisional grade in that subject. Schools are used to it, and it is better discussed in August than in January. The alternative where a grade sits just below a boundary is an enquiry about results, submitted by the school within a short window after results for a board fee.

Dates are revised and Cambridge timetables are zone-specific, with every centre allocated to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Plan from the live official timetable your school holds, not from any tutoring page.

sections.heading: Scheduling from a community with nothing inside the gates
paragraphs: Jumeirah Islands has no school and no tuition centre within it, so every child travels out and back. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30, and a bus route serving this community usually calls at two or three others first, putting arrivals home between about 15:40 and 16:50 depending on the school and the route order.

The dependable weekday start is therefore 17:00, or 17:30 for a child travelling from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. A 16:30 session begins before a teenager has eaten or changed, and the first twenty minutes go on settling, which is the mechanism by which arrangements end in week five without anyone being able to explain why.

Bus routes are built around schools rather than communities, so two households inside the same gates can differ by twenty minutes. Ask the transport office for your own route timings rather than copying a neighbour's slot. It is a two-minute question that decides whether an hour works.

Weekend slots are where the long work belongs. A Saturday morning session is the only ninety-minute block in a week here, which makes it the right place for a full timed paper, with Sunday used to mark it together. Marking the paper is where the learning happens; sitting it only generates the data.

During Ramadan the pattern shifts again: shortened school hours, later households, and a post-Iftar or late-morning weekend session working better than anything at five in the afternoon. We reschedule rather than cancel, because the June series does not move.

sections.heading: Rates, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier at AED 650. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65.

In-home visits carry a travel premium at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's figures, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500. For monthly planning, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. All figures are the providers' own, read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price.

On claims: IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute with premises. Any provider implying that a regulator has vetted its tutors is worth questioning closely.

Individual tutors in the UAE do need a permit, and that is a fair thing to ask about. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's app, website or e-services with a two-working-day completion time.

We also publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage, do not reproduce or distribute past papers or mark schemes, and do not write or supply coursework of any kind. Where an IGCSE subject carries an assessed component, a tutor teaches the criteria and comments on work your child has written.

faqs.question: Is there anyone around here who actually knows my child's IGCSE syllabus?
faqs.answer: Some, and fewer than you would hope, and the limiting factor is the entry rather than the subject. A tutor needs to know the syllabus code, the tier, whether a non-calculator component applies, how practical skills are assessed on that entry, and which series a UAE candidate sits. Plenty of competent subject tutors cannot answer those five questions. Narrow it further to someone willing to drive into a gated community at half past five and the list is very short, which is why we match online.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who taught UK GCSE prepare my child for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, once they have checked the entry details, which are where the two diverge. The content overlaps heavily. The administration does not: UAE Cambridge candidates have June and November series, Cambridge allocates centres to one of six zones each with its own timetable, Pearson offers modular entry in some subjects, and practical science is assessed through a laboratory examination or a written alternative depending on the entry. Ask about those rather than about the teaching.

faqs.question: What should I hand a tutor in a trial session?
faqs.answer: One marked paper for your child's exact syllabus code, and the five facts from the exams officer: code, tier, series, practical route and internal deadlines. Then watch what the tutor does. A specialist reads the questions rather than the total, asks your child what they were thinking on two or three of them, and within ten minutes names whether the losses are content, method or exam conduct. A general tutor reads the grade and proposes revising the topics.

faqs.question: Do your tutors travel into Jumeirah Islands?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no office or centre here either. Lessons are live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time. Since there is no school and no tuition centre inside these gates, online removes a journey from the day rather than adding one. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour including travel if presence in the room is essential for your child.

faqs.question: Why does the exam zone system matter to us?
faqs.answer: Because it decides the dates your child actually sits. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The version that applies is the one your school's exams officer holds. No tutoring page, including this one, should be the source of an exam date you act on.

faqs.question: Our tutor mentioned a March exam window. Should we be worried?
faqs.answer: Yes, enough to check. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only; UAE candidates sit June and November. Checkpoint tests at lower secondary do run in March, May and October, so there is a legitimate March reference at that stage, but for an IGCSE candidate here a February or March examination window does not exist. A tutor planning around one has not prepared UAE candidates, and the rest of their timeline assumptions are worth checking too.

faqs.question: Which subjects can you not easily staff for us?
faqs.answer: Computer Science at the specialist end, and Additional Mathematics, which has a smaller pool and fills early in the year. Mathematics, the three sciences, English and the business subjects are well covered and usually matched within the same week. For the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies subjects, support means working with the school's own material, because using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited.

faqs.question: How do we know the practical skills are being prepared properly?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer whether your child sits a laboratory practical examination or a written alternative-to-practical paper, then ask the tutor what that changes. Both routes test method writing, variables, instrument precision, tabulation, plotting and criticising a method. The trap in the written route is revising it as theory, which it is not. A block of four to six sessions on these skills earns marks in all three sciences at once and is rarely bought.

faqs.question: Our child is in Year 11 already. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, and the mock paper is your best asset. If the mock sits in January or February and the series is in June, a six-week programme attacking the specific question types that failed, with timed papers and explicit work on showing working and timing, usually moves marks. What does not work is restarting at the beginning of the specification. Be aware that the scarce weekday slots between 17:00 and 19:00 fill from September, so expect less choice of hour.

faqs.question: What does it mean if a tutor cannot name the paper structure?
faqs.answer: That they have not taught this entry recently, whatever their subject expertise. It is not a disqualification on its own, and it does mean the next question matters: will they confirm the structure with the school before building a plan? A tutor who says yes and then does it is fine. A tutor who glosses over it will be guessing about calculator rules, tier content and the practical route, which are the things that decide what your child should be practising.

faqs.question: Should we use a tuition centre instead of one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For a shared gap, a centre can be genuinely good value. A class on frequency density, on mole calculations or on structuring an evaluation question works well because everyone needs the same thing. It stops working when your child's problem is their own specific pattern of errors, because the hour runs on someone else's weakness. If you use one in Dubai, note that a premises-based training institute requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is fair to ask to see.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match someone, and what if nobody is free?
faqs.answer: For most subjects, within the same week. The scarce resource is the hour rather than the subject: weekday slots between 17:00 and 19:00 in the spring term are what every Year 11 household in Dubai wants. If your preferred combination is not free you are told, with a date, and offered an off-peak or weekend slot with the specialist or an interim tutor with a stated handover. Where a tutor is based outside the UAE, we say so before you book.

faqs.question: Does a Core or Foundation entry limit what comes next?
faqs.answer: Usually, in two ways. It caps the grade available and it removes content that post-16 courses assume, which is the part families discover later. If your child needs the subject at A Level or in the Diploma, contest it in Year 10 with marked evidence rather than accepting it silently, and ask the receiving sixth form directly what they expect. A term of weekly work on the content separating the tiers, plus strong school assessment marks, is what changes a head of department's view.

faqs.question: What time of day should we book?
faqs.answer: 17:00 on weekdays, or 17:30 if your child travels from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. With no school inside Jumeirah Islands every pupil travels out, and the return leg usually serves two or three other communities first, so arrivals home run from roughly 15:40 to 16:50. Ask your transport office for your own route's timings, because households inside the same gates differ by twenty minutes. Keep Saturday morning for a full timed paper and Sunday for marking it.

faqs.question: What would you tell us not to pay for?
faqs.answer: Three things. An in-home travel premium for a tutor who cannot name your child's syllabus code, because you are funding a drive rather than expertise. A twenty-session package bought before the match has been tested, because unused sessions are the commonest complaint in this market. And one hour split across three subjects, which completes nothing in any of them. If a marked paper shows the real issue is uncompleted school homework, we will say that too.

intro.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs here, and what it is worth
paragraphs: The published Dubai market runs from about AED 33 an hour to about AED 650, which is a twentyfold spread for something sold under one name. That alone tells you the word 'tutor' describes several different products. At the bottom you are buying company and routine from a university student. At the top you are buying scarcity. Most IGCSE grades move in the middle, and knowing where the middle sits is the whole point of this page.

Three of the six strongest competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do quote US dollars at families who transact in dirhams. One page contradicts its own prices in two different sections. So the first useful thing we can do for a Jumeirah Park family is put the figures in one table, attributed to whoever published them, with the month we read them.

The second useful thing is to reframe the question. An hourly rate is almost useless for planning; a monthly or annual figure is what decides whether an arrangement survives. Bestimate's Dubai rate survey puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Two subjects doubles it. Work from that number, not the hourly one.

On delivery we are straightforward. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. What a Jumeirah Park family gets is live online IGCSE tutoring, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers shared on screen. We target the near-me phrase because that is what parents search, and then tell you what the service is rather than leaving you to discover it.

That matters to the cost conversation because the in-home premium is real. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. You are paying for somebody's drive across Al Khail Road at half past five, and you are choosing from the smaller group of people willing to make it.

One piece of household context before the numbers. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. The school-fee line in your budget is therefore stable while you plan the tutoring one, which is a better position than families in this city have had for several years.

Everything below is built so you can price the decision properly: the annual arithmetic, the provider models compared, the five predictable ways money disappears, the questions to ask before you pay, and the cost of a resit against the cost of preventing one. Use it on any provider, including us.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary

programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, externally examined by Cambridge or Pearson. This is where almost all tutoring spending happens, and where most of it happens too late. programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge's June and November series, or Pearson's May/June and November. A resit means a second entry fee and a term of sixth-form applications made on a provisional grade, which is the real cost of leaving it late.

programmes.description: Three or four subjects, with higher tutoring rates because the specialist pool is smaller. Families who supported IGCSE properly often need less here, because the gap at A Level is independence rather than content, and independence is built in Years 10 and 11.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-pa.subjectsIntro: Not every IGCSE subject costs the same to support, because scarcity differs. These are the subjects Jumeirah Park families most often pay for, and what the money is actually buying in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject families spend most on and the one where spending early pays best. Extended work is method-led: multi-step questions where the student knows the content and drops marks in the middle. Marked past papers under time are most of the value, and that work does not need a tutor in the room.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: A smaller specialist pool, so rates sit at the upper end of the qualified-tutor band. Taken alongside the main course by students heading for A Level Maths. Calculus arrives early and exposes any weakness in indices and surds, which is cheaper to fix before the course starts than during it.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and moments are the two topics most often rebuilt from scratch rather than revised, which is why physics blocks tend to run longer than parents budget for. The practical paper rewards precise method description, a skill that transfers across all three sciences and is worth buying once.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations decide a large share of the Extended grade and are entirely trainable, which makes chemistry one of the better-value subjects to tutor. Qualitative analysis and separation techniques carry marks students routinely drop for no reason other than never having been drilled on them.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The cheapest science to support in theory and the slowest to shift in practice, because the problem is precision of language rather than content. Answer construction against real mark schemes works, but it takes more weeks than a maths intervention, so budget time rather than money.

subjects.name: English Language and English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Directed writing responds quickly to tutoring and composition does not, so a block aimed at reading comprehension and directed writing is better value than an open-ended one. Check which English qualification your child is entered for; students entered for the wrong one lose marks nobody explains.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Level-of-response marking means an undeveloped correct point earns little, so the work is structure and evaluation rather than content. Good value because the technique transfers across both subjects and across papers, and a small number of sessions usually produces a visible change.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: A thinner tutor pool pushes rates up. Computer Science wants pseudocode, trace tables and algorithmic reasoning in a written paper; ICT is practical and applied. The two are confused at option time, and a wrong choice is expensive to unwind in Year 11.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Compulsory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Excluded from the five subjects Ministry of Education equivalency counts, which affects where support money is best spent.

What the bands buy differs more than the numbers suggest. sections.heading: The five ways IGCSE tutoring money gets wasted here
paragraphs: These are specific, predictable and avoidable, and we see all five from this part of Dubai. None of them is about choosing an expensive tutor over a cheap one; the most expensive mistake on the list costs nothing per hour.

The biggest is board-blind tutoring. A tutor working from Cambridge past papers for a child entered with Pearson, or the reverse, will teach competently and change nothing. One email to the school's exams officer asking for the syllabus code and tier prevents it. The second biggest is paying for Extended content when a child is entered for Core, or vice versa, which wastes the hour and damages confidence.

The third is timing: starting in February for a June series. The fourth is buying a twenty-session package before testing the match, then using eleven. The fifth is spreading one weekly hour across three subjects, which produces three partial interventions instead of one that works. The table sets out each with what it costs and the alternative.

A note on the fifth, because it is the one parents defend hardest. Splitting an hour between maths and physics feels fair and reads well on a schedule, but neither subject gets a complete piece of work and neither gets a past paper marked properly. If two subjects genuinely need support, buy two hours or pick one and do it properly for a term. Fairness between subjects is not a teaching principle.

There is a sixth that belongs in a different category. Anyone offering to produce coursework for your child is selling an academic-integrity breach, not a service, and the consequence falls on the student. That is not a waste of money; it is a risk to a qualification.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, at model level
paragraphs: Comparing individual companies is less useful than comparing models, because the model determines who actually teaches and what happens when something goes wrong. There are six models operating around Jumeirah Park and they behave differently on price, replacement and accountability.

The questions that separate them are not about teaching quality, which you cannot assess from a website. They are structural: who employs the tutor, whether you can change tutor without losing money, whether the rate quoted includes travel, and whether anyone has checked that the tutor holds a Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition permit.

The table compares models rather than named brands, and quotes published rates only where the provider published them with a date. This is deliberate: comparing against an unnamed worse competitor is what every page in this market does, and it tells a parent nothing.

The model that most often surprises families here is the tuition centre. Per student per hour it is the cheapest option after school support, and for a shared gap such as mole calculations or evaluation technique it can be genuinely good value. It stops working when your child's problem is specific, because the hour runs on somebody else's weakness, and in Dubai a centre with premises needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a fair thing to ask to see.

We select and brief the tutor, you keep the same tutor week to week, and if the match is wrong we change it rather than asking you to persist. sections.heading: Questions to ask before you pay anyone
paragraphs: Hidden extras are where a quoted rate stops resembling the bill. These are the questions worth asking in writing, of us or of anyone else, before money changes hands. None of them is awkward, and a provider who evades one has answered it.

Start with the unit. Is the price per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? A fifty-minute lesson priced as an hour is a ten per cent difference nobody mentions. Then ask whether VAT is included in the figure quoted. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a general fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, so ask any provider specifically whether their quoted dirham figure is the figure you pay.

Then the mechanics. What happens to a session you cancel with a day's notice, and to one the tutor cancels? Is there a minimum commitment, and what happens to unused sessions in a package? Does the rate change closer to the exams, which it does with several providers? Is there a charge for the first consultation, and is the trial genuinely free without card details?

Finally the people. Who is the tutor, where are they based, do they hold a MoHRE private tuition permit, and have they taught this syllabus code at this tier? And one closing question that sorts providers quickly: what will you not do? The right answer includes not writing coursework and not promising a grade.

sections.heading: The cost of a resit against the cost of prevention
paragraphs: This is the arithmetic that most changes behaviour, and almost nobody sets it out. A UAE Cambridge candidate has two series available, June and November; the February/March series is offered to India only and is not an option here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. So a resit means the November series.

The Pearson precedent shows the timing cost. The November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026. A November resit therefore means a sixth-form application season carried out with a provisional grade in that subject.

Against that, set the cost of prevention. A weekly hour in the relevant subject from the autumn of Year 10, at the published qualified-tutor band, spread across the two years. It is not a trivial sum, but it is spread, it is cancellable, and it does not carry the second entry fee, the lost term or the uncertainty in a sixth-form conversation.

There is a third option between the two, which families often miss: an enquiry about results. Where a grade sits just below a boundary, the school can submit a review of marking within a short window after results, for a fee set by the board. It is not a resit and it does not involve more teaching, and it is worth asking the exams officer about on results day rather than a fortnight later when the window has closed.

Dates and timetables are revised and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone's timetable, so plan from the live official timetable your school's exams officer holds rather than from any date on a tutoring page.

sections.heading: What we will not sell you
paragraphs: A cost page should be clear about what is not on the menu, because in this market some of it is. We do not write, part-write, rewrite or supply coursework of any kind. Where an IGCSE subject carries an assessed component, a tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on work your child has written, and that is the limit. Submitting work that is not the student's own puts the qualification at risk and the risk falls on the student.

We do not sell grade guarantees, score promises or money-back improvement schemes, because no honest provider can deliver one. We do not publish a star rating, a review count or a satisfaction percentage, because any statistic we put on this page would need its sample size, date and method attached, and we would rather publish nothing than publish a number you cannot check.

We do not supply or reproduce Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are cited and linked; your child's school holds licensed access to what they need. Anyone offering you a folder of exam material is offering a copyright problem rather than an advantage.

And we claim no approval we do not hold. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit. We explain what those bodies do because parents ask, not because any of them endorses us.

faqs.question: What is a fair hourly rate for IGCSE tutoring in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150. Below AED 100 you are generally buying supervision rather than subject teaching; Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. Specialist work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Those are the providers' own figures read in October 2026, and none of them is our price.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor more expensive than the same tutor online?
faqs.answer: Because you are buying the commute. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. A tutor driving into Jumeirah Park in the 17:30 peak loses forty to ninety minutes in round-trip travel, and that appears in the rate whether or not it is itemised. The smaller cost is the cash; the larger one is choosing from only those tutors willing to make the journey.

faqs.question: Should I buy a monthly package or pay session by session?
faqs.answer: Pay for a small number of sessions until the match is proven, then consider a package if the price genuinely improves. Published monthly packages in Dubai run from around AED 799 for eight online sessions to AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. The risk in a package bought early is unused sessions, which is the most common complaint in this market. Ask in writing what happens to sessions you do not use and whether a cancelled session is credited or lost.

faqs.question: How much should a Jumeirah Park family budget for a full Year 11?
faqs.answer: Using Bestimate's monthly bands, one subject weekly with a qualified tutor sits at roughly AED 600-1,200 a month, or about AED 5,400-10,800 across nine months. Two subjects roughly doubles that. Specialist exam-year support in a single subject is estimated at AED 1,000-2,000 or more monthly. Add exam entry fees charged by the school, and a second entry fee if a resit follows. Those are market figures rather than ours, and they are indicative; the point is to plan from a yearly number.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a nearby centre better value than one-to-one for a Jumeirah Park family?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and per unit of improvement it depends entirely on the problem. A group class works where the whole group shares a gap: a class on mole calculations or on structuring an evaluation question can be excellent value. It works badly where your child's problem is specific, because the hour is spent on somebody else's weakness. Check the group size and ask whether the centre holds a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is required for a training institute with premises in Dubai.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai go up closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: With several providers they do, and it is worth asking before you commit. Demand concentrates in the spring term, specialist slots in the weekday 17:00 to 19:00 window fill, and the market prices accordingly. The practical consequence is that booking in September both secures the slot and avoids the squeeze. Ask any provider directly whether the rate quoted in October is the rate you will pay in March, and get the answer in writing rather than in conversation.

faqs.question: Does the price I am quoted include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly, and get a written answer. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, so the useful question is narrower: is the dirham figure you have been quoted the figure that will be charged? A provider who cannot answer that clearly has told you something about how they handle the rest of the paperwork. The same applies to whether the price is per hour or per lesson, and how long a lesson is.

faqs.question: What is the single most expensive mistake families make here?
faqs.answer: Board-blind tutoring. A tutor working from Cambridge past papers for a child entered with Pearson Edexcel, or the reverse, will teach competently and move nothing, and the parent usually discovers it after a term. It costs the entire spend. One email to the school's exams officer asking for the syllabus code and tier in each subject prevents it before any money is committed. The second most expensive is teaching Extended content to a Core candidate, which wastes the hour and knocks confidence.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start tutoring in Year 10 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, substantially, and it is also more effective. One hour a week from the autumn of Year 10 spreads a mid-band monthly figure across roughly seventy weeks, keeps the higher tier reachable while that decision is still open, and usually removes the need for an intensive programme later. Starting in February of Year 11 concentrates a larger figure into twelve weeks at the highest cost per unit of improvement, and competes for the scarcest slots in the market.

faqs.question: What does a November resit actually cost us?
faqs.answer: More in timing than in money. A UAE candidate's resit route is the November series, since Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. The Pearson precedent is instructive: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January, and November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026. So you pay a second entry fee, lose a term, and apply to sixth form with a provisional grade. Prevention is cheaper on every measure.

faqs.question: Can we spend less by sharing a tutor between two children?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the children are close in curriculum and level. Two siblings in the same subject and tier can share an hour productively, and some providers price that below two separate hours. Two children in different years or different subjects cannot, and attempting it produces two half-sessions. Ask how the provider prices a shared session rather than assuming it halves. In our case the honest answer is that it works for genuinely matched siblings and is a false economy otherwise.

faqs.question: How do I compare two quotes that look completely different?
faqs.answer: Reduce both to four numbers: cost per sixty minutes of teaching, cost per month at the frequency you actually need, what happens to a cancelled session, and what happens if you change tutor. Then ask both providers the same two structural questions: who employs the tutor and where are they based, and does the tutor hold a Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition permit. Most quotes that look cheaper are either shorter lessons, group sessions, or supervision sold as teaching.

faqs.question: Is there any point paying for a premium examiner-led tutor?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and with caution. The top of this market reaches AED 650 an hour on BartyED's published figures, and for a scarce Extended subject in the final weeks a genuinely expert tutor can be worth it. But examiner status is hard to verify, it should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, and it is not a substitute for teaching skill. Ask what evidences the claim. For most IGCSE subjects the AED 150-300 band does the work.

faqs.question: What should we expect to see for the money after six weeks?
faqs.answer: Specific question types that previously lost marks now scoring on timed work, and your child able to explain the method without being prompted. Not a predicted grade, and not a feeling that sessions are going well. If after six sessions the marked evidence has not moved, the problem is the match, the frequency or the diagnosis, and one of those should change rather than more hours being bought. No honest provider will promise a grade or a number of marks.

faqs.question: Do you have a centre in Jumeirah Park we could visit?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, and no in-home service here either; home visits are an India-only service. Everything is delivered as live one-to-one online lessons on Gulf Standard Time. We say this plainly because at least one competitor in this market shows a Dubai footer address on pages about other emirates, and because a parent comparing prices needs to know exactly what is and is not included in the thing being priced.

intro.heading: Comparing neighbourhoods is the wrong comparison
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Circle sits inside a ring of communities that look interchangeable on a map and feel quite different to live in. JVT is next door and quieter. Al Barsha South holds much of the nearby school provision. Motor City is eight to fifteen minutes along Hessa Street with a large British-curriculum campus. Families here compare all four constantly: for schools, for rent, for the commute, and for tutoring.

On three of those four, the comparison is genuinely informative. School provision differs. Commute times differ by twenty minutes or more at the edges. Session timing differs, because a student in Al Barsha South is home before a student travelling from Arabian Ranches 3. Those are real distinctions and this page sets them out in a table.

On tutoring quality, the comparison collapses, and it is worth understanding why. The supply of people who teach a specific IGCSE syllabus code to a specific tier is set at the level of the emirate, not the neighbourhood. There are not Cambridge 0580 specialists in Motor City and a different set in JVT; there is one small pool of people in Dubai who teach that code well, almost all employed full time, and they are distributed by where they happen to live rather than by any logic connected to your address. Moving from the Circle to Al Barsha South would change your school run and would not change which tutors can actually help.

So the comparison that matters is not between areas. It is between provider models — agency, international marketplace, independent freelance tutor, tuition centre group class, school-run support, and online one-to-one — because those differ enormously in price, accountability and what they actually deliver. Most tutoring pages compare themselves against an unnamed set of other platforms. This one compares the models, with the rates attributed to whoever published them.

There is a second comparison this page insists on, and it is the one that actually changes outcomes: Cambridge IGCSE against Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. They are different qualifications with different paper structures, different tier names, a different calculator position in mathematics and a different practical route in the sciences. A tutor working from the wrong scheme of work spends your money on topics your child will never be asked about, and that mistake is far more expensive than any difference between one of these neighbourhoods and the next.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, matched by syllabus code. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Our fee follows a free trial lesson, because an honest number depends on a session count only a marked paper can establish.

subjects.description: The most requested subject in every one of these areas. Losses are habitual rather than conceptual: unrounded intermediate values carried forward, and method lines omitted on four and five-mark questions where the steps are the marks.

sections.heading: What actually differs between these four communities
paragraphs: The honest comparison first, because the rest of the page argues that it does not matter much for tutoring and it genuinely matters for other things. School provision differs: Al Barsha South and JVT hold several campuses this whole cluster uses, Motor City has a large British-curriculum school inside it, and the Circle itself has provision but fewer secondary options. Whether a campus offers three separate sciences, the coordinated double award, or Additional Mathematics 0606 varies by school rather than by area, which is a reason to compare schools specifically.

Commute differs. From the Circle, JVT and Al Barsha South are five to fifteen minutes and Motor City is eight to fifteen, so a student lands home around 3.45pm. From Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square the same school day ends after 4.30pm. Housing type differs, and it has a small tutoring consequence. The Circle and Dubai Sports City are apartment-heavy; JVT, Arabian Ranches and Mudon are villa and townhouse communities. A student working at a kitchen table in a two-bedroom apartment with siblings present has a different environment from one with a study, and that affects whether a session needs headphones and a closed door more than it affects anything else.

sections.heading: Why the tutoring answer is the same in all four
paragraphs: Think about how the supply of IGCSE specialists is actually produced. A school needs roughly one physics teacher per few hundred students, and only some of those have taught Extended-tier Cambridge 0625 rather than a national curriculum or Pearson 4PH1. Across the whole of Dubai that produces a small population of people who teach any particular code to any particular tier, and nearly all of them are employed full time at the schools that offer it.

Those people live wherever they live. There is no mechanism that concentrates Cambridge 0580 specialists in Motor City or Pearson 4CH1 specialists in JVT. So when a family compares tutoring between these four communities, they are comparing samples of the same emirate-wide pool, drawn by the accident of where individuals happen to rent. Moving house would change the school run, the rent and the commute, and would not change which tutors can teach your child's code.

This is also why the local search result is such a poor guide. A place-name query returns whoever optimised for that place name, and research across sixty-odd competitor pages in this market in October 2026 found agencies routing UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, one page displaying a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page, and several listing twenty-five or more schools as clients with no apparent relationship. Local presence in a search result is a claim, not a fact.

The consequence is straightforward. Stop comparing areas and start comparing provider models and syllabus-code coverage. Ask which school a tutor teaches at and at what tier, which code they work from, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Those three answers are checkable from any of these four addresses and they are the same three answers that matter in all of them.

paragraphs: Here is the comparison worth making. Every tutoring page in this market compares itself favourably against an unnamed set of other platforms, which tells a parent nothing. A model-level comparison, with rates attributed to whoever published them, is more useful and more honest.

An agency matches you to a tutor and takes a margin, and quality depends entirely on how it vets. An international marketplace gives you volume and reviews and typically quotes in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in — two of the six best-ranking pages in this market do exactly that. An independent freelance tutor is often the best value and carries no replacement if the match is wrong or they leave mid-term. A tuition centre group class is cheaper per student and cannot diagnose an individual error. School-run support is free and limited to what the timetable allows. Online one-to-one widens the pool to everyone who teaches the code.

On rates: budget online tuition is advertised in Dubai from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with one platform listing from AED 33 to AED 52 and another from AED 45 to AED 65. Specialist provision is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, one UK agency at AED 270, and premium examiner-led work as high as AED 650. All read from the providers' own pages in October 2026.

The three questions that separate the models are not about price. Does somebody replace the tutor if the match is wrong, and at what cost? Is marking between sessions included or billed? sections.heading: The board comparison, which does matter
paragraphs: Having argued that the area is the wrong variable, here is a comparison that is genuinely load-bearing and that most families cannot make. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are different qualifications with different paper structures, different tier names and, in some subjects, different content. A tutor working from the wrong scheme of work spends your money on topics your child will not be asked about.

Find the answer on the last report or the entry confirmation, where the syllabus code appears. Cambridge is four digits: 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610, 0654, 0500. Pearson combines a digit and letters: 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1, 4SD0, 4EA1. In Dubai it is entirely normal for one student to sit different subjects with different boards, because schools choose per department, so check every subject rather than assuming.

The structural differences worth knowing: the current Cambridge mathematics model assesses through two papers of equal weight, one without a calculator and one with, while Pearson permits a calculator on both of its mathematics papers. Tier names differ — Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher — with the same effective grade ceiling of 5 on the lower tier. Practical assessment in the sciences differs between a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper depending on the entry.

And one supply difference that is emirate-wide rather than local: Pearson specialists are scarcer in Dubai than Cambridge specialists. That affects how early you need to book rather than what you pay, and it is identical whether you live in the Circle, JVT, Al Barsha South or Motor City.

sections.heading: The tier ceiling, identical in every one of these areas
paragraphs: If this page persuades a Jumeirah Village Circle parent of one thing, let it be this. A Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum available grade at 5, and a Pearson Foundation entry does the same. A student needing a 6 or 7 for science A Levels or IB Diploma Higher Level cannot reach it from the lower tier, in any community, at any rate, with any provider.

Schools in all four of these areas make the decision for the same defensible reason: a borderline candidate entered for the higher tier can score below its lowest available grade and come away with nothing, where the lower tier would have produced a secure 4 or 5. It is a risk judgement rather than administrative caution. But it is made on Year 10 evidence, and a student whose work changes in the first term of Year 11 can sometimes be moved if somebody asks before the final entry deadline.

A five or six session block on higher-tier material is the purchase that has leverage here, because it produces a clear answer and, more usefully, written evidence a head of year can act on. Both possible outcomes are worth having, and the one that says the gap is too wide saves considerably more money than the one that says it is not.

Where the tier cannot change, the options are to revise the post-16 plan or to enter the November series on the higher tier, potentially as a private candidate through an approved Dubai centre. Both are legitimate. Buying thirty weekly sessions against a ceiling is not, and we will say so before taking a booking rather than after the first invoice.

paragraphs: Families in this cluster do move between these communities, and tutoring access is occasionally cited as a reason. It is worth being direct: it is not a good reason, and three other reasons are.

Moving from the Circle to Al Barsha South or JVT buys you a shorter school run, which is genuinely valuable — fifteen or twenty minutes twice a day is a real quantity of a teenager's week, and it moves a session slot earlier by half an hour. Moving to Dubai Hills Estate buys you access to a different set of schools, which may matter if the current campus does not offer three separate sciences or Additional Mathematics 0606. Moving away from the Dubai Sports City edge may reduce academy pull on the four-to-six window, though families usually keep the academy.

What a move does not buy is a better tutor. The specialist pool for your child's syllabus code is drawn from the whole emirate, and it is sampled by where individuals happen to live rather than by anything connected to your address. A family that moves for tutoring access has paid moving costs to change a variable that was never the constraint.

The same logic applies in reverse and is more useful: if you are staying, you are not disadvantaged. Whatever is available to a family in Al Barsha South is available to a family in the Circle once the travel requirement is removed, which is the entire argument for online delivery in a cluster like this one.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor, in any of these communities
paragraphs: The rules are federal and emirate-level, so they are identical across this whole comparison. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category explains much of the AED 45 to AED 150 band: a very low rate usually signals tutor category rather than illegality. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure can honestly be quoted and we do not quote one.

One boundary applies everywhere in this cluster. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being treated as exact wording. The practical rule holds regardless: do not engage your child's own teacher privately.

And what nobody in any of these areas holds. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA — which is a thing a tuition centre in Motor City may legitimately hold and an individual tutor cannot. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB.

From Jumeirah Village Circle, JVT and Al Barsha South, students travel five to fifteen minutes and are home around 3.45pm. From Motor City it is eight to fifteen. From Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square it is twenty to thirty-five minutes and home is after 4.30pm.

That ought to open an early slot for the inner three, and mostly it does not, because Dubai Sports City sits next to the Circle and its academies take students out between four and six. So the workable windows across this cluster are around 5.30pm for students without a club, 7pm to 8.15pm for those with one, and the later end of that range for anybody commuting from the outer belt.

Put the session after a first attempt at the school's work rather than before. A student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, which a specialist resolves quickly; scheduled earlier, the session becomes supervised homework at a specialist rate. This holds in all four communities and is not an area-level question at all.

Weekend mornings are the most underused slot across this whole cluster and the right one for whole timed papers, which need ninety uninterrupted minutes. Online delivery is what keeps the arrangement robust: sessions move within the week when a mock or an academy fixture collides, shift post-Iftar during Ramadan, and stop cleanly at study leave, agreed on day one.
