intro.heading: Four decisions that matter more than which tutor is closest
paragraphs: The search term says tutor, but the problem is usually a decision. Before a single lesson is booked, a family looking for an IGCSE tutor near me in Jumeirah Village Triangle normally needs an answer to one of four questions, and getting those wrong costs more than any tutor can recover. How many subjects should the child enter. Triple science or combined. English as a First Language or as a Second Language. And, if a grade has already come back short, whether a November resit is the right response or a distraction.

Take subject count first. Dubai schools typically enter students for eight to ten IGCSEs. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. Sixth-form and A Level courses add their own requirements, usually grade 6 or 7 in the subject to be continued. Beyond those two constraints, extra subjects buy breadth at the cost of attention, and a student carrying ten subjects at grade 5 is in a weaker position than one carrying seven at grade 7.

Then the science decision, which quietly closes doors. Separate sciences — Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610 as three distinct IGCSEs — is the route that keeps every A Level and IB Higher Level science open without argument. Combined or coordinated science counts for fewer qualifications and some sixth forms treat it as insufficient preparation for an HL science. A Year 10 student intending to read medicine or engineering needs this decision made deliberately, not by timetable default.

English next. English as a First Language and English as a Second Language are different qualifications with different papers and different university recognition. Second-language entry is appropriate for many students in a multilingual city and is a sensible protective choice, but some destinations treat first-language English as the stronger signal. Ask the school which entry is planned and why, because the answer is sometimes about the set a child was placed in two years earlier rather than about current ability. A short diagnostic on first-language reading questions settles it faster than a conversation does, and it gives you something concrete to take back to the school if the planned entry looks wrong for the destination the family has in mind.

Finally the resit question. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, so a June grade can be improved in November with results reaching students in January. Whether that is wise depends on what the grade is needed for and when. This page sets out all four decisions with the figures behind them, then covers rates, formats, the examination calendar and the regulator position. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-vi.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects most requested from the Jumeirah Village Triangle area, with the Cambridge code and what actually decides the grade in each. Resit candidates most often come to us for the first three.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended rewards method shown step by step; a right answer with no working loses marks that were available. The recurring losses are algebraic fractions, graph transformations and multi-step problems where rounding is applied before the final line. Resit candidates usually need timing work more than content.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Circuits, electromagnetic induction and graph work account for most lost marks. The alternative-to-practical paper assesses method on paper, including apparatus choice and precision, and is routinely the least practised paper in a school revision programme.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic and ionic equations without state symbols cost the most. Qualitative analysis — the tests for cations, anions and gases — is recall rather than reasoning, which makes it the fastest recoverable block of marks in the last month of a course.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: The volume of content is the difficulty, not its depth. Answer length has to match the mark allocation, and command terms decide what is wanted: 'state' takes a phrase, 'explain' takes a reason. Transport in plants and genetics are the recurring weak topics.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: Covers all three sciences in one or two IGCSEs rather than three. Content is reduced across each discipline, which makes it a manageable load but can limit entry to an A Level or Higher Level science. Check the sixth-form requirement before the Year 9 option form is signed.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading responses must quote precisely and analyse effect rather than restate content. Directed writing is marked on register and audience as much as on accuracy. Timed practice moves the grade more reliably than additional content teaching does.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Comprehension marks depend on lifting the correct phrase rather than paraphrasing well. The summary task has a strict word limit and credits content points. Speaking is assessed separately on some entries and is usually prepared too late.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 in stronger sets. Introduces calculus and trigonometric identities a year early, which flattens the step into A Level or Higher Level mathematics considerably. Students who struggle here despite handling 0580 are short on algebraic fluency.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram marks are allocated separately from the prose: axes labelled, curves shifted, new equilibrium marked. The four-part structured questions escalate to an eight-mark evaluation, and students routinely spend their time budget before reaching it.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the named firm in the stimulus separates a 5 from an 8. Generic theory scores low. Break-even and ratio arithmetic is a dependable source of marks for a student willing to drill it, and is often skipped in favour of essay content.

sections.heading: How many IGCSEs does a Dubai student actually need?
paragraphs: Fewer than most timetables offer. Two separate requirements govern the number, and both are smaller than the eight to ten subjects a Dubai school typically enters. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Sixth-form and A Level entry adds its own threshold, usually grade 6 or 7 in each subject to be continued.

That matters because a competitor page ranking for UAE searches states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The published figure is five. A parent planning around six over-subscribes their child by a subject, and a subject's worth of attention spread across a crowded entry is not free.

The sensible planning order is backwards from the destination. List the sixth-form or Diploma courses the student is likely to want, find the grade each one requires, and make sure those subjects are on the list at a tier that can reach the grade. Then confirm the five-subject equivalency floor is comfortably cleared. Whatever slots remain are genuinely discretionary, and that is where breadth belongs.

What this does not mean is that fewer subjects is automatically better. A student capable of ten strong grades should take them. The failure mode is the student carrying ten subjects at grade 5 when seven at grade 7 would have opened more doors, and that student is usually carrying subjects nobody checked the purpose of.

sections.heading: Separate sciences or combined: the decision that closes doors
paragraphs: Separate sciences means three IGCSEs: Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, each with its own full syllabus and papers. Combined or coordinated science covers all three disciplines in one or two IGCSEs with reduced content in each. Both are legitimate qualifications and schools in Dubai offer both, often with set placement deciding which a student is put forward for.

The difference is what happens at sixteen. A student who took separate sciences can walk into A Level Chemistry or IB Chemistry Higher Level without an argument. A student who took combined science sometimes can and sometimes cannot, because the receiving school judges whether the reduced content is sufficient preparation, and some will not accept it for a Higher Level science at all. For a child who might read medicine, dentistry, engineering or a physical science, that is a live risk rather than a theoretical one.

The trade is load. Three separate sciences is substantially more content than combined, and three mediocre science grades serve a student worse than two solid ones plus a stronger entry elsewhere. The decision therefore depends on genuine capability in Year 9, which is exactly what set placement is a rough proxy for and sometimes a bad one — a child placed on a lower set in Year 8 because of a weak term can find the science route decided by that term two years later.

The useful intervention is evidence. A few sessions of real Extended-standard questions across the three sciences will show whether the load is realistic, and the result is something a parent can take to the school rather than an opinion.

sections.heading: Reading the grade scale, and the resit route after a short result
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE results now come on a 9-1 numeric scale, with 9 the highest, alongside legacy A*-G reporting on some syllabuses and in some regions. Parents who sat GCSEs themselves tend to read the numbers against the old letters incorrectly, usually assuming 9 maps to A* exactly and 7 maps to B. It does not; the scales were set so that the numeric grades spread the top end more finely. What matters practically is the threshold the receiving school names, which will be stated in the scale it uses.

If a result comes in short, the UAE resit route is the November series. Cambridge runs June and November for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Critically, Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route for a UAE candidate however often a search result suggests it.

The timing decides whether a resit is useful. Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. A result in January is mid-academic-year, so before entering, ask the receiving sixth form in writing whether a January grade will satisfy a conditional offer. For an equivalency file rather than a school place, a January result is usually fine.

A student retaking after leaving school may need to enter as a private candidate through an approved examination centre. Deadlines and fees for private entry are set by the centre, not by the board, and they fall well before the series. Confirm both in writing before planning a revision programme around them, and work the schedule backwards from the entry deadline rather than the examination date.

sections.heading: Group class, private visit or one-to-one online
paragraphs: Three delivery models compete for a Dubai family's tutoring budget and they are rarely compared honestly. A tuition centre group class is the cheapest per hour and works for a student who needs structure and company rather than diagnosis. A private home visit is the most expensive and buys presence in the room. One-to-one online sits between them on price and gives the widest choice of tutor.

On published figures: Tutopiya advertises online tuition from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table places qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or above, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Every figure here is the provider's own, read in October 2026.

The variable most families underweight is attention per hour. A group class at a low hourly rate can deliver less individual attention in a term than a smaller number of one-to-one sessions, and for a student whose problem is a specific recurring error — rounding early in 0580, omitting state symbols in 0620 — group teaching cannot see the error at all. Conversely, a student whose problem is simply not working is often better served by a structured group than by an expensive private hour they coast through.
IB Gram delivers one-to-one online only in the UAE. No home visits, no centre, no group classes. The table compares the three models on the factors that actually differ.

sections.heading: What the IGCSE calendar looks like from a JVT kitchen table
paragraphs: The useful version of an examination calendar is the one that says what should already be done by each point. Counting forwards from today produces a revision plan; counting backwards from results day produces a plan that accounts for the deadlines that close options rather than the ones that merely add pressure.

The fixed points are these. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, plus Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always open the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

The rule that catches families out is Cambridge's zoning. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. If you are printing a timetable to put on the fridge, get the zone from the examinations officer first.

And the reminder that belongs on every UAE page: the February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November. A plan built around a March window is a plan built around a date that does not exist for your child.

sections.heading: The regulator picture, and what nobody can claim
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Elsewhere in the country the map is different: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools; Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits with the emirate in those cases rather than inspection alone.

For a Jumeirah Village Triangle family the relevant regulator is KHDA, and the relevant document is your own school's published inspection report. The headline band on the six-point scale from Outstanding to Very Weak is the least informative line in it. The subject-level commentary is where a tutoring decision should be made, because it names the specific weakness in the cohort rather than in your child.

KHDA also sets the mandatory-subject rules that shape a Dubai timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with any mandatory-subject lesson advised to run at least 25 minutes, and using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is strictly prohibited.

What no tutoring provider can claim: approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from any of those bodies, or from Cambridge or Pearson, unless it actually holds it. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises in Dubai, with annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds none of these, has no UAE office or examination centre, and cannot enter a candidate for an examination. Entry goes through your school or an approved centre.

sections.heading: Booking, matching and the availability we will admit to
paragraphs: Start by sending the board, syllabus code and tier per subject if you have them, the specific worry, and a marked piece of work. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson and sends a written note within a working day naming the repeating errors and estimating sessions. You decide after reading it. Nothing is charged before that note exists, and if the honest conclusion is that the target is out of reach in the time available, the note says so.

On availability: mainstream specifications have deep cover for UAE evening slots and normally match within one to three working days. Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English 0500 and 0510, Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 are all in that group. Minority entries are not. An uncommon language, a Pearson code a Dubai school has only just adopted, or a subject with a very small cohort may have no free UAE-resident specialist at all, and then the tutor comes from our India-based faculty working on Gulf Standard Time. We say which before you book.

Scheduling around the Triangle is simple enough in practice. Children at Sunmarke School or Arcadia Global School inside the community can take a 16:30 slot. Families driving back from Motor City, Dubai Hills or the Dubailand schools usually want 17:30 or later. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00 and often 45 minutes rather than an hour. Mock weeks are generally paused outright, then resumed with a session spent reading the marked scripts.

On permits, because it is a fair question to ask any tutor. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here. The route is MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, with no listed fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our house in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do offer it, at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors once travel is included. IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE — home visits are an India-only service for us. UAE students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with a shared whiteboard and a session recording. The practical gain is that the tutor is chosen for having taught your child's syllabus code rather than for living within a short drive of the Triangle.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should a Dubai student actually enter?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from two requirements rather than filling the timetable. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. Sixth-form entry adds its own threshold, usually grade 6 or 7 in each subject to be continued. Beyond those, extra subjects buy breadth at the cost of attention. One competitor page states six IGCSEs are required; the published figure is five, and planning around six costs a subject's worth of focus.

faqs.question: Should my child take separate sciences or combined science?
faqs.answer: If there is any chance of an A Level or IB Higher Level science, separate sciences is the route that keeps it open without argument. Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 as three IGCSEs carry the full syllabus in each. Combined or coordinated science reduces content across all three, and some receiving schools treat it as insufficient preparation for a Higher Level science. The trade is load: three mediocre science grades serve a student worse than two strong ones. Test the load with real Extended-standard questions before the Year 9 option form is signed.

faqs.question: Is English as a Second Language a weaker qualification than First Language?
faqs.answer: They are different qualifications rather than strong and weak versions of one. English as a Second Language, Cambridge 0510 and 0511, assesses comprehension, summary and controlled writing, and for many students in a multilingual city it is the appropriate and protective entry. English First Language, 0500, demands analysis of literary effect and reading responses that quote precisely. Some destinations treat first-language English as the stronger signal. Ask the school which entry is planned and on what basis, because the answer is sometimes a set placement made two years earlier rather than a judgement about current ability.

faqs.question: Can my child retake an IGCSE in November after a June result?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, so November is the UAE resit route. The February/March series is offered to India only and is not available to a UAE candidate. The thing to check first is timing: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a resit grade arrives mid-academic-year. If a sixth-form place depends on it, get written confirmation from the receiving school that a January result satisfies the offer.

faqs.question: What does entering as a private candidate in Dubai involve?
faqs.answer: A candidate no longer attending the school usually has to enter through an approved examination centre, and the centre rather than the awarding body sets the deadlines and the fees. Those deadlines fall well before the examination window, which is why a revision programme should be built backwards from the entry date and not from the paper date. IB Gram is not an examination centre and cannot enter anybody; we teach, and the family arranges entry. Confirm the centre's fee and deadline in writing before planning anything around the series.

faqs.question: How do the 9-1 and A*-G IGCSE grade scales line up?
faqs.answer: Not as neatly as parents expect. The 9-1 numeric scale runs with 9 highest and was designed to spread the top end more finely than A*-G did, so assuming 9 equals A* and 7 equals B will mislead you. Some Cambridge syllabuses and regions still report letters. What matters in practice is the threshold the receiving school names and the scale it names it in: a sixth form asking for grade 6 is asking in numbers, and a school asking for a B is asking in letters. Get the requirement in the scale your child's certificate will use.

faqs.question: Is a cheap group class at a Dubai centre a false economy?
faqs.answer: Not always, and it depends on what is wrong. A group class delivers structure, routine and company at the lowest hourly cost in this market, and for a student whose real problem is simply not sitting down to work, that can be exactly right. What it cannot do is see an individual error pattern — early rounding in Mathematics 0580, missing state symbols in Chemistry 0620 — because the teaching is pitched at the group. Where the problem is a specific recurring mistake, a smaller number of one-to-one sessions usually moves the grade further for the same money.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge timetable zone is a Dubai school in?
faqs.answer: Your examinations officer knows, and it is worth asking before you print anything. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The realistic risk is a parent downloading a timetable PDF from a search result and planning a family trip around a date that belongs to a different zone entirely.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth a slot for a JVT student?
faqs.answer: For a student heading to A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level, usually yes — Cambridge 0606 introduces calculus and trigonometric identities a year early and flattens the step into sixth form noticeably. For a student who finds 0580 Extended demanding, it is an extra examination for limited gain and the slot is better spent securing the subjects that offers and equivalency actually depend on. A student who copes with 0580 but struggles with 0606 is almost always short on algebraic fluency rather than on understanding, and that is fixable.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 11 student in the Triangle usually need?
faqs.answer: For one subject with a diagnosed error pattern, six to ten weekly sessions is the normal range. Moving a whole subject from a 4 to a 7 is a two-term project rather than an eight-week one, and anyone promising otherwise is guessing. A resit programme over the summer and autumn for a November series typically runs longer, twelve to twenty sessions, because the student has no school timetable holding the structure. The written diagnosis after the free first lesson gives a specific figure, and says plainly when the time left is not enough.

faqs.question: Do Dubai's mandatory subjects reduce the slots available for IGCSEs?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, which is why the discretionary part of a timetable is smaller than the subject count suggests. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those subjects also sit outside the five that Ministry equivalency counts on the British track, so they add load without adding to that total.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram enter my child for a Cambridge or Pearson examination?
faqs.answer: No. We are a tutoring service, not an examination centre, and we hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. Entries are made by your child's school or by an approved private-candidate centre, which also sets its own deadlines and fees. Treat any provider claiming to be an approved centre with care and ask to see the centre number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is what a Dubai training institute with premises needs, is a separate thing again and we do not hold one.

faqs.question: How fast can you start for a Year 11 student at a Motor City or JVT school?
faqs.answer: One to three working days for a mainstream specification in a UAE evening slot: Mathematics 0580, the three separate sciences, English 0500 and 0510, Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450 all have deep cover. Minority entries take longer and occasionally cannot be filled from UAE-resident tutors at all — an uncommon language, a Pearson code newly adopted by one school, a very small cohort subject. Where that is the case the tutor comes from our India-based faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and you are told before the booking rather than after it.

faqs.question: What happens to our slot during Ramadan and mock weeks?
faqs.answer: Both are arranged at the start of term so nothing is lost. During Ramadan sessions shift to post-Iftar timing, usually 20:30 to 22:00 on Gulf Standard Time and often shortened to 45 minutes. Through a school's internal examination or mock week, most Triangle families pause entirely so the student has their own evenings, then restart with a session spent reading the marked scripts, which is usually the most productive hour of the term. Every session is recorded, so a pause costs nothing: autumn work can be rewatched before the summer series at no extra charge.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-vi.closingHeading: Fix the decisions first, then book the hours
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-vi.closingBody: For most families in Jumeirah Village Triangle the money is better spent getting four decisions right than buying an extra term of lessons. How many subjects, measured against the five that Ministry equivalency counts and the grades a sixth form wants. Separate sciences or combined, measured against whether a Higher Level science is in the plan. Which English entry, and why. And if a grade has already come back short, whether a November result arriving in January is useful to the school that has to accept it. Send the subject list and a marked script, take the free diagnostic lesson, and make those calls on evidence.

intro.heading: Proximity has one job here, and a fixed hour does it better
paragraphs: When a Karama parent types IGCSE tutor near me, the underlying want is usually not geography. It is reliability and oversight: somebody who turns up, every week, in a slot that works, with a parent able to tell whether the hour was used. Proximity looks like the way to get that. In this part of Dubai it is actually the thing most likely to undermine it, because the variable that breaks a weekly arrangement is travel, and a nearby tutor still has to travel.

The reason reliability matters so much at IGCSE is that the term has a cadence rather than a single deadline. Homework comes back weekly. Class tests land every few weeks. End-of-unit assessments feed a reporting cycle. Reports go home two or three times a year. Somewhere in Year 11, predicted grades are produced and used for sixth-form and college applications. Each of those is a date, each one can be prepared for, and a tutoring arrangement that holds every week can be aimed at the next one. An arrangement that moves twice a month cannot be aimed at anything.

Karama makes this concrete. Students here generally attend schools in Bur Dubai, Al Mankhool or Oud Metha, sometimes across the creek, and get home between half past four and six depending on the road. The usable window is narrow. A travel-based arrangement inserts a second journey into it, so two commutes now have to succeed rather than one, and the five o'clock creek crossing is unpredictable in both directions. Across a twenty-week term that is not a theoretical risk; it is three or four lost sessions, and those are weeks that never come back.

There is also a calendar most families in this district have never been shown: the one running alongside Year 11 for the next stage. Predicted grades are produced by the school, used by sixth forms and colleges, and based on evidence the student generates before the series. A student whose class test and end-of-unit marks improve through the autumn of Year 11 is predicted differently from one whose marks improve in May, and the prediction is what applications are judged on. That makes the autumn term of Year 11 far more consequential than its position in the year suggests.

On delivery, plainly, because the search term invites the question: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video, in the same Gulf Standard Time slot each week, and we say so before anyone pays. We also hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE, so there is nowhere to visit. What we offer against a near-me search is the one thing proximity cannot guarantee: an hour that happens.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-karama.subjectsIntro: Where a weekly hour pays best, subject by subject, and what the cadence of that subject looks like through a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject with the most frequent class testing and therefore the fastest feedback loop, which makes it the best candidate for a standing weekly hour. Cambridge now sets a non-calculator paper worth half the grade; Pearson permits a calculator in both papers. The weekly hour should include hand arithmetic for Cambridge candidates.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Weekly homework tends to expose algebra rather than physics: a formula rearranged wrongly, a prefix not converted, an answer without a unit. A standing hour that starts each week with the returned homework catches these as they happen rather than at mock season, which is the whole argument for cadence.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Splits into a recall half - tests, colours, reactivity - and a calculation half built on relative formula mass and moles. The recall half suits short weekly quizzing; the calculation half needs a concentrated block. A weekly hour can carry the first and should make room for the second.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest content volume and marked on precision of language, which makes it ideal for a weekly cycle: ten minutes of mark-scheme wording each session, accumulated across a term, outperforms a revision block. Six-mark questions need six distinct points rather than one fluent paragraph.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing, descriptive and narrative tasks and reading response work. The weekly rhythm that works is one piece planned, written and marked against the criteria per fortnight. Students who write a great deal and plan nothing lose structure marks that twenty minutes of planning practice recovers.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Rewards close analysis of a writer's choices with quotation embedded rather than appended. The weekly hour is best spent on paragraph structure and quotation integration using the texts the class is currently studying, which keeps it aligned to the school's own assessments.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main mathematics by students heading for A Level or Diploma Higher Level mathematics, and introducing calculus. It is also the first subject to be sacrificed when a Year 11 week overflows, which is a decision worth making deliberately rather than by attrition.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, precise technical vocabulary and answers applied to the stimulus rather than recited. Evaluation questions need a judgement at the end rather than a balanced list. Both are structural habits that a weekly hour builds and a revision block rarely does.

subjects.name: History and Geography
subjects.description: Source or data-based components alongside extended writing. History rewards evaluating sources for origin, purpose, value and limitation; Geography rewards case-study specificity with named places and named figures. Case-study knowledge accumulates well across a term and badly in a fortnight.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Theory papers rewarding precise technical definition plus practical or pseudocode components. Students who code lose theory marks on terminology; students who know the theory lose practical marks on trace tables. The weekly hour should alternate between the two halves rather than favour one.

subjects.name: Arabic and additional languages
subjects.levels: Cambridge and Pearson first and foreign language options
subjects.description: Separate from the mandatory Arabic a Dubai school runs, and examined across reading, writing, listening and speaking. The speaking component responds far better to short frequent rehearsal than to long sessions, which makes it one of the strongest cases for a weekly cadence.

subjects.name: Exam technique across subjects
subjects.description: Command words, mark allocation, question triage, showing working and attempting rather than abandoning a question. Ten minutes at the end of every weekly session, applied to whatever came back from school that week, builds these habits across nine subjects without buying nine hours.

sections.heading: The weekly cadence of an IGCSE term, and what each part tells you
paragraphs: An IGCSE term is a sequence of small signals, and families generally read only the last one. Homework comes back with a mark. Class tests happen every few weeks. End-of-unit assessments are set, often using past-paper questions. Those feed a report, and in Year 11 they feed a predicted grade. By the time a report arrives, three or four more informative documents have already come and gone.

Marked homework is the most frequent and most under-used of them. It is low-stakes, it is returned quickly, and it shows the error pattern while the topic is still fresh. A weekly hour that begins by opening the returned homework catches a misconception in the week it formed rather than in March, and that is the single strongest argument for cadence over intensity. A revision block in the spring is archaeology; a weekly hour is maintenance.

Class tests are the next signal up, and the useful question about them is whether they were marked to a real scheme or to a classroom one. A generously marked class test conceals exactly what the exercise exists to reveal. Asking the teacher is reasonable, and so is asking whether the test used past-paper questions, because if it did then the losses on it predict the losses in the series.

End-of-unit assessments are where the term's evidence consolidates, and they are the marks a report is built from. This is why the timing of any tutoring purchase should be read against the reporting calendar rather than against convenience: an hour started six weeks before a report has end-of-unit evidence to show for itself, and an hour started a fortnight before does not. Ask the school for the reporting dates at the start of the year, and ask whether the marks behind the grade can be shared rather than just the grade.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, and why the autumn of Year 11 is the term that counts
paragraphs: Here is the part of the IGCSE calendar that Karama families are least often shown, and it reorders the year once you see it. Sixth forms, colleges and Diploma programmes make offers before examination results exist. What they judge is a predicted grade, produced by the school from internal evidence - class tests, end-of-unit assessments, mocks - and issued at a point the school decides.

The consequence is arithmetical. Evidence generated in the autumn and early spring of Year 11 feeds the prediction. Evidence generated in April and May does not, because the prediction has already been issued and the application already judged. A student whose marks climb through the autumn is predicted differently from one whose marks climb in May, even if both finish at the same standard. For a family choosing when to buy tutoring, that makes the autumn term of Year 11 worth considerably more than its position in the year implies.

There are three questions to put to the school, and all of them are reasonable. When are predicted grades generated? What evidence feeds them - which assessments, over what period? And is there any route by which a prediction can be revised if later evidence is stronger? The third answer varies by school and is the one families most want and least often ask for. Having those three answers at the start of Year 11 rather than after the prediction arrives is the difference between planning and reacting.

A note of honesty about what tutoring can do here. It can improve the evidence that feeds a prediction, if it starts early enough and is aimed at the assessments that count. It cannot change a prediction that has been issued, it cannot persuade a school to revise one, and it certainly cannot guarantee any grade, predicted or actual. Anyone implying otherwise is selling something that does not exist. What we will do is tell you where in the cycle you are and what that realistically allows.

sections.heading: Building a nine-subject week that a Karama student can actually hold
paragraphs: A Year 11 student carrying nine or ten subjects cannot revise them all every week and should not try. The weekly plan that works is built from the school's own cadence rather than from an even division of hours, and it starts by accepting that most subjects get nothing in most weeks.

The method is simple and unpopular because it feels neglectful. Each week, identify the two subjects with an assessment in the next three weeks, and give them the bulk of the available time. Give one short slot to the subject with the largest accumulating content volume - usually biology or a humanity - because case-study and terminology knowledge builds well in small frequent doses and badly in blocks. Give ten minutes to exam technique applied to whatever came back from school. Everything else gets nothing that week, deliberately, and gets its turn when its assessment approaches.

In a Karama flat the physical constraints matter as much as the plan. There is typically one quiet surface and often several children needing it, plus a shared device. Staggering study and session times across siblings does more good than optimising any individual timetable, and it has to be agreed as a household rather than imposed on one child. An online session that can run in a bedroom with headphones leaves the shared table free for somebody else, which is a small thing that compounds across twenty weeks.

Two further calendar features need building in rather than discovering. Dubai school weeks carry mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and a minimum advised lesson length of 25 minutes - real hours in an already full week. And Ramadan, in some years, falls inside the Year 11 term, shortening school days and changing routines. Agreeing in advance that the weekly slot shifts for that period, often to a later post-Iftar time, is what keeps the cadence intact instead of losing three weeks to rescheduling.

sections.heading: Past papers on a fortnightly rhythm, marked properly
paragraphs: The most under-rated arrangement in IGCSE tutoring is not a weekly teaching hour. It is a fortnightly past paper, attempted under timed conditions at home and then marked together in a session against the official scheme. For a student who understands the content and loses marks to technique, which is a large share of them, this does more per dirham than content teaching.

The mechanics matter. The paper must be from the correct syllabus code - Cambridge 0580 and 0607 are different examinations, as are Pearson 4MA1 and 4MB1, and working the wrong one is a common and wasteful error. It must be timed, because a paper attempted leisurely measures knowledge rather than performance. And it must be marked against the real scheme rather than generously, because generous marking conceals exactly the losses the exercise exists to find.

What a fortnightly rhythm teaches, beyond the marks, is the mark scheme's language. After four or five papers a student starts to anticipate what a six-mark question wants, to notice when a command word has changed, and to show working automatically because they have seen method marks awarded and withheld. That is a habit rather than a piece of knowledge, and habits form on repetition over weeks rather than on explanation in a single session.

On the supply of papers: we do not host or redistribute Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or syllabus documents, because reproducing them is the boards' copyright rather than ours to share. We reference them and cite the official source. In practice your child's subject teacher can usually provide past papers directly, and that is both the correct route and the easiest one. Any tutoring site offering a download library of official papers is taking a risk a family has no reason to join.

sections.heading: When near me is actually the right answer
paragraphs: It would be dishonest to write nine sections against proximity and not state where it wins, so here it is. There are circumstances in which a nearby tutor is genuinely the better arrangement, and a family in Karama should know which ones apply to them before reading the rest of this page as settled.

The clearest is age. For a younger child - primary, or the early years of secondary - physical presence holds attention in a way a screen does not, and the support required is less specialised, so the local pool is adequate. Our view is that the near-me instinct is defensible there and becomes progressively less so as a student moves towards examinations and towards subject-specific technique.

The second is connectivity and equipment. An online lesson needs a stable connection, a device that is not simultaneously being used for something else, and headphones. In a household where those cannot be guaranteed on a given evening, a tutor in the room removes a failure mode rather than adding one. That is a real consideration and we would rather name it than pretend every flat is equally equipped.

The third is supervision of a student who will not work unless somebody is physically present. That is a behavioural situation rather than an academic one, and online lessons are less effective at it. What we would say is that this is worth testing rather than assuming, because many students who are described this way engage perfectly well in a one-to-one video session where there is nowhere to hide - a shared screen is a more exposing environment than a table with a tutor looking at a book from the wrong angle. The free trial exists partly to find out.

sections.heading: What a weekly IGCSE hour costs in this market, counted by the term
paragraphs: Because the argument of this page is cadence, the honest way to present cost is per term rather than per hour. A twenty-week term at one session a week is twenty sessions, and that is the commitment a family is actually weighing when it chooses a weekly arrangement over an occasional one.

The market figures, each attributed and read in October 2026. At the budget end Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which buys homework supervision rather than examination coaching - though for a student whose only problem is that homework does not get done, supervision is sometimes exactly the purchase. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IGCSE, IB and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270; BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Two things follow for a weekly plan. First, the fortnightly past-paper rhythm costs roughly half a weekly arrangement and for a conversion problem frequently does more, so it should be considered before the weekly hour rather than after it. Second, in-home pricing is structurally worse for a weekly cadence than for an occasional session, because the travel premium is paid every single week. The monthly packages make this plain: AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions - the same eight hours for roughly double, repeated monthly.

None of these are IB Gram prices; we publish no rate card on a landing page and would rather quote against a real requirement. We hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE. sections.heading: A weekly session in a Karama flat against a fixed online hour
paragraphs: Set the two arrangements side by side over a twenty-week term rather than over a single lesson, because that is where the difference shows. One session is much the same either way. Twenty are not.

Our position first, stated before anyone pays: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video in a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. We say so on the page because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits, and a family should not learn that at the end of a billing month.

Over twenty weeks the reliability difference compounds. An in-home arrangement requires the tutor's journey to succeed every week, on the same roads and the same creek crossing that already make the student's own return unpredictable. Three or four lost sessions across a term is a realistic expectation rather than a pessimistic one, and in a cadence-based plan a lost week is a missed assessment preparation rather than merely a missed hour. The fixed online slot has no commute to fail, and a student who gets home late joins late rather than losing the lesson.

The other twenty-week effects are smaller and real. A tutor physically present occupies the one quiet table for the whole visit, twenty times, in a flat where siblings also need it. The travel premium is paid twenty times. The pool of available teachers is narrowed to whoever can reach a Karama address at the one hour that works, twenty weeks running - and if that person's availability changes mid-term, the arrangement ends. An online slot can be rematched within the same week.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and the mandatory subjects in the week
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. In 2024-25 the sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students and Indian at 26 per cent - which is why IGCSE provision and IGCSE tutoring supply are both deeper in this district than IB provision is. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

The mandatory subjects affect the weekly plan directly. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, since curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and requires teachers of those subjects to hold the appropriate KHDA approval.

On permits, the position is checkable by any parent and worth checking whoever you hire. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published officially, nobody should quote you an amount.

One rule bears on a near-me search specifically, because the nearest qualified person is often a teacher at the school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct likewise bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The most convenient local arrangement is therefore the one to decline. And for completeness: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, and no premises anywhere in the UAE.

sections.heading: Equivalency and the next stage, so a weekly plan points somewhere
paragraphs: A weekly hour is easier to sustain when everyone knows what it is for, and in Year 10 and 11 the destination is usually sixth form, A Levels or the Diploma, with Ministry of Education equivalency sitting behind it for families who intend to stay in the UAE.

On equivalency, the sourced position for the British track is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five. For the American track the published requirements are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT Math. Verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel.

Subject-specific entry requirements for the next stage matter at least as much, and they are the reason a weekly plan should not treat all nine subjects as equal. A science A Level or a Higher Level Diploma science generally assumes a particular IGCSE science route and grade. Mathematics at a higher level assumes a higher tier and often a specific grade. Those requirements are published by the receiving school or college, and reading them in Year 10 rather than Year 11 is what makes a tier decision and an option choice make sense.

Two things we will not do here. We do not present equivalency or attestation as something IB Gram performs or guarantees - it is a Ministry process, we describe it and point to the official channel, and tutoring is not a requirement of it. And we do not imply that tutoring is needed for university admission, school progression or equivalency. It is not, and suggesting otherwise would be a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process rather than an honest description of a service.

faqs.question: What does a nearby IGCSE tutor have to beat?
faqs.answer: A weekly hour that never moves. The thing a near-me search is really after is reliability and oversight, and in Old Dubai the variable that breaks a weekly arrangement is travel - which a nearby tutor still has to do. A Karama student already commutes from a school in Bur Dubai, Oud Metha or across the creek; adding the tutor's journey means two commutes have to succeed every week. Across a twenty-week term that reliably produces three or four lost sessions, and in a cadence-based plan a lost week is a missed assessment preparation.

faqs.question: What are predicted grades and why do they matter so much?
faqs.answer: They are grades the school produces from internal evidence - class tests, end-of-unit assessments, mocks - and they are what sixth forms, colleges and Diploma programmes judge applications on, because offers are made before examination results exist. The consequence is that evidence generated in the autumn and early spring of Year 11 feeds the prediction and evidence generated in May does not. Ask the school when predictions are issued, what feeds them, and whether there is any route to revision.

faqs.question: Which term of Year 11 is most worth buying tutoring in?
faqs.answer: The autumn, which surprises most families because it feels early. That is the term producing the internal evidence predicted grades are built from, and applications to the next stage are judged on those predictions rather than on examination results. A student whose marks climb in the autumn is predicted differently from one whose marks climb in May, even where both finish at the same standard. The spring term still matters for the examination itself, but the prediction is already closed by then.

faqs.question: Why is marked homework more useful than a school report?
faqs.answer: Because it arrives while the topic is still fresh and it shows the error pattern rather than a consolidated judgement. A report is weeks of evidence compressed into a grade and delivered long after the misconceptions formed. Marked homework is low-stakes, returned quickly, and specific. A weekly session that opens by looking at the returned homework catches a misconception in the week it formed, which is the core argument for a steady cadence over an intensive block in the spring.

faqs.question: How do we plan a revision week across nine or ten subjects?
faqs.answer: By accepting that most subjects get nothing in most weeks. Each week, give the bulk of the time to the two subjects with an assessment inside three weeks, taken from the school's assessment calendar. Give one short slot to the subject with the largest accumulating content volume, usually biology or a humanity, because that knowledge builds in small frequent doses. Give ten minutes to exam technique on whatever came back from school. Everything else waits its turn, deliberately.

faqs.question: Is a fortnightly past paper better value than a weekly lesson?
faqs.answer: For a conversion problem, often yes. If a student understands the content and loses marks to technique - wrong command word, too few creditable points, no working shown, premature rounding - then a full timed paper every fortnight, marked together against the official scheme, costs roughly half a weekly arrangement and teaches the mark scheme's language through repetition. The paper has to match the exact syllabus code and the marking has to be honest rather than generous, or the exercise conceals what it exists to reveal.

faqs.question: When is a local in-home tutor genuinely the better choice?
faqs.answer: Three situations. For a younger child, because physical presence holds attention differently and the support needed is less specialised, so the local pool is adequate. For a household that cannot reliably provide a device, a connection and headphones on a given evening, since in-home removes a failure mode rather than adding one. And for a student who genuinely will not work without somebody present - though that is worth testing first, because a one-to-one video session is often more exposing than a tutor reading a book from across a table.

faqs.question: Is there any way to get a tutor physically in the room through IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video in a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, and we say so before you pay. We also hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE, so there is nowhere to visit either. Two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where their tutors actually sit.

faqs.question: How much does a weekly IGCSE hour cost over a term in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Count it as twenty sessions rather than as an hourly rate. Market figures read in October 2026: Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour, Bestimate's Dubai table places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and the budget end runs AED 33 to 65 with Tutopiya and EdFlik. Bestimate estimates a weekly hour at AED 600 to 1,200 monthly mid-market. In-home pricing is structurally worse for a weekly cadence, because the travel premium is paid every week rather than once.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school at the start of the year?
faqs.answer: Four things. The assessment calendar, so a tutoring hour can be aimed at the next test rather than at a generic plan. The reporting dates, which are the honest measurement points. In Year 11, when predicted grades are issued and what evidence feeds them. And whether the marks behind a report grade can be shared rather than just the grade, because the marks are what make a report usable as a diagnostic. All four cost one email.

faqs.question: How should a weekly tutoring slot handle Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Agree in advance that it moves, rather than renegotiating week by week. School days shorten and household routines change, so a fixed 5pm slot that worked in January often will not hold, and families who try to keep it typically lose two or three weeks of cadence to repeated rescheduling. A later post-Iftar slot, settled before the period begins, keeps the hours intact. Dubai school weeks also carry mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies throughout, on a 40-minute lesson unit.

faqs.question: Our flat has one quiet table and three children. Does that affect the choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more than families expect over a full term. A tutor physically present occupies the one quiet surface for the whole visit, twenty times across a term, in a household where siblings also need it. An online session runs in a bedroom with headphones and leaves the table free. Staggering study and session times across the household does more good than optimising any single child's timetable, and it works better agreed as a household in week one than improvised in week five.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supply the past papers for the fortnightly rhythm?
faqs.answer: We do not host or redistribute them. Cambridge and Pearson past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and syllabus documents are the boards' copyright, so we reference them, cite the official source and link out. In practice your child's subject teacher can usually supply past papers directly and will often have the mark schemes too, which is both the correct route and the easiest. A tutoring site offering a download library of official papers is taking a risk a family has no reason to share.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to know which school my child attends?
faqs.answer: The syllabus code and the tier matter more than the school name, and those are what we ask for first. The school's own calendar matters too - assessment dates, reporting dates, predicted-grade timing - because a weekly hour is aimed at those. What a tutor does not need, and should decline, is to be your child's own school teacher: ADEK's ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled students, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct does likewise.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does a UAE family need for equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case through the Ministry's own channel - we describe the process and neither perform nor guarantee it.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working weekly with a Karama student need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the question is worth asking whoever you hire. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and states a two-working-day completion time. Since it costs nothing, there is no reason for a tutor not to hold one.

intro.heading: Where you are in the IGCSE year decides what tutoring can do
paragraphs: Dubai Knowledge Park is an education free zone off Al Sufouh Road, not a residential community. University campuses, training institutes and corporate learning centres sit there; the families who search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Knowledge Park are almost always living a few minutes away in Al Sufouh, Barsha Heights, Dubai Media City, The Greens or the Marina towers, or working inside the free zone itself. That matters for one practical reason: the search is about proximity, and proximity is the one thing that turns out not to govern the answer.

What does govern the answer is the date. An IGCSE course is two years long on paper and about fourteen usable teaching months in practice, and the value of a tutor changes completely depending on which of those months you are in. In October of Year 10, tutoring is about building the habit of writing answers in the command-term language the mark scheme uses. In February of Year 11, it is about converting known content into marks under timed conditions. Six weeks out from the first paper, it is triage: find the two topics that are costing the most marks across the whole paper and fix those, and leave the rest.

Most parents arrive at this search after a specific event. A mock grade came back two bands below the predicted grade. A science practical write-up was returned with a comment about variables. The school's reporting portal showed a drop in one subject while the others held. Those events are diagnostic, and they are far more useful than the general feeling that a child is struggling, because each points at a different fix. A mock grade that collapsed on Paper 2 but held on Paper 1 is a timing and extended-writing problem, not a knowledge problem, and it needs a different eight weeks.

The two boards your child's school may be entered with have different calendars, and parents routinely assume the wrong one. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and its February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate sitting Cambridge papers sits June or November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and again in November. Those are the windows the whole plan has to be counted back from, and your school's exams officer holds the exact entry cut-off, which falls months before the first paper rather than weeks.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition to Knowledge Park and the communities around it. We do not offer home visits in Dubai; sending a tutor to a UAE address is a service we run only in India. The trade that buys you is specific rather than vague: a student taking Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Edexcel Further Pure 4PM1 gets a tutor who has taught that exact paper, instead of whichever generalist is willing to drive to Al Sufouh at 4.30pm on a Tuesday for a travel premium.

Everything below is organised the way the year is organised. The sessions table counts backwards from the June series. The eight-week table says what a block of focused work can and cannot achieve. The board comparison exists because the two calendars diverge, and acting on the wrong one is the most expensive mistake available to a Year 11 family.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-knowledge-p.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Knowledge Park and Al Sufouh families ask about most often, with the component that usually decides the grade named rather than a general description of difficulty.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers, no coursework. Extended tier is the one almost every A Level or Diploma pathway expects. Marks drain away in algebraic manipulation, in transformations of graphs, and in the long multi-step questions at the back of Paper 4 where method marks are available but never claimed because nothing was written down.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606) and Further Pure (Edexcel 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths syllabus by students aiming at Higher Level or A Level maths. Calculus, trigonometric identities and series arrive a year earlier than they otherwise would. It is the subject most often under-taught in a timetable because it is squeezed into an option block.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism is where Extended candidates lose most, followed by anything requiring a graph gradient to be interpreted rather than calculated. The practical or alternative-to-practical component rewards students who can write a method precisely, which is a writing skill rather than a physics one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables are the two reliable mark losers. Organic chemistry is usually taught last and revised least. Students who can balance equations but cannot convert between moles, mass and concentration lose marks across every paper rather than in one topic.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem rather than the difficulty of any single idea. Extended-response questions on transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance need the specification's own vocabulary; a correct answer in everyday words frequently scores nothing because the mark scheme lists the term.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: The route many Al Barsha and Al Sufouh students take when the timetable cannot fit three separate sciences. It covers all three disciplines at reduced depth, and it narrows post-16 options in ways families often discover only in the Year 11 A Level or Diploma conversation.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 and 0990 / Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading-comprehension summary carry most of the volatile marks. Students who read widely still lose marks for failing to shape a response to the audience and purpose the question actually states, which is a mark-scheme habit rather than a comprehension problem.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Common among the international families living around Media City and Barsha Heights. The listening component and the exercise requiring notes to be made from a spoken text are the ones that need practice under timed conditions rather than vocabulary work.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455) and Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward students who answer the command term rather than the topic. An 'evaluate' question answered as a description scores in the lower band regardless of how accurate the description is, and that single habit is usually worth more than any additional content.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478) and ICT (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables in Computer Science need deliberate practice; the practical ICT components need method fluency against a specific software version. Both are popular near the Knowledge Park free zone, where a number of parents work in technology roles.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires schools to run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Support here has to match which of the two pathways the school has placed the student in.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460) and History (Cambridge 0470)
subjects.description: Both are source-skill subjects wearing content-subject clothing. Geography's paper on data response and the case-study requirement, and History's source evaluation, are learnable techniques that most students are never explicitly taught. Case-study specificity is what separates a grade 6 from a grade 8.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The district Knowledge Park sits inside, running from Al Sufouh Road to the beach. Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International are here, so a meaningful share of this search comes from families whose school is a five-minute drive away and whose IGCSE subject still has no local specialist.

regions.name: Dubai Media City and Barsha Heights
regions.note: High-rise, heavily expatriate, and the closest residential density to the free zone. Parents working in Media City often finish after 6pm, which makes a 7pm or 8pm online session the only one that happens reliably every week rather than being rescheduled.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise apartments on the Sheikh Zayed Road side, feeding Regent International School and several British-curriculum schools in Al Barsha. Short school runs, but Al Khail Road congestion between 3pm and 5pm makes a fixed in-person slot fragile in a way a video call is not.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Dense tower living with the longest internal travel times in the cluster; parking and lift waits add fifteen minutes at each end of any visit. Families here commonly run two children on back-to-back online sessions in the same evening, which is impossible with a visiting tutor.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road from the Marina and a separate free zone. Mixed curricula, with a large IGCSE cohort attending schools in Al Barsha and Al Quoz. Crossing the interchange at 4pm is the single biggest argument against an in-person slot here.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: The school belt for this whole catchment: Dubai American Academy, Repton Al Barsha and several large British-curriculum schools sit here. Students finish between 2.30pm and 3.30pm, which makes a 4.30pm start realistic once travel is taken out of the equation.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, The Springs, The Meadows and The Lakes
regions.note: Villa communities inland of Al Khail Road, feeding Dubai British School and Emirates International School Meadows. Long internal roads mean a visiting tutor's travel time is spent inside the community itself, and it is billed.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah and Dubai Harbour
regions.note: Reached from Knowledge Park in minutes without traffic and in considerably longer with it. The single access route is why evening appointments here are the first to be cancelled, and why families on the Palm are among the readiest to move a weekly session online.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Media City and The Greens
schoolClusters.note: The schools immediately around Knowledge Park, most running IGCSE in Years 10 and 11 before splitting into A Level or the IB Diploma. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; check each school's current curriculum and inspection report on KHDA's own site, because post-16 offers change between intakes.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Quoz and the inland villa communities
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, a short drive inland, carrying much of the IGCSE cohort for families living in The Greens, The Springs and The Meadows. Several of these schools run both IGCSE and a post-16 Diploma pathway, which is why Year 11 subject choices here are made with two destinations in view.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the year
modes.description: One or two sessions a week in a fixed slot, starting in Year 10 or early Year 11 and running through to the series. The tutor works to the student's own school scheme of work and internal deadlines, which means the session reinforces what was taught that week rather than running a parallel course the student has to reconcile alone.

modes.title: An eight-week focused block
modes.description: A defined run with a named target: recover a mock grade, fix one paper, or close a specific topic set before the next assessment. The block opens with a timed paper used diagnostically and ends with another, so the comparison is evidence rather than impression. Parents who want a measurable answer before committing to a year usually start here.

modes.title: Pre-series intensive
modes.description: Short, frequent sessions in the weeks immediately before the June or November papers, built almost entirely from past papers under timed conditions. This is triage rather than teaching: identify the two highest-yield gaps across the whole paper and work on those. It is the most expensive way to buy improvement and the one most families end up needing.
