sections.heading: What this search means in week six of a term
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Knowledge Park is asking two questions at once, and only one of them is about geography. The first is whether anybody within reach knows the specific syllabus their child sits. The second, unspoken, is whether it is already too late in the year to change the outcome. The honest answer to the second is that it depends on which month it is and which paper is failing, and that is a much more useful conversation than a list of tutor credentials.

Take the two most common October scenarios in this catchment. A Year 10 student who has just started Cambridge Extended Mathematics 0580 and is finding algebraic fractions impossible has twenty months and a genuine chance to end up with a grade 8; the work is foundational and the time is there. A Year 11 student in the same month, entered for the June series, with a mock Paper 4 at grade 4, has roughly twenty-four usable teaching weeks before the papers, minus mocks, minus the school's own revision programme, minus a fortnight of winter break. Those two students need different tutors, different session lengths and different promises.

The reason the free zone itself does not change this is simple. Knowledge Park holds university campuses and training institutes rather than homes, so nobody is looking for a tutor who lives there. They are looking for someone close to Al Sufouh, Media City or the Marina, on the reasonable assumption that distance governs availability. Once lessons run over video, distance stops governing anything, and the only question left is whether the tutor has taught the exact paper. That is the trade this page is making, and it is worth being explicit that it is a trade rather than a free upgrade: a video call is not a room, and a student who will not engage on a screen is a real limitation rather than a marketing objection.
bullets: Year 10 in October: time is the asset, so build foundations rather than drill papers
Year 11 in October: about twenty-four usable weeks remain, so triage by paper
Year 11 in March: one paper, two topics, timed practice only

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a session calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what parents actually need. The table below counts backwards from the June series, the one UAE Cambridge candidates sit alongside November. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate planning around a February exam has been given the wrong country's calendar.

Two details in the table repay attention. The first is that the entry deadline sits months ahead of the first paper. By the time a parent feels the urgency in February, the subject list, the tier and the board have been fixed since the autumn, and changing any of them is a conversation with the school's exams officer rather than a form. The second is that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the school which zone it sits in rather than downloading whichever timetable a search returns.

Dates in the table that look backwards keep their year, because that is what makes them checkable. Dates that look forward are named by month only, because a page that says 'the June series' is still correct next year while a page that names a year is quietly wrong twelve months later. Always open the board's live timetable rather than trusting a restated date, including this one: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, planned honestly: what a focused block can and cannot do
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block length parents most often ask for, usually because it maps onto the gap between a mock and the next report. It is enough time to do something real and not enough time to do everything, and the difference between a block that works and one that does not is almost always whether a target was named at the start.

The structure below assumes two sessions a week on one subject, a timed paper at each end, and a student who does the set work between sessions. Remove any of those three and the outcome shifts. The last column is deliberately about evidence rather than feeling, because 'he seems more confident' is not something a mark scheme recognises, and a parent paying by the hour deserves a harder measure than that.

What eight weeks cannot do is replace two years of unbuilt foundations. A Year 11 student entered for Extended Mathematics who cannot reliably manipulate algebraic fractions is not going to reach a grade 8 in a block, and saying so at the start is more useful than discovering it in week seven. What eight weeks does do well is convert content a student already half-knows into marks, which is where most of the recoverable grade sits.

One more thing about the eight-week shape: it works far better on one subject than on three. Parents in this catchment often ask for maths, physics and chemistry support simultaneously after a disappointing report, and the arithmetic of that is six hours a week of tuition on top of a full school timetable, homework and whatever coursework is live. Students stop doing the between-session work first, and at that point every subject moves slowly instead of one subject moving properly. If three subjects genuinely need attention, sequence them: take the one where the marks are cheapest to recover, finish the block, then move on. The report at the end of the first block also tells you whether the second one is worth buying.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: find out which calendar your child is on
paragraphs: Parents in this catchment frequently do not know which board their child is entered with, and the schools around Al Sufouh and Al Barsha use both. It is a five-minute question to the school office and it changes the syllabus codes, the tiering, the practical arrangements and the results timing. Buying a revision guide for the wrong board is a common and avoidable waste.

The practical differences are not about difficulty. They are about structure, and structure is what a tutor plans around. Cambridge's Core and Extended tiers cap the attainable grade at the point of entry. Pearson's International GCSE is single-tier in most subjects and modular in some, which changes when marks can be banked. Science practical assessment differs, and for a family considering any period of online schooling or private candidacy, that difference is decisive rather than incidental.

One more reason to get this right: Cambridge Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, which is a separate calendar from the IGCSE series and is often the source of the confusion when a parent has a younger child as well. The checkpoint calendar has nothing to do with when a Year 11 sits papers.

A mixed entry is also more common in this catchment than parents expect. A student can sit Cambridge papers in some subjects and Pearson papers in others at the same school, because departments choose independently and because a student who transferred mid-course sometimes keeps the board they started on. So the question to the school office is not 'which board are we' but 'which code is each subject entered under'. Write the list down and keep it; it is the single document that makes every later decision about revision material, tiering and resits straightforward instead of guesswork.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs around Al Sufouh, read as a monthly number
paragraphs: Most rate discussions start with an hourly figure, which is the least useful way for a family to think about it. A household budgets monthly, so start there. One hour a week for a month is four or five sessions depending on where the weeks fall, and on the market rates published in this city that lands between roughly AED 600 and AED 1,200 a month for a qualified subject tutor working online. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table puts monthly spend for weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Translated to the hour, those bands come from identifiable sources. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, which is the university-student end of the market. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist IB and IGCSE work, and Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED sits at the top at around AED 650 for examiner-led sessions. Monthly packages advertised in this market include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

That last pair of figures is the one worth sitting with. The in-home package is roughly double the online one for half the number of sessions, and the difference is travel. A tutor crossing Al Sufouh Road at 4.30pm is paid for the crossing, and is not teaching while doing it. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page because quoting a price without knowing the subject, the level and the frequency would be a number rather than information; the trial lesson and the consultation are free, and the figures above are the market's rather than ours.

sections.heading: Why proximity stops mattering once the subject gets narrow
paragraphs: The case for a local tutor is strongest for a broad need and weakest for a narrow one. If a Year 7 needs general maths support, the pool of competent people within fifteen minutes of Al Sufouh is large, and a familiar face in the room has real value. If a Year 11 needs Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, or Edexcel Further Pure 4PM1, or the qualitative analysis section of Chemistry 0620 specifically, that pool collapses to a handful of people in the whole emirate, and the chance that one of them is both free at 5pm on Tuesday and willing to drive to Barsha Heights is small.

This is the honest argument for online delivery, and it is an argument about matching rather than about technology. Running lessons over live video widens the pool from one neighbourhood to every tutor who teaches that syllabus, which is why a narrow subject is where the gain is largest. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - that is a service we run only in India - so this is the model rather than an upsell, and it should be judged on whether the match is better.

There are real costs. Screen-sharing a diagram is slower than pointing at a page. A thirteen-year-old who is going to drift will drift faster on a video call than in a room. Science practical technique can be taught and discussed but not performed together. Against that: the session is recorded work on a shared whiteboard the student can return to, two children can be tutored in the same evening without a second journey, and the 4pm Al Khail Road traffic that cancels in-person appointments has no effect at all. The comparison below is the one a parent in this catchment is actually making.

sections.heading: Academic honesty with a deadline approaching
paragraphs: Pressure near a deadline is exactly when the line between help and malpractice gets tested, and it is worth stating plainly where that line sits before anyone is tempted. A tutor may teach content, explain a mark scheme, model a method on a different question, ask the questions that make a student notice a flaw in their own argument, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not produce the work.

That distinction is not a matter of taste. For IGCSE coursework and practical components, and for every IB internal assessment, the authentication a teacher signs is a statement that the work is the candidate's own. Work that is not loses the candidate the marks and can trigger a malpractice finding against them personally. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price. Buying that is a risk transferred entirely onto the student, who is the only person who can be sanctioned for it.

The same applies to materials. We reference IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes, we cite where to find them, and we link out to the boards. We do not reproduce or supply them as downloads, because they are the boards' copyright and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure in themselves. A tutor who offers you a folder of mark schemes is telling you something about how they work.

There is a second honesty question specific to this catchment, and it concerns who is teaching. Abu Dhabi's ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Those are press-reported positions rather than wording we can quote verbatim, so verify them against the current policy document. The principle, though, is one parents should hold to anywhere in the UAE: paying your child's own classroom teacher privately is the arrangement most likely to put that teacher in breach, and it is never worth the convenience.
bullets: A tutor teaches, models on a different question, and gives feedback on the student's own draft

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the timetable squeeze
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai's private sector ran 227 schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum schools the largest group by enrolment at 37 per cent, Indian at 26 and US at 14. For an IGCSE family, the practical consequence of KHDA oversight is the inspection report, which is public and which names subject-level strengths rather than only an overall band.

The part that affects a Year 10 or Year 11 timetable most directly is the mandatory UAE subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA sets instructional time against a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes.

Those lessons occupy real timetable space, which is one reason an IGCSE option block can feel tight and why a subject like Additional Mathematics sometimes gets fewer contact hours than it needs. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited. Schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and the use of different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. That last rule constrains what any tutor can legitimately offer in those subjects.
bullets: KHDA oversees private education in Dubai; ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and SPEA covers Sharjah
Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required alongside any licensed international curriculum
Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with at least twenty-five minutes advised per mandatory lesson

process.title: Send the mock paper, not a description
process.description: The most useful thing a parent can send is the marked script and the school's paper-level breakdown. A grade tells us very little; a script tells us whether marks were lost to content, to timing, or to not answering the command term. That distinction decides what the first eight weeks look like.

process.title: Confirm the board, the tier and the series
process.description: Ask the school office for the syllabus codes, whether maths and the sciences are entered at Core or Extended, and which series the student is sitting. Five minutes here prevents a term of work against the wrong past papers, and tells us which calendar the plan counts back from.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a real topic
process.description: Not an interview. The tutor teaches something the student is currently stuck on, and you see how that goes. A trial on live content tells you more about the match than any credential list, and if it does not work there is nothing to cancel.

process.title: Agree the target and the review point
process.description: One named target for the block, with a timed paper at the start and another at the end. We say at this stage if the target is not reachable in the time available, because finding that out in week seven is worse for everyone than hearing it in week one.

process.title: Fix the slot to the school day, not the parent's day
process.description: Schools in this catchment finish between 2.30pm and 3.30pm. A 4.30pm start works for a student who comes straight home; a 7pm or 8pm slot works for families where a parent in Media City finishes late. The slot that survives the whole term is the one that fits the student.

process.title: Escalate honestly if the match is wrong
process.description: If two or three sessions in it is clear the pairing is not working, say so and we change the tutor rather than persisting. A mismatch discovered in February on an exam-year plan costs weeks that cannot be recovered, so the early conversation is the cheap one.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from the series the student is entered for and counts backwards through the entry deadline, the mocks and the coursework dates. That is the opposite of a generic scheme of work, and it is the thing no competitor page in this market publishes at all.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, not to 'maths'. Past papers, mark schemes and tiering differ between them, and a term spent on the wrong board's material is a term spent well and wasted.

whyPoints.title: The pool is national, not local
whyPoints.description: Delivering over live video means the match is made from everyone who teaches that syllabus rather than everyone who can reach Al Sufouh by 5pm. For a narrow subject that is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available.

whyPoints.title: Evidence rather than impression
whyPoints.description: Blocks open and close with a timed paper marked against the official mark scheme, compared at topic level. Confidence matters, but a parent paying by the hour is entitled to a measure that a mark scheme would recognise.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits, stated early
whyPoints.description: We say what eight weeks cannot do, we say when a tier decision has already capped a grade, and we say when no specialist is free for a niche subject. A disclosed limit is worth more than an optimistic promise that unravels in April.

whyPoints.title: Honest about academic integrity
whyPoints.description: Coursework and internal assessment support is teaching, feedback and process coaching on the student's own work. We do not produce assessed work, and we do not supply boards' papers or mark schemes as downloads.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near Dubai Knowledge Park who actually knows my child's syllabus code?
faqs.answer: For a broad need, yes - the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha area has plenty of competent general tutors. For a narrow one, the pool shrinks fast. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Edexcel Further Pure 4PM1 is taught by a small number of people in the whole emirate, and the chance one of them is free at your preferred time and willing to drive to Barsha Heights is slim. Online one-to-one lessons widen the match to everyone who teaches that code, which is why we deliver this way rather than by home visit.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit in Dubai, and is the February series an option?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International offers its February/March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. If any revision plan you have been given counts down to a February exam, it is built on the wrong country's calendar. Ask your school's exams officer which series the student is entered for and which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, because the timetable differs by zone.

faqs.question: My son's Year 11 mock came back at a grade 4. Is October too late to aim for a 7?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the marks were lost rather than on the grade itself. From October to the June series there are roughly twenty-four usable teaching weeks once mocks, winter break and the school's own revision programme are taken out. If the mock shows content gaps across every topic, a three-grade jump is unlikely and we will say so. If it shows most topics half-known and marks lost to timing and command terms, that is the recoverable kind of grade 4, and an eight-week block followed by exam-paper work has a real chance.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay each month for one weekly IGCSE session in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Budget monthly rather than hourly. Published market figures for Dubai put weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours. Our trial lesson and consultation are free, and a quote depends on subject, level and frequency.

faqs.question: Does an eight-week block actually change anything, or is it just a way of selling a package?
faqs.answer: It changes something if a target is named and measured. We open with a full paper sat cold and marked against the official mark scheme, broken down by topic. Weeks two to four teach the two highest-cost topics properly. Weeks five to six drill them inside exam questions. Week seven works on timing across the whole paper, and week eight repeats the timed paper for comparison. You end with two marked scripts side by side. Without that opening paper there is nothing to compare against, and the block becomes a feeling rather than a result.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our apartment in Al Sufouh or the Marina?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; tutors visiting a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. The honest trade is this: you give up a person in the room, and you gain a tutor matched to your child's exact syllabus rather than one selected from whoever can cross Al Sufouh Road by 5pm. For a Year 11 sitting a specific paper, that is usually the better side of the trade.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office for the syllabus codes on the entry. Cambridge codes look like 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry; Pearson codes look like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. It takes one email and it matters, because past papers, mark schemes and revision guides are not interchangeable. Cambridge also tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended at the point of entry, which caps the attainable grade, while Pearson's International GCSE is single-tier in most subjects.

faqs.question: What time can a session start if my daughter's school in Al Barsha finishes at 3pm?
faqs.answer: A 4.30pm start works well for a student who goes straight home, which is most of this catchment. Because the lesson is online, no travel time has to be built in at either end, so you are only budgeting for the journey the student already makes. Families where a parent works in Media City or the free zone often prefer 7pm or 8pm instead. The slot that matters is the one that survives a whole term without being rescheduled, and that is usually the one built around the student's energy rather than the parent's diary.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line between coursework feedback and a tutor doing the work for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, model a method on a different question, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, finish or edit a piece of assessed work to completion. The school signs an authentication that the work is the candidate's own, and if that is untrue the sanction falls on the student. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments; the entire risk of that purchase sits with the candidate.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how can I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Is it five IGCSE passes or six that the UAE equivalency rule actually asks for?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One competing tutoring site tells UAE parents six subjects are required. Verify the current rule on the Ministry of Education's own pages before planning around it, and treat equivalency as a floor rather than a university target.

faqs.question: My child takes Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE. Can those be tutored too?
faqs.answer: They can, but the rules are tighter than for other subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires that schools ensure teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so any support must track the school's own material.

faqs.question: Our evenings change completely in Ramadan - can an IGCSE slot near Knowledge Park move after Iftar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families in this catchment do. School days shorten during Ramadan, afternoons become unproductive, and a 9pm or 9.30pm session after Iftar is frequently the most alert hour of the day. Because delivery is online, moving a slot costs nothing and involves no one rearranging a drive. We would rather shift the whole term's timetable than keep a 4.30pm slot that is attended in body only. Ramadan also falls close to the run-up to the May and June papers, which makes the scheduling question a practical one rather than a courtesy.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for a niche IGCSE subject we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Some combinations are genuinely thin: a specific Pearson modular unit, a minority language, or a less common option within a science syllabus. When that happens you get three honest answers - how long a match is likely to take, whether a closely related specialist could cover part of the need, and whether the school's own department is the better route. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is a reason to ask every provider the question directly.

faqs.question: Should my child resit in November, and when does that decision need making?
faqs.answer: Make the decision before results arrive, not after. Work out in advance what grade would be worth resitting for in each subject, because November entries close well before the late-October start and the window between results and the deadline is short. Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November resit means a January result. Ask for the paper-level breakdown of the June grade: a near-miss caused by one paper is a far better resit case than a uniform shortfall.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-knowledge-p.closingHeading: Start from the date, not from the search
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-knowledge-p.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai Knowledge Park, the most useful next step is not choosing a tutor. It is finding out three things from the school: the syllabus codes, whether maths and the sciences are entered at Core or Extended, and which series the student sits. With those three facts the plan is almost self-evident, and a trial lesson becomes a test of the match rather than a guess. Send the marked mock paper, tell us the date the papers start, and we will say honestly what the weeks between now and then can achieve.

intro.heading: Start at the cheap end and work up, because that is how the money spends
paragraphs: Most pages answering this search open with premium pricing and work down, which flatters the writer and misleads the reader. Do it the other way. The cheapest published online tutoring in the Dubai market starts at AED 33 to AED 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik. Those figures are real and they are sometimes exactly right: for a Year 8 student who needs someone to sit with them while they work, the cheap tier does the job and anything more is waste. The error families make is not buying cheap. It is buying cheap for a Year 11 Extended candidate, where the person on the other end has never seen the mark scheme for the paper being sat.

One step up, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing its IGCSE tuition from AED 150. A specialist in an examined subject runs AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table giving 200 to 450 or more. At the top, premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. Every one of those numbers was read from the provider that published it in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price, and this page publishes no IB Gram price list, because a made-up figure sitting next to sourced ones would poison all of them.

Now the number that actually matters, which nobody publishes: hours per subject. An IGCSE subject that is going adequately and needs polishing takes something like eight to twelve hours across a year. A subject with a real gap in the Core foundations takes twenty-five to forty. A student starting Extended content from a weak Core base can absorb more than that and still be short. Multiply hours by rate and you get the real decision, and once you do the arithmetic the hourly rate stops being the variable that dominates. The hour count does.

This is also where the near me part of the search becomes a cost line rather than a convenience. A tutor who drives to a LA Mer address prices the drive into the hour, and on the Jumeirah Road at six in the evening the drive is long. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to AED 500 including travel against AED 150 to AED 300 for the same tutor online. Ask a visiting tutor for their online rate and the gap is usually AED 80 to AED 150 for identical teaching. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; that is an India-only service, and everything for LA Mer is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

What follows is the arithmetic in full: hours by subject at three price points, what the Core and Extended decision costs, how Cambridge and Pearson differ on the same subject and why booking the wrong board wastes the lot, the extras that appear on invoices, which five subjects your spend should protect for Ministry of Education equivalency, when group teaching is genuinely the better buy, and what a November resit should be budgeted at before results day rather than after it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-la-mer.programmesIntro: Spending decisions differ sharply by stage, and the cheapest grade is almost never bought in the examined year. These are the stages a LA Mer family passes through and where the money does most work at each.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, before IGCSE begins
programmes.description: No external certificate at stake, Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. The budget tier genuinely works here, because the task is usually fluency and habit rather than examination technique. An hour a week at AED 60 on algebraic manipulation in Year 8 does work that forty hours at AED 300 in Year 11 cannot replicate.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving on the Jumeirah coast mid-year frequently land in Years 7 to 9 with a method mismatch rather than an ability gap, which no school assessment will name for them. This is the cheapest window a Dubai family will ever get to fix it, and the one most commonly skipped.

programmes.name: IGCSE year one
programmes.description: Content is taught for the first time and the tier decision is usually made or confirmed. Support here costs mid-band rates and buys the most grade movement per dirham of any stage, because a topic learned properly the first time does not have to be relearned under exam pressure. Eight to twelve hours across the year is a common and sufficient commitment.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is also the year the KHDA mandatory subjects start showing up on reports in a way parents notice, since Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum. Budget for it rather than meeting it as a surprise in a January report.

programmes.name: IGCSE examined year
programmes.description: The most expensive year and the least efficient, because recall and method cannot be rebuilt as fast as they were lost. Specialist rates apply, hours climb, and the useful work is past papers under timing with mark schemes read by the student. Exam-year specialist support is the only tier where the Dubai market routinely exceeds AED 2,000 a month.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; the February and March series is India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Knowing which series and which zone your school uses determines when the money should be spent.

programmes.name: A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: Where the IGCSE decisions get paid for or get expensive. A student who took Additional Mathematics and did it properly walks into AS Mathematics; one who scraped Extended maths meets calculus notation unprepared. Specialist post-16 tuition sits in the same AED 200 to AED 450 band in published market data.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, is required alongside the five IGCSE subjects. That sourced requirement is worth checking before dropping a fourth AS to save a tuition line.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: The hour counts below are the realistic shape of a year's support per subject on the Jumeirah coast, not a price list. Multiply by the tier you intend to buy and you have your actual budget.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The subject most often bought and most often over-bought. A student with solid number and algebra needs eight to twelve hours of technique work across Year 11. A student whose algebra is unreliable needs thirty or more, because every later topic depends on it. Diagnose the algebra before agreeing a package.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading to A Level Mathematics, often at Dubai College and Jumeirah College. Calculus and proof structure appear here first. Twelve to twenty hours spread across the year, and it is one of the few subjects where paying specialist rates in Year 10 saves real money at AS.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Three components including a practical or alternative-to-practical paper. Electricity reasoning with real component values is where Extended candidates in Dubai schools lose most. Twelve to eighteen hours typically, concentrated on two or three topics rather than spread evenly across the syllabus.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic carries through most of the course, so a Year 10 weakness is still costing marks in Year 11 organic questions. Qualitative analysis is recall and is the cheapest set of marks on the paper to recover. Ten to eighteen hours, front-loaded onto quantitative work.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy but command-term sensitive. The expensive misdiagnosis here is buying content revision when the problem is answering the verb in the question. Eight to fourteen hours is usually enough, and a tutor who starts with a marked paper will see which of the two it is in one session.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading response, summary and directed writing carry the marks. Sitting the wrong specification for a student's actual fluency costs a grade before teaching starts, and that is a free fix made by asking the school. Ten to sixteen hours, mostly on timing and on writing to a specified audience.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Argument rather than retelling. A paragraph summarising the plot of a set text sits in the bottom band however well written, and breaking that habit takes about four sessions. Eight to twelve hours total, which makes Literature one of the better value subjects to buy help in.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Data response plus extended writing with heavy evaluation weighting. UAE students have abundant real context and rarely use it. The marks sit in the judgement sentence at the end of an evaluative answer. Eight to twelve hours, almost all of it on answer structure rather than content.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory plus problem solving and programming. Pseudocode conventions are examined precisely, so fluent Python coders still drop marks on paper. Trace tables and binary arithmetic are high-yield and under-practised. Eight to fourteen hours, with a disproportionate return on the paper-based technique.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Short frequent sessions beat long weekly ones, so the efficient purchase is thirty minutes three times a week rather than ninety once.

sections.heading: Price per grade, not price per hour
paragraphs: The useful calculation multiplies hours by rate, and the hours vary far more than the rate. Take a Year 11 Cambridge 0580 Extended student whose problem is two topics rather than the whole subject. Twelve hours with a specialist at AED 280 is AED 3,360. The same student put on a weekly generalist hour from September at AED 180 buys thirty-six hours for AED 6,480, covers the entire syllabus again, and may never touch the two topics that were losing the marks. The cheaper hourly rate produced the more expensive year.

Run it the other way and the logic still holds. A Year 8 student who needs company and structure while doing homework gets nothing extra from a specialist. Forty hours at AED 60 is AED 2,400 and does exactly the job. Forty hours at AED 280 is AED 11,200 and does the same job with a more qualified person sitting through it. Matching tier to task is the entire skill in buying tutoring, and it is the thing no provider page explains because explaining it reduces what they sell you.

The table below runs three realistic LA Mer scenarios against three tiers. The point is not the exact figures, which depend on how many hours a particular child needs, but the shape: for a diagnosed, narrow problem the specialist is cheaper in total; for broad content coverage the mid tier is sufficient; for supervision the budget tier is correct. Diagnose first, then choose a tier, then ask about the rate. Doing it in the other order is how families end up with the wrong three thousand dirhams.

sections.heading: The Core and Extended decision is a budget decision
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered, and the tier your child is entered for sets a ceiling on the grade available. On the 0580 Mathematics structure, Core caps at a mid grade while Extended reaches the top. That single fact reframes a great deal of tutoring spend. A family paying specialist rates for forty hours chasing a top grade while their child is entered for Core is buying something the specification does not sell, and no amount of teaching changes that.

The inverse error is more common and more expensive. A student is moved up to Extended on the strength of effort rather than attainment, arrives with gaps in the Core content that Extended assumes, and then needs the Core material closed before any Extended technique is worth teaching. That doubles the hours. A tutor who checks the tier and the Core foundations in the first session will tell you this; a tutor who starts teaching Extended content on day one will bill you for the discovery three months later.

So ask the school two questions before you buy anything, in writing if you can. Which tier is my child entered for in each tiered subject, and when is that entry confirmed? Entry deadlines sit months before the exam window, which means there is a period in which the tier can still be changed and a period in which it cannot. Spending decisions made inside that window are reversible; spending decisions made after it are not. The table sets out what each tier actually buys.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: booking the wrong board wastes every hour
paragraphs: A LA Mer parent hiring an IGCSE tutor near them is rarely asked which board, and it is the question that determines whether the hours are useful. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award International GCSE qualifications, in the same subjects, with different syllabus codes, different paper structures and different tiering arrangements. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology. Pearson uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1.

The practical consequences are concrete. Past papers from the wrong board teach the wrong question style. Mark scheme conventions differ. The availability and operation of tiering differs by subject and board. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November. A tutor who works from the wrong board's material will teach your child competent content and leave them unprepared for the paper in front of them, which is the most expensive form of competent teaching available.

There is a second trap. Schools do not always enter every subject with the same board. A Dubai school may use Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson for maths, or the reverse, and a parent who asks once and assumes it applies across the board will book two tutors correctly and one wrongly. Get the board and the syllabus code per subject from the school in writing, give it to the tutor before the trial lesson, and ask the tutor to confirm which board's papers they will use. That exchange costs nothing and protects the whole budget.

sections.heading: The extras that appear on an invoice
paragraphs: The hourly rate is the advertised number and rarely the whole bill. A travelling tutor's time is priced in, but so sometimes is a minimum session length, a cancellation window, a materials charge, a registration or matching fee, and a minimum package commitment. None of these are improper. All of them are worth establishing before the first session, because a family comparing AED 180 with AED 220 an hour may be comparing a flexible hourly arrangement with a ten-session minimum and a seventy-two-hour cancellation rule.

Three specific things to settle in writing. First, whether the quoted rate is per hour or per session, because a ninety-minute session at a per-session price is a different unit from an hourly one. Second, the cancellation policy and how much notice avoids a charge, which matters more in Dubai than elsewhere because school events, travel and Ramadan all move plans. Third, what happens if the match is wrong: whether there is a replacement policy, and whether unused sessions in a package are refundable or transferable.

On VAT, this page takes the careful position. UAE VAT treatment of tuition is not something to assert without a Federal Tax Authority citation, and this page offers none. What a parent can reasonably do is ask any provider directly whether their quoted dirham figure is inclusive or exclusive, and ask for a tax registration number if one is claimed. A provider who cannot answer that question clearly has told you something useful about their invoicing generally.

sections.heading: Which five subjects your spending should protect
paragraphs: If the household has a finite tutoring budget, the subjects to protect are the ones that carry forward. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. That is the sourced requirement. One UAE tutoring site ranking for these searches states six subjects are required; publishing the correct five is both more accurate and more useful.

There is a second layer. The British track also requires proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. On the American track, English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB, no points threshold has been read on an official source, so none is published here.

None of this makes tutoring necessary for equivalency, and it would be a false urgency claim to suggest otherwise. What it does is tell a family which grades are load-bearing. A student comfortably above the threshold in five subjects has already secured that requirement, and spend is better directed at the subjects their intended degree needs. A student at risk of dropping below it in a sixth subject has a clearer priority. Equivalency itself is a process the Ministry administers; IB Gram does not perform it, guarantee it or submit anything on a family's behalf.

sections.heading: When a group or a school class is genuinely the better buy
paragraphs: One-to-one is not always the right purchase, and a page that never says so is selling rather than advising. There are three situations in which a group is better value and one in which it is better outright. Better value: when the content is new to everyone and the task is coverage rather than diagnosis; when the student is motivated and the constraint is pace rather than understanding; and when the budget simply does not stretch to enough one-to-one hours to be useful, where a well-run group beats two isolated private sessions.

Better outright: when the student's problem is confidence in speaking up, and watching peers ask the question they were afraid to ask does something a private session cannot. That is a real effect and it is worth knowing before spending on individual hours. The counter-case is equally clear. A diagnosed, narrow, individual problem is exactly what a group cannot address, because the group runs at the group's pace and your child's two topics are not the group's two topics.

The free option is also real and routinely ignored. Most Dubai schools run subject support sessions, revision clubs or clinics, and many teachers will mark an extra past paper if asked directly. That costs nothing, uses the teacher who knows the entry, the tier and the board, and should be exhausted before any invoice is signed. Families who approach the school first often discover the problem was a missed topic during an absence, which the school fixes free. IB Gram delivers one-to-one online only, so this recommendation costs us a sale and is still the right first step.

sections.heading: Budget the resit before results day, not after it
paragraphs: The November series exists and almost nobody plans for it. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For a UAE candidate, November is the resit route after June. The financially sensible move is to decide in advance what you would do if a grade comes back below what a sixth-form place requires, because the decision window after results day is short and the tutoring market tightens quickly.

Timing makes this concrete. June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026 for Pearson, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. A June result arriving in late August gives roughly eight to ten weeks before a November window that runs through to mid-November. That is enough time for a focused block and not enough time for a rebuild, which means the resit plan has to be narrow: one or two subjects, specific papers, past papers from the first session.

The honest financial framing is that a resit block is a concentrated purchase at specialist rates, and it is one of the few cases where premium pricing is justified by the calendar rather than by the content. Set aside the possibility of it when you plan the year's spend, rather than discovering it as an unbudgeted emergency in late August. And confirm the entry route with the school's exams officer, including the centre's zone, since Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

sections.heading: Checking a tutor is permitted, before money changes hands
paragraphs: Cost and legitimacy are the same conversation, because an unpermitted tutor is one who can disappear mid-block. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone quoting a permit fee is describing something that does not exist. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so this page quotes no amount and you should treat any specific figure you see online as unverified. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is different again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.

One more boundary, which is free to observe and expensive to breach. Do not arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately for payment. The MoHRE permit code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school. For completeness and because several competing pages blur this: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, and operates no office or centre in the UAE.

process.title: Get the board, code and tier from the school
process.description: In writing, per subject, because schools mix boards across subjects. Cambridge 0580 Extended is a different booking from Pearson 4MA1, and a tutor working from the wrong board's papers teaches competently towards the wrong examination. This one email protects the entire budget.

process.title: Find a marked paper and name the problem
process.description: A recent assessment with a mark on it tells a tutor whether the issue is content, method, timing or question interpretation. Those four need four different plans at four different costs. Without it, your first two paid sessions are diagnosis at full rate.

process.title: Pick the tier to match the task, then ask the rate
process.description: Supervision needs the budget tier. Broad content catch-up needs the middle. A diagnosed narrow weakness is cheapest with the most expensive tutor, because it needs fewest hours. Choosing the rate before the task is how families buy the wrong three thousand dirhams.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson and settle the invoice terms
process.description: One lesson per family, before any payment. In the same conversation, settle whether the rate is per hour or per session, the cancellation notice, any minimum commitment, and what happens if the match is wrong. All four belong in writing before session two.

process.title: Review at six sessions against the named problem
process.description: Not against a feeling about how it is going. Either the specific weakness has moved or it has not, and if it has not, change the tutor or the plan. Families who never set a review point are the families still paying in May for a match that was wrong in October.

whyPoints.title: Hours are quoted, not just rates
whyPoints.description: This page gives realistic hour counts per IGCSE subject so you can calculate a total rather than guess from an hourly band. Hours vary roughly three-fold by subject and starting point, while rates vary much less, which makes the hour count the number that decides the bill.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium is removed rather than absorbed
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to AED 500 including travel against AED 150 to AED 300 online for comparable tutors. Online delivery takes the Jumeirah Road out of the invoice. IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service, stated plainly.

whyPoints.title: Board and tier are confirmed before teaching starts
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4MA1, not to IGCSE science or maths. Getting that wrong is the single most complete way to waste a tutoring budget, and it happens because nobody asked the school which board each subject is entered with.

whyPoints.title: Market figures are attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is credited to the provider or rate table that published it, read in October 2026. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no average grade and no star rating, because we cannot produce the underlying data for any of them and neither can the pages that do.

whyPoints.title: Cheaper options are named, including free ones
whyPoints.description: Group teaching beats one-to-one for coverage, pace and confidence, and most Dubai schools run free subject clinics that should be exhausted first. Saying so costs us sessions and is still the right advice, which is the test of whether a page is advising or selling.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, not implied
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a subject at your hour, we say so and give a realistic match time rather than putting a generalist in the slot. No competitor page in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, which is precisely why discovering one in March is a common experience.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor near me in LA Mer work out to across a whole year?
faqs.answer: Multiply hours by rate rather than reading a rate alone. A Year 11 subject with two misfiring topics needs about twelve hours, which at specialist rates of around AED 280 is near AED 3,400. A Year 10 subject with broad gaps needs nearer thirty hours, which at mid-band rates around AED 180 is about AED 5,400. Published Dubai bands run AED 33 to 65 at the budget end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, from sources read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutoring tier in Dubai ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific job. Published rates from AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik suit a Year 7 to 9 student who needs structure and company while working, where the task is habit rather than examination technique. Forty hours at that level costs a fraction of the same hours with a specialist and does the same job. It is the wrong choice for a Year 11 Extended candidate, because examination technique requires someone who has worked the mark scheme.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board my child's school enters each subject with?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly and get it in writing per subject, because Dubai schools commonly mix boards. A school may use Cambridge for sciences and Pearson Edexcel for mathematics, or the reverse. You want the awarding body and the syllabus code for each subject, such as 0620 or 4MA1, plus the tier where the subject is tiered. Give that list to any tutor before the trial lesson and ask which board's past papers they will use. Mismatched board material is the most complete way to waste a tutoring budget.

faqs.question: Does the Core tier cap the grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: Yes, in tiered Cambridge subjects. On the 0580 Mathematics structure, Core reaches a middle grade while Extended reaches the top grades. So paying specialist rates to chase a high grade while a child is entered for Core buys something the specification does not offer. Ask the school which tier each tiered subject is entered for and when that entry is confirmed, because there is a window before the deadline in which the tier can change and a period afterwards in which it cannot.

faqs.question: Which five subjects should we prioritise if the budget is limited?
faqs.answer: The ones carrying your child above the equivalency threshold and towards their intended degree. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. A student comfortably clear in five has secured that requirement, so spend belongs on subjects their degree needs. Equivalency is a Ministry process; no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it, and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: What extras should I check before agreeing an hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Six things, all settled in writing. Whether the rate is per hour or per session, since a ninety-minute session priced per session is a different unit. The cancellation notice that avoids a charge. Any minimum package or session commitment. Whether materials or a registration fee are added. What happens if the match is wrong, including unused sessions. And whether the quoted dirham figure includes VAT, which you should ask the provider directly rather than read from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Would a small group be cheaper and just as good for my child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes genuinely better, not just cheaper. A group suits new content where the task is coverage, a motivated student whose constraint is pace, and a child whose real problem is not speaking up, because watching peers ask the awkward question does something private sessions cannot. A group cannot address a diagnosed narrow weakness, since it runs at the group's pace and your child's two topics are not the group's. IB Gram delivers one-to-one online only, so this is advice against our own sale.

faqs.question: Should we budget for a November resit before results arrive?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the window afterwards is short. Cambridge runs June and November series and Pearson runs May/June and November, so November is the UAE resit route. Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, leaving roughly eight to ten weeks before a November window running to mid-November. That is enough for a narrow block on one or two subjects at specialist rates, and not enough for a rebuild. Deciding in advance what you would do turns an emergency into a plan.

faqs.question: Why is a specialist sometimes cheaper in total than a generalist?
faqs.answer: Because they need fewer hours for a diagnosed problem. Twelve hours at AED 280 is about AED 3,360 and closes two named topics. Thirty-six weekly hours at AED 180 is about AED 6,480, covers the whole syllabus again, and may never reach those two topics at all. The lower hourly rate produced the larger bill and the smaller result. This inversion only applies where the problem is narrow and identified, which is why diagnosis from a marked paper comes before any purchase.

faqs.question: Can we use the school's own support instead of paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Start there. Most Dubai schools run subject clinics, revision sessions or support groups, and many teachers will mark an additional past paper if asked directly. That costs nothing and uses someone who knows the entry, the board and the tier. Families who ask the school first frequently find the problem was a topic missed during an absence, which the school closes for free. Exhaust that before signing anything. We deliver one-to-one online tuition and still think this is the correct first step.

faqs.question: How many hours does IGCSE Chemistry usually take to fix?
faqs.answer: Between ten and eighteen across a year for a typical Cambridge 0620 Extended student, weighted heavily towards the quantitative work. Moles arithmetic runs through most of the course, so a Year 10 weakness there is still costing marks in Year 11 organic questions and has to be closed first. Qualitative analysis is pure recall and the cheapest set of marks on the paper to recover, usually two sessions. A tutor who starts with new content rather than with the arithmetic will take considerably longer and cost more.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send someone to a LA Mer address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video to families across the UAE and does not make home visits anywhere in the Emirates; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We target the near me search because it is the phrase parents type, and the honest answer is that removing the drive removes both the travel premium from the rate and the twenty-minute radius from your shortlist. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time with a shared whiteboard and an optional recording.

faqs.question: Is there a fee for the tutor's UAE permit that we end up paying?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and the MoHRE service page lists no fee with a two-working-day completion time. Anyone adding a permit cost to your quote is charging for something that does not exist. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific dirham figure you read online as unverified.

faqs.question: When in the year is tutoring money best spent?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families spend it. Hours bought in Year 10 while content is being taught for the first time cost mid-band rates and prevent the relearning that makes Year 11 expensive. Hours bought in the eight weeks before a series cost specialist rates and can only reorganise what is already there. The single best-value block available is the summer between the two IGCSE years, on the one subject that went badly, because nothing else is competing for the student's time.

faqs.question: What review point should we set so we do not overspend?
faqs.answer: Six sessions, measured against a named weakness rather than against a general impression. Six is enough to see whether a specific topic or technique has moved and not enough to have committed a term's budget. Signs of a weak match are concrete: the tutor talks more than the student, sessions cover ground without ending in anything specific, or the board and tier never came up. Changing tutor at session six is inexpensive. Discovering the mismatch in May costs the examined year.

intro.heading: Can the tutor near you name your child's specification?
paragraphs: Finding somebody to teach International GCSE subjects is not difficult. Verifying that they know the qualification your child is actually sitting is, and it is the only part that matters. International GCSE is awarded by both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel. Cambridge reports on an A* to G scale and tiers several subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson reports on a 9 to 1 scale and tiers mathematics into Foundation and Higher. The syllabus codes differ, the papers are structured differently, and the command terms carry slightly different weight.

That distinction is invisible in a search result and almost invisible in conversation unless a parent asks for it. A tutor can speak fluently about Year 11 chemistry and have no idea whether your child is entered for Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1, whether they are on the Extended tier, or whether the school is reporting them on a letter scale or a number scale. All three facts change what the hours should be spent on, and a plan built without them is built for an average student rather than yours.

Living Legends makes the verification problem worse in a mundane way. It is a single gated community of villas and apartment towers off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, sitting between Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Remraam, with no secondary school inside it. The local supply of tutors is small by definition, so the practical choice is often between whoever is nearby and whoever is actually qualified for the specification. When those two are different people, proximity is an expensive tiebreaker.

The good news is that verification is cheap. One email to the school's examinations officer produces the board, the code and the tier. Three questions in a first conversation reveal whether a tutor has worked the specification: which board and code have you taught most recently, what is the commonest mark loss on the long questions in this subject, and what is the student examined on in place of a performed practical? A specialist answers all three immediately and concretely. A generalist answers in terms of confidence, revision and organisation, which would be the same answer for any subject at any level.

IB Gram's part is simple to state. We match on board, syllabus code and tier, we teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send anybody to a Living Legends address because home visits are a service we run only in India. The first session is a free full-length trial with no card. What follows is the verification detail: the two grading scales, how command terms work, what a specialist knows subject by subject, how the written practical paper is assessed, and what the market charges.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-living-lege.programmesIntro: Four routes cover nearly every request from this community, and the differences change which papers a student sits.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely entered International GCSE in Dubai schools, reported on an A* to G scale. Several subjects are tiered: Core papers lead to grades C to G and Extended papers to A* to E, with the tier set at entry. Syllabus codes identify the specification precisely, for example 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics and 0610 Biology. Cambridge runs June and November series.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this community making the Core or Extended decision are usually doing so in Year 10 on the basis of limited internal evidence. It is the most consequential academic decision taken before sixteen, because it fixes a grade ceiling that no later effort can lift.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Reported on a 9 to 1 scale in most subjects, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics and 4BI1 Biology. Pearson generally examines a single tier in the sciences, with Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics, and offers a modular route in some subjects so units can be sat across more than one series. Examinations run May/June and November.
programmes.countryNote: Households arriving in this community from a UK state school meet Pearson most often, and the modular option is the part they usually do not know about. Whether a centre uses it is a centre decision rather than a published default, so it has to be asked.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage before International GCSE, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. Diagnostic rather than certificating, and their real function is to indicate a Core or Extended trajectory. Weaknesses visible here in algebra, scientific explanation or extended writing are the ones that decide the tier two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Nearby provision in Motor City, Sports City and Remraam covers these years, so students from this community have short journeys and usable afternoon time. Work done now is both cheaper and more effective than remediation in the examination year.

programmes.name: AS and International A Level progression
programmes.description: The route most British-curriculum students here take after International GCSE, alongside the IB Diploma. Subject choice at sixteen is constrained by tier and grade, which is why the tier decision reaches beyond the certificate. Cambridge International A Level also runs in June and November series.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, is required alongside five International GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-living-lege.subjectsIntro: The difference between a specialist and a generalist is visible subject by subject. These notes name the specification detail a real specialist will raise unprompted.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: A specialist asks for the tier before anything else, because Core caps the grade at C and Extended reaches A*. They will also say that most lost marks are unshown method rather than wrong method, which is a habit with a defined fix.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A specialist names units, significant figures and undrawn diagrams as the standard losses, and knows the practical content is examined in writing rather than performed. A generalist talks about physics being conceptually hard.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A specialist raises state symbols in equations and half equations unbalanced for charge without being asked, and knows where moles work sits relative to the tier. Those two details alone separate experience from familiarity.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A specialist talks about answer structure on long questions rather than content volume, because that is where the marks go. They will ask whether the student is writing in prose when the markscheme wants discrete points.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: A specialist asks which award before anything else, because content is reduced unevenly across the three sciences and separate-science material over-prepares. This is the single commonest waste in science tutoring in this market.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: A specialist asks whether the entry is first or second language, since Cambridge 0500 and 0510 are separate specifications. They will also ask how much marked writing the student currently produces, because that is the only lever that moves the grade.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Its own reading and listening components, and material built for the first-language specification is of limited use. Families are frequently unsure which of the two their child is entered for, and the school's entry record settles it.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: A specialist will say that application and evaluation carry the top band and definitions do not, and will start with past-paper evaluation questions rather than a glossary. Hours spent on definitions at this level are close to wasted.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: A specialist checks which of the two is entered before agreeing anything, because 0478 carries algorithms and pseudocode while 0417 is application-based. Booking the wrong one is a term of fees spent on the wrong subject.

sections.heading: Three questions that identify a real specialist
paragraphs: A parent cannot assess subject expertise directly, but specificity is a reliable proxy, and three questions in a first conversation produce it. Which board and syllabus code have you taught most recently, and in which year? What is the commonest mark loss on the long questions in this subject? What is a student examined on in place of a performed practical?

A specialist answers the first with a code and a year: 0620 last June, or 4MA1 Higher tier through to the November series. They answer the second concretely, naming state symbols, unshown method, undrawn diagrams or prose answers where the markscheme wants discrete points. They answer the third by describing written practical questions: identifying variables, criticising a method, processing data, evaluating reliability. None of those answers requires preparation from somebody who has taught the specification.

A generalist answers differently and the pattern is easy to recognise. The first answer becomes a statement about years of teaching experience. The second becomes an observation that students find the subject hard or do not revise enough. The third becomes a comment about the importance of laboratory work. None of it is dishonest and none of it is useful, because it would be the same answer for any subject at any level.

Why this matters more than a qualification is that International GCSE grading depends on markscheme behaviour as much as on knowledge. A graduate can explain a topic clearly and not notice that the student is losing a third of the available marks to a presentation habit. The table below extends the three questions into a short verification list a parent can work through before paying for anything.

sections.heading: Two grading scales, and how to read a school report properly
paragraphs: Parents in this community frequently hold reports that mix conventions, because siblings may be on different boards and schools report in different ways. Cambridge International GCSE reports on an A* to G scale. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on a 9 to 1 scale in most subjects. These are different scales, not different labels for the same thing, and converting casually between them produces wrong conclusions about how close a student is to a target.

The second complication is tiering, which interacts with the scale. A Cambridge Core entry can produce grades C to G only; an Extended entry reaches A* to E. So a report showing a predicted C means something quite different depending on the tier: on Core it is the top of what is available, and on Extended it is mid-range with headroom. A parent reading the letter alone cannot tell which situation they are in, and nor can a tutor who did not ask.

The third is that school reports often show a working grade, a target grade and a predicted grade, generated by different methods. A working grade reflects recent classwork. A target may be derived from prior attainment data. A predicted grade is a professional judgement for a specific purpose. Treating all three as measurements of the same thing is how families end up alarmed by a report that says something quite ordinary.

The useful action is to ask the school three things: which board and tier each subject is entered for, which scale each subject is reported on, and what method produced the target. With those answers a report becomes readable and a tutoring brief becomes precise. The table below sets out what each scale and tier combination actually means.
