sections.heading: Command terms and assessment objectives: the invisible curriculum
paragraphs: Every International GCSE paper is written against assessment objectives, and every question uses a command term that signals which objective is being tested. Students are rarely taught this explicitly, and it is responsible for a large share of lost marks across every subject. A student who knows the content and reads state as explain writes three times too much and runs out of time; one who reads explain as describe writes the right facts and scores half.

The terms are consistent enough to learn in a few sessions. State and name want a short answer with no justification. Describe wants what happens, in order, without reasons. Explain wants the reason or mechanism. Suggest wants an answer applied to an unfamiliar situation, where more than one response may be credited. Compare wants both things addressed in the same sentence rather than in separate paragraphs. Evaluate wants a judgement supported by both sides. Calculate wants working shown, because the method carries marks independently of the answer.

Mark allocation is the second half of the signal, and students ignore it. A two-mark question wants two distinct creditable points, and a student writing a paragraph has wasted time that the six-mark question at the end of the paper needed. Teaching a student to read the mark allocation as an instruction about length is one of the fastest grade improvements available in any subject, and it is purely technical.

This is also where boards differ in ways that matter. Cambridge and Pearson phrase questions differently and weight their command terms slightly differently, and their data questions look different on the page. A student drilled on the wrong board's past questions arrives with the right knowledge and an unfamiliar interface, which costs time and composure in the opening minutes. Board-specific practice is not a refinement; it is the difference between prepared and nearly prepared.

sections.heading: Why a gated community cannot supply an Extended-tier specialist
paragraphs: This is arithmetic rather than a complaint. A tutor builds a diary from the families within reach. Living Legends is a single gated community; of the households inside it, only some have examination-year students, only some of those need a particular subject, and only some need it at Extended or Higher tier in a given year. Follow that chain and the local demand for any one specialism is a household or two, which cannot sustain a specialist.

What specialists do instead is locate by road access and travel, pricing the journey, or stay local and widen their subject range until the diary fills. Both are rational. Neither delivers what a family here wants, which is somebody who has taught their child's exact specification recently and is reliably available at a fixed hour. The visiting specialist charges the top of the in-home band and arrives through a gate; the local generalist teaches an adjacent subject competently.

There is a wider scarcity underneath this that gets misdiagnosed as a local shortage. Extended and Higher tier depth, and particularly in physics, chemistry and computer science, is thin across the whole emirate rather than only in one community. Narrowing a search by distance therefore reduces an already small pool on the one variable that has nothing to do with whether a tutor can read a markscheme.

Remove distance and the question becomes answerable: who has taught 0620 Extended or 4PH1 recently, and can they take six o'clock on a Tuesday? That has a real answer, and it is the same answer inside the Living Legends gate as in Motor City. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced Cambridge and Pearson teachers outside the Emirates, and a parent should know that at the outset.

sections.heading: The written practical paper, and why online suits it
paragraphs: Science families in this community reliably ask how practical work is handled when tuition is delivered over video. The answer rests on how the qualification actually assesses it, and once understood the objection mostly disappears.

In the main International GCSE science routes, practical skills are examined through written questions about experimental method rather than through a performed experiment marked on the day. Candidates identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, criticise a given method, read an instrument scale, process data into a table, plot a graph, assess reliability and suggest a specific improvement. Those are writing and reasoning skills, and they are the most reliably recoverable block in the whole qualification because almost nobody teaches them explicitly.

They also suit a shared screen better than a bench. Both people can annotate the same data table and graph in real time. A tutor can display a deliberately flawed method and ask what is wrong with it, which is exactly the format the paper uses. The most valuable session of all is one where the student brings their own messy data from a school practical and has it processed properly, which converts a frustrating afternoon into transferable technique.

The laboratory work itself belongs to the school, which has the equipment, the technician and the safety framework, and nothing about online tutoring substitutes for that. The division of labour is therefore clean: the school runs the laboratory and the tutor teaches the paper. Since the marks sit on the paper, that is where the tutoring belongs, and a specialist will say so without being prompted.

sections.heading: What verification-grade tutoring costs around here
paragraphs: Having established what a specialist is, it is worth knowing what one costs, because the bands correspond roughly to what a tutor knows rather than only to how they market themselves. Every figure below names the provider or source that published it, which matters in a market where three of the six most visible pages publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. That band is frequency and patience, which is often right for Years 7 to 9. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150; that band is specification knowledge and marking. Specialist International GCSE and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting examination-year specialist support at AED 200 to 450 plus. Premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

The in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel sits across all of those, and it is a delivery tier rather than a quality tier. In a gated community it also costs minutes: a tutor booked for six who clears security at ten past has delivered fifty minutes of a paid hour, and that recurs twice a week for a school year. Monthly, four two-hour in-home sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions.

One figure should be zero and sometimes is not. The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Any licensing or registration line item in a quote is charging for something free, and it is a reasonable question to ask about. None of the figures above is an IB Gram price list; our answer to the price question is a free full-length trial lesson and a conversation.

sections.heading: Coursework, board material and what we will not do
paragraphs: International GCSE carries less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but where assessed personal work exists the boundary is the same, and it is worth stating because one page ranking in this market sells completed assessed work outright. The penalty for that falls on the student rather than the seller.

A tutor may teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, test whether a proposed approach is workable, read what the student has written and identify where it is losing marks, demonstrate a technique on different material, and teach citation and referencing properly. Where a school requires an authentication declaration, the student signs it, and a tutor who has crossed the line has put that signature at risk.

On materials the position is firm. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are their copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure in addition. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. A provider advertising a download library of papers is offering an unresolved copyright problem rather than an advantage.

A parallel rule applies to the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the International GCSE timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students, and for those subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. Support there works from the school's own material by design.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and availability stated honestly
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the facts are short enough that every page should carry them. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

There is a second rule a family tempted by a convenient arrangement should know. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. That reporting is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy text, so verify against the current ADEK document before relying on the exact wording.

School regulation sits with the emirate. Dubai is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education and inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

On availability, the honest version: single-subject support at either tier matches quickly, and the limiting factor is usually the contested half past five to seven weekday window rather than the subject. The narrowest requests are specific tiers in physics, chemistry and computer science at short notice, and where no specialist is free we give a date rather than putting a near-fit in front of a Year 11 student. No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere.

whyPoints.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate ask for different things, and mark allocation is a length instruction. Teaching that explicitly is one of the fastest grade improvements available in any subject and it is almost never taught deliberately.

whyPoints.description: Variables, method criticism, data processing and evaluation are examined in writing across all three sciences, and they transfer between them. A shared annotated screen suits that work better than a bench, while the laboratory stays with the school.

whyPoints.description: A gated community cannot supply an Extended-tier specialist by local demand, and that depth is thin across the whole emirate. Removing distance from the match filters on the variable that actually predicts whether hours convert into marks.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names who published it, including the in-home figures that make the travel premium visible. The MoHRE private tutor permit is free of charge for two years, so no licensing cost belongs in anybody's quote.

whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, Cambridge or Pearson approval, no UAE office, no grade promise, and no statistic without the number of students, the date and the method. Board material is cited and linked rather than reproduced.

faqs.question: How do I check that a nearby IGCSE tutor knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions in the first conversation. Which board and syllabus code have you taught most recently, and in which year? What is the commonest mark loss on the long questions in this subject? What is a student examined on in place of a performed practical? A specialist answers with a code and a year, with something concrete such as omitted state symbols or prose where the markscheme wants discrete points, and with a description of written practical questions. A generalist answers about confidence, revision and laboratory access.

faqs.question: Why do my children's reports use letters for one and numbers for the other?
faqs.answer: Because they are on different boards. Cambridge International GCSE reports on an A* to G scale and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on a 9 to 1 scale in most subjects. These are different scales rather than different labels for the same thing, so converting casually between them produces wrong conclusions about how close each child is to a target. Ask the school which board and which scale applies to each subject, and whether a shown grade is a working grade, a target or a prediction.

faqs.question: What does a predicted C actually mean on a Cambridge report?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the tier, which is why the tier has to be in the brief. A Cambridge Core entry can produce grades C to G only, so a predicted C is the ceiling of what is available rather than a midpoint. An Extended entry reaches A* to E, so the same letter sits mid-range with real headroom above it. A parent reading the letter alone cannot tell which situation applies, and nor can a tutor who did not ask. One email to the examinations officer settles it.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE command terms trip up students here most?
faqs.answer: Explain and describe, read as each other. A student who describes accurately when the question asked for an explanation writes the right facts and collects about half the marks, because the markscheme is paying for the reason or mechanism. Suggest is the second, because students recite a textbook example rather than applying knowledge to the unfamiliar case in front of them. Calculate is the third: a final number with no working forfeits the method marks, which are often most of the available credit on the question.

faqs.question: Is there any IGCSE specialist actually based in Living Legends?
faqs.answer: Unlikely at Extended or Higher tier, and the reason is structural rather than local. A single gated community holds a limited number of households, only some have examination-year students, and only some need a particular subject at the higher tier in a given year. That cannot sustain a specialist. Visiting specialists price the journey; local generalists widen their subject range. IB Gram does not send anybody to a UAE address at all, and matches on board, code and tier instead, which is the variable that predicts usefulness.

faqs.question: How are practical skills examined if my child never performs an experiment with the tutor?
faqs.answer: Through written questions, which is how the qualification assesses them in the main routes. Candidates identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, criticise a given method, read an instrument scale, process data, plot a graph, assess reliability and suggest a specific improvement. Those are writing and reasoning skills, taught better on a shared annotated document than at a bench. The laboratory work belongs to the school, which has the equipment and the technician. The marks sit on the paper, so that is where the tutoring should be.

faqs.question: Does the mark allocation really tell you how much to write?
faqs.answer: Yes, and treating it as an instruction is one of the quickest improvements available. A two-mark question wants two distinct creditable points; a student writing a paragraph has spent time the six-mark question at the end of the paper needed. A six-mark question wants six creditable points or three developed ones depending on the subject, structured rather than written as continuous prose. Teaching a student to read the number in the margin before writing changes their timing across the whole paper, not just one question.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson papers really need separate practice?
faqs.answer: Enough that it matters in the opening minutes. The underlying content overlaps heavily, but question phrasing, command-term weighting and the presentation of data questions differ, and Cambridge tiers several subjects while Pearson generally examines a single tier in the sciences. A student drilled on the wrong board arrives with the right knowledge and an unfamiliar interface, which costs time and composure. Board-specific practice is not a refinement; it is the difference between prepared and nearly prepared on the day.

faqs.question: Can the tier be changed once the school has decided?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only before entries close. The tier is set at entry by the school, usually on internal assessment evidence, and after the deadline no amount of tutoring lifts the ceiling. If the grade a family needs sits above the Core ceiling, a short diagnostic against the real specification, written up with a gap list and a realistic timescale, is the thing to take to a head of department. Occasionally the evidence argues the other way, and an honest Core entry with a strong grade is the better outcome.

faqs.question: What does a verified specialist cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150. Specialist International GCSE and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150, which is often right for Years 7 to 9. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel, and in a gated community they also lose minutes at the gate.

faqs.question: Should a tutor offer us a library of past papers?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer like that should prompt a question rather than gratitude. Cambridge and Pearson past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade boundary tables are their copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A specialist cites the official source, works from material the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. A download library is an unresolved copyright problem that a family using it would be participating in.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child sit from a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge International qualifications, the June series and the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE page quoting a spring window is giving you a date you cannot act on. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Checkable anchors from past series: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge centres also sit in one of six administrative timetable zones.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working online still need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: The permit requirement applies to private tuition regardless of format. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist be matched for a Year 11 subject?
faqs.answer: Usually within days for mathematics, the sciences, English and the humanities, with the limiting factor being the hour rather than the subject, because half past five to seven on a weekday is contested across the whole city. Shifting twenty minutes later or taking a weekend morning normally resolves it. The narrowest requests are specific tiers in physics, chemistry and computer science at short notice, and where no specialist is genuinely free we give a date instead of substituting a near-fit.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, one afternoon, and a drive in between
paragraphs: The problem a Meydan parent brings to this search is not usually finding a tutor. It is deciding what to do with the single afternoon their child has free. A Year 11 student in a British-curriculum school is sitting nine or ten examined subjects. They are commuting, because Meydan has almost no schools inside it. Sport, clubs and in the spring term school revision sessions take one or two afternoons. What remains is one weekday slot and part of a weekend, and nine subjects competing for it.

Distance is therefore the least useful filter available. What matters is triage: which two or three subjects are genuinely at risk of a grade the student needs, and which of those will respond to the hours available. A student losing marks on timing across every paper has a different problem from one missing a term of chemistry, and only one of those can be fixed between February and June. Deciding honestly is worth more than finding somebody nearby.

The geography still shapes the answer, just not in the way the search implies. Meydan children travel to Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland, to Kings' School Nad Al Sheba, Repton School Dubai and GEMS Modern Academy in Nad Al Sheba, or further to Safa Community School in Al Quoz and the Al Barsha and Silicon Oasis schools. Arrival home ranges from before 15:30 to after 17:00, and that range decides session length more than the subject does.

Dubai held 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with UK-curriculum schools at 37% of enrolment across seventeen licensed curricula. That makes IGCSE maths, English and the three sciences well supplied locally. It does not make everything well supplied: a student needing Additional Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics at a specific board, or a second language is looking for somebody far scarcer, and the distance filter actively works against them.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India. The practical effect on triage is that the scarce-subject problem largely disappears, because the pool is the timezone rather than the drive, and the one free afternoon is not shortened by somebody else's journey into a district with no schools in it.

Before reading further, it is worth writing two lists. The first is the subjects where your child needs a specific grade for a specific next step, which is usually shorter than expected and often has only two or three subjects on it. The second is the subjects where their last marked script showed lost marks you can describe — not a grade you were disappointed by, but a pattern you could name. Where the two lists overlap is where the afternoon should go. Everything else on this page is detail about how to spend it once that decision has been taken.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-meydan.programmesIntro: Triage looks different at each stage, because what is fixable changes. These are the stages a Meydan family passes through on the British route, described by what support can realistically achieve at each.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The only stage at which everything is fixable and nothing is urgent, which makes it the best value and the least bought. A genuine subject gap closed in Year 8 costs a fraction of the same gap closed in Year 11, because there is no examination pressure forcing the pace and the week has room in it. Year 9 is also where the subject and science-route options are chosen.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this stage runs alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons, required in all private schools regardless of curriculum. Meydan has a high share of families in their first or second UAE year, and Arabic from a standing start is the request that most often arrives at this stage and most often pays for itself.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10
programmes.description: Nine or ten examined courses begin properly and coursework starts in the subjects that carry it. Content is still fixable here, which is the key fact: a missing foundation in algebra or the mole concept can be rebuilt without sacrificing anything else. By the spring of Year 11 the same gap is a triage decision rather than a repair job.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is also when the tier decision in tiered subjects should be evidenced rather than assumed, by sitting a timed higher-tier past paper and marking it against the official scheme. For Meydan families who arrived mid-Year 10 from another system, a syllabus audit against the school's scheme of work comes before any teaching.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11
programmes.description: The triage year. School revision sessions appear at short notice, the mock series takes a term, coursework deadlines cluster and the final weeks need two or three sessions a week in whichever subject was chosen. Technique — timing, command terms, question selection — remains fully recoverable; missing syllabus content only partly does.
programmes.countryNote: Across this corridor Year 11 carries the post-sixteen decision too, because several nearby schools offer both A Level and the IB Diploma. Leaning one way by the January mocks lets a family target the remaining months; deciding in July means choosing from whatever the results allow rather than from what was planned.

programmes.name: After Year 11
programmes.description: A Level or the IB Diploma. Both assume specific IGCSE content: A Level Mathematics and Higher Level IB maths both expect the higher-tier syllabus, and the sciences at either level expect separate-science content. The IGCSE subject and tier decisions therefore constrain the exit, usually in ways noticed after the entry deadline rather than before.
programmes.countryNote: For universities inside the UAE there is a separate Ministry of Education equivalency step: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Verify current rules on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-meydan.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Meydan students bring, each described by how recoverable it is late in the year — which is the information triage actually needs and which no competitor page provides.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Partly recoverable late. Timing, method-mark discipline and mechanical topics like circle theorems and bounds move quickly. Missing algebraic fluency does not, and a student weak there in February will be weak in June. Cambridge sets a non-calculator paper and Pearson does not, which decides what practice should contain.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Recoverable if the problem is mathematical execution — rearrangement, units, gradients — which it usually is. Not recoverable late if whole topics are missing, because the calculation-heavy content compounds. Experimental-method questions are the fastest marks and are shared with the other two sciences.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Among the most recoverable subjects late in the year, because the losses are precision habits rather than ignorance: state symbols, ionic equations, trends described rather than explained. Those are drillable in three or four sessions and apply to every paper the student sits.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: Recoverable in two ways and not in a third. Command-term accuracy and six-mark answer structure move fast. Content is learnable late because it is recall rather than compounding skill. What does not move late is a student who has never practised writing a sequenced extended answer under time.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Recoverable mainly through task compliance rather than writing quality. A strong writer who ignores form, audience or purpose loses marks no prose can rescue, and that is a one-session realisation. Timing across the reading responses is the second fix and takes about three sessions.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: The summary task carries concentrated marks and is a technique rather than a language ability, which makes it the most recoverable component. Speaking and listening are harder to move late. Register accuracy in writing matters as much as range and is the more teachable of the two.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Highly recoverable, because most lost marks are application rather than knowledge: a correct definition untied to the case scores the bottom of the band. Break-even and cash-flow calculations are reliable marks routinely skipped under time pressure, and both are mechanical.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Recoverable through diagram discipline, which is the single best short block in the subject: labelled axes, shifted curves, new equilibrium marked. Evaluation questions needing a judgement rather than a balanced list are the second fix, and together they cover most of the available improvement.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Recoverable but thinly supplied locally. Pseudocode is marked to syllabus conventions, which catches fluent Python coders who translate loosely, and trace tables are high-value and low-glamour. Both are mechanical, and both need a tutor who knows the convention rather than the language.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.levels: Extended or Higher tier students only
subjects.description: The scarcest subject in this list locally, because it is timetabled thinly in schools and taught by few teachers. Not recoverable late: it front-loads calculus and advanced trigonometry, so a student behind in February is behind in June. Worth supporting early or not at all.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Recoverable, because the skills paper is mechanical — map reading, graph interpretation, data response — and all of it is practisable in a few sessions. Extended answers need named located examples, which is recall and therefore learnable late, unlike compounding calculation skills.

subjects.name: Arabic and second languages
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules regardless of curriculum, and thinly supplied outside school at examination level. Support works within the school's own approved material, because KHDA prohibits different or additional content for mandatory subjects without Ministry permission.

sections.heading: Triage: which of nine subjects gets the afternoon
paragraphs: Nine or ten examined subjects and one clear afternoon is an allocation problem, and allocating by whichever report was worst produces the wrong answer almost every time. The right question is narrower: which subject is both at risk of a grade the student actually needs and responsive to the hours available between now and the papers.

Those are two separate tests and both matter. A subject can be at risk and unresponsive — Additional Mathematics in February, where the content front-loads calculus and a student behind now will be behind in June. A subject can be responsive and not at risk — economics diagram discipline for a student already heading for a strong grade. The afternoon belongs to a subject that passes both tests, and a parent can usually identify it from marked scripts in half an hour.

The third factor is what the grade is for. A student needing five subjects at grade 3 or above for Ministry of Education equivalency has a different floor from one needing a 7 in maths to enter Higher Level IB. The subject that matters is the one standing between the student and a specific next step, and that is a family decision rather than a tutoring one. Making it explicitly is what stops the afternoon being spent on whichever subject produced the most recent argument.

The table below sets out the triage grid as it usually resolves in this corridor. Read it with marked scripts beside it: the categories are only useful once you know whether your child's lost marks are technique, precision or missing content, and that is what a script shows and a grade does not.

sections.heading: The subjects nobody near you teaches
paragraphs: There is a real supply problem in Dubai IGCSE tutoring and almost nobody writes about it, because admitting a coverage limit looks like a weakness. It is more useful than the alternative. Maths, English and the three sciences are well supplied, because UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of Dubai's private-school enrolment and those subjects are taken by nearly everybody. Several other subjects are not supplied at all well, and a distance filter makes finding them harder rather than easier.

The thin list is predictable once you think about who teaches these subjects. Additional Mathematics is timetabled in few schools and taught by fewer teachers. Computer Science needs somebody who knows the syllabus pseudocode conventions rather than a working programmer. Economics and Business Studies at a specific board are taken by smaller cohorts. Second languages at examination level are scarce outside school. Arabic at first-language level is a specific credential rather than a general one — KHDA requires schools to ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

For a Meydan family that produces a straightforward conclusion. On the well-supplied subjects, a local tutor and an online one are both available and the choice comes down to format preference and the travel premium. On the thin subjects, insisting on somebody who will drive to Mohammed Bin Rashid City narrows a small pool to a very small one, and the practical outcome is either a long wait or a generalist with the right label.

What any provider should do in the thin cases is say so. If the subject at the level you need has nobody free this term, the right answer is a date or a straight no, with the alternative options named — a short technique block in a different subject, a weekend arrangement, or waiting. The researched competitor set in this market tends instead to promise a fast match and route enquiries onwards, and several route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without saying so.

sections.heading: Five questions for your school, before you pay anybody
paragraphs: A parent who walks into a tutoring conversation with five facts from the school gets a precise answer in one message. A parent without them pays a tutor to establish those facts during billable sessions. The five take a single email to the exams officer or head of year and they are the highest-return thirty minutes in this whole process.

First, the syllabus codes. Not the board name — the codes, such as 0580 or 4MA1, plus the tier where the board tiers. Some schools split boards between subjects, so the answer for maths may not be the answer for science. Second, which practical component the science subjects sit, because Cambridge separate sciences include either a laboratory practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper and the written one is highly coachable.

Third, the entry deadline the school is working to and whether tier decisions can still change. That date is the school's rather than the board's and it closes the decision. Fourth, the mock window and whether scripts will be returned, because a returned script is the diagnostic instrument and a grade alone is not. Fifth, the activity and revision-session calendar for the term, which is how you find the one afternoon that will still be free in March.

A sixth question is worth asking if there is any history of extra time or other support: how access arrangements work at this centre, what evidence is needed, and when the deadline falls. Those arrangements are applied for by the school as the exam centre, they are evidence-based, and the deadlines sit well before the series. No tutoring provider arranges them, influences them or should imply otherwise — but a family that discovers the deadline afterwards has lost something that was available.

sections.heading: The honest study week, counted in minutes
paragraphs: Most revision advice assumes a student with free evenings. A Year 11 student in Meydan does not have them, and the useful exercise is to count what is actually there rather than to prescribe what should be. Families who do this arrive at a realistic plan; families who do not buy an hour that was never available.

Start with the school day and the journey. Depending on which cluster the school sits in, a Meydan student is out of the house from early morning until somewhere between 15:30 and 17:00. Then homework across nine or ten subjects, which in Year 11 is not optional. Then one or two afternoons gone to sport or clubs, and in the spring term school revision sessions appearing at short notice. Then, inside the school week itself, the KHDA mandatory subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum.

What is left in a typical week is one clear weekday afternoon and part of a weekend. That is the honest budget, and the whole argument of this page is that it should be allocated deliberately rather than spread. One subject in the weekday slot, held for a term. One technique block at a time, finishing before the next begins. One weekend session for the tasks that cannot be split.

The counting exercise also tells you what not to buy. A family who counts the week and finds no clear afternoon at all should not book a weekly slot: it will be rescheduled until it stops, and they will conclude that tutoring does not work when what happened is that it was never scheduled. For that family the right purchase is a weekend block or a short technique block, and a provider who says so rather than selling a standing hour is being straight with them.

sections.heading: School revision sessions against outside help
paragraphs: Most schools in this corridor run their own revision sessions in the spring term, usually free and usually in the afternoons. For a family triaging nine subjects into one slot, the question of whether those sessions replace outside support is a real one and the answer is: partly, and in a specific way.

What a school session does well is cover the syllabus. A teacher with a class works through content in a planned sequence, and for a student whose problem is a missing topic that is exactly right and already paid for. What it cannot do is diagnose. A room of twenty students moving through a sequence cannot stop at the line where one student's working breaks, and in maths and the sciences that line is where the marks are.

So the sensible division is to let the school cover content and buy diagnosis and technique. A short block on experimental method, command terms, method-mark discipline or diagram accuracy does something the school session structurally cannot, applies across more than one subject, and finishes. For a student with nine subjects that is a better use of a scarce afternoon than paying somebody to re-cover material a teacher is covering for free three doors away.

There is a scheduling consequence too, and it catches families every spring. School revision sessions appear at short notice and take the obvious afternoons — frequently the exact afternoon a weekly tutoring slot was placed on in September. Expect it, and when it happens treat the school session as the priority and move the paid one, which online costs a message and with a visiting tutor costs a route change or a cancellation.

sections.heading: What the cheapest option actually gets you
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because for a family triaging nine subjects into one afternoon the bottom is a serious option rather than a compromise. Budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, figures read in October 2026. What it buys is a confident undergraduate with no board marking experience.

For some triage outcomes that is the correct purchase. Re-covering a single Core-tier topic, drilling arithmetic fluency, working through recall in biology or geography: an able undergraduate does those perfectly well at a third of the specialist rate, and spending more on them is waste. Where it reliably fails is anything requiring mark-scheme judgement — whether a method mark would be awarded, whether an extended answer meets a six-mark structure, whether a practical write-up answers the question asked.

Above it, a qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. An IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table giving 200 to 450 plus. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 including travel, and the premium end reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Monthly, Bestimate gives AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with published packages at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

The practical rule for a Meydan family is to match the band to the task rather than to the anxiety. Budget band for recall and fluency. Mid band for course support across a term. Specialist band for mark-scheme work, tier judgement and coursework feedback. Paying specialist rates for recall is the commonest overspend in this market, and buying budget help for a tier decision is the commonest false economy.

sections.heading: Measured in minutes: travelling against video
paragraphs: For a student with one afternoon, the comparison between a visiting tutor and live video is best made in minutes rather than principles, because minutes are the scarce resource and they can be counted.

A visiting tutor in Meydan loses minutes at both ends of the session. The journey in runs against every school run in the surrounding communities, and District One's internal roads absorb around twenty minutes before a car reaches Al Khail. A 16:00 start becomes 16:30 or 16:40 routinely. If the school bus is late, the session is short rather than shifted, because the tutor has a route to continue. And the slot cannot move when the school adds a revision session, which in the spring term it will.

What the visiting format gives in exchange is presence — a parent can see the session happening and a fifteen-year-old cannot drift — and in Year 10 that is worth something real. The market prices it at roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour above the equivalent online rate: in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. sections.heading: Coursework and the honesty line at IGCSE
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects carry coursework or controlled assessment, and the boundary around outside help is narrower than parents often assume. It is worth knowing precisely, because the consequence of crossing it falls on the student rather than on whoever offered.

What a tutor may do: teach the content and the skills, explain what the mark scheme rewards, discuss whether a chosen topic or question is manageable, and give feedback on work the student has written. What a tutor may not do: write, rewrite or edit any part of submitted work to completion, supply content for it, or produce data or results. Where a piece is produced under controlled conditions in school, the school's own rules govern what preparation is permitted and those are the rules that bind.

The practical advice is to ask the school what is allowed before arranging any support around a coursework piece, and to tell the tutor what the school said. Schools differ in how much pre-work they permit, and a tutor who has not been told will assume whatever is normal elsewhere. That assumption is where problems come from rather than from bad intent.

The same line covers materials. Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright, some unreleased, so we reference and link cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than hosting or distributing them. Your school holds licensed access. Separately, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

sections.heading: Results day, and the two exits from Year 11
paragraphs: Triage decisions made in February are really decisions about August, because the IGCSE results decide which of two post-sixteen routes a student in this corridor can take. Several schools around Meydan offer both A Level and the IB Diploma, which makes the exit a genuine choice rather than a formality — and makes the subject at the top of the triage list a strategic question rather than an emotional one.

A Level Mathematics and Higher Level IB maths both assume the higher-tier IGCSE syllabus. A Level and Higher Level sciences assume separate-science content. If either route is the plan, the subjects standing between the student and it are the ones that deserve the scarce afternoon, even if another subject's report looks worse. If neither route requires a particular subject, a secure pass in it is sufficient and spending the afternoon there is a misallocation.

There is also a floor to clear that is easy to forget in the pursuit of a ceiling. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. One ranking competitor states the requirement as six subjects; the published figure is five. For most students in this corridor that floor is cleared comfortably, but for a borderline student it is worth checking which five the equivalency five actually are.

If results do disappoint, the November series on both Cambridge and Pearson is the standard resit route for UAE candidates, and the Feb/March Cambridge route is offered to India only. Before committing to a retake, request the script rather than the grade: if the losses were timing and technique, a short block before November is realistic. If whole topics were missing, the following June is usually the honest answer and a tutor should say so rather than sell the shorter one.

sections.heading: What a free trial should settle
paragraphs: The free trial lesson is the only part of this market a parent can evaluate before paying, and for a triage decision it should be used as an assessment rather than a sample lesson. Treated as a sample, it tells you whether the tutor is pleasant. Treated properly, it settles which subject gets the afternoon.

Set it up to answer that. Send marked scripts from the two or three subjects under consideration, and ask for the session to be spent on them: mark these with my child against the official scheme and tell me which subject will respond fastest to the hours we have. A specialist will answer in method marks, command terms and mark allocations and will be willing to name a subject. A generalist will offer to help with all of them.

Then ask two more questions before it ends. How many sessions does this pattern suggest, and what would you deliberately not work on? The second answer is the more informative. A tutor willing to say that a subject is not worth the afternoon, or that a particular topic should be abandoned, is planning. A tutor proposing an open-ended weekly arrangement across several subjects is selling.

On the word free: the trial is one lesson, with no payment and no card required, and that is the whole condition. Any provider using the word should state its condition on the same screen, and in this market that is worth checking rather than assuming. Nobody can promise a grade either — not us, and not the providers in the researched set who publish outcome promises and self-asserted ratings.

process.title: Get the five facts from the school
process.description: Syllabus codes and tiers, which practical component the sciences sit, the entry deadline and whether tiers can still change, the mock window and whether scripts come back, and the activity and revision calendar. One email, and it saves paying a tutor to establish them during billable sessions.

process.title: Count the week honestly
process.description: School day plus commute, homework across nine subjects, sport and clubs, and in spring the school revision sessions. What is left is usually one weekday afternoon and part of a weekend. That is the budget. A family that finds no clear afternoon should not book a weekly slot at all.

process.title: Triage against two tests
process.description: Which subject is both at risk of a grade the student needs and responsive to the hours available? Chemistry precision and biology structure respond fast; Additional Mathematics in February does not. Marked scripts answer this in half an hour, and the answer is often not the subject with the worst report.

process.title: Use the free trial to settle the choice
process.description: One live session with no payment and no card, spent marking scripts from two or three subjects against the official scheme. Ask which subject will move fastest with the hours available, how many sessions it suggests, and what the tutor would deliberately leave alone.

process.title: Hold one subject for a term
process.description: The weekday slot stays in the triage subject rather than rotating by whichever report was worst that month. Rotating produces thin passes across several subjects and movement in none. Short technique blocks run alongside and finish, and they are chosen to improve more than one subject where possible.

process.title: Rebuild on the mock scripts, then run the final block
process.description: After mocks, sort every lost mark into content, command term, slip or timing and work only the dominant category for a fixed fortnight. Then two or three sessions a week of timed sections for a set number of weeks before the series, with a written list of topics to stop revising.

whyPoints.title: Triage before hours
whyPoints.description: Nine subjects and one afternoon is an allocation problem. We ask which subject is both at risk and responsive before proposing anything, which frequently points away from the subject with the worst report and towards the one standing between the student and their next step.

whyPoints.title: Honest about thin supply
whyPoints.description: Maths, English and the sciences are well supplied locally. Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and first-language Arabic are not. Where a subject at the level you need has nobody free this term, you get a date or a straight no rather than a generalist with the right label.

whyPoints.title: The band matched to the task
whyPoints.description: Recall and fluency sit in the budget band at AED 45 to 150. Mark-scheme judgement, tier decisions and coursework feedback sit in the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 plus. Paying specialist rates for recall is the commonest overspend in this market and we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that improve more than one subject
whyPoints.description: Experimental method serves all three sciences. Command terms serve the humanities. Method-mark discipline serves maths and physics together. For a student with one afternoon, a block that covers two or three subjects is worth more than a weekly hour in one.

whyPoints.title: Slots that survive the school calendar
whyPoints.description: School revision sessions appear at short notice in the spring and take the afternoon booked in September. Online, that costs a message to move; with a visiting tutor it costs a route change or a cancelled session, which in a commuter district adds up quickly.

whyPoints.title: No promises and no borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: Nobody can promise a grade and we do not. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none; where a provider claims one, ask for the number.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in Meydan, or is everything online?
faqs.answer: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. For this district the distance question matters less than it appears: Meydan has almost no schools inside it, so a visiting tutor would drive in against every surrounding school run, and District One's internal roads absorb around twenty minutes before reaching Al Khail. A 16:00 in-home slot routinely starts at 16:30 or later.

faqs.question: My child has nine subjects. Which one should we actually support?
faqs.answer: The one that passes two tests: it is at risk of a grade the student genuinely needs, and it will respond to the hours available between now and the papers. Chemistry precision habits and biology answer structure respond quickly. Additional Mathematics in February does not, because its content compounds. The subject with the worst report is often not the right answer. Marked scripts settle it in about half an hour, which is why the free trial is built around them.

faqs.question: Are some IGCSE subjects hard to find a tutor for in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth knowing before you start. Maths, English and the three sciences are well supplied, because UK-curriculum schools are 37% of Dubai's private-school enrolment and nearly everyone takes them. Additional Mathematics is timetabled in few schools and taught by fewer teachers. Computer Science needs somebody who knows the syllabus pseudocode conventions rather than a working programmer. First-language Arabic is a specific credential. Insisting on somebody who will drive narrows a small pool further.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school before hiring a tutor?
faqs.answer: Five things, in one email. The syllabus codes and tiers, not just the board name. Which practical component the sciences sit, because Cambridge's written alternative-to-practical paper is highly coachable. The entry deadline and whether tier decisions can still change. The mock window and whether scripts will be returned. And the activity and revision-session calendar, which is how you identify the one afternoon that will still be free in March rather than guessing at it.

faqs.question: Do the school's own revision sessions replace a tutor?
faqs.answer: Partly, and in a specific way. A school session covers the syllabus well: a teacher works through content in a planned sequence, and for a missing topic that is exactly right and already paid for. What it cannot do is stop at the line where one student's working breaks, which in maths and the sciences is where the marks are. The sensible division is to let the school cover content and buy diagnosis and technique, which also applies across more than one subject.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor ever the right answer?
faqs.answer: For some tasks, yes, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. Budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour — EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, read October 2026 — buys a confident undergraduate, and for recall, arithmetic fluency or re-covering one Core-tier topic that is the correct purchase. Where it fails is mark-scheme judgement: whether a method mark would be awarded, whether a six-mark answer meets the structure, whether a write-up answers the question.

faqs.question: How long before the exams is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is wrong rather than on the date. Technique — timing, command terms, question selection, method-mark discipline — stays fully recoverable into the final weeks because the gain is concentrated in a skill. Missing syllabus content is only partly recoverable, and compounding content such as Additional Mathematics barely at all. The trial lesson exists to tell you which case you are in before you spend, and a tutor who will not give that answer straight is booking rather than planning.

faqs.question: Should the weekly slot rotate between subjects?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most common way a scarce afternoon gets wasted. Rotating by whichever report was worst that month produces thin passes across several subjects and measurable movement in none, because each subject gets re-diagnosed rather than worked. Hold the slot in one subject for a term and run short technique blocks alongside, choosing blocks that serve more than one subject — experimental method for all three sciences, command terms across the humanities.

faqs.question: What time will a session start if we are home at 16:45?
faqs.answer: Then do not plan an hour. A student home at 16:45 should be doing 45 minutes, and the subject in that slot should be one that survives tiredness — biology or geography recall rather than physics calculation, because an abandoned rearrangement loses the back half of a question. Families on the long school run to Al Barsha, Al Quoz or Silicon Oasis generally do better with one longer weekend block and one short weekday session than with two tired weekday hours.

faqs.question: Where is the line on coursework help at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Within a narrow boundary, and the school's own rules govern it. A tutor may teach the content and skills, explain what the mark scheme rewards, discuss whether a topic is manageable, and give feedback on work the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit submitted work to completion, supply content, or produce data. Ask the school what preparation is permitted and tell the tutor what the school said, because assumptions are where problems come from.

faqs.question: What are access arrangements and when do we have to ask?
faqs.answer: They are exam adjustments such as extra time, applied for by the school as the exam centre, based on evidence, with deadlines that sit well before the series. No tutoring provider arranges them, influences them or should suggest otherwise. What matters practically is the timing: a family who raises it after the deadline has lost something that was available. If there is any history of support in school, ask the exams officer or learning support lead early what evidence is needed and by when.

faqs.question: Is it possible to support two or three subjects in parallel?
faqs.answer: One properly, plus short blocks that happen to serve others. A Year 11 week in this district yields about one clear weekday afternoon and part of a weekend, and dividing that across three subjects produces three thin passes at the same total cost as one that works. The exception is a shared technique block: experimental method improves biology, chemistry and physics together, which is why it is the best-value purchase on this page for a multi-subject problem.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost here, by task?
faqs.answer: Match the band to the task. Recall and fluency: budget online at AED 45 to 150 an hour. Course support across a term: a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Mark-scheme work, tier judgement and coursework feedback: an IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270. Monthly, Bestimate gives AED 240 to 600 budget, 600 to 1,200 mid and 1,000 to 2,000 plus for specialist exam-year support.

faqs.question: If results disappoint, is a November retake worth it?
faqs.answer: It depends on the script rather than the grade, so request the script first. Both Cambridge and Pearson run a November series available to UAE candidates and that is the standard resit route; the Feb/March Cambridge route is offered to India only. If the losses were timing and technique, a short block before November is a realistic target. If whole topics were missing, the following June is usually the honest answer, and a tutor should say so rather than sell the shorter option.

faqs.question: Does the IGCSE subject choice limit what my child can do at sixteen?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than families expect. A Level Mathematics and Higher Level IB maths both assume the higher-tier IGCSE syllabus, and A Level and Higher Level sciences assume separate-science content. Several schools around Meydan offer both A Level and the IB Diploma, so the exit is a real choice. That is why the subject standing between your child and their intended route deserves the scarce afternoon even if another subject's report reads worse.

faqs.question: What should the free trial lesson settle for us?
faqs.answer: Which subject gets the afternoon. Send marked scripts from the two or three under consideration and ask for the session to be spent marking them with your child against the official scheme, then ask which will respond fastest to the hours available. A specialist answers in method marks and mark allocations and is willing to name one subject. A tutor who offers to help with all of them has answered a different question from the one you asked.

The first lesson is a free diagnostic with no payment and no card, spent marking those scripts and naming which subject will move fastest with the hours you have.

intro.heading: What the words near me are really doing in that search
paragraphs: A search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Mirdif is doing two jobs. It is a request for speed, because something has gone wrong and the next assessment is close. And it is a proxy for trust, because near feels verifiable in a way that an online listing does not. Both are reasonable. Neither is well served by proximity, and this page sets out why, using the only measure that matters to a Year 10 or Year 11 student: what can be achieved between now and the next thing that gets marked.

The Dubai school year runs in three terms, and each has a different job. The first, from late August to mid-December, is where content is laid down and where a weak start compounds quietly. The second, from January to late March, carries the mock season and the real diagnosis. The third, from April to the end of the academic year, is the exam term for June candidates and is not a teaching term at all. For a Mirdif candidate that exam term means the June series, with November as the only other sitting Cambridge offers here; the February and March sitting is an India-only option, so any page quoting a February exam window was not written for Dubai. A tutor booked in week two of term one is doing a completely different job from one booked in week two of term three, and the plans should look nothing alike.

Mirdif sits in the eastern suburbs, between Al Mizhar, Al Warqa, Al Khawaneej and Nad Al Hamar, with the schools families here use spread across an arc out to Festival City and Academic City. Proximity within that arc is almost meaningless for tutoring: a tutor four streets away is still forty minutes from your child at 16:00, and a tutor in a different emirate is zero minutes away over video.

What near does buy is worth naming honestly, because it is not nothing. A tutor in the room reads body language, notices a phone, and keeps a fourteen-year-old on task in a way a screen does not. If that is your child's actual problem, in-home tuition is a sensible purchase and the Dubai market rate is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. IB Gram does not sell it: home visits are a service offered only in India, and UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video.

What near costs is choice and reliability. A list restricted to tutors who will drive to Mirdif for a single weekday slot is short, and in subjects like Cambridge 0620 Chemistry or 0478 Computer Science it is frequently empty. It is also fragile: one tutor, one car, one traffic incident, and the lesson before a mock does not happen. The sections below put numbers and dates against all of that.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Mirdif families ask for most, listed with the specific thing that tends to move when a term of weekly lessons is spent on it.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency first, then multi-step problem structure. The commonest recoverable loss is a correct answer with no method shown, which forfeits marks the scheme awards for working rather than for the result.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves take the most time; required practical skills are examined on a written paper. Describing a method precisely enough to score is a writing skill, not a laboratory one, and it is teachable in four lessons.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables. The tables are pure recall worth real marks and are almost always left unlearned until the fortnight before the paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides the grade more than content does. Describe, explain and suggest want different answers, and a student who writes one style for all three stalls in the middle grades.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Structure marks on directed writing are independent of ideas, so they can be secured by drilling format alone. Reading answers lose marks for long quotations with thin analysis attached.

subjects.name: Mathematics (International and Additional)
subjects.description: 0607 assumes a graphic display calculator and assesses investigation; 0606 is a harder algebraic course. Buying help for one when the child sits the other is a frequent and avoidable mistake.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus, not definitions, carries the marks. Students who learn terminology thoroughly and apply none of it sit mid-range for the whole course and cannot see why.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The theory paper is the cheapest source of marks and the most neglected. Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are drillable, and the tutor pool for this subject in Dubai is thin enough to make local-only searching risky.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source skills and case-study recall in fixed proportions. Case studies are learnable in a term; source technique takes a term and then holds, which makes the order of work matter.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum, and streamed separately for Arabs and non-Arabs. Any support must work from the school's own prescribed material rather than imported content.

sections.heading: The Dubai academic year, and what each term can actually achieve
paragraphs: Tutoring works or fails on whether the plan matches the term. The table below sets out the three Dubai terms with what each realistically delivers. The hard edge in it is the end of term two: for a June candidate, that is when teaching time ends, whatever remains unlearned. After it, the only things that move marks are technique, timing and recall.

Term one is undervalued. Nothing is at stake, the student is not frightened, and a weekly hour laid alongside school teaching compounds for sixteen weeks. It is also the cheapest time to buy: specialist tutors have free evening slots in September that they do not have in February. Families in this cluster overwhelmingly book in February, which is the point at which both the price and the availability have turned against them.

Term two is where the real information arrives. Mocks are the most accurate diagnostic a family gets without paying for it, and they are frequently misused: read as a verdict rather than as data. A marked mock sorted into content, technique and timing tells you exactly what the remaining weeks should contain, and sorting it takes an hour.

Term three is not a teaching term and should not be bought as one. A tutor still earning their fee in April is marking whole papers, drilling question order and fixing the five recurring losses the student cannot name. A tutor teaching new topics in April is spending your money on content that will not be retrievable under exam pressure.

sections.heading: What proximity buys, and what it costs you
paragraphs: This deserves a straight accounting rather than a sales pitch, because a parent typing near me has a real reason for it. An adult physically present supervises in a way a screen does not. They see the phone, the slumped shoulder, the page that has not been turned. For a Year 10 student with an attention problem rather than a knowledge problem, that is the actual service being bought, and it is worth the premium.

The premium is measurable. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Monthly packaging makes it starker: AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month advertised for four two-hour in-home visits against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. The gap is not a quality gap. It is the hour and a half a tutor spends in a car for every hour spent teaching your child.

The cost of insisting on proximity is choice and resilience. Restricted to tutors who will drive to Mirdif for one weekday slot, a shortlist for Cambridge 0580 mathematics is usable, a shortlist for 0620 Chemistry qualitative analysis is short, and a shortlist for 0478 Computer Science is often empty. It is also a single point of failure: one tutor, one car, and the lesson before a mock can simply not happen.

IB Gram resolves that by not offering home visits in the UAE at all. For a Mirdif family that means the trade is explicit rather than hidden. You give up the adult in the room, and you gain a specialist matched on syllabus code and a slot that cannot be lost to traffic. For most Year 11 students the trade is worth taking; for a distractible Year 9, the sensible mitigation is a visible laptop, a camera left on, and a parent within earshot.

sections.heading: Coverage and fallback: what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is strange, because every provider has one. A platform that always says yes is either very large or not telling you something, and the version of that which damages a student is the near-enough substitute: a general maths tutor given a Cambridge 0607 brief, or an A Level physicist handed a 0625 Core candidate in April.

Our position is stated before booking. Common subjects at common tiers are typically matched within a few working days. Thin subjects, especially Computer Science and some language combinations, can take longer, and occasionally nobody suitable is free in the window you need. When that happens we say so and you keep your money, which is a less impressive sentence than a promise and a more useful one.

The second disclosure concerns where the tutor is. Delivery is over live video, and a specialist matched to your child may be anywhere. That is the mechanism by which a Mirdif student gets a 0620 specialist at all, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. What does not vary is the time zone: lessons are scheduled to Gulf Standard Time around your child's actual week, including Ramadan and study leave.

The table sets out typical match times by subject band. Treat the right-hand column as the commitment that matters: what we do when we cannot deliver. Everything else on a tutoring site is easy to write, and most of it is written without a single number behind it.

sections.heading: Mock results are data, not a verdict
paragraphs: The most valuable document in an IGCSE year arrives free in term two and is usually read for thirty seconds. A marked mock is not a prediction. It is a list of specific losses, each with a reason, and the reasons fall into three groups that need entirely different responses.

Content not known is the group parents assume dominates and the one that usually does not. It needs teaching, it takes weeks, and it is the only group for which term two is the last available window. Technique not applied is the largest group in most scripts from this cohort: the student knew the material and answered a different question from the one asked, or wrote no method, or quoted at length and analysed nothing. That group moves in three to four lessons. Time not managed shows up as blank final questions and is a strategy problem with a strategy fix.

Sorting the script properly takes an hour and is the single highest-return hour of the year. It converts a grade on a page into a plan with named topics and a drill schedule. It also prevents the two classic mistakes: panic-buying three subjects of tutoring because the overall grade was low, and buying none because the overall grade looked acceptable while a 40 per cent component was being carried by a 70 per cent one.

A tutor's first lesson should be exactly this. If a prospective tutor is willing to start teaching before seeing the marked mock, that tells you what their lessons will be like for the rest of the term.

sections.heading: Checking whether your tutor is legally permitted to teach here
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent can check. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow for a family in Mirdif. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, so the question is a fair one to ask any independent tutor directly. And because the permit is free and takes two working days, there is no cost-based excuse for not holding one.

A separate rule catches a tempting arrangement. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document; the practical point is that your child's own class teacher, privately, is not the arrangement to seek.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and should never be described as holding regulator approval of any kind. Any provider that implies otherwise is making a claim worth checking.
