sections.heading: Grade boundaries, and why a 2 per cent gap feels unfair
paragraphs: Every IGCSE year produces the same conversation: a child missed a grade by a handful of marks, and the family wants to know how that is possible. Understanding how boundaries work changes revision behaviour, which is the only reason to explain it.

Boundaries are set after the papers are marked, per subject, per series and per tier, so they are not a fixed percentage and cannot be predicted from last year's figures. What that means in practice is that the marks nearest the boundary are the cheapest ones in the whole qualification. Three method marks recovered across a paper by writing down working is worth more than a fortnight of extra content, because content gains are spread thinly and technique gains cluster.

This is why the last fortnight should be whole papers, strictly marked. A student collecting two or three marks per paper that they were previously leaving behind is doing more for their grade than one revising another topic. The marks are already inside their head; they are being lost on the way to the page.

One more consequence. Because boundaries move, no tutor can tell you what mark your child needs, and anyone offering a target score is inventing it. What a tutor can do is name the five recurring losses on your child's scripts and remove them, which raises the mark whatever the boundary turns out to be, and does so whether the paper is sat in the June series or at a November resit.

sections.heading: Ramadan, study leave and the weeks that do not look like weeks
paragraphs: Two periods in the Dubai year break a weekly timetable, and both are predictable enough to plan for. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the household's rhythm moves to the evening. For most IGCSE students the productive window shifts to after iftar, and a lesson there is worth considerably more than the same lesson at 16:00 during fasting hours. Because delivery is over video, moving a slot by two or three hours for a month takes a message.

Study leave is the other. Once it starts, the student is at home all day, and the best use of that is not six hours of solo revision. Two shorter sessions a week moved to the mornings, sequenced so that each sits the day before the relevant paper, is a far better structure. That re-sequencing is trivial online and close to impossible for an in-home arrangement, where each visit has to be slotted around a drive.

The third disruption is the school's own revision programme, which is usually announced late and lands on exactly the evenings a tutoring slot occupies. The correct response is to move the tutoring rather than to double up, because a student doing school revision at 15:30 and tutoring at 17:30 on the same day retains very little from the second.

Planning for all three at the start of the block is better than reacting to them. We ask at the outset which weeks are already compromised, and build the lesson count around the weeks that will actually happen.

sections.heading: The sixth-form decision that IGCSE grades quietly make
paragraphs: The eastern-suburbs arc contains both British sixth forms and IB Diploma schools, so a Mirdif student genuinely chooses at 16 rather than continuing by default. That makes the shape of the grade profile matter as much as the headline. A Level entry typically wants depth in three subjects; the Diploma wants six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, and it is unforgiving of a weak subject because every subject counts.

The practical implication is counter-intuitive. A student with one weak subject and five strong ones is better placed for A Level than for the Diploma, where the weak subject still has to be taken and still contributes points. A student who is even across the board is well placed for either. That is worth knowing in Year 10, because it changes which subject is worth tutoring.

Mathematics is the subject that governs most routes. A Core or Foundation entry closes some A Level and Diploma mathematics options two years later, and a grade threshold missed by one in mathematics can redirect a whole plan. If a family in this cluster can only afford to tutor one subject properly, mathematics is usually the one with the largest downstream effect.

None of this requires tutoring, and it should not be presented as if it does. Schools in this arc have university counsellors who do this conversation professionally, and having it in Year 10 costs nothing. The only argument being made here is about sequence: decide the route first, then spend money on the subject that route depends on.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in Mirdif who can start this week?
faqs.answer: For common subjects at common tiers, usually yes, and the match is typically made within a few working days rather than the same afternoon. Thin subjects such as Computer Science or Additional Mathematics take longer and occasionally cannot be matched at all in the window you need, in which case we say so. Delivery is one-to-one over live video rather than at your address, which is what makes a fast match possible: the search is not limited to people who will drive out to the eastern suburbs.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether the tutor lives near Mirdif?
faqs.answer: Less than it feels. A tutor four streets away is still forty minutes from your child at 16:00 once the school run is moving, and over video the distance is zero either way. What proximity genuinely buys is an adult in the room, which matters for a distractible younger student. What it costs is choice: the list of people willing to drive here for one weekday slot is short, and in some subjects it is empty. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Which term is the last chance to fix something properly?
faqs.answer: Term two. For a June candidate, teaching time effectively ends in March, and term three is revision, technique and timing only, whatever remains unlearned. That makes the weeks after the mocks come back the practical deadline for anything that needs teaching rather than drilling. Families in this cluster typically book in February, which is both the most expensive point in the year and the point at which specialist tutors have the fewest free evening slots left.

faqs.question: How should we read my child's mock results?
faqs.answer: As a list of specific losses rather than a verdict. Sort every lost mark into three groups: content not known, technique not applied, and time not managed. In most scripts from this cohort the second group is the largest, and it moves in three or four lessons. Content needs weeks and term two is the last window for it. Timing needs a question-order strategy. One hour spent sorting a marked mock is the highest-return hour of the whole year, and it should be the tutor's first lesson.

faqs.question: Why can't a tutor tell me what mark my child needs for a grade 7?
faqs.answer: Because grade boundaries are set after the papers are marked, per subject, per series and per tier, and they move. Anyone quoting you a required mark is inventing it. What this means for revision is useful: marks near a boundary are the cheapest in the qualification, so recovering two or three method marks per paper by writing working down is worth more than another fortnight of content. A tutor can name and remove recurring losses; nobody can promise a boundary.

faqs.question: Do you ever turn families away?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the cases are predictable. If no specialist in your child's exact syllabus and tier is free in the window you need, we decline rather than substitute a generalist. We also push back when a family asks for a two-year syllabus to be covered in six weeks, or for three subjects at one lesson a fortnight, because neither produces a measurable change and both spend money for nothing. Declining a booking is less impressive than promising one and more useful.

faqs.question: Is my child's own school teacher allowed to tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: That is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the holder from serving students affiliated with their own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document. The practical answer for a Dubai parent is to look outside the school for paid one-to-one help.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor in Dubai is permitted?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly, because the permit is free and quick, so there is no good reason not to hold one. The MoHRE private tutor work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time via its smart app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no amount is published.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they generally should. School hours shorten, the household rhythm moves to the evening, and for most IGCSE students a post-iftar lesson is worth considerably more than the same lesson at 16:00 during fasting hours. Because teaching is over live video, shifting a slot by two or three hours for the month takes a message rather than a renegotiation of anybody's drive. We ask at the start of a block which weeks are affected and count the lessons from the weeks that will actually happen.

faqs.question: What should we do during study leave?
faqs.answer: Fewer, shorter, better-placed sessions rather than long days of solo revision. Once study leave starts the student is home all day, so morning slots open up and the block can be re-sequenced so each session sits the day before the relevant paper. That re-sequencing is straightforward over video and close to impossible for an in-home arrangement, because each visit has to be built around a journey. Whole papers under time, strictly marked, is the only content worth running in those weeks.

faqs.question: With one subject's worth of budget for a Mirdif student, which subject earns it?
faqs.answer: Usually mathematics, because it governs the most downstream routes. A Core or Foundation entry closes some A Level and Diploma mathematics options two years later, and a mathematics threshold missed by one grade can redirect a whole sixth-form plan. The exception is a student whose profile is strong apart from one subject that blocks a specific named course, in which case tutor that subject. Decide the post-16 route first with the school's counsellor, then spend on the subject the route depends on.

faqs.question: Does the Diploma or A Level suit a child with one weak subject?
faqs.answer: A Level, generally. Diploma students take six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, and every subject contributes, so a persistent weakness keeps costing points. A Level allows depth in three chosen subjects and leaves the weak one behind. A student who is even across the board is well placed for either route. Because the eastern-suburbs arc contains both kinds of sixth form, this is a real choice here rather than a theoretical one, and it is worth making in Year 10.

faqs.question: How many lessons a week actually helps?
faqs.answer: One, done properly, for a single subject across a term. Two in a week on the same subject helps during a post-mock repair block or in study leave, when there is a specific deadline to work to. More than two is rarely productive for an IGCSE student who is also at school all day, and three subjects at a lesson a fortnight each is worse than doing nothing with the same money, because none of the three gets enough contact to change.

faqs.question: What do I get in writing after each lesson?
faqs.answer: A short note naming what was worked on, the specific loss addressed and the next target. That is deliberately checkable: at six weeks you can hold it against a real marked piece of school work and see whether the named thing moved. If it has not, the plan changes or the tutor does, and we raise that rather than waiting to be asked. No grade is promised anywhere, because no honest tutor can promise one, and a named loss that disappears from a script is the measurable alternative.

intro.heading: Map the week before you buy the hour
paragraphs: The thing that defeats IGCSE tutoring in this district is almost never the quality of the tutor. It is arithmetic. A Year 11 student carries eight to ten subjects, each setting work, and the school day ends between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm. After the journey home, which from the western school cluster can run to forty minutes, and after the after-school revision classes many schools now run in the spring term, what is left is four weekday evenings with homework already in them.

Into that a worried parent often inserts two or three weekly tutoring sessions. The sessions happen, the homework does not, and by February the student is behind on the work that gets collected and marked by their own teachers. That is not a tutoring failure, it is a scheduling failure, and it is entirely avoidable by doing the sum before buying anything.

There is a second thing almost nobody checks first. Most schools serving this district run some form of free revision provision for Year 11: subject clinics at lunchtime, after-school sessions in the spring term, holiday revision days, and in several cases past-paper workshops run by the department that wrote the mock. That provision is already inside the fees you pay, it is delivered by the teachers who know the specification your child is entered for, and it is the first thing to use. Paid tutoring should begin where it stops.

What paid tutoring adds, properly placed, is three things a group revision class cannot: a diagnosis of this particular student's loss pattern, marked practice between sessions aimed at that pattern, and the flexibility to put the work in the hour your child can actually concentrate in. Those are worth paying for. A second group revision class, or a weekly hour that duplicates what the school is already providing on Tuesdays, is not.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Mohammed Bin Rashid City as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which removes the journey at both ends and lets the session sit in the hour that is genuinely free. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below map a Year 11 week, set out what the school usually provides free, and show where a paid session earns its place.

Nothing here promises a grade. It gives you a method for deciding how many hours the week can absorb and which of them will count, which for most households in this district turns out to be fewer hours than they were about to buy.

One more reason to do the arithmetic before the booking. A session that displaces school homework does not simply waste an hour; it costs the student marks with the people who will write their predicted grades and administer their entries. Protecting the work that gets collected is not a modest ambition, it is the point, and a tutoring plan that competes with it has misunderstood its own job.

sections.heading: A Year 11 week in this district, hour by hour
paragraphs: The first honest step is to look at the week as it is rather than as a tutoring plan imagines it. The table below sets out a plausible term-time week for a Year 11 student living in this district and attending a school in the western cluster, which is the commonest arrangement here. It is an illustration rather than a prescription, and the method matters more than the specific hours.

What the exercise shows is that the number of genuinely free evenings is three or four rather than five, and that the free ones are not the ones a parent expects. Monday and Wednesday are usually heaviest for homework because work set on Sunday and Tuesday falls due. Thursday is lighter. Any evening with a club, a sport fixture or a school revision class in it is gone, and in the spring term more of them have school revision classes in them than in the autumn.

The second thing it shows is where the best hour sits. For a student home at a quarter past four, the hour from half past four to half past five is the one in which they can still do timed work. After that, capacity declines steadily, and anything requiring sustained concentration after half past seven is being done badly. A session placed at eight because that was the available slot is an hour billed and largely wasted.

Use the map to find the free hour before you choose the tutor. The alternative, which is how most arrangements in this district are made, is to accept whichever slot a tutor offers and then discover over a term that the student is too tired, or that the session clashes with the school's own Wednesday clinic, or that the homework simply stops getting done.

sections.heading: What the school already provides, and what tutoring should add
paragraphs: This is the section that will save some households money, and it is the one no tutoring site writes. Most schools serving this district provide a meaningful amount of free examination support in Year 11, and it is delivered by the teachers who entered your child for the specification and who wrote the mock they just sat. It is inside the fees you have already paid. It should be the first thing used and the thing a paid session is designed around rather than duplicating.

Typical provision includes lunchtime subject clinics, after-school revision sessions in the spring term, past-paper workshops run by departments, holiday revision days, and in many cases a published revision timetable and access to practice material through the school's own platform. The quality varies, as it does anywhere, but the specification knowledge is guaranteed in a way that no external tutor's can be, because these are the people administering the entry.

What free group provision cannot do is diagnose your particular child. A revision class covers topics for a cohort; it does not notice that this student loses method marks because they work mentally, or that they answer Business Studies questions generically, or that their English route is the wrong one. It also cannot set and mark individual practice between sessions, and it cannot move to an hour that suits one family.

So the sensible structure is school provision for coverage, paid tutoring for diagnosis and individual practice. A household that does that often buys one weekly session instead of three and gets more from it. A household that skips the first step frequently pays an external tutor to re-cover ground their child's own department is covering free on a Wednesday, which is the most common avoidable waste in Year 11.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, three free evenings: choosing what gets the slot
paragraphs: With three or four usable evenings and nine subjects, allocation is unavoidable, and doing it on the basis of which grade looks worst is usually wrong. The better rule is to fund the subject where one hour a week changes the most, which is a different question and has a more useful answer.

Look first for the shared cause. Weak grades across maths, physics and chemistry are usually one problem, which is arithmetic and algebra, not three. Weak grades across English, history and business are usually writing structure. Fixing a shared cause once shows up in several grades and consumes one evening instead of three, which in a week this full is the difference between a workable plan and an unworkable one.

Then look for the subject where the loss is procedural rather than content-based. A student writing no working in maths, misreading command terms in biology or answering generically in business studies has habits that change in weeks with marked practice. A student who has genuinely not learned a year of chemistry needs teaching, which takes longer and is harder to fit into a crowded term. In Year 11 specifically, procedural wins because the time is short.

Finally, check the subject against the clock. If the one subject that needs the slot requires timed practice, it has to sit in the early window, which may mean moving a club or accepting a different evening. If it is discussion-led it can sit later, which frees the early window for something else or for a sibling. Choosing the subject and the hour together, rather than separately, is what makes a single weekly session do the work of two.

sections.heading: Mock season, and the one week that matters most
paragraphs: Year 11 mocks reshape the whole term, and a tutoring arrangement that ignores them wastes money twice: once during, when sessions compete with revision for the next morning's paper, and once after, by missing the most valuable week of the year. Both are avoidable with a decision made in advance rather than in reaction.

During mocks, pause. A student revising for tomorrow's chemistry paper does not benefit from an hour of general maths, and the session will either be cancelled late or attended resentfully. The exception is a session aimed precisely at the next paper, which can work, but only if the tutor is prepared to abandon their plan and work on whatever is sat tomorrow.

The week after results is the one to protect, and it should be booked in October rather than requested in February. For the first time there is a marked script in every subject, which means a diagnosis can be made from evidence rather than from impression. One session spent going through a script question by question with the student produces a list of named losses that shapes every subsequent hour. Nothing else in the year is worth as much.

After that, the structure that fits a crowded Year 11 is a short surgical block of four to six sessions on the named losses, finishing before the school's own final revision programme ramps up. That sequencing matters: paid tutoring should finish as free school provision intensifies, not run alongside it. Households who get this order right spend less and arrive at the series less exhausted.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards in usable weeks
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series that appears in some online revision material is offered to India only and has no place in a Dubai plan, so material quoting it should make you doubt the rest of the document. November functions as the resit route inside the same academic year for both main awarding bodies.

For a household whose problem is the clock, the useful way to count backwards is in usable weeks rather than months. Remove the weeks consumed by mocks, by coursework and non-written component deadlines, by school holidays if the family travels, and by the final fortnight when nothing new can be absorbed. What remains is a surprisingly small number, and it is almost always earlier in the year than parents assume.

On actual dates, the published record shows the pattern: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Those are past dates, cited so the rhythm is visible rather than so they can be diaried.

For anything ahead, use the awarding body's live timetable rather than a restatement, including this page's, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables and revises them. And ask the school which administrative zone your centre sits in: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and why there is less free time than you think
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For a household here the departmental commentary inside a report is more useful than the band, and it is also a free second opinion on whether a weak grade reflects the student or the provision.

The scheduling fact that matters is the mandatory UAE subjects, which run alongside IGCSE rather than instead of it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. It also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Instructional time for those subjects is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. For a Year 11 student carrying nine examined subjects as well, the effect is fewer free periods in the school day, which means more work comes home and the three free evenings this page keeps referring to are doing more than a parent assumes.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or accredited by Cambridge, Pearson or Oxford AQA, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. KHDA separately requires that school teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a question for a school rather than for a tutoring service.

sections.heading: Full weeks, deadlines and the integrity risk nobody connects
paragraphs: There is a link between an overcommitted week and an academic-honesty problem that this market never mentions. A student with a coursework or portfolio deadline tomorrow, no free evening left and a tutoring session they did not want is the student most likely to accept help they should not accept. At least one operator ranking for UAE curriculum queries sells completed assessed work at a published price, and the market for it is made out of weeks that were overcommitted months earlier.

Most IGCSE subjects are assessed entirely by written paper, which removes much of the temptation. Where a coursework, portfolio or spoken component exists, the rule is unchanged: the work must be the student's own. A tutor may explain the criteria, question a chosen focus until it is workable, teach the skills it requires, rehearse a spoken component in the specification's format, and give feedback on a draft the student has written.

What a tutor may not do is choose the focus, supply content, write or rewrite text, or hand over an example close enough to copy. We say that to the student in the first session rather than burying it, because the pressure arrives later and a boundary explained under deadline is explained too late. We also do not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the awarding body's own page.

The scheduling remedy is to leave the deadline weeks empty rather than filling them. A session that would otherwise sit in a coursework week is better moved forward, and the useful intervention is the one that happens before the work starts: a conversation about the focus, the criteria and what finished looks like, placed early enough that the student has room to do the work themselves.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the three questions we ask first
paragraphs: We ask three things before proposing anything, and all three are about the week rather than the subject. What free revision provision does the school already run, and on which days. What fixed commitments exist, including clubs, sport and music. And which evening, in your judgement, your child could genuinely work in. Parents answer the third one accurately far more often than tutoring services assume.

Then the usual information: the awarding body and specification code per subject from the examinations officer, the tier, the latest grades labelled as mock or classwork, the teacher comments quoted rather than summarised, and a photograph of a marked script if you have one. That decides who we propose. The slot decision comes first and the tutor decision second, which is the reverse of how it usually happens.

We run a free trial lesson in the hour you would actually use, not a convenient showcase slot, because the question is whether your child can work with this person at half past four on a Thursday rather than at eleven on a Saturday. Afterwards, ask for a written account of the losses, and ask whether the tutor thinks the week can absorb what they are proposing.

And the honest part. The early-evening Gulf Standard Time hours this district wants fill first, and the week after mock results is the most contested booking of the year. When the hour you need is unavailable we say so and offer a different hour, a different evening, a weekend morning, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed as such. We will also say when the answer is that the school's own provision is enough, which costs us the booking and is sometimes the correct advice.

faqs.question: How many tutoring sessions can a Year 11 week in this district actually absorb?
faqs.answer: Usually one, sometimes two for a short bounded period. A Year 11 student carries eight to ten subjects setting work, the school day ends between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the journey home from the western cluster can take forty minutes, and in the spring term several evenings have school revision classes in them. That leaves about three genuinely free evenings with homework already in them. A third weekly session does not add teaching; it displaces the school work that gets collected and marked.

faqs.question: Should I use my school's free revision classes before paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the step most households skip. Schools serving this district typically run lunchtime clinics, spring-term after-school sessions, department past-paper workshops and holiday revision days, delivered by the teachers who entered your child for the specification and wrote the mock they just sat. That provision is already inside your fees. Paid tutoring should begin where it stops, by adding diagnosis of your particular child's losses and individual marked practice, rather than re-covering topics on a Wednesday that the department covers free on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start from this district?
faqs.answer: Online, between about 3:45pm and 4:45pm depending on the school. A student at a school inside the district or in Nad Al Sheba is home by half past three and settled by a quarter to four. One travelling from Al Safa or Al Barsha is often not home until a quarter past four. With an in-home tutor add roughly forty-five minutes throughout, because the tutor meets the same school-run traffic and then the gated access at this end. Build in twenty minutes to arrive and eat before the session starts.

faqs.question: Would a tutor come to the house here, or is this all remote?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We say it plainly because near me is the phrase parents search. For a Year 11 household the gain from online delivery is the three quarters of an hour at the start of the evening, which is the part a student can concentrate in, plus a session that can move inside the same week when a mock or a fixture appears without anyone wasting a journey.

faqs.question: My child has five weak subjects. How do we choose which gets the one slot?
faqs.answer: Look for the shared cause first. Weak grades across maths, physics and chemistry are usually one problem, which is arithmetic and algebra. Weak humanities grades usually share writing structure. Fixing a shared cause once shows up in several grades and uses one evening rather than three. Then prefer the procedural loss over the content gap, because habits such as not writing working change in weeks while a missing year of content takes a term, and in Year 11 there are weeks rather than terms available.

faqs.question: Should we book sessions during the mock exams?
faqs.answer: Generally no. While mocks are running, a student's evenings belong to the next morning's paper, and a session on an unrelated subject will be cancelled late or attended resentfully. The exception is a session aimed at tomorrow's paper, which works only if the tutor will abandon their plan to do it. What should be booked, and booked early, is the week after results, when for the first time there is a marked script in every subject to diagnose from.

faqs.question: Why is the week after mock results worth so much?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only point in the year when there is marked evidence in every subject. One session spent going through a script question by question with the student converts a vague sense of weakness into a list of named losses: method marks not shown, command terms misread, a topic genuinely unlearned, time running out on the second paper. Every subsequent hour is aimed by that list. It is also the most contested booking in this district, so reserve it in October rather than requesting it in February.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session better than a weekday evening for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For whole timed papers, yes. A Saturday morning reaches a rested student, and ninety minutes of properly timed work then is worth more than two tired weekday hours, with no traffic involved at either end. The drawback is that weekend slots are easier to cancel than a weekday routine, so they work best as a bounded block before a series rather than as the permanent arrangement, with weekday evenings left for the school's own homework.

faqs.question: How should practice between sessions be set in a crowded week?
faqs.answer: In short daily pieces rather than one long exercise. A Year 11 week can absorb ten or fifteen minutes a night and cannot absorb ninety minutes on a Sunday, so a tutor who sets a long weekly task has guaranteed it competes with school homework and loses. Short, frequent, marked practice also suits the things that actually move grades at this level, which are procedural: writing working, reading command terms, keeping units, finishing the required final statement.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for UAE students, and is there a resit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE runs June and November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The February and March series seen in some online guides is offered to India only and should not appear in a Dubai plan. November functions as the resit route inside the same academic year for both. For actual dates use the awarding body's live timetable rather than any restatement, since Pearson publishes provisional timetables and revises them, and use only the timetable your school issues.

faqs.question: What timetable should we revise from, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Only the one the school issues. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A timetable downloaded online may belong to another zone entirely. Ask the examinations officer which zone your centre sits in; it is a thirty-second question that removes an entire category of risk from a crowded spring term.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education requirement affect the week?
faqs.answer: It does, and families new to Dubai underestimate it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For a Year 11 carrying nine examined subjects as well, the effect is fewer free periods, so more work comes home each evening.

faqs.question: Should we book anything during a coursework deadline week?
faqs.answer: No. Where a subject has a coursework, portfolio or spoken component, those weeks are already full and adding a session produces a tired student and a worse piece of work. The useful intervention happens earlier: a conversation about the chosen focus, the criteria and what finished looks like, placed before the work begins. A tutor can give feedback on a draft the student has written, but the draft has to exist first, and that needs protected time rather than more appointments.

faqs.question: Is school holiday tutoring worth it, or should they rest?
faqs.answer: Both, and the holidays are the most underused usable time in the IGCSE year. Three to five sessions across a holiday week, with nothing competing and a rested student, address a foundation gap properly rather than squeezing it between homework. That is not the same as a holiday revision programme filling every day, which produces diminishing returns. If the family travels, sessions follow the student, with the time zone agreed in advance so nobody is working at six in the morning.

faqs.question: What if the evening we need is already taken?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than booking a slot we cannot hold reliably. The early-evening Gulf Standard Time hours this district wants fill first, and the week after mock results is the most contested of the year. The alternatives are a different hour, a different evening, a weekend morning, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed as such. The trial lesson is free and comes first, so establishing whether a workable slot exists costs nothing.

faqs.question: What should I send so the slot survives the whole term?
faqs.answer: Three things about the week and three about the subject. The school and the time the day ends; the fixed commitments including clubs, sport and music; and what free revision provision the school runs and on which days. Then the awarding body and specification code per subject, the tier, and the latest grades with the teacher's comment quoted rather than paraphrased. A photograph of one marked script is worth more than the grades, because it shows which losses are procedural and which are content.

intro.heading: The problem is usually the week, not the tutor
paragraphs: Motor City is one of the easier parts of Dubailand for a school week, because GEMS Metropole School is inside the community and the school run is short. A Year 10 or Year 11 student here is often home by half past three, which is genuinely unusual across this corridor and changes what is possible. The obstacle is rarely the drive. It is the four other things already in the evening.

That is what a search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Motor City is really trying to solve. A weekly session is only worth paying for if it happens weekly, and the thing that stops it happening is a fixture that moves, a music lesson that overruns, a sibling's commitment on the other side of the city, or a tutor who can only offer Tuesdays at five. Consistency beats intensity in every subject on an IGCSE timetable, and consistency is a scheduling achievement before it is an academic one. Which means the first useful question is not who teaches 0620 well but which hour in your household is genuinely free in week one and still free in week eleven.

So this page starts with the week. It sets out which slots in a Dubai school week actually work, why short and frequent beats long and weekly for most IGCSE content, and how a 45-minute session changes what can be scheduled. Then it counts twelve weeks backwards from a June series, week by week, with a stated target for each — the plan a family can print and check against rather than a general promise about revision.

It also covers the part of revision that is a schedule rather than a subject: spaced retrieval. Recall content across the IGCSE sciences and humanities — chemistry test tables, biology definitions credited against specific wording, physics formulae not provided in the examination, case-study detail in geography — is held by testing at increasing intervals, not by rereading. The intervals are specific and a plan can be built on them, which is why they appear here as a table rather than as advice. A student who runs that schedule from the start of the spring arrives at the series with a block of marks already secured, and it costs under three hours of their time across the whole term.

Two practical notes before the detail. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series; Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around a March window is built around a date that does not apply. dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-motor-city.subjectsIntro: IGCSE subjects most requested from the Motor City area, each with a note on the session rhythm that suits it. Frequency matters more than total hours for about half of this list.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Short and frequent. Manipulation speed is built by daily practice with weekly marking, so three 45-minute sessions a fortnight outperforms one long weekly hour. Extended Paper 4 timing is the exception and needs a full-length sitting every second week from the mock onwards.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Mixed rhythm. Circuit reasoning needs a full session to work through properly, while formula recall and unit handling suit short frequent testing. The alternative-to-practical paper is best done as a concentrated block of four sessions inside a fortnight.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: The most schedule-dependent science. Qualitative analysis is recall content and responds to spaced retrieval at increasing intervals; moles arithmetic is procedural and responds to repetition. Both suit short sessions, so a 45-minute slot three times a fortnight works well.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Heavily recall-weighted, with definitions credited against specific wording, which makes it the subject that gains most from a retrieval schedule. Long single sessions are the least efficient way to revise it, and most families default to exactly that.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Needs length. A timed piece of writing with feedback cannot be done in 45 minutes, so a full hour weekly is the right shape here, with the writing produced between sessions and the session spent on marking it against the criteria.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Mixed. Reading comprehension technique suits shorter sessions; the summary task and any separately assessed speaking component need a full hour. Speaking preparation is almost always scheduled too late in the year to be useful.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram drill is short and frequent; the eight-mark evaluation at the end of a structured question needs a full session with a timed attempt and feedback. Splitting the subject across both rhythms is more effective than treating it as one block.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus is a writing habit and needs a full session with marked attempts. Break-even and ratio arithmetic is procedural and suits short repetition, so the same split applies as in Economics.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode in the board's own notation needs regular short practice to displace Python habits. Trace tables and number-base conversion are ideal spaced-retrieval content, and both are reliable marks that get neglected in favour of theory.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Needs both: short frequent work on identities and calculus technique, plus a longer session for multi-step problems. Students who cope with 0580 and struggle here are short on algebraic fluency, which is a frequency problem rather than a content one.

sections.heading: Where tutoring actually fits a Dubai school week
paragraphs: A Dubai school week runs Monday to Friday with the weekend on Saturday and Sunday, and the useful question for a family is not whether there is a free hour but which free hour will survive a whole term. A slot that collides with a fixture once a month is not a weekly slot; it is a three-weeks-in-four slot with the pattern broken each time, and for fluency work the broken pattern costs more than the missed session.

Motor City's advantage is early availability. With GEMS Metropole School inside the community, a Year 10 student can often be at a desk by half past four, and early sessions are measurably better for procedural work than late ones. Students commuting back from Dubai Hills, Arabian Ranches or the wider Dubailand schools are typically not available before half past five, and from the newer phases later still.

The second variable is length, and it is the one families underuse. A 45-minute session fits where an hour does not: between the end of the school day and a fixture, or after a fixture but before a reasonable bedtime. Three 45-minute sessions a fortnight is more total contact than one weekly hour and fits a congested week far better, and it is the right rhythm for most of what an IGCSE student needs.

Weekends deserve a mention because they are both the easiest and the least productive slots. Saturday morning is reliably free and reliably resented; Sunday afternoon sits in the shadow of the school week restarting. Where a weekend slot is the only option that survives the term, it is better than a weekday slot that does not — but it should be the second session rather than the only one where the subject needs frequency.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks out: a week-by-week countdown
paragraphs: Twelve weeks is the window most families actually have when they decide to act, and it is long enough to do real work if the weeks are allocated rather than filled. The plan below is the one built for a Year 11 student with a marked mock, aiming at a June series, whose content has been taught once but whose paper performance is below target. It is adjusted after the diagnostic session, but the shape holds.

The first three weeks are diagnosis and habit change. Week one reads the marked mock and names the habits costing marks. Weeks two and three install the two most expensive fixes, which are almost always writing method as it is produced and rounding once at the end rather than partway through. Those two habits are worth more than any topic revision because they apply to every question on every paper.

Weeks four to seven are content and closed skill sets: the two or three weakest topics worked through past questions, plus the alternative-to-practical block for a science entry and the start of the retrieval schedule for recall content. This is also the period in which full timed papers should begin, one every second week, because timing is a skill that needs more than a fortnight to develop.

Weeks eight to twelve are execution. Full timed papers weekly, marked against the published scheme, with the error log updated after each one and the retrieval schedule continuing underneath. No new topics after week nine: a topic started that late competes for attention with consolidating everything already learned, and the trade is almost never worth it. If Ramadan falls inside this window, the long papers move earlier and the late weeks become review and recall.

sections.heading: Spaced retrieval: the schedule that holds recall content
paragraphs: A surprising share of an IGCSE entry is recall rather than reasoning, and recall is held by a schedule rather than by effort. Chemistry's qualitative analysis tests and their observations, biology definitions credited against specific wording, physics formulae not provided in the examination, geography case-study detail, and business and economics definitions are all content a student either produces from nothing or does not.

Rereading does not produce it. Recognition — the feeling of familiarity when looking at a table — is not the same ability as reproduction, and the examination asks for reproduction. What produces it is retrieval: writing the content from blank paper, being marked for completeness, and then repeating at increasing intervals so that each attempt happens just as the memory starts to fade.

The intervals can be scheduled, which is what makes this a planning section rather than a study-skills platitude. A first attempt on the day the content is learned, a second the next day, a third three days later, a fourth a week later, then a fortnight, then monthly through to the series. Each attempt is short — five to ten minutes for a single table — and the cumulative time across twelve weeks is under three hours per block of content.

The practical implementation is that the tutor sets and marks the retrieval attempts rather than delivering them. A session is a poor use of time for something a student can do alone in eight minutes. What the session does is check the attempt honestly, identify which specific lines keep failing, and reset the interval for those lines while letting the secure ones stretch out. That is why the schedule below has a column for what the tutor does with it.

sections.heading: When the slots actually fill, and what that costs a late booking
paragraphs: Tutoring supply in Dubai is not evenly available across the year, and nobody says so. The published rate bands are the same in October and in April, but what is available at those rates is not. The 17:30 and 18:00 weekday slots across the Dubailand corridor are the most contested hour in the market, and they are taken progressively from the autumn, filling hard from February as mock results circulate.

The consequence for a family booking late is not usually a higher price; it is a worse slot, a less suitable tutor, or both. A student offered 19:30 on a Thursday when they needed 17:00 on a Monday will attend fewer sessions and get less from the ones they attend. A student offered a generalist because the specialist in 0620 Extended is fully booked is paying a specialist price for general help.

Which turns an argument about geography into an argument about timing. The family that books a weekly slot in the autumn keeps the same tutor and the same hour through to the series, and their twelve-week countdown runs on a timetable that already exists. The family that starts in March builds a plan around whatever is left, in the period when the plan matters most.

This is also why the free diagnostic lesson matters more than it looks. It costs nothing and it reserves nothing, but it establishes whether the tutor and the slot work before the contested period begins. Booking it in October for a June series is not premature; it is the cheapest insurance available in this market, and the diagnosis that comes out of it is useful whether or not you proceed immediately.

sections.heading: What a block costs, compared by shape rather than by hour
paragraphs: Comparing hourly rates across providers tells you less than comparing what a block of work costs and what it buys. A 45-minute session is three-quarters of an hour's cost, so three a fortnight is close in price to one and a half weekly hours, and for fluency work it does considerably more. That arithmetic is worth doing before accepting a quote framed as a flat hourly figure.

The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 or above for IGCSE and IB specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650. Published packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Note what the in-home package implies: four two-hour visits a month is eight hours delivered in four appointments, which cannot be short and frequent by construction. The AED 799 package for eight online sessions is the same money for twice the number of contacts, and for recall and fluency work the number of contacts is the variable that matters. That is a structural difference rather than a marketing one.

IB Gram publishes no fixed hourly rate on this page because subject, tier and urgency move it, and a quote follows the free diagnostic lesson. One context figure worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat; the tutoring block is the variable decision.

sections.heading: The dates a Motor City family should have on the fridge
paragraphs: A countdown is only as good as the date it counts to, and for an IGCSE candidate several of the relevant dates are not the examination. The entry deadline is handled by the examination centre to the awarding body's schedule and falls months before the papers. The zone timetable arrives ahead of the series. The mock window is the school's. And results day sits a long way after the final paper.

The published positions, with their sources. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and the February/March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official timetable rather than trusting any restatement.

The administrative rule to check before printing anything: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and notes that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your examinations officer knows the zone. Ask before booking travel around a date.

And the Dubai-specific variable, which almost no tutoring page mentions. Where Ramadan falls in the weeks before a June series, school hours shorten and the productive study window moves to after Iftar. Full-length timed papers should therefore be front-loaded into the earlier part of the countdown, and the Ramadan weeks used for retrieval testing, review and marking papers already sat. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing between 20:30 and 22:00 on request, at no additional cost.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will and will not claim
paragraphs: The first message should say the board, the syllabus code and the tier if you have them, which weeks remain before the series, and which slots actually survive a term in your household. Send a marked mock. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson and sends a written note within a working day naming the habits costing marks, with a week-by-week plan for whatever window remains. Nothing is charged before you read it.

Availability is deep for mainstream specifications at UAE evening slots — Mathematics 0580, the three separate sciences, English 0500 and 0510, Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450, Computer Science 0478 — and a match normally takes one to three working days. The constraint between February and the series is the slot rather than the specialist. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the tutor comes from our India-based faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking.

On materials, because it comes up. Cambridge and Pearson specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright. We work through them on screen in session and link the official sources so you can download them legitimately. We do not distribute scanned folders of marking material, which is a copyright problem rather than a service.

And the claims we do not make. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. We are not an examination centre and cannot enter a candidate; entries go through your school or an approved private-candidate centre, which sets its own fees and deadlines. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is what a Dubai training institute with premises requires, and we have no UAE office or branch. Private tutoring is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws — no fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears here.

process.title: Find the slot that survives a term
process.description: Before anything else, work out which hour in your week is genuinely free every week — not most weeks. A slot broken monthly by a fixture is not a weekly slot, and for fluency work the broken pattern costs more than the missed session does.

process.title: Match the rhythm to the subject
process.description: Mathematics fluency, chemistry recall and pseudocode practice want three 45-minute sessions a fortnight. English and essay-based evaluation want a full hour weekly. The alternative-to-practical paper wants four sessions compressed into a fortnight. These are not interchangeable.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge spent on the student's own marked work, with a written note following within a working day. Booked in the autumn it costs nothing and reserves nothing, but it establishes whether the tutor and the slot work before the contested spring.

process.title: Get a week-by-week plan, not a promise
process.description: However many weeks remain, the plan should say what each one produces and how you will check it. Habits in the first three weeks, content and closed skill sets in the middle, timed papers and retrieval in the last five, and no new topics after week nine.

process.title: Run the retrieval schedule underneath everything
process.description: Recall content is tested from blank paper at increasing intervals — next day, three days, a week, a fortnight, then monthly — in five to ten minute attempts the student does alone. The session marks them honestly and resets the interval for whatever keeps failing.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling treated as part of the work
whyPoints.description: A weekly session is only worth paying for if it happens weekly. We ask which slot survives a full term before discussing subjects, because consistency beats intensity in almost everything on an IGCSE timetable.

whyPoints.title: A countdown with checkable weeks
whyPoints.description: Twelve weeks laid out with a stated output for each and a way to verify it, rather than a general undertaking to revise. At week four you can tell whether the plan is working, which is the point of writing it down.

whyPoints.title: Retrieval scheduled, not recommended
whyPoints.description: Recall content is held by testing at increasing intervals, and the intervals are specific. The tutor sets and marks the attempts rather than spending session time on something a student can do alone in eight minutes.

faqs.question: How do we find a tutoring slot that survives a Dubai school term?
faqs.answer: Work out which hour is free every week rather than most weeks, and build around it. A slot broken once a month by a fixture is not a weekly slot, and for fluency work the interrupted pattern costs more than the missed session. Motor City has an advantage here: with GEMS Metropole School inside the community, students are often home by about 15:30 and a 16:30 start is realistic, which is unusual across this corridor. Online sessions also run to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, so a second slot can sit after an activity rather than displacing it.

faqs.question: Should we book 45 minutes three times a fortnight or one full hour weekly?
faqs.answer: For most of what an IGCSE student needs, yes, and often better than an hour. Fluency in mathematics, recall in chemistry and biology, formula handling in physics and pseudocode practice in computer science are all built by frequency rather than duration, so three 45-minute sessions a fortnight outperforms one weekly hour and fits a congested week more easily. The exceptions are English and the extended-response end of Economics and Business Studies, where a timed piece of writing and feedback on it genuinely needs a full hour.

faqs.question: What should happen in each of the twelve weeks before a June series?
faqs.answer: Week one reads the marked mock and produces a written list of habits costing marks. Weeks two and three install the two most expensive fixes, usually writing method as it is produced and rounding once at the end. Weeks four to seven cover the weakest topics through past questions, the alternative-to-practical block for a science entry, and the first timed paper. Weeks eight to twelve run weekly timed papers with a retrieval schedule underneath. No new topics after week nine, because consolidation beats coverage that late.

faqs.question: Why does rereading notes not work for chemistry test tables?
faqs.answer: Because recognition and reproduction are different abilities, and the examination asks for reproduction. Reading a qualitative analysis table produces a feeling of familiarity that does not survive a question asking the student to state a test with nothing in front of them. What works is retrieval: writing the table from blank paper, being marked for completeness, then repeating at increasing intervals — next day, three days, a week, a fortnight, then monthly. Each attempt takes five to ten minutes, and the whole schedule costs under three hours across a term.

faqs.question: Should a tutor spend session time on recall testing?
faqs.answer: Mostly not, and a provider who does is billing you for something your child can do alone in eight minutes. The efficient division is that the student runs the retrieval attempts between sessions and the tutor marks them honestly in the session, identifies which specific lines keep failing, and resets the interval for those while letting the secure ones stretch out. That turns a five-minute task into a managed schedule, which is the part a student will not maintain unsupervised.

faqs.question: When do the good tutoring slots in this part of Dubai disappear?
faqs.answer: The 17:30 and 18:00 weekday hours across the Dubailand corridor are the most contested in the market and go progressively from the autumn, filling hard from February as mock results circulate. What a late booker loses is usually not money but fit: a worse hour, a less suitable tutor, or a generalist because the specialist in that syllabus code is full. A student offered 19:30 on a Thursday when they needed 17:00 on a Monday attends fewer sessions and gets less from each one.

faqs.question: Does it help to book a diagnostic lesson months before we need help?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest insurance in this market. The free diagnostic lesson costs nothing and reserves nothing, but it establishes whether the tutor and the slot work before the contested spring period, and the written diagnosis that follows is useful whether or not you proceed immediately. Booking it in October for a June series is not premature. A family that has a working slot and a known tutor in place by February runs its countdown on a timetable that already exists rather than building one under pressure.

faqs.question: Is the AED 799 monthly online package better value than four in-home visits?
faqs.answer: For most IGCSE work, yes, and the reason is structural rather than financial. Published market packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Both deliver roughly the same total hours, but one delivers them in eight contacts and the other in four. For recall and fluency work the number of contacts is the variable that matters, and four two-hour appointments cannot be short and frequent by construction.

faqs.question: Can we do three short sessions a fortnight with a visiting tutor?
faqs.answer: Not economically. A tutor driving across Dubai spends forty to sixty minutes each way in term traffic, which is why in-home bookings normally carry a two-hour minimum — the journey has to be worth making. That rules out the 45-minute session, which is the shape most IGCSE fluency and recall work actually wants. Published in-home bands are AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: How should the twelve weeks change if Ramadan falls inside them?
faqs.answer: Front-load the long papers and change the kind of work in the Ramadan weeks rather than trying to continue unchanged. School hours shorten, afternoon concentration drops, and the productive window moves to after Iftar. So the full-length timed papers that would normally sit in weeks eight to twelve should start earlier, and the Ramadan weeks used for retrieval testing, review and marking papers already sat. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing between 20:30 and 22:00 on request, at no additional cost, and recall work suits those slots particularly well.

faqs.question: Is Saturday morning a good time for an IGCSE session?
faqs.answer: It is the most reliably free slot in a Dubai week and the most reliably resented, which is a genuine trade. Where a weekend slot is the only one that survives a full term, it is better than a weekday slot that collapses in week four. It also suits a longer session or a full timed paper, which is hard to fit on a school night. What it should not be is the only session for a subject that needs frequency, because one contact a week is the wrong rhythm for fluency and recall regardless of the day.

faqs.question: What does GEMS Metropole School being inside Motor City change?
faqs.answer: It shortens the school run, which is the single biggest scheduling variable in this corridor. Students are often home by around 15:30, so a 16:30 session is realistic, and early sessions are more productive than late ones for procedural work. It also makes three short sessions a fortnight practical rather than theoretical. Families commuting back from Dubai Hills, Arabian Ranches or the newer Dubailand phases are generally unavailable before 17:30, and from Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square later still.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will a Dubai candidate sit?
faqs.answer: June or November on the Cambridge route, and May/June or November on the Pearson route. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it and a plan built around a March window is built on a date that does not apply. What does run in March, May and October are Cambridge Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which are a different assessment entirely. Confirm the series and the entry with your examinations officer, and ask which of Cambridge's six administrative timetable zones your centre is in.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start if we are already inside the final weeks?
faqs.answer: One to three working days to match a mainstream specification, but the constraint between February and the series is the slot rather than the specialist. Mathematics 0580, the three separate sciences, English 0500 and 0510, Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450 and Computer Science 0478 all have deep cover; what may not be available is the hour you need. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the tutor comes from our India-based faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we state that before the booking rather than after it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-motor-city.closingHeading: Fix the slot, match the rhythm, count the weeks
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-motor-city.closingBody: Most IGCSE tutoring that disappoints was scheduled badly rather than taught badly. Find the hour that is free every week rather than most weeks. Match the rhythm to the subject: three short sessions a fortnight for fluency and recall, a full hour weekly for writing, a compressed block for the alternative-to-practical paper. Then count the weeks that remain and get a plan that says what each one produces. Send the board, the code, the tier, a marked mock and the slots that genuinely work in your household, and take the free diagnostic lesson while there is still a choice of hours.

intro.heading: Five kinds of answer to one search, compared properly
paragraphs: Search for an IGCSE tutor near Mudon and the results mix business models that have almost nothing in common. A tuition centre sells group classes on its own premises at its own times. A freelancer sells their own hours and nothing else. An agency sells a match and takes a margin. A marketplace sells access to a list and leaves the vetting to you. An online platform sells a scheduled one-to-one lesson. The rates differ, but so does what happens when a tutor stops answering messages.

That last point is the one families discover late. A freelancer who leaves Dubai mid-year takes the arrangement with them. A centre will move your child to another teacher, not necessarily one who knows the board. An agency with a replacement policy will find someone else, and the quality of that policy is worth more than twenty dirhams an hour on the headline rate. None of this appears in a search result, which is why this page puts it in a table instead.

Mudon adds a second variable. The community sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand, villas and townhouses across Al Salam, Rahat, Arabella, Naseem and Mudon Views, with no secondary school inside its own boundary. Students travel to Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, South View School towards Remraam, or further along Al Khail Road. Any model that requires somebody to travel therefore prices in a drive, and any model that requires the family to travel costs an evening.

The third variable is the board. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are different qualifications with different codes, different paper structures and different mark-scheme conventions, and Dubailand schools do not all use one board across the whole timetable. A tutor who is strong on Cambridge 0580 Mathematics is not automatically the right choice for Pearson 4MA1, and practice from the wrong board teaches habits that cost marks.

IB Gram sits in one of the five columns and says so: an online one-to-one model, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen by board and paper rather than by proximity. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers in India only. The comparison tables below are written to be checkable rather than flattering, and every AED figure in them is attributed to whoever published it.

sections.heading: The five provider models, compared on what matters
paragraphs: Rate is the first thing families compare and the least useful. What separates these models is cover, accountability and board knowledge. A tuition centre has premises and staff, which in Dubai means it operates under a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval and renewed annually. A freelance tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead. A marketplace usually holds neither, because it is not the one teaching.

Cover is where the models diverge hardest. If a freelancer's visa situation changes in March of Year 11, there is no replacement built into the arrangement. A centre will reassign a teacher, who may not know your child's board. An agency or platform with a stated replacement policy will propose someone else and the clock barely stops. Ask every provider the same question: what happens if this tutor becomes unavailable six weeks before the papers.

Board knowledge is the second differentiator and the least visible. A centre running a group class has to teach to a common denominator, which in a mixed Cambridge and Pearson room means teaching content rather than papers. A one-to-one arrangement can work the exact code the student is entered for. For Mathematics and the sciences, where paper structure drives technique, that difference shows up in marks.
The table below compares the five models on the terms a Mudon family can actually verify before paying anything.

One more column that never appears in a search result: who employs the tutor. In a marketplace nobody does, which means the vetting and the recourse are both yours. In a centre the teacher is staff, so the institution carries the responsibility but also sets the group size. In a managed match the platform stands between you and the individual, which is what a replacement policy actually means in practice.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the same subject, different paper
paragraphs: Parents often treat IGCSE as a single qualification, and schools rarely correct the impression because it does not matter for day-to-day teaching. For tutoring it matters a great deal. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 cover overlapping content with different paper counts, different tier names, different question phrasing and different conventions about what has to be written down to earn method marks.

The practical consequence is that past papers are not interchangeable. A student entered for 4PH1 who spends eight weeks on 0625 papers practises the wrong structure and learns to expect questions that will not appear. The reverse is equally true. This is the single most common avoidable error in self-directed revision in this city, and it is free to prevent: look at the front of any past paper the student has been given and check the code against their entry.

Tiering also differs in name and in effect. Cambridge uses Core and Extended in several subjects; Pearson Mathematics uses Foundation and Higher. In both cases the entry caps the grade, and in both cases the decision is usually made by the school late in Year 10 on the strength of existing work. A student who wants a science A Level needs the higher tier and needs the conversation early.
Ask your school for a written list: subject, board, code, tier. One message, and every subsequent revision decision gets easier.

There is a smaller difference worth knowing about: modular availability. Some Pearson subjects can be sat in a pattern that lets a student bank a result earlier, depending on what the centre offers, while Cambridge International GCSE is linear. That changes when revision pressure peaks across a two-year course, and it is a question for the school rather than for a tutor.

paragraphs: Proximity has a cash value and it is not the same for every community in Dubailand. A family in DAMAC Hills with Jebel Ali School inside the gates can plausibly use a local freelancer and a centre class, because both are close. A family in Remraam has South View School on the edge of the community and similar options. Mudon sits further from both the schools and the tuition centres, which means every travel-based model costs either money or an evening.

Count the evening rather than the dirhams. A Year 11 home at four, a centre class at six in Motor City, twenty minutes each way plus parking, and the student is back at eight having spent four hours on a ninety-minute class in a group of eight. The same ninety minutes one-to-one at home over video starts at 4.30pm and the evening still contains homework and dinner. For a household running two children on two timetables, that is the whole argument.

The visiting-tutor model inverts the problem: the family keeps the evening and pays for the drive. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, Bestimate's range being AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. From Mudon that loading sits at the upper end, because the tutor pool is concentrated around Motor City and Dubai Sports City rather than in Dubailand itself.

sections.heading: Questions that separate a good provider from a plausible one
paragraphs: Every provider in this market will say the tutors are experienced and the approach is personalised. Those sentences carry no information. What separates them is answerable, specific questions, and a provider who cannot answer them quickly is telling you something.

Ask which papers the tutor has actually marked, by code. Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and whose MoHRE service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable in the final term. Ask whether the first lesson is free and whether payment is taken before it.

Then ask two questions about honesty. What will the tutor do with a coursework draft, and what will they refuse to do. A provider who answers that a tutor gives criterion feedback on the student's own writing and will not draft, rewrite or supply text is describing the correct boundary. A provider who offers to handle it, or who sells completed work, is describing something that can cost a student their qualification.

Finally, ask for a rate with its basis: per hour or per lesson, what the lesson length is, and whether any quoted figure includes travel. In a market where published rates run from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, an unexplained number is not a price.

Write the answers down. Four providers contacted on the same day will give four different answers to the permit question alone, and the differences are easier to see on paper than in memory. Families who keep a short comparison note also find it useful a year later, when a sibling reaches Year 10 and the whole exercise would otherwise start again from nothing.
