sections.heading: Group classes against one-to-one, honestly
paragraphs: Group tuition is cheaper per student and it is genuinely better in one situation: a cohort sitting the same paper from the same board with the same gap, working through past questions together with a teacher who can run the room. IGCSE Mathematics revision in the spring term fits that description often enough that dismissing group classes would be dishonest.

The problems are structural rather than pedagogical. A group has to be assembled, and in Dubailand children from one community attend five or six different schools on three different curricula, so the Cambridge and Pearson students end up in the same room. The teacher then teaches content, because papers cannot be taught to a mixed-board group. The pace is set by the median student, which means the strongest and weakest both lose time.

One-to-one inverts all of that. The pace is the student's, the paper is theirs, and a session can be rebuilt mid-hour when a marked script shows something unexpected. It costs more per hour and, where the diagnosis is accurate, fewer hours are needed, which narrows the monthly gap more than the hourly rates suggest.

The honest recommendation is sequencing rather than loyalty: a group class for broad revision if one exists at a workable time, and one-to-one for the two subjects where the marked work shows a specific repeatable loss.

There is also a social argument for groups that deserves acknowledging. Some students work harder in a room with peers and stall in a one-to-one hour, particularly in the middle of Year 10 when urgency is low. If that describes your child, a group class is the better product for that phase, and switching to one-to-one closer to the series is a sequence rather than a contradiction.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and what each provider legally is
paragraphs: The legal shape of a tutoring arrangement in the UAE is clearer than most pages admit. An individual giving private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students.

MoHRE's own service listing is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any figure quoted to you as the penalty is unverified and should be treated as such.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal. It requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a specific authorisation issued to specific institutions, and no platform without premises should describe itself using it.

There is one arrangement to decline outright. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. If a teacher offers to tutor your child privately, that is the first question to ask them.

sections.heading: What a coursework boundary looks like in practice
paragraphs: International GCSE carries less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but where a centre runs coursework or a practical write-up, the rule is identical: the work is the student's and must be authenticated as such. A provider's position on this is the clearest single signal of how it operates, because the temptation is real and one provider in this market has monetised it openly.

What a tutor may legitimately do is teach the subject content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, ask the questions the criteria imply, critique an approach that will not work, and mark a draft the student has written against published descriptors. That is teaching, it is useful, and it leaves a student better able to do the next piece unaided.

What a tutor may not do is write, complete, produce, draft or edit the work to completion, or supply text for adaptation. The distinction is not subtle in practice: after a legitimate session the student has a list of decisions to make, and after an illegitimate one they have a better document they did not write.

Board material carries its own boundary. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to their publishers; sessions reference and link to the official pages rather than distributing copies, and nobody has access to unreleased material whatever is claimed.

Say it out loud to the student as well as the provider. Offers of completed work circulate in student groups more than in parent groups, and a teenager who has been told clearly why an unauthenticated document is worthless is better protected than one who has only been told to work hard. The consequence is not a lower mark; it is a qualification put at risk.
bullets: Permitted: content teaching, criterion explanation, approach critique, marking the student's own draft
Prohibited: writing, drafting, completing, editing to completion or supplying text
After a legitimate session the student has decisions to make, not a better document

process.title: Get the board list in writing from school
process.description: Ask for subject, board, code and tier for every IGCSE entry. One message to the school, and every revision decision afterwards becomes concrete. It also prevents the most common waste in this market, which is eight weeks of past papers from the wrong board.

process.title: Decide which model you are actually buying
process.description: Centre class, freelancer, agency match, marketplace listing or online one-to-one are different products with different failure modes. The comparison table on this page is there to be used before you contact anybody, including us.

process.title: Send one marked script and the codes
process.description: A marked past paper or mock, plus the syllabus codes, is enough to propose something specific. Without them any proposal is generic, and a generic proposal is how families end up paying for hours that were never aimed at the actual loss.

process.title: Use the free trial as the test
process.description: A trial lesson over live video at no cost, before any payment, with the student doing most of the talking. The question afterwards is simple: did the tutor identify something specific about how the marks are being lost. If not, ask for a different tutor.

process.title: Fix the slot and review monthly
process.description: Sessions sit on Gulf Standard Time around the school run, and because nobody is driving they can move within the evening or shift after Iftar during Ramadan at no cost. The plan is reviewed against the school's deadlines every few weeks rather than running unchanged to the series.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is published, not implied
whyPoints.description: Most providers in this market compare themselves to an unnamed alternative. This page names five models, including its own, and compares them on rate, permit position, cover and board specificity, with every rate attributed to whoever published it.

whyPoints.title: Board and code are fixed before the first session
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different conventions. Confirming the code per subject costs one message and prevents the single most common revision error in Dubai.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price and none in the evening
whyPoints.description: From Mudon, a centre class costs most of an evening and a visiting tutor costs a travel loading inside the hourly rate. An online session starts when the student sits down, which is why the slot can move when a bus runs late.

whyPoints.title: The permit question is answered, not dodged
whyPoints.description: Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition permit; centres with premises need a KHDA Educational Services Permit. IB Gram holds no regulator permit and says so, rather than attaching a regulator's name to its tutors as several competing pages do.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help has a stated limit
whyPoints.description: Criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own draft are teaching. Writing, drafting and editing to completion are not, and are refused. One provider in this market sells completed assessed work outright, which is the thing this boundary exists to rule out.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: Some subject and board combinations have thin availability, and you are told with a timescale rather than matched to a generalist. The free trial exists so the match is tested before money moves rather than after.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tuition centre inside Mudon itself?
faqs.answer: Not a secondary tuition centre serving IGCSE in the way families ask about. The centres advertising to Dubailand are mostly based around Motor City, Dubai Sports City and Al Barsha South, which means a round trip at peak time for a ninety-minute group class. The practical cost is the evening rather than the fee: a Year 11 home at four can lose four hours to a class that lasted ninety minutes. IB Gram's alternative is a one-to-one lesson over live video that starts when the student sits down, with no travel on either side.

faqs.question: Which is better value, a centre class or a one-to-one session?
faqs.answer: A centre class is cheaper per hour and is genuinely good where the whole room sits the same paper from the same board with the same gap, which happens most often in spring-term Mathematics revision. Where the room mixes Cambridge and Pearson students, the teacher has to teach content rather than papers, and the pace follows the median student. One-to-one costs more per hour, works the exact code the student is entered for, and usually needs fewer hours, which narrows the monthly difference more than the headline rates suggest.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a freelance tutor in Dubai is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Should a Mudon family care which of the two IGCSE boards their school uses?
faqs.answer: Not for the quality of the qualification, but enormously for tutoring. Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 cover overlapping content with different paper counts, tier names, question phrasing and conventions about the working that earns method marks. Practice from the wrong board teaches a student to expect questions that will not appear. Check the code on the front of any past paper against the school's entry list. Several Dubailand schools use different boards for different subjects, so one answer for the whole timetable is usually wrong.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor leaves Dubai halfway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Ask every provider this before you commit, because the answers differ sharply. A freelance arrangement simply ends, which is the single biggest risk in the cheapest tier. A centre reassigns a teacher who may not know the board. With IB Gram a replacement tutor is proposed and a free trial lesson applies again, so you are not paying to discover whether the new match works. The question is worth asking in writing rather than verbally, because the answer tells you what you are actually buying.

faqs.question: Are marketplace listings with US dollar prices a problem for a UAE family?
faqs.answer: They are a sign to read carefully. Two of the most visible pages in this market quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in, and some route enquiries to non-UAE phone numbers. Neither is illegal, but both make comparison harder and both suggest the page was not written for this market. Ask for a rate in AED, per hour or per lesson, with the lesson length stated and travel either included or excluded explicitly. In a market where published rates run from AED 33 to AED 650, an unexplained number is not a price.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both Physics and Chemistry for a Year 11?
faqs.answer: Often yes at IGCSE level, and it has advantages: shared calculation technique, shared graph skills and one review conversation instead of two. The question to ask is which papers they have marked in each subject rather than whether they can cover both. Where the two subjects sit with different boards, which happens in this belt, confirm that the tutor is comfortable with both sets of conventions. If the honest answer is that one subject is a stretch, two tutors is the better arrangement and costs the same per hour.

faqs.question: We are already in the spring term of Year 11. Is starting now worth it?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but it changes what is possible. With a term to go, technique moves: working shown, timing, command-term reading, equations balanced with state symbols, graphs drawn as the question specified. Those are habits and they respond to drilling. Rebuilding two years of absent foundations does not happen in a term, and a provider who says otherwise is selling. The way to tell which situation you are in is a marked mock script, which separates scattered small losses from whole questions abandoned.

faqs.question: Do group classes exist for Pearson Edexcel specifically in this area?
faqs.answer: They exist but they are harder to find than Cambridge groups, because Cambridge is more widely used across Dubai schools and a centre fills a Cambridge room faster. That is precisely why mixed-board groups form: the centre needs the numbers. If your child sits Pearson and the only available group is mixed, you are paying for content teaching rather than paper technique. Ask the centre directly which codes the room is working from, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

faqs.question: How many subjects is it sensible to tutor at once from Mudon?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. Three subjects at one hour each is three hours of input and three sets of homework, which usually means none of them gets practised properly between sessions. The better sequence is one or two subjects chosen by where the marked scripts show the largest recoverable loss, run properly, then reassessed. Splitting one hour across three subjects helps nobody. Where a student genuinely needs several, a split week with clear priorities works, but it should be a deliberate choice rather than a default.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre in Dubai need its own licence?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a different authorisation from a tutor's permit. A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That permit belongs to institutions with physical premises. IB Gram has no premises in the UAE and holds no such permit, which is why it never describes itself with a regulator's name attached.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with my daughter's coursework draft?
faqs.answer: With her own draft, yes, as teaching and feedback. A tutor can explain what the assessment criteria reward, ask the questions the criteria imply, say that an approach will not produce what the task needs, and mark her writing against the published descriptors. A tutor must not write, draft, complete or edit the work to completion, or supply text for her to adapt. The test is simple: after a legitimate session she has a list of decisions to make, not a better document she did not write.

faqs.question: Are tutors in Remraam easier to find than tutors for Mudon?
faqs.answer: Slightly, for travel-based models, because South View School sits on the edge of Remraam and tutors who work with its students are already nearby. For Mudon the nearest school is outside the community in every direction, so a visiting tutor is driving from Motor City or Dubai Sports City and the quote reflects it. For an online arrangement the two communities are identical, because the pool is defined by subject and board rather than by distance. That is the whole reason the recommendation does not change between them.

faqs.question: What should the first session cover if we start now?
faqs.answer: A marked script, read properly. The first hour should separate four things that feel identical to a student: content never learned, technique that lost earned marks, timing collapse visible as an abandoned final page, and misreading caused by skipping a command term. Each has a different fix and a different timescale. By the end of the hour the student should be able to state their own error pattern in one sentence, and the next fortnight should be planned against it and retested. A first session that only sets homework has wasted itself.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-mudon.closingHeading: Compare the models, then test one for free
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-mudon.closingBody: The useful order from Mudon is: get the board, code and tier list from school; decide which provider model you are actually buying; then test one with a free trial lesson before any payment is taken. Send the codes and one marked script and the trial can be arranged with a tutor who works that board. If the lesson does not identify something specific about how the marks are being lost, ask for a different tutor. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; home visits are a service IB Gram offers in India only.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Muhaisnah IGCSE enquiries teach to a named syllabus code and are priced by their specialism rather than by how far they would have to travel to reach you.

intro.heading: The numbers first, then where the money leaks
paragraphs: Almost every IGCSE tutoring page in this market refuses to publish a price. The research behind these pages found that three of the six strongest-ranking competitor pages quote no figure at all, and that the two which do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. One agency's own frequently-asked-questions section asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. So the first thing this page does is put the dirham figures on the screen, attributed, with the month they were collected.

Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most Muhaisnah families start. Budget online provision, generally university students or recent graduates, is published from AED 45 to 65 by one Dubai content-led provider and from roughly AED 33 to 52 by a regional platform. That tier buys content help and homework supervision. It does not reliably buy somebody who knows what Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 looks like or why a student is losing presentation marks on a graph.

The next band up is where most IGCSE tutoring actually transacts. Qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with one Dubai agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted higher, roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel built in: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts the range at 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise 200 to 500. Specialists in IB, IGCSE and A Level run AED 200 to 450 and above, with one UK agency publishing AED 270, and a premium examiner-branded provider publishing AED 650.

Monthly, the published packages tell the same story from a different angle: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are the brackets a Muhaisnah family is choosing between, and the gap between the top and bottom of them is a factor of eight.

Which is why the second half of this page is about waste rather than price. A factor of eight in the rate does not produce a factor of eight in the result, and the families who get least for their money in this catchment are rarely the ones who paid least per hour. They are the ones who bought three subjects at once, or started in March, or paid for a tutor teaching the wrong syllabus code, or kept a slot the school run had already killed. Each of those is avoidable and none of them is about the rate.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.programmesIntro: Cost per grade varies enormously by stage, and the cheapest intervention is almost always the earliest one. Here is how the spend behaves across a British-curriculum school career in this catchment.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: No external examination, which makes this the cheapest and least popular time to buy support. Rates sit at the lower end of every published band because the content is less specialised. A gap in algebraic manipulation or written structure fixed here costs a fraction of what the same gap costs once it is carrying an IGCSE grade.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Muhaisnah families buy tutoring at this stage, and the ones who do spend less overall across the five years than those who start in Year 11. Slots are also easier: a Year 8 can genuinely manage a 5.30pm session, which a Year 11 in this catchment usually cannot.

programmes.name: Year 10
programmes.description: The first IGCSE year, and the point where tiering decisions in mathematics and the sciences are made or confirmed. Rates are mid-band because the specialism required is real but the pressure premium has not arrived. The work available here is foundational rather than remedial, which is why it moves grades more cheaply.
programmes.countryNote: This is where we would advise a Muhaisnah family to spend if they are going to spend at all. One subject, one weekly slot through the autumn and spring, costs less than a Year 11 intensive and has a larger effect, because the tier decision it influences sets the grade ceiling.

programmes.name: Year 11
programmes.description: The examination year, when demand peaks and so do rates at the specialist end. Published monthly estimates for specialist exam-year support run AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for a weekly hour. The work is necessarily narrower: technique, pacing and paper structure rather than new content, because there is no time for foundations.
programmes.countryNote: Most families in this catchment start here, which is why most of them pay more per grade than they needed to. Weekday slots are also scarce by January because school revision clinics have taken them, so Year 11 bookings frequently end up at 7.30pm or on Saturday mornings.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Specialist rates apply throughout, and the hours required per subject are higher than at IGCSE because the independent practice load roughly doubles. Published specialist bands of AED 200 to 450 and above are the realistic planning figure, with examiner-branded provision higher still.
programmes.countryNote: Sixth-form students in eastern Dubai often have free periods, which opens up morning and early-afternoon slots nobody competes for. That is worth money: an uncontested slot is easier to keep, and a slot that is kept for twenty-eight weeks is worth more than a better-timed one that collapses.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.subjectsIntro: Cost per grade is not uniform across subjects. These are the IGCSE courses Muhaisnah families ask about, with a note on where the hours actually go.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Extended
subjects.description: The most commonly tutored subject in this catchment and among the most efficient per hour, because the losses are specific and diagnosable. Unlabelled working, bearings taken from the wrong reference, transformations described without being named. A term of weekly work usually shows.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Core
subjects.description: Cheaper to support than Extended and often better value, because the grade ceiling makes the target clear. The question worth asking before spending is whether the tier itself is right, which the school decides and which no amount of tutoring overrides late.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The most requested science from this catchment and the one where hours multiply fastest, because electricity and waves both need rebuilding when they go wrong. Expect a longer block here than in mathematics for the same grade movement.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and electrolysis absorb time; organic families are quick wins by comparison. A student who can write equations but cannot explain a trend is a two-month job, not a two-week one, and pricing a block honestly means saying so.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Deceptively cheap to support because the content feels familiar, and the marks sit in command-term discipline rather than knowledge. Often the fastest grade movement available per dirham spent, provided the tutor works on answer shape rather than content coverage.

subjects.name: Coordinated or Combined Science
subjects.description: One booking covering three sciences looks economical and frequently is not, because the weak strand still needs its own attention. Establish which of the three is costing the grade before buying hours across all of them.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and unseen analysis. Among the best value per hour for students who speak another language at home, because the fixable issue is usually structure and planning rather than vocabulary, and structure teaches quickly.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Expensive to tutor badly and efficient to tutor well. Hours spent re-reading texts are wasted; hours spent on integrating quotation into argument and writing about language rather than plot move bands. Ask any tutor which of those they plan to do.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Evaluation technique is the whole game in the spring of Year 11, and it is a narrow, teachable skill. Four to six sessions aimed at eight-mark question structure is usually a better purchase than a term of content coverage.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are drillable in a handful of sessions, which makes targeted work unusually good value. Open-ended programming practice is not what the paper rewards, so a tutor proposing project work is spending your money on the wrong thing.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study recall with figures attached, and in History provenance reasoning on sources. Both reward short, frequent work over long blocks, so a weekly hour across two terms outperforms an intensive in the final month.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Specialist rates apply and fewer tutors cover it properly. Before buying hours, establish whether the entry is appropriate at all, because a student entered late for 0606 may be better served by consolidating 0580 Extended.

sections.heading: Published Dubai rates in AED, cheapest tier first
paragraphs: Here is the market, ordered from the bottom up, so you can see where your budget actually sits rather than being anchored by a premium headline. Each row carries the provider or rate table that published the figure and the indicative monthly cost of one session a week at that rate. All of it was collected in October 2026 and all of it belongs to the provider named, not to IB Gram.

The jump that matters is between the first and second rows. Moving from the budget tier to a qualified subject tutor roughly triples the hourly rate, and it is the only step in the table that reliably changes what happens in the lesson. The steps above it buy scarcity, brand and sometimes examiner experience; they do not automatically buy a better teacher for a Year 10 student who cannot plot a graph to scale.

Note what the in-home row contains. The AED 180 to 500 band includes the tutor's travel, so part of what you are buying is a drive to Muhaisnah through the Al Ittihad Road peak. If you are comparing it against the qualified online row, the honest comparison is between AED 150 to 300 and AED 180 to 500 for the same teacher quality, and the difference is logistics rather than teaching.

On our own pricing: IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages, and we are explicit about why. The right figure depends on subject, tier, cadence and whether the work is a weekly slot or a bounded block, and a single number would be misleading for most of the families reading it. We sit in the qualified-specialist part of this table rather than the budget part, the trial lesson is free, and the figure is agreed at the consultation before anything is charged.

sections.heading: Five ways families in this catchment overspend
paragraphs: None of these is about the rate, and all five are common enough that we see them every intake. First, buying three subjects at once. A Year 11 carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies has very little slack, and three tutored hours a week usually produces three mediocre efforts rather than one good one. The cost is tripled and the effect is often smaller.

Second, starting in March. By the spring of Year 11 the content window has closed, the available work is technique only, and the specialist slots are gone. The identical intervention bought in the previous autumn costs less per hour, has more to work with, and does not compete with the school's own revision programme. Families who start late are buying a worse product at a higher price.

Third, paying for the wrong syllabus. A tutor teaching Cambridge 0580 to a student entered for Pearson 4MA1 is not useless, but a material share of the final weeks is about paper structure and formula provision, and that part is wasted. Establish the code before the first booking, from the school rather than from the student.

Fourth, keeping a slot the school run has already killed. A 4.30pm booking that the student arrives late and flustered to delivers perhaps forty useful minutes out of sixty, every week, and the family pays for all sixty. Fifth, paying for homework supervision at a specialist rate. If what your child needs is somebody sitting with them while they work, that is a real need and it is available far cheaper than a subject specialist; the two are different purchases and conflating them is expensive.
bullets: Three subjects at once: triple cost, usually less effect than one done properly

sections.heading: Hourly, monthly package or bounded block: the same money, bought differently
paragraphs: How you buy changes the real cost more than most families expect, and the published packages in this market are not comparable without doing arithmetic. An AED 799 monthly package of eight online sessions works out around AED 100 a session, which looks excellent until you ask how long a session is and what happens to unused sessions at the end of the month. A high hourly rate with no commitment can be cheaper in total if the engagement is short and bounded.

The table sets out the structures on offer in this market, what each really costs across a term, and the question to ask before signing. The recurring trap is the monthly package with expiring sessions: a Dubai family will miss sessions, for school trips, travel over Eid, and illness, and a package that does not roll over converts missed lessons into pure cost.

The second trap is the discount for volume bought upfront. Twenty hours purchased at a lower rate is a saving only if all twenty hours are the right hours. Buying twenty before you know whether the match works is how families end up persisting with a tutor they would otherwise have changed in week two, which is the most expensive outcome in this entire page.

Our own structure is deliberately dull: start with a free trial, then a weekly slot with no upfront block, reviewed at session six. If you want a bounded intensive before a series, that is quoted as a block with a fixed start and end so the total is known in advance. We do not sell expiring session bundles, and we would rather you kept the right to leave at session two than bought a discount that makes leaving expensive.

sections.heading: Tutoring in context: what else a Muhaisnah family is already paying
paragraphs: A tutoring decision is never made in isolation. It sits on top of school fees, transport, uniform, exam entry and whatever else the year demands, and the useful question is not whether tutoring is expensive in the abstract but whether it is the best available use of the next AED 1,000 in this particular year. Framing it that way changes what families buy, usually for the better.

One piece of good news on the backdrop: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family with two children in private school, a flat fee year is a meaningful change in what is available for everything else.

The table below puts tutoring configurations alongside each other in monthly and annual terms so the comparison is concrete. It deliberately does not invent school fee figures: those vary enormously by school and KHDA publishes them per school, so look up your own. Exam entry costs as a private candidate likewise vary by centre and should come from your school's exams officer or the centre directly rather than from any tutoring page.

What the table tends to show families in this catchment is that the realistic choice is not between tutoring and no tutoring. It is between one subject supported properly for two terms and three subjects supported thinly for one, at a similar total. The first produces evidence you can act on. The second produces a feeling that something was done.

sections.heading: One-to-one, small group or tuition centre: what you give up at each price
paragraphs: The cheapest way to reduce an hourly rate is to share it, and in this catchment that usually means a small group or a tuition centre class. Both are legitimate and both cost something other than money. Knowing what is being given up makes the decision honest rather than purely financial.

In a group of four, the teaching is aimed at the group's modal difficulty. For a student whose problem is the same as everybody else's, that is efficient and the saving is real. For a student losing marks for an idiosyncratic reason, which is most students by Year 11, group teaching addresses somebody else's problem at a quarter of the price. The marginal value of the hour drops much faster than the rate does.

A tuition centre adds structure, a fixed timetable and premises, and for some families that structure is exactly what was missing. Note that a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. A centre should be able to evidence that; an individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead.

Our position is that one-to-one is the right purchase when the problem is specific, and that we would rather tell a family their child's difficulty is generic and a group would serve them better. The table sets out the trade-offs so you can judge. What we would avoid in all cases is a group sold at a one-to-one price, which does exist in this market and is the worst value available.

sections.heading: The extras that are not in the hourly rate
paragraphs: Ask about these before the first session, because each one has caught families in this catchment. Session length: an hour is not always sixty minutes, and a fifty-minute hour at AED 250 is a different rate from the one quoted. Travel for in-home work: usually included in the band but not always, and a tutor quoting AED 200 plus travel is quoting a different number from one quoting AED 250 inclusive.

Materials and past papers. A tutor should be using the board's own published papers and syllabus documents, which are freely available through the school or the board's site, and should be linking you to them rather than selling a pack. We will not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. Referencing and linking is the correct approach and it costs nothing.

Marking and feedback between sessions. Some providers include it, some charge for it, and some do not do it at all. It matters: a written task marked before the next session is most of what makes a weekly slot work, and a tutor who only teaches inside the hour is selling you half the product. Ask explicitly whether work set between sessions is marked and by whom.

Finally, cancellation terms and VAT treatment. Agree the notice period in writing before you start, because a Dubai family will need to move sessions. On tax: we will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion on a tutoring page. What any provider should tell you plainly is whether the price they quoted you includes VAT, and you are entitled to ask.

sections.heading: How long before a spend can fairly be judged
paragraphs: Six sessions, measured against something agreed in advance. Any shorter and you are judging rapport; any longer and you are paying to postpone a decision. What makes six sessions sufficient is naming the target at the start in terms you can check from the student's own marked work, rather than in terms of a feeling or a predicted grade.

Good targets for IGCSE are narrow and mechanical. Tabulating and plotting a data set without losing presentation marks. Structuring an eight-mark evaluation so it reaches a judgement rather than listing two sides. Completing a Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 section in the time allowed. Each of those is visible in a marked script, and either it has happened or it has not.

Bad targets are the ones most tutoring is sold against: improve in maths, build confidence, cover the syllabus. Confidence is a consequence rather than a purchase, and syllabus coverage is the school's job. If a provider will not commit to a checkable six-session target, you have no way to evaluate the spend and you will end up renewing out of uncertainty, which is precisely the behaviour the vague target produces.

If the target has not moved at session six, the correct response is to change something rather than to add hours. Usually it is the tutor or the diagnosis. Occasionally it is the conclusion that tutoring was not the lever, and the honest recommendation is the school's own provision, a conversation with the subject teacher about tiering, or simply more sleep. We would rather give that advice and lose the booking than take a seventh payment for an hour we do not believe in.

sections.heading: What a free trial should and should not mean
paragraphs: Free trials are near-universal in this market and they vary wildly in what they actually are. The version worth having is a full-length one-to-one session with the tutor who would teach your child, in the slot you intend to use, with no card details taken and no obligation afterwards. Anything less is a sales call with a different name.

Watch for three substitutions. A twenty-minute assessment rather than a lesson, which tells you nothing about how the person teaches. A session with a consultant rather than the tutor, so the person you meet is not the person who turns up in week two. And a trial that requires payment details upfront with a cancellation window, which is a subscription with a trial period attached and should be described as one.

There is a related rule we hold to on these pages: nothing described as free should carry an unstated condition. If a trial requires a minimum booking afterwards, that has to be said on the same screen as the word free, not in terms linked from the footer. We say it here because the research behind these pages found several providers in this market doing the opposite.

Use the trial properly and it is the most valuable thing in this entire page, because it is the only part that costs nothing and tells you the most. Ask the tutor to describe the papers for your child's syllabus code. Ask what they will not do with coursework. Ask what your child should be able to do in six sessions. Then ask your child, afterwards and alone, whether the hour was useful. A fifteen-year-old's verdict on that question is unusually accurate.

process.title: Set the budget before the shortlist
process.description: Decide what the next AED 1,000 is for this year, then look at the rate table and see which tier it reaches. A family that picks a tutor first and a budget second almost always ends up buying thinner support across more subjects than it intended.

process.title: Send the syllabus code and the marked work
process.description: The board and code from the school, not the student, plus the most recent marked paper. A specialist reads more from one marked script than from a paragraph of description, and it prevents the commonest waste in this market: paying for the wrong syllabus.

process.title: Pick one subject and one checkable target
process.description: Name the narrow capability that should exist by session six, in terms visible in a marked script. Plotting without losing presentation marks, or an eight-mark evaluation that concludes. Vague targets make the spend impossible to evaluate later.

process.title: Use the free trial as a test, not a formality
process.description: A full lesson with the actual tutor in the slot you intend to keep, nothing charged. Ask them to describe your child's papers, ask what they will refuse to do with coursework, then ask your child privately whether the hour was useful.

process.title: Review at session six and decide, not drift
process.description: Look at the marked work against the target. Continue, change the tutor, change the diagnosis or stop. Renewing because you are unsure is the single most expensive habit in this market and a clear target at the start prevents it.

whyPoints.description: Every dirham amount on this page names the provider or rate table that published it and the month it was collected. Three of six strongly ranking competitor pages in this cluster publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not what a Dubai family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: No expiring session bundles
whyPoints.description: A monthly package with sessions that do not roll over turns a school trip or a week of travel into pure cost, and Dubai families miss sessions. We run a weekly slot with no upfront block, or a bounded block with a fixed start and end so the total is known.

whyPoints.title: We will say when a cheaper option is better
whyPoints.description: If a child's difficulty is generic, a small group or the school's own revision clinic serves them better than one-to-one at a specialist rate. If what is needed is homework supervision, that is a different and far cheaper purchase. Both conversations cost us revenue.

whyPoints.title: Travel is not priced into the lesson
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means you are paying for teaching rather than for a drive through the Al Ittihad Road peak. The in-home band of AED 180 to 500 includes that journey, and from a Muhaisnah address the journey is a substantial part of what the premium covers.

whyPoints.title: Six sessions, one checkable target
whyPoints.description: We agree in advance what should be true by session six in terms visible in the student's own marked work, and we review it. A spend that cannot be evaluated gets renewed out of uncertainty, which is how families in this catchment end up spending the most for the least.

whyPoints.description: Past papers and syllabus documents are linked from the board rather than sold as a pack, we publish no self-asserted ratings or student statistics, and we claim no approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education or any examination board.

faqs.question: What is the going rate for an IGCSE tutor around Muhaisnah?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates span a factor of eight. Budget online provision starts at roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour depending on the provider. Qualified subject tutors working online sit around AED 150 to 300, with one Dubai agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and a premium examiner-branded provider publishes AED 650. Those figures belong to the providers named, collected in October 2026. The step that changes the lesson is from the budget tier to the qualified tier.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutor in this market a false economy?
faqs.answer: Not always, and it depends what you actually need. If the requirement is homework supervision and someone to keep a Year 9 student on task, the budget tier does that and paying specialist rates for it is waste. If the requirement is moving a Year 11 Extended mathematics grade, the budget tier generally cannot describe the papers, which is most of what the final months are about. The expensive mistake is not buying cheaply; it is buying the wrong category. Decide which of the two problems you have before comparing rates.

faqs.question: What does a monthly tutoring package work out to per session?
faqs.answer: An AED 799 monthly package of eight online sessions, as published in this market, works out around AED 100 a session, which is well below the qualified-tutor hourly band. Two questions decide whether it is genuinely cheaper. How long is a session, because fifty minutes is not an hour. And do unused sessions roll over, because a Dubai family will miss some for school trips, travel and illness. A package with expiring sessions converts every missed lesson into pure cost, and that is where the apparent discount goes.

faqs.question: Where do families in eastern Dubai waste the most money on tutoring?
faqs.answer: Five places, none of them the hourly rate. Booking three subjects at once, which triples the cost and usually produces three thin efforts. Starting in March, which buys a worse product at a higher price. Paying for a tutor teaching the wrong syllabus code. Keeping a slot the school run has already defeated, so sixty minutes are paid for and forty delivered. And paying specialist rates for homework supervision, which is a genuine need available far more cheaply. Each is avoidable before the first session.

faqs.question: Should we buy twenty hours upfront to get the discount?
faqs.answer: Only after you know the match works. Bulk hours at a lower rate are a saving if all of them are the right hours, and a trap if they are not, because they make leaving expensive and families persist with a tutor they would otherwise have changed in week two. That is the costliest outcome available. The sensible order is a free trial, then a small number of sessions, then a review at session six against a stated target, and only then a longer commitment if you want one.

faqs.question: How much should a Year 11 family in Muhaisnah expect to spend across the year?
faqs.answer: Using the published bands, one hour a week with a qualified online tutor across a thirty-week year lands at roughly AED 4,500 to 9,000, and specialist exam-year support at roughly AED 7,500 to 15,000 or more. Four two-hour in-home visits a month works out near AED 12,000 to 13,500 annually. A bounded ten-week pre-series block of two sessions a week is roughly AED 3,000 to 6,000 in total. The realistic choice is usually one subject supported properly for two terms versus three subjects supported thinly for one.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper enough to be worth it?
faqs.answer: A group of three or four costs roughly a third to a quarter of a one-to-one rate, which is a real saving, and it works when a student's difficulty is the same as everybody else's. The problem is that by Year 11 most students are losing marks for idiosyncratic reasons, and group teaching aims at the group's modal difficulty. So the marginal value of the hour falls faster than the price does. Before choosing, ask the subject teacher whether your child's error pattern is common or particular to them.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: Specialist availability tightens and so do prices at that end of the market, and the published monthly estimates for exam-year specialist support, roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for a weekly hour, reflect that. The bigger cost of starting late is not the rate, it is the product: by March the content window has shut, only technique work remains, and the better weekday slots have been taken by school revision programmes. The identical intervention in the preceding autumn is cheaper per hour and has more to work with.

faqs.question: Are past papers and revision materials an extra cost?
faqs.answer: They should not be. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB publish syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes, and a tutor should be pointing you to the official source or working from what the school supplies. We will not reproduce or sell board material as downloads, because reproducing it is a copyright matter and, for unreleased content, worse than that. If a provider is charging for a pack of past papers, ask where the material came from and whether they are permitted to distribute it.

faqs.question: What should I check before paying for the first session?
faqs.answer: Five things in writing. Whether an hour is sixty minutes. Whether work set between sessions is marked, and whether that is included. The cancellation notice period, because a Dubai family will need to move sessions. Whether the quoted figure includes VAT, which you are entitled to ask and nobody should be vague about. And whether the free trial is a full lesson with the actual tutor in the slot you intend to use, rather than an assessment call with a consultant.

faqs.question: With fees flat for 2026-27, is this the year to add tutoring?
faqs.answer: It changes the backdrop rather than the logic. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family with two children in private school a flat fee year genuinely frees capacity. The useful question stays the same: is the next AED 1,000 better spent on one subject supported for two terms, or spread across three subjects for one?

faqs.question: How soon can I tell whether the money is doing anything?
faqs.answer: Six sessions, judged against a target agreed in advance and visible in the student's own marked work. For IGCSE good targets are mechanical: tabulating and plotting without losing presentation marks, completing a paper section in the time allowed, structuring an eight-mark evaluation that reaches a judgement. Bad targets are improve in maths, build confidence and cover the syllabus, because none can be checked and all of them lead to renewing out of uncertainty. If the target has not moved, change the tutor or the diagnosis rather than adding hours.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor more expensive if the lesson is the same length?
faqs.answer: Because the rate includes a drive. The published in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour covers travel to the address, and from a Muhaisnah apartment at six in the evening that journey crosses Al Ittihad Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at the worst hour. You are also paying in delivered minutes: arrival slippage of ten to fifteen minutes is normal and is not refunded. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so for us the question is academic, but it is worth understanding before comparing quotes.

faqs.question: Would you ever tell us not to spend anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we do. If the marked work shows the content is secure and only pacing fails, a short bounded block is enough and a year-long weekly slot is waste. If the school runs its own revision clinic in that subject, it is free, aligned to the school's own entries, and competing with it is counterproductive. If a student is sleeping five hours a night, no tutoring will fix the grade. Each of those conversations costs us a booking, and the three-session diagnostic block exists precisely so that it can end in one.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.closingHeading: Decide the budget, then buy one thing properly
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-muhaisnah.closingBody: The rate you pay matters far less than what you buy with it. One subject, the right syllabus code, a slot that survives the school run, a checkable target at session six: that configuration beats a cheaper hour spread across three subjects every time, and it costs less than most families in this catchment end up spending. Send us the subject and code, the last marked paper and the two slots you trust, and we will come back with a named specialist, a figure, and a free trial lesson in the slot you asked for. Nothing is charged before that lesson, and if a cheaper route would serve your child better we will say so.

intro.heading: Four neighbourhoods, four search results, one sensible answer
paragraphs: Families in the eastern suburbs of Dubai run the same search with different place names in it and get different answers, which feels like useful information and mostly is not. Nad Al Hamar, Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Khawaneej sit within fifteen minutes of each other, draw on an overlapping set of schools, and have a local tutor supply that varies by accident rather than by design. The list a search returns reflects who advertised, who lives nearby, and which tuition centres have premises, none of which tells you whether anybody on it has taught your child's syllabus code.

The genuine differences between these four places are worth setting out, because they do affect a plan. Mirdif has the highest density of both schools and tuition centres, so a parent there has real in-person options. Al Warqa has large British and Indian curriculum schools with mock windows that sit a fortnight away from the Festival City cluster. Al Khawaneej is further out with long internal roads and late, predictable arrivals. Nad Al Hamar has no secondary school inside the district and a commute in every direction.

Where those differences stop mattering is in the one thing a parent is actually buying, which is a person who has taught Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 or whichever code appears on the statement of entry. A tutor who has taught the code is scarce in all four neighbourhoods and plentiful across the whole of a video-delivered market. That is why the answer to the near-me question is the same in Nad Al Hamar as in Mirdif, even though the search results look different.

It is also why we say plainly what the delivery model is before anything else. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a fixed weekly hour. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run in India only. The in-home market here is real and is priced in this page with sources attached, so a parent can weigh the alternative with numbers rather than with impressions.

What follows is the comparison in detail: the four neighbourhoods side by side, what tuition centre density does and does not buy you, which subjects each cluster's schools are short of, how to read a Dubai inspection band so the rating means something, the grade scales both boards report on, the provider models with published rates, and what to send when asking anybody for a quote.

One framing note. This page compares models and areas, not brands. We do not claim that a named competitor is worse, and where a competitor's price appears it appears as their published figure with the date it was read, which is the only honest way to use somebody else's number.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-nad-al-hama.programmesIntro: Across these four neighbourhoods the same three stages generate the same requests, with the useful work different at each.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years in which the IGCSE tier is quietly decided. Algebraic fluency, quantitative confidence in science and written structure in English are built here, and a student who leaves Year 9 unable to rearrange a formula will be recommended for the capped tier two years later. Support at this stage is cheap, infrequent and disproportionately effective.
programmes.countryNote: All four of these neighbourhoods feed schools that deliver the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the licensed curriculum, because Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies whatever curriculum they are licensed for. That is timetable time, and it makes a Year 9 week fuller than the subject list suggests.

programmes.name: Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects, externally examined, with the tier entry submitted months before the papers. The mock window after the winter break is the main diagnostic event of the two years, and reading the marked scripts rather than the grades is what turns it into useful information. Most families buy help after the mocks and buy it too broadly.
programmes.countryNote: Mock windows differ between the Festival City cluster and the Al Warqa cluster by roughly a fortnight, which matters to households with two candidates at different schools. Eastern-suburb schools between them use both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, sometimes for different subjects within the same school.

programmes.name: Where the IGCSE grades lead
programmes.description: A sixth form place, a subject set, and in many cases a choice between A Levels and the IB Diploma. Thresholds are set by individual schools rather than nationally, so the grade needed for A Level Mathematics in one school is not the grade needed in the next one along. Ask in Year 10 rather than after results.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE certificate equivalency the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. That floor is far below the threshold any competitive sixth form applies.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-nad-al-hama.subjectsIntro: Demand is not uniform across these four neighbourhoods, because the school mix differs. These are the subjects asked for most, with what the help consists of.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested subject in all four areas, and the one that gates physics, chemistry and economics. Higher-tier work means functions, graph transformations, circle theorems and vector proofs, which candidates leave blank rather than attempt badly, making them pure recoverable marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Most heavily requested from the British-curriculum schools in Al Warqa and Mirdif. Formula rearrangement and the treatment of experimental uncertainty account for more lost marks than any gap in physics knowledge does.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, yield and electrolysis calculations, plus organic nomenclature as a memory task. Accuracy and significant figures explain most of the loss, which is a routine problem rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Requested more from the Indian-curriculum schools in this part of Dubai, where content volume is handled well and command-term precision less so. Describe, explain and suggest ask for different things and are answered identically by most candidates.

subjects.name: English as a first language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response. Marks follow structure and task handling rather than vocabulary, and three minutes of planning is worth more than ten extra minutes of writing. One of the faster subjects to improve.

subjects.name: English as a second language
subjects.description: A substantial entry across the eastern suburbs. The written paper rewards accuracy and register control, and the speaking component rehearses well on video because the format is already a structured conversation.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Definition precision, diagram accuracy and evaluation structure. Students describe rather than apply, which is a writing-shape problem, and it is why these subjects often move faster than the sciences under tutoring.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the theory paper's exact vocabulary. Students who code competently frequently score poorly on the written paper, because the paper tests its own conventions rather than practical skill.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language

sections.heading: Nad Al Hamar against Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Khawaneej
paragraphs: The four areas differ in ways that matter to logistics and barely at all to teaching. Mirdif has the most schools and the most tuition centres within a short drive, so a parent there has genuine in-person options and a longer local search list. Al Warqa has a heavier concentration of large British and Indian curriculum schools, which shifts demand toward higher-tier mathematics and physics. Al Khawaneej is further out, with long internal roads, late but predictable arrivals and the thinnest local supply of the four. Nad Al Hamar has no secondary school at all inside the district.

What this does to a search result is straightforward. The Mirdif list is longer and contains more centres; the Al Khawaneej list is shorter and contains more generalists willing to travel. Neither list is sorted by whether anybody on it has taught the syllabus code your child is entered for, which is the only attribute that reliably changes a grade in a subject-specific problem. A longer list of the wrong thing is not better than a shorter one.

The commute pattern is the real difference and it is worth planning around. From Nad Al Hamar, Festival City is twelve to fifteen minutes off-peak and twenty to twenty-five at pickup; Mirdif is eighteen to twenty and thirty to thirty-five. From Al Khawaneej, everything is longer. Door times therefore land between about 3.50pm and 4.45pm across the four areas, and in each of them the slot that survives a full term is between 6pm and 7.30pm.

So the comparison resolves to one conclusion. The logistics differ; the answer does not. In all four neighbourhoods, a parent with a specific syllabus problem is better served by a tutor chosen for the code and tier, delivered over video at an hour that fits the local school run, than by whoever is physically closest. In Mirdif that conclusion is a preference. In Nad Al Hamar and Al Khawaneej it is closer to a necessity.

sections.heading: What tuition centre density actually buys you
paragraphs: Mirdif's advantage over Nad Al Hamar in a search result is largely a centre advantage, so it is worth being precise about what a centre is good for. A group class is the cheapest option per head in this market. It supplies structure, a fixed weekly commitment, peer pressure and a scheme that gets through the syllabus. For a student whose problem is doing the work at all, or doing enough practice, that combination is genuinely effective and cheaper than one-to-one by a wide margin.

What a centre class cannot do is stop and spend forty minutes on the one topic your child cannot do, three different ways, until it lands. The class moves at the scheme's pace because it has to. For a student who is broadly fine and stuck on functions, or on moles, or on evaluation structure in economics, the group format spends most of each session on material they already have.

There is also a regulatory point parents rarely know. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval first, with a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a real licence attached to real premises. It is not the same thing as an individual tutor's MoHRE permit, and neither is a quality rating.

The practical test is simple. If you can name the topic that is wrong, buy one-to-one time on that topic. If you cannot name anything beyond the grade, a structured group programme plus timed practice at home may be enough and will cost less. A parent in Mirdif has both options locally; a parent in Nad Al Hamar has the second one at a drive. Both have the first one on video.

sections.heading: Reading a Dubai inspection band so the rating means something
paragraphs: Parents comparing neighbourhoods usually end up comparing school ratings, and the ratings are more informative than the headline band suggests. Dubai private schools are inspected annually by KHDA and rated on a six-band scale running from the highest to the weakest. Abu Dhabi schools are inspected by ADEK, Sharjah schools by SPEA. The band is a summary of a long report, and the report is where a parent learns whether the strength or weakness sits in the years their own child is in.

A school can hold a strong overall band while being weaker in a specific phase or a specific subject, and the reverse happens too. For an IGCSE family the sections worth reading are secondary attainment and progress in mathematics, English and science, and the commentary on teaching for effective learning in the secondary phase. A school rated highly overall on the strength of its primary phase tells you very little about Year 11 mathematics.

Two cautions about ratings and tutoring. First, we do not publish ratings we have not read on the regulator's own site, because a stale or invented rating on a page about your child's school is worse than no rating. Second, a school's band says nothing about whether tutoring is needed; a strong school with a large class and a specific topic gap produces the same problem as a weaker one.

On fees, which parents compare alongside bands: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's intake for that year also adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened the previous year and enrolment rose six per cent.

sections.heading: Grades, boundaries and the two different bars
paragraphs: Both boards report International GCSE on a nine-to-one numeric scale, with grade 9 highest, and older certificates and some subjects carry the A star to G letters. Families arriving in Dubai from a letter-graded system want a clean translation and there is not one, because boundaries were redrawn when the scale changed. Grade 4 is generally treated as a standard pass and grade 5 as a strong pass, and that is the limit of a safe generalisation.

Grade boundaries are set after each series is marked, against the difficulty of that paper and the performance of that cohort. The same raw mark can produce different grades in different series. Anyone telling you the mark needed for a grade 7 in a future series is guessing, and we do not reproduce boundary tables here because they belong to the boards and your child's school has them.

There are two separate bars and families conflate them constantly. The lower bar is UAE certificate equivalency, where the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. A ranking competitor page states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. The higher bar is the sixth form's own entry threshold for a chosen subject, which will sit well above the equivalency floor.

The practical consequence is to ask what the grade is for before deciding what counts as good enough. If the goal is equivalency, mathematics at grade 3 clears it. If the goal is A Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the school's threshold is the number that matters and it is usually a 7. Those two answers lead to completely different tutoring decisions, and tutoring is not required for equivalency at all.

sections.heading: What the four provider models cost, and which suits what
paragraphs: Prices in this market are published inconsistently, so here they are in one place with the source attached, read in October 2026. Budget online platforms advertise from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IGCSE and IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and more, with BartyED at AED 650.

In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen include about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for an examination-year specialist.

Matching the model to the problem is where families save real money. Practice volume and motivation: a centre class or a budget platform. A named topic gap at the higher tier: a qualified or specialist tutor, one-to-one. An oral component: short frequent sessions with a specialist, which is cheap because the block is short. A whole-year drift with no identifiable cause: a diagnostic first, then one subject, rather than three subjects bought simultaneously.

Three of six ranking pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. IB Gram does not post a fixed hourly rate on these pages because it depends on board, tier and proximity to a series; the trial lesson is forty-five minutes, costs nothing, takes no card details, and is where a real number is given.

sections.heading: What to send when you ask anybody for a quote
paragraphs: A parent who sends the right five things gets a useful answer in a day; one who sends a general description gets a week of exchanged messages and a generic proposal. The five are: the subjects with board and syllabus code, the tier where tiers exist, the year group and school, the most recent marked assessment or mock script, and the date you are working to. The marked script is the single most valuable item and the one almost nobody sends.

Then ask five questions back. Which syllabus codes has this tutor taught and over how many cohorts. What would they do in the number of weeks we actually have. What is the rate in AED per hour, and is anything charged on top. What happens if the match is wrong after two sessions. And, if you are considering an in-home arrangement, do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit and may you see it. It is free to obtain and valid for two years, so there is no reason for a legitimate tutor to be unable to show it.

A word on what you are handing over. A tutoring enquiry about a child involves personal data about a minor, and under the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection a parent is entitled to know what is collected, why, and how to have it deleted. Be wary of forms asking for a child's school, grades and photograph without stating a purpose. We ask for the subject, the level, the school, the year group and the deadline, because those are what a tutor match needs, and no more than that.

Finally, the question people hold until last. No tutor will come to your address in Nad Al Hamar, Mirdif, Al Warqa or Al Khawaneej through us. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we provide in India only. If a person in the room is your requirement, hire independently, check the permit, and use the rate bands above to judge the quote.

sections.heading: What we will not claim, and why that is the useful part
paragraphs: A comparison page is only worth reading if it is honest about its author. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge International or Pearson, and it claims none. It operates no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. It does not describe any named school or school group as a client or partner; students we support attend schools across Dubai, which is a different statement.

We publish no star rating, review count or satisfaction statistic, because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method behind it is not information. Competitor pages in this market show ratings of 4.92 out of 5 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 reviews on the same page, and one shows 5.0 from twenty reviews alongside a claim about the number of students taught that the review count cannot support. Fabricated review markup is a structured-data violation and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure.

We do not guarantee grades, points, improvements or university admission, and no refund is tied to an outcome. We do not produce, rewrite or edit assessed work in any subject, and where an IGCSE subject carries coursework a tutor teaches the content, explains the criteria, demonstrates an example on a different task and questions the student's own draft. One site ranking for these searches sells completed assessments; the consequence falls on the candidate.

And we do not host syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables for download. They belong to Cambridge International and Pearson, the boards publish specifications on their own sites, and your child's school has proper access. A tutor using them in a session is normal practice. A website offering a download library of them is handing you someone else's property.

faqs.answer: Two, almost always. Each works to a named syllabus code and a named paper, and plans backwards from the series your child is entered for rather than forwards from the first chapter of the textbook.

intro.heading: Where you are in the IGCSE year decides what tutoring can do
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a parent in Nad Al Sheba can know before hiring an IGCSE tutor is the date. Not the tutor's availability — the exam date, the entry deadline, the mock window and the coursework hand-in. Those four fix what is possible. A student eight months out from a June series can still fix missing syllabus content. A student eight weeks out cannot, and a tutor who pretends otherwise is selling hours rather than a plan.

Nad Al Sheba sits in a British-curriculum heartland. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, and UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of enrolment, the largest single share of the emirate's seventeen licensed curricula. Inside and beside the district that means Repton School Dubai, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba, GEMS Modern Academy, Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai, with Safa Community School and the Al Quoz and Dubai Hills schools a drive away. Most of those run IGCSE at sixteen before splitting students into A Level or the IB Diploma, so Year 11 in this corridor is a year with two exits.

The calendar is also more complicated than most parents are told, because there are two boards and they behave differently. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones — Cambridge states it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The resit routes differ, the results dates differ, and a parent planning a retake needs to know which board their child sits before planning anything.

There is a UAE layer on top. Ramadan moves school hours and family routines, Eid takes days out, and KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons occupy timetable minutes that a revision plan has to work around rather than through. None of the competitor pages measured for this project names a single exam series: the words November and June returned zero hits across every fetchable page in the cluster. A calendar is therefore the cheapest competitive advantage available on a page like this, and it is the spine of everything below.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to addresses in the UAE — home visits are a service we offer only in India. On a calendar page that matters for one specific reason: in the eight weeks before a series, when sessions go from one a week to three, travel time is the first thing that makes the plan impossible. Three visits a week to a Nad Al Sheba villa is three return journeys through 15:00 traffic, and somebody pays for them.
