dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-nad-al-sheb.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to a Nad Al Sheba family on the British route, and each has its own calendar pressure. The IGCSE years are the examined middle of it, but the decisions that shape them are taken a stage earlier and spent a stage later.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE begins, and the only point at which a subject gap can be closed cheaply. Year 9 is where option choices are made, and those choices set the IGCSE subject count, the tiering decision in maths and the science route — single award, double award or three separate sciences. A student choosing three separate sciences in Year 9 has committed to roughly a third more examined content than one choosing double award.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, KS3 runs alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirements, which apply in every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. For a Nad Al Sheba family arriving mid-KS3 from outside the region, Arabic from a standing start inside a timetable already full is the most common first tutoring request, and the earliest one worth making.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, terminal papers in the summer series with November available as a resit route. Cambridge syllabus codes run 0580 for Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics and 0610 Biology; Pearson equivalents include 4MA1 and 4PH1. The code matters because the papers, tiering and practical arrangements differ, and a tutor who does not ask for it is working from a guess.
programmes.countryNote: Nad Al Sheba schools sit as centres inside the Cambridge zone system, so the timetable version your school uses is the one that governs your child's dates. Ask the exams officer which zone the school is in and take the dates from the school rather than from a search result; Cambridge is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone timetable.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The most common exit from IGCSE in this corridor, usually three or four subjects with AS as either a staging post or a standalone qualification. The grades that matter for MoE equivalency on the British track sit here: one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Several Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland schools offer both A Level and the IB Diploma after Year 11, which turns the IGCSE results into a sorting mechanism rather than an endpoint. Families planning that fork benefit from knowing by the January mocks of Year 11 which way they are leaning, because the subject combination needed differs.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The other exit, and a genuinely different animal: six subjects rather than three or four, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and CAS. IGCSE prepares students well for DP content and poorly for DP volume, because nothing in Years 10 and 11 runs three internal assessments and two core components in parallel.
programmes.countryNote: IB in Dubai accounts for around 7% of private-school enrolment, and the emirate's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new openings, creating 16,846 new places. For a Nad Al Sheba Year 11 student considering the switch, the useful preparation during the IGCSE year is extended writing under a word limit, which is the skill the Diploma assumes and IGCSE rarely drills.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-nad-al-sheb.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Nad Al Sheba families ask about most, with the Cambridge syllabus code where one applies, described by what the papers do rather than what the subject covers. Syllabus-code specificity is one of the eighteen gaps nobody in this market fills.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers, no coursework, and the tiering decision governs the grade ceiling. Extended carries algebra, functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and more demanding probability. Marks go missing on method shown but not completed, and on calculator answers given to the wrong accuracy. The non-calculator demand catches students who have never practised without one.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Multiple choice, theory and a practical paper or alternative-to-practical depending on route. Students lose marks on unit conversion, on describing a graph rather than using its gradient, and on experimental-design questions that ask for a control they never name. Formula recall is less decisive than knowing which rearrangement the data invites.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and the mole concept decide most grades. Students who can balance equations still drop marks on state symbols, on ionic equations, and on explaining a trend rather than stating it. The practical component rewards precision about method, and the usual gap is describing what was done instead of why that step controls the variable.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-term sensitive. Describe and explain earn different marks here more sharply than in the other sciences, and six-mark extended answers need a structure the student practised rather than improvised. Diagrams are marked for labelled accuracy, not artistry, and transport and homeostasis questions reward sequencing.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing, then composition. The highest-cost error is writing well but not to the task: a response that ignores form, audience or purpose loses the marks that the quality of prose cannot recover. Timing is the second cost, because most students over-run the reading responses and compress the composition.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Four skills with listening and speaking components alongside reading and writing. Accuracy of register matters as much as range, and the summary task is where marks concentrate: selecting the right points and compressing them is a drillable technique rather than a language ability.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study driven, and application to the stimulus is where the marks are. Students who define a concept correctly and never tie it to the business in the case score the bottom of the band. Calculation questions on break-even and cash flow are reliable marks and are often skipped under time pressure.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are assessed, so an unlabelled axis or a missing new equilibrium point costs marks the prose cannot rescue. Evaluation questions need a judgement, not a balanced list. The data-response paper rewards reading the table before the question, which is the opposite of what most students do.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory plus algorithms and problem-solving. Pseudocode is marked to the syllabus conventions, which catches fluent Python coders who translate loosely. Trace tables are high-value and low-glamour: students who practise them score reliably on questions that others leave blank.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure (Cambridge 0606 route)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or a Higher Level IB maths course. It front-loads calculus and advanced trigonometry, so it is the single best preparation for either exit from Year 11 and the subject where a tutor's level specificity matters most.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. Where the school enters students for an IGCSE Arabic qualification, the examined grade sits alongside an obligation, and support works within the school's own approved material.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall plus skills, and the skills paper is where a prepared student gains most: map reading, graph interpretation and data response are all practisable in a few sessions. Extended answers need named located examples, and generic answers about 'a country' score poorly however fluent.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from the summer series
paragraphs: Every useful IGCSE plan is built in reverse. You start from the series your child is entered for, work back to the results date, back to the final papers, back to the entry deadline, back to the mock window, back to coursework hand-ins, and only then decide what this month is for. Done forwards, revision covers chapter one thoroughly and chapter fourteen never.

The reason entry deadlines sit months before the papers is administrative rather than academic: centres have to be allocated, materials despatched to each zone and candidate numbers fixed. For a Nad Al Sheba parent the practical consequence is that the decision about which subjects and which tier your child sits is taken in the autumn of Year 11, not in the spring, and after it closes a Core entry cannot become an Extended one. That deadline is held by your school's exams officer and nobody else.

The table below is the shape of the year rather than a list of dates, deliberately. Boards publish provisional timetables ahead of each series and revise them, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables well in advance, so any page restating specific dates goes stale without anybody touching it. Take the dates from your school or from the live official timetable; use the table for the ordering and for what should already be done by each point.

What the ordering shows is where tutoring money works hardest. The three highest-value windows are the term before the mock series, the fortnight after mock results, and the six weeks before papers — and they want completely different sessions. Buying the same weekly hour across all three is the most common way an IGCSE tutoring budget in this corridor gets spent without moving a grade.

sections.heading: Two boards, two timetables, six Cambridge zones
paragraphs: A Nad Al Sheba parent planning around exam dates needs to know which board their child's school enters them with, because the answer changes the calendar. This sounds obvious and is routinely unknown: several families each year plan a summer holiday around a date they read online that belonged to the other board.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The part that catches people is zoning: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The timetable your child sits is therefore the school's version, not the generic one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The published results pattern is the useful planning anchor because it is checkable: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a session table should link the live official timetable rather than restating dates.

One correction worth making loudly, because it has been published wrongly to UAE parents before. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. If anybody plans your child's revision around a February-March exam window or a late-November entry deadline, they are using the wrong country's calendar.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision with an expiry date
paragraphs: In tiered IGCSE subjects — Mathematics 0580 most visibly, and the sciences on some routes — the tier decides the grade ceiling. Core cannot reach the top grades. Extended can, and punishes a student who is not ready with a paper full of questions they cannot start. The decision is made with the school in the autumn of Year 11 and it closes with the entry deadline.

The honest way to take it is from data rather than ambition. Sit the student a past Extended paper under the clock in Year 10 and mark it against the official scheme. If they can reach the lower grade boundaries on Extended, Extended is the right entry, because the ceiling is worth more than the comfort. If they are scoring far below, the question becomes whether eight months of focused work closes that distance, and that is a judgement a subject specialist can make from the paper and a parent cannot make from a report card.

The decision interacts with the exit from Year 11, which is why it belongs on a calendar page. A student heading for A Level Mathematics or a Higher Level IB maths course needs the Extended content and benefits from the Additional Mathematics route on top. A student heading for subjects that do not require maths beyond the basics may be better served by a secure Core grade than a scraped Extended one. Both are defensible; drifting into one by default is not.

There is also a grade-floor consideration specific to the UAE. MoE equivalency on the British track requires five accredited IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five. That floor is low, but it is a floor, and a tier decision that leaves a borderline student at risk of missing it on a core subject deserves a conversation rather than an assumption.

sections.heading: What a month of IGCSE tutoring costs in this market
paragraphs: Think in months rather than hours, because the calendar does. An hourly rate tells you very little about what a term of support will cost, and the number that actually lands on a Nad Al Sheba family's card is a monthly one that changes three times during Year 11 as the cadence changes.

Monthly packages visible across the providers researched for this project run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates, for a weekly one-hour session, come out at AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are the market's figures, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list.

Convert that into a Year 11 shape and the spend is uneven by design. Autumn at one session a week in one subject sits at the lower monthly band. The mock cycle in January, at two or three sessions a week, roughly doubles it for six to eight weeks. The final run before the series does the same again for a shorter stretch. A family budgeting a flat monthly figure across the whole year either overspends in the autumn or runs out of room in the spring, and the second is the expensive mistake.

Converted to hourly for comparison, the market's bands sit at AED 45-150 for budget online tutoring, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit with travel included, AED 200-450 or more for an IGCSE specialist, and AED 500-650 upwards at the premium end. Ask any provider three questions before booking: the session length behind the rate, whether VAT is included, and what happens to the money if you stop after one lesson.

sections.heading: Mocks: the most useful data a parent gets all year
paragraphs: The January mock series is treated by most students as a rehearsal and by most parents as a progress report. It is neither. It is a diagnostic instrument, and it has a short shelf life — the fortnight after results is when a mock paper is worth something, because that is when the student still remembers what they were thinking.

The work is unglamorous. Take the actual script back from the school, not just the grade. Go through it mark by mark and sort every lost mark into one of four buckets: content not known, command term misread, arithmetic or notation slip, or ran out of time. Tally the buckets across all subjects. One bucket almost always dominates, and in this corridor it is usually timing in maths and the sciences, and command terms in the humanities.

Then act on the dominant bucket only, for a fixed period, and leave the others alone on purpose. A student whose losses are 60 per cent timing does not need more content; they need twenty timed sections and a rule about when to abandon a question. A student whose losses are content needs a stop-revising list, because with four months left they cannot cover everything and spreading effort evenly is the same as choosing randomly.

A mock grade also has a second use that nobody mentions: it is the evidence for the tier conversation if that is still open, and the evidence for the Year 11 exit conversation if it is not. A Nad Al Sheba student mocking two grades below the entry requirement for Higher Level IB maths has useful information in January that would be useless in May.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the UAE calendar inside a revision plan
paragraphs: Any revision plan written for a Nad Al Sheba family that ignores the UAE calendar will fail in its second month. Ramadan shortens school hours and reorganises the day around Iftar and later sleep; Eid takes days out; and the spring half-term in Dubai schools sits differently from the UK pattern that most online revision timetables assume.

The practical approach is to decide in advance which weeks are low-intensity and protect them rather than pretend they are not coming. During Ramadan, sessions generally move later or to post-Iftar timing, and the productive length drops — a focused 45 minutes beats a tired 90. Students sitting papers in the summer series usually keep the cadence and change the clock, rather than pausing, because a four-week gap in March is expensive in May.

The timetable also carries a standing commitment most international revision advice knows nothing about. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and a recommendation that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those minutes are inside the school week, and they are not optional, so an IGCSE revision plan competes with them rather than borrowing from them.

One more local factor worth diarising: family travel. Long Eid and summer absences are normal in this corridor, and in-person tutoring simply stops during them. Because sessions run over live video, a plan can follow the student to another country and resume on the same clock, which in the spring of Year 11 is the difference between a plan and an aspiration.

sections.heading: A travelling tutor against live video in the eight weeks that matter
paragraphs: Most comparisons of online and in-home tutoring are written about a normal week. The interesting comparison is the abnormal one: the final two months before a series, when the cadence goes from one session a week to three and every other constraint tightens at the same time.

At one session a week, a tutor travelling into Nad Al Sheba is a manageable arrangement with real benefits — a parent can see the session, and a child cannot drift. At three sessions a week it becomes three return journeys through pick-up traffic, a fixed slot that cannot move when the school adds a revision class, and a premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour over the equivalent online rate paid three times instead of once. That is where the model breaks for most families, and it breaks in the exact weeks it matters.

Online one-to-one trades presence for flexibility and reach. A session can move by a day with a message. The tutor is drawn from the whole timezone rather than the few IGCSE specialists within driving distance of the district. Mark-scheme work is genuinely better on a shared screen than on one paper copy between two people, because the examiner's wording sits beside the student's answer and both people are reading the same line.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. So the table below is not a pitch disguised as a comparison — it is the reasoning behind a decision already made, set out so a Nad Al Sheba parent can check it against their own week rather than take it on trust.

sections.heading: Private candidates, retakes and the November route
paragraphs: Some Nad Al Sheba families end up outside the school's entry process: a student who left a school mid-year, one taking an extra subject the school does not offer, one home-educating, or one retaking a single subject after a summer result. The route exists and it is ordinary, but the deadlines are the parent's responsibility rather than the school's, and that is where it goes wrong.

A private candidate sits through an approved exam centre, which handles the entry, the fee and the timetable. The centre's own internal deadline sits earlier than the board's, because it has to collate entries, so the real date is always the centre's. For UAE candidates the series available are June and November for both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, and November is the standard resit route; the February-March Cambridge series is offered to India only and does not apply here.

Practical arrangements need checking rather than assuming. Subjects with practical or speaking components have specific requirements that not every centre can host, and a student who enters as a private candidate for a science without confirming the practical route can find the entry invalid for the paper they expected to sit. Ask the centre which papers and components it can offer for the specific syllabus code before paying anything.

For a retake the planning question is narrow and answerable: what exactly went wrong in August, and is it fixable in the weeks before the November series? If the script shows timing and question selection, that is a realistic target for a short intensive block. If it shows whole topics missing, November is tight and the honest advice may be the following June. A tutor who will not give you that answer straight is not planning, they are booking.

sections.heading: Which regulator governs your child's exams, and which does not
paragraphs: Parents in this corridor routinely conflate two separate systems. The school is regulated by the emirate; the examination is governed by the board. Confusing them produces the belief that a regulator can intervene in an exam result, and the belief that a tutoring provider can be approved by a regulator to teach a board's syllabus. Neither is true.

Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

What sits with the board instead is everything about the examination: syllabus content, paper structure, timetabling by zone, marking, grade boundaries, enquiries about results and access arrangements. A grade query goes to the school's exams officer and from there to Cambridge or Pearson. No emirate regulator reviews a mark scheme, and a tutoring platform cannot be accredited by one to deliver a board's course.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with physical premises, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. If a provider says a regulator has approved its tutors, ask for the permit number.

sections.heading: The equivalency floor hiding inside Year 11
paragraphs: Equivalency converts a school-leaving qualification into something UAE authorities recognise, and it is the step that governs university applications inside the country. Four of the ten query clusters researched for this project contained no competitor mention of it, and one ranking competitor publishes the wrong subject count. For an IGCSE family it carries a quiet deadline, because the subjects it counts are chosen in Year 9 and graded in Year 11.

The published British-track rule is specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Alongside that, the student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five.

That gives a Year 11 parent a checkable question to ask in the autumn: which five subjects are the equivalency five, and is the tier decision on each of them consistent with clearing the floor comfortably? For most students in this corridor the answer is yes with room to spare. For a borderline student entered at a tier that puts a core subject at risk, it is a conversation worth having before the entry deadline rather than after results.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority before acting on anything.

process.title: Say where you are in the year
process.description: The first message should name the school, the year group, the board and syllabus code if you have it, the tier, and the next three dates: coursework hand-in, mock window, entry deadline. That is enough to say what this term can realistically achieve and what it cannot. A subject name alone starts a longer conversation.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: One live session with the tutor we think fits, spent working a past-paper section on the correct tier and marking it together rather than teaching a topic. You get a written note naming the dominant pattern in the lost marks and how many sessions that pattern suggests. No payment is involved in this lesson.

process.title: Build the plan backwards
process.description: From the series date, back through the entry deadline and mock window, to this week. The plan names which topics are being covered, which are deliberately being left until the mock data arrives, and which are being left alone entirely. Writing down what is not being revised is the part that makes it a plan.

process.title: Weekly sessions against the school's scheme
process.description: The tutor asks for the current unit and the next assessment each week and works to those rather than to the textbook order. Session notes name the topic, what was set, and which command term or paper section is next. Parents here generally prefer the note to a progress percentage, which would be invented.

process.title: Rebuild on mock results
process.description: When mock scripts come back, the plan is rewritten rather than continued. Lost marks are categorised, the dominant category becomes the work for a fixed period, and a stop-revising list is written. This is the single highest-value fortnight of the year and it is wasted if the sessions simply carry on as before.

process.title: Switch to paper blocks for the final run
process.description: Six to eight weeks out, content coverage stops and the sessions become timed sections marked against official schemes, with question-selection drill for papers offering a choice. Cadence rises to two or three a week. Papers come from your school's licensed access or the board's own platform.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the series, not from chapter one
whyPoints.description: Every plan is built backwards from the June or November series your child is actually entered for, through the entry deadline and the mock window. The researched competitor pages name no series at all: June and November returned zero hits across the fetchable set.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject labels
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different demands, and the tier changes the job again. The tutor is matched to the code and tier your child sits, which is why we ask for it before matching rather than after the first session.

whyPoints.title: Monthly costs you can check
whyPoints.description: The AED figures on this page are attributed to the provider or rate table that published them and dated to October 2026. Three of six researched competitors publish no price at all. Monthly bands are given because that is the number that actually lands on a card.

whyPoints.title: The UAE calendar built in
whyPoints.description: Ramadan timings, Eid absences and KHDA's mandatory-subject lessons are planned around rather than discovered. Sessions move later or post-Iftar during Ramadan, and a travelling family keeps its cadence because delivery is over live video.

whyPoints.title: No regulator borrowed as a credential
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education are explained here because parents need to understand them. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them, nor from Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

whyPoints.title: Straight answers about what is still fixable
whyPoints.description: Eight weeks out, technique and timing are fixable and a missing syllabus is not. You get that answer plainly, with a written list of what to stop revising, rather than an encouraging number of sessions. Nobody can promise a grade and we do not.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in Nad Al Sheba, or are the lessons online?
faqs.answer: Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. For an IGCSE plan the difference shows in the final two months, when the cadence rises to two or three sessions a week. Three slots online are three slots. Three visits to a Nad Al Sheba villa are three return journeys through pick-up traffic, at a market premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour over the online rate, paid each time.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams actually held for UAE students?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The February-March Cambridge series is offered to India only and does not apply to UAE candidates, so any plan built around a February exam window is using the wrong country's calendar. Take your child's exact dates from the school's exams officer, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones with its own timetable version.

faqs.question: What are the six Cambridge zones and why does it matter which one we are in?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, so the same subject can be examined at a different time in different zones. Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Nad Al Sheba parent the practical rule is simple: the only timetable that governs your child is the one the school issues. Never plan around a generic one found online.

faqs.question: How much should we budget per month for IGCSE tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, according to Bestimate's Dubai rate table. Published packages elsewhere in the market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Expect the figure to roughly double during the mock cycle and the final run, because the cadence changes rather than the rate.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for Core or Extended, and when is that decided?
faqs.answer: The decision is taken with the school in the autumn of Year 11 and it closes at the entry deadline. Core caps the grade ceiling below the top grades; Extended opens the full range and punishes an unprepared candidate. The only real evidence is a past Extended paper sat under the clock in Year 10 and marked against the official scheme. If the student reaches the lower Extended boundaries, enter Extended, because the ceiling is worth more than the comfort. Check the exit route first: A Level Maths and IB Higher Level maths need Extended.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE for us?
faqs.answer: They are separate boards with separate syllabuses, codes, papers and timetables. Cambridge uses codes like 0580 for Mathematics and 0625 for Physics, Pearson uses 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge zones its timetables across six administrative regions; Pearson publishes a single international timetable plus provisional versions ahead of each series. Results patterns differ too: Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and its November 2025 results on 22 January 2026. Ask your school which board it enters students with before planning anything.

faqs.question: My child's mocks were poor. What should we do in the two weeks after results?
faqs.answer: Get the script back, not just the grade, and sort every lost mark into four categories: content not known, command term misread, arithmetic or notation slip, and ran out of time. Tally them across subjects. One category almost always dominates. Work only that one for a fixed fortnight and deliberately leave the others. If content dominates with four months left, write a stop-revising list, because covering everything is no longer available and spreading effort evenly is the same as choosing at random.

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from the papers. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the lost marks are. If the pattern is timing, question selection or command terms, eight weeks of marked timed sections moves a grade reliably, because the recovery is concentrated in a skill rather than spread across a syllabus. If whole topics are missing, eight weeks buys a partial fix and an honest list of what to abandon. The diagnostic trial lesson exists to tell you which case you are in before you spend anything, and nobody can promise a grade either way.

faqs.question: Can lessons work around Ramadan and the Dubai school calendar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are planned around it rather than disrupted by it. During Ramadan sessions generally move later or to post-Iftar timing, and the productive session length drops, so a focused 45 minutes is set rather than a tired 90. Students sitting the summer series usually keep the weekly cadence and change the clock instead of pausing, because a four-week gap in the spring is expensive in June. Eid and travel absences are handled by the session following the student, since delivery is over live video.

faqs.question: How does my child sit IGCSE exams if they are not entered through a school?
faqs.answer: As a private candidate through an approved exam centre, which handles the entry, the fee and the timetable. The real deadline is the centre's internal one, which sits earlier than the board's because entries must be collated. The series available to UAE candidates are June and November for both Cambridge and Pearson. Confirm before paying that the centre can host every component for your specific syllabus code, because practical and speaking components are not available at every centre and an entry without them can be invalid.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE tutor be matched for a Nad Al Sheba student?
faqs.answer: For the core subjects — Mathematics, the three sciences, English, Business Studies, Economics — a trial session is usually arrangeable within a few days at either tier. Less common subjects, and requests for one tutor across two subjects, take longer, and some cannot be met in a given term. When that happens you are told so with a date rather than matched to a generalist, because a generalist presented as a specialist is discovered in session three and the term is gone by then.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects get requested most from this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: In this corridor the requests concentrate in Mathematics at Extended tier, Chemistry and Physics, and English as a First Language. The reasons differ: maths is tiering and timing, the sciences are command terms and experimental-design questions, and English is writing well but not to the task. Arabic is the other recurring request, particularly from families new to the UAE, because KHDA requires it in every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum and it arrives as a timetabled subject from a standing start.

faqs.question: Is the person teaching my child permitted to tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', showing no fee and two working days.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE actually require for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track rule is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Alongside that, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade is required. One ranking competitor states six subjects; the published figure is five. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae, because the authority sets them, not us.

faqs.question: Will a tutor do my child's coursework or practical write-up?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor teaches the content, explains the mark scheme, discusses method and scope, and gives written feedback on a draft the student has written. No part of a submitted piece is written, rewritten or edited to completion, and no data is supplied. The boundary is stated to the student at the start because the declaration they sign is theirs, not ours. We also do not host or distribute board papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, which are the board's copyright.

faqs.question: What if we book sessions and then want to stop?
faqs.answer: The trial lesson is free and carries no payment, so the first session costs nothing to walk away from. After that, ask any provider in this market three questions before paying: the session length behind the quoted rate, whether VAT is included, and what happens to unused sessions if you stop. Those three answers separate providers more reliably than the headline rate does. Changing tutor mid-term is also free and normal here, and is usually the right move if a mark pattern has not shifted in six to eight sessions.

From those we can say what this term can realistically change and what it cannot, which is a more honest answer than a number of sessions. intro.heading: The honest answer to "near me", and what it costs you
paragraphs: Oud Metha has an unusual property for Dubai: the schools are close together and so are the families. The Indian High School sits on the Oud Metha Road, St Mary's Catholic High School and Dubai Gem Private School are within a few minutes of it, and Dubai English Speaking School and Pakistan Education Academy are inside the same loop. A parent searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in Oud Metha is not facing a sixty-minute drive to find one. They are facing something subtler and more expensive: a short list of whoever happens to live in that square kilometre, charging a travel premium for a journey that takes nine minutes.

That is the cost problem this page is about. Proximity feels like it should be cheap, and in Oud Metha it genuinely is cheaper than a tutor crossing Dubai to Arabian Ranches. What proximity does not buy is syllabus match. Your child might be sitting Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended, or Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 alongside it, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 with its own tiering and its own calculator rules. A tutor nine minutes away who learned the other board is not a bargain at any hourly rate. The sessions feel productive, the past paper questions look familiar, and the first proper mock reveals that half the technique was for a different paper.

So the spend breaks into two decisions, and only one of them is about the hourly figure. The first is whether you are buying the right syllabus. The second is how you buy the hours: by the hour, by the month, by the term, or in a short diagnostic block before committing to anything. Dubai providers price all four differently, and the published monthly packages are not simply the hourly rate multiplied out. One provider advertises AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. In-home monthly packages in the same market sit at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those two offers are not the same product, and the gap between them is almost entirely travel.

Every dirham figure on this page comes from a provider's own published rate card or from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price. We publish the market because the rest of this search result does not: of the competitor pages measured for this project, three of six publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, a currency no Oud Metha family pays school fees in. A parent cannot judge value against a blank.

What follows is the spend, laid out so you can argue with it: the monthly commitment first, then what the travel premium actually buys minute by minute, then the Core and Extended tier decision that is worth more than a term of tuition, then the exam-entry costs nobody mentions, and finally how many subjects the Ministry of Education counts, because over-entering is the single largest avoidable cost in an IGCSE year.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.programmesIntro: Oud Metha's school belt runs more than one route to a sixteen-plus qualification, and the fee you pay for support depends on which one your child is on. These are the four that matter inside this catchment, with the cost implication of each spelled out rather than implied.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year course most British-curriculum schools in the Bur Dubai belt run to age sixteen. Subjects are coded: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, English as a Second Language 0510. Many subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, which changes the grade ceiling and the paper set. Cambridge runs the exams in a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones.
programmes.countryNote: Across Dubai's private sector the UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent of the emirate's 387,441 private pupils in 227 schools, the largest single share. Inside Oud Metha that share is spread across schools that mix British and Indian provision, so a household can easily have one child on IGCSE and a sibling on a CBSE track with a completely different fee and tuition profile.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board sat widely in Dubai, with its own codes and its own structure: Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher, Physics is 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1. Exams run in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - the sort of gap that decides whether a resit fits before a university deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so any session plan built for an Oud Metha family should link the live official timetable rather than trusting a date restated on a tutoring page. Pearson's modular structure is also the practical reason some Bur Dubai schools split entries across two boards: a subject can be banked earlier.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The alternative route to sixteen in the IB continuum schools near Oud Metha, including Swiss International Scientific School Dubai in Al Jaddaf. MYP is assessed against four criteria per subject group on a 1-8 scale rather than by a terminal examination paper, so the support a student needs looks nothing like IGCSE past-paper drilling and should not be priced as though it were.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate programmes account for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three IB - creating 16,846 new places. A family weighing IGCSE against MYP in this belt has more IB capacity arriving nearby than it did two years ago.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where a large share of IGCSE students in this catchment go next, the other share going to A Level. The Diploma's six subjects plus Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service load is heavier than most Year 11 students expect, and the subjects chosen at IGCSE constrain which Higher Levels are realistic. Mathematics is the usual pinch point.
programmes.countryNote: The practical cost consequence for an Oud Metha household is that money spent on IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 in Year 11 often removes the need for a full remedial block in Diploma year one. Deciding that in Year 11 is cheaper than discovering it in Year 12, and considerably cheaper than a Higher Level subject change in October.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.subjectsIntro: Prices in this market do not vary much by subject, but the number of hours a subject needs varies enormously. Below are the IGCSE subjects most requested by families in the Bur Dubai belt, each with the code to confirm against your child's entry statement and a note on where the hours actually go.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Tiered, and the tier decision sets the grade ceiling. Extended carries the algebra, functions, trigonometry and probability content that a Diploma Mathematics course assumes. Most lost marks are not conceptual: they are method marks surrendered by unshown working and by misreading a command verb.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The Edexcel alternative, Foundation and Higher tiered, two papers each. Question style differs from Cambridge enough that past-paper technique does not transfer cleanly. A tutor working from the wrong board's papers will look competent for about six weeks.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Higher Level Mathematics or engineering. It introduces calculus, logarithms and matrices early. Families who fund this in Year 11 frequently need fewer remedial hours in Diploma year one.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where UAE candidates most often lose structured-question marks, usually by describing an effect when the verb asked them to explain it. Practical skills are examined through the alternative-to-practical paper where a centre does not run the practical option.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic chemistry take the hours. The six-mark extended-response questions reward a structured answer with linked reasoning, which is a trainable skill rather than a content gap, and therefore cheap to fix if diagnosed early.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to revise badly. Students read notes and feel prepared, then lose marks on data interpretation and on the precision of definitions. Sessions are better spent on past-paper mark schemes than on re-reading.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: A double-award route covering all three sciences, common where a timetable cannot fit three separate sciences. It limits depth, which matters if a student intends Higher Level Chemistry or Physics later. Worth checking before funding three separate science tutors.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510)
subjects.description: Counts towards the five subjects MoE equivalency recognises on the British track. Marks are won on reading-comprehension technique and on the controlled writing tasks, where a rubric-led approach moves grades faster than general conversation practice.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis of unseen passages. The gap for many Oud Metha students is not vocabulary but the ability to write about how a writer achieves an effect rather than what the passage says. That is a technique fix, usually six to eight sessions.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Both reward structured evaluation and the correct use of diagrams. Students who revise definitions and ignore the eight-mark evaluation questions cap themselves in the middle of the grade range regardless of how many hours are bought.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory paper plus algorithm and programming problem-solving. Pseudocode conventions carry marks, and students who code fluently in Python still drop marks by writing Python where the mark scheme expects the syllabus pseudocode.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: Sat by many students in this belt alongside the KHDA-mandated Arabic provision. Note for budgeting: Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five subjects required for MoE equivalency on the British track, so they are taken for other reasons.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.regionsTitle: Where our Oud Metha students actually live
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.regionsIntro: Oud Metha sits inside a tight cluster of older Dubai districts where the school run is short and the apartment blocks are dense. Each neighbouring district changes the sums slightly, usually through what an in-home tutor would charge to reach it and what time a session can start.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: The school belt itself, with The Indian High School, St Mary's Catholic High School, Dubai Gem Private School and Dubai English Speaking School within minutes of one another. Short pick-up times mean a 3.30pm or 4pm session is realistic here in a way it is not in outer Dubai.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Dense, walkable, and the district where the cheapest advertised tuition in Dubai tends to circulate by word of mouth. The AED 45 to 65 an hour band exists here, and it is almost always a university student rather than a subject specialist.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Immediately west of Oud Metha across the Al Mankhool Road, feeding Ambassador School and the Bur Dubai schools. Families here frequently compare an in-home visit with online delivery, because the drive genuinely is short and the premium looks harder to justify.

regions.name: Bur Dubai
regions.note: The wider historic district, mixed British and Indian curriculum provision, and a high proportion of two-child and three-child households. Shared-sibling scheduling is the main cost lever families here use, and it works better online than in-home.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Dubai Healthcare City
regions.note: Newer towers and the IB continuum option at Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. Parents working hospital or clinic shifts in Healthcare City often need a session that can move week to week, which rules out most in-home arrangements.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Across the creek toward Festival City, with Deira International School and Universal American School within reach. Garhoud traffic between 4pm and 6pm adds real minutes to a journey that looks trivial on a map.

regions.name: Al Nasr and Za'abeel
regions.note: Between Oud Metha and the Trade Centre, with a working-parent profile that pushes sessions toward 7pm or later. Evening slots are the ones that tend to carry a surcharge in the in-home market.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: Further out along the Green Line, with Al Ittihad Private School and a large Indian-curriculum cohort. An in-home tutor crossing from Oud Metha to Al Qusais is adding thirty to forty minutes of round-trip travel to the bill.

schoolClusters.city: The Oud Metha and Bur Dubai school belt
schoolClusters.note: These schools sit within a few minutes of one another, which is what makes the area's search for a nearby tutor feel so reasonable. They also run a mix of Cambridge and Pearson entries, which is exactly why the syllabus code matters more than the postcode.

schoolClusters.city: Al Jaddaf, Al Garhoud and Festival City
schoolClusters.note: The nearest IB continuum and American-curriculum options, reachable from Oud Metha but far enough that an in-home tutor crossing between them is charging for the car as much as for the teaching.
schools: Al Ittihad Private School, Al Mamzar

sections.heading: Buy by the month, not by the hour, and compare what the month contains
paragraphs: An online IGCSE tutor in Dubai costs roughly AED 100 an hour at the cheapest published monthly package and roughly AED 300 an hour at the top of the qualified-tutor band, reviewed October 2026. The hourly figure is the number every provider advertises and the one that tells you least, because the sessions per week, the session length and whether marking happens between sessions all sit outside it. A household in Oud Metha deciding between two offers at AED 150 and AED 220 an hour is not comparing two prices; it is comparing two different products with a price attached to each.

Start from the monthly commitment instead. One Dubai provider publishes an online package at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. In-home monthly packages in the same market are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Both amount to eight hours of teaching. The first costs about AED 100 an hour, the second about AED 200 to 225, and the difference is not teaching quality - it is a car, a driver's time, and a fixed arrival window that cannot flex when a school adds a late revision clinic.

Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, estimates monthly spend on weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those bands are wide because they fold together several different things: who is teaching, how long each session runs, and whether anybody reads the student's written work between sessions.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys, minute by minute
paragraphs: In-home tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, and the gap is travel. In most of Dubai that premium is easy to understand: a tutor crossing from Mirdif to Arabian Ranches is giving up an hour of their evening to deliver one hour of teaching, and somebody pays for that. In Oud Metha the arithmetic looks different, and families here are right to interrogate it.

The drive from Karama to the Oud Metha school belt is a few minutes outside peak. From Al Mankhool it is shorter. So the obvious conclusion is that an in-home tutor in this district should cost barely more than an online one. In practice the premium holds, for a reason that has nothing to do with distance: the tutor's available pool shrinks to whoever is willing to travel at all, and a scarce pool prices itself. The parent is not paying for nine minutes of driving. They are paying for the small number of qualified people prepared to sell a fixed arrival time in a specific postcode.

There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice. A tutor who has committed to arriving at 5pm in Oud Metha cannot also teach at 5pm in Al Qusais, so the slots available to you are the ones left over after their geography is solved. When a school adds a late mock or a Ramadan timetable shifts the evening, an in-home arrangement is the hardest thing in the week to move. Families in this belt discover that in the fortnight before a series, which is the worst possible fortnight to discover it.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Oud Metha students run one-to-one over live video, which is what makes a Higher-tier Physics 0625 specialist available to a family whose nine-minute radius contains none. sections.heading: The tier decision is worth more than a term of tuition
paragraphs: Before a family in Oud Metha buys a single hour, there is a free decision worth more than most of the hours they are about to purchase: whether the child is entered for Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. Cambridge tiers many IGCSE subjects, and the tier caps the available grade. Pearson Edexcel tiers Mathematics A 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher on the same principle. A student entered on the lower tier cannot reach the top grades no matter how much tuition is bought, and a student stretched onto the higher tier without the groundwork loses marks across every paper rather than only the hard ones.

This is where tuition money is most often wasted in this belt, and it is wasted invisibly. A family funds a weekly hour for two terms, the child works hard, the grade arrives, and it is the ceiling of the tier they were entered on. Nobody did anything wrong. The decision that governed the outcome was taken in a school office months before the first session, and it was never discussed at home.

The useful purchase here is small and early: one or two diagnostic sessions on a past paper from each tier, to find out which one the student is actually sitting against. That costs a fraction of a term and changes what the term is for. If the student is comfortably clearing Extended questions, the hours should go to technique and timing. If they are not, the hours should go to the specific content gap, and the conversation with the school about tier should happen now rather than in Year 11.

sections.heading: The costs around the exam that nobody quotes you
paragraphs: Tuition is the visible cost of an IGCSE year. It is not the only one, and the others arrive on a timetable that a family planning only for hourly rates does not see coming. Exam entry is the first. Where a student sits as a private candidate rather than through their own school, the entry is arranged through an approved examination centre and carries a fee set by that centre, not by the board. Those fees vary by centre and by subject, so the only honest instruction is to ask the centre directly and get the figure in writing before the entry deadline rather than after it.

The second is the resit. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. A subject that goes wrong in June can usually be retaken in November, which means a second entry fee and a concentrated block of tuition in a short window. Families who assume the year ends with the summer results are the ones who meet both costs unplanned. The gap between sitting and receiving results matters too: November 2025 Pearson results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November resit is not a quick fix if a deadline falls in December.

The third is the one Cambridge itself warns about. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the board states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A tutoring plan built from a timetable PDF found through a search engine rather than from the school's own entry statement is a plan with an avoidable failure mode in it.

A note on one date circulating widely in UAE tutoring content: the Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November. Any plan, page or tutor that has your child revising toward a February or March window has the wrong country's calendar, and that is a scheduling error with money attached.

sections.heading: How many subjects you are actually paying for
paragraphs: The largest avoidable cost in an IGCSE year is not the hourly rate. It is funding support across more subjects than the next stage requires. Families in Oud Metha routinely spread tuition thinly across seven or eight subjects, and the consequence is predictable: nothing moves far enough to change a grade, and the spend is the same as concentrating it would have been.

The Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements for the British track are specific and publicly stated. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; that is not what the published requirement says.

Equivalency is not the same thing as university admission, and neither is a reason to buy tutoring in a subject your child does not need. A UAE or international university sets its own entry requirements, and those requirements name subjects. Working backwards from the two or three subjects that the intended degree route actually names, and funding those properly, buys more than a thin layer across everything. Nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency - it is a documentation process, performed by the authority, not by a tutoring platform.

Verify your own child's position on the Ministry of Education's own channel rather than on any tutoring page, including this one. No IB points threshold for equivalency appears in the sourced material available for this project, so no figure is published here. The table summarises what the British track must show.

sections.heading: Where the hours disappear without buying a grade
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of the tuition money that produces no measurable change in this belt, and all four are diagnosable in a single session. The first is re-teaching. A tutor who explains the topic again, clearly and patiently, is giving the student a second version of the lesson they already sat through. If the student could follow the school's explanation and still cannot answer the question, the gap is not the explanation.

The second is working from notes instead of papers. Revision that consists of reading is comfortable and feels productive, which is exactly why it persists. IGCSE marks are awarded against a mark scheme for a specific question, and the only way to find out whether a student can satisfy one is to put a past paper in front of them under time and mark it honestly against the official scheme. A session that ends without the student having written anything that was marked has produced a pleasant hour and no information.

The third is ignoring the command verb. Describe, explain, calculate, suggest and evaluate each demand a different shape of answer, and a student who writes a description where an explanation was asked for can know the physics perfectly and still score two marks out of four. This is the cheapest thing on the list to fix and the thing least often taught, because it is not content and therefore does not feel like teaching.

The fourth is buying hours in the wrong month. Tuition bought in the eight weeks before a series competes with the school's own mock timetable, the student's coursework deadlines and everybody's fatigue. The same money spent two terms earlier, on diagnosis and technique, does more and costs less per mark. Rates across this market also tend to firm up as a series approaches, so late is expensive twice.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor is legally permitted, and what it adds to the bill
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is a question a parent can settle for themselves before paying anybody. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Two things follow from that, and both are useful when you are comparing quotes. The permit costs the tutor nothing, so no part of an hourly rate is a permit fee being passed on. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here; a figure circulating in UAE tutoring content as a specific dirham penalty could not be verified against any official source.

The permit is a different instrument from the one a tuition business needs. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds neither a KHDA institute permit nor any regulator's accreditation, and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any tutoring page in this search result claiming otherwise is making a claim you should ask it to evidence.

One further rule is worth knowing before you ask a teacher at your child's own school for private lessons. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on the exact wording, but do not build a plan around your child's own classroom teacher.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with your child's coursework
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but where it exists - and across the sciences, where the alternative-to-practical paper tests practical reasoning - the boundary between teaching and producing the work is a line with consequences on the wrong side of it. The same line governs the Diploma work that follows for many students in this belt: the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay.

A tutor may teach the technique, explain the assessment criteria, model the method on a different example, question the student's reasoning, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite it to completion, supply a draft to adapt, or produce the work in any form. IB Gram tutors do not write assessed coursework. That is not a disclaimer; it is the service description, and it is the thing that distinguishes legitimate tuition from several operations ranking for these searches. One of them sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published dirham price. For the student that is a malpractice finding, and the consequences land on the student.

The same boundary applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those are published by the boards, your child's school holds the current versions, and a tutor's job is to teach against them rather than to hand them over. If a provider offers a library of mark schemes as a selling point, ask who owns the copyright in it.

Where this becomes a cost question is simple. The hours that buy marks on a coursework component are the hours spent on the student's own reasoning, not on polishing a document somebody else shaped. A parent paying for the second thing is paying for a risk, and the risk is carried entirely by their child.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects sitting on top of the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Any budget built only around IGCSE subjects misses a block of the week that is not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. For a student in Oud Metha on a British curriculum, that is real timetable time competing with IGCSE content.

KHDA is specific about how it runs. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask a school about. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited - which constrains what any tutor can legitimately offer in those subjects.

The practical consequence for an Oud Metha family's spend is one of sequencing. Remember that Arabic and Islamic Education do not count toward the five IGCSE subjects MoE equivalency recognises, so they are carried for other reasons and should not be the subjects a stretched tuition budget is spent on. Fund the subjects the next stage names, and treat the mandatory block as timetable pressure to schedule around rather than content to buy support for by default.

process.description: Send the subject and the syllabus code from your child's school entry statement - 0580, 0625, 4MA1 - along with the tier, the school and the series they are entered for. That single message removes most of the ways a match goes wrong, and it costs nothing to send.

process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video, at no charge, with a tutor matched to that code. It is a teaching session rather than a sales call, and it is the cheapest reliable test of whether this tutor and this student can work together for a term.

process.title: A written diagnosis before a plan
process.description: After the trial you get a short list of what is actually costing marks, in priority order, separating content gaps from technique gaps. Families frequently find the plan is shorter than they expected to buy, because technique moves faster than content.

process.description: Oud Metha's short pick-up times make a 3.30pm or 4pm session genuinely workable, which most Dubai districts cannot hold. Lock the same hour each week; a session that moves around the week is the first one to be dropped when the term tightens.

process.title: Review against the school's own marks
process.description: Progress is measured against your child's school assessments and mock results, not against a tutor's impression of how sessions are going. If the marks are not moving after a block of sessions, the plan changes or the tutor does.

whyPoints.description: A tutor nine minutes from your building who learned the other board is not a saving. We match on the confirmed code and tier - 0580 Extended, 4MA1 Higher, 0625 Extended - because that is the variable that decides whether the hours convert into marks.

whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the pool is every specialist on the right code rather than the small number prepared to drive to Oud Metha at 5pm. For a tiered science or Additional Mathematics 0606, that is the difference between a specialist and a generalist.

whyPoints.description: The first useful purchase is finding out what is wrong, which usually takes three or four sessions. We would rather sell a short block that answers the question than a term that postpones it, because a plan built on a guess spends the same money for less.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work. Several operations in this search result do otherwise, and the risk falls on the student.
