faqs.question: What should a family in Oud Metha expect to pay per month for IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Reckon in months rather than hours. At one session a week, published Dubai rates put a budget online tutor at roughly AED 180 to 600 a month, a qualified subject tutor at AED 600 to 1,200, and an IGCSE specialist at AED 800 to 1,800 or more. The cheapest monthly package found in this market is AED 799 for eight online sessions, which works out near AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those figures are the providers' own, read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Does living close to the Oud Metha school belt make a tutor cheaper?
faqs.answer: Less than you would expect. The drive from Karama or Al Mankhool to the Oud Metha schools is only a few minutes outside peak, yet in-home rates in Dubai still run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor. The premium survives because the pool shrinks to whoever is willing to travel at that hour, and a scarce pool prices itself. You are paying for a committed arrival time in one postcode, not for nine minutes of driving. Online delivery removes both the premium and the geography constraint.

faqs.question: Which document tells me the exact IGCSE code and tier we are paying to support?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the entry statement, which lists the board, the subject code and the tier for every subject. It is the single most useful document in the whole budget and it is free. Cambridge codes look like 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry; Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1 for Physics. Do not rely on the subject name alone. The two boards' question styles differ enough that past-paper technique does not transfer cleanly, so paying for the wrong board's papers wastes the whole block.

faqs.question: Can the tier my child is entered for limit the grade, however much tutoring we buy?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where tuition money disappears most quietly in this area. Cambridge tiers many IGCSE subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher. The lower tier caps the available grade, so hours spent chasing a grade the tier cannot award produce nothing. One or two diagnostic sessions on past papers from each tier will tell you which one the student is genuinely working at, and that is a conversation to have with the school in Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11, when a change is no longer practical.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book several subjects with one tutor in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, often, and weaker per mark. One tutor covering Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry is a generalist by definition, and the subject where your child is furthest behind is the one that needs a specialist on the exact code and tier. A better way to use the same budget is to concentrate it: fund the one or two subjects that the next stage actually names, properly, with a specialist each, and let the school's own provision carry the subjects that are already stable. Spreading a fixed budget thinly is the most common way to spend it without moving a grade.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time in the year to start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families start. Rates across this market tend to firm up as a series approaches, and tuition bought in the final eight weeks competes with the school's mock timetable, coursework deadlines and general fatigue. The same money spent two terms earlier buys diagnosis and technique work, which moves marks faster per hour than late content cramming. If your child is in Year 10 now, a short diagnostic block this term is the cheapest useful purchase available and usually shortens the plan you end up buying.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to enter an IGCSE exam as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The fee is set by the approved examination centre rather than by Cambridge or Pearson, so it varies by centre and by subject and no single figure can honestly be quoted here. Contact centres directly, ask for the per-subject fee in writing, and get it before the entry deadline rather than after. Budget for the possibility of a second entry too: a subject that goes wrong in the June series can usually be retaken in November, which means a second fee and a concentrated block of tuition in a short window.

faqs.question: Which exam series do IGCSE students in the UAE actually sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The February/March series that appears in a lot of tutoring content is offered to India only, so any revision plan pointing a UAE student at a February or March window is using the wrong country's calendar. Confirm against your school's entry statement and the board's live timetable.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge ask which administrative zone our centre is in?
faqs.answer: Because the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a family in Oud Metha this means the authoritative dates come from the school's own entry statement and the board's live timetable, not from a PDF found through a search engine. A tutoring schedule built on the wrong zone's timetable has an avoidable failure built into it.

faqs.question: Are we funding more IGCSE subjects than the equivalency rule counts?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five. One competitor page ranking for these searches states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify your child's own position through the Ministry of Education's channel, and note that tutoring is not required for equivalency at all.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does it add to the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: They need one, and it adds nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. So no part of any quoted rate is a permit fee being recovered. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you either.

faqs.question: Can we ask a teacher from my child's own school to tutor privately?
faqs.answer: That is the one arrangement to avoid. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on the wording, but do not build a plan around your child's classroom teacher. A specialist on the same syllabus code, with no conflict of interest and no stake in the school's own grades, is a cleaner arrangement.

faqs.question: Will an online session really work for a fourteen-year-old who fidgets?
faqs.answer: It depends far less on age than on what the hour contains. A session where the student watches an explanation will lose any fourteen-year-old, online or in a kitchen. A session where they are writing answers to past-paper questions under time, with the work screen-shared and marked as they go, holds attention because they are the one doing the work. Shorter, more frequent slots help, and so does a fixed hour in the week. Start with the free trial lesson, which is a real teaching session, and judge this child rather than the format.

faqs.question: Does Arabic or Islamic Education eat into the week we are planning around?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth mapping before you buy hours. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Those periods compete with IGCSE content for timetable space. Since they are excluded from the five-subject equivalency count, treat them as scheduling pressure rather than as subjects to fund support in by default.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist on our exact syllabus code is free?
faqs.answer: We say so, rather than putting a generalist in the slot and charging for it. For a common combination such as Mathematics 0580 Extended or Physics 0625, a match is usually straightforward. For narrower entries the wait can run longer, and the honest options are to wait for the right tutor, to start with a related specialist on a stated interim basis, or to not book at all. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, so the pool is every specialist on that code rather than the few willing to travel to Oud Metha, which is why the gaps are narrower than they would otherwise be.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers, mark schemes or grade boundaries with the sessions?
faqs.answer: No, and no provider should. Those documents are published and owned by Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and reproducing or redistributing them is copyright infringement. Your child's school holds the current versions and the boards publish what is available openly. A tutor's work is to teach against a mark scheme, show how marks are allocated in a specific question, and mark the student's own written answers honestly against it. If a provider advertises a downloadable library of board material as a selling point, ask who owns the copyright in it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.closingHeading: Start with the entry statement, then the free trial
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-oud-metha.closingBody: Two things cost nothing and decide most of what follows. Ask your child's school for the entry statement, so you know the board, the code and the tier you are actually buying support for. Then take the free trial lesson with a specialist matched to that code, and treat it as a teaching session rather than a sales call. What you should have at the end is a short written list of what is costing marks, separated into content and technique, and a plan whose length is set by that list rather than by a package. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time around the Oud Metha school run. Every dirham figure on this page belongs to the provider that published it.

intro.heading: The day ends later than the timetable says
paragraphs: Every IGCSE tutoring plan that collapses in Dubai collapses for the same reason: it was built on the school's finishing time rather than on the time the child actually gets home, eats something and becomes capable of thinking. For a family on Palm Jumeirah those are an hour apart, sometimes more. The school day may end at 15:00, the bus leaves at 15:20, it crosses the trunk and threads the fronds, and a Year 11 student walks through the door between 15:45 and 16:45 depending entirely on which direction the campus is and which exit the route uses.

That gap is the whole subject of this page. Island families commute in two directions. Westward into Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, where most of the British-curriculum campuses they use sit. Eastward along Jumeirah Beach Road into Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah and Al Safa, where several more do. Both runs are predictable and both are slow at the end of a school afternoon, and the practical consequence is that there are roughly four usable hours in a weekday evening for a Year 11 student who still has homework, and a tutoring plan has to live inside them honestly.

The second thing nobody plans for is the shape of the year. A Dubai school year has a long first term with October and winter breaks inside it, a mock examination fortnight that absorbs everything around it, a spring break, Ramadan with a changed daily rhythm, and then an exam series that starts earlier than families expect because entry deadlines sit months before the papers. Plan a weekly session without those on the calendar and it gets cancelled six times, at which point the family concludes that tutoring does not work for them.

So this page answers the near-me question as a scheduling question. It sets out the campuses island families use and what the journey home does to the evening. It shows which weekday evenings genuinely survive and which do not. It separates the Year 10 job from the Year 11 job, because they are different. It maps mocks, half-terms and Ramadan. It puts the published Cambridge and Pearson dates on the page, from the boards' own sources, including the entry deadlines nobody mentions. And it does the hour arithmetic for a year, so a parent can see the real commitment before buying any of it.

Delivery, stated once. Tutoring for UAE families is one-to-one and live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the emirates; home visits are a service we run only in India. On a scheduling page that is worth more than usual: an online session has no travel in front of it, so a 16:45 start is a 16:45 start, and a cancellation on a mock Monday costs nobody a wasted drive across the city.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-palm-jumeir.programmesIntro: An island family in Years 10 and 11 is sitting one of two boards and heading in one of two directions afterwards. These are the routes we support and what each means for a weekly schedule.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: The board most British-curriculum campuses near the island use, with Core and Extended entry tiers in many subjects and syllabus codes that identify the exact specification. Candidates are entered by the centre, and the tier sets the grade range available. Science subjects carry a practical component, either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on how the centre enters candidates.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your campus which zone it sits in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Used by a substantial minority of Dubai campuses and by almost all private candidates sitting through a centre. Codes such as 4MA1 for mathematics and 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for the sciences identify the specification. Practical skill in the sciences is assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical test, which changes what preparation looks like.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May and June and again in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official PDF.

programmes.name: A Level
programmes.description: The destination for most island students on a British route, and the reason the IGCSE tier decision matters. A Level teaching assumes fluency with Extended-tier content rather than Core, particularly in the sciences and mathematics. Students arriving from a single-award science route usually need a short bridging block before A Level teaching makes sense.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses within reach of Palm Jumeirah run IGCSE into A Level rather than into the Diploma. A family intending a particular sixth-form route should confirm that the Year 10 campus offers it, and ask which subject combinations actually run next year rather than which appear in a brochure.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The other sixth-form route, available at the IB campuses in Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and along the coast. A student crossing from IGCSE into the Diploma meets a different assessment language - internally assessed components with published criteria, and six subjects plus a core - and the shift is best introduced in the summer rather than discovered in October.
programmes.countryNote: Three of the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 run International Baccalaureate programmes, widening the sixth-form choice for island families. The IGCSE grades that make that choice possible are being earned in Years 10 and 11, which is the practical argument for starting support in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-palm-jumeir.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects island families most often ask about, with the specific thing each one tends to cost a candidate. Scheduling matters here too: the subjects that need weekly continuity are not the same as the ones that respond to a short block.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Needs weekly continuity more than any other subject, because fluency decays. Marks go on method lines never written down, on premature rounding, and on calculator work presented without the reasoning. The tier decision matters most here and is reviewed latest.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity is the commonest complaint and formula rearrangement is usually the real problem. Graph questions reward gradients taken from widely separated points, and unit conversion done at the start of a question rather than the end.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations decide the grade. State symbols, units and significant figures leak marks from students who understand the chemistry perfectly. The organic sequence rewards pattern recognition over separate memorisation of each reaction.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Extended-response technique rather than content. Answers that describe when an explanation was asked for earn nothing, and the named example a mark scheme expects is not optional. Responds well to a short block of marked written answers.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses carry the paper. Students lose marks for summarising a text instead of analysing how it achieves its effect, and for ignoring the audience and purpose the question specified.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Quotation handling and argument structure. A student who knows the text and cannot build a paragraph around a short embedded quotation plateaus in the middle grades, and that is a few weeks of deliberate practice rather than a rereading.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Command-term discipline and diagram accuracy. Evaluation questions answered with description earn little however fluent, and application to the specific case in the stimulus is what separates the top band.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main mathematics course by students heading for A Level mathematics or engineering. A genuine extra workload in Year 11, and worth timetabling deliberately rather than absorbing into an existing session.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithm and pseudocode questions reward tracing code by hand before writing anything. The theory sections are memorisable and the practical sections are not, so the two need different kinds of session.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Timetabled in every Dubai private school alongside the IGCSE programme whether or not it is entered as an examined subject. It does not count towards the five subjects the Ministry of Education requires at equivalency, which families planning a subject list need to know.

sections.heading: The Palm Jumeirah school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Start with the only number that matters: when is the child capable of a lesson? Not when school ends, and not when the bus arrives. A Year 11 student who walks in at 16:15 needs food, a change of clothes and twenty minutes of nothing before anything useful happens. That puts the real start of the evening somewhere between 16:45 and 17:30 for most island addresses, and a tutoring plan that pretends otherwise gets abandoned inside a month while everybody blames the tutor.

The table below is built from the two directions island families commute. Westward into Al Sufouh and Al Barsha is the shorter and more predictable run. Eastward along Jumeirah Beach Road is longer and less consistent, because the road narrows in places and the afternoon flow is unforgiving. Within the island, trunk and Golden Mile addresses are consistently quicker than the fronds, and the Crescent and Shoreline are consistently slowest, because a bus threads several fronds before it reaches the outer edge.

Treat every time in the table as indicative. Your campus's transport office is the only authority on its own routes, and routes change between terms as enrolment shifts. What the table is really showing is a shape, and the shape is stable: the further the campus and the further out the island address, the later the first usable slot, and the more valuable a weekend morning becomes relative to a weekday evening.

One practical recommendation that costs nothing. For the first fortnight of a new academic year, write down the actual arrival time every day. Families consistently remember the best day rather than the median one, and then book a 16:30 session that works on Mondays and fails on the other three. Fifteen minutes of record-keeping produces a slot that survives the year, which is worth more than any amount of negotiating with a tutor afterwards.

sections.heading: Which weekday evenings actually survive a Dubai school week
paragraphs: Dubai's school week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday and Sunday weekend, and the days are not interchangeable. Monday carries the weekend's unfinished homework and a fresh set on top. Tuesday and Wednesday are the quietest and the most reliable. Thursday is the day assessments and hand-ins cluster, because teachers set deadlines before the weekend. Friday finishes earlier at many campuses but is also the day a family actually wants back. Choosing the wrong day is the most common reason a weekly slot gets cancelled repeatedly.

Our experience across Dubai families is that Tuesday and Wednesday evenings survive at a far higher rate than Monday or Thursday, and that a Tuesday slot booked in September is still running in March while a Thursday one is not. For island families the effect is amplified, because Thursday evening is often when a family travels or has commitments off the island and the journey makes a late cancellation likelier. If you only take one scheduling recommendation from this page, take that one.

The weekend deserves its own treatment rather than being an afterthought. Friday and Saturday mornings have no commute in front of them and no competing homework behind them, which makes them the best available hours for anything requiring sustained thought: essay subjects, extended writing, long mathematics problems, past papers under time. They also open almost any tutor time zone, which widens the choice of specialist considerably. The cost is family time, and that is a real cost, so one weekend session is sustainable and two usually are not.

The table sets out what each day competes with. It is written for a Year 11 student because that is when the pressure is highest, but the pattern holds for Year 10 with lower stakes. One addition for island families specifically: if a sibling attends a campus in the opposite direction, the family's evening is governed by the later of two school runs, and the honest fix is usually a weekend slot rather than an earlier weekday one.

sections.heading: Year 10 and Year 11 are two different jobs
paragraphs: Families treat IGCSE tutoring as one thing bought at different times. It is two things. In Year 10 the job is to keep a student level with a specification while there is still room to change course, and the available levers include the entry tier, the subject combination and the board-specific habits that take months to build. In Year 11 the job is to convert what exists into marks, and the levers are technique, timed practice and triage. Confusing the two wastes money in both directions.

Year 10 support is cheaper per mark and almost nobody buys it. One session a week on the subject where the gap is widening, with marked written work in between, costs a fraction of what the same subject costs in the February of Year 11 and does far more, because content taught early is still available to be revised. It also keeps the tier decision open. A student demonstrating Extended-standard work on past paper questions through Year 10 has a case to make to a head of science; a student who only starts in Year 11 may find the entry already submitted.

Year 11 support is a different conversation and should be framed honestly. By the spring, new content will not be secure in time, and the work that moves marks is command-word discipline, working shown, units, timed practice at the correct tier, and attacking the two or three topics an error log says cost the most. That is genuinely valuable and it is finite. A tutor proposing to cover three subjects from scratch in March is selling hours, and an island family should read that proposal as information about the provider.

There is a third case worth naming because it is common on the Palm: the student who arrives mid-year from another country or another curriculum. Here the job is neither Year 10 build nor Year 11 triage but a gap audit, subject by subject, against the specification the new campus uses. That is a few diagnostic hours followed by a short targeted block, and it is the situation where an outside tutor adds the most value relative to what the school can do with a full timetable.

sections.heading: Mock fortnights, half-terms and Ramadan: planning the year rather than reacting to it
paragraphs: A Dubai school year has predictable disruptions, and every one of them is a reason families give up on tutoring. The mock examination fortnight is the biggest. During mocks a student is sitting papers most days and has no capacity for new input, and a tutor who insists on continuing is burning goodwill and hours. The right move is to pause the weekly slot, use the mock papers as the diagnostic they are, and restart afterwards with a plan built from what the mocks actually revealed.

Half-terms and the longer breaks cut the other way. An October break or a spring break is the best available time for concentrated work, because there is no homework competing and a student can do a two-hour session without an energy penalty. Island families often travel during breaks, which is fine - an online session follows the student, and a lesson from a hotel room in a different time zone is a scheduling question rather than a cancellation.

Ramadan changes the daily rhythm rather than removing it. School hours shorten, afternoons are quieter, and energy is at its lowest in the hour before Iftar, which is precisely when a conventional after-school slot sits. Post-Iftar sessions work well and are a normal request rather than an exception; so does moving to a morning slot at weekends for the month. What does not work is leaving the usual time in place and hoping. Decide before the month starts.

The table maps the year. Two notes alongside it. First, build the pauses into the plan at the start rather than negotiating them individually, because a pause agreed in advance is a plan and a pause requested on the day is a cancellation. Second, the weeks immediately after a mock fortnight are the single highest-value tutoring weeks in the year: the diagnosis is fresh, the student is motivated by a recent shock, and there is still time to act on it.

sections.heading: Exam season logistics: zones, entry deadlines and the November option
paragraphs: The dates that catch families out are not the exam dates. They are the entry deadlines, which sit months earlier and are handled by the centre rather than the family, and the zone question, which almost nobody outside an exams office knows about. Both are published by the boards, both are checkable, and both belong on a scheduling page because they determine when work has to be finished rather than when it has to start.

Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. For a Dubai parent that translates into one question to the campus: which zone is this centre in, and may we have the timetable for it? A printout of the wrong zone's dates on a kitchen wall is a real risk, not a theoretical one.

The entry-deadline pattern is best shown with Pearson, because Pearson publishes its windows in full and they apply here without qualification. The November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026; and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read those three facts together and the lag is plain: a November candidate waits into the new year for a grade, which is why a resit decision taken after results day is already a decision about the series after next. Cambridge has the same months-ahead structure across the two series a Palm Jumeirah candidate can enter, June and November, with entries closing in the spring and over the summer respectively. The February and March series is offered in India only, so a Dubai plan never counts on it, and the precise Cambridge entry date belongs to your centre's key dates rather than to a figure restated on a tutoring page.

The November series is the option island families ask about most and understand least. Both boards offer a November or winter sitting, which creates a genuine second chance for a single subject and a planning complication for everything else. It is a centre decision rather than a family one, and the entry deadline is the constraint. If a resit is a possibility, ask the exams officer about it in the term before, not after results. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official PDF rather than any restatement, including this one.

sections.heading: What a year of weekly sessions actually comes to, in hours and in AED
paragraphs: Do the hour arithmetic before looking at any rate, because the hours are what a family is really committing to. A weekly session from September to the exam series, with the mock fortnight paused and the breaks partly used, comes to roughly twenty-eight to thirty-two sessions. At one hour each that is around thirty hours for one subject across one academic year. Two subjects weekly is sixty hours and about four hundred hours of a teenager's remaining attention, which is the real constraint rather than the money.

Now put the published Dubai rates against those hours. A qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Thirty hours at the lower end of that band is a different order of commitment from thirty hours at the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table reaches AED 450 and beyond. The honest guidance is that most IGCSE problems are well served in the middle band, and the specialist band earns its premium on Extended-tier sciences and on mathematics aiming at A Level.

At the bottom, budget online tutoring is published from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Thirty hours there is inexpensive and frequently wasted, because the hour buys supervision rather than specification knowledge. At the top, premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED; thirty hours at that level is a figure most families would want a very specific reason for. In-home visits price a different product at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure, and monthly packages in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits.

Every figure above was read from the provider's own page in October 2026 and none of them is an IB Gram price. For context on scale, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. The useful conclusion from the arithmetic is not which band to choose but how few hours a year really contains: thirty hours is not very many, which is exactly why they should be aimed at a diagnosed problem rather than spread across three subjects hopefully.

sections.heading: Why the search says near me, and why the answer is a screen
paragraphs: Everything above is a scheduling argument, and the scheduling argument resolves the proximity question on its own. An online session has no journey in front of it. A 16:45 start is 16:45, not 16:45 plus whatever the trunk road is doing. A session paused for a mock fortnight costs nobody a wasted drive, so it gets paused honestly rather than pushed through. A session moved to a Saturday morning because a sibling's school run collides with Tuesday is a calendar edit rather than a renegotiation. These are the practical reasons island families settle on online delivery, more often than any argument about tutor quality.

The quality argument exists as well and it is simple. A drive-time radius from Palm Jumeirah selects for willingness to travel to the island, which is not a teaching qualification. Choosing by subject, board and tier selects for the ability to teach the thing your child is sitting. For Extended-tier Cambridge Chemistry or Pearson 4MA1 at the top of the grade range, the second criterion is the only one that matters, and it is not satisfied by anybody's proximity.

What online delivery does not do is replace the school or supervise an examination. Practical work and any practical examination happen at the centre, under the centre's entry and supervision. Nothing about our model changes that, and any provider implying otherwise should be treated with suspicion. What the screen does is deliver teaching, marking and technique coaching, and for all three it is at least as good as a kitchen table and better at marking, because written work can be annotated live while the student watches each mark being awarded or withheld.

Stated plainly for the record: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Palm Jumeirah families are one-to-one and live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, in a slot built around the island school run rather than around a tutor's convenience.

sections.heading: Starting from Palm Jumeirah, and the weeks we will tell you not to book
paragraphs: The sequence is short and the first step is the one families skip. Record the actual arrival time home for a fortnight, then tell us the campus, the board, the syllabus codes and the entry tiers, the subject that is causing the problem, and what the last marked piece of work looked like. With the arrival times we can propose a slot that survives; without them we are guessing at a time that works on the best day of the week.

Then a free trial session with a subject specialist, in the proposed slot so that the timing is tested as well as the teaching. The session opens with a timed section at the correct tier rather than with introductions, because that is the only way to separate a content gap from a technique gap. Afterwards you receive a written note naming the gaps in priority order with an hour count against each, and a recommended day of the week based on what the subject actually needs.

Now the weeks we will advise against. The mock fortnight itself, for the reasons above. The first fortnight of a new academic year, when timetables have not settled and a slot booked then usually has to move. The week immediately before a family's travel, where a single session achieves nothing and resets the rhythm. And the final three weeks before a series, if you are starting from nothing, because what can honestly be done in that window is triage and a tutor who promises more is not being straight with you.

And the things we will not do. We will not promise a grade or an improvement; a provider who does is describing their own sales process. We will not write or redraft coursework. We will not describe IB Gram as approved, accredited or partnered with Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA or any school, because we hold none of those and in this market the claim is as common as it is risky. What we will do is set a slot that survives a Dubai school year, mark the work honestly, and review it against the school's own marks at six weeks rather than against a feeling.

process.title: Record the actual arrival time for a fortnight
process.description: Two weeks of real data on when your child gets back to the island, rather than the school's finishing time. Families remember the best day and book around it. Fifteen minutes of record-keeping produces a slot that still exists in March, which is worth more than any negotiation afterwards.

process.title: Send the board, the codes and the tiers
process.description: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, the syllabus code for each subject, and the entry tier where there is one. Ask the department in writing if you do not have them, and ask which Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in while you are there.

process.title: A free trial in the proposed slot
process.description: We schedule the trial at the time we think will work, so the timing gets tested alongside the teaching. The session opens with a timed section at the correct tier rather than a conversation, because that separates a content gap from a technique gap inside an hour.

process.title: A written plan with a day and an hour count
process.description: You receive a note naming the gaps in priority order with hours against each, plus a recommended day of the week. Tuesday and Wednesday are recommended far more often than Thursday, for reasons the calendar section explains rather than for anybody's convenience.

process.title: A year calendar with the pauses already in it
process.description: Mock fortnight paused, breaks used or skipped by agreement, Ramadan moved to post-Iftar or a weekend morning, and the post-mock weeks protected as the highest-value block. Agreeing the pauses in advance is what turns a weekly slot into a plan rather than a series of cancellations.

whyPoints.title: The slot is built around your commute, not our diary
whyPoints.description: A Palm Jumeirah Year 11 student is home between 15:45 and 16:45 depending on direction and address, and the first usable slot follows from that rather than from a tutor's availability. We propose a time, test it in the trial, and change it if the first fortnight shows it does not hold.

whyPoints.title: Tuesday and Wednesday, not Thursday
whyPoints.description: Thursday is when Dubai campuses cluster hand-ins and assessments before the weekend, and a Thursday slot is cancelled far more often than a midweek one. We recommend days on that basis. It sounds trivial and it is the difference between twenty-eight sessions a year and sixteen.

whyPoints.title: Pauses planned, not negotiated
whyPoints.description: The mock fortnight is paused by prior agreement, the post-mock weeks are protected as the most valuable in the year, and Ramadan is moved before the month starts rather than during it. A pause agreed in advance is a plan; a pause requested on the day is a cancellation with a reason attached.

whyPoints.description: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and says using the wrong zone's timetable is the centre's risk. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers. We put the published dates on the page with the board named, and tell you to work from the live official PDF.

whyPoints.title: The hour arithmetic before the rate
whyPoints.description: A weekly session across an academic year is roughly thirty hours, which is not very many. Seeing that first changes how a family spends them: one diagnosed subject rather than three hopeful ones. Every AED figure we publish is attributed to the provider who published it, read in October 2026.

whyPoints.description: The mock fortnight, the first fortnight of a new year, the week before family travel, and the final three weeks if you are starting from nothing. Declining those bookings costs us and is the only honest answer, and it is the clearest signal we can give about how the rest of the advice is meant.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE schools do children living on Palm Jumeirah attend?
faqs.answer: Island families commute in two directions. Westward into Al Sufouh, Al Barsha 1 and Al Barsha South, which is the shorter and more predictable run and where most of the British-curriculum campuses they use sit. Eastward along Jumeirah Beach Road into Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah and Al Safa, which is longer and less consistent. Several campuses in both directions run IGCSE into A Level and some into the IB Diploma, so a family intending a particular sixth-form route should confirm the campus offers it rather than assume the sixth form follows the school.

faqs.question: What time does the school bus usually get back to Palm Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: Somewhere between 15:45 and 17:00, depending on which direction the campus is and where on the island you live. Trunk and Golden Mile addresses on the shorter westward run are often home by 15:45. The outer fronds, Crescent and Shoreline on the longer eastward run can be 16:45 or later, because a bus threads several fronds before reaching the outer edge. Treat any published figure, including ours, as indicative and record the real arrival times for a fortnight before booking a recurring slot.

faqs.question: When is the earliest a weekday IGCSE session can realistically start?
faqs.answer: For most island addresses, 16:45. A trunk or Golden Mile address on the short westward run can manage 16:30. The outer fronds and the Crescent are realistically 17:00 to 17:30. The reason is not the bus time but what has to happen after it: food, a change of clothes and twenty minutes of nothing before a teenager can think. A plan that starts at the arrival time looks efficient on paper and is abandoned inside a month, usually with the tutor taking the blame.

faqs.question: Is Sunday a usable tutoring day for a Dubai school week?
faqs.answer: Sunday is part of the Dubai weekend, so it is usable in the sense that there is no school run, and it is the day most families least want to give up. Where it works well is as a single longer session for an essay subject or a timed past paper, with no homework competing. Where it fails is as a second weekend session on top of a Saturday one, which almost no family sustains past November. Friday and Saturday mornings are the slots island families choose more often.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week fit around Year 11 homework?
faqs.answer: One in almost every case, two when there are genuinely two separate problems and the student has the capacity, and three essentially never. A Year 11 student in Dubai carries eight or nine subjects, mandatory UAE subject hours, and a commute that eats an hour a day. The constraint is attention rather than money: a weekly session across an academic year is only about thirty hours, and spreading those across three subjects produces three thin plans instead of one that works.

faqs.question: Do lessons have to stop during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: No, but the time has to change and the decision should be made before the month starts rather than during it. School hours shorten, afternoons are quieter, and energy is lowest in the hour before Iftar, which is exactly where a conventional after-school slot sits. Post-Iftar sessions work well and are a normal arrangement rather than a special request, and a weekend morning slot for the month is the other common solution. Leaving the usual time in place and hoping is what produces a string of cancellations.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams actually sat by students in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and those two are what a Palm Jumeirah candidate can enter. Checkpoint tests in March, May and October are a lower-secondary diagnostic, not an IGCSE sitting, and the February and March series is offered in India only, so neither belongs in a Dubai plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Which series your child sits is a centre decision, so ask the exams officer, and work from the board's live official timetable rather than any restatement.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge timetable zone matter for an island family?
faqs.answer: Because the dates differ by zone and the wrong printout is a real risk. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The practical action is a single question to your campus: which zone is this centre in, and may we have that zone's timetable? Then check every date you have written down against it.

faqs.question: Can my child sit the November IGCSE series instead of June?
faqs.answer: Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run a November series, so it is possible, but it is a centre decision rather than a family one and the entry deadline is the constraint. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers. Cambridge closes November entries over the preceding summer, which is before June results have even been issued, and Pearson's November 2026 series had closed its entries long before its papers began in late October. If a resit or a split series is a possibility, raise it with the exams officer in the term before results rather than after them, because by then the entry window for the next series may already be closing.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost for a family living on the Palm?
faqs.answer: Start from the hours. A weekly session from September to the exam series, with the mock fortnight paused, is roughly thirty sessions. Against that, published Dubai rates read in October 2026 run AED 45 to 150 for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Those are market figures with sources, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is a weekend block better than two weekday sessions?
faqs.answer: For essay subjects, extended writing and timed past papers, usually yes. A Friday or Saturday morning has no commute in front of it and no homework behind it, so a ninety-minute to two-hour session is genuinely productive rather than endured. It also opens almost any tutor time zone, which widens the choice of specialist. For mathematics, where fluency decays between sessions, a weekly weekday slot still beats a longer weekend one, because the rhythm matters more than the total minutes.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions during the school's mock exam fortnight?
faqs.answer: We pause them, by agreement made at the start of the year rather than on the day. During mocks a student sits papers most days and has no capacity for new input, so a session either gets cancelled or gets endured, and neither helps. The mock papers themselves are the best diagnostic available all year. The weeks immediately after are the highest-value tutoring weeks in the calendar, because the evidence is fresh and specific and there is still time to act on it, so we protect those instead.

faqs.question: How far ahead should we book for the spring term?
faqs.answer: Before the autumn mock results arrive, if you want a particular evening. Demand for midweek slots rises sharply in January across Dubai, and Tuesday and Wednesday evenings fill first because they are the days that survive. For Extended-tier sciences and mathematics aiming at A Level the pool of specialists is smaller, so a January start arranged in November is comfortable and the same request made in February often is not. If a slot is more than a fortnight away we tell you so rather than keeping you waiting.

faqs.question: Do you follow the school's scheme of work or the full specification?
faqs.answer: Both, in that order of priority. Week to week the sessions track what the class is doing, because a student needs to succeed at the work in front of them and because arriving at a lesson ahead of the class causes confusion rather than confidence. Alongside that, the tutor keeps a checklist against the published specification for the exact syllabus code, so anything the scheme reaches late or lightly is flagged and planned for rather than discovered in the revision term.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry of Education count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One competitor page currently ranking in this market states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own pages, and note that tutoring is not a requirement of the process.

You will leave with a plan that already has the mock fortnight, the breaks and Ramadan written into it. Lessons run one-to-one and live online, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Reading the Dubai rate ladder from the bottom up
paragraphs: Almost every comparison of tutoring rates in this market starts at the premium end and works down, which flatters the expensive option. Start at the bottom instead, because that is where a family's money is genuinely at risk of being wasted and where the decisions are easiest to get wrong in both directions. The cheapest published online rates in Dubai are AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik. Qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350. Specialists sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium examiner-branded providers reach AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Every figure there belongs to the provider named and was read in October 2026.

Read from the bottom, the ladder stops being about quality and becomes about capability. The AED 33 to AED 65 band buys somebody who can explain a textbook question and keep a fourteen-year-old working through the homework the school set. That is a real service and for a Year 9 student with a motivation problem it is the right purchase. What it does not reliably buy is somebody who can take a marked Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 2, identify the two method marks lost on a reverse-percentage question, and design three weeks of work around them. Those are different jobs and only one of them needs the specialist rate.

The second thing the ladder conceals is subject count. A Year 11 student in this cluster sits eight or nine IGCSE subjects. Nothing in a rate card tells a parent how many of those should be funded, and the instinctive answer, all the weak ones, is usually wrong. A week filled with paid sessions removes the unsupervised practice time where the subjects are actually learned, and the effect is that nine partly-tutored subjects produce less than three properly-tutored ones.

The third is Pearl Jumeira itself. The island is reclaimed land off the Jumeirah 1 shoreline reached by a single causeway, which means in-home quotations here sit towards the top of the Dubai band for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. A tutor crossing Al Wasl Road at the end of the school day and queueing onto the island spends thirty to fifty minutes each way, and that time is inside the hourly figure whether or not anybody itemises it. It is a distance premium presented in the same currency as a quality premium.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. On a page about cost the honest version of that is simple arithmetic: nothing in the rate pays for the causeway, and the band a family ends up in is determined by what the work requires rather than by where they live.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-pearl-jumei.subjectsIntro: A Year 11 student sits eight or nine subjects and almost no family should fund eight or nine. These are the subjects Pearl Jumeira households most often pay for, with an honest note on how much tutoring each tends to need.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The most funded subject and usually the right first choice, because it is compulsory, it gates post-16 options, and gaps compound. Needs a standing weekly hour rather than a block, which makes it the largest single line in most budgets here.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Tends to need help with calculation technique rather than content, which is a short, well-defined job. Frequently resolvable in a block of six to eight sessions rather than a two-year booking, provided the diagnosis is accurate.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry is where the grade separates, and it is procedural. A funded term aimed specifically at moles, limiting reagent and percentage yield is usually better value than year-long general support.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and recall-dependent, which means it responds to frequent short contact. Often the subject where a cheaper band is genuinely adequate, because the task is testing and consolidation rather than diagnosis.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Improves with marked writing rather than with explanation, so the useful arrangement is fewer sessions with real writing between them. Over-funded more often than any other subject in this community.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Text-specific, which means a tutor must have taught the set texts the school has chosen. Ask about the texts before the rate; a mismatch here wastes more money than a higher hourly figure would.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Command terms carry the grade and students write knowledge where evaluation is wanted. A bounded problem that responds to a handful of sessions, which makes it a poor candidate for a standing weekly booking.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: One tutor across all three disciplines rather than three specialists, which is a significant saving families frequently miss. Engaging three subject tutors for a 0654 candidate is one of the clearest overspends in this market.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Specifications have been revised in recent years, so an out-of-date tutor is hard to detect and expensive to discover. Worth paying the middle band here for somebody current rather than the cheapest available.

subjects.levels: Cambridge and Pearson specifications, alongside KHDA requirements
subjects.description: Sits beside the KHDA mandatory subject requirement. Teachers of Arabic in Dubai schools need appropriate KHDA approval for the subject, and additional content requires prior Ministry permission, which limits how tutoring here can be described.

sections.heading: The ladder, cheapest first, and what each band stops being able to do
paragraphs: The table reads from the lowest published rate upwards. The right-hand column is the one to read first, because it names what the band cannot do rather than what it claims. All figures belong to the providers named and were read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price list.

Two transitions on this ladder matter and the rest are marketing. The first is between the budget band and the qualified subject band, somewhere around AED 150. Below it you are buying explanation and supervision; above it you are buying teaching against a named syllabus code. For a Year 11 student twelve weeks from a series, that transition is the whole decision, and paying below it is a false economy of exactly the kind that looks sensible on a spreadsheet.

The second is between the qualified band and the specialist band, somewhere around AED 270. That one is worth paying only for specific work: converting a marked paper into a diagnosis, rebuilding non-calculator technique, or moving a strong candidate from a grade 7 to a grade 8 or 9 where the remaining marks are all technique. For general subject teaching the qualified band is adequate and the specialist premium buys very little.

The premium band at AED 500 to AED 650 is a different product again, and it is honest to say that most families in this community do not need it. It prices reputation and scarcity. There are situations where that is rational, usually involving a narrow subject with almost no supply, and there are many more where it is a parent buying reassurance at four times the rate that would have done the job.

sections.heading: What you actually give up at the bottom of the ladder
paragraphs: This deserves its own section because the cheap band is both underrated and misused. Underrated, because a great deal of what families need is not diagnosis. Misused, because it gets bought for the one job it cannot do.

What the AED 33 to AED 65 band does well is presence and momentum. A student who will not start their homework will start it with somebody on a call. A student who needs biology definitions tested will have them tested. A Year 8 student who has drifted in maths will be pulled back by somebody competent working through the textbook. For all of that, paying four times the rate adds nothing, and a family who does so has not bought better teaching, only a more expensive version of the same service.

What the band cannot do is read a marked Extended past paper and tell you that your child is losing marks because they are not writing the method line before the answer, that this costs roughly four marks a paper, and that three weeks of specific work will recover most of it. That requires somebody who has marked those papers against the published scheme and knows what the examiner awards. It is a genuinely different skill and it is the thing the middle and specialist bands are selling.

The practical rule is to match the band to the task rather than to the stage. In Year 10, with time available and no diagnosis in hand, the cheaper band plus one specialist diagnostic hour is frequently the best value arrangement in the whole market. In the twelve weeks before a series, with marks to recover and little time, it is not.

sections.heading: How many of eight or nine subjects should actually be funded
paragraphs: This is the question that moves more money than the hourly rate does, and almost nobody addresses it. A Year 11 student sits eight or nine IGCSE subjects. A parent looking at a report with four weak grades feels the obvious answer is four tutors. The obvious answer is wrong, for two reasons that compound.

The first is the week. School in this cluster ends between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the causeway approach and the drive home take thirty to forty-five minutes, activity programmes run to roughly 6pm, and useful work stops around 8:30pm on a school night. That leaves two, at most three, tutored hours a week before unsupervised study time starts disappearing. Four standing bookings do not fit into that week; they displace the practice where subjects are actually learned.

The second is that weak grades frequently share a cause. Four subjects losing marks on extended response questions is one problem about writing to the mark allocation, not four subject problems. Four subjects losing marks on calculation is one problem about quantitative technique. A single diagnostic hour across the marked scripts will usually show which, and when it does, the budget halves and the outcome improves.

The table below sets out a spending sequence that fits a real week. It is deliberately conservative, because the pattern that produces the best results in this community is one well-funded subject, one diagnosed block, and nothing else. Families who fund more than that generally report the same outcome: more sessions attended, the same marks, and a student with no time to think.

sections.heading: Group classes, one-to-one, and where the saving actually is
paragraphs: Small group tuition is presented as the budget alternative to one-to-one and it sometimes is. Whether it is depends entirely on what the student needs, and the distinction is sharper than the marketing suggests.

A group works when the content is the same for everybody and the task is exposition. A session walking four Year 10 students through Cambridge 0580 Extended trigonometry is a genuinely efficient use of a teacher, and splitting the cost is a real saving rather than a compromise. A group also works for recall testing, where the competitive element helps, and for timed paper practice followed by shared mark-scheme discussion.

A group fails when the task is diagnostic. Four students lose marks in four different places, and an hour divided four ways is fifteen minutes each on the thing that matters to them. This is why group classes are often good value in Year 10 and poor value in the term before a series, when the remaining gains are individual. Families who switch at the right point get the saving without the cost.

There is a second consideration that cost comparisons miss. Tuition-centre group classes in Dubai are delivered by organisations with premises, which is a different legal category from an individual tutor. An operation with premises and staff requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific permit for a specific kind of business, and it is a reasonable thing for a parent to ask about before enrolling a child in a centre.

sections.heading: The cost nobody includes: exam entry, retakes and the calendar
paragraphs: A tutoring budget that ignores the examination calendar will be wrong by the amount of one resit, and families regularly discover this in August. Setting the dates out properly also happens to be something no competitor page in this search does.

UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any February or March dates quoted to a Dubai family should be disregarded entirely. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Entries are made months before the papers, by the school, and they carry fees that appear on a school bill rather than a tutoring one.

Checkable reference points help with planning. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations that give the shape of a year reliably, though the live official timetable is what should be checked before acting, since provisional timetables get revised.

There is also a Cambridge administrative point with a real cost attached. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the timetable differs by zone, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A revision plan built from the wrong timetable is money spent against the wrong dates. Ask the school which zone it sits in. The practical budgeting consequence of all this is to hold a reserve: a November resit decided in August needs funding in September, and the result then arrives the following January rather than in the summer.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of a Dubai school bill
paragraphs: Tutoring is one line in a larger education budget, and in Dubai the rest of that budget has recently been unusually stable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total.

The wider market continues to expand. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six openings during 2025-26 and a 6 per cent rise in enrolment.

Two consequences follow for a family on this island. A stable fee position means a tutoring budget can be set across the two IGCSE years rather than revised annually, which favours the steady weekly arrangement over reactive block-buying when a report arrives. And a market with deep UK curriculum supply means plenty of available tutors and no reliable price signal distinguishing those who have taught your child's specification from those who have taught the subject, which is why the questions matter more than the rate.

The last point about context is proportion. Against school fees, a weekly hour at the middle band across two IGCSE years is a modest addition. Against the same two years funded at four standing bookings and specialist rates, it is not, and the second arrangement does not produce proportionally better results. The expensive mistake in this market is rarely the hourly rate; it is the number of hours bought and the time they take away from the student's own practice.

sections.heading: Checking who you are paying, which costs nothing
paragraphs: Before money changes hands there is one free set of checks worth running, and it takes two questions. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years.

Because there is no fee, a missing permit is a decision rather than an obstacle, and eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, a specific amount quoted at you cannot be substantiated by anybody.

The second question concerns who may teach whom. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So the parent asks whether a permit is held, and whether their child attends the school where the person teaches.

A final point on money and claims. No tutor should be promising a grade, a specific improvement or any guaranteed outcome, and no refund tied to a result should be offered, because nobody can honestly stand behind it. A provider publishing a satisfaction percentage, a star rating or a success statistic without stating the sample size, the date and the method is publishing a number that cannot be checked. Those are the signals to weigh alongside the rate, and all of them are free to examine.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest realistic rate for an IGCSE tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The lowest published figures are AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik, both online. That band is honest about what it provides: explanation, homework momentum and recall testing. It is the right purchase for a Year 8 or 9 student who has drifted, and the wrong one twelve weeks before a series, because it cannot reliably read a marked Extended past paper against the published mark scheme and tell you which method marks were lost and what they cost.

faqs.question: Where on the Dubai rate ladder does the capability actually change?
faqs.answer: At two points. Around AED 150 the purchase shifts from explanation and supervision to teaching against a named syllabus code, which is the transition that matters most for a Year 11 student. Around AED 270 it shifts again to mark-scheme level work: converting a marked script into a costed diagnosis, rebuilding non-calculator technique, or moving a strong candidate from a 7 to an 8 or 9. Everything above that prices reputation and scarcity rather than a further capability.

faqs.question: Is the AED 650 premium band ever worth paying for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and less often than it is paid. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. It is rational where a subject has almost no supply and the alternative is nobody, or where a very specific niche within a specification is involved. For general subject teaching it buys nothing the qualified or specialist bands do not, and in this community most of what it sells is reassurance at roughly four times the rate that would have done the work.

faqs.question: Why are tutors more expensive for Pearl Jumeira than for Jumeirah 1?
faqs.answer: Because of the causeway. The island is reclaimed land reached by a single access road from the Jumeirah 1 shoreline, so a visiting tutor crosses Al Wasl Road at the end of the school day and then queues onto the island, thirty to fifty minutes each way in the late afternoon. That unpaid time is inside the hourly figure whether or not it is itemised. Identical tutoring quoted a few streets inland is often lower, which is the cleanest measure of how much of a rate is distance.

faqs.question: How many of my child's nine IGCSE subjects should we pay for?
faqs.answer: Usually one standing booking plus one diagnosed block, and almost never four. School here ends between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the drive home takes thirty to forty-five minutes, activities run to about 6pm and useful work stops around 8:30pm. That leaves two or three tutored hours before unsupervised practice time disappears, and unsupervised practice is where subjects are learned. Four weak grades also frequently share one cause, which a single diagnostic hour across the marked scripts will reveal.

faqs.question: What is the single best-value hour in an IGCSE tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic session at the specialist band, bought first, spent reading marked scripts across several subjects and producing a topic list with approximate mark values attached. It costs AED 270 to AED 450 once and it regularly halves what follows, because it distinguishes four subject problems from one shared problem such as writing to the mark allocation or quantitative technique. It is also the hour families least often buy, because it does not feel like progress until the list arrives.

faqs.question: Are small group IGCSE classes better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For exposition, yes. Walking four Year 10 students through Cambridge 0580 Extended trigonometry is an efficient use of a teacher and splitting the cost is a genuine saving. For diagnosis, no: four students lose marks in four different places, and an hour divided four ways gives each fifteen minutes on what matters to them. The sensible pattern is group work in Year 10 and one-to-one in the term before the series, which captures the saving without paying for it in results.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre need a different permit from an individual tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is reasonable to ask. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal category and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

faqs.question: Should we budget for a November resit from the start?
faqs.answer: Holding a reserve is sensible rather than pessimistic. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in June and November, and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November, so a resit route exists. The timing is what needs planning: a decision taken in August needs funding in September, and the grade then arrives months later. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which gives the shape. Confirm current deadlines with the school's exams officer rather than relying on any website.

faqs.question: Could a revision plan be built against the wrong exam timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is an avoidable waste of money. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the timetable differs by zone, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school which zone it sits in and make sure any tutor planning a revision schedule is working from that version rather than one found through a search.

faqs.question: Does Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 need three separate science tutors?
faqs.answer: No, and engaging three is one of the clearest overspends available in this market. 0654 is a double award: one set of papers covers biology, chemistry and physics and produces two grades, with a longer combined theory paper and a practical component at 20 per cent. The depth in each discipline is shallower than in the separate sciences. What the student needs is one tutor comfortable across all three at the level the combined paper demands, which is a third of the cost of three specialists.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees going up, and does that affect tutoring plans?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For a tutoring budget that stability is genuinely useful, because it means a two-year figure can be set in advance rather than revised each year, which favours a steady weekly arrangement from Year 10 over reactive block-buying whenever a report arrives.

faqs.question: Should I trust a tutoring company that publishes a success rate?
faqs.answer: Not without the sample size, the date and the method on the same page. A satisfaction percentage, a star rating or a pass statistic published without those three things is a number nobody can check, and the competitor audit for this market found pages showing different review totals in different places on the same page. No grade or improvement can honestly be guaranteed either, and no refund should be tied to a result. Those signals are free to examine and more informative than the rate.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram charge more for coming to Pearl Jumeira?
faqs.answer: The question does not arise, because IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so nothing in the rate covers the causeway approach, and the figure is identical whether a family lives on the island, in Jumeirah 1 or further along the coast. On a cost page that is the most relevant thing about the delivery model.
