intro.heading: Start with what costs nothing, then buy what does not exist for free
paragraphs: A tutoring search is usually the third thing a worried family does and should be the fifth. Before it, there are four free sources of help that most students in this corridor have not fully used: the subject teacher, who sets the papers and knows the mark scheme; the school's own clinic or support sessions, which exist in most schools and are poorly attended; the published mark schemes, which are the clearest statement available of what earns credit; and the student's own marked mock script, which almost always goes in a drawer.

That is not an argument against paying for help. It is an argument for knowing what paid help is for. A tutor is worth money where something cannot be obtained free: individual diagnosis across a whole paper, sustained one-to-one attention on one student's specific error pattern, and the discipline of timed practice someone else marks and reconciles. Those are real and they are not available in a classroom of twenty-four.

Remraam makes the free options unusually accessible. South View School sits close to the community and takes students through Year 11, so a student here can realistically stay after school for a clinic and still be home at a reasonable hour, which is not true from Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square. A family in this community that has not tried the school route first is leaving something genuinely useful unused.

The second half of this page is about where paid hours go once the free help is exhausted, and the answer is not evenly distributed across subjects. Some IGCSE subjects return marks for an hour of tutoring very quickly because their losses are mechanical. Others need weeks of steady work. Spending the same money on the wrong subject is the commonest waste in this market after buying the wrong board's past papers.

One more reason to order things this way: a family that has used the free help arrives at a paid session with better information. They know what the subject teacher said, they have read a mark scheme, and they have the mock script in hand. A first session built on that is worth two built on a general description of worry, and it often turns out that the paid help needed is a single diagnostic hour rather than a term of weekly sessions.

IB Gram delivers lessons one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the board and code the student is entered for. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and no sentence here should be read as an offer to arrive at an Al Thamam or Al Ramth address. The sections below take the free options first, then the paid ones, in that order on purpose.

programmes.name: Cambridge International GCSE
programmes.description: Linear two-year courses with Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, where Core caps the available grade in the middle of the scale. Codes are public: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and the February and March series is offered in India only. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states the correct zone timetable must be used, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes include 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology and 4EA1 English Language A, with Mathematics tiered Foundation and Higher. Question phrasing and the expected amount of written method differ from Cambridge.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. As dated examples, the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: The tier decision
programmes.description: Where a subject is tiered, the entry caps the grade. Core and Foundation cannot reach the top of the scale however well a student performs on the day, and the entry is lodged months before the papers on the basis of work already produced.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one decision worth spending free help on first. Ask the school which tier a child is entered for, what evidence would change it, and the last date an amendment is possible. Those three answers are more valuable than a term of general tutoring.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-remraam.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most requested from this corridor, with a note on how quickly an hour of help tends to return marks in each.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The fastest returns in the set. Diagram labelling, axis conventions and precise terminology are mechanical, so a fortnight of drilling moves marks reliably without any new content being learned.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Fast, for the same reason. Unbalanced equations, missing state symbols and unclaimed qualitative analysis marks are presentation failures rather than knowledge gaps, and they are drillable.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Fast for technique, slow for foundations. Early rounding, unshown method and question-order discipline move in weeks; absent algebraic fluency needs months and should be said so.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fast where the cause is mathematical. Rearrangement, standard form and gradients carry marks across the paper, and repairing them lifts chemistry at the same time.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Moderate. Application to the named business is a trainable habit, but it has to be practised across several case studies before it holds under exam pressure.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Slower. Terminology precision and command-term reading respond to steady practice over four to eight weeks rather than to a sharp intervention, so it should be started earlier.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Slower still. Register and task form can be taught quickly; the writing fluency underneath improves over months, and promising otherwise would be dishonest.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Slow but reliable. Quotation security and essay structure respond to repetition, and timing failures are fixable quickly even where the analysis takes longer to develop.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Fast in the mechanical areas. Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and data representation are rule-based, and students who code well often lose exactly these marks.

sections.heading: Six sources of help, four of them free
paragraphs: Comparing paid help against nothing is the wrong comparison. The right one puts every available source side by side, including the ones that cost nothing, because the free ones are genuinely good at some things and useless at others, and knowing which is which saves money.

The subject teacher is the strongest free resource and the most underused. They set the mock, they know the mark scheme, they know the student's work across two years, and in most schools they will answer a specific question about a specific loss. The limitation is availability: a teacher with five classes cannot sit with one student for an hour a week, which is precisely the thing a tutor sells.

School clinics and support sessions exist in most Dubai private schools and are poorly attended. Published mark schemes are the clearest available statement of what earns credit, and almost no student has read one properly. The marked mock script is the single best diagnostic in the year and is usually filed after the grade is read. None of those four costs anything, and together they close a meaningful share of a typical gap.

What they cannot provide is individual diagnosis across a whole paper, sustained attention on one student's own error pattern week after week, and timed practice that somebody else marks and reconciles against the scheme. That is the honest case for paying, and it is the only case this page makes.

There is a sixth source worth naming, which is other students. A study pair sitting the same code and tier, marking each other's papers against the published scheme, is genuinely effective and costs nothing. It fails where neither student can interpret the scheme, which is why one session on how to read a mark scheme can be worth more than ten on content.

sections.heading: Which subjects repay a tutoring hour fastest
paragraphs: Subjects are not equal in how quickly they convert help into marks, and the difference is large enough to change where a family spends. The pattern follows one rule: the more mechanical the loss, the faster the return. Where marks go missing because of a convention the student does not follow, a fortnight of drilling recovers them. Where they go missing because something was never learned, months are needed.

Economics sits at the fast end. Diagram labelling, axis conventions, curve-shift explanations and precise terminology are rule-based, and a student who already understands the economics can gain visibly within two or three weeks. Chemistry is close behind, because equations, state symbols and qualitative analysis marks are presentation rather than comprehension. Computer Science behaves the same way with pseudocode and trace tables.

Mathematics and physics are split cases. Their technique losses are fast: rounding discipline, shown method, question order, rearrangement at speed. Their foundation losses are slow, and a provider who does not distinguish between the two is guessing. The same marked script that reveals one reveals the other, which is why diagnosis precedes any proposal here.

Biology, English Language and English Literature sit at the slower end. Their marks depend on terminology precision, register and sustained writing, which improve steadily rather than sharply. They are worth tutoring and they should be started earlier, and anyone promising a transformation in them six weeks out is selling something that does not exist.

A caution about the ranking itself. It describes typical cases rather than any individual student, and the marked script overrides it every time. A student whose chemistry losses are genuinely conceptual will not gain in three weeks whatever this table says, and a student whose biology problem is purely command-term reading will gain faster than the slow label suggests.

sections.heading: What a student can genuinely fix without paying anybody
paragraphs: Several of the most common IGCSE losses are self-correctable, and saying so is more useful than pretending otherwise. The qualification for a self-fix is that the student can detect the error themselves once they know to look for it, which rules out anything requiring interpretation of a whole paper.

Early rounding qualifies. The rule is to hold full precision until the final line and round once, and a student who writes that rule on the front of their folder will apply it. Unshown method qualifies partly: a student who reads one mark scheme properly, for a paper they have already sat, usually sees where the marks sat and adjusts. Question-order discipline qualifies, because it only requires a decision made in advance and a watch.

Command-term reading is the best self-fix available. Take ten past-paper questions, cover the stems, and state what each command term obliges before writing anything. It needs no teacher, works in a fortnight, and lifts every subject at once. The same is true of learning the conventions of a text type in English or a practical-method answer in science: both are lists to be learned rather than skills to be coached.

What is not self-fixable is the diagnosis itself. A student cannot usually tell whether they are losing marks to method, timing, misreading or absence, because all four feel like not knowing enough. That interpretation is what the single diagnostic session on this page exists for, and for some students it is the only paid hour they need.

sections.heading: When one-to-one is the only thing that works
paragraphs: There are situations where free help and group help both fail, and they are worth naming so a family can recognise themselves. The first is a student whose losses are spread thinly across every question rather than concentrated in topics. That pattern needs somebody watching one student work, because the fault is in how answers are built and it shows up in the act rather than in the result.

The second is a mismatch between apparent ability and outcome. A student who contributes well in class, understands explanations and then scores two bands below expectation is almost always failing at execution, and a classroom cannot see it because the classroom sees the understanding. Diagnosing that takes a whole marked paper and somebody who knows the scheme.

The third is a board mismatch. Where a student is entered for Pearson and the school's group revision is pitched at Cambridge, or the other way round, group help actively misleads. One-to-one is the only format that can work the exact code the student sits, which is why the entry list matters before anything is booked.

The fourth is confidence. Some students stop attempting questions they could do, and that pattern does not respond to more teaching. It responds to a sequence of questions at the right difficulty, marked promptly, until the evidence of competence accumulates. That is slow in a group and straightforward one to one.

A fifth situation is a student carrying three sciences plus mathematics into a mock fortnight with no plan. That is a triage problem rather than a teaching problem, and it needs somebody to read all the scripts together and say which two subjects get the remaining weeks. A group class cannot do that, and a subject teacher sees only their own subject.

sections.heading: Remraam specifics: short school run, thin tutor pool
paragraphs: Remraam is a low-rise apartment community in Dubailand, built as the Al Thamam and Al Ramth clusters with its own park and retail, reached from Al Qudra Road and Emirates Road. South View School sits close by and takes students through Year 11, which gives families here two advantages the rest of this belt does not have.

The first is that free school help is practical. A student can stay for a clinic or a support session and still be home at a reasonable hour, which is not a realistic proposition from Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square where the run is considerably longer. Any family in this community that has not tried that route is leaving the cheapest useful help on the table.

The second is that evening sessions can start early. A student home by four has a usable hour at a quarter past four, when they are not yet tired, and that hour is worth more than the same hour at eight. Families who moved here from communities with long commutes often do not realise the option exists.

The disadvantage is the tutor pool. The people advertising along this corridor are based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, and most cover several subjects at IGCSE level rather than one deeply. For a specific Extended-tier paper close to a series, that pool is shallower than its advertising suggests, which is the argument for selecting by board and code rather than by distance.

sections.heading: Choosing between two tutors at the same price
paragraphs: Once a family has decided to pay, the choice is usually between options that cost about the same, and rate tells you nothing at that point. Four questions separate them, and all four have checkable answers.

Which papers have you marked, by code. A tutor who can name 0620 Paper 4 or 4MA1 Paper 2 and describe what the scheme rewards there is in a different category from one who says they teach chemistry. Second, what will you do in the first session. The right answer involves a marked script; an answer involving a syllabus overview means the diagnosis has been skipped.

Third, what will you refuse to do with coursework. A tutor who says they give criterion feedback on the student's own writing and will not draft, rewrite or supply text is describing the correct boundary. A tutor who offers to handle it is describing something that puts the student at risk. Fourth, do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge, valid two years and issued in a stated two working days, so there is no cost reason not to hold one.

A fifth question is worth asking of any provider rather than of a tutor: what happens if this person becomes unavailable six weeks before the papers. A freelance arrangement simply ends. A centre reassigns somebody who may not know the board. A managed match proposes a replacement with a fresh trial. The answers differ sharply and the question is never answered in a search result.

sections.heading: What the paid options cost, with sources
paragraphs: Published rates in this city span a wide range, and knowing where an offer sits in that range is most of what a parent needs. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. That tier can be reasonable value for working through exercise sets with an organised student and is a poor fit for diagnosis.

A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded into the price, Bestimate's range being AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors publishing AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Across a month, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27. These are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and coursework limits
paragraphs: There is a fifth free check that belongs beside the four in the first section, and almost no Remraam parent runs it: ask whoever you are about to pay whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. The eligibility list explains what you will find in a pool this thin, because it covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. The neighbour offering maths at a kind rate is therefore often a serving teacher or an undergraduate rather than a full-time tutor, and either one can be properly permitted. The instrument behind it is Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years, so no part of the rate you are quoted can honestly be attributed to the cost of holding one.

MoHRE's own service listing is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any amount quoted to you as the penalty is unverified.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs a different authorisation: a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram has no UAE premises, holds no such permit, and does not use a regulator's name to describe its tutors.

One arrangement to decline: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. Separately, where a centre runs assessed coursework it must be the student's own, so a tutor explains criteria, critiques an approach and marks a draft the student wrote, and never writes, drafts, completes or edits the work to completion.

process.title: Use the school first
process.description: Ask the subject teacher one specific question about one specific loss, and find out whether a clinic or support session exists. From Remraam that is practical in a way it is not from most of this belt, and it is the cheapest useful help available.

process.title: Get the entry list in writing
process.description: Subject, board, code and tier for each IGCSE entry. Schools in this corridor do not all use one board across a timetable, and group revision pitched at the other board actively misleads. One message, and every later decision gets easier.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic session
process.description: Send a marked mock script and book a single session. The output is a written list of where the marks went and what each loss will take to close. For some students that is the only paid hour needed, and we will say so when it is.

process.title: Then buy the block the diagnosis implies
process.description: Mechanical losses need four to six weeks of twice-weekly technique work. Genuine content gaps need a term. Those are different products with different prices, and the script decides which, not the level of worry in the house.

process.title: Fix a slot and set an end date
process.description: Sessions sit on Gulf Standard Time and can start early given the short run from South View School. Because nobody travels, a slot can move within the evening or after Iftar during Ramadan at no cost, and every block ends on a stated date.

whyPoints.title: The free options are compared honestly
whyPoints.description: The subject teacher, school clinics, published mark schemes and the marked mock cost nothing and close a real share of a typical gap. A page that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising, and families notice eventually.

whyPoints.title: Subjects are ranked by return, not by demand
whyPoints.description: Economics, chemistry and computer science repay an hour within weeks because their losses are mechanical. Biology and English take longer. Spending the same money on the wrong subject is a common and avoidable waste.

whyPoints.title: One session is a product we actually sell
whyPoints.description: A single diagnostic session on a marked script, with a written plan the student can follow unaided, is offered on its own. Sometimes that is the whole answer, and nothing further is proposed when that is the case.

whyPoints.title: Blocks end on a date
whyPoints.description: Mechanical losses close in four to six weeks or they are not mechanical. Open-ended weekly arrangements are easier to sell and worse value, so every block proposed here carries a length and a purpose.

whyPoints.title: Board and code come before teaching
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson phrase questions differently and expect different written method. Confirming the code per subject costs one message and prevents a term of practice that teaches the wrong habits.

whyPoints.title: No regulator names used as credentials
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration, no board affiliation and no UAE office. Where a competing page attaches a regulator's name to its tutors, that is a claim to check.

faqs.question: Should a Remraam family try school support before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this community is better placed for it than most of the belt. South View School sits close by, so staying for a clinic or support session and getting home at a reasonable hour is realistic, which it is not from Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square. The subject teacher sets the mock, knows the mark scheme and has two years of context on your child. What school support cannot provide is an hour of individual attention each week on one student's own error pattern.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject gives the quickest improvement for the money?
faqs.answer: Economics, usually, followed closely by chemistry and computer science. All three lose marks mechanically: diagram labelling and terminology in economics, equations and state symbols in chemistry, pseudocode conventions and trace tables in computer science. A student who already understands the material can gain visibly in two to four weeks because nothing new has to be learned. Biology, English Language and English Literature move more slowly, since they depend on terminology precision, register and sustained writing that improve over months.

faqs.question: Can my daughter fix her own timing problems without a tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is one of the better self-fixes available. Timing collapse shows as a strong first half and an abandoned final page, and the repair is a decision rather than a skill: choose a question order in advance, keep a watch visible, and allocate time by marks available rather than by how interesting a question looks. Three or four full papers sat under those rules settle it. What she probably cannot do alone is work out whether timing is actually her problem, which needs a marked script read by someone who knows the scheme.

faqs.question: What exactly does a single diagnostic session produce?
faqs.answer: A written list. The session reads a marked mock or past paper and separates content absence, visible as untouched questions, from method loss where the approach was right and the presentation lost marks, from timing collapse, from misreading caused by skipping a command term. Each has a different repair time, from a fortnight to several months. The output is that classification plus a plan the student can follow unaided. For some students no further paid help is needed, and we say so rather than proposing a block.

faqs.question: Is a cheap online tutor at AED 50 an hour ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, yes. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour in this market, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, and for working steadily through exercise sets with an organised student that is defensible value. What that tier rarely provides is diagnosis: recognising from a marked script which of four failures is costing the marks and which three topics carry the most recoverable ones. Ask any tutor at any price which papers they have marked.

faqs.question: Why does group revision sometimes make things worse?
faqs.answer: Board mismatch, mostly. If a student is entered for Pearson 4CH1 and the room is working from Cambridge 0620 papers, the practice teaches question styles and method conventions that will not appear, which is worse than no practice. Mixed-board groups form because centres need the numbers, and the teacher then has to cover content rather than paper technique. Ask the centre which codes the room is working from, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

faqs.question: How do we choose between two tutors who charge the same?
faqs.answer: Four questions with checkable answers. Which papers have you marked, by code. What happens in the first session, specifically. What will you refuse to do with coursework. And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free, valid two years and issued in a stated two working days. A tutor who can name a paper and describe what its scheme rewards is in a different category from one who says they teach the subject. Rate tells you nothing at this point.

faqs.question: Our son understands everything in class and then underperforms. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the classroom sees understanding and the paper tests execution. The three failures behind this pattern are predictable: no question-order strategy, so the last page is abandoned; no habit of showing method, so multi-step marks go uncollected; and command-term misreading, so a good answer addresses a question that was not asked. None of them is visible to a teacher watching him contribute well. All three show in a marked paper and all three move within a few weeks once named.

faqs.question: What should a student do with a published mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Mark their own paper with it, line by line, for a paper they have already sat. Reading a scheme properly is a skill: understanding that a mark is awarded for a specific statement, that bracketed alternatives are acceptable, that consequential marks can follow a correct method to a wrong value, and that a right answer without required working does not always score. Students who learn this stop guessing what examiners want, and it costs nothing. Most have never been shown how.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring English Language eight weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer is narrower than families want. Register and task form can be taught quickly: a task asking for a speech that receives an essay loses marks that strong writing cannot recover, and learning the conventions of each text type is a short piece of work. The writing fluency underneath improves over months, not weeks. So eight weeks can secure the mechanical marks and will not transform the analysis, and anyone promising otherwise is selling something that does not exist.

faqs.question: How many paid hours does a typical Year 11 actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families buy, if the sequence is right. A single diagnostic session, then four to six weeks of twice-weekly work on the one or two subjects showing mechanical losses, is enough for a large share of students. A term-long block is appropriate where a script shows whole questions abandoned rather than scattered losses, because content genuinely absent needs months. Buying three subjects at once produces three sets of homework and no practice time, which is the most common way money gets wasted here.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to an apartment in Al Ramth or Al Thamam?
faqs.answer: Not one arranged through IB Gram. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only. Visiting tutors exist in Dubai and are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, per Bestimate's Dubai cost table and the rates home tutors publish. The online route also avoids a fixed arrival window, which matters when a bus runs late and a visiting tutor has another household to reach afterwards.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor leaves Dubai before the papers?
faqs.answer: Ask every provider that before committing, because the answers differ sharply and none of them appears in a search result. A freelance arrangement simply ends, which is the main risk in the cheapest tier. A centre reassigns a teacher who may not know the board. With IB Gram a replacement is proposed and a free trial lesson applies again, so you are not paying to find out whether the new match works. Getting the answer in writing is worth more than twenty dirhams off the rate.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach along this corridor?
faqs.answer: The individual does. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so there is no cost reason not to hold one. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

intro.heading: What 'near me' costs a Serena household in hours
paragraphs: Serena sits off Al Qudra Road at the far side of the Dubailand belt, built around clusters including Bella Casa and Casa Viva. Search for a tutor from that address and the results are shaped by who has a verified business location: tuition centres in Motor City and Dubai Sports City, directory listings for agencies based across the city, and freelance adverts whose stated service area is optimistic. It is a geography answer to a question about teaching.

The more useful question is how much of your week each option consumes, because that is the cost nobody puts on an invoice. A round trip from Serena to a centre in Motor City is thirty to forty minutes each way in the late afternoon, plus parking and waiting: call it two hours of household time per session. Two children on different days is four hours a week, which is most of a working morning.

A visiting tutor removes your driving and charges for their own. Serena is far enough out that a round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes, which is why market in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor online. You are paying for the journey either way; the only question is whose.

IB Gram removes both. There is no IB Gram centre or office in the UAE, no tutor travels to a UAE address — home visits are a service we run only in India — and Serena students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical consequence is that the session time becomes a choice rather than a constraint, which matters in a community where children arrive home anywhere between 15:45 and 16:40.

This page is therefore about the week rather than the hour. What the local search actually returns and what each option costs in time and money. How to build a Year 10 or Year 11 week around your child's arrival band. What support your school already provides free, which many families buy twice. How to choose between two tutors who are both available. And the administrative decisions — board, tier, entry, Cambridge zone — that quietly decide the year.

Every figure names its source. Where something depends on your child's specific entry, the answer is in the school's entry statement rather than on any page, including this one. For scale, Dubai's private sector runs 227 schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 students, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of enrolment, according to Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25. In a market that size, the nearest option and the right option are rarely the same thing, and the gap between them is measured in the hours a family spends driving.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-serena.programmesIntro: The shape of a sensible week changes with the year group, because the amount of unavoidable schoolwork changes with it.

programmes.name: Year 9
programmes.description: The year with the most spare evening capacity, which makes it the cheapest year to fix anything. One session a week, or a short block of six to ten, aimed at algebraic fluency and writing that answers the question set. Families who use Year 9 well rarely need a weekly arrangement in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Option choices are made in this year in Dubai schools, and in this belt they interact with the commute: a subject that depends on frequent after-school catch-up is harder to sustain from a school fifty minutes away. Ask the school what each option expects outside lesson time before choosing.

programmes.name: Year 10
programmes.description: Content is delivered across the year, so the useful pattern is one subject supported weekly with past-paper questions by topic as each topic is taught. Sixty minutes at a realistic hour beats ninety minutes that starts too late, particularly for students on the Al Barsha run who reach Serena after 16:20.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai schools enter students for a subject in the June series at the end of Year 10, which moves the entry deadline months earlier and turns the Year 10 evening into an exam-year evening. Confirm the entry list in writing with the exam office rather than assuming the standard two-year pattern.

programmes.name: Year 11
programmes.description: The year where the week has to be designed rather than filled. Timed papers need a fresh student, so for a long commute they belong at the weekend, with weekday evenings used for marking and corrections. A paper attempted at 20:00 after fifty minutes in traffic measures tiredness and misdirects the next month of work.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The second series is a resit route, so a poor January mock is a decision rather than a disaster — provided the family has kept a reserve for a second entry fee.

programmes.name: After IGCSE
programmes.description: A Level or IB Diploma, and in this belt often a change of school and commute. The step up rewards sustained argument and independent work rather than coverage, which is why a short bridging block over the summer consistently outperforms remediation in the first term of Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at E. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-serena.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Serena families ask about, with the codes to quote and a note on how each one fits into a week with limited evening time.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The subject most worth a dedicated weekly slot, because progress compounds and because method marks recover quickly. Confirm the tier before booking, since it sets the ceiling and determines which past papers are worth the hour.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Needs concentration for problem setup, so it belongs in the earliest slot available or at the weekend. Electricity is the reliable weak point in UAE cohorts and is the right first target for a short block.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations need a fresh student; qualitative analysis wording and organic reaction types are recall-based and work fine late in the evening. That split makes chemistry easy to schedule around a difficult commute.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The most late-slot-tolerant science. Command-term marking, diagram labelling and data interpretation all work at 19:30, and the dominant loss — describing where explanation was required — is a marking habit rather than a content gap.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: All three disciplines feed one or two shared grades, so the weakest sets the ceiling. For a family with limited evening time, targeting that one discipline is both cheaper and more effective than three weekly sessions.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Composition needs an alert student; reading technique and annotation practice do not. A useful subject to place in whichever slot the maths or science work cannot use.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different course from First Language and frequently confused with it at booking. Speaking and listening are examined, and speaking practice works in any slot because it is conversation rather than sustained writing.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Evaluation question structures take two or three sessions to install and transfer immediately. Case reading is homework rather than tutored time, which makes these subjects efficient for a household with a short week.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 / 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and hand-tracing need focus; binary and data representation are formulaic and survive a late slot. Students who code fluently still lose marks on board-standard written notation.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Real timetabled work competing for the same evening, and excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track equivalency.

sections.heading: What the local search actually returns
paragraphs: Type the phrase from a Serena address and you get three kinds of result, none of which is ranked on teaching quality. Tuition centres with verified locations in Motor City and Sports City, which rank because they are the nearest businesses in the category. Agencies based elsewhere in Dubai that list Dubailand as a service area, which rank on prominence. And individual adverts whose location field describes an aspiration rather than a commute.

That is not a criticism of any of them; it is how local search works. A map pack ranks proximity, prominence and category relevance. 'Can teach Cambridge 0580 Extended to the standard that moves a 5 to a 7' is not a category, and no amount of reviews makes it one. The result set answers a question about geography while the parent was asking about a specification.

The practical response is to run two searches and keep them separate. Use the local one to find out what venues and in-home options genuinely exist near you and what they charge, which is real information and is priced in this page's tables. Then search on board, code and tier — 0580 Extended, 4CH1, 0610 — and compare the two shortlists. For a mainstream subject they may overlap; for a tiered subject with a specific target grade they often do not.

IB Gram belongs on the second list only. There is no centre near Serena, no UAE office, and no tutor who will arrive at a Dubailand address, because home visits are an India-only service. If a venue or a visitor is what you want, the local list is genuinely worth working through, and this page gives you the numbers to judge it with.

sections.heading: Centre, visitor or screen: the week's time budget
paragraphs: Here is the comparison that decides it for most households in this community, and it is not about money. It is about how many hours of the week each option takes from the family, counting the parts that never appear on an invoice.

A centre visit costs the parent sixty to eighty minutes of driving plus the waiting time, so roughly two hours of household time per session. For one child once a week that is manageable. For two children on different days it is four hours, which in practice means one parent's evening is spent in a car park twice a week for a school year.

An in-home visit costs the family nothing in driving and is paid for in the rate, because nobody absorbs a hundred minutes of unpaid travel. It also narrows the choice of tutor to those willing to make that drive at that hour, and it fixes the session time to whatever suits their route rather than your bus.

An online session costs neither side any travel, which is why the slot can be chosen around the arrival time and why a clashed session can usually be moved inside the same week rather than forfeited. The table sets all of it out, including the two options families forget: free school support, and a student working alone with properly marked papers, which costs nothing and is better than a badly aimed paid hour. Read the table by column rather than by row: the time column is the one families get wrong, and the last column is the one that decides whether the teaching will be any good.

sections.heading: Building a week that survives Year 10 and Year 11
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in this belt fail for scheduling reasons rather than teaching ones. A family books the slot that was offered, it half works, attendance slips, and by February everyone has concluded that tutoring does not help. The fix is to design the week around the arrival band before choosing anything else.

The principle is that work requiring sustained reasoning needs a fresh student, and work that responds to something already on the page does not. New mathematical technique, physics problem setup, extended writing and timed papers belong in the best hour available. Marking, corrections, recall material, command-term phrasing and planning survive a late start perfectly well, and some of them are better when the student is calm rather than sharp.

From that, three week shapes emerge for the three arrival bands in this community. Early arrivals, home by 16:05, get the most valuable tutoring hour in the belt and should spend it on the hardest content rather than on checking homework. Middle arrivals, home around 16:20, can run a single weekday session at 17:30 if the content is chosen sensibly. Late arrivals, home at 16:40 or after, need the weekend-plus-short-weekday split, and will waste money on anything else.

sections.heading: What your school already provides free
paragraphs: Before buying anything, find out what is already included, because families in this belt routinely pay for things their school offers. This is not a small saving: it can be the difference between needing a weekly arrangement and needing a short block.

Most Dubai secondary schools run some combination of after-school subject clinics, departmental revision sessions in the run-up to mocks, lunchtime catch-up for specific topics, and a head of department who will tell you candidly how a cohort is doing. Several also provide access to question banks and will mark additional past papers if a student asks. None of that is advertised to parents in the way a tuition centre advertises.

The reason to start there is not only cost. The school's teachers know what has been taught, what is coming, and how the student performs in class, which no external tutor can see. Where school support is good, the efficient purchase from outside is narrow: one diagnosed gap, or exam technique, or the thing the school cannot provide — a second explanation from a different direction for a student who has not clicked with the first.

The one thing to count honestly is the time cost. After-school support often means a late pick-up or a second run from Serena, which for the Al Barsha cluster is another forty-minute drive. That is a real constraint rather than an excuse, and it is why the honest comparison includes your car as well as your money.

sections.heading: What each option costs in AED
paragraphs: With the time budget established, the money. These are published Dubai market figures from the parties named, not IB Gram's price list; we quote per student after the free trial lesson, once somebody has looked at marked work.

Budget online tuition is advertised from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya publishing from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table showing AED 200 to 450+. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, per BartyED.

In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and Serena sits at the upper end because of the drive. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one hour a week are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Set those against the time column from the earlier table and the comparison changes shape. A group class at a centre is the cheapest hourly option and the most expensive in household time. An online specialist is the most expensive hourly option and the cheapest in everything else. Which is right depends on whether your constraint is money or the week, and most families in this community discover it is the week.

sections.heading: Choosing between two tutors who are both available
paragraphs: Once scheduling and budget are settled, families are often left with two plausible options and no way to choose. These are the questions that separate them, and none of them is about experience in general.

Ask which syllabus code and tier they would work from, and listen for whether the answer arrives immediately or after a request for the textbook. Ask what they would want to see before the first session: the right answer is marked work and task sheets, not a placement test. Ask how they mark — whether work is marked to the board's mark scheme with method marks and notation treated seriously, or ticked for being broadly correct.

Then ask two questions about the arrangement rather than the teaching. How many sessions do you think this will take, and what happens when it is done? A tutor who names a number and a finish point is thinking about your child; one who cannot is thinking about a standing slot. And what happens if a school event clashes — because in this community it will, repeatedly, and the answer determines how much of what you buy you actually receive.

Finally, the boundary question for anyone who will go near coursework: what will you not do? A tutor who states the line without hesitation is safe. One who offers to 'help with the writing' is a risk to the entry rather than to the budget. That question costs nothing to ask and is the single most informative thing in the conversation.

sections.heading: The admin that quietly decides the year
paragraphs: Three administrative facts do more to shape an IGCSE year than any tutoring decision, and all three live with the school rather than with a tutor. Getting them in writing early is free and prevents the most expensive kinds of mistake.

The first is the entry statement: board, syllabus code and tier for every subject. Departments within one Dubai school sometimes differ, so check subject by subject rather than school-wide. This settles which past papers are worth any hour you buy, and it occasionally contradicts what a family has assumed for two years.

The second is the series. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to your child, whatever a general article says. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable having run from late October to 19 November 2026 and June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so work from the live official one.

The third is specific to Cambridge and almost nobody knows it. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states in its exams officers' guide that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam where the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school's exam officer which zone the centre sits in, before anything is printed or put in a family calendar.

sections.heading: Permits, and what you can verify at no cost
paragraphs: If you are hiring an individual directly, one check costs nothing and is worth making regardless of price. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work rather than unregulated work.

The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, with a two-working-day completion time and no listed fee.

Two things follow. Because the permit is free, nobody should be adding a licensing cost to a quote. And because u.ae states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, a tutor who describes it as optional has told you something useful about how they operate. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted at you is unverified.

Separately, an operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. That is a specific licence with initial approval, completion steps and annual renewal, and it is the thing a tuition centre should hold. IB Gram holds none, claims none, has no UAE office or centre, and names no school as a client or partner. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai; that is a fact about the regulator rather than an endorsement of any provider, including us.

faqs.question: Why does searching for a tutor near Serena return centres in Motor City?
faqs.answer: Because local search ranks businesses by proximity, prominence and category relevance, and a tuition centre with a verified address in Motor City satisfies all three from an Al Qudra Road postcode. 'Can teach Cambridge 0580 Extended well' is not a category any map can rank. Use the local results for what they are good for — finding out what venues and in-home options exist near you and what they charge — then run a separate search on board, syllabus code and tier for the teaching question.

faqs.question: How much time does a tuition centre actually cost a Serena family?
faqs.answer: Thirty to forty minutes each way to Motor City or Sports City in the late afternoon, plus parking and waiting, so roughly two hours of household time per session. For one child once a week that is manageable; for two children on different days it is four hours, which is most of a working morning spent in a car. That cost never appears on an invoice, which is exactly why it is easy to accept, and it is the item most families in this belt underestimate.

faqs.question: My child gets home at 16:40. Is weekly tutoring pointless?
faqs.answer: No, but a single weekday evening session will underperform and probably lapse. The arrangement that works is a weekend morning slot for the demanding work — new technique, timed papers, extended writing — and a shorter weekday evening slot for marking the week's attempts, working corrections and recall material. That split takes more planning and holds for a full year. A forced 17:30 session after fifty minutes in traffic usually happens two weeks in three and then stops.

faqs.question: What free information should a Serena parent get from the school first?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. The entry statement, naming the board, syllabus code and tier for every subject, checked subject by subject because departments sometimes differ. What support the school already runs — subject clinics, pre-mock revision, lunchtime catch-up, extra marking — since families in this belt routinely buy what is already included. And for Cambridge entries, which of the six administrative zones the centre sits in, because the zone determines which version of the timetable applies.

faqs.question: How do I choose between two tutors who are both free at the right time?
faqs.answer: Ask five questions. Which syllabus code and tier would you work from, answered without a request for the textbook. What do you want to see before the first session — the right answer is marked work, not a placement test. How do you mark: to the board's mark scheme, or ticked as broadly right. How many sessions do you think this takes, and what happens when it is done. And what will you not do with coursework. The last one is the most informative and costs nothing to ask.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor cost less than one who visits Serena?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the difference is the drive rather than the teaching. Market in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with Serena at the upper end because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. The same qualified tutor online is AED 150 to 300, and an IGCSE specialist AED 200 to 450 or more. The premium buys presence, which is worth paying for in specific cases only.

faqs.question: Does a Motor City group class beat one-to-one once the drive is counted?
faqs.answer: Per hour, clearly; packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions. Per outcome it depends on the diagnosis. A group delivers one pace and one sequence to everyone, which suits a student who is broadly on track and wants more practice, and cannot address an individual gap. Add the two hours of household time each visit costs from Serena and, for a specific diagnosed problem, a short one-to-one block is usually cheaper to the finish line.

faqs.question: What should the session look like during mock week?
faqs.answer: Keep the slot and change its use. Mock weeks fill a student's evenings, so teaching new content during them wastes the hour. Spend it on targeted review, then do the valuable work afterwards: mark the returned scripts properly, label every lost mark as knowledge, method or reading the question, and rebuild the plan from the totals. Mocks are the most accurate diagnostic a family will get and they are free, yet most households read only the overall grade.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our home in Serena?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, there is no IB Gram centre or office in the country, and home visits are a service we run only in India — so nobody will arrive at a Dubailand address. Independent in-home tutors do work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. If a person in the room is what your child needs, that market exists and this page gives you the figures to judge it with.

faqs.question: Can we move a session when a school event clashes?
faqs.answer: With an online arrangement, usually within the same week, because there is no journey to re-plan on either side. That matters more than families expect across two years: school events in this community move at short notice, and a missed in-home visit is a wasted journey that is normally charged in full. Between mock weeks, travel and illness, the difference between rescheduling and forfeiting adds up to several hours of teaching either kept or lost.

faqs.question: Do both of my children need their own tutor and slot?
faqs.answer: Usually their own slot, and often their own tutor. Siblings in this belt are frequently on different boards or tiers and on different bus routes with arrival times forty minutes apart, so staggered slots work better than a shared one — commonly the younger child earlier and the exam-year student later. A genuine pair session needs the same board, tier, subject and a similar starting point, which is more often found between neighbouring households in Serena, Villanova and Mudon than between siblings.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams fall for a candidate sitting in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered to India only, so any article quoting a February window is describing another country's candidates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November — the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026. Because provisional timetables for later series can be revised, use the board's live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Should I check a tutor's UAE permit myself?
faqs.answer: If you are hiring an individual directly, yes, and it costs nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service with a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Since the permit is free, no tutor should pass on a licensing cost.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education compete with tutoring time in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are mandatory. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes must be organised for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are prohibited. For a non-Arab student these are real timetabled periods and real homework, and they are frequently the part of the week nobody is supporting.

Send us the arrival time, the subject with its code and tier, and the last marked paper, and you will get a proposed week rather than a list of slots. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online.

intro.heading: Six different people answer a near-me search. They are not interchangeable
paragraphs: The honest answer to "is there anyone near me who knows this syllabus" starts with a different question: who is it that actually responds when you search? In Dubai, the answer is six distinct categories of provider, and a parent in Sobha Hartland comparing three quotes is often comparing three different business models without realising it. The rates look similar. The accountability, the legal position and the subject knowledge do not.

First, school teachers tutoring in the evenings, who know a specification well and are bound by rules about which students they may teach. Second, university students and recent graduates, who are inexpensive and genuinely useful for a missed topic. Third, full-time freelance tutors, who vary more than any other category because nothing in the market distinguishes a good one from a confident one. Fourth, tuition centres with premises, which are a different regulated entity entirely. Fifth, agencies that match and take a margin. Sixth, international marketplaces that present a local appearance and deliver from elsewhere, sometimes behind a non-UAE phone number.

Each category has a different answer to the syllabus question. A moonlighting teacher usually knows one awarding body thoroughly and may assume the others are similar. A university student may know the subject and not the mark scheme. A freelance tutor may have taught four specifications or none. A marketplace may not know which board your child sits because nobody asked. That is why this page spends its space on verification rather than on reassurance: the useful thing we can give you is a way to test the claim, not another version of it.

There is also a legal dimension that almost nobody in this market explains. Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-regulated. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it is free, a tutor has no cost-based reason not to hold it, which makes it a reasonable thing to ask about and a telling thing to be evasive about.

IB Gram sits in the fifth category and says so: we match tutors and deliver lessons one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India, and we do not route UAE families to a non-UAE number while implying otherwise. The sections below give the category comparison, the permit table, the verification checks, the availability picture and the administrative details of the June and November series that almost nobody passes on to parents. None of it promises a grade; all of it is checkable, which is the more useful thing to offer a parent comparing three quotes.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the course begins
programmes.description: No specification exists yet, which means the syllabus question hardly matters and the cheapest competent tutor is often the right one. What matters here is securing algebraic fluency, reading stamina and scientific vocabulary. A student who reaches Year 10 without those spends two years catching up while new content arrives weekly, and that is the expensive scenario this stage prevents.
programmes.countryNote: Transfers between schools and curricula are common in the central corridor during these years, and a transfer leaves specific identifiable gaps rather than general weakness. For a Sobha Hartland family, one diagnostic session on a transfer student is worth more than a term of general support.

programmes.name: Years 10 and 11, the examination course
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects sat as external examinations, with tiering set by the school where it applies. This is the stage where the specification question becomes decisive, because the awarding body determines paper structure, tier names, calculator rules and how practical or spoken components are assessed. A tutor who knows the subject but not the specification can look wholly competent while rehearsing the wrong paper.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use more than one awarding body, sometimes within the same school for different subjects. Ask the examinations officer for the code in writing, subject by subject. In this corridor it is a two-minute email that eliminates the most common cause of wasted tutoring hours.

programmes.name: After results, A Level or IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE grades gate post-16 entry, and schools set their own thresholds for A Level and Diploma courses. A bare pass is not the same as readiness: a student heading for Higher Level sciences or A Level Mathematics needs fluency rather than a borderline grade, which is a different target from the one most Year 11 revision aims at.

sections.heading: The six providers who answer a near-me search, compared
paragraphs: Three quotes from a near-me search can look like three versions of the same thing and be three different businesses. The table sets out the six categories operating in Dubai with what each is good at, what each tends to get wrong, and what the permit position is. None of these categories is bad. Matching the wrong one to your problem is what costs money.

The pattern worth noticing is that cost and accountability move independently. A university student is cheap and has no institutional backing if the match fails. A tuition centre has premises, a licence and a timetable, and correspondingly little flexibility. An agency adds a margin and, if it is doing its job, adds replacement if the match is wrong and a check on the tutor's permit. A moonlighting school teacher may be the most specification-literate person available and is also the one most constrained by rules about which students they may teach.

The category that deserves the most scrutiny is the international marketplace, because it is the one designed to look like something else. Several providers ranking for Dubai queries present a local appearance and route families to a non-UAE number, quote in US dollars, or name no UAE neighbourhood anywhere on the page while claiming local coverage. There is nothing wrong with a tutor based outside the UAE teaching a UAE student, provided you are told. The problem is the concealment, and the test is simple: ask where the tutor is and what time zone they work to.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question nobody in the market answers properly and it has a clear answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two facts about it are worth holding onto. It is granted free of charge for two years, which means a tutor has no financial reason to avoid holding one. And eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students may all apply. So the permit is not a quality signal, it is a compliance signal, and a tutor who cannot or will not discuss it is telling you something.

Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount you see quoted in a parents' group or on a competitor's page, including the figure that circulates for this. One further constraint matters for families considering their child's own teacher: in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify against current policy before relying on it.

sections.heading: What "knows the IGCSE syllabus" actually means, and how to verify it
paragraphs: Every provider claims syllabus knowledge and the claim is almost never defined. At IGCSE it has a precise meaning, and a Sobha Hartland parent can test the whole of it in a single trial lesson without understanding the subject themselves. These are the questions we would apply to our own tutors, and we would rather you asked them of us than took the claim on trust.

A tutor who knows the specification can name the awarding body and the code without being told. They can state the paper structure and the tier names correctly: Core and Extended for Cambridge, Foundation and Higher for Pearson. They know whether a calculator is permitted in each paper, which in maths determines the entire drill. They know how practical or spoken components are assessed on that specification. They treat command terms as instructions with different mark expectations rather than as synonyms.

And they can tell you what is costing your child marks, which they can only do by looking at your child's own work. That is the real test, and it separates a tutor performing competence from one demonstrating it. A tutor who spends the trial lesson explaining the subject in general terms is auditioning. A tutor who asks for a marked paper, reads it, and names the pattern in specific language has done the job. Ask afterwards for that account in writing, and judge its precision rather than its tone. A tutor who is pleasant and general will be good company for a year and leave the grade exactly where it started.

sections.heading: Online against nearby for an IGCSE student in Hartland
paragraphs: A near-me search has already narrowed the field before you have compared anything, so it is worth seeing what the two delivery models do differently for an IGCSE student specifically. The relevant variables here are not identical to a Diploma student's, because the IGCSE problem is usually breadth: nine subjects, several mediocre, and a parent unsure which to attack.

On matching to the specification, online wins decisively, because the pool is the whole market and the code can be honoured rather than approximated. On covering more than one subject, online wins because a different specialist can take each subject rather than one person being stretched across four. On continuity, online wins in a community like this one, where families move apartment or school more often than they expect and an in-home arrangement has to be rebuilt each time.

On evidence, online tends to win because written feedback and marked practice survive in a way that verbal comments at a kitchen table do not, and a parent can check they exist without understanding the subject. On cost, online wins by the travel premium, roughly AED 30 to 150 an hour in this market. The one variable where a nearby tutor has a genuine claim is supervision of a reluctant student, which is a real category rather than a marketing objection. We do not offer home visits in the UAE, so if that is the requirement we will say so rather than talk you out of it.

sections.heading: Where tutor availability is genuinely thin, and what we do about it
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery entirely. Since the question behind this page is whether anyone available actually knows the syllabus, the useful thing we can offer is an honest map of where supply is good and where it is not, with the fallback stated in advance rather than discovered in week three.

It is also worth saying why availability moves at all. The tutors who know a specification best are usually teaching it full time, so their capacity for evening work is a few hours a week and those hours are taken early in the academic year. A family asking in September has a wider choice than the same family asking in March, which is the one genuine argument for booking before a crisis rather than after one.

The pattern follows how many schools teach a subject rather than how hard it is. Maths, Biology and Business Studies are well covered. Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English Language are reasonable. The thin areas are English Literature where set texts are unusual, Computer Science, Additional Mathematics, second languages beyond the commonly taught ones, and any subject entered through Oxford AQA, simply because fewer tutors have taught that specification.

What we do when a subject is thin is tell you before you book. The options are a different time slot, a short wait while we look, or a tutor based outside the UAE who has taught that specification and works to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed as such. What we will not do is accept the booking and let a tutor learn an unfamiliar specification on your time, because the differences matter most in the final eight weeks when there is no time left to absorb them. The table states the picture as it stands, and it changes, so treat it as the start of a conversation rather than a fixed list.

sections.heading: June and November: the administrative details nobody passes on
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series that circulates in online revision guides is offered to India only, and a Dubai plan built around it is wrong in a way that matters, because a parent acts on exam months. If you see those months in material sold to you, question the rest of the document.

Here is the detail almost nobody relays. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A parent revising from a timetable found online, rather than from the one their school issued, is exposed to exactly that. Ask the school which zone the centre is in and use their timetable only.

On the pattern of dates, the published record is instructive. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results following in January: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the summer series, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Those are past dates, cited so you can see the rhythm. For anything ahead, open the awarding body's live timetable rather than any restatement, including this page's, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables and revises them.
