sections.heading: KHDA, the Hartland schools and the five-subject equivalency rule
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Annual inspection runs on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, published school by school. For a Hartland parent the departmental commentary in a report is more informative than the band, because a strong department can sit inside an averagely rated school.

The scale of the market explains the variation in tutoring quality. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. A market that large, growing that fast, with that many curricula, produces a tutoring supply where nothing distinguishes an experienced specification teacher from a confident generalist unless a parent asks. Hence this page.

The grade's later use is worth planning for. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside that, equivalency requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a requirement of six subjects, which is incorrect. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs; verify your own case through its attestation channel rather than through any tutoring service, this one included, and do not treat tutoring as a requirement for it.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or accredited by Cambridge, Pearson or Oxford AQA, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit is the only thing the phrase could properly refer to, and it does not describe an individual tutor at all.

sections.heading: Coursework, speaking components and practical work: the limits
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects are assessed entirely by written paper, which removes much of the temptation that exists at Diploma level. Where a coursework, portfolio or spoken component does exist, the rule is unchanged: the work must be the student's own, and a tutor offering to produce it is offering malpractice with the consequence falling on the student. At least one operator ranking for UAE curriculum queries sells completed assessed work at a published price, which tells you what the market will do if nobody draws a line.

What a tutor legitimately does with such a component is explain the criteria, question a chosen focus until it is workable, teach the skills it requires, rehearse a spoken component in the format the specification sets, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. What a tutor does not do is choose the focus, supply content, write or rewrite text, or hand over an example close enough to copy. We say this to the student in the first session rather than burying it, because a fifteen-year-old under pressure deserves the boundary in advance.

Practical science deserves its own note because it is the question Hartland parents ask most often about online tuition. Nobody runs a laboratory over video, and a provider implying otherwise is overselling. What is taught online is the examinable part: experimental method, independent and dependent variables, controls, uncertainty, graph work and the written conventions the mark scheme rewards. Whether that is assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper or inside the written papers depends on the specification, which is one more reason to get the code. We also do not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the awarding body's own page.

sections.heading: Getting started from Sobha Hartland, and what we disclose up front
paragraphs: Start by emailing the school's examinations officer for the awarding body, the specification code and the tier in each subject you are considering. Send that with the latest grades labelled as mock or classwork, the teacher's last comment quoted rather than summarised, and the time the school day ends. In Hartland that last detail is better than in most of Dubai, because two schools sit inside the community and some students are home before three.

We propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson, which is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. Run the verification checks from earlier on this page. Ask where the tutor is based and what time zone they work to, ask them to name the specification before you tell them, and ask afterwards for a written account of what is costing marks. If the answers are vague or the location is evasive, do not book, with us or with anyone.

What we disclose up front, because this market generally does not: we are a matching service delivering online, our tutors may be based in the UAE or outside it and we will tell you which, we do not send tutors to UAE homes, we hold no KHDA or awarding-body accreditation, and some subjects on the coverage table above may take a week or be unavailable. If any of that rules us out for your situation, that is a better outcome than finding out in week three, and the trial lesson costs nothing either way.

process.title: Get the awarding body, code and tier in writing
process.description: One email to the examinations officer, subject by subject. It eliminates the most common cause of wasted tutoring hours, which is a competent tutor rehearsing the wrong paper, and it gives you something concrete to test a prospective tutor against.

process.title: Ask us where the tutor is based
process.description: We will tell you whether a proposed tutor is in the UAE or elsewhere and what time zone they work to, before the first lesson. Several providers in this market conceal that behind a local-looking presence, and the concealment rather than the location is the problem.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then run the checks
process.description: The first session costs nothing. Ask the tutor to name the specification before you tell them, check they use the right tier names, and ask afterwards for a written account of what is costing marks. Vague answers are a reason not to book at any rate.

process.title: Review the tier early, not in Year 11
process.description: A tier entry sets a grade ceiling for two years and is occasionally wrong in a way that is visible in one marked paper. We flag it in the first fortnight so you have evidence for a conversation with the department while a change is still possible.

process.description: Each session ends with named past-paper questions from the correct specification, and the next begins with them marked against the published criteria. Checking that this is happening needs no subject knowledge from you, which makes it the most practical accountability available.

process.description: The plan is checked against the June or November series and the block ends when its purpose is met. If the tier was the problem rather than the teaching, we will say so even though it ends the arrangement.

whyPoints.description: Six kinds of provider answer a near-me search in Dubai and they are not interchangeable. We set out what each is good at and where each fails, and we say which one we are rather than implying a local presence we do not have.

whyPoints.title: The permit explained properly

We explain it and link to the official route. We do not publish the unverified fine figure that circulates in this market.

faqs.question: Who actually turns up when I search for an IGCSE tutor near me in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Six quite different kinds of provider: school teachers tutoring in the evenings, university students and recent graduates, full-time freelance tutors, tuition centres with premises, matching agencies, and international marketplaces presenting a local appearance. They differ in cost, in accountability and in legal position. A moonlighting teacher usually knows one specification thoroughly; a university student is cheap and rarely mark-scheme literate; a centre has structure and little flexibility. Matching the wrong category to your problem is what wastes money, more often than the hourly rate does.

faqs.question: Are your IGCSE tutors MoHRE licensed, and can I ask them directly?
faqs.answer: You can and should ask, and a permitted tutor will not mind. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Because it costs nothing, a tutor has no financial reason to avoid holding one, which makes evasiveness informative. Note that the permit is a compliance signal rather than a quality one: eligibility extends to school teachers, employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to homes in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: Ours do not. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We state it plainly because near me is the phrase parents search and leaving the impression open would be easy. Local in-home arrangements certainly exist in this community, and in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. If physical supervision is what your child needs, that is the right route and this page gives you the figures to judge it.

faqs.question: How can I check a tutor knows my child's specification and not just the subject?
faqs.answer: Six checks, all testable in one lesson. Can they name the awarding body and code before you tell them? Do they use the correct tier names, Core and Extended for Cambridge or Foundation and Higher for Pearson? Do they know the calculator rules for each paper? Can they describe how practical or spoken components are assessed on that specification? Did they ask for your child's marked work before teaching anything? And will they confirm they hold a MoHRE permit? Six yeses is a demonstration; a warm manner is not.

faqs.question: Is it a problem if the tutor is based outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: Not in itself, provided you are told. A specialist elsewhere who has taught your child's exact specification and works to Gulf Standard Time is often a better match than a generalist nearby. The problem is concealment: several providers ranking for Dubai queries route families to non-UAE numbers, quote in US dollars, or name no UAE neighbourhood while implying local coverage. Ask where the tutor sits and what time zone they keep. We will tell you before the first lesson, and we flag it in the coverage table when a subject is only available that way.

faqs.question: A teacher at my child's school has offered evening sessions. Is that allowed?
faqs.answer: It is usually the wrong arrangement and in Abu Dhabi it is barred. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify against current policy before relying on it. Beyond the rules, a second explanation from outside the school is often more useful than more of the same one.

faqs.question: What is the fine for tutoring in Dubai without a permit?
faqs.answer: No figure can honestly be given, which is itself worth knowing. Official sources state that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and press reporting records that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties. A figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source, so we do not publish it and you should treat any site that does with suspicion about the rest of its content.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in the UAE?
faqs.answer: English Literature where the set texts are unusual, Computer Science, Additional Mathematics, second languages beyond the commonly taught ones, and any subject entered through Oxford AQA, simply because fewer tutors have taught that specification. Mathematics, Biology and Business Studies are well covered; Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English Language are reasonable. We publish that picture before you book, with the fallback stated, rather than accepting a booking and having a tutor learn an unfamiliar specification on your time.

faqs.question: What should I use as my child's exam timetable?
faqs.answer: Only the one the school issues. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and its guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A timetable found online may belong to a different zone. Ask the examinations officer which zone your centre is in, and for anything ahead of time open the awarding body's live timetable rather than a restatement of it.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find a tutor once we decide?
faqs.answer: For the well-covered subjects, usually days, and sometimes the same day if you send a photograph of a marked paper with the specification code. For thinner subjects, a week or more, and occasionally we cannot cover it at all, in which case we say so. The free trial lesson comes before any commitment, so the timeline you should plan around is trial lesson first, decision second. What we will not do is fill the slot with someone who has not taught the specification in order to answer quickly.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre a better bet than an individual tutor?
faqs.answer: It is a different thing rather than a better one. A centre has premises, a KHDA Educational Services Permit as a training institute, a timetable and group economics that make it the cheapest option per head. What it has less of is flexibility and individual diagnosis: a habit such as never writing working will not be noticed in a class of six. Centres usually teach one awarding body, which matters if your child's school uses another. For a shared topic gap across a cohort, a centre is often the efficient answer.

faqs.question: How are practical science skills taught if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The examinable part is taught and the laboratory part is not, and anyone claiming otherwise is overselling. Online sessions cover experimental method, independent and dependent variables, controls, uncertainty, graph work and the written conventions the mark scheme rewards. Whether those are assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper or inside the written papers depends on the specification, so the code matters here too. The hands-on work belongs to the school's practical programme, and a good tutor will ask what that programme has actually covered this term.

faqs.question: My child transferred schools mid-year. What kind of tutoring do they need?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic block rather than a weekly arrangement, in most cases. Transfers leave specific gaps rather than general weakness, and the common error is re-teaching a whole year when three topics are missing. Three to five sessions, with the first spent establishing what is actually absent in writing, usually closes it. The second thing to check is whether the new school uses a different awarding body from the old one, because a student who has studied one specification for a year and will sit another needs that difference mapped.

faqs.question: Does the IGCSE grade matter for staying in the UAE for university?
faqs.answer: It matters for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, which requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is wrong. Equivalency is a process the ministry performs, so verify your own case through its attestation channel and do not treat tutoring as a requirement for it.

faqs.question: What do you disclose that other providers do not?
faqs.answer: Four things, up front. That we are a matching service delivering online rather than a local presence. That a proposed tutor may be based in the UAE or outside it, and which. That we send no tutors to UAE homes at all. And that we hold no KHDA or awarding-body accreditation, because a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a licence for training institutes with premises and we do not have one. If any of that rules us out for your situation, better to establish it now than in week three.

faqs.question: What should I send to get a useful recommendation?
faqs.answer: Five things, and a photograph of one marked paper is worth more than all of them. The awarding body and specification code per subject, from the examinations officer. The tier where tiering applies. The latest grades, labelled as mock or classwork. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than paraphrased. And the time the school day ends, which in Sobha Hartland is often earlier than elsewhere because two schools sit inside the community, making a genuinely early session slot possible.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-tecom.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who teach Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE to Dubai students, matched by syllabus code and tier rather than by subject label. Ask any of them which paper your child sits and which tier they are entered for; the answer tells you more than a profile does.

intro.heading: The honest answer about the tutor pool around Barsha Heights
paragraphs: TECOM, which the maps now call Barsha Heights, is unusual among Dubai neighbourhoods in one specific way: it has no large school campus of its own. It is towers, offices and apartments wedged between Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai Internet City and Al Barsha, and almost every secondary-age child living in it is bussed outward in the morning. That single fact shapes the answer to the question you typed, because the local tutoring market in a community without a school is different from the market in a community with three.

What exists near you, in practice, is a scatter of freelance tutors advertising on building noticeboards, community groups and classified sites, plus the tuition centres along the Al Barsha and Dubai Marina corridors. Some of those freelancers are excellent. The problem is not quality, it is verifiability: you cannot tell from a community post whether somebody has taught Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended with Paper 6 or whether they once did A Level chemistry themselves. The post looks identical either way, and the rate often does too.

So the useful thing this page can do is not to insist that nearby is bad. It is to hand you the questions that tell the two apart in five minutes, whoever you end up hiring. There are about ten of them, the answers are short, and a genuine specialist gives them without hesitating. We have published them below with the right answers alongside, which is an odd thing for a tutoring company to do and is also the only version of this page worth writing.

Alongside that, there is a legal question most families never ask and should. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers specific categories of person including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Nobody advertising on a noticeboard volunteers this.

On what we provide: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the past paper and the mark scheme shared on screen. For a Barsha Heights family that trade is unusually clean, because the children are already commuting outward for school and the last thing the week needs is another journey. What the online format buys is the specialist your postcode does not contain.

One more thing is worth setting straight before the detail. Nearby is not a proxy for good, and distant is not a proxy for cheap. The published Dubai bands run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget floor up to AED 650 at the premium end, and there are generalists and specialists at almost every point on that range, advertising in almost identical language. The variable that predicts whether an hour helps your child is whether the person has taught the exact syllabus code and tier your child is entered for. Everything on this page is organised around letting you check that for yourself, with whoever you end up hiring.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-tecom.programmesIntro: Before verifying anybody, be clear about what your child is actually sitting. These are the four things an IGCSE tutor has to be matched against, and families routinely know only the first.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The most common route in the British-curriculum schools that Barsha Heights children travel to. Single sciences are tiered Core or Extended, with Core capped at the middle grades and Extended reaching the top. Mathematics 0580 is similarly tiered. The practical component in the sciences is either Paper 5, a laboratory test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and the school chooses which.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June series with November as the resit route. The February and March series is offered to India only. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Structurally different from Cambridge in ways that matter when matching a tutor. Mathematics 4MA1 is tiered Foundation or Higher rather than Core or Extended. The sciences, 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, are untiered and have no separate practical examination at all, with practical skills examined inside the written papers. A tutor used only to Cambridge will prepare an Edexcel candidate for the wrong thing.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in a May or June window and a November window. The published record is checkable: the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: The Tier Your Child Is Entered For
programmes.description: The least-known and most consequential fact on the whole course. Cambridge Core candidates sit different papers from Extended candidates and cannot reach the top grades. Pearson Foundation and Higher work the same way in mathematics. The tier is fixed at the final entry deadline, months before the exam, and no amount of tutoring afterwards changes which paper the student sits.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools generally form the tier decision at the end of Year 10 or early Year 11 using internal assessment evidence. A family wanting an Extended entry has to make that case while the evidence can still be produced, which means during Year 10 rather than during the term the entry is submitted.

programmes.name: What the Grades Are Used For
programmes.description: IGCSE grades gate sixth-form entry into A Level or the IB Diploma, and they feed Ministry of Education equivalency for students who later apply to UAE universities. The second use catches families out because it arrives years later. A dropped subject in Year 10 can turn into an equivalency problem when nobody remembers the decision.
programmes.countryNote: The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Verify the current rules with the Ministry rather than with any tutoring site.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: An IGCSE tutor near TECOM is usually wanted for one of these. The code is the thing to match on; the subject name is not enough, because two boards teach the same subject differently and tier it differently.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Tiered, so the first verification question is which tier. Extended covers functions, transformations, vectors and more demanding algebra that Core does not. Marks are lost on unshown working, which gives away method marks that were already earned, and on misreading a question that asks for an exact answer rather than a rounded one.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two written papers and a Foundation or Higher tier rather than Core or Extended. The question-style distribution differs from Cambridge enough that pacing has to be relearned, which is a two-session job if caught before a mock and a lost paper if not. A tutor should know which tier and which paper structure without asking twice.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity decides grades: series and parallel resistance, potential dividers, electromotive force against potential difference. Ask any prospective tutor whether your child sits Paper 5 or Paper 6. If they do not know the difference between a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper, they have not taught this syllabus.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The Extended tier separates students on quantitative work: moles with a limiting reagent, ionic equations with state symbols, and electrode products in the electrolysis of aqueous solutions. Qualitative analysis, the tests for cations, anions and gases, is pure recall and the cheapest set of marks on the paper to secure.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Command terms matter more here than anywhere else in the sciences. Osmosis has to be explained in terms of water potential rather than described, transpiration and translocation are routinely confused, and genetic crosses need complete notation because the marks sit in the working rather than in the final ratio.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Sciences 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1
subjects.description: Untiered, two written papers each, and no separate practical examination. Practical skills are examined inside the theory papers, so a method-evaluation question can appear without warning mid-paper. A tutor preparing an Edexcel candidate for a Paper 6 that does not exist on their specification is a real and common mismatch.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: Heavily structured and therefore heavily coachable. The summary and directed-writing tasks have formats that reward precision in register and length. Students who learn the formats gain faster than students who read more widely, which makes this a strong choice for short, focused blocks of work.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Marks live in structured evaluation: a point, an explanation, a consequence, a judgement. Content-rich answers with no judgement cap mid-band regardless of accuracy. Because the structure is a template, these subjects respond unusually well to a small number of late, disciplined sessions.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three sciences in two subjects' worth of teaching time, reported as a double award. The matching risk is specific: a tutor who is strong in one of the three and merely competent in the others. Ask directly which of biology, chemistry and physics they have taught to examination, and in which years.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Higher Level Diploma mathematics or A Level. Calculus and kinematics arrive here before anywhere else on their timetable. Content density is high, so this is the clearest case for starting early rather than booking a rescue block in the second term.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Theory and problem-solving across two papers, with pseudocode and trace tables as recurring mark-earners. Students who can program fluently still lose marks because the paper wants pseudocode in the board's conventions rather than working code, which is a specific habit a specialist teaches directly.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside IGCSE in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. For non-Arab students these occupy the timetable space that independent study would otherwise use, which is part of why Year 11 past-paper time is scarcer in Dubai than the syllabus assumes.

sections.heading: Is there anybody near TECOM who knows the syllabus? The honest answer
paragraphs: Probably not many, and the reason is structural rather than a comment on anybody. Barsha Heights has no large school campus inside it, so it does not have the teacher population that grows around a campus. The adults within a short drive who have taught Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended with Paper 6 through to examination are few, and the ones advertising locally are mostly offering general tutoring across several subjects and year groups, which is a different product.

That is not a reason to dismiss local tutors. It is a reason to verify rather than assume. A general tutor who supervises homework and keeps a Year 9 student on top of their work is genuinely useful and reasonably priced, with published Dubai budget rates starting at AED 33 to 65 an hour. The failure happens when a family buys that product in Year 11 for an Extended-tier science and expects a diagnosis, which it cannot deliver because the person has never marked the paper.

The published market gives you a rough map of who is who. Budget online and university-student tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists across IB, IGCSE and A Level run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, travel included. Every figure there was published by somebody else and read in October 2026.

What the price does not tell you is whether the person has taught your child's code. That is why the next section is a list of questions rather than a sales argument. Ask them of us, ask them of the tutor on the building noticeboard, ask them of the centre on Sheikh Zayed Road. The answers sort the market faster than any review page, and they cost nothing.

sections.heading: Ten questions that separate a specialist from a generalist
paragraphs: Here is the test, with the answers a genuine specialist gives. It takes five minutes on a phone call and works on anybody, including us. Nothing in it requires you to know the subject; it only requires you to notice whether the answers are specific or general. A generalist is not lying when they answer vaguely, they simply do not have the information, and that is exactly what you are trying to find out.

The first three questions establish whether the person has looked at your child's situation at all. The syllabus code, the tier, and the practical paper. A specialist asks to see the timetable rather than guessing. The middle questions establish whether they know the paper structure, which is where a Cambridge-only tutor preparing an Edexcel candidate is exposed, because they will reach for Paper 6 on a specification that does not have one.

The last questions are about conduct rather than knowledge, and they matter just as much. Whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. Whether they will write any part of a coursework submission, which the correct answer declines. Whether they teach at your child's own school, because the permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school and ADEK's rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of their own students. And what happens if the match is wrong.

One note on how to use this. The point is not to catch anybody out; it is to buy the right product. If the answers come back general and the price is low and your child is in Year 9 needing routine, that may be exactly the right purchase. If the answers come back general and the price is at specialist level, that is a mismatch worth walking away from. The list simply makes the mismatch visible before the money moves.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor privately in the UAE
paragraphs: This is the section nobody in this search publishes properly, and it is the one with legal substance. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The eligible categories are specific and broader than most families assume. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. That last pair explains much of the local advertising around Knowledge Village and Dubai Internet City: a university student tutoring with a permit is operating entirely legitimately, and is a reasonable purchase for the right job.

Two things must not be said, and you should be suspicious of anybody who says them. First, that a permit is optional. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. Second, any specific fine amount. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so no number should be quoted to you by anybody, including us.

There is a separate regime for operations with premises. A tutoring business with staff and a location in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a specific instrument issued to specific institutions. IB Gram does not hold it, does not operate premises in the UAE, and does not describe itself as KHDA approved. Any provider using that phrase should be asked to produce the permit number.

sections.heading: The red flags in this market, with what they actually indicate
paragraphs: Research for this project fetched and read more than sixty competitor pages in this market, and the same handful of problems recurred. Publishing them is more useful than claiming to be different, because a parent who recognises the patterns can evaluate anybody, including whoever ranks above this page next month.

Self-asserted star ratings are the most common. One competitor publishes an AggregateRating of 4.9 in its structured data with nothing countable behind it. Another shows 4.92 out of 5 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 reviews on the same page, which cannot both be true. A third shows 5.0 from 20 reviews alongside a claim of serving 2,500 students. Fabricated review markup breaches Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, is a consumer-protection exposure. A rating you cannot click through to individual dated reviews tells you nothing.

Price opacity is the second. Three of six researched pages publish no price at all, and one page's own FAQ asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. Two quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. A separate page's structured-data price range contradicts the figure in its visible text. If a provider will not state a rate, a session length and a VAT position in writing, that is information about how the eventual invoice will be constructed.

The third is the serious one. One page found during this research sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published price. That is not tutoring. It is an academic-integrity breach that triggers malpractice proceedings against the student, not the seller, and a family who buys it is buying a risk to their child's qualification. Any provider willing to produce assessed work is also willing to misrepresent other things. Treat the offer itself as the disqualifying signal.
bullets: A star rating with no clickable, dated individual reviews behind it
A price range in structured data that contradicts the visible page

A non-UAE phone number as the only contact route on a UAE page
A stated Dubai address on a page about a different emirate
Any offer to write, complete or supply an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay

sections.heading: Why IGCSE tutor is not a job description
paragraphs: The phrase covers at least a dozen different jobs, and matching the wrong one is the most common waste of money in this market. A Year 10 student on Cambridge 0580 Core who needs confidence and routine, and a Year 11 student on Pearson 4CH1 who needs titration arithmetic and method-evaluation questions eight weeks before a paper, are both asking for an IGCSE tutor. Almost nothing about the right person is the same.

The variables are few enough to list and specific enough to match on. The board, because Cambridge and Pearson tier differently and assess practical work differently. The tier, because it caps the grade and determines the paper set. The practical route, Paper 5 or Paper 6 or examined-within-the-written-papers. The year group, because Year 10 is a content job and Year 11 term three is an execution job. And the component the marks are being lost in, which a marked paper reveals and a conversation usually does not.

The table below is the version of this a parent can use. Find the row that matches your child and you have a specification for the person you need, which you can then test against the ten questions in the earlier section. It also shows why one tutor covering three sciences at Extended tier is usually a compromise rather than a convenience: the rows are genuinely different jobs, and a person who is excellent at one is often merely adequate at the next.

This is also the honest basis for us to say when we are not the right purchase. A family needing light weekly homework supervision for a Year 9 student is better served by a budget tutor at the published floor than by a specialist rate, and we will say so. A family eight weeks from a series wanting five subjects covered is going to get a recommendation for two. Matching correctly sometimes means a smaller sale, and a provider who never says that is not matching anything.

sections.heading: What the local pool and the wider pool each actually offer
paragraphs: Set the two side by side honestly. A nearby in-person tutor gives you presence in the room, a face your child sees weekly, and no technology to go wrong. Those are genuine goods and for some students they are decisive. The published Dubai in-home band is AED 180 to 350 an hour from Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, with travel inside the price, and monthly in-home packages seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

A wider online pool gives you specification match, scheduling that flexes, and a selection that is not limited by who will drive to Barsha Heights at half past five. Published rates for qualified online subject tutors are AED 150 to 300, with monthly online packages seen at AED 799 for eight sessions. The gap between the two columns is not a quality gap; it is a travel cost, and what matters is whether travel is what your particular student needs to buy.

For Barsha Heights specifically, three local factors push the answer one way. The community has no campus of its own, so the nearby teacher population is thin. Children already commute outward daily, so the week has no appetite for another journey. And the roads out, towards Al Barsha across the interchange and towards Sheikh Zayed Road, are at their worst in exactly the window a session would run. A tutor driving in at 17:30 arrives with a variable twenty minutes attached.

The table sets out the comparison with the verification question attached to each option, because that is the part a parent can act on. Whichever column you choose, the ten questions from earlier still apply. The worst outcome in this market is not choosing the wrong format; it is paying a specialist rate for a generalist in either format, which happens because the advertising for both looks the same.

sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the boundaries we keep
paragraphs: A verification page has to cover this, because the willingness to cross the line is itself a verification signal. A tutor may teach content, explain a mark scheme, model how a question type is answered, mark the student's own work and give feedback on it, and coach planning and revision. That is teaching, and a reasonable test is whether your child's own teacher could do the same thing openly.

A tutor may not produce assessed work on a student's behalf, dictate answers for transcription, or edit a submission until the words are no longer the student's. For IGCSE science, where an internally assessed practical component or investigation contributes, the work must be the candidate's own and the school signs a declaration to that effect. A provider offering to help with coursework in unspecified ways has usually chosen those words carefully, and the right response is to ask exactly what help means.

Past papers carry a copyright dimension that the market routinely ignores. Cambridge, Pearson and the International Baccalaureate own their syllabus documents, question papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables. We reference them, cite the official source and link out to cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than hosting copies, and we do not distribute them as downloads. A service offering your child a downloadable library has a copyright problem of its own, and the official material is reachable through the school anyway.

The accreditation question belongs here too. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none of those relationships. We explain what each body does because understanding the framework helps you evaluate providers. Anybody using the phrase KHDA-approved tutors should be asked to produce the permit, because the permit it refers to is a specific instrument issued to institutions with premises.

sections.heading: Booking, and the limits we will tell you about first
paragraphs: Send the board, the syllabus codes, the year group and the tier if you know it. If you have a marked piece of work, send that instead of a description, because it answers in two minutes what a conversation takes twenty to establish. We match a tutor who has taught that code at that tier, and the first session is free and runs as a timed past-paper section rather than an introduction.

You then get a short written note: which marks went to content, which to method, which to technique and which to timing, and a realistic number of sessions for the window you have. Use that note to compare us against anybody else you are considering, which is what it is for. If the honest recommendation is fewer sessions in fewer subjects, the note will say so, and if a budget tutor is the right purchase for your situation it will say that too.

Three limits are worth stating before you book. First, availability concentrates: requests for a 17:30 weekday slot in the second term, which is exactly what Barsha Heights bus schedules produce, are the hardest to staff in the year. Second, some combinations are thin, particularly Edexcel science specialists for specific weekend hours. Third, if no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will tell you whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you may decline. No competitor researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

On format, once more and plainly: IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai and no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the past paper and the mark scheme shared between tutor and student. Sessions for Barsha Heights families generally start at 17:30 or 18:00 because bus routes rather than bells decide when a child is home, and during Ramadan they move to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there.

They determine which papers are sat and therefore what is worth teaching. A request that includes them is matched in one step; a request that says IGCSE science takes two sessions to narrow down and you pay for those.

We would rather be tested than trusted, and the same questions work on every other provider you are considering. A vague answer from anybody, including us, is the information you were looking for.

process.description: Cambridge 0620 Extended with Paper 6 and Pearson 4CH1 are different teaching jobs, and preparing an Edexcel candidate for a Paper 6 that does not exist on their specification is a real and common mismatch. We match on all three variables rather than on the subject name.

process.description: Timed past-paper section, marked honestly, with a written note afterwards naming where the marks went and how many sessions the remaining window realistically needs. You read it before committing anything, and you can take it to another provider for comparison without any awkwardness from us.

process.title: Hours put where the marks are
process.description: The plan ranks work by marks at stake on a real paper rather than by syllabus order, which is why chemistry recall sheets often come before organic chemistry and showing working comes before new content. You see the order before we begin, and you can change it.

process.title: Reviewed on marks, replaced on request
process.description: Every fourth session includes a timed section measured against earlier attempts at the same question types. If the marks have not moved where we worked, the approach was wrong and we change it rather than adding hours. If the tutor is the wrong fit, say so after the second session and we change the tutor without an argument.

whyPoints.description: Second-term 17:30 slots are the scarcest hours of the year, and Edexcel science specialists for specific weekend times can take longer to staff. We give you a date rather than taking a booking and hoping, and we say when a tutor is based outside the UAE so you can decline.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IGCSE specialist living near TECOM?
faqs.answer: Fewer than you would expect, and the reason is structural. Barsha Heights has no large school campus inside it, so the teacher population that usually grows around a campus is not there. Most secondary students in the community are bussed outward, and the local tutoring advertising comes largely from freelancers and from the university pool near Knowledge Village and Dubai Internet City. That can be a good purchase for routine and homework supervision. What it rarely provides is somebody who has marked Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended Paper 6 and can diagnose from it.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor really knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask five short questions. Which syllabus code is my child entered for. Which tier. Do they sit Paper 5 or Paper 6. What is the practical component worth. And how will you diagnose in the first session. A specialist asks to see the timetable and then answers precisely: 0620, Extended, Paper 6, a fifth of the grade, a timed past-paper section marked honestly. A generalist answers in general terms, which is not dishonesty but is exactly the information you were trying to obtain before paying a specialist rate.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai actually need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is officially published, so be suspicious of anybody quoting an amount. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

faqs.question: Can a university student in Dubai Internet City legally tutor my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, because university students are explicitly listed among the eligible categories under the 2023 resolution. Whether they are the right tutor is a separate question from whether they are a legal one. For a Year 9 student needing structure and homework supervision, a permitted university student at the published Dubai budget rate of roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour can be an entirely sensible purchase. For an Extended-tier diagnosis in Year 11, it usually is not.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA permit actually cover, and does IB Gram hold one?
faqs.answer: The KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute is issued to tutoring operations with premises and staff in Dubai. It involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold it, operates no premises, office, centre or branch in the UAE, and does not describe itself as KHDA approved. If any provider uses the phrase KHDA-approved tutors, ask them to produce the permit number, because it refers to a specific institutional instrument.

faqs.question: Should I hire a teacher from my child's own school privately?
faqs.answer: Be careful. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and check the current policy document, but the direction is clear. There is also a practical reason to look elsewhere: an independent specialist gives you a genuinely independent read on where the marks are going.

faqs.question: Why do some tutoring sites show star ratings I cannot verify?
faqs.answer: Because self-asserted review markup is easy to publish and rarely checked. Research for this project found one competitor publishing a 4.9 rating in structured data with nothing countable behind it, another showing 4.92 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 reviews on the same page, and a third showing 5.0 from 20 reviews next to a claim of 2,500 students. Fabricated ratings breach Google's structured-data policy and are a consumer-protection exposure in the UAE. A rating with no clickable, dated individual reviews behind it tells you nothing.

faqs.question: Why will some providers not tell me their hourly rate?
faqs.answer: It varies, but the pattern is worth noticing. Three of six researched pages in this market publish no price at all, and one page's own frequently asked questions ask what tutoring costs and then decline to answer. Two quote in US dollars rather than dirhams, which UAE families do not transact in, and one publishes a structured-data price range that contradicts its visible text. Ask for a rate, a session length and a VAT position in writing. A provider unwilling to supply all three has told you how the invoice will eventually be built.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge and Pearson for my child?
faqs.answer: Enough to change who you should hire. Cambridge single sciences are tiered Core or Extended and carry a separate practical component, either Paper 5 as a laboratory test or Paper 6 as the alternative to practical. Pearson International GCSE sciences are untiered with no separate practical examination, and practical skills are examined inside the written papers. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is Core or Extended while Pearson 4MA1 is Foundation or Higher. A tutor preparing an Edexcel candidate for a Paper 6 that their specification does not contain is a common and expensive mismatch.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Often, and we would rather say so than pretend otherwise. For a Year 9 or early Year 10 student who needs routine, company and somebody to check that homework has been done, published Dubai budget rates start at roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour and the purchase is sound. What a budget hour cannot deliver is a tier-specific diagnosis, mark-scheme wording for an alternative-to-practical paper, or a plan built from a marked script. Buying the cheap product in Year 11 for an Extended-tier science is where families lose money, not in buying it at all.

faqs.question: What time do sessions run for families in Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: Later than in the villa communities nearby, because bus routes rather than school bells decide when a child is home. A 17:30 start is normal for Barsha Heights and 18:00 is often better, particularly for a second sibling. Those happen to be the scarcest slots in the year during the second term, so booking them early matters. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there, with the same tutor keeping the same student rather than a reshuffle.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a tutor to our apartment in TECOM?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and we state that plainly rather than letting a family discover it after a call. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the past paper and the mark scheme shared on screen. For Barsha Heights the trade is unusually clean: your child already commutes outward for school every day, the roads out are at their worst at exactly the hour a session runs, and what the online format buys is the specialist the postcode does not contain.

faqs.question: What should I do if a provider offers to help with coursework?
faqs.answer: Ask precisely what help means, in writing. Legitimate help is teaching the assessment criteria, explaining what a top band contains, marking the student's own draft and asking the questions that expose a weak section. Illegitimate help is writing, drafting or editing a submission until the words are no longer the student's. Research for this project found a page selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach whose consequences fall on the student, and the offer itself should end the conversation.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers and mark schemes for us to download?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody legitimately can. Cambridge, Pearson and the International Baccalaureate own their syllabus documents, question papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, and distributing copies is copyright infringement. We reference them, cite the official source and link out to cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, and we work from them inside a session. Your child's school can reach the official material directly, which is the right route. A provider advertising a downloadable library has a copyright problem of its own.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find a tutor for our subject and slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date, rather than taking the booking and hoping. Demand concentrates in the second term and in the weeks before a series, and the 17:30 and 18:00 slots that Barsha Heights bus schedules produce are the scarcest hours of the year. Some combinations are thin, particularly Edexcel science specialists for a specific weekend time. If no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you are free to decline.

intro.heading: Where an IGCSE tutor for The Greens actually has to be
paragraphs: The Greens is a low-rise apartment community on the Al Thanyah side of Sheikh Zayed Road, sandwiched between Dubai Internet City, Barsha Heights and the Emirates Golf Club. It has a metro station on its doorstep and Al Khail Road behind it, which makes it one of the easier addresses in Dubai to reach. That convenience is exactly why the phrase "IGCSE tutor near me" misleads parents here. Reach is not the constraint. Time is.

Count the hours honestly. A Year 10 or Year 11 student in The Greens is usually on a bus or in a car between about three and four in the afternoon, depending on whether the school sits in the community itself, in Al Sufouh, in Al Barsha or further south in Jumeirah Village. Add an after-school club and the arrival slides past four. Add the eastbound crawl on Sheikh Zayed Road and it slides again. The usable window for a focused academic hour on a school night runs from roughly four o'clock to half past seven, and a sibling, a prayer time and a meal are all competing for the same slice of it.

A tutor who travels into that window spends part of it travelling. A tutor who appears on screen at 16:15 does not. That single difference is why online IGCSE tutoring in The Greens is not a compromise on a local tutor; it is the only version of the service that reliably fits the day a Greens family actually has. It also widens the choice from whoever happens to drive this side of Interchange 4 to whoever genuinely teaches Cambridge 0580 Extended, or Pearson 4PH1, or English as a Second Language at the level your child is entered for.

The syllabus point matters more than parents expect. Schools around The Greens do not all sit the same IGCSE. Some run Cambridge International, some run Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a few split by department so a child sits Cambridge sciences and a Pearson maths paper in the same summer. A tutor who knows one board well and the other vaguely will coach the wrong paper structure for half the year. Asking for the syllabus code on the exam entry is a two-minute job that removes most of the risk.

What follows is the practical version of this page: which schools this neighbourhood feeds, what time each of them releases a secondary student, when a session realistically starts, which boards those schools enter, what the Dubai market charges, and how the Cambridge and Pearson calendars run backwards from an exam to the decision you have to make months earlier. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India, and every UAE lesson is delivered over live video.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to a family in The Greens: the lower secondary years that decide which IGCSE tier a child is entered for, the two IGCSE years themselves, the Pearson Edexcel route some local schools prefer, and the post-16 fork into A Level or the IB Diploma.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, ending in Checkpoint tests that many Dubai schools use to set groups and recommend Core or Extended entry. Checkpoint is low-stakes in itself and high-stakes in effect: the set a child lands in at the end of Year 9 often decides the tier they are entered for two years later, and moving up afterwards takes a term of catch-up on topics the Core group never saw.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which for a Greens family means the decision window sits in the middle of a Dubai school year rather than at its end. Support at this stage is usually one session a week on the two subjects that will gate the tier choice, almost always mathematics and a science.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, examined in a June or November series, with most subjects sat as two or three written papers. Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended; the sciences 0625, 0620 and 0610 are tiered and carry a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Grades run 9 to 1 on the reformed scale, and the tier a child is entered for caps the grade available to them.
programmes.countryNote: A Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tutor in Dubai will ask one question first: Core or Extended. For a student in The Greens the answer is on the exam entry the school submits, and the entry deadline falls months before the paper. Getting that wrong is the single most expensive mistake available in Year 11, because the ceiling is fixed by the tier rather than by the revision.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other British-curriculum route, examined in May/June and November each year. Codes look different and so do the papers: 4MA1 mathematics is tiered Foundation and Higher over two papers, while 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical test. Some subjects also offer a coursework alternative.
programmes.countryNote: A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE tutor in Dubai has to teach a different paper shape, not a different subject. The November series is the quiet advantage here: Pearson publishes a November window each year, so a Greens student who misses a grade in the summer does not lose a full academic year waiting for the next chance.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma after IGCSE
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools in Dubai run IGCSE at 16 and then split into A Level or the IB Diploma. The choice is made in the spring of Year 11, before results, on the strength of mock grades and subject interest. Entry requirements for the harder A Levels and for Higher Level Diploma subjects are usually expressed as IGCSE grades in that subject.
programmes.countryNote: Around The Greens both routes are available within a short drive, which means the Year 11 decision is real rather than theoretical. Schools in the Emirates Living cluster and in Al Barsha offer A Level, the IB Diploma, or both, so a child's IGCSE grade profile decides options rather than a change of address.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects families in The Greens, The Views and The Springs ask for most often. The syllabus codes are Cambridge unless a Pearson equivalent is named, and every one of them should be checked against your child's own exam entry.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers, one without a calculator on the Pearson route. Marks are lost most often on algebraic fractions, transformations of graphs and the multi-step problems that carry four or five marks at the end of a paper. Extended adds functions, vectors and conditional probability that Core never sees.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. It introduces calculus, logarithms and binomial expansion a year early, and it is the cleanest bridge between IGCSE and the first term of a post-16 maths course.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Cambridge candidates sit three papers including a practical test or alternative to practical; Pearson assesses practical skills inside two written papers. Electricity, moments and the graph-interpretation questions in the alternative-to-practical paper are where the predictable marks go missing.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations separate the top grades from the middle ones, and organic chemistry arrives late enough in Year 11 that it is often under-practised. Ionic equations and the practical paper's planning questions reward technique more than recall.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume, not the difficulty, is what catches students out. Marks concentrate in genetics, transport in plants and the data-handling questions, where a precise command term answer scores and a general description does not.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: The double-award and single-award routes for students who need science without three separate subjects. Coordinated Sciences 0654 counts as two IGCSEs across three papers; it compresses all three disciplines, so the common failure is thin coverage rather than weak understanding.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading and writing papers that reward structure and precision over length. Directed writing and the summary question are the two places where a confident speaker of English still drops marks, because both are tested against a mark scheme rather than against fluency.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Common across Dubai's international cohorts and frequently under-prepared because the student speaks English all day. The exercises are formulaic, which makes them very trainable: note-making, summary and the extended writing task each have a repeatable shape.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper and a structured paper. Students who read widely still lose marks on the eight-mark evaluation questions, which require a judgement supported by a diagram rather than a list of advantages and disadvantages.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study driven, so the skill being tested is applying a term to the business in front of you rather than defining it. Calculation questions on break-even and cash flow are the reliable marks most students leave on the table.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers data representation, networks and security; Paper 2 covers algorithms and programming. Pseudocode tracing and the longer program-design question are where the grade is decided, and both improve quickly with timed practice.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Foreign Language (0508 / 0544)
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Tutoring has to match the stream a child is actually in.

sections.heading: What a search for an IGCSE tutor near The Greens actually returns
paragraphs: A local search answers the wrong question. It ranks providers by how close their office is to the Al Thanyah interchange, and a tuition centre two kilometres away is no more likely to employ someone who has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended to a Year 11 than one in Al Quoz. Proximity is a proxy for convenience, and for a family in The Greens convenience is a function of the clock, not the map.

The second problem is that most results are not teaching at all. The listings for this kind of query mix agencies, marketplaces, individual freelancers and essay-writing operations that sell completed coursework. The last category is worth recognising on sight: anyone offering to supply a finished Internal Assessment or a written-up piece of coursework is selling a malpractice risk that falls on the student, not on them.

The useful questions are narrower and all of them can be answered in a first phone call. Which board and syllabus code is my child entered for, and have you taught it this academic year? Which tier is the entry, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher? What time can you start on a Sunday and a Tuesday in Gulf Standard Time? What do I get in writing after each session? A provider who answers those four cleanly is a better bet than one whose address is closer.

IB Gram answers them the same way every time. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, the tutor names the syllabus they teach before the first paid session, the trial lesson is free and needs no card details, and nothing is sent to a UAE address because home visits are an India-only part of the service.

sections.heading: The Greens school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Every tutoring plan in this community lives or dies on one number: the time your child is actually free. The table below sets out the typical secondary finish at the campuses Greens families use most, the journey back into the community, and the earliest hour at which a focused academic session is realistic rather than theoretical. The windows are indicative rather than measured, so check them against your own school's published day and your own bus route.

Two patterns show up every year. The first is that the published finish time is not the departure time. Secondary buses load after form groups, and a school that finishes at 15:15 often releases its buses closer to 15:30. The second is that clubs are not optional in practice. A student in a school team or a Duke of Edinburgh group loses two or three afternoons a week to 16:30, which is why fixed weekday slots in The Greens cluster around the back half of the afternoon rather than the front.

The practical consequence is that a one-hour window beginning at 16:00 or 16:30 is the only slot that survives a full term. Earlier and it collides with the commute; later and it collides with dinner, prayer times and the school homework that still has to be done. Families who try to run tutoring at 15:30 usually abandon it by October. Families who book 16:30 keep it until May.

This is also where the case for live video stops being an argument about technology. A tutor crossing Sheikh Zayed Road westbound at four in the afternoon cannot promise 16:30, and a tutor who cannot promise 16:30 cannot hold a weekly slot through a Dubai winter term.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE board the schools around The Greens actually sit
paragraphs: Dubai runs seventeen different curricula across its private schools, and the British curriculum carries the largest share of enrolment at thirty-seven per cent. Inside that share sit two distinct examination boards, and a family only discovers which one applies to them when the exam entry arrives. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are not interchangeable: the paper counts differ, the practical assessment differs, and the tier names differ.

The table below maps the subjects most often requested in this cluster. Read it alongside your child's entry rather than instead of it, because schools occasionally split boards by department. A student sitting Cambridge sciences and a Pearson maths paper in the same series is not unusual in Dubai, and a tutor who assumes one board for everything will coach the wrong paper structure in at least one subject.

The most consequential difference is practical science. Cambridge candidates sit a separate practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, which rewards a very particular skill: reading an unfamiliar method, spotting the controlled variable, and interpreting a table of someone else's results. Pearson folds those skills into the written papers instead. A student who has only practised one of these formats will find the other distinctly unfamiliar in the hall.

Verify every code on the board's own site rather than on a tutoring page, including this one. Cambridge publishes syllabus documents at cambridgeinternational.org and Pearson at qualifications.pearson.com, and both revise specifications on a published cycle.

sections.heading: Why distance stops mattering in Year 10
paragraphs: Up to about Year 9, a capable generalist can help with most subjects. From Year 10 the work narrows sharply. The question stops being "can you explain quadratics" and becomes "can you show my child how Cambridge words a four-mark question on transformations of graphs, and what the mark scheme actually accepts". That is board-specific, tier-specific and paper-specific knowledge, and it does not correlate with how close someone lives.

This is where a radius search works against a Greens family. Restricting the search to tutors who can drive to Al Thanyah by half past four shrinks the pool to whoever is free in the western half of Dubai at that hour. Removing the travel requirement widens it to everyone who teaches that syllabus at that tier, which is the only variable that changes a grade. A parent is trading a convenience they do not need for a specialism they do.

The second gain is continuity. Tutors who travel lose slots to traffic, roadworks and the school-run peak on Sheikh Zayed Road, and a missed session in March is worth more than three in October. A video session is cancelled by illness and almost nothing else, and it survives a family trip, a school exchange and a half-term abroad without renegotiating the arrangement.

To be plain about the model: IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address, and it does not operate a centre in Dubai. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted by local agencies from roughly AED 180 an hour upwards, and that figure is a market rate rather than ours. What IB Gram sells in the UAE is one-to-one teaching over live video, with screen sharing for past papers and marked scripts.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from The Greens
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a session calendar, which is strange, because every real decision in IGCSE is made months before the exam. The entry deadline fixes the tier. The forecast-grade deadline fixes what the school tells universities. The results date fixes how long a re-sit takes. A family that sees those dates in order plans differently from one that sees only the exam week.

The table below is built on Pearson's published International GCSE dates, because Pearson publishes a whole series in detail, with Cambridge rows showing the shape of the two sittings a Dubai candidate can actually enter: June and November. Read the gap between an entry row and its paper row carefully. Pearson's November 2026 papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry that fixed the subject list and tier for them had closed in the preceding summer. The tier decision is therefore taken a term or more before the first paper, and it cannot be undone by revision afterwards.

One Cambridge rule deserves its own sentence for any Dubai family. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone your centre sits in and work only from that timetable.

IB Diploma dates are deliberately absent from this page. The IB's own site is not reliably readable by automated checks, and nothing on these pages publishes an IB session or results date that has not been read from ibo.org or confirmed by a school's IB coordinator. If your child is heading for the Diploma, take those dates from the school rather than from any tutoring site.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number a household budget actually feels. A single weekly hour is four or five sessions a month. On the rates published across the Dubai market in 2026, that lands a budget online tutor somewhere around AED 240 to 600 a month, a mid-market qualified subject tutor between roughly AED 600 and 1,200, and an exam-year specialist from about AED 1,000 to beyond AED 2,000. Those monthly bands come from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026.

The hourly bands behind them are easy to summarise. University-student and budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit between about AED 150 and 300. IGCSE, IB and A-Level specialists are quoted from around AED 200 to 450 and upwards. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650. In-home one-to-one visits, with travel built into the price, are quoted from about AED 180 to 500 an hour, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions have been advertised in Dubai at AED 1,599 to 1,799.

Compare those last two lines and the travel premium becomes visible. The same qualification level costs more in a car than on a screen, and the extra buys transport rather than teaching. For a family in The Greens, where the usable evening window is ninety minutes wide, paying a premium for a format that consumes part of that window twice over is the clearest waste available in this market.

None of the figures above is an IB Gram price. They are market rates gathered from published Dubai rate cards and aggregator tables in 2026, and they are here so you can judge any quote, including ours, against something. Our own starting point is a free trial lesson with no card details, followed by a quoted rate for the specific subject, tier and session length your child needs.
