sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and your child's week
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and it publishes each school's report. Read the subject-level commentary rather than the headline band: a school rated the same overall can be strong in science and weak in mathematics, and that difference is what decides whether you need a tutor.

What surprises many families new to Dubai is that an international curriculum does not replace the UAE's own requirements. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. These subjects occupy real timetable space alongside the IGCSE courses and they generate their own homework.

Those rules shape your child's week in ways the timetable does not explain. Arab and non-Arab students sit Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies in separate classes, which KHDA requires because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction are genuinely different; combined classes are prohibited outright. Time is counted in forty-minute units, and a school may run longer or shorter lessons so long as the weekly total holds, with KHDA setting twenty-five minutes as the floor for any mandatory subject lesson. For a Greens family, the practical consequence is that these periods are fixed points the rest of the week has to move around, so tutoring slots are easier to find on the evenings the mandatory subjects do not already own.

For Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring in Dubai there is one more constraint worth knowing. For these mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so support has to work with the school's own material rather than import a parallel syllabus. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA permission to teach those subjects in school, which is a credential a parent can ask about directly.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: Several providers ranking for this query sell finished assessed work. One advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. A parent needs to understand what that transaction actually is: submitting work a student did not produce is malpractice under examination board rules, and the consequence falls on the candidate, up to and including loss of the qualification. The provider carries none of that risk.

The honest boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, model a worked example on a different question, discuss a plan the student has written, give feedback on a draft the student has produced, and ask questions that make a weak argument visible to the student. That is teaching, and it is exactly what the criteria reward, because a student who can explain their own method scores better than one reciting someone else's.

What a tutor must not do is also clear. No tutor at IB Gram will write the coursework, produce a draft for submission, supply a model answer to be copied, or edit a piece of work to the point where the words are no longer the student's. If a session drifts towards that, the tutor is instructed to stop and say so in the session note that goes to you.

The same line applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the examination boards and are not redistributed here. Tutors reference them, cite the official source, and link out to cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com so a parent can read the original.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the shape of the Dubai school year
paragraphs: A tutoring plan built on a European school calendar fails in Dubai. The academic year starts in late August or early September, breaks for a fortnight around December, breaks again in spring, and finishes in late June or early July. Those breaks sit awkwardly relative to the examination series, and a family that does not plan around them loses the three or four weeks that matter most.

Ramadan reshapes the day rather than removing it. School hours shorten, afternoons are quieter, and evening energy arrives after Iftar rather than before it. Sessions move to a late slot and often work better than usual, because the student is not coming off a full school day. Families who ask for a post-Iftar time in advance keep their weekly rhythm; families who try to hold a four o'clock slot through Ramadan usually lose the month.

The summer break is the other lever. Nine or ten weeks is long enough to undo a year of fluency in mathematics and long enough to fix one. A short block through July on the two or three topics a report card flagged costs less than the same work bought in a panic in April, and it lands at a point in the year where nothing else is competing for the student's attention.

Public holidays and the UAE's own national observances also interrupt weekly slots, which is a scheduling matter rather than an academic one. A fixed weekly session that can be moved rather than lost is the only arrangement that survives a Dubai year intact, and that flexibility is far easier to offer when nobody has to plan a drive.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in The Greens, or is it all online?
faqs.answer: IB Gram delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video, so there is no tutor who comes to a Greens address. Home visits are an India-only part of the service. Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do offer in-home visits, and the market quotes them from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel built in. For a family in The Greens the practical argument against that format is the clock: the usable evening window is about ninety minutes wide, and a car journey eats into it at both ends while adding nothing to the teaching.

faqs.question: What time does the school day end for Greens families, and when can a session start?
faqs.answer: Secondary days at the schools this community uses typically finish between about 15:00 and 15:30, but buses load after form groups and clubs regularly run to 16:30. Once the journey back across Al Thanyah or Sheikh Zayed Road is counted, the earliest reliable start for a focused session is around 16:00 for schools inside Emirates Living and closer to 16:30 for the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha campuses. Treat those as indicative and confirm against your own school calendar and bus route before fixing a weekly slot.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE schools do children living in The Greens usually attend?
faqs.answer: Three clusters cover most of it. Inside Emirates Living there is a British-curriculum school in The Greens itself plus campuses in The Meadows and towards Emirates Hills. Ten to twenty-five minutes out sits the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha belt, which includes several of the longest-established British-curriculum schools in Dubai. South down Al Khail Road are the newer Jumeirah Village, Al Furjan and Motor City campuses. Schools are named on this page as neighbourhood context only; no affiliation or endorsement is implied by listing them.

faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE tutor need to live in The Greens to be useful?
faqs.answer: No, and insisting on it narrows the search in the wrong dimension. From Year 10 the useful knowledge is board-specific and tier-specific: how Cambridge words a four-mark question on transformations, what the mark scheme accepts, how the alternative-to-practical paper is structured. None of that correlates with an address. Filtering for someone who can reach Al Thanyah by half past four shrinks the pool to whoever is free in western Dubai at that hour, which is a convenience constraint standing in for an academic one.

faqs.question: How late can a weekday IGCSE session run before homework suffers?
faqs.answer: Most families in this community find the practical limit is a finish by about 19:00. School homework, the mandatory UAE subjects and a meal all have to fit after that, and a student working past eight on a Tuesday is usually too tired for the Wednesday lesson. A sixty-minute session starting between 16:15 and 18:00 is the pattern that survives a full term here. Ninety-minute sessions work better in a school break than on a school night.

faqs.question: Can a Greens family book IGCSE sessions on a Friday or at the weekend?
faqs.answer: Yes, and weekends are where longer sessions belong. The UAE working week leaves Saturday and Sunday free for most school-age students, and a ninety-minute weekend block handles whole-topic repair in a way a weekday hour cannot. Friday arrangements depend on the family's own routine around prayer times, and the slot is agreed in Gulf Standard Time so there is no ambiguity about which hour was booked. Weekend slots fill earliest in the run-up to a mock series.

faqs.question: Which exam board do schools near The Greens use for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are sat in this part of Dubai, and some schools split boards by department. That is why the exam entry matters more than the prospectus. Cambridge science candidates sit a separate practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson assesses those skills inside the written papers. Cambridge maths is tiered Core and Extended while Pearson is Foundation and Higher. Check the syllabus code on the entry and verify it at cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE tutors charge around The Greens and Dubai Internet City?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates in 2026 put budget and university-student online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online at about AED 150 to 300, and IGCSE specialists from around AED 200 to 450 and upwards. In-home visits are quoted from about AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the price. Aggregator estimates for a single weekly hour run from AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end to AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an exam year. None of those is an IB Gram price.

faqs.question: What happens to our sessions when Sheikh Zayed Road traffic makes the school bus late?
faqs.answer: Nothing, which is the point of the format. A video session starts when your child sits down, so a bus arriving twenty minutes late costs twenty minutes rather than the whole hour, and the tutor is already there. Where a late arrival becomes routine, the standing slot is simply moved back to a time that matches reality. A tutor who had to drive in would be caught in the same traffic, which is why travelling arrangements in this community tend to drift and then lapse.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai Internet City metro station make an in-home IGCSE tutor practical?
faqs.answer: It makes one easier to reach than in most Dubai communities, which is worth knowing when comparing quotes. It does not change the arithmetic. A tutor arriving by metro still arrives inside the same narrow evening window, still cannot guarantee a half-past-four start, and still charges the in-home market rate of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour rather than the online rate. The convenience of the station is real; the premium you pay for travel still buys transport instead of teaching.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects can one tutor realistically cover for a Greens student?
faqs.answer: One well, sometimes two if they are closely related, such as mathematics and physics. Beyond that the claim usually means a generalist who knows each syllabus a little. In Year 11 the common pattern here is two subjects on one evening with two different specialists back to back, which keeps the rest of the week clear for school homework and the mandatory UAE subjects. Asking a single tutor to carry maths, chemistry and English is where parents most often feel the money was wasted.

faqs.question: When should a Year 10 living in The Greens start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Early in Year 10 if the tier decision is still open, because that is when it can still be influenced. In the UAE a Cambridge candidate sits June or November, and entries for the June series close in the spring, months before the paper, so the Core or Extended decision is effectively made a term or more ahead and cannot be revised by revision afterwards. If the entry is already fixed, the useful starting point is a diagnostic session on a past paper to find out which topics are actually costing marks rather than which ones feel difficult.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to post-Iftar timing for a Greens family during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually should. School hours shorten during Ramadan, afternoons go quiet and useful energy arrives after Iftar. Families who ask for a late slot in advance keep their weekly rhythm through the month; families who try to hold an afternoon time generally lose it. Because nobody is planning a drive, moving a video session to a post-Iftar hour is a scheduling change rather than a renegotiation, and the slot usually reverts to its normal time afterwards.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in those subjects, since the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. They take real timetable space and generate homework, which is why a realistic tutoring plan counts them rather than ignoring them.

faqs.question: What can an IGCSE tutor do with my child's coursework, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, model a worked example on a different question, discuss a plan the student wrote, and give feedback on the student's own draft. No tutor here will write the coursework, produce a draft for submission or edit work until the words stop being the student's. Submitting work a candidate did not produce is malpractice under board rules and the consequence falls on the student. Providers advertising finished assessed work are selling that risk, not a service.

faqs.question: How quickly can IB Gram match an IGCSE tutor for a student in The Greens?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects such as mathematics, the three sciences and English, a shortlist usually comes back within a working day or two and the free trial lesson follows soon after. Niche syllabuses take longer, and where nothing suitable is free in the hour you need, we say so instead of offering a generalist. The honest version of availability is more useful than a promise: a tutor who cannot hold your slot in February is not a match, however quickly they were found in October.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-lakes.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE subjects into Gulf Standard Time evenings. Ask two questions before the subject question: what time can they teach, and what is their permit position. Both answers tell you whether the arrangement will still exist in March.

intro.heading: Your child's school is not near you, and that changes the search
paragraphs: The Lakes has no secondary school inside it. Emirates Living as a whole has one IB continuum school, in The Meadows, and the British-curriculum schools that Lakes teenagers attend for IGCSE sit outside the community - mostly in Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and Al Sufouh, with a scatter down Al Khail Road into Motor City and Sports City. So a proximity search is being run from a house, about a school that is twenty-five minutes away, for a subject taught by somebody who probably lives near the school rather than near you.

That geography produces a specific problem. The tutors available within a short drive of Deema or Maeen are the ones who happen to live in Emirates Living or the communities beside it, and they teach whatever they teach. Your child needs a particular subject at a particular tier on a particular board - Cambridge 0580 Extended, say, or Pearson 4CH1 - and the intersection of 'lives nearby' and 'teaches that exact thing' is often empty. Hiring from a radius means hiring the available rather than the appropriate.

The second problem is the week rather than the map. A Year 10 or Year 11 student at a British-curriculum school in Dubai does not simply finish at 15:15 and become available. There is a prep load of an hour or more most nights, co-curricular commitments that the school expects to be honoured, and in many schools a fixture or a rehearsal that owns one evening entirely. Count those and most households find two evenings that can genuinely hold a lesson, not five.

State the delivery position plainly, since the phrase in the heading points the other way. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service offered only in India, and nobody arrives at a Lakes address under any arrangement sold here. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the paper open on a shared screen and marked during the lesson. Dubai's in-home market does exist and is published at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 online for equivalent credentials.

What the rest of this page covers is deliberately not a rate card. It sets out which schools The Lakes actually feeds and what each offers to 18. It explains how to check whether a tutor is legally permitted to teach your child, which is a free, two-day, two-year permit that almost nobody asks about. It names the five regulators covering UAE private schools, because four of them appear nowhere in the competing pages. And it covers the mandatory UAE subjects that run alongside IGCSE in every Dubai private school.

subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core or Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation or Higher
subjects.description: The subject that gates most sixth-form routes, and the one where tier matters most: Cambridge Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, while Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5. Most of the recoverable marks sit in showing working and in the multi-step questions at the end of each paper.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: The route most students take if they are not sitting three separate sciences. It is a different specification from the separate sciences, not a reduced version of them, so tutoring from separate-science material adds content the student will never be examined on. Confirm the code before the first lesson.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge centres enter either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper; Pearson examines practical skills inside the theory papers. Either way the recoverable marks are in units, circuit analysis and stating assumptions, all of which are written skills taught well on a shared screen.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ionic equations, mole calculations and precise observation language carry most of the losses. A student who can recite the reactivity series still loses marks describing a colour change loosely. Written practice marked against the published criteria is the only format that shifts this.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than conceptual difficulty, with command terms doing the decisive work. Describe, explain and compare each demand a different answer shape, and a well-prepared student can lose half a question by choosing wrongly. Data and graph questions are the fastest recovery.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis questions carry the marks and both are technique-led. The common failure is retelling a passage where the question asked how the writer achieves an effect. Six to eight marked pieces of writing move this grade more than any amount of reading.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Quotation accuracy and a sustained argument separate the top bands, and the unseen component punishes students who have only studied set texts. Timed essays marked against the criteria are the working format; discussion alone does not transfer to a paper under time pressure.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus material rather than definition recall. High-tariff evaluation questions ask for a judgement, and students who write everything they know land in the middle band. Diagram accuracy in economics is worth more marks than most students believe.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Named examples with figures attached in geography, source evaluation in history. Both subjects punish generic answers, so the efficient work is building a small bank of well-rehearsed case studies rather than covering more of the specification.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.levels: KHDA mandatory streams, Arab and non-Arab
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Tutoring must follow the Ministry-set content, since different or additional material needs prior Ministry permission.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-lakes.regionsTitle: The Lakes and the catchment around it
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-lakes.regionsIntro: Six clusters inside The Lakes and the communities beside them, described by where their teenagers actually go to school and what that does to a tutoring week.

regions.name: Deema
regions.note: Golf-club side of The Lakes. Children here are frequently on the earlier part of the Al Barsha bus loop, which is why Deema households are the ones most likely to manage a 16:15 lesson.

regions.name: Forat
regions.note: Mid-loop, close to the community centre. The practical consequence is a predictable arrival time, which makes a fixed weekly slot easier to hold here than in the clusters at the far end of a route.

regions.name: Ghadeer
regions.note: Lake frontage with a longer internal drive. Families who collect by car arrive earlier than bus families from the same street, so two neighbours can have quite different workable slots.

regions.name: Hattan
regions.note: Large villas, furthest internal stop on several routes, and the cluster where a Year 11 student most often walks in after 16:30. A 17:00 slot is the standard recommendation rather than a fallback.

regions.name: Maeen
regions.note: Close to the exit onto Sheikh Zayed Road. Sibling pairs at two different schools commonly arrive forty minutes apart here, which forces staggered sessions rather than a shared evening.

regions.name: Zulal
regions.note: Quietest cluster, and the one where children most often go straight to an activity rather than home. Later slots dominate and a 18:00 lesson is normal rather than an exception.

regions.name: The Meadows and The Springs
regions.note: Share bus routes with The Lakes. The Meadows has Emirates International School Meadows inside it, so Meadows teenagers are more often on MYP 4 and 5 than on IGCSE.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Greens
regions.note: Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Regent International School sit here on the British route, giving these households the shortest commute in Emirates Living and the earliest realistic lesson times.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Where most Lakes IGCSE students actually study. This is also where most in-home tutors are based, which is why a visit to an Emirates Living address is quoted at the upper end of the published range.

schoolClusters.city: Schools The Lakes feeds for Years 10 and 11
schoolClusters.note: The British-curriculum schools Lakes teenagers most commonly attend for IGCSE, all outside Emirates Living and all regulated by KHDA. Each sets its own prep expectations and co-curricular calendar, which matters more to a tutoring timetable than the distance does.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: The schools reachable without crossing Sheikh Zayed Road. Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Regent International School run the British route; Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills run IB programmes, so a family choosing at 14 is choosing between IGCSE papers and criterion-marked MYP.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Khail Road and Jumeirah Village belt
schoolClusters.note: A secondary catchment for Lakes households, and the one with the longest return journey at the end of the school day. Students bussed from here are usually the last home in a two-child household, which is what forces the stagger.

modes.title: One protected evening a week
modes.description: A single hour on the evening that has no fixture, no rehearsal and the lightest prep load, set after the bus with a buffer. Protecting one evening properly beats booking three and losing two, and in a Year 11 week it is usually all that genuinely exists. Written work is set and marked between sessions.

modes.description: Most Dubai private schools now run Monday to Friday with a shortened Friday, which puts a secondary student home by early afternoon with energy left. That is where a timed paper belongs: ninety minutes under conditions, marked immediately, with the gaps it exposes worked on during the weekday hour.

sections.heading: Why a proximity search fails subject by subject
paragraphs: The radius around The Lakes contains a certain number of tutors, and what they teach is fixed by who they are. Your child needs a specific board, a specific syllabus code and a specific tier - Cambridge 0580 Extended, Pearson 4CH1, Cambridge 0654 Double Award - and the overlap between 'available within fifteen minutes of Ghadeer' and 'has taught that exact specification recently' is frequently empty. The search returns results anyway, because a search always does.

This matters more in IGCSE than people assume, because the tiers carry hard ceilings. Cambridge Core papers are graded C to G and Extended A* to E; Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5 while Higher runs 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. A tutor who teaches the wrong tier is not merely less effective, they are preparing material that cannot be examined. That is the clearest argument against hiring by distance, and it costs a term to discover.

The second failure is subject count. A Year 11 student is sitting eight to ten subjects and, realistically, needs help in two. Those two are rarely both covered by one local tutor, so a proximity search either produces two separate in-home arrangements, two sets of travel premiums and two diaries to coordinate, or one tutor stretched across both subjects who ends up supervising homework. Neither is what the parent set out to buy.

Set against that, what a video arrangement changes is only the delivery, and it changes it in the direction of supply. The tutor is chosen because they teach 0580 Extended, and the lesson starts when the student sits down rather than when a car finds a parking space. For a Lakes household, where the school is already twenty-five minutes away, the proximity of the tutor was never the thing keeping the arrangement together. The slot was.

sections.heading: Which schools The Lakes feeds, and what each offers to 18
paragraphs: A Lakes family's realistic school list is a ring around Emirates Living rather than anything inside it, and the route a child takes to 18 is decided by which school in that ring they attend. Some run the British curriculum straight through to A Level. Some run the IB continuum. A few offer both at sixth form, which is the most useful arrangement for a family that has not decided. The table sets out the local picture with the regulator named, because the regulator is who publishes the inspection report.

Reading an inspection report before reading a tutor profile is worth the half hour. Dubai private schools are inspected by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The report says what a school is strong and weak at by phase and subject, which is a better guide to where tutoring will be needed than any general reputation. We do not reproduce ratings here; read them on the regulator's own site, where they are published and current.

A scale note worth having. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. That mix explains the tutoring market a Lakes family is shopping in: British-curriculum demand dominates, which is why IGCSE tutors are easier to find than MYP ones and why the IB specialists concentrate at the top of the price range.

One more fact that affects planning rather than price. Dubai added seven new private schools for 2026-27 - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. And KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for 2026-27, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Supply is widening and the fixed cost is flat.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Almost nobody asks, and the answer is both simple and free. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The eligible categories are deliberately broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. That breadth is the reason the low end of the Dubai rate market exists at all - a university student on a free permit can legitimately charge AED 45 an hour, and some do. It also means there is no honest reason for a tutor to be without one.

Two cautions. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified and ignored. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry.

IB Gram is not a Dubai training institute, occupies no UAE office, and holds no permit, registration, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. The regulators are named on this page to explain what each one does. Any provider implying endorsement by one of them should be asked to produce the permit or centre number, and the phrase to be most careful of in this market is a claim of regulator approval attached to tutors.

sections.heading: Who regulates the school your child attends
paragraphs: A Dubai parent rarely needs the whole map, until the family moves emirate or a relative asks. Private schools in the UAE are overseen by five bodies and only one of them is KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

The powers are not identical, and the differences matter if you move. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. In Dubai, KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, publishes inspection reports and, in May 2026, confirmed the fee position for the following academic year.

There is also a federal baseline worth knowing. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single rule is why a British-curriculum school in Al Barsha teaches Arabic alongside IGCSE, and why an IB school in The Meadows does the same. It is not a school policy; it is the federal floor every emirate regulator builds on.

One Abu Dhabi rule is worth carrying even from Dubai, because Lakes families do relocate within the UAE. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct to similar effect. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording. The practical instruction holds in any emirate: do not go looking for your child's own class teacher privately.

sections.heading: The after-school week at a British-curriculum school
paragraphs: Parents choosing a tutoring slot usually subtract the journey from the final bell and stop there. The schools Lakes teenagers attend subtract rather more. A Year 10 or Year 11 student typically carries an hour or more of prep most nights, set by subject teachers who are not coordinating with each other. Co-curricular commitments are expected to be honoured rather than optional, and in many schools a fixture, a rehearsal or a squad session owns one evening outright.

Work it through for a Hattan household. The bus arrives at 16:35. Prep is ninety minutes on a normal Tuesday. Squad training runs Monday and Wednesday. There is a Friday fixture in season. Dinner is at seven. What remains is Thursday, and possibly Tuesday if prep is light, which is two evenings - not five. A provider proposing three sessions a week into that week is proposing something the household will cancel, and cancellations are how arrangements die.

The right response is to pick the single best evening and defend it absolutely, then put anything longer at the weekend or on Friday afternoon. Most Dubai private schools now run Monday to Friday with a shortened Friday, so a secondary student is often home by about 12:15 to 13:15 with the afternoon intact. That is the slot for a timed paper, and it is the most under-used teaching time in the city. Check your own school's calendar, because a small number kept a Sunday-to-Thursday week.

Two household rules follow. First, the lesson should not sit immediately after prep on the same subject, because the student has nothing left for it; alternate the subjects across the evening instead. Second, where two children share one evening, use the natural arrival gap between their schools as the stagger rather than stacking them back to back in the same room. Headsets solve the audio problem; nothing solves a child listening to their sibling's lesson.
bullets: Count prep and fixtures before counting free evenings; two is the usual answer
Pick one weekday evening, protect it, and put long sessions on Friday or the weekend
Avoid scheduling a lesson directly after prep in the same subject

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches these subjects regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for, and essentially no competing tutoring page in this market mentions them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 the equivalent point for schools whose year begins in April. For a Lakes family this is timetable reality rather than an optional extra.

The organisational rules are specific and they explain things parents find confusing. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Two further details matter to anyone arranging support. Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. And teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic are required by KHDA to hold appropriate approval from the regulator to teach those subjects - a concrete credential point a parent can ask about.

The constraint on tutoring is real and worth stating. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited. So support in these subjects means working with the school's own set material rather than importing a syllabus from elsewhere, and a provider offering an alternative curriculum for Arabic or Islamic Education is describing something that is not permitted. Ask what material will be used before the first lesson.
bullets: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum
Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs; combined classes are prohibited

sections.heading: Year 9 options and the grades that gate sixth form
paragraphs: The options evening in Year 9 is the cheapest high-value hour in this whole sequence, and it is usually spent on the wrong question. Parents ask which subjects the child enjoys. The decisive questions are narrower: how many subjects, triple science or combined, which tier each subject will be entered at, and whether the resulting grade set keeps the sixth-form routes open that the student might want at 16.

Triple science against combined is the one that recurs. Three separate sciences - Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 - produce three grades and the strongest position for Higher Level or A Level sciences. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 produces a double award across all three. Combined or double award is a perfectly sound route for a student not heading into science at 16, and a liability for one who is, so the choice should follow the intended destination rather than the current comfort level.

Tier is the other gate and it is less visible. Cambridge Core papers cap at grade C and Extended run to A*; Pearson Foundation caps at grade 5 against Higher's 9. A sixth form asking for a grade 6 in mathematics cannot be satisfied from a Foundation entry at all, however well the student performs. Because tier decisions effectively lock at the board's final entry deadline - which sits months before the examination - the conversation has to happen in Year 10, not in the spring of Year 11.

There is a documentation layer too, which almost nobody raises at an options evening. The reported Ministry of Education requirement for the British track is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. A student dropping to a very small subject load, or counting Arabic among their five, can meet a school's requirements and still have a documentation problem later. Verify the current rule at the source.
bullets: Decide triple or combined science from the intended route at 16, not from comfort

sections.heading: Arriving mid-stream: transferring into IGCSE from another system
paragraphs: Lakes households move, and a student arriving into Year 10 or Year 11 from another curriculum meets a specific set of gaps rather than a general difficulty. From an Indian curriculum the usual gaps are extended written answers against command terms and the practical-skills written components, because the content coverage is often ahead rather than behind. From an American system the gap is typically depth in a smaller number of subjects and the unfamiliarity of a terminal examination.

From the IB Middle Years Programme the gap is assessment style rather than content. An MYP student is used to criterion marking out of 8 against published descriptors and to coursework-style tasks; IGCSE asks for timed answers to a mark scheme with command terms carrying strict meanings. That transition is six to eight weeks of marked written practice, and it is almost entirely technique. It is also the transition most likely to be mistaken for a content problem and tutored expensively in the wrong direction.

The practical sequence for a transferring student is the same in each case. Get the syllabus codes and tiers from the new school in writing. Find out which papers have already been sat if the student arrives mid-series, because that constrains the options. Ask the examinations officer whether the entry deadline for the next series has passed. Then diagnose with one marked piece of written work before buying any hours, because the gap is rarely where the previous school's reports suggest.

On timing, the entry deadline is the hard constraint and it is easy to miss when arriving. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE series shows the shape of it in published dates: the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry that fixed the subject list for those papers had closed in the preceding summer. Cambridge's June and November series, the two a UAE candidate can enter, work on the same lag, with June entries closing in the spring on a date printed on the centre's statement of entry. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so plan against the live document rather than a restated date. A family arriving in January should ask about entries in their first week, not their first term.

sections.heading: Getting started from The Lakes, and what we will not say
paragraphs: Four things make the first lesson useful: the school, the year, the syllabus codes with their tiers, and the one evening in the week that is genuinely free. We come back with a tutor who teaches that code at that tier and who can teach in that window, plus a proposed focus for the first three lessons and a rate. The trial lesson is free, covers one subject, and takes no card details collected to book it.

The limit worth hearing in advance is availability for narrow combinations. Mainstream IGCSE subjects match within a few days. A specific code at a specific tier in a less common subject, or a request for one tutor across two boards, can take longer, and the tutor may be based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We say which, and from where, before anything is agreed - something no competitor page researched in this market does at all.

What we will not say is as load-bearing as what we will. No grade promise and no improvement figure, because neither can be evidenced. No statistic about past students without the number, the date and the method behind it. No claim of approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because IB Gram holds none. No UAE office, because there isn't one. And no tutor described as an examiner unless their current status can be shown.

Nor do we supply board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson; we reference them, cite the official URL and link out. A provider sending you a pack of mark schemes is distributing someone else's copyright, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure for the student. Official past material is available through your school's examinations officer and from the boards' own sites.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in The Lakes, or does the lesson happen online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The practical argument in an IGCSE context is supply rather than price: your child needs a specific board, syllabus code and tier, and the overlap between tutors who live near Ghadeer and tutors who teach that exact specification is often empty. Dubai's in-home market is real and published at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 online for equivalent credentials.

faqs.question: Which schools do Lakes children attend for Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: Almost all of them outside Emirates Living. The common IGCSE destinations are in Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and Al Sufouh - including Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha, Safa Community School, GEMS Wellington International School and Dubai College - with Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Regent International School in The Greens closer to home. Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills run IB programmes instead. All are regulated by KHDA, and named here as local context rather than as partners.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is legally allowed to teach my child in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask for the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, there is no good reason for a working tutor not to have one. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a KHDA permit as well as a MoHRE one?
faqs.answer: Not as an individual. The MoHRE private tuition work permit covers an individual providing private lessons. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a different instrument, issued to a training institute with premises and staff in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. The two are frequently confused in marketing copy. IB Gram is not a Dubai training institute, occupies no UAE office and holds no permit from KHDA, so it claims none. If a provider implies regulator endorsement, ask for the permit or centre number.

faqs.question: Who inspects my child's school, and what does an inspection report actually tell me?
faqs.answer: In Dubai it is KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes inspection reports on its own site. The reports are more useful than a school's reputation because they break performance down by phase and by subject, which tells you where tutoring is likely to be needed rather than whether the school is generally good. Read them at the source. No inspection rating is reproduced on this page, because ratings should be read where they are published and kept current.

faqs.question: Can a university student legally charge for tutoring my child in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they hold the permit. MoHRE's eligible categories for the private tuition work permit explicitly include university students, alongside registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals and school students aged 15 to 18. The permit is free and valid for two years. This is why the bottom of the Dubai rate market exists: platform rates from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour are genuinely available and genuinely lawful. Whether a university student is the right teacher for a tiered IGCSE paper is a separate question from whether they may be paid.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable for my child's own class teacher to tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Treat it as something to avoid. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct to similar effect. Verify the current ADEK wording against its own policy document before relying on it. Even in Dubai the arrangement creates an obvious conflict around marking and predicted grades, so the practical answer in any emirate is to find a teacher from outside the school.

faqs.question: At Year 9 options, should my child take triple science or combined science?
faqs.answer: Decide from the intended route at 16 rather than from current comfort. Three separate sciences - Cambridge 0610, 0620, 0625 or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 - produce three grades and the strongest position for A Level or Higher Level sciences. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award across all three and is a sound choice for a student not heading into science, and a liability for one who is. It is also a different specification rather than a reduced one, so it must be tutored from its own material.

faqs.question: How much prep does a Year 10 student get, and where does a tutor fit around it?
faqs.answer: Commonly an hour or more on a normal night, set by subject teachers who are not coordinating with each other, which is why the load is uneven rather than predictable. The working rule is not to schedule a lesson immediately after prep in the same subject, because the student has nothing left for it - alternate subjects across the evening instead. Add fixtures and rehearsals and most Year 10 and Year 11 weeks leave two genuinely free evenings. Pick the better one and protect it rather than booking three and cancelling two.

faqs.question: Two clubs a week and a Friday fixture. Which evening is actually left?
faqs.answer: Usually one, sometimes two. Work it through: the bus into Hattan arrives around 16:35, prep runs ninety minutes on a typical night, squad training owns two evenings, the fixture owns a third in season, and dinner is at seven. What survives is often a single weekday evening, with Friday afternoon available because most Dubai private schools now run a shortened Friday that puts a secondary student home by early afternoon. That Friday slot is the best place in the week for a ninety-minute timed paper with a fresh student.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education continue through Years 10 and 11 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. They are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, alongside social and moral studies, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. This follows a federal rule: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. They also sit outside the five-subject count the Ministry uses for British-track equivalency, which is a separate and important point.

faqs.question: Does a non-Arab student study Arabic in the same class as an Arab student?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE grades gate entry to A Level or the IB Diploma afterwards?
faqs.answer: Sixth forms set their own conditions, and the gate is usually a specific grade in the subject plus mathematics and English. The hidden constraint is tier: a Cambridge Core entry caps at grade C and a Pearson Foundation entry at grade 5, so a condition asking for a 6 or a B cannot be met from those tiers however well the student performs. Higher Level Diploma sciences normally assume Extended or Higher tier grades. Because tier locks at the board's final entry deadline months before the papers, this is a Year 10 conversation.

faqs.question: We are transferring from an Indian curriculum school into Year 10. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Usually not content. Students arriving from an Indian curriculum are often ahead on coverage and behind on two specific things: extended written answers shaped to command terms, and the written assessment of practical skills. Both are technique and both respond to six to eight weeks of marked written practice. The first practical steps are administrative: get the syllabus codes and tiers from the new school in writing, ask whether the entry deadline for the next series has passed, and diagnose from one marked piece of work before buying hours.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for the subject and tier we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is not the norm in this market - no competitor page researched discloses a coverage limit at all. For mainstream IGCSE subjects a match usually takes a few days. For a narrow combination, a less common subject, or a request for one tutor across two boards, it can take longer, and the proposed tutor may be based outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We state the expected wait and the tutor's location before anything is agreed, so the decision is yours rather than a surprise later.

intro.heading: Sorting tutors by distance sorts them by the wrong thing
paragraphs: A proximity search is a sensible instinct applied to the wrong market. If you were looking for a dentist or a car service, distance would be a decent first filter, because the quality range inside a five-kilometre radius is narrow and the thing you are buying happens in one visit. IGCSE tutoring is the opposite: the quality range is enormous, the thing you are buying happens over thirty weeks, and the single variable that predicts the outcome is whether the tutor knows the specific paper your child will sit. Distance predicts none of that.

It is worth being precise about what the radius around The Meadows actually contains. Emirates Living is residential and gated, with no tuition centres inside it. The first ring out, The Springs, The Lakes, The Views and The Greens, is also residential, so what you find there is individual tutors advertising locally, mostly teaching whatever is asked for. The commercial supply, the centres and the agency offices, sits in Al Barsha, Tecom and Barsha Heights, which is a fifteen-to-thirty-minute drive that becomes considerably longer between four and seven in the evening.

So the honest version of the question is not whether there is an IGCSE tutor near The Meadows. There are many. The question is whether any of them has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended Chemistry, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher, to a Year 11 cohort recently enough to know where this year's candidates lose marks. That is a much smaller group, it is not distributed geographically, and a search sorted by distance will not surface it. This page exists to give you a way of finding out, in a trial lesson, which group a tutor belongs to.

IB Gram's own position is simple and worth stating before the argument rather than after it. We do not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home visiting is a service our India operation runs, and pretending otherwise on a page that ranks for a proximity search would be dishonest. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around your child's actual school week. Dropping the drive radius is not a compromise we are apologising for; it is the mechanism that makes a syllabus-matched tutor possible for a family in Meadows 8.

What follows is written to be used rather than admired: a ring-by-ring map of the local supply, six questions with notes on what a good answer sounds like, a comparison of one-to-one against small-group and centre formats with the published rates attached, the scheduling reality of a Dubai school week including Ramadan and mock season, the regulator map for whichever emirate your child's school sits in, and a way of judging progress from outside the room. None of it requires you to take our word for anything.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: Which route your child is on changes what tutoring is for. Around Emirates Living four routes are in play, and the handover points between them are where families most often discover a gap that has been widening quietly for a year.

programmes.name: Year 9 and the options decision
programmes.description: The year the IGCSE subject list is chosen, usually in the spring term, and the year nobody books a tutor. Subject choice at this point quietly sets up the A Level and university options available four years later: dropping a separate science, or taking Co-ordinated Sciences instead of three sciences, closes doors that are difficult to reopen. The assessment is internal, so there is no external signal to prompt a parent into action.
programmes.countryNote: Schools serving The Meadows run options evenings in Year 9, and the conversation is almost always framed around what a child enjoys. Worth adding to it: which subjects the intended A Level route requires, and whether the Cambridge or Pearson entry the school plans is tiered. A single diagnostic hour in Year 9 maths is a better purchase than ten hours in Year 11.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Eight to ten separately entered subjects, assessed mainly by terminal written papers, with Cambridge tiering many subjects into Core and Extended and Pearson tiering maths into Foundation and Higher. Year 10 teaches most of the content; Year 11 teaches technique and sits the papers. The two years need different tutoring, and treating them the same is the most common planning error families make.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's UK-curriculum sector carried 37 per cent of private-school enrolment in 2024-25, which makes IGCSE the dominant Year 11 qualification in the schools that buses from Emirates Living serve. It also means the local tutor supply advertises IGCSE heavily, and that the words on a profile tell you very little about whether the tutor has seen the current papers.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The usual post-16 continuation in British-curriculum schools here, with three or four subjects and either linear or modular assessment depending on board and subject. The step up in Maths, Physics and Chemistry is in the amount of unprompted reasoning expected: IGCSE questions scaffold, A Level questions do not. For Ministry equivalency on the British track, one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade sit alongside the IGCSE requirement.
programmes.countryNote: Because the sixth form is usually on the same campus, families around Emirates Living treat the transition as administrative. The tutoring enquiries that arrive each November from Year 12 students who held a grade 7 at IGCSE suggest it is not. The fix is a short diagnostic block in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, which almost nobody buys.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years and Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative route running in parallel in the same neighbourhood: criterion-referenced assessment through MYP, then six Diploma subjects with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight throughout, so support is about deadline management and feedback on the student's own drafts rather than past-paper volume. The IB accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills run the IB continuum, so two children in the same Meadows villa can be on completely different assessment systems. Families who buy one tutoring arrangement for both usually end up with a compromise that fits neither, because MYP criteria and IGCSE mark schemes reward different behaviour.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: Subjects are listed with what a parent can verify about each one, because a tutor's claim to cover a subject is only checkable if you know what the assessment contains. Match on code and tier, then test the claim in the trial lesson.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 · 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers and no coursework, which makes progress unusually easy to measure: a timed paper marked against the published scheme gives you a number every fortnight. Ask a prospective tutor whether they mark to the scheme or to impression. The answer predicts whether you will ever see evidence of progress.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654 · 4SD0)
subjects.description: Two grades from one block covering biology, chemistry and physics. The thing to check is which of the three disciplines the tutor actually trained in, because a single tutor covering all three is the standard arrangement and the weakest one. Physics content inside a co-ordinated course is where the grade usually drains away.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 · 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: The most content-heavy science and the one most often revised by rereading. Ask how the tutor will handle extended-response questions, which are marked on linked reasoning. If the plan is flashcards and recall, the ceiling is a grade 6 regardless of how many hours are bought.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 · 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic pathways carry the grade. A useful test question for a tutor: how would you teach a student who can define an exothermic reaction but cannot predict one? A specialist answers with a sequence of question types; a generalist answers with encouragement.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 · 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Cambridge candidates sit three papers including a practical or alternative-to-practical component; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Ask which of those two situations your child is in. A tutor who does not know is not reading the entry, and the two require different preparation entirely.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 · 0990 · 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading response, directed writing and composition. Progress here is slower to see than in maths and easier to fake, so ask for marked work with the band descriptors attached rather than a comment. A student can improve their writing and lose marks for continuing to answer the wrong question.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475 · 0992 · 4ET1)
subjects.description: Set texts, extract analysis and essay structure, with some schools offering coursework instead of a paper. Check which route the school has chosen, because a coursework entry changes the work from exam technique to drafting and feedback, with a strict boundary on whose words appear on the page.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417 · 0983)
subjects.description: A theory paper plus practical document, data and presentation tasks assessed under controlled conditions. It is widely assumed to be an easy grade and widely under-taught, particularly the spreadsheet modelling and database tasks, where precision in formulae and in file naming carries marks on its own.

subjects.name: Geography (0460 · 4GE1)
subjects.description: Skills paper, physical and human topics, and case-study recall. The skills paper is the most tutorable component in the subject and the one most students lose marks on, because map, graph and cross-section work is a technique rather than knowledge and is rarely drilled in class.

subjects.name: History (0470 · 4HI1)
subjects.description: Source evaluation and structured argument on named depth studies. Marks go to provenance-aware source use and to a line of argument, not to quantity of detail. Ask a tutor which depth studies your child's school teaches; the answer is on the scheme of work and a specialist will want it before the first session.

subjects.name: French (0520 · 4FR1)
subjects.description: Listening, reading, writing and speaking, with the speaking component assessed by the school. The predictable weak point is the writing task's register and tense control. Short, frequent sessions work far better here than long ones, which is a scheduling question as much as a teaching one.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language (0544)
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students in Dubai alongside the school's mandatory Arabic provision. Support has to work inside the school's own material: KHDA rules prohibit using different or additional content for the mandatory UAE subjects without prior Ministry permission, so a parallel course is not an option.

sections.heading: What a proximity search returns from a Meadows address, ring by ring
paragraphs: Searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in The Meadows produces a list ordered by distance, and the useful thing to know is what each distance band actually contains. Inside Emirates Living there is no commercial tuition provision at all: it is a gated villa community, so the supply is individuals who live here and advertise within it. That supply is real and some of it is good, but it is selected by residence rather than by subject, and the pool of adults in a two-kilometre radius who have recently taught a tiered IGCSE science to an exam cohort is small.

The first ring out changes very little. The Springs, The Lakes, The Views and The Greens have the same residential profile, so a search radius extended by a kilometre returns more of the same category rather than a different one. The commercial supply, the centres and the agency offices, begins in Al Barsha and Barsha Heights at eight to twelve kilometres, and that is where distance stops being a number and becomes an evening: the same trip that takes eighteen minutes at eleven in the morning takes forty-five at half past four, each way, four days a week.

sections.heading: Six questions that separate a specialist from a confident generalist
paragraphs: Use these in the trial lesson, on any tutor including ours, and judge the specificity of the answer rather than its warmth. First: which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for, and what does that change about how you would teach them? A specialist asks for the statement of entry before answering. Second: how many papers will my child sit in this subject, and what is each one worth? If the answer is vague, the tutor has not read the assessment structure of the subject they are proposing to teach.

Third: where do candidates lose marks on that specific paper? A real answer is granular and unflattering, about unwritten method, unit conversion, unlinked reasoning or missing judgement in evaluation questions. Fourth: how will you mark my child's timed work, against the published mark scheme or by impression? Only one of those produces a number you can track. Fifth: what will you not do with coursework? A tutor who cannot describe a boundary on assessed work is a risk to your child's qualification, not just to your budget.

Sixth, and most revealing: what would make you tell me this is not working? Good tutors have an answer, usually involving a named gap that has not moved in four weeks, or attendance, or a mismatch of level. A tutor who cannot imagine the arrangement failing has not thought about it, and you will be the one who eventually has to raise it, three months and nine thousand dirhams later. None of these six questions requires you to understand the subject. They only require you to notice whether the answers are about the assessment or about atmosphere.

sections.heading: Year 10 and Year 11 are not the same problem
paragraphs: Most tutoring in this neighbourhood is bought in the January of Year 11, and most of it is bought to do the job that Year 10 tutoring does cheaply. The two years ask for different work. In Year 10 the content is still being taught, so an hour a week spent consolidating what the class covered last week keeps the pace of the syllabus and leaves marked evidence behind for the tier decision. In Year 11 the content is mostly delivered and the work is technique: timed papers, mark schemes, command terms, and the discipline of writing down method.

The consequences of mixing them up are predictable. A Year 11 student in February given content teaching will cover topics competently and still lose the same marks, because the loss is procedural rather than conceptual. A Year 10 student given past-paper drilling will sit papers on content they have not been taught, score badly and conclude they are bad at the subject. Both arrangements run for weeks before anybody notices, because both look like tutoring and both produce a session note every week.

The table below sets out what the work is at each stage, how many hours it usually takes, and what the specific risk is at that point. It is deliberately conservative on hours. The honest pattern across these subjects is that early light-touch support beats late intensive support at roughly a third of the total cost, and the reason almost nobody takes that deal is that in Year 10 nothing has visibly gone wrong yet.

sections.heading: One-to-one, small group or centre: what each format buys per dirham
paragraphs: The comparison most families make is per hour, and the number that matters is per hour of attention. A ninety-minute one-to-one session is ninety minutes of attention. A ninety-minute group class of six is, arithmetically, fifteen minutes each, and the pace is set by the median student in the room rather than by your child's gap list. That is not an argument against group teaching, which works well for shared content delivery and is considerably cheaper. It is an argument for knowing which of the two things you are buying.

The published Dubai rates make the trade visible. Tuition-centre group classes are advertised at roughly AED 60 to 150 per student per hour. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject tutor is published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget online tutoring starts lower, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 500, on Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 band of AED 180 to 350 plus independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, with BartyED published at AED 650 at the premium end.

Each figure above belongs to the provider named beside it and was read from that provider's own published material in October 2026. None is an IB Gram price; we publish a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a rate card, because the subject, the session length and the number of weeks change the answer. Use the table as a calibration tool: if a quote from a tutor near The Meadows sits well outside these bands in either direction, that is worth a question, and the answer will usually be about travel, group size or examiner experience.

sections.heading: How a weekly session survives contact with a Dubai school week
paragraphs: Tutoring arrangements in Emirates Living usually fail on logistics rather than on teaching. The school day ends between 2:45pm and 3:20pm depending on the campus, the bus loop through nine Meadows sub-communities adds twenty to fifty minutes, and a Year 11 student who walks in at 4:20pm needs to eat before anything useful happens. A 4:30pm slot booked in September is being quietly cancelled by October. A 6pm slot survives the year. Getting this right at the outset matters more than any other scheduling decision.

Then there is the rest of the calendar. Mock seasons in November and February consume two weeks each, during which a tutoring hour spent on new content is wasted and an hour spent on paper technique is not. Half terms, the long winter break and the spring holiday interrupt continuity, and families here travel during all three. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the useful working window moves: an evening session after iftar is more productive than an exhausted one at 5pm, and planning for that in advance is better than discovering it in week two.

The practical answer is to design the year rather than the week. Fix the slot around your sub-community's actual arrival time, not the school's finish time. Agree in advance that mock weeks switch to technique and that exam weeks pause rather than cancel. Plan the Ramadan timing before Ramadan. Set the stop date for pre-series intensive work so the final week belongs to the student alone. None of this is complicated, and all of it is the difference between an arrangement that reaches April and one that quietly stops in November.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what the inspection band tells you
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map, and most tutoring sites in this market name none of them.

Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates curriculum and fee approval sits with the regulator rather than only inspection. In Dubai, KHDA publishes inspection outcomes on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and it confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

What the inspection band is good for is narrower than parents assume. It is a whole-school judgement across many measures, and it tells you very little about the specific thing that matters to a tutoring decision, which is how a particular department teaches a particular syllabus to a particular cohort. A school rated Outstanding can have a weak year in one subject; a Good school can have an exceptional maths department. Read the published report for the subject-level commentary rather than the headline band, and treat the band as context rather than a verdict. Ratings should only ever be taken from the regulator's own site.

sections.heading: Judging progress from outside the room, in four weeks
paragraphs: The hardest part of buying tutoring is that the parent is not in the room, and the two signals most readily available, your child's mood and the tutor's enthusiasm, are both unreliable. A student can enjoy sessions with a tutor who is teaching the wrong thing, and dislike sessions with one who is finally addressing the actual gap. Neither feeling predicts a grade. What does predict it is a short list of artefacts you should expect to see, and the absence of any of them is the signal to act.

Four things. A written gap list after the diagnostic work, by topic and command term. A mark out of a known total on timed work, repeated at intervals, against the published mark scheme rather than impression. A short note after each session saying what was covered and what to practise. And a monthly comparison between the error log and the original gap list. With those four you can see movement in four weeks. Without them you are relying on a term's end and a school report, which arrive too late to change anything.

The rule that follows is uncomfortable but worth stating. If a named gap has not moved in four weeks, change the method or change the tutor. Families routinely wait a full term because the tutor is pleasant, the child is compliant and nobody wants a difficult conversation in a community where everybody shares a school bus route. That delay is the single most expensive thing in private tutoring, and the fix is to agree at the start what evidence would trigger a change. Ask for it in writing before the first invoice.
