sections.heading: Changing board or school part-way through IGCSE
paragraphs: Dubai is a mobile market and mid-course moves are common, either between schools in the emirate or into the UAE from another system. Where the move crosses boards, between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, the content usually transfers and the assessment does not. A student who has prepared for a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper arrives in a Pearson cohort where practical skills are assessed inside the written papers; the physics is the same, the rehearsal is wasted, and nobody flags it because the subject name on the timetable has not changed.

Where the move crosses systems the gaps are structural. A student arriving from a CBSE background usually has stronger procedural maths and less experience of extended written reasoning in science. A student arriving from an American curriculum often has broader coverage and less depth in the specific topics an IGCSE paper examines. In both cases the right first purchase is a subject-by-subject comparison of what has and has not been covered, produced in writing, before any weekly arrangement is agreed.

Timing is the part families underestimate. A move in Year 10 is manageable with a short transition block per subject. A move in the autumn of Year 11 collides with entry deadlines, tier decisions and forecast grades, and the administrative work, confirming which codes and tiers the new school has entered, matters as much as the teaching. Get the statement of entry from the new school early, compare it against the old one, and prioritise subjects by the size of the assessment difference rather than by the size of the content gap.

sections.heading: Starting from The Meadows, and the three limits we state first
paragraphs: Getting started takes two messages and a trial. You send the subject, the syllabus code and tier from the statement of entry, the year group, and the earliest time a session can realistically start given which part of The Meadows you are in. We propose a tutor who has taught that code, and you take a free 45-minute trial with that same tutor, not a consultant. No card details are required. If the fit is wrong, you say so and we propose someone else; there is no notice period and no tie-in.

Three limits, stated before you book rather than after. First, availability: common subjects at common times fill within days, but a narrow combination of board, tier, niche subject and late evening slot can take longer, and in the weeks before a series everything takes longer because demand across Dubai peaks simultaneously. Where no UAE-based tutor covers a niche subject, the match may be an experienced IGCSE specialist teaching from outside the UAE on the same live video format and the same Gulf Standard Time slot, and we tell you that in advance.

Second, delivery: lessons are one-to-one over live video. No tutor will arrive at an address in Emirates Living, because in-home visiting is not a service we sell in the UAE. Third, outcomes and claims: no tutor will promise a grade, no tutor will produce assessed work that must be your child's own, and nothing on this page claims approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. IB Gram holds none of those, operates no UAE office, and holds no KHDA training-institute permit.

process.title: Send the entry details, not just the subject
process.description: Subject, board, four-character syllabus code, tier if the subject is tiered, year group and school. The statement of entry from your school's exams officer carries all of it. This is the field that makes the difference between a tutor who matches the paper and a tutor who matches the subject name, and it takes one email to obtain.

process.title: Name the earliest realistic start time
process.description: Tell us which part of The Meadows you are in and what time your child actually walks through the door. The nine sub-communities sit at different points on the bus loop, and a slot set against the school bell rather than the arrival time is the most common reason a weekly arrangement quietly stops by half term.

process.title: Use the trial as an interview
process.description: Forty-five minutes, one-to-one over live video, with the tutor who would teach the term. Put the six vetting questions from this page to them and listen for specificity. No card details are needed to book it, and a tutor who answers in terms of the assessment rather than attitude is the one worth keeping.

process.title: Insist on the written gap list
process.description: Before any package is agreed, you should hold a written list of what is wrong, by topic and command term, derived from timed work marked against the published scheme. That document is what the plan is built on and what progress is later measured against. A refusal to produce one is itself a complete answer.

process.title: Agree the review trigger up front
process.description: Decide at the start what evidence would mean the arrangement is not working, usually a named gap that has not moved in four weeks. Agreeing it before the first invoice turns a difficult conversation into an administrative one, and removes the term-long drift that costs families more than any hourly rate does.

process.title: Map the series onto a calendar
process.description: Mark the entry deadline, the mock windows, the exam window and the results date from the dates your school's exams officer holds, read against the board's live timetable PDF. Work scheduled against that calendar is different work in October and in February, which is the point of planning rather than simply booking.

faqs.question: Is searching for an IGCSE tutor near me in The Meadows the wrong approach?
faqs.answer: It is a reasonable instinct applied to a market where distance does not predict quality. Emirates Living has no tuition centres inside it, so a proximity search returns individual tutors selected by where they live rather than by which syllabus they have taught. The commercial supply starts in Al Barsha, eight to twelve kilometres away, which at the school-run peak is a sixty-to-ninety-minute round trip. A better first filter is the syllabus code on your child's statement of entry, because that determines the board, the papers, the tier and the mark scheme a tutor needs to know.

faqs.question: How many tuition centres are inside Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: None. The Meadows, The Springs, The Lakes, The Views and The Greens are residential communities without commercial tuition provision, which is why local supply consists of individuals who live there and advertise within the community. The nearest cluster of centres and agency offices sits in Al Barsha and Barsha Heights. That geography is the practical reason in-home tutoring became the default here: it was easier for one tutor to drive than for several families to. It is also why removing the drive, rather than shortening it, is the change that widens the choice of tutor.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor in the first conversation?
faqs.answer: Six things, and judge the specificity rather than the warmth of each answer. Which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for, and what does that change? How many papers, and what is each worth? Where do candidates lose marks on that specific paper? Will timed work be marked against the published mark scheme or by impression? What will you not do with coursework? And what would make you tell me this is not working? A specialist answers all six in terms of the assessment. A generalist answers in terms of confidence and effort, which is pleasant and much easier to find.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a tuition centre good value compared with one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends what you are buying. Centre group classes in Dubai are advertised at roughly AED 60 to 150 per student per hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online one-to-one tutor, so the hourly saving is real. The attention is not comparable: a class of six divides an hour six ways and sets the pace by the median student. Group teaching works well for shared content delivery and structure. It works poorly for closing a specific diagnosed gap, which is what most families in Year 11 are actually trying to do when they start looking.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start in The Meadows on a school day?
faqs.answer: Later than most parents book. Campuses serving Emirates Living finish between roughly 2:45pm and 3:20pm, the bus loop through nine Meadows sub-communities adds twenty to fifty minutes, and a Year 11 student needs to eat before anything productive happens. Families in Meadows 1 to 3 can often make 4:15pm work. Meadows 6 to 9 usually cannot start before 5pm in term time, and 6pm is the slot that survives the whole year. Setting the time against actual arrival rather than the school bell prevents the slow cancellation drift that ends most arrangements by half term.

faqs.question: How soon should I expect to see evidence that tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Four weeks, if the right artefacts exist. You should hold a written gap list by topic and command term from the diagnostic work, marks out of a known total on timed papers marked against the published scheme, a short note after each session, and a monthly comparison of the error log against the original list. With those, movement is visible within a month. Without them you are waiting for a school report, which arrives too late to change anything. Agree at the start what evidence would mean the arrangement is not working, and the later conversation becomes administrative rather than awkward.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week in Year 10 better value than three hours in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is cheaper in total and more effective, and almost nobody does it. While content is still being taught, an hour a week consolidates it and leaves marked timed evidence behind in time to make the Core or Extended decision properly. By January of Year 11 the content gap is a year old, every family on the same bus route is looking at once, specialists are booked and rates sit at the top of their bands. The reason the better deal goes untaken is simply that in Year 10 nothing has visibly gone wrong yet, so the urgency is absent.

faqs.question: Does a KHDA inspection rating tell me whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: Hardly at all. KHDA publishes outcomes on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the judgement is whole-school across many measures. It does not tell you how one department teaches one syllabus to one cohort, which is the only thing relevant to a tutoring decision. An Outstanding school can have a weak year in a subject, and a Good school can have an exceptional maths department. Read the subject-level commentary in the published report rather than the headline band, and take any rating only from the regulator's own site.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school if we move out of Dubai?
faqs.answer: It changes by emirate. Dubai is KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and both of those approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Federally, private schools must provide Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies beyond their chosen curriculum. Verify current arrangements on u.ae or with the relevant authority before relying on them.

faqs.question: My child is moving from a Cambridge school to a Pearson school mid-course. What changes?
faqs.answer: The content mostly transfers; the assessment does not. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended and sets a separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences. Pearson tiers maths into Foundation and Higher, leaves most other subjects single-tier, and assesses practical skills inside the written papers. A student who has rehearsed for a Cambridge practical paper arrives in a cohort that will never sit one. Ask the new school's exams officer for the statement of entry immediately, compare codes against the old ones, and prioritise the subjects where the assessment difference is largest.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to post-iftar timing in Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning it in advance works better than adjusting in week two. The school day shortens during Ramadan and the useful working window shifts later, so an evening session after iftar is usually more productive than a tired one at 5pm. Agree the alternative slot before the month begins, keep the same tutor and the same subject order, and treat the shortened days as a reason to do technique and past-paper review rather than new content. The same logic applies to the long summer, when many families in Emirates Living are out of the country and time zones shift.

faqs.question: Do online lessons work for a student who says they learn better face to face?
faqs.answer: For one-to-one IGCSE work the match matters far more than the medium. A shared screen with a graphics tablet shows working line by line, past papers are annotated live, and the written note after each session lets a parent see what happened. What online genuinely removes is travel and the drive radius, which is how a family in Meadows 7 reaches a tutor who has taught their exact paper. Where face-to-face wins is with young children and students who need physical presence to stay on task. For a Year 10 or 11 student, the deciding factor is usually whether the room at home is quiet.

faqs.question: Is private tutoring in Dubai legal, and does the tutor need a licence?
faqs.answer: It is legal and it is permitted by licence rather than by default. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so quoted amounts should be treated as rumour. Asking a tutor whether they hold the permit is an ordinary question, not an accusation.

faqs.question: Can I hire my child's own subject teacher privately?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement families most often want and the one most likely to be prohibited. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document, but do not build a plan around it. A specialist who has taught the same syllabus elsewhere carries the same knowledge without the conflict.

faqs.question: What if the tutor we try turns out to be wrong for my child?
faqs.answer: You say so and a different tutor is proposed, with no notice period and no tie-in. The point of a free 45-minute trial with the actual tutor rather than a consultant is to make that decision before money changes hands, and the point of the six vetting questions is to give you something concrete to base it on. Mismatches are not rare and they are not usually about competence: a tutor who is excellent with a confident Extended candidate can be wrong for a student who has lost faith in the subject entirely.

faqs.question: Do you cover subjects beyond maths and the sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, including English Language and Literature, Geography, History, Economics, Business Studies, ICT, Computer Science, French and Arabic as a Second Language. Availability is deeper in the subjects with the largest Year 11 cohorts and thinner in the niche ones, and we say which situation applies before you book rather than after. For the mandatory UAE subjects, support has to work inside the school's own material, because KHDA rules prohibit different or additional content without prior Ministry permission.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects to students living in The Springs and the wider Emirates Living cluster. Each one works from the syllabus code your child's school entered them for, and every lesson is one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: The Springs timetable, not the map, is what makes a tutor usable
paragraphs: A search for an IGCSE tutor near me in The Springs is really a search for someone who can teach at 17:00 on a Tuesday. The community sits inside Emirates Living, bounded by Sheikh Zayed Road on one side and Al Khail Road on the other, and almost nobody who lives here attends a school inside the gates. Children leave by bus or by car to Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Jumeirah Park and Dubai Sports City, and they come back between 15:20 and 16:45 depending on which ring of schools they belong to. That return time, not a tutor's postcode, sets the whole week.

Once the bus has gone, the usable window is short. A Year 10 student has roughly ninety minutes before the evening collapses into homework, football, Arabic practice and a 21:00 bedtime that parents in exam years defend fiercely. A tutor who lives twelve minutes away in The Greens is no use if the drive out and back eats forty of those ninety minutes. A tutor who happens to be the right person for Cambridge Physics 0625 Extended is useful at 17:00 whether they are sitting in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or Mumbai, because the lesson arrives on a screen in the room your child is already in.

This is the part worth stating plainly before anything else. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recorded summary of what was covered. That is not a workaround for lacking local staff. It is the only model under which a Springs family can book a specialist in a narrow subject at the exact half-hour the family has free, rather than taking whoever is physically available in a twenty-minute radius.

The second thing worth saying is that the word IGCSE covers two different qualifications in this community. Cambridge International runs IGCSE with syllabus codes such as 0580 for Mathematics and 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson runs the International GCSE with codes such as 4MA1 and 4CH1. Schools around Emirates Living use both, sometimes in the same building for different subjects, and a tutor who has only ever taught one of them will teach the wrong paper structure with complete confidence. Finding out which code is on your child's entry is a five-minute email to the exams officer and it changes who you should be looking for.

The rest of this page is written from the school run outwards. It names the schools The Springs actually feeds, shows where an hour exists in a weekday by year group, explains what a KHDA inspection band does and does not tell you about subject teaching, sets out what the Dubai market charges in dirhams with the sources named, and ends with what the Ministry of Education will eventually count when your child applies to a UAE university. Nothing here is an estimate dressed as a fact; where a figure is not verifiable, it says so.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: A Springs household often has children in two different stages at once: a Year 9 choosing options, a Year 11 sitting the real thing, and sometimes a younger sibling still in a primary programme. These are the stages this page covers and what each one needs from a tutor.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and the options year
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE decide which subjects are even available. Algebraic fluency, scientific notation, graph interpretation and extended writing all get set here, and gaps left in Year 8 reappear in Year 10 disguised as a problem with the new syllabus. Tutoring at this stage is about building the habits a two-year course assumes, not about exam technique.
programmes.countryNote: Schools serving The Springs make option choices in the spring term of Year 9, usually with a parents' evening and a form due within a fortnight. Three of the decisions made that week determine whether a child can sit triple-award science, whether they can take a second language, and whether Additional Mathematics stays open at the end of Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Subjects carry four-digit codes and many are tiered Core or Extended, which caps the grade available. Papers are set per administrative zone, and Cambridge warns that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's responsibility.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres are allocated to one of six Cambridge administrative zones, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version of the timetable was used. For a Springs family this matters only in one practical way: the dates your child revises towards must come from the school's own copy of the zone timetable, not from a forum.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE sits in May/June and November each year. Many subjects are untiered, with Foundation and Higher only where the specification offers both, and the paper count differs from Cambridge in several subjects. Mathematics A is assessed by two papers; Mathematics B by one longer paper. Codes begin with a 4, as in 4PH1 for Physics.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson published a November 2026 International GCSE timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables in advance, so always revise towards the live PDF.

programmes.name: What follows at 16
programmes.description: Emirates Living families split roughly three ways after IGCSE: A Levels at the same school, the IB Diploma at an IB World School nearby, or a move abroad. Each route reads the IGCSE grade sheet differently. A Level maths departments look at the algebra grade; IB Diploma coordinators look at the spread across six subject groups and at written English.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. For a Year 11 in The Springs that means the post-16 choice set is wider in 2027 than it was for an older sibling, and worth re-checking rather than assumed.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Emirates Living parents most often ask about, with the codes a Dubai school is likely to have entered. The description says what the subject actually assesses, because that is what decides whether a tutor is the right one.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers in both boards, with a non-calculator component in Pearson Mathematics A. Marks are lost on algebraic manipulation under time pressure, on bearings and vectors, and on multi-step probability. Extended and Higher entry carries the only route to the top grades.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: The graphics-calculator route many IB-track schools prefer, with an investigation paper and a graded calculator expectation throughout. Students moving in from 0580 mid-course find the exploration-style questions unfamiliar even when their algebra is sound.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Equation rearrangement, unit discipline and graph gradients carry most of the marks. Cambridge Extended candidates sit a practical component, and Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Electricity and waves are where Dubai cohorts most often stall.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables decide the grade. Students who can recite reactivity series still lose marks on titration calculations and on writing state symbols. Organic nomenclature is cheap to fix and often simply untaught.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: A terminology subject before it is a science subject. Mark schemes accept specific words and reject near-synonyms, so answers that sound right score zero. Enzyme graphs, transport in plants and genetic crosses are the recurring Dubai weak points.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: One qualification worth two grades, covering biology, chemistry and physics in less depth than three separate sciences. A child on 0654 does not need three specialist tutors; they need one who knows which parts of each discipline the double award actually includes.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the comparative reading question carry the weight. Dubai students who read widely still lose marks for ignoring the audience and form instructions in the question stem. Timed writing under forty minutes is the single most trainable component.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with a different mark scheme, and a frequent source of confusion in multilingual Springs households. Listening and the short-response reading tasks reward precision rather than fluency.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 and 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study papers where marks come from applying a term to the given firm rather than defining it. Six- and twelve-mark evaluation questions need a structure, and most students have never been shown one explicitly.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and logic gates in Paper 1, with algorithm design in Paper 2. Students who code confidently in Python often lose marks because the paper wants Cambridge pseudocode conventions, not working code.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 First Language, 0544 Foreign Language)
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, and the examined IGCSE route is separate from that requirement. Non-Arab students on the foreign-language syllabus need vocabulary drilling and script fluency more than grammar theory.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 and 0470)
subjects.description: Both reward case-study specificity: a named place, a named date, a figure. Students lose marks writing generically about urbanisation or causation when the mark scheme is looking for the example they were taught in Year 10.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.regionsIntro: The Springs is fifteen numbered sub-communities with meaningfully different school runs, and it sits inside a cluster where families move between neighbours constantly. These are the areas this page serves and what changes between them.

regions.name: The Springs 1 to 4
regions.note: Closest to the Al Khail Road exit and to Dubai British School Emirates Hills, so pick-up is often a short car run rather than a bus route. Sessions here can realistically start at 16:30 on most weekdays.

regions.name: The Springs 5 to 9
regions.note: The middle ring, where most households are on school buses to Al Barsha and Al Sufouh. Arrival home clusters around 16:00 to 16:30, which makes a 17:00 slot the reliable one rather than 16:00.

regions.name: The Springs 10 to 15
regions.note: Furthest from the main exits and usually last on the bus loop. Families here more often choose a 17:30 or post-dinner slot, and a sibling pair is easier to run back to back than in parallel.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Villas rather than townhouses, directly adjacent and sharing the same bus contractors. Emirates International School Meadows sits inside the community, so IB and British curricula appear in neighbouring houses.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Smaller and quieter, with a high proportion of long-term residents and a heavier tilt towards the Emirates Hills school ring. Often paired with The Springs in the same tutoring schedule for sibling groups.

regions.name: The Views and The Greens
regions.note: Apartment living on the Emirates Living edge nearest Sheikh Zayed Road. Regent International School sits in this ring, and study space at home is usually a bedroom desk rather than a dedicated room.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Large villas, two of the area's best-known school campuses on its boundary, and the shortest school run of the cluster. Families here most often ask for subject specialists rather than general support.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Where a sizeable share of Emirates Living children actually go to school. A 15:15 finish in Al Barsha South becomes a 16:15 arrival in Springs 11 once the bus loop is done.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and JBR
regions.note: Ten to twenty minutes along Sheikh Zayed Road and a common destination when a family moves out of a townhouse. Lessons continue unchanged on a move, because nothing in the model depends on the address.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: The schools closest to a Springs front door. Two of them run the IB alongside or instead of IGCSE, which is why a single street can contain a Year 11 sitting Cambridge papers and a Year 11 finishing MYP.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, reached by bus in twenty to thirty-five minutes depending on the Al Khail junction. Most of the British-curriculum IGCSE cohort from The Springs sits in this ring.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah Park, JVT and Dubai Sports City
schoolClusters.note: The newer ring to the south, growing fastest as Dubai adds places. Journey times are the longest of the three, which is what pushes a Springs session into the 17:30 slot.

sections.heading: Which schools The Springs actually feeds, and what each one sits
paragraphs: Almost no secondary school sits inside The Springs, so the first useful piece of local knowledge is which campuses the community's buses go to. The table below groups them by ring and names the qualification each one examines at 16. This matters more than it sounds: a tutor matched to a child at an IB World School needs to understand MYP criterion marking, while a tutor matched to a child in the British ring needs the syllabus code and tier.

Dubai is the densest private-school market in the UAE. The Dubai Media Office reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at seven per cent. In Emirates Living that national picture compresses into a handful of campuses, and the British share is far higher than the city average.

The practical consequence for a Springs parent is that the school ring sets the finish time, and the finish time sets the tutoring slot. A child in the Emirates Hills ring is home before a child in the Dubai Sports City ring by nearly an hour. Booking a 16:00 lesson because a neighbour's child manages it is the most common scheduling mistake in this community, and it produces a tutor waiting on an empty call.

Inspection context is included because KHDA publishes it and parents read it, but a school-level band says nothing reliable about one department. The later section on inspection reports explains how to read that properly.

sections.heading: The Year 9 options evening decides more than any tutor can
paragraphs: The single highest-leverage week in a British-curriculum Springs household is not the week before exams. It is the week in the spring term of Year 9 when option forms go home. Three choices made in that fortnight set a ceiling that no amount of tutoring in Year 11 can lift, and most families make them in an evening with a glossy booklet and twenty minutes of thinking time.

The first is the science route. Triple award, double award and co-ordinated science are three different qualifications with three different grade outcomes, and a child who takes double award cannot later present three separate science grades to an A Level department that asks for them. The second is mathematics: whether Additional Mathematics 0606 or Further Pure 4PM1 is available as a fourth option, and whether the school will enter at Extended or Higher tier. The third is the second language, which affects the IB Diploma route far more than the A Level one.

A tutor can help with the decision, and that is often a better use of two hours than six months of weekly lessons later. What a tutor cannot do is reverse it. By the autumn of Year 10 a school has bought the textbooks, built the timetable and registered a tier, and moving a child between routes mid-course means re-teaching content they were never shown.
The table sets out the decision with its consequence rather than its description, which is the part the options booklet usually leaves out.

sections.heading: Where a weekday hour actually exists in a Springs household
paragraphs: This is the section that decides whether tutoring survives past November. The theory is that a child has four free hours after school. The reality in a Springs townhouse is that the hour between arrival and dinner is spent eating, changing and arguing, the hour after dinner belongs to school homework, and anything booked at 19:30 for a Year 10 produces a tired lesson and a cancelled one the following week.

The workable pattern that holds across a full term is a single protected slot that starts after the bus but before homework, treated as fixed rather than negotiable. For most of the community that lands between 16:30 and 17:30. Younger children can go earlier; Year 12 and 13 students can go later, because their own study blocks are already self-directed and a 19:00 lesson fits the way they work.

Two practical details matter more than they should. The first is the room: a townhouse rarely has a spare study, so the lesson usually happens at a bedroom desk or at the dining table with headphones, and deciding that once is better than renegotiating it weekly. The second is the Dubai weekend. The school week runs Monday to Friday, with Friday afternoons often shortened, so Saturday morning is the single most reliable ninety minutes in the week and the slot that survives exam season intact.

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA inspection report before you blame your child
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection outcomes are published on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and most Springs parents have read their school's band without reading the subject-level pages behind it.

The band is a whole-school judgement. A school rated Very Good can contain a mathematics department judged Good and a science department judged Acceptable, and the report usually says so explicitly, by phase as well as by subject. That is the page to read before concluding that a child who suddenly struggles in Year 10 chemistry has a problem. Sometimes the department has had three teachers in two years and the child is a symptom rather than the cause.

What an inspection band does not do is predict an individual grade. It is a judgement about provision, measured against criteria that include attainment and progress but also leadership, safeguarding and the teaching of Arabic. A parent deciding whether to buy tutoring should read the subject paragraphs, the progress judgements for the relevant phase, and any recommendation that names the subject in question. Those three things together tell you whether you are filling a gap the school already knows about.

Fee context belongs here too. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A flat fee year is the right moment to decide whether a tutoring budget is worth committing, rather than discovering it alongside a fee rise.

sections.heading: Target grades, working-at grades and the report that worries you
paragraphs: Twice a year a Springs household receives a report with two numbers against each subject, and the gap between them causes more unnecessary tutoring purchases than any other document in Dubai. One number is a target, usually generated from a baseline test taken in Year 7 or Year 9. The other is a working-at or current grade, which is a teacher's judgement of where the child would land if examined today on the content covered so far.

Neither number is a prediction. A target generated from a cognitive-ability test is a statistical expectation for a cohort, not a promise about a person, and a working-at grade in November of Year 10 is based on perhaps a fifth of the syllabus. A child two grades below target in the autumn of Year 10 is often just behind on content, while a child on target in Year 11 whose marks collapse in the mocks usually has an exam-technique problem that no amount of extra content teaching will fix.

The useful move is to ask the subject teacher two specific questions: which topics the current grade is based on, and whether the gap is content, accuracy or timing. Those three causes need completely different tutoring. Content gaps need teaching. Accuracy problems need marked written practice with feedback on the writing itself. Timing problems need whole papers under the clock, which almost no child does voluntarily at home.

Where a school supplies a question-level analysis of the mock, that document is worth more to a tutor than the report. It shows exactly which command words and which topics lost marks, and it turns a vague request for help into a four-lesson plan with a measurable endpoint.

Separate content gaps from accuracy and from timing before buying hours

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what the money buys
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring providers in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Springs family transacts in. Here are the dirham bands, cheapest first, with who publishes what. At the lower end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which generally buys a university student working from a textbook. Qualified subject tutors working online sit between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

Above that, named IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted between AED 200 and 450 or more: TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 shows 200 to 450 and above. Premium and examiner-branded tutoring runs from AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The pattern a Springs parent should notice is that the in-home band overlaps the specialist band almost exactly. Paying AED 300 an hour for someone who drives to Emirates Living buys the driving, not a better teacher; paying AED 300 for a specialist online buys the subject knowledge instead. That is the whole argument, and it is an arithmetic one rather than a preference.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are published market figures read in October 2026, quoted so a family can judge a quote they receive from anyone. Our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation about what the week can actually hold, which is where the real cost question gets answered.

sections.heading: Half terms, the long summer and the three weeks that move a grade
paragraphs: The Dubai academic year gives a Springs family more usable tutoring time than a UK one, and most of it goes unused. There is a long winter break, a spring break, a half term in each term, and a summer that runs from late June or early July into the first days of September. For a Year 10 heading into Year 11, those weeks are the only block of time in two years when a child can rebuild a topic from the beginning without a homework deadline interrupting.

Ramadan reshapes the day rather than removing it. School hours shorten, afternoons are quieter, and the productive window for many families moves to after iftar. Sessions that normally sit at 17:00 move to 20:30 or later for the month, and families who plan that in advance keep continuity instead of losing four weeks. The same applies to travel: lessons run on a screen, so a family in the UK or India for three weeks of summer can keep a weekly slot if they want it.

The three weeks that move a grade most are not the three before the exam. They are study leave, where a Year 11 has whole days and no supervision, and the two weeks after mock results, when a child knows exactly what went wrong and is briefly motivated to fix it. A tutor booked for those weeks with a question-level analysis in hand is worth more than the same hours spread thinly across the autumn.

What should not happen is a family booking an intensive block in April of Year 11 and expecting it to substitute for two years. Cambridge and Pearson entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and by April the tier and the subject set are fixed. The honest answer at that point is that six weeks of focused work on two or three high-yield topics can move a borderline grade, and that promising more than that would be dishonest.
bullets: Half terms and the long summer are the only interruption-free blocks in two years

sections.heading: What the Ministry of Education will count later
paragraphs: IGCSE grades matter twice: once for post-16 entry, and again years later if your child applies to a UAE university and needs their secondary certificate recognised. The second use is where most families discover a rule they did not know about, and it is not mentioned on a single competitor page we examined.

For the British track, Gulf Today reported in July 2026 that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must additionally submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. The same report states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold appears in that source, which is why this page publishes none: an unsourced equivalency number would be worse than no number at all.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutor performs, and nobody needs tutoring in order to obtain it. The reason it belongs on a page about a Year 10 subject choice is simpler: a family that knows five subjects at grade 3 or better is the floor can make a calmer decision about which borderline subject deserves the tutoring budget this term.

sections.heading: Starting from The Springs, and the limits we will say out loud
paragraphs: The first conversation is about the week, not the syllabus. What time does the bus arrive, which evenings are already taken, where in the house the lesson will happen, and which single subject would make the biggest difference if it improved. A family that answers those four questions has usually designed the right plan before any teaching starts.

Then the syllabus code. One email to the school's exams officer produces a line like Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4CH1, and that line decides who the right tutor is. Matching without it is guesswork, and guesswork is how a family ends up paying a Cambridge specialist to teach an Edexcel paper structure. The trial lesson is free and is used to diagnose rather than to sell: the tutor works through a past question with the student and writes down what they saw.

Three limits, stated before anyone pays. Lessons are online one-to-one over live video; IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and a page that implied otherwise would be selling something we do not have. Some narrow combinations - a specific board and tier in a minority subject at a specific hour - cannot always be filled from the UAE pool, and when that happens we say so and offer a specialist elsewhere at the same rate rather than substituting someone unsuitable. And no tutor can guarantee a grade; anyone who offers one in this market should be treated with real scepticism.

What a tutor will do with coursework is worth stating too. They teach method, review drafts the student has written, and give feedback. A tutor must never write the coursework, and any provider offering to produce assessed work is exposing your child to a malpractice finding rather than helping them.
bullets: Four questions about the week before any subject conversation
Syllabus code from the exams officer, then the match
A free trial lesson used to diagnose and write down what was found
Coverage gaps and the online-only model stated before payment

process.title: Tell us the clock
process.description: Bus arrival time, which evenings are already committed, and where the lesson will physically happen in the house. For most Springs families this conversation alone fixes the slot that will still be running in March.

process.title: Get the syllabus code
process.description: One email to the exams officer gives the board, code and tier: Cambridge 0580 Extended, Pearson 4MA1 Higher, and so on. Everything about the match depends on that line, and it takes a day to obtain.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: Sixty minutes with the matched tutor, working through a real past question rather than a sales conversation. The tutor writes down what they saw: content gaps, accuracy, timing, and which of the three is actually the problem.

process.title: Agree the plan and the slot
process.description: A written plan naming the topics for the next four lessons, the fixed day and time, and how progress will be visible to you. If a sibling needs a consecutive slot, it is built in here rather than added later.

process.title: Review at four lessons
process.description: A short check against the plan: what moved, what did not, and whether the slot is surviving the week. Families either continue, change tutor, or stop - and stopping after four lessons is a legitimate outcome we would rather you reach honestly.

whyPoints.title: The slot is designed around your school ring
whyPoints.description: A child in the Jumeirah Park ring is home nearly an hour after a child in the Emirates Hills ring. Scheduling starts from that fact instead of offering a standard time and hoping, which is why these slots survive past November.

whyPoints.title: Board and tier before personality
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different papers with different structures. Matching begins with the code on your child's entry, so the tutor is teaching the examination your child will actually sit.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, every week
whyPoints.description: Continuity is most of the value in one-to-one teaching. The same tutor keeps a running picture of what has been covered and what has not, so no lesson is spent re-establishing where the student is.

faqs.question: Is there really an IGCSE tutor near me in The Springs, or will the lesson be online?
faqs.answer: The lesson is online, one-to-one over live video, and that is deliberate. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. In practice a Springs family gets more from this: instead of choosing from whoever can drive to Emirates Living by five o'clock, you get a tutor matched to the exact board, tier and subject your child is entered for, at the half-hour your week actually has free. Nothing about the teaching depends on the address, which is also why lessons keep running when you travel.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in The Springs usually attend?
faqs.answer: Four rings cover most of the community. Closest are Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Regent International School, Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. The second ring is Al Barsha and Al Sufouh, including Kings' School Al Barsha, GEMS Wellington International School and Dubai College. The third is Al Barsha South and Motor City, and the fourth is Jumeirah Park, JVT and Dubai Sports City. Which ring you are in matters because it sets the arrival time home, and that sets the only workable lesson slot.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start after the Springs bus arrives?
faqs.answer: For most of the community, 17:00. Secondary students reach The Springs between 15:20 and 16:50 depending on the school ring and the bus loop, and the half hour after arrival is lost to eating and changing. Years 7 and 8 can usually manage 16:15 or 16:30. Year 11 students in the run-up to mocks tend to hold a weekday slot at 17:00 plus a Saturday morning block, which is the most reliable ninety minutes in a Dubai week. Sixth-formers often prefer 19:00, because their study time is already self-directed.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE board and syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Email the school's examinations officer and ask for the board, the four-digit or alphanumeric code and the tier for each subject. You will get a line such as Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher. This matters because Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE are different qualifications with different paper counts, durations and tiering, even in the same subject. A tutor who has only ever taught one of them will confidently teach the wrong paper structure. The reply usually arrives within a working day and it is the single most useful thing you can get before booking.

faqs.question: Why is the Year 9 options evening more important than tutoring in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Because three decisions made that fortnight set a ceiling nobody can lift later. The science route determines whether your child ends up with three separate science grades or a double award. The maths tier determines the top grade available at all. The second language affects whether the IB Diploma stays a realistic post-16 route. By the autumn of Year 10 the school has built timetables and registered tiers, so changing route means re-teaching content your child was never shown. Two hours of advice at option stage often beats six months of lessons afterwards.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Dubai at the moment?
faqs.answer: Published market rates, read in October 2026, run from the low end upwards: EdFlik advertises AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, which generally buys a student tutor. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Named specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table showing 200 to 450 and above. These are other providers' figures, not ours, quoted so you can judge any quote you receive.

faqs.question: Does an in-home tutor around Emirates Living cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: The published bands overlap almost exactly, which is the interesting part. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate at 180 to 350; named online specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above. So at AED 300 an hour you are choosing between a tutor who drives to Emirates Living and a tutor who specialises in your child's exact syllabus. The money buys the journey or it buys the subject knowledge. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai, so the choice we offer is the second one.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection band actually tell me about my child's teaching?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. KHDA publishes a whole-school judgement on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and a school rated Very Good can contain a department judged Acceptable. The useful pages are the subject paragraphs for your child's phase, the attainment and progress tables, and the named recommendations at the end. Read two consecutive reports side by side to see direction of travel. If a department has been through several staff changes, a child struggling in that subject may be a symptom rather than the cause, and that changes what tutoring is for.

faqs.question: My child's report shows a target grade and a working-at grade two bands apart. Should I worry?
faqs.answer: Not immediately. A target is usually generated from a baseline test taken years earlier and is a cohort expectation, not a forecast for a person. A working-at grade in November of Year 10 is based on perhaps a fifth of the syllabus. Ask the subject teacher two questions: which topics the current grade is based on, and whether the gap is content, accuracy or timing. Those three causes need completely different work. Content needs teaching, accuracy needs marked written practice, timing needs whole papers under the clock.

faqs.question: Should we use one tutor for two IGCSE subjects, or two specialists on one evening?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Maths and physics frequently sit with one person, as do biology and chemistry. Three separate sciences at Extended tier rarely do well with one tutor, because each has its own mark-scheme habits. In a Springs household the more common arrangement is two specialists in consecutive slots on the same evening, which keeps four weekday evenings completely free. For a double-award course such as Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, one tutor who knows what that qualification includes is usually the better answer.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring in the spring term of Year 11?
faqs.answer: It is late but not pointless, and the honest framing matters. Entry deadlines and tier decisions are already fixed by then, so nothing structural can change. What six focused weeks can do is lift a borderline grade by working on two or three high-yield topics and on timing, using the question-level analysis from the mock. What it cannot do is substitute for two years of content. Any provider who tells you otherwise in April is selling something, and a grade guarantee at that stage is not credible from anyone.

faqs.question: Do lessons carry on during Ramadan and the long Dubai summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing changed rather than the plan. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the productive window moves later, so a 17:00 slot usually becomes 20:30 or later for the month. Families who arrange that in advance keep continuity instead of losing four weeks. The long summer break, from late June or early July into early September, is the only interruption-free block in a two-year course and the best time to rebuild a topic from the beginning. Lessons also continue while a family travels, since everything runs over video.

faqs.question: Should I ask an IGCSE tutor to show me a MoHRE tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the u.ae guidance states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted.

faqs.question: Will five IGCSEs be enough for my child's certificate to be recognised in the UAE later?
faqs.answer: On the sourced British-track rule, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no less than E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. That is what Gulf Today reported in July 2026, and one ranking competitor publishes six subjects instead, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutor performs or can speed up, and verification should always be done on the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IGCSE coursework without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the method, explains what the mark scheme rewards, and gives feedback on drafts the student has written themselves. That is legitimate and valuable. A tutor must never write the coursework, produce a draft for a student to submit, or edit a piece to completion. One provider in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments; buying work like that risks a malpractice finding against your child rather than a better grade. Ask any prospective tutor where they draw this line, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for our exact subject, tier and time slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is not standard practice in this market. A narrow combination - one board, one tier, a minority subject, a fixed half-hour - sometimes cannot be filled from the UAE-based pool. When that happens the options are a specialist elsewhere teaching at the same rate in your Gulf Standard Time slot, a different time with the right person, or a wait with an honest estimate. What we will not do is put an unsuitable tutor in the slot because the slot was booked.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Book the slot that fits your week, then find the tutor
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-springs.closingBody: Start with the clock rather than the subject. Tell us when the bus reaches your part of The Springs, which evenings are already gone, and which single subject would change the most if it improved. Get the syllabus code from the exams officer while you wait. Then take the free trial lesson: sixty minutes of real teaching on a past question, with a written note of what the tutor found. If the diagnosis does not match what you were told at parents' evening, that is useful information on its own, and there is no obligation to continue.

intro.heading: Which term you are in decides what tutoring is for
paragraphs: Six terms make up an IGCSE course and each one has a different job. In the first, the content is new and nothing is at stake. By the fourth, tier and entry decisions are closing. By the sixth, the only work that pays is paper technique. A family that books tutoring without naming which term they are in tends to buy the wrong thing: general support when a specific gap needed closing, or frantic revision when there were still four terms available to build properly. The term is the single most useful fact in any enquiry.

A proximity search is a poor way to find this. Sorting tutors by distance from The Sustainable City returns a list ordered by an attribute that has no bearing on whether your child's grade moves. What matters is whether the tutor teaches the specific syllabus your child is entered for, knows the paper structure and tiering, and can diagnose where marks are going. Those are all answerable questions, and the section on what you can verify sets out how to ask them.

The community helps in one respect and hinders in another. The Sustainable City sits off Al Qudra Road with a school inside its own gates, which means children at that school are home early and the late afternoon is genuinely available. The hindrance is scale: five hundred or so villas do not contain a resident specialist in Extended-tier mathematics, separate sciences and English as a Second Language, waiting to be discovered. The local pool is thinnest in exactly the subjects where a Year 11 student most needs depth.

Both boards report on the 9 to 1 scale and both run series open to UAE candidates. Cambridge International examines in June and November, and its February and March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route for a Dubai candidate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Your child's actual dates and tier come from the school, which handles entries and timetable zones, and the school's published calendar is the authority to plan against.

One thing to be clear about before any of the detail: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Lessons into The Sustainable City are one-to-one, live over video, with past-paper questions on screen and a recording available on request. Household visits are a service we run in India only, and no part of this page should be read as offering one here. What the model buys in this community is a tutor chosen by syllabus code rather than by driving distance, and a session that can start while a teenager is still able to concentrate rather than after two unpaid car journeys have been fitted around it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-sustain.programmesIntro: Three stages, three different jobs for a tutor. What follows is what each stage actually involves and the point at which intervening stops being cheap.

programmes.name: Years 8 and 9, before the course starts
programmes.description: Nothing external is assessed, so weaknesses stay invisible. The ones that matter later are narrow and identifiable: fluency with fractions and negatives, rearranging formulae, writing a paragraph that justifies rather than asserts, and reading a question carefully enough to notice what it asks. A term of work here removes the need for two years of catch-up afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: Mid-phase arrivals are common in this part of Dubai, with families moving in from American, CBSE or other systems. A child joining a British-curriculum school in Year 9 usually has a specific curriculum-sequence gap rather than a general weakness, and identifying it before the IGCSE course begins is the cheapest intervention available to a family here.

programmes.name: Year 10, terms one to three
programmes.description: Content is covered for the first time, coursework components begin in some subjects, and the school forms its view on tier. Internal end-of-year examinations in most Dubai schools feed directly into entry decisions for Year 11. The signal that a plan is behind is simple: a student who cannot do last term's topics now, rather than one who finds this term's topics hard.
programmes.countryNote: In this community, Year 10 is when the honest tier conversation should happen. Core and Extended in a Cambridge subject are different papers with different grade ceilings, and the decision sits with the school ahead of the board's entry deadline. Deciding in the final terms removes the option; deciding in Year 10 leaves a year to make Extended realistic.

programmes.name: Year 11, terms four to six
programmes.description: One mock block, a set of entry deadlines months ahead of the papers, predicted grades drawn from the mocks, then study leave and the series. Nearly all measurable improvement in this year comes from technique rather than new content. The behind-schedule signal here is a student still meeting syllabus content for the first time after the mock block has finished.
programmes.countryNote: The November series is the planned resit route for a Dubai candidate who misses a grade in June, and a November entry closes months before the papers, so the decision is made within weeks of results. Pearson's published history gives a sense of the rhythm: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: After the results: A Level, Diploma or a resit
programmes.description: IGCSE grades act as entry thresholds for whatever follows, and Dubai schools set their own requirements for specific A Level or Higher Level subjects. A student aiming at a mathematics-heavy route needs a named grade in a named subject rather than a strong overall profile, so the useful question is which single grade the target route depends on.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university plans, Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Verify current rules on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-sustain.subjectsIntro: The subjects families in this belt ask about most, with the syllabus codes and the specific failure that recurs in each. Booking against a named paper and a named weakness is faster than booking against a subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Method marks are available on almost every multi-step question and students who write nothing down forfeit them. Algebraic manipulation is the bottleneck far more often than any single topic. Non-calculator fluency is assumed in parts of both specifications, and that is where Extended-tier students lose easy marks.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level mathematics or a Higher Level route, and it moves fast. Calculus and trigonometric identities are the usual pressure points. Students who cope by pattern-matching rather than understanding tend to fail the unfamiliar questions that distinguish the top grades.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Circuits, moments and equilibrium questions are where Extended candidates reliably drop marks. The practical skills paper rewards students who have practised interpreting apparatus diagrams and criticising a method, not students who have simply read the theory again.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations are the single largest source of lost marks, followed by qualitative analysis answers written imprecisely. Students who learn ionic equations as patterns rather than as memorised recipes handle unseen questions far better.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty is the problem, and terminology precision decides the band. Osmosis answers lose marks for omitting concentration gradient; genetics answers lose them for incomplete notation. Data questions reward reading axes and units before the question stem.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry most of the marks, and the common failure is good writing in the wrong register for the stated audience. Reading questions need quotation plus comment, and a quotation left to speak for itself scores nothing.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification from English Language with different papers, and an incorrect entry costs far more than a few marks. Listening and speaking components need rehearsal rather than revision, and accuracy outranks ambitious vocabulary throughout.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Command terms govern the mark more than content does. An answer that explains where the question said evaluate caps itself regardless of accuracy. Ratio and elasticity calculations need drilling separately from the written responses.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These grades appear beside IGCSE subjects on the report and are routinely the weakest line for a mid-phase arrival.

sections.heading: The two-year course mapped term by term
paragraphs: This is the table that should exist on every IGCSE tutoring page in this market and exists on none of them. Each of the six terms has a different job, a different thing a tutor should be doing, and a different signal that the plan has slipped. Reading it is usually enough for a parent to place their own child and work out whether what they are about to buy matches where the child actually is.

The pattern worth noticing is that the cheap interventions are all early and the expensive ones are all late. Fixing algebraic fluency in the first term of Year 10 takes a handful of sessions. The same gap, discovered in the fifth term, has to be fixed while five other subjects compete for the same hours and while the mock results have already gone into a predicted grade. Nothing about the gap changed; the cost of closing it multiplied, because the time available shrank and the stakes rose.

The behind-schedule signals in the final column are the practical part. They are deliberately specific, because general worry is not actionable. A student who finds this term's work hard is normal. A student who cannot do last term's work now has a retention problem that will compound, and that is the point at which a term of weekly sessions is worth more than a block of panic revision eighteen months later. Parents who use the final column as a checklist each term rarely find themselves buying the expensive version of the same fix.

sections.heading: What you can actually verify before paying a tutor
paragraphs: This is the section the market avoids, which is strange, because it is the one a parent most needs. Almost every claim a tutoring service makes is either checkable in two minutes or unverifiable in principle, and knowing which is which is most of what protects a family. A near me search surfaces proximity, which is checkable and nearly useless. It does not surface syllabus currency, permit status or what happens when a tutor turns out to be wrong for the child.

Start with the permit, because it is a matter of law rather than opinion. An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any specific amount you read online should be treated with suspicion.

Then test the claims that sound impressive. Approval language is the one to probe hardest: a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for a training institute with physical premises in Dubai, and plenty of websites use wording that implies they hold one. IB Gram does not. Ratings are the next: self-asserted star ratings that differ from a company's own page text are common in this market and are a structured-data violation as well as a trust problem. The table below is the short version to work through.

sections.heading: Grades 9 to 1, and the only grade that actually matters
paragraphs: Both boards report International GCSE on the 9 to 1 scale, and parents arriving from other systems frequently misread it. The scale is not a renumbering of A to G with the same meaning per letter; the top of the old A* band was split, so 9 is deliberately rarer than A* was. What follows from that is a practical point: a target of all 9s is a different proposition from a target of all A*s, and treating them as equivalent leads families to buy tutoring in subjects that did not need it.

The more useful exercise is to identify the single grade the post-16 route depends on. A student heading for A Level mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches needs a specific grade in mathematics, usually in the top bands, and the school will state its own threshold. A student heading for an arts or humanities route needs something quite different. One named grade in one named subject is almost always worth more attention than a general lift across nine subjects, and it is far cheaper to pursue.

The other grade to understand is the predicted one. Predicted grades come out of the mock block and travel with post-16 applications, which means mocks have consequences beyond practice. A family that understands this engages tutoring before the mocks rather than after them. A family that discovers it afterwards is negotiating with a prediction already recorded, and schools reasonably expect evidence rather than argument before revising one.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of revision should look like, week by week
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the commonest commitment and it is long enough to be worth structuring properly. The mistake families make is to spread it evenly across every subject and every topic, which produces familiarity rather than performance. The structure that works concentrates on a small number of recurring, high-mark topics for the specific syllabus code, and it tests retention rather than re-reading notes.

The mechanism to use is retrieval under timing. A student who re-reads a topic feels prepared because the material is recognisable; the same student under examination conditions discovers that recognition is not recall. So each week should end with questions attempted cold, marked against the official scheme, and lost marks classified by reason — content, command term, method, arithmetic or time. The classification is the useful output, because it tells you what next week should contain.

The table sets out the shape we run. It front-loads diagnosis, which parents often find uncomfortable because weeks one and two look slower than teaching would. They are, and they are what makes weeks three to eight efficient rather than broad. The between-session work matters at least as much: one tutored hour is roughly 1% of a student's week, so the hour has to change what the other days contain. Each week we set a named output rather than an instruction to revise — three questions on one topic, attempted under timing and self-marked, with the student's own corrections brought back to the next session. A family that treats the hour as the whole intervention gets a fraction of what a family that treats it as a weekly planning meeting gets, and that difference is far larger than the difference between any two tutors.

sections.heading: What a term of tutoring costs, and what the alternatives cost
paragraphs: Because this page is organised by term, the useful unit is a term rather than an hour. A term is roughly twelve to fourteen weeks in a Dubai school year. At the published market rate for a qualified online subject tutor of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, one weekly session comes to roughly AED 1,800 to AED 4,200 across a term in a single subject. That is the number a family should compare against, rather than an hourly figure that sounds small in isolation.

Set that against the other published options. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, which over a term is a few hundred dirhams in a single subject. In-home visits are published at AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350 — a term of weekly home visits therefore sits materially above the online equivalent, and the difference is a car journey. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider advertising AED 650.

Monthly packages are the other format in this market: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. All of those figures belong to the companies and rate guides that published them and were read in October 2026. They are the market's numbers. sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and what a tutor may never do
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects carry assessed work completed outside the examination hall, and parts of this market will offer to complete it. That offer should be refused without discussion. Assessed work must be the student's own and is authenticated by the school; a submission that is not is a malpractice matter whose consequences fall on the candidate. One operation in this market sells completed internal assessments for a different qualification at AED 3,750, which tells you the trade exists and what it costs. It is not a shortcut with a risk attached.

The workable boundary is specific. A tutor may teach the content a task draws on, explain the assessment criteria, question whether a method is reproducible, point out a conclusion that outruns the evidence, and comment on writing the student has produced. A tutor may not write any part of a submission, redraft a paragraph into final form, select and carry out an investigation, or provide a model to be edited. The test is whether a sentence in the final submission exists because a tutor wrote it.

Practical science in both boards' international specifications is examined on a written paper rather than assessed in a laboratory, which has a useful consequence for online tuition. What that paper tests — reading apparatus diagrams, identifying independent and controlled variables, criticising a method, handling results tables and plotting graphs — is entirely teachable over a screen using the boards' own past questions. Laboratory handling remains the school's responsibility, and we do not pretend otherwise.
