sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the emirate you happen to live in
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The market is large: 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the IB at 7%. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the following academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Two regulator facts affect an IGCSE plan directly. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited; instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those grades appear on the report beside IGCSE subjects. And the emirate decides the regulator: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Why that last point matters to a family in this community: Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, so a school's assessment calendar can differ by emirate. If your household moves, the term structure your tutoring plan was built around may change with it. IB Gram holds no permit, approval or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office. We describe the regulators because it helps you read your school, not to borrow their standing.

sections.heading: Timing, Ramadan and the slot that has to survive the term
paragraphs: A revision plan collapses for scheduling reasons more often than for teaching reasons. The UAE working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, so Saturday and Sunday are the only full days free and also the days families travel and host. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful study window moves to the evening, which means a post-Iftar session is frequently the most productive hour available and an afternoon slot is frequently wasted.

Where you live in this belt changes what is possible. A student at school inside The Sustainable City is home early enough for a 3.30pm or 4pm start, which is when concentration is still available. A student travelling to Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Arabian Ranches is realistically unavailable until 5.30pm, and in a sports-heavy household that slot is contested four evenings a week. The families whose plans survive are the ones who decide in the first term which evening belongs to tutoring and then defend it against everything else.

Our side of that is simple. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time; they move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan with the same tutor; and a block can pause during a school's own examination fortnight, when adding sessions produces fatigue rather than marks. What we do not do is move a student between tutors to keep a diary full. For a Year 11 student in the fifth term, continuity with someone who already knows which questions go wrong is worth more than an uninterrupted schedule.

faqs.question: Does a tutor really need to be near The Sustainable City?
faqs.answer: For an IGCSE subject, no, and distance is a misleading first filter. What decides whether a grade moves is whether the tutor teaches the exact syllabus code and tier your child is entered for and can diagnose where marks are going. A community of five hundred villas does not contain a resident Extended-tier specialist in every subject. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses at all; lessons are one-to-one over live video, which is what allows the match to be made on syllabus instead of postcode.

faqs.question: Which term should we start tutoring in for the best value?
faqs.answer: Year 10, and the earlier in it the better. Fixing algebraic fluency or calculation layout while content is still being met for the first time takes a handful of sessions. The identical gap discovered in the fifth term has to be closed while five other subjects compete for the same hours and while mock results have already fed a predicted grade. The gap did not change; the cost of closing it multiplied. Starting in Year 10 usually removes the need for an intensive final-term block altogether.

faqs.question: What does grade 9 actually mean compared with the old A*?
faqs.answer: The 9 to 1 scale is not a straight renumbering of A to G. The top of the old A* band was split, which makes 9 deliberately rarer than A* was. The practical consequence is that a target of all 9s is a materially harder proposition than a target of all A*s, and families who treat them as equivalent often buy tutoring in subjects that did not need it. A more useful exercise is identifying the single grade the intended post-16 route depends on and working on that.

faqs.question: How do we check whether a tutor is legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly about the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted online with suspicion. A straight answer names the permit; a dodge talks about being fully compliant without naming it.

faqs.question: How much does one weekly session cost across a whole term?
faqs.answer: At the published market rate for a qualified online subject tutor of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, one weekly session in a single subject comes to roughly AED 1,800 to AED 4,200 over a twelve to fourteen week term. Budget online tutoring at AED 33 to AED 65 an hour is a few hundred dirhams across the same period, and in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 sit materially higher. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our prices; we quote after a free trial.

faqs.question: Why do mock examinations matter more than practice?
faqs.answer: Because predicted grades come out of them and travel with post-16 applications. A mock is practice in form and consequence in effect. Families who understand this engage tutoring in the weeks before the mock block, which is when a grade can still be influenced. Families who discover it afterwards are negotiating against a prediction already recorded, and schools reasonably want evidence rather than argument before revising one. If there is one moment in Year 11 worth paying attention to, it is the fortnight before mocks.

faqs.question: My daughter says she revises for hours. Why are the marks not moving?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the revision is recognition rather than retrieval. Re-reading notes or a topic summary makes material feel familiar, and familiarity collapses under timed conditions. The fix is to attempt questions cold, mark them against the official scheme without charity, and classify every lost mark by reason: content, command term, method, arithmetic or time. That classification is what tells you what the next week should contain. Four questions processed that way beat an afternoon of highlighting.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor prepare a student for the IGCSE practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, because in both boards' international specifications practical skills are examined on a written paper rather than assessed in a laboratory. That paper tests reading apparatus diagrams, identifying independent and controlled variables, criticising a method, completing results tables and plotting graphs, all of which can be taught and practised over a screen using the boards' own past questions. Actual laboratory handling stays with the school, and no online tutor should claim to replace it. The paper, though, is what the grade depends on.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring more than one subject in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually not more than two, and often one is better. A Year 11 student carries school, coursework, the mandatory UAE subjects and generally a sport; three tutored hours a week tends to produce fatigue and incomplete between-session work, which means nothing gets prepared properly. The better approach is to identify the subject where a grade gap most affects the intended post-16 route, address that, and reassess after a month. We would rather start at one and add when a diagnosis justifies it.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not right for our child?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we propose another. It is worth asking any provider this question before booking rather than after, because the answer separates a service from a sales process: a straight answer names a replacement route and no penalty for using it, while a dodge offers reassurance that it rarely happens. Fit matters more at this age than credentials beyond a threshold, and a student who does not want to be in the session will not do the work between sessions either.

faqs.question: Can you teach my son's science specification if he is on Pearson rather than Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we match to the code rather than the subject, because the specifications differ in paper structure, tiering and in some cases modular options. Cambridge Physics is 0625 and Chemistry 0620; the Pearson equivalents are 4PH1 and 4CH1. Past papers are not interchangeable between them, so a tutor who teaches one fluently is not automatically fluent in the other. If you do not know which your child is entered for, the school's examinations officer can confirm it, and it is worth knowing before the first session.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around prayer times and Ramadan hours?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning for it is better than reacting to it. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time and can sit wherever in the evening the household needs. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the productive window moves late, so a post-Iftar session is often the most useful hour of the day for a fasting teenager while an afternoon slot is largely wasted. The slot moves and the tutor stays, because continuity with someone who knows the student's error patterns is worth more than a tidy calendar.

faqs.question: A competitor site says six IGCSE subjects are needed for equivalency. Is that right?
faqs.answer: No, the sourced figure is five. Equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae before acting on them, because equivalency is a process your family manages with the Ministry rather than a service a tutoring company performs.

faqs.question: How quickly can a first session be arranged?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects on either board, usually within a few days: a short diagnostic conversation, a free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue, then a written plan anchored to a date. Less common subjects and unusual tier combinations take longer, and we will say how long rather than book a placeholder session. If a school deadline makes the timing urgent, say so in the first message, because that changes which tutors we approach and the order in which they are asked.

faqs.question: Why no star rating or success statistics on this page?
faqs.answer: Because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method is a marketing claim rather than evidence. Several providers in this market publish self-asserted ratings that differ from their own page text, and one shows a review count that cannot be reconciled with its own student numbers. Self-serving review markup is also a structured-data policy problem. What we publish instead is checkable: AED figures with their publisher and the month read, regulator descriptions quoted from u.ae, and a stated boundary on assessed work.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-valley.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects to students living in The Valley and along the Al Ain road. Each is matched to a specification and tier, because the two boards differ in paper length, question style and the conventions their mark schemes reward.

intro.heading: What a proximity search leaves out of an IGCSE enquiry
paragraphs: A list of tutors sorted by distance tells you who is nearby and nothing about whether a grade will move. For IGCSE the variables that matter are narrow and checkable: the syllabus code your child is entered for, the tier, which paper the marks are disappearing on, and which command words they keep answering past. A tutor who can name those four things in the first conversation is worth more than one who lives ten minutes away and cannot.

The Valley makes the point sharply. This is a newer community on the road to Al Ain with no school inside its own boundary at the time of writing, so students here travel outward in two directions and attend several different schools. There is no single local cohort and no school-gate network passing on recommendations about who teaches Extended-tier chemistry well. A proximity search in this neighbourhood returns a short list, and a short list is not a shortlist.

Start with the code, because everything else depends on it. Cambridge International Mathematics is 0580 with Core and Extended tiers; the Pearson Edexcel equivalent is 4MA1 with Foundation and Higher tiers. The sciences are 0610, 0620 and 0625 against 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. These are separate qualifications whose past papers are not interchangeable, and in a community where neighbours attend different schools you cannot infer the board from a conversation at the park.

Then work out which paper and which skill. IGCSE marks are unusually diagnosable because mark schemes are explicit about what earns each mark: method marks on multi-step calculations, reason marks on angle questions, specific terminology in biology explanations. A student losing eight marks a paper to habit rather than ignorance is the commonest profile we see, and it is also the fastest to improve, which is why a marked paper is worth more to us than any description.

Delivery is stated plainly rather than implied: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with questions shared on screen, a whiteboard where working appears as it is written, and an optional recording. Home visits exist in our India operation only. In a community with no local pool, that model is what makes a specification-matched tutor available at all. It also removes the two car journeys either side of a visit, which is what allows a session to start while a student who has already travelled twice that day can still concentrate on a multi-step calculation. The remainder of this page is the subject detail that should drive the choice, with the local map treated as a scheduling constraint rather than a selection criterion.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-valley.programmesIntro: Three stages, and in a community whose children attend several schools the stage your own child is at matters more than what the neighbourhood is doing.

programmes.name: Year 9, before the specification begins
programmes.description: The specification assumes fluency in operations it does not examine directly: negatives and fractions, rearranging, units and prefixes, and reading a question closely enough to notice its instruction. A student who has to think about those cannot think about the problem containing them, and all of them are cheap to fix at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: The Valley fills largely with families moving within Dubai or into the emirate, so mid-phase school changes are routine here. A child joining a British-curriculum school in Year 9 usually has two or three specific unmet topics rather than a general weakness, and a diagnostic before the course starts is the cheapest intervention available to a family in this community.

programmes.name: Year 10, meeting the specification
programmes.description: Content is met for the first time and the habits that decide the final grade form here: writing method out, stating reasons, checking a result against the context described. Students who get through Year 10 on recall rather than understanding tend to stall in the examination year, when questions stop resembling the exercises.
programmes.countryNote: Tier decisions are informed by internal Year 10 examinations and have an entry deadline set by each school. Because Valley children attend several different schools, those dates differ between neighbours, so a family wanting to keep Extended or Higher tier open should ask its own school rather than assume a shared timetable.

programmes.name: Year 11, converting knowledge into marks
programmes.description: Almost all measurable improvement in this year comes from technique: command words, showing method, pacing against marks, and answering the question asked rather than the one revised for. A student who understands the material and loses marks to habit can move a grade in a term; a student who has not met the content cannot.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the June series, with November as the resit route; Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. For Valley students the practical constraint is the commute, which means one protected weekday evening plus a weekend block for whole papers is the structure that survives a full term.

programmes.name: After the results
programmes.description: IGCSE grades act as thresholds for A Level or IB Higher Level study, set per school and often per subject rather than overall. The useful question is which single grade the intended route depends on, because one named grade in one named subject is a far cheaper target than lifting an entire profile by half a grade.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university plans, Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects. Verify current rules on moe.gov.ae.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: What follows is the subject detail: the papers, what decides the grade and the specific place marks go. An enquiry naming a subject and a paper is worth three describing a general difficulty.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Method marks sit on nearly every multi-step question, so an answer arriving alone scores nothing when it is wrong. Algebraic manipulation is the bottleneck more often than any topic, and the current Cambridge specification includes assessment without a calculator while Pearson permits one throughout.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Circuits, moments and equilibrium cost higher-tier candidates the most. Many physics losses are mathematical rather than scientific: rearranging before substituting, prefixes, and reading a gradient from a graph that is not quite straight, which is diagnosable from marked work.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations lead the losses, followed by qualitative analysis described imprecisely. Students who learn ionic equations as patterns rather than memorised recipes cope with unfamiliar questions considerably better than those who do not.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology decides the band. Osmosis answers lose marks for omitting concentration gradient, enzyme answers for saying killed rather than denatured, and genetics answers for incomplete notation. Volume rather than conceptual difficulty is what makes the subject hard.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response carry most of the marks, and the common failure is strong writing in the wrong register for the stated audience and purpose. Reading questions need quotation plus comment; a quotation left to speak for itself earns nothing.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification with its own papers including listening and speaking, not an easier version of English Language. An incorrect entry costs far more than a few marks. Accuracy outranks ambitious vocabulary, and the speaking component needs rehearsal rather than revision.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Command words set the ceiling. An answer that explains where the question said evaluate caps itself whatever its accuracy, and numerical work on ratios and elasticity needs drilling separately from the written responses it sits beside.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source-handling and case-study specificity decide the higher bands. Students lose marks describing a source rather than using it as evidence, and using generic examples where a named, dated case study was expected by the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode and algorithm questions reward a consistent, legible convention more than clever code, and data representation answers need exact vocabulary. The ICT practical component is a skills examination that improves with repetition rather than with reading.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These grades appear beside IGCSE subjects and frequently slip for families who arrived mid-phase.

sections.heading: What each subject's papers actually assess
paragraphs: Parents are often told their child needs help with a subject, which is not actionable. What is actionable is knowing which paper carries which skill, because the subjects differ more than their shared grade scale suggests. A mathematics paper is a sequence of largely independent problems where method marks accumulate. An English Language paper is two or three extended tasks where register and purpose decide the band. A science paper carries explanation questions, calculations and a separate practical skills component.

That difference changes what a tutor should do. In mathematics the work is fluency and method discipline, and progress is visible within weeks. In English Language the work is reading the task for audience and purpose, then writing to it, which is a slower change but a large one. In the sciences the work splits three ways between terminology precision, calculation discipline and the practical paper, and a tutor who treats all three as one subject will spend the term on whichever they prefer.

The table below sets out, per subject, what decides the grade and the trap that recurs. It is worth reading alongside your child's own marked paper, because the combination of the two usually produces a specific plan in about ten minutes. Specifications are revised periodically, so confirm paper structures with the school rather than relying on any website, including this one. The principle holds even when a paper number changes: find out what the paper assesses, then work on that rather than on the subject in general.

sections.heading: Tier ceilings, and the decision that closes before the papers
paragraphs: Tiering is the part of IGCSE that surprises families most, because it is an entry decision rather than something adjustable in the examination hall. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capping the achievable grade and Extended reaching the top bands while containing harder content. Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in some subjects. The school decides the entry against the board's deadline, informed in most cases by internal Year 10 results.

The consequence is that a family wanting to keep the higher tier open has a deadline much earlier than the examination. By the time a parent is worried about a grade in the final terms, the ceiling may already be fixed. In The Valley this is worth asking about explicitly, because children here attend several different schools whose entry timetables differ, and a neighbour's reassurance about when decisions are made carries no information about your own child's school.

The honest advice is to have the conversation in Year 10 rather than Year 11, and to ask two questions: what tier is my child currently expected to be entered for, and what specifically would need to change for the higher tier to be realistic. Those are answerable questions with a timeline attached. The table below sets out what each tier implies so that the conversation starts from the same facts the school is working from rather than from a parent's impression of what a tier means.

sections.heading: The command words that decide bands
paragraphs: More IGCSE marks are lost to command words than to gaps in knowledge, and this is the cheapest thing on the whole page to fix. Mark schemes award a specific shape of response per command word. A student who describes when the question said explain has answered a different question, and the overlap earns nothing. The words are published by both boards, they are consistent across subjects, and they can be learned properly in a handful of sessions rather than over a term.

The students most vulnerable are the articulate ones. Fluency disguises the problem: a well-written paragraph that states rather than gives a reason reads convincingly and scores in the middle band, so neither the student nor the parent can see why the mark is what it is. The correction is mechanical rather than literary. Underline the command word, write the mark allocation beside it, and produce exactly the structure that word requires before writing anything else.

The table below covers the words that cost the most marks in the subjects Valley families ask about, with the error that recurs in each. Both boards publish full definitions in their specifications and your child's teacher can provide them; we reference those documents rather than reproducing them, because they are the boards' copyright. The useful habit for a student is to keep the list beside them while working through past papers rather than reading it once and assuming it has been absorbed.

sections.heading: The components that cannot be revised by reading
paragraphs: Some parts of an IGCSE cannot be prepared by rereading notes, and those are precisely the parts students neglect. The practical skills paper in the sciences is the clearest case: in both boards' international specifications it is assessed on a written paper rather than in a laboratory, and it asks for variable identification, apparatus reading, method criticism, results tables and graph work. There is nothing to highlight and no notes to reread, so it gets skipped by almost everybody.

The same applies to the speaking and listening components in Cambridge English as a Second Language, to ICT's practical skills examination, and to extended writing tasks in English Language, where the skill is matching register to a stated audience rather than recalling content. All of these improve through repetition against the official question types, and all of them are heavily patterned, which means a student who has worked twenty examples recognises almost everything the paper can ask.

The practical consequence is a planning one. If a family has a limited number of tutored hours, these components usually give the best return, because they are both under-practised and highly repetitive. A four to six session block on the science practical paper raises marks across all three sciences at once. sections.heading: Reading a marked paper properly
paragraphs: A marked paper is the most useful document a family has and it is usually read for the wrong information. The score at the top says very little; the distribution of the losses says almost everything. Four lost marks on method, three on command words and one on arithmetic is a plan for the next month. Sixty-one per cent is a feeling. The first thing any session here does is convert the former into the latter's replacement.

The classification we use has five categories: content not known, command word misread, method not shown, arithmetic slip, and ran out of time. Each has a different fix and a different timescale. Content needs teaching, topic by topic. Command words need two weeks of enforcement. Method needs two to four weeks of enforcement, because it is a habit rather than a misunderstanding. Arithmetic needs fluency drilling over four to eight weeks. Timing needs full papers under the clock.

Parents can do this themselves, and we would rather they did, because it makes the first conversation precise. Go through the marked paper with the student and write beside each lost mark which of those five categories it belongs to. The pattern that emerges is usually obvious and often surprising: students who describe themselves as bad at a subject are frequently losing most of their marks to two habits that have nothing to do with the subject at all, which is a considerably more cheerful diagnosis than the one they arrived with.

sections.heading: What subject tuition costs here, and what a diagnosis costs
paragraphs: The band a distance-sorted list never shows you is the one travel creates. In-home visits in Dubai are published at AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, and The Valley sits at the far end of most tutors' drive, so the upper half of that range is the realistic one here rather than the lower. Teaching live online removes the charge entirely: a qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150. Below that, budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. Above it, specialists in IGCSE and A Level are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The gap between the cheapest online hour and the dearest home visit is better than fifteenfold, and not one dirham of it is explained by who happens to live closest to you.

For IGCSE subject work the qualified online tier is usually the right purchase, because the work is diagnosis and enforcement rather than rare expertise. The more useful framing for a family is the cost of finding out versus the cost of a term. Two or three diagnostic sessions at the mid-market rate is a small fraction of a term's weekly tutoring, and it answers the question most families spend a whole term guessing at: which subject, which paper, which habit.

Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Every figure here belongs to the company or rate guide that published it and was read in October 2026. IB Gram publishes no hourly list on these pages and quotes after a free trial, for the specific subject, board and tier.

sections.heading: Coursework, materials and the boundaries that matter
paragraphs: Where a subject carries assessed work completed outside the examination hall, the boundary has to be explicit. Submitted work must be the student's own and is authenticated by the school, and a submission that is not is a malpractice matter whose consequences fall on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. One operation in this market sells completed internal assessments for a different qualification at AED 3,750, which establishes both that the trade exists and what it costs.

What a tutor may legitimately do is teach the content a task draws on, explain the assessment criteria, question whether a method is reproducible, point out a conclusion that outruns its evidence, and comment on writing the student produced. What a tutor may not do is write any part of a submission, redraft a paragraph into final form, select and carry out an investigation, or supply a model to be edited. Our test is whether a sentence in the final piece exists because a tutor wrote it.

Materials are the second boundary. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright. We reference them, cite the official sources, and work from material your child's school legitimately holds, with questions shown on screen during sessions. Any service advertising an unlimited paper bank invites a fair question about provenance, and the school's own holdings are in any case the papers your child will be marked against.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In 2024-25 that covered 227 private schools and 387,441 students across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the following academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Two further facts are worth a parent's attention. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited; instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. And the emirate determines the regulator: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

On our own position: IB Gram holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, no ADEK or Ministry approval, no Cambridge or Pearson partnership, and no office, branch or centre in the UAE. An individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years; those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted online with suspicion.

faqs.question: Does proximity matter at all when choosing an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Much less than the specification does, and in The Valley it barely matters at all. There is no school inside this community at the time of writing, so there is no local cohort and no school-gate network passing on subject-specific recommendations. A proximity search returns a short list here, and a short list is not a shortlist. What decides whether a grade moves is whether the tutor teaches your child's exact syllabus code and tier, which is why IB Gram matches on specification and delivers one-to-one online.

faqs.question: Which command words cost IGCSE students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain, suggest and evaluate, in roughly that order. Explain requires a reason or mechanism and students routinely describe the effect instead, earning the description marks and none of the explanation ones. Suggest requires an applied answer to an unfamiliar context, and students supply a recalled textbook answer that does not fit. Evaluate requires a judgement weighed against evidence, so a list of advantages and disadvantages without a conclusion caps the band. All three are correctable in a handful of sessions, which makes them the cheapest marks available.

faqs.question: How is a tier decided and can it be changed later?
faqs.answer: The school decides the entry against the board's deadline, usually informed by internal Year 10 results, and once entries are made it is not adjustable on the day. Cambridge Core caps the achievable grade while Extended reaches the top bands; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher tiers in some subjects. That means a family wanting to keep the higher tier open has a deadline well before the examination. Ask the examinations officer what tier your child is expected to be entered for and what would need to change.

faqs.question: Our daughter writes well but keeps scoring in the middle band. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always command words rather than writing ability, and fluency is what hides it. A well-constructed paragraph that states a position without giving a reason reads convincingly and scores in the middle band, so neither student nor parent can see the cause. Mark schemes award a specific shape of response per command word. The correction is mechanical: underline the command word, write the mark allocation beside it, and produce exactly that structure. It is one of the fastest improvements available at this level.

faqs.question: What should we actually look at on a marked paper?
faqs.answer: The distribution of the losses rather than the score. Go through the paper and write beside each lost mark which of five categories it belongs to: content not known, command word misread, method not shown, arithmetic slip, or ran out of time. Four method marks and three command-word marks is a plan for the month; sixty-one per cent is a feeling. Parents can do this themselves in about fifteen minutes, and it frequently shows that a student who feels bad at a subject is losing marks to two habits.

faqs.question: Why is the science practical paper worth tutoring separately?
faqs.answer: Because it is examined on a written paper in both boards' international specifications, it is heavily patterned, and almost nobody practises it, since there is nothing to re-read. It asks for variable identification, apparatus reading, method criticism with stated effects, results tables with correct units, and graph work. The same question shapes recur across series, so a student who works twenty past questions recognises nearly everything it can ask. A four to six session block on it raises marks across all three sciences at once.

faqs.question: Is English as a Second Language easier than English Language?
faqs.answer: It is a different qualification rather than an easier one, with its own papers including listening and speaking components, and an incorrect entry costs far more than a few marks. Accuracy outranks ambitious vocabulary throughout, and the speaking component needs rehearsal rather than revision, which students rarely do because it cannot be practised silently. Confirm with the examinations officer which qualification your child is entered for, because the preparation differs substantially and the past papers are not interchangeable.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to fix unwritten method?
faqs.answer: Two to four weeks of enforcement rather than an explanation, because it is a habit and not a misunderstanding. Most students already understand the point when told; what changes behaviour is a tutor declining to assess an answer that arrives with no working above it, week after week, until writing method becomes automatic. Over a two-hour paper the difference is routinely worth several marks, and several marks is frequently a grade boundary, which makes this the cheapest single improvement in mathematics and physics.

faqs.question: What does a diagnosis cost compared with a term of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Two or three diagnostic sessions at the published mid-market online rate of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour is a small fraction of a term's weekly tutoring, and it answers the question most families otherwise spend a whole term guessing at: which subject, which paper, which habit. We would rather sell the diagnosis than the guess. Those rates were read in October 2026 and belong to the companies that published them; we quote after a free trial for your child's specific subject, board and tier.

faqs.question: Can sessions happen at the weekend rather than after school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this community they often should. There is no school inside The Valley, so every run is outbound and a secondary student is realistically home around a quarter past five. Whole papers, mark-scheme review and practical paper work all need uninterrupted time, which genuinely exists only at the weekend here. One weekday evening hour for content plus a weekend block for papers is the structure that lasts a full term in a Valley household.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to The Valley for a subject lesson?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with questions on screen and a shared whiteboard where working appears as it is written. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. For IGCSE subject work the format costs very little, because the diagnostic information a tutor needs is the line where the student hesitates, which is visible either way.

faqs.question: Our son is strong in biology and weak in chemistry and physics. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Usually that the cause is arithmetic rather than three separate content problems. Chemistry and physics both carry calculation, rearranging, prefixes and significant figures, while biology carries terminology and volume. A student who holds up in biology and drifts in the other two is almost always losing marks to the mathematics inside science, and one engagement on that fixes two subjects at once. It is worth confirming from marked papers in all three before committing to anything.

faqs.question: Do you cover geography and history as well as the sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the work is different in kind. Those subjects are decided by source handling and case-study specificity: students lose marks describing a source rather than using it as evidence, and offering generic examples where the mark scheme expected a named, dated case study. The fix is building a small bank of precise case studies and practising source questions against the official mark schemes. Coverage is strongest in the mainstream Cambridge specifications; if we cannot match a particular option we will say so.

faqs.question: How soon will we see marks move?
faqs.answer: For command-word and method causes, about three to four weeks, because the change appears directly in the next marked paper. For arithmetic fluency, four to eight weeks, since it improves through repetition. Genuine content gaps take one to three weeks per topic. Each session note records which error classes appeared rather than which topics were covered, so the trend sits in the record. We publish no improvement statistics, because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method is not evidence.

faqs.question: Why does this page not name the best tutor in the area?
faqs.answer: Because there is no honest way to do it and the phrase would be a claim we could not support. What we can publish is checkable: the syllabus codes, what each paper assesses, the command words that cost marks, AED figures with their publisher and the month read, and a statement of what we hold no approval for. Several providers in this market publish self-asserted ratings that contradict their own page text. A page that shows its working is more useful than one that asserts a ranking.

intro.heading: The real question behind "does anyone near me know this syllabus?"
paragraphs: Families in The Views are usually one or two years into a British-curriculum school before they discover that "IGCSE" is not one qualification. It is a family of specifications issued by competing awarding bodies. Cambridge International runs its own suite, identified by four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSEs with codes like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. OxfordAQA runs a third suite. Two children in neighbouring apartments in Panorama or Turia can both be sitting IGCSE Maths next summer and be preparing for papers that differ in tier structure, calculator rules and grade range.

That is why the honest answer to "is there an IGCSE tutor near me" is a question back: which code does your child sit? A tutor who taught Cambridge Extended Mathematics for a decade is a strong match for a 0580 candidate and a weaker one for a Higher tier 4MA1 candidate until they have worked through that specification's own past papers. The mismatch rarely shows up in the first session, because the content overlaps heavily. It shows up in the mock, when the student meets a paper structured differently from the one they practised.

The supply problem follows from that. The Views is a compact community of apartment clusters overlooking the Emirates Golf Club fairways. Its secondary students travel out to schools in Emirates Hills, Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and The Meadows, and between those schools you will find Cambridge centres, Pearson centres and some that enter candidates with both depending on the department. Finding a specification-matched specialist for Chemistry, Economics and Second Language English inside a twenty-minute radius, free at 7pm, is not a realistic expectation of any neighbourhood.

IB Gram answers it by removing distance from the equation. Every lesson for a UAE family runs live, one-to-one, over video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Saying that in the fourth paragraph rather than the fortieth is deliberate, because the alternative is a parent assuming someone is coming. What replaces the drive is a tutor chosen for the code on the statement of entry, with the past paper, the mark scheme and the student's own script on a shared screen.

The rest of this page is written to make you dangerous in a parents' evening. It shows how to read the specification code off your child's own documents, what Core and Extended and Foundation and Higher actually cap, where marks go on each paper type, how far ahead the entry deadline sits, what the Ministry of Education's equivalency rule really requires, and what the Dubai market charges for an IGCSE hour in dirhams, with each figure attributed to whoever published it.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.programmesIntro: Two routes dominate this catchment and a third sits underneath them. Which one your child is on determines what a tutor should be doing in Year 10 and Year 11, and the three are assessed in genuinely different ways.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge issues each subject its own four-digit syllabus number and publishes the full specification, assessment structure and past papers openly. Most subjects are tiered: a Core route with a capped grade range and an Extended route reaching the top grades. Sciences add a practical component, either a laboratory test or a written alternative, which changes how a tutor should prepare a student.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your Dubai school which zone it sits in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson codes its International GCSEs differently, with Mathematics A as 4MA1 and the sciences as 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Tiering is Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, the grade scale is numerical, and the assessment design differs paper by paper. Some Pearson subjects also allow a different entry pattern from the Cambridge equivalent, which affects how a two-year course is sequenced.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson offers International GCSE exams in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so plan from the live PDF.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and the run-up to Year 10
programmes.description: The years before IGCSE are where the gap that shows up in Year 11 is usually created. Algebraic fluency, scientific explanation and extended writing are all built here, and none of them is examined, so weakness is easy to miss. A diagnostic in Year 9 is cheaper and more useful than a rescue in Year 11, and it also informs the tier decision the school will make.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. For a Views family that means the timetable carries more subjects than the IGCSE subject count suggests, which matters when planning a week.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects The Views families ask for most, with the code in each of the two main suites and the part of the course where marks go missing. Sessions are built from your child's own marked scripts against the published mark scheme.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The current 0580 assessment design separates a non-calculator paper from a calculator paper, which catches out students who have practised everything with a handheld. Pearson 4MA1 sits two papers of equal weight. Most lost marks are arithmetic fluency, incomplete working on method marks, and algebraic manipulation that was never secured in Year 9.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 candidates sit either a practical test or a written alternative to practical, and the alternative is a technique in its own right: reading apparatus diagrams, spotting control variables, and explaining a method without having performed it. Electricity and the equations of motion are where most students in this catchment lose marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables are the recurring failures. The practical or alternative-to-practical component asks for precise observation language, not general description. Students who can recite the reactivity series still drop marks explaining why a particular displacement happens.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A terminology subject that punishes approximation. Marks are lost on command terms, on describing where an explanation was asked for, and on data questions where a trend is stated without reference to the figures. Work usually starts by annotating the student's own script against the published mark scheme wording.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis of an unseen passage reward structure over style. Strong talkers underperform because they narrate instead of analysing, and because they do not budget the time the paper actually gives them. Sessions drill a repeatable reading method and a timed writing plan.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A large entry across Dubai schools and a different skill set from First Language English. Listening and speaking components carry real weight, and the written tasks are assessed against format conventions as much as language. The commonest avoidable loss is ignoring the register and audience the task specifies.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the mark. Unlabelled axes, shifts drawn in the wrong direction and evaluation paragraphs that repeat the analysis account for most dropped marks. The data-response question rewards students who quote the figures given rather than recalling general theory.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Easy to learn and hard to apply under timed conditions. Students lose marks by describing a business tool rather than applying it to the case study in front of them, and by skipping the justification that higher-tariff questions require. Case-study drill with a stopwatch moves grades faster than more content.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or an IB Higher Level course, and often taught in a thin slot alongside the main maths option. Calculus and trigonometric identities are where the course gets steep. A tutor here is usually filling the time the school timetable could not give the subject.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. Schools must also ensure teachers of these subjects hold the appropriate KHDA approval, which is worth knowing when comparing in-school and private provision.

sections.heading: How to read your child's specification code in five minutes
paragraphs: Before buying a single hour, establish what your child is actually sitting. There are four reliable places to look. The statement of entry the school issues before each series lists the awarding body, the syllabus or specification code and the component numbers. A school report or subject handbook usually prints the code next to the subject name. The department head will confirm it in one email. And the student's own past-paper practice carries the code in the header, which is often the fastest route of all.

Once you have the code, the awarding body's own site gives you the rest free of charge. Cambridge publishes the full syllabus for each four-digit number, including the assessment structure, the component weightings and which papers a Core or Extended candidate sits. Pearson does the same for its International GCSE specifications. Nothing on this page should be taken in preference to those documents for your child's own exam year, because specifications are revised and a structure that applied two years ago may not apply now.

The table below lines up the two main suites side by side for the subjects this catchment takes most. Its purpose is not to say which body is better. It is to show you that the difference is real, so that a tutor who shrugs when you say 4MA1 can be ruled out in the first minute of a conversation. If a provider cannot name the code they have taught, the specialism being sold is generic.

One practical warning about Cambridge timetables. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. Dubai schools know their zone. Parents planning revision from a timetable found through a search engine sometimes do not, and that is an avoidable way to lose a paper.

sections.heading: Tiering: the grade ceiling that is set before revision starts
paragraphs: Tiering is the single most consequential decision in an IGCSE year and the one parents in The Views are least often shown the arithmetic for. In tiered Cambridge subjects, a Core entry sits different papers from an Extended entry and cannot reach the top grades. In Pearson Mathematics A, a Foundation entry has a numerical ceiling and a Higher entry has a floor below which no grade is awarded except a narrow allowance. The entry is made months before the exam, and once it is made the ceiling is fixed regardless of how well the student then works.

Schools make the tier decision on evidence, usually a Year 10 mock and classwork. The decision is not arbitrary and it is not an insult. A student entered Extended who cannot complete the harder paper will score poorly on it and may finish below where a confident Core performance would have landed them. The error runs both ways, though, and the one that causes lasting damage is the capped entry made because a student had a bad term in Year 10 rather than because the ceiling is genuinely right for them.

This is where a specification-matched tutor earns the fee rather than by teaching extra content. The useful work is to find out, by the autumn of Year 10, which tier the evidence supports, and then either secure the higher tier in time for the entry deadline or make the capped entry deliberately rather than by default. That requires someone who can mark a script against the right mark scheme and say what the ceiling realistically is. It cannot be done in March of Year 11.

Ask the school two questions in writing. Which tier is my child currently projected for, and what evidence is that based on. And when is the entry deadline, after which the decision cannot change. Those two answers reframe the whole tutoring question, because they convert a vague worry about grades into a dated decision with a measurable target.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost, paper by paper
paragraphs: Marks are not lost evenly across a specification. They cluster in a handful of predictable places, and a tutor who knows the paper can name them before meeting the student. In mathematics, the losses are arithmetic fluency on the non-calculator paper, method marks forfeited because working was not shown, and algebra that was never secure in Year 9 reappearing inside a trigonometry or a functions question. None of those is fixed by covering more topics.

In the sciences, the single largest avoidable loss is the practical component. A Cambridge 0625 or 0620 candidate sitting the written alternative to practical is being assessed on experimental reasoning without a bench: reading an apparatus diagram, identifying the control variable, explaining why a step was done in that order, and judging the reliability of someone else's data. Students who are good at the theory frequently treat this paper as an afterthought and lose a block of marks on skills nobody taught them explicitly.

In the essay and data subjects the loss is command terms. Describe, explain, compare, evaluate and justify ask for structurally different answers, and the mark scheme awards accordingly. A student who writes an excellent description where an explanation was required has produced good prose and few marks. This is diagnosable in twenty minutes from a marked script, which is why we ask for one before quoting anything.

The fourth cluster is timing. Most IGCSE papers are generous in content and tight in minutes, and a student who answers the first third beautifully and the last third in a rush has a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem. Timed practice with a real clock, marked against the real scheme, exposes it immediately. Doing it under a tutor's eye is worth more than doing it alone, because the student cannot see where their own minutes went.

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the exam
paragraphs: Parents routinely discover the entry calendar after it has closed. Awarding bodies need entries, forecast grades and component choices long before candidates sit anything, and the school's own internal deadline runs earlier still. In the UAE a Cambridge candidate has two sittings, June and November, and the June entry closes in the spring, months ahead of the papers, with the exact date printed on the statement of entry the centre issues. Forecast grades are then due on Cambridge's own published deadline for that series, results reach the centre on Cambridge Direct once marking closes, and certificates follow later again. Read that sequence in order and the point is unmissable: the decision that fixes the tier is taken while the candidate is still months from the exam hall, and no amount of revision reopens it.

Pearson's pattern is similar in shape. Pearson offers International GCSE exams in May or June and in November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why the live PDF on the awarding body's site, rather than a date restated on a tutoring page, is the only safe thing to plan against.

What this means operationally is that the useful tutoring conversation happens in the term before the entry, not in the term before the exam. Tier decisions, whether to add or drop a subject, whether to sit a subject in November rather than June, and whether a private-candidate entry is needed, are all live questions at the entry deadline and dead questions afterwards. A family that knows the date can act; a family that does not simply inherits whatever the default was.

Three dates belong on the fridge. The school's internal entry deadline, which comes first. The awarding body's final entry deadline. And the results date for the series, because an enquiry about results or a remark has its own short window after it. Ask the examinations officer for all three in writing at the start of Year 11.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E: what MoE equivalency actually requires
paragraphs: This is the gap in the market that costs families real money in misplaced effort, because one page ranking for these searches publishes the wrong number. Gulf Today's report on the UAE's clarified equivalency requirements states that British-track students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion. The same report states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A student carrying seven IGCSEs of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has five counting subjects only if the other five all clear the threshold. That is a planning fact worth knowing in Year 9, when subject options are chosen, rather than in the summer after results when the certificate is being submitted for attestation.

For the American track the same report gives a different test: English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is stated in that article, and none should be taken from any tutoring page, including this one. Anything about IB equivalency has to be read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed with the attestation authority directly.

Two boundaries matter here. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry of Education and the relevant authority run, not something a tutoring platform performs or can promise. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression; any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. What a tutor can legitimately do is help a student clear a grade threshold in a counting subject, which is a teaching job with a measurable target.

sections.heading: Why a code-matched specialist beats a nearby generalist
paragraphs: Put the two options side by side honestly. A generalist within a twenty-minute drive of The Views offers continuity, the ability to read the room, and a parent who can see the lesson happening. Those are real advantages and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. What the generalist typically cannot offer is familiarity with the specific paper: the way 0580 splits calculator and non-calculator work, the way an alternative-to-practical question is marked, the exact phrase a mark scheme wants for an explanation mark in 0610.

The specialist's advantage compounds over a two-year course. Knowing the paper changes what gets practised, which changes the mock, which changes the tier decision, which changes the grade ceiling. It also changes how quickly a problem is identified: a tutor who has marked a hundred scripts against the same scheme sees in one page what a generalist might take three sessions to find. Over a Year 10 and Year 11 that difference is worth considerably more than the drive time saved.

Online delivery is what makes the specialist option available at all to a community this size. It also brings its own practical gains inside the hour: the student's own marked script, the official specification page and the past paper open side by side, annotated live and saved for later. Nothing is photographed and emailed afterwards, and the student keeps their own calculator and their own notes, which are the ones they will take into the hall.

The honest conditions for online to work are the same three every time. A stable connection, a door that closes, and a laptop rather than a phone. In an apartment with siblings and a shared table, the third is the one that fails. Solve it before the first lesson. And for the sciences, be clear about what online cannot replace: the school's laboratory. A tutor can teach experimental reasoning and the alternative-to-practical paper thoroughly, but bench time belongs to the school.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE hour costs in Dubai, and what it should include
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible pages competing for IGCSE searches in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. The figures below are AED market rates drawn from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, each attributed. They are not an IB Gram price list. Our position is a free trial lesson first and a quoted rate once the specification, the tier and the target are known, because an hour of Higher tier 4MA1 technique is a different product from an hour of Year 8 support.

What should the hour include at each band? At the budget end, content re-explained competently by someone who knows the material. That is fair value for a Year 8 or 9 student who missed a topic and poor value for a Year 11 candidate three months from a paper. At the qualified band, syllabus-aware teaching and marking. At the specialist band, assessment technique against the published criteria, with the tier conversation included. The premium band is bought mainly in the final weeks, and what it buys is judgement about what to leave out.

The money that gets wasted in this catchment usually goes the same three ways. Hours bought before anyone looked at a marked script, so the first sessions are spent on diagnosis. Group classes bought for a tiered subject, where the whole point of the hour is that the questions are the student's own. And a long weekly commitment started in Year 10 that has burned out by the spring of Year 11, exactly when the mock evidence and the tier decision needed attention.

Ask three questions before paying anyone. Which specification code have you taught, and for how many series. What will the first session produce in writing. And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which u.ae records as introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The permit costs nothing, so there is no honest expense-based reason not to hold one.

sections.heading: Private candidates, retakes and sitting in November
paragraphs: Not every IGCSE candidate in Dubai sits through their own school. Students who have moved mid-course, who want a subject their school does not offer, who are retaking a single paper, or who are being educated outside a school roll, enter as private candidates through a centre that accepts them. That is a logistical process with its own deadlines, and it sits with the centre and the awarding body rather than with a tutor. What matters here is knowing that it exists and that it has dates.

The November series is the quiet tool most families never consider. Both main bodies run two series a year, so a subject that went wrong in the summer can often be re-sat a few months later rather than waiting a full year, and a crowded subject load can sometimes be split across two sittings. Whether that is sensible depends on the subject, the school's policy and the student's wider timetable, and the honest answer is sometimes no. But it is a conversation worth having before the entry deadline rather than after results day.

Retakes need a clear-eyed diagnosis to be worth the fee. A grade that missed by a narrow margin because of timing or one weak paper is a good retake candidate. A grade that reflects a genuine content gap across the whole specification needs a longer run of teaching, not a second attempt in ten weeks. The way to tell the difference is to read the component breakdown rather than the overall grade, and that breakdown is available to the school.

For any of these routes the first call is the school's examinations officer, then the awarding body's own guidance for private candidates. faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE specification my child's school actually enters?
faqs.answer: Four places give you the answer within minutes. The statement of entry the school issues before each series names the awarding body, the syllabus code and the components. School reports and subject handbooks usually print the code beside the subject. The department head will confirm it by email. And your child's own past-paper practice carries the code in the header. Once you have it, the full specification is free on the awarding body's own site, which is the document to plan from for your child's exam year rather than anything restated elsewhere.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE tutor near me in The Views who knows the exact paper?
faqs.answer: Within a twenty-minute drive, not reliably across every subject. The Views is a compact cluster of apartment towers, and a specification-matched specialist for Chemistry, Economics and Second Language English who is also free at 7pm is not something a community of this size contains. IB Gram solves it by matching on the code and delivering lessons live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What is the practical difference between Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: They are separate specifications with separate papers. Cambridge 0580 uses Core and Extended tiering and its current design separates a non-calculator paper from a calculator paper. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher tiering with two equally weighted papers and a numerical grade scale. Content overlaps heavily, which is why a mismatch does not show up in early sessions, but paper structure, tier language and calculator rules differ. Check the current specification on the awarding body's site for your child's exam year before planning any revision.

faqs.question: Does a Core or Foundation entry cap the grade my child can be awarded?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the point of tiering. A Cambridge Core entry sits different papers from an Extended entry and cannot reach the top grades. A Pearson Foundation entry in Mathematics A has a numerical ceiling. The entry is made months before the paper and cannot be changed afterwards, so the decision deserves evidence rather than a default. Ask the school in writing which tier your child is projected for, what evidence supports it, and when the entry deadline falls, then work from those two answers.

faqs.question: Why does my child suddenly have a maths paper without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Because the current Cambridge 0580 assessment design separates non-calculator work from calculator work, so arithmetic and algebraic fluency are examined in their own right. Students who practised every topic with a handheld meet that paper cold and lose marks on operations they can do but have not done unaided for years. The fix is short, regular, unaided practice rather than more topics. Confirm the exact paper structure for your child's exam year on the Cambridge syllabus page, because specifications are revised between cohorts.

faqs.question: Can my child sit subjects with two different awarding bodies at once?
faqs.answer: In practice, yes, and it happens routinely in Dubai schools where departments choose independently. A student might sit Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics in the same series. It is the school's entry decision rather than the family's, and it has a consequence worth knowing: the student is preparing for two different mark-scheme cultures at the same time. A tutor should be told both codes rather than being left to assume one body covers the whole timetable.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the exam do IGCSE entries close?
faqs.answer: Months, and the school's internal deadline comes earlier still. Pearson's published dates are the clearest illustration: the November 2026 International GCSE papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry that fixed the subject list for them had closed in the preceding summer. Cambridge is the same in shape for the two series a UAE candidate can enter, with June entries closing in the spring and November entries over the preceding summer, on dates printed on the centre's statement of entry. Ask your examinations officer for the school's internal date, the awarding body's final date and the results date, in writing, at the start of Year 11.

faqs.question: How is the science practical assessed if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The assessment itself happens through the school. Cambridge science candidates sit either a practical test or a written alternative to practical, and the alternative is examined on experimental reasoning rather than bench skill: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying control variables, explaining why a step was ordered that way, judging the reliability of supplied data. All of that can be taught thoroughly over a shared screen using past papers and mark schemes. What cannot be replaced remotely is laboratory time, and that belongs with the school.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE actually count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. Gulf Today's report on the clarified requirements states that British-track students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, alongside one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One page ranking in this market publishes six, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before relying on it, because this is a regulatory process rather than something a tutor administers.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the five subjects in The Views?
faqs.answer: No. The same report states plainly that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That has a real planning consequence: a student holding seven IGCSEs, two of which are Arabic and Islamic Education, only meets the requirement if the remaining five all clear the threshold. It is a Year 9 options conversation rather than a results-day discovery. Dubai schools must still teach these subjects under KHDA rules regardless of the licensed curriculum, so they will be on the timetable either way.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do students in this catchment struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at the tier boundary, the science practical and alternative-to-practical papers, and Second Language English where the task format carries as much weight as the language. In mathematics the problem is usually Year 9 algebra resurfacing inside later topics. In the sciences it is a paper nobody taught explicitly. In English it is ignoring the register and audience the task specifies. All three are visible from one marked script, which is why we ask for one before quoting anything.

faqs.question: Is Year 10 or Year 11 the better time to start?
faqs.answer: Year 10, by a wide margin, because that is when the tier decision is still open and the entry deadline has not passed. A Year 10 start means no topic is met for the first time under exam pressure and the tier is chosen on evidence. Year 11 is still worth doing, but the work changes: it becomes paper technique, timing and triage built from marked mocks rather than a build through the specification. A single-subject rescue after a bad mock is a legitimate and common reason to start late.

faqs.question: What should a tutor know about my child's school before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things. The awarding body and specification code for each subject. The tier the school currently projects. The internal assessment and mock calendar, because a session three weeks before a mock should look different from one in October. And the Cambridge administrative zone if the school is a Cambridge centre, since Cambridge states that using the correct zone timetable is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE hour in Dubai cost, and what should it include?
faqs.answer: Market rates published by providers and in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table run roughly AED 45-150 for budget online tutoring, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200-450 and above for an IGCSE or IB specialist, and AED 500-650 at the premium end, with in-home visits quoted at AED 180-500. Those are the market's numbers, not ours. At the specialist band the hour should include marking against the published scheme and an explicit view on tier. IB Gram quotes after a free trial, once the code and target are known.

faqs.question: Can my child retake one paper in the November series?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, because both main awarding bodies run two series a year, which makes a re-sit a few months later possible rather than a full year's wait. Whether it is sensible depends on why the grade fell short. A near miss caused by timing or one weak component is a reasonable retake; a gap running across the whole specification needs teaching rather than a second attempt in ten weeks. Read the component breakdown with the school, and talk to the examinations officer about entry routes early.
