intro.heading: Six providers, one search box
paragraphs: The results for an IGCSE tutor near me in Tilal Al Ghaf mix together six business models that have almost nothing in common. There are agencies that place a tutor and take a margin. Marketplaces that list independents and leave the vetting to you. Freelancers you find through a community group. Tuition centres with premises and group classes. Your child's own school, which usually runs intervention sessions at no extra cost. And online one-to-one providers, including this one. They differ on price by a factor of ten, on accountability almost completely, and on what happens when a tutor turns out to be wrong for your child.

Nobody compares them honestly, because every provider's comparison is written to win. The six-row table further down this page compares them on criteria you can actually check: the rate with its published source, whether a permit can be produced, whether you meet the tutor before paying, what the replacement process is, and whether anything is free to try. Where IB Gram scores badly on a row, the row says so, because a comparison that flatters its author is not information.

Tilal Al Ghaf is a useful place to make this argument, because the community removes the variable that usually dominates. There is a school inside the boundary, and DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City next door have their own provision, so the school run is short and pupils are often home before four. Travel time, which in most Dubailand villa communities decides which tutors are even available, is not the binding constraint here. What is left is the question of which model gives you a tutor who knows the specification and will still be there in eight weeks.

Before any of that, one piece of information has to be established, and it is the same regardless of which model you choose. Ask your child's exams officer for the awarding body, the syllabus code and the tier, in writing. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1; they tier differently and, in mathematics, differ on calculator access. A tutor from any of the six models who is working from the wrong specification will teach well and leave your child unprepared.

Most Dubai schools run subject intervention or clinic sessions for pupils who are behind, included in fees that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year. Those sessions are taught by the person who will mark your child's mock and who wrote the scheme of work. For a pupil whose problem is keeping up rather than a specific diagnosed gap, that is frequently the correct first move, and it costs nothing.

sections.heading: The free option, and when it is the right one
paragraphs: Almost every Dubai school runs some form of subject intervention: a clinic before or after school, a lunchtime session, a targeted group for pupils below expectation. It is included in fees that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. No tutoring company has an incentive to tell you about it, so it is worth stating clearly.

The school's intervention has two advantages no external provider can match. It is taught by the person who wrote the scheme of work and will mark your child's mock, so it is guaranteed to be on the right specification at the right tier. And it is free. For a pupil whose difficulty is keeping up with the pace rather than a specific diagnosed gap, that combination is hard to beat, and a family who pays for external tutoring without first asking what the school offers has skipped the obvious step.

Where it falls short is individual diagnosis. An intervention group is organised around content the department judges the group needs, which may not be where your child's marks are actually going. If a marked mock shows losses concentrated in method, units, command terms and timing rather than in content, no amount of content reteaching will touch them, and a group cannot stop to work on one pupil's habits. That is the case in which one-to-one earns its rate.

So the sequence we would recommend, against our own commercial interest, is: ask the school what intervention exists and put your child in it; get the most recent mock marked properly with losses categorised; and only then decide whether an external tutor is addressing something the school is not. Families who do that in Year 10 frequently need no external tutoring at all, and the ones who do need it arrive with a clear brief.

sections.heading: Group class or one-to-one: read the mock to decide
paragraphs: The group-against-individual question is usually answered by budget, and it should be answered by the shape of the losses. A marked mock paper tells you which, and the test is simple enough to apply yourself.

If lost marks are spread fairly evenly across the paper, with no topic conspicuously worse than the rest, the problem is coverage and pace. The pupil has met everything and consolidated none of it. That is exactly what a group class does well: more exposure, more practice, more questions worked at a manageable speed, at a fraction of the one-to-one rate. Paying individual rates for that is paying a premium for attention the pupil does not specifically need.

If lost marks cluster — three or four topics accounting for most of the deficit, or one paper much weaker than the other, or a pattern of method and unit errors running through everything — a group will not touch it. A group cannot pause on one pupil's sign errors for twenty minutes, and it cannot run a session on the alternative-to-practical paper because two of the twelve pupils present never sat one. Clustered losses are the case for one-to-one.

There is a third pattern worth naming: a paper with large sections unattempted. That is a timing and pacing problem, and it is the cheapest of all to fix because it needs practice under a clock rather than teaching. It can be addressed with a tutor, with school intervention or alone with a timer and a mark scheme, and a family should not pay specialist rates for something a disciplined fortnight would solve.

sections.heading: Why the nearest tutor still needs checking
paragraphs: Even in a community where distance is not the constraint, a local recommendation carries a specific risk in this part of Dubai. Tilal Al Ghaf pupils attend the school inside the community, schools in DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City, and a spread of others across Dubailand and Al Barsha South. Those schools do not all use the same awarding body, and in the sciences they do not all enter the same award.

So the tutor who taught your neighbour's child superbly may have no working knowledge of the specification your own child sits. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry is 0620 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry is 4CH1; they examine similar chemistry with different paper structures. In mathematics the difference is sharper still, because Edexcel permits a calculator in both papers while Cambridge's current structure pairs a non-calculator paper with a calculator one. A tutor who has only ever prepared Edexcel candidates has never had to take a calculator off a desk.

The check costs one email and two minutes. Get the board, code and tier in writing from the exams officer, then ask any candidate tutor to describe the papers for that code: how many, how long, what each covers, whether a calculator is permitted. The answer is either specific or it is not, and that single question sorts this market faster than any amount of reading reviews.

The same question works across all six models. An agency should be able to confirm which of its tutors teaches that code. A marketplace profile should state it. A tuition centre should be able to say which board its class follows, and if the class mixes boards you should know that before enrolling. Your child's school teacher obviously knows. And an online provider has no excuse for not asking you the question in the first place.

sections.heading: How to verify any provider, in order
paragraphs: This is the section that makes the rest of the page usable, because a comparison is only worth having if you can test the claims. Each of these checks costs nothing and takes minutes, and together they eliminate most of what goes wrong in this market.

Start with the permit, because it is free to hold and therefore free to produce. Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance. Then ask the specification question above. Then ask who will teach every session: a named individual, or whoever is available that week. Rotating tutors are workable for homework supervision and useless for a Year 11 repair block, because the first ten minutes of every session go on rediscovering where the pupil is.

Then ask what the first session will produce. 'We will get to know each other' is a weak answer for a paid hour; 'a marked paper and a list of where the marks went' is a strong one. Then ask what you will receive after each session. A written note the same day is checkable. A monthly summary is not, and it conceals stalled sessions for three weeks longer than a weekly note would.

Finally, two things to ask whose answers should make you walk away. Any guarantee of a specific grade or improvement, which nobody can control and which no legitimate provider offers. And any claim of approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson without a permit number to show. IB Gram holds none of those, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai rather than something a tutoring brand can imply.

paragraphs: Hourly rates are not comparable across models, because the models deliver different amounts of attention per hour. So here is the same commitment — the weeks between a January mock and a June series — priced across all six, using market figures read in October 2026.

Roughly twenty weeks is forty hours at two sessions a week. School intervention: free, included in fees, typically one or two group sessions a week. A tuition centre group class: below one-to-one rates per hour, so a materially smaller total, with the attention divided among the class. A budget online or university-student tutor at AED 45 to AED 150 an hour: roughly AED 1,800 to AED 6,000. A qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to AED 300: roughly AED 6,000 to AED 12,000. An IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 and above: roughly AED 8,000 to AED 18,000 or more. In-home at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel: roughly AED 7,200 to AED 20,000.

The honest reading of that range is that the differences are large enough to matter and the right answer is rarely the top of it. A pupil with evenly spread losses placed in a group class plus school intervention may do as well as one in a specialist one-to-one block, at a tenth of the cost, because what they needed was practice volume. A pupil with clustered losses in a group class will not improve regardless of how many hours are purchased, because the format cannot address the problem.

IB Gram publishes no hourly rate on this page. The reason is that the right figure depends on board, tier, subject and weeks remaining, and a single number across all of those would mislead. What we publish is the market band so any quote can be checked, including ours, plus a free first lesson so the first hour costs nothing and you judge the teaching rather than the brochure. If that first lesson suggests school intervention would serve your child better, we will say so.

sections.heading: The series, and the dates that are verifiable
paragraphs: Whichever model you choose, the calendar is the same and it is worth getting right because UAE-facing pages repeatedly get it wrong. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists and is offered to India only; a candidate in Dubai does not sit it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

Cambridge adds one further operational detail. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in before planning study leave around any timetable you have downloaded.

The Pearson dates worth quoting are backward-looking, which is what makes them checkable. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For any series still ahead, use the month and check the live official timetable, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised.

The practical point for a family choosing a provider is that entries close months before papers are sat, and a resit is an entry for the next series rather than something taken on demand. That means the window in which a model choice can still change an outcome is narrower than it feels. A family comparing six providers in April for a June series is comparing options that can realistically deliver technique and a handful of topic repairs, not content coverage, and any provider implying otherwise is selling comfort.

sections.heading: Permits, papers and claims to distrust
paragraphs: The regulatory position is the same whichever of the six models you choose, and knowing it gives a parent real leverage. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services.

What happens to a provider operating without one is the question the search results cannot answer, and nor, honestly, can this page. The law says only that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified, so there is no amount to quote and none is quoted here. Put that through the verification order in section four. Of the six models, the marketplace listing and the community-group freelancer are the two most likely to show you a penalty figure as a reason to sign up this evening, and a number that nobody has published is not a reason to decide anything today.

There is one further question to ask, particularly of a freelance or agency arrangement. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to pupils enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK document if it affects your decision. Either way, 'your child's own class teacher, privately' is an arrangement to avoid rather than to seek.

On materials: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. We do not supply them, and a provider offering a bundle of papers and answers is offering something it should not. We also do not describe tutors as examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, and examiner experience gives no access to marking, boundaries or unseen paper content. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: What kinds of IGCSE provider will a local search actually return?
faqs.answer: Six, with very different economics. Your child's own school, which usually runs intervention sessions included in fees. A tuition centre offering group classes. An agency that places a tutor and takes a margin. A marketplace listing independents with the vetting left to you. A freelancer found through a community group. And online one-to-one providers. They differ by a factor of ten on price and almost completely on accountability, particularly on what happens when a tutor turns out to be wrong for your child.

faqs.question: Should we try the school's intervention sessions before paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and almost nobody says so because nobody has an incentive to. School intervention is included in fees that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise for 2026-27, it is taught by the person who wrote the scheme of work and will mark the mock, and it is therefore guaranteed to be on the correct specification and tier. Where it falls short is individual diagnosis: a group cannot stop for one pupil's method or timing habits. Ask what exists, then decide.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a group class will be enough?
faqs.answer: Read the marked mock. If lost marks are spread fairly evenly across the paper with no topic conspicuously worse, the problem is coverage and pace, and a group class gives exactly that at a fraction of one-to-one rates. If losses cluster in three or four topics, or in one paper, or in a pattern of method and unit errors running through everything, a group cannot address it however many hours you buy, because it cannot pause on one pupil's sign errors for twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram offer in-home IGCSE tutoring in Tilal Al Ghaf?
faqs.answer: No, and the comparison table on this page lists in-home delivery as a model we do not provide rather than pretending it does not exist. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. For a pupil who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, in-home is the right answer and we are the wrong provider, which we would rather say than sell you a format that cannot work.

faqs.question: What should I ask before paying any tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Six things, in order. May I see your MoHRE private tuition permit? Which board, syllabus code and tier do you teach? Who teaches every session — one named person or whoever is available? What will the first session produce? What do I receive after each session? And do you make any promises about the outcome? The last one is a trick: a promise of a specific result is a reason to walk away, because nobody controls it. All six checks are free and take minutes.

faqs.question: Is an agency worth the margin it charges?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the thing you are paying for is the replacement process rather than the teaching. If a tutor is pleasant but wrong for your child, an agency usually has a defined way to change them, whereas a marketplace leaves you to start the search again and a freelance arrangement found through a community group has no process at all. Whether that is worth the margin depends on how much risk you want to carry yourself and how quickly you need a working arrangement.

faqs.question: Why should I check a tutor recommended by a Tilal Al Ghaf neighbour?
faqs.answer: Because the schools serving this community do not all use the same awarding body. Pupils attend the school inside Tilal Al Ghaf, schools in DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City, and others across Dubailand and Al Barsha South. Cambridge Chemistry 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 examine similar chemistry with different paper structures, and in mathematics Edexcel permits a calculator in both papers while Cambridge's current structure does not. Ask your neighbour which code their child sits, then compare it with yours.

faqs.question: What does a Year 11 block cost across the different models?
faqs.answer: Take twenty weeks at two sessions a week, about forty hours. School intervention is included in fees. A tuition centre group class costs well below one-to-one totals. A budget online tutor at AED 45 to AED 150 an hour is roughly AED 1,800 to AED 6,000. A qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to AED 300 is roughly AED 6,000 to AED 12,000. A specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 and above is AED 8,000 to AED 18,000 or more. In-home at AED 180 to AED 500 is AED 7,200 to AED 20,000. Market figures, read October 2026.

faqs.question: Can I just buy two or three sessions to find out what we need?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we would rather you did that than commit to a term on a guess. A diagnostic block of two or three sessions establishes what the marked mock is actually telling you, with every lost mark categorised and a written recommendation at the end. Sometimes that recommendation is that school intervention plus timed practice will serve your child better than paid one-to-one. Reaching that conclusion with evidence after three sessions is a better outcome than reaching it after a term.

faqs.question: Which series will a Tilal Al Ghaf candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a UAE-facing page quoting a February window is describing a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer which zone applies.

faqs.question: Is a university student an acceptable IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: For lower secondary work and content reinforcement, often yes, and the budget band of roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour exists for that. University students are explicitly eligible for the MoHRE private tuition permit, so the arrangement is lawful when the permit is held. For Year 11 at the higher tier it is usually a false economy, because what you need is someone who can say where the mark scheme awards credit on a multi-step question, and that comes from teaching the specification rather than from having passed it.

faqs.question: What is the replacement process if a tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Ask before you commit, because the answer differs completely across the six models. With us it is a rematch: you say the first lesson or a later session did not work and we propose a different named tutor. With an agency there is usually a defined process. With a marketplace you begin the search again. With a freelance arrangement there is no process, only an awkward conversation with someone you may see at a community event. None of that is a reason to avoid any model, but it should be known in advance.

faqs.answer: They should not, and one offering a bundle of papers with answers is offering something it has no right to distribute. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing them is copyright infringement. What a tutor does is work through questions from legitimately obtained material and teach your child to read a mark scheme themselves, which changes how they write on every remaining paper in a way handed-over answers do not.

faqs.answer: It is an arrangement to avoid. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to pupils enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK document if it matters to your decision. Beyond the rules, it puts a teacher in the position of marking work they were paid to prepare, which serves nobody well.

For online delivery the early slot is simply available; for an in-home tutor it would depend on their own drive.

intro.heading: Which IGCSE subjects can you actually get a tutor for near Town Square?
paragraphs: The question behind the search is whether anybody nearby knows the syllabus, and the honest answer varies enormously by subject. For IGCSE maths and the three sciences, Dubai has a deep market and the only real question is whether a given tutor teaches your board. For Business Studies, Economics, Computer Science, Arabic first language or a Pearson modular entry, the market thins quickly, and in some terms a specific combination cannot be covered at all by anybody.

Nobody publishes that asymmetry, which is why families spend weeks discovering it. A parent in Town Square searching for a Business Studies tutor is not failing to search properly. They are looking for something that a Dubai market built around maths and science tuition does not supply in volume, and the sooner somebody says so the sooner the family can plan around it — a different subject prioritised, a November entry, or more weight on the school's own support.

Town Square compounds this. It is a Nshama community off Al Qudra Road, populated recently by younger families, and Dubai's tutoring supply clusters around the older school corridors rather than the newer Dubailand ones. So the subset of tutors willing to work out here is already smaller, and once you require the correct board, the correct tier and a less-common subject, the subset can be empty.

IB Gram does not solve the thin subjects by pretending. Lessons for Town Square families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which widens the pool from whoever will drive to Al Qudra Road to the whole roster — and that genuinely fixes maths, sciences, English and most mainstream subjects. For the scarce ones it improves the odds without guaranteeing them, and we tell you which case you are in before you commit to anything. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only.

There is a second reason to think subject by subject rather than in general, and it is the Ministry of Education equivalency rule. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That changes which subjects a plan actually depends on, and it is the kind of detail that should shape where tutoring money goes.

KHDA reported 387,441 pupils across Dubai's 227 private schools in 2024-25, with UK-curriculum schools at 37% of enrolment — the largest single bloc. A cohort that size is why general IGCSE tutoring is plentiful and why nobody bothers to tell you which specific subjects are not.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-town-square.subjectsIntro: This is the coverage audit. For each subject: the codes to check, where marks go, and how easy the subject genuinely is to cover from Town Square.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Deeply covered in Dubai and straightforward to match online, provided the board and tier are known. Marks go on non-calculator fluency, multi-step unstructured problems and method not written down. Tier decides the grade ceiling, so establish it first.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Well covered. Precise definitions, units carried through and formula rearrangement under pressure. Where the Alternative to Practical route applies, it is reliably where the most marks sit relative to the preparation effort required.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Well covered. Moles and stoichiometry are the wall, and the required ion tests and qualitative analysis are heavily examined and quick to secure once identified as the gap.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Well covered. Recall volume plus command-term precision — describe, explain and suggest want different answers, and a knowledgeable student writing the wrong shape scores low regardless of what they know.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Well covered. Directed writing and the extended response carry the marks and are won on structure and register rather than vocabulary. Reading questions reward precise textual reference, not retelling.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reasonably covered and good value for targeted work, because the component skills are discrete and measurable. A short block aimed at one weak strand produces visible movement quickly.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Thin. Dubai's tutoring market is built around maths and science, and Business Studies specialists are a much smaller group. Marks sit in applying a concept to the case material and reaching a judgement; definitions alone plateau at the lower bands.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Thin. Diagrams must be drawn and then used in the answer, and data-response questions reward application over recall. Availability varies by term, so a Year 10 start is considerably safer than a Year 11 one.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Thin at the theory end. The written paper tests data representation, logic and networks at least as much as code, and students comfortable at a keyboard lose marks hand-tracing algorithms and writing pseudocode to convention.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Scarce as a tutoring subject despite being mandatory in Dubai schools. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and support must match the stream the student actually sits.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Also scarce, and a different course from the first-language route. Worth knowing that neither Arabic route counts towards the five subjects required for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Moderately covered, usually by maths specialists who also teach A Level or Diploma maths. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive early and expose any residual algebraic weakness immediately. Worth buying only if the post-16 route needs it.

sections.heading: The coverage audit: which IGCSE subjects are easy and which are not
paragraphs: This is the table nobody publishes, and it is the thing a Town Square family most needs before spending time searching. Dubai's tutoring market grew around maths and the three sciences, because that is where demand concentrates and where qualified supply followed. Everything else is thinner, and some things are very thin indeed.

The practical consequence is that the right strategy differs by subject. For maths or physics, you can afford to be fussy: insist on the correct board, the correct tier and a tutor who can describe where marks go, and there will be candidates. For Business Studies or Computer Science theory, the sensible approach is to secure a specialist when one is available rather than waiting for the ideal match, because the ideal match may not exist this term.

For Arabic, the picture is different again and worth setting out properly. It is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, so every student takes it, and yet it is one of the scarcest tutoring subjects in the market. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, so support has to match the stream the student actually sits. KHDA also requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education in schools hold appropriate approval to teach those subjects.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E: what actually counts
paragraphs: If a UAE university or an attested certificate is anywhere in the plan, the Ministry of Education's equivalency rules decide which grades matter, and they do not match the intuition that all passes are equal.

The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The detail that catches families is which subjects count: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Both are mandatory in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, and neither counts here.

So a student holding five passes of which two are Arabic and Islamic education does not have five for this purpose. That is worth checking against an option form in Year 9 rather than against a results slip in Year 11, and it is a reason to think about tutoring spend subject by subject rather than in general. One competitor page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that candidates must take six subjects; that is not what the published rule says.

For comparison, the American track requires English proficiency of a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB, no points threshold has been verified from an official Ministry source, so we publish none and you should ask anybody who quotes you one where they read it. IB Gram does not perform, process or guarantee equivalency, and no provider should imply tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: Board and syllabus code, per subject, before anything else
paragraphs: Whatever the subject, the first practical step is the same and it is free. Email the school office and ask for the exam board and syllabus code for each subject your child takes. One message returns all of them.

You are looking for either a Cambridge four-digit number — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0450 Business Studies, 0455 Economics, 0478 Computer Science — or a Pearson code such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 or 4BI1. Dubai schools are not obliged to use one board across the curriculum and plenty do not, so a household can genuinely have maths on Pearson and sciences on Cambridge without anybody mentioning it.

Why it matters is paper structure. The content overlaps heavily between boards; tiering, paper pairing, formula provision, practical assessment route and the command-term vocabulary each board favours do not. A term of the wrong board's past papers teaches real and correct material while training the wrong instincts about what a question is asking for, and it is invisible until the real paper arrives. Pearson also offers modular assessment in some subjects, which changes when a result can be banked and therefore changes the whole planning picture.

Bring the codes to any tutoring conversation. A specialist will tell you immediately which specification they teach; a generalist will talk about the subject in general and move on. That is the fastest filter available, and it costs one email to obtain. Keep the reply, because you will use the same codes again when the November entry question comes up.

sections.heading: The June series, November as a route, and the series that is not ours
paragraphs: Start with the series that does not exist here, because a family with several weak subjects is the family most likely to be sold it. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. In the UAE a candidate sits the June series and the November series, and there is no third date to spread subjects across. Anyone who has told you a March resit is available in Dubai is describing another country's provision, sometimes honestly, having moved from a school in India, and sometimes because a tutor would like the autumn booked without the June deadline doing the arguing. Either way the consequence is identical: a subject parked for March is a subject parked for a year.

The two series that do exist are June and November, covering Cambridge International GCSE and O Level, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October lower down the school. For a child entered in eight or nine subjects the shape of those weeks is the whole plan, and it is not a national document. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. With nine subjects there are enough papers that one misread date is close to inevitable if the wrong version is the one circulating at home. Ask the school office which zone the centre sits in and work from the version it gives you, never from a timetable found by search.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For how the November route times out: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January — the November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so always work from the live official PDF rather than any date restated on a tutoring site.

For a Town Square family with a thin subject, the November route is strategically useful rather than a consolation. If nobody can tutor Business Studies before June, entering it in November and using the summer for a secured fixed-scope block is a better plan than a diluted spring across five subjects. A January result still updates post-16 applications.

sections.heading: What to do when a subject genuinely cannot be covered
paragraphs: This is the section the market does not write, and it matters more than another description of how committed everybody is. Sometimes the answer is that no specialist is available, and a family deserves to hear it early enough to act.

Our sequence is this. If a specialist is free, we propose them and you take a free trial lesson with that person, no card required. If the only available specialist works from another time zone, we say so and offer the slots that genuinely exist. If nobody suitable is free, we say that too, and we will not substitute a general tutor for a subject specialist in an exam year — we would rather lose the enquiry, and we have.

What a family can do instead is usually one of four things. Reprioritise: concentrate the tutoring budget on a well-covered subject where a grade can move, and accept that the thin subject rests on the school. Re-enter: plan the thin subject for the November series with a secured block over the summer. Lean on the school: ask the department directly for additional support, which is free and frequently available if asked specifically rather than generally. Or narrow the brief: in Computer Science theory, for instance, hand-traced algorithms and pseudocode conventions are a narrow enough target that a non-specialist maths tutor can genuinely help, where the full syllabus would be beyond them.

What we will never offer as a fallback is a UAE home visit, because there is no UAE visiting service to fall back on. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE and nobody on our roster will arrive at a Town Square address.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you find permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: A near-me search puts you in front of community noticeboards, building WhatsApp groups and classified listings, which is precisely where the licensing question gets skipped, and most parents have never been told there is one to ask. Private tuition in the UAE is a permitted activity rather than an unregulated one. The permit was created by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, it is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it is granted free of charge for two years. The process itself sits on MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services, with a stated completion time of two working days.

Because it costs nothing and takes two working days, lacking one is a choice rather than an obstacle. Eligibility is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the amounts, so disregard any figure circulating informally.

The permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition for Abu Dhabi school staff. This is particularly relevant for the thin subjects, because the obvious local answer in a scarce subject is the school's own teacher, and that is exactly the arrangement the rules exclude.

There are two different licences behind the two things a near-me search returns, and conflating them is how a parent ends up reassured by the wrong document. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE permit. A business running tutoring from premises anywhere in Dubai, whether that is the small centre above the shops or the study club advertising in a community hall, needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit as a training institute, and KHDA asks for annual renewal to be requested at least thirty days before expiry, so a centre showing you a lapsed one has told you something useful. For our own part, IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, claims none, and has no UAE office or centre, which is why nothing on this page invites you to visit one.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs, and what scarcity does to it
paragraphs: Read the published Dubai bands, all taken from provider pages in October 2026, by what each one can actually cover rather than by price order. Budget online tutoring from AED 33-65 an hour, with Tutopiya at AED 33-52 and EdFlik at AED 45-65, buys supervised practice in one subject the tutor already knows well, and covering four subjects at that band usually means finding four different people. Qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, is the band at which one tutor can plausibly hold two related subjects. Specialist IGCSE, IB and A Level tutors run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting the band at AED 200-450 plus, while BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end, where you are buying one subject properly rather than breadth. In-home visits are AED 180-500 including travel, and the travel is charged once whether the session covers one subject or three, which is the only argument for the format that survives contact with a Town Square timetable.

Scarcity affects price less than parents expect and availability far more. A Business Studies specialist does not generally charge double a maths specialist; they are simply harder to find and may not be free when you need them. That makes timing the real cost in a thin subject: a block secured in Year 10 is available, and the same request in February of Year 11 may not be fillable at any price.

The monthly numbers are where a multi-subject plan either works or quietly does not. Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 a month for one weekly hour at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. The figure a parent searching for an IGCSE tutor near Town Square actually faces is that band multiplied by the number of subjects in trouble, which is rarely one: three weak subjects at the mid-tier band is AED 1,800-3,600 a month, not AED 600-1,200. Packaged offers compress it a little, at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits. Eight sessions spread across three subjects is under three hours per subject per month, which is a maintenance rate rather than a repair rate.

Each figure belongs to the provider named beside it. None is an IB Gram price — we publish no rate card on these pages, because the honest number depends on subject, board, tier and weeks remaining. Take the free trial lesson and get a quote after the diagnostic.

sections.heading: What we do not claim
paragraphs: Some things are absent from this page deliberately, and each is something a competitor in this search result does carry.

No guarantee of a grade or an improvement in any subject, and no suggestion that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression. That last one is a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process, and it is worth noticing whenever anybody makes it to you.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which in practice means none. No average grades achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, occasionally in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never state how any of them was produced.

No awarding-body material hosted or sold: past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and we cite and link them instead. No regulator or awarding-body approval claimed, no UAE office or address, no examiner descriptions we cannot evidence, and no home visits anywhere in the UAE at any price. And no school named here as a partner or client — the lists above describe the landscape around Town Square, which is why a disclaimer sits under every one of them. Several competitors list twenty-five or more schools under a trusted-by heading with no relationship behind any of them, and one lists a school that appears not to exist at all.

We also publish no specific exam dates beyond naming the series. Awarding bodies revise timetables, Cambridge allocates centres to administrative zones with different versions of the same timetable, and a date restated on a tutoring page is the version a family should trust least of all the versions available to them.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a tutor for near Town Square?
faqs.answer: Business Studies, Economics, Computer Science theory and both Arabic routes. Dubai's tutoring market grew around maths and the three sciences, where demand concentrates and qualified supply followed, so those are deep and reliable to match. The rest are thinner, and in some terms a specific combination cannot be covered by anybody. That asymmetry is not published anywhere, which is why families spend weeks discovering it rather than planning around it from the start.

faqs.question: Why is Arabic so hard to get tutoring for when every Dubai school teaches it?
faqs.answer: Because mandatory does not mean well supplied. Arabic is required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, stating combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. So any support must match the stream the student actually sits, which narrows an already small tutoring pool. KHDA also requires school teachers of Arabic to hold appropriate approval to teach it.

faqs.question: Does Arabic count towards the five subjects for MoE equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and neither does Islamic education. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Both are mandatory school subjects in Dubai and neither counts here, so a student with five passes of which two are Arabic and Islamic education does not have five for this purpose. Check an option form in Year 9 rather than a results slip in Year 11.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the Ministry actually require?
faqs.answer: Five, plus an Advanced Level component. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, together with either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states six subjects are required, which is not what the published rule says. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae; IB Gram does not process equivalency.

faqs.question: What do I ask the school before looking for a tutor?
faqs.answer: The exam board and syllabus code for each subject. One email returns all of them. You are looking for Cambridge four-digit codes — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0450 Business Studies, 0455 Economics, 0478 Computer Science — or Pearson codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Ask per subject rather than assuming one answer covers everything, because Dubai departments make independent board decisions and a household can genuinely be split across both.

faqs.question: Does a thin subject cost more to tutor?
faqs.answer: Generally no, and that surprises people. A Business Studies specialist does not charge double a maths specialist; the published Dubai bands apply to both, with qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300 an hour and specialists at AED 200-450 and above. Scarcity shows up as availability rather than as price. The practical consequence is that timing is the real cost: a block secured in Year 10 exists, and the same request in February of Year 11 may not be fillable at any price.

faqs.question: What should we do if nobody can tutor my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Four things, in roughly this order. Reprioritise the budget onto a well-covered subject where a grade can still move. Plan the thin subject for the November series and secure a narrow block over the summer. Ask the school department directly for additional support, specifically rather than generally, because it is free and often available when asked properly. Or narrow the brief: hand-traced algorithms and pseudocode conventions, for instance, are a target a strong maths tutor can genuinely cover even without the full Computer Science syllabus.

faqs.question: Will you substitute a general tutor if no specialist is free?
faqs.answer: Not in an exam year. If a matching specialist is free we propose them and you take a free trial lesson with that person. If the only one available works from another time zone, we say so and offer the slots that genuinely exist. If nobody suitable is free, we say that and decline rather than putting a generalist in front of a Year 11 candidate. We have lost enquiries doing it, which is the only reason the commitment is worth stating.

faqs.question: Is it harder to find a tutor in Town Square than in older parts of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, for two compounding reasons. Dubai's tutoring supply clusters around the older school corridors — Jumeirah, Al Barsha, Mirdif, the Greens — rather than the newer Dubailand communities, so the subset willing to work out along Al Qudra Road is already smaller. And Town Square is a recently populated Nshama development, so the informal parent network that recommends tutors elsewhere is still thin. Online matching removes the first constraint entirely, which is why we work that way.

faqs.question: Can my child resit a subject in the February or March series?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The belief circulates widely here and planning around it costs a term, so confirm with your school. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For a thin subject the November route is genuinely strategic rather than a consolation: enter it in November, secure a narrow block over the summer, and the January result still updates post-16 applications.

faqs.question: When do November IGCSE results arrive?
faqs.answer: In January. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January; the November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. For context, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Schools are used to receiving updated grades in January and post-16 applications can be amended then. Always work from the awarding body's live official timetable rather than dates restated on any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any individual charging for private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Eligibility covers school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Since it costs nothing and takes two days, lacking one is a choice. MoHRE states tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties; no amounts are published.

faqs.question: Can we ask my child's own teacher to tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: No, and this bites hardest in exactly the scarce subjects where it would be most tempting. The MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition for school staff there. What you can do instead is ask the department for additional support within school — specifically, naming the topic rather than asking generally — which is free and frequently available if requested properly.

faqs.question: Which schools near Town Square offer the broader IGCSE option blocks?
faqs.answer: The larger secondary schools in Motor City, The Villa and Dubai Sports City generally carry the wider option lists that include Business Studies, Economics and Computer Science: GEMS Metropole, GEMS FirstPoint, GEMS United, Safa Community School, Dubai Heights Academy. The nearer schools on short runs from Town Square — South View School, The Aquila School, Jebel Ali School, Ranches Primary, JESS Arabian Ranches, Fairgreen International School — vary. We name these as context and have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor visit our home in Town Square?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Town Square one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only, and there is no UAE visiting arrangement at any price. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel. Worth noting that in-home delivery narrows the available pool further before subject expertise is even considered, which matters most in exactly the thin subjects.

intro.heading: Count backwards from the paper, not forwards from today
paragraphs: Every revision plan a family builds forwards from the day they start runs out of road. Plans built backwards from the paper date do not, because they begin with the fixed point and then ask what has to be true at each stage before it. That single change in direction is the most useful thing a tutor can bring to an Umm Al Sheif household in Year 10 or Year 11, and it costs nothing to adopt.

The fixed points for a UAE candidate are known. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series. Its February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate never sits it, whatever a generic revision site suggests. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026.

Results dates give the rhythm its shape. Pearson June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So the November series functions as a repair route with a result the following January, which matters if a post-16 place depends on a specific grade. Entry deadlines for both boards sit months ahead of the papers themselves.

There is a Cambridge administrative detail that catches families out every year. Each centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A timetable downloaded from a search result is a genuine risk; ask the school which zone it is in.

Umm Al Sheif itself helps rather than hinders. This is a villa district off Al Wasl Road between Umm Suqeim and Al Safa, with unusually short school journeys by Dubai standards, so most children are home between 14:45 and 15:45 and the session window is wide. The constraint through exam term is the school's own revision programme and study leave, not the road, and that is a materially better position than families in the outer communities are in.

IB Gram delivers to Umm Al Sheif as one-to-one teaching over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-umm-al-shei.programmesIntro: The British pathway through an Umm Al Sheif household has three distinct calendars, and support is worth very different amounts at each. The cheapest effective intervention sits earliest, which is also when families are least inclined to buy it.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external exams and therefore no deadline pressure, which is exactly why the calendar matters here. Algebraic fluency, scientific notation and essay structure are built in these three years, and a Year 10 student missing them spends the first IGCSE term relearning Year 8 rather than starting the specification. Thirty minutes twice a week beats ninety minutes once.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Sheif Years 7 to 9 students generally attend schools in Umm Suqeim, Al Safa or Jumeirah with short journeys, so they are frequently home before 15:15 with the lightest homework in the house. This is the one stage where a 16:00 session is genuinely workable here, and where the whole year is available rather than only the gaps between deadlines.

programmes.name: IGCSE year one
programmes.description: The year nobody treats as an exam year and the year that decides the tier. Schools form provisional Core or Extended judgements from Year 10 attainment, and those judgements set the grade ceiling. Content coverage also begins here, so a gap opened in Year 10 is carried into Year 11 revision rather than fixed by it.
programmes.countryNote: The Umm Al Sheif Year 10 week has room in it, which is the argument for using it. A single weekly session from the spring term of Year 10 removes the panic buying that happens in the February before papers, and it is the window in which a tier conversation with the school can still change an outcome.

programmes.name: IGCSE examination year
programmes.description: Final entries, coursework deadlines, mock season, study leave and the papers, in that order, compressed into roughly thirty teaching weeks. The grade is decided at least as much by pacing and mark-scheme reading as by knowledge. Students who can do the mathematics still lose marks for unshown working, and students who know the biology still lose them for imprecise terminology.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools typically run mocks in the winter term and release students for parts of them, which creates the rare possibility of a daytime session. Umm Al Sheif families get more from four sessions across mock fortnight, working from a fresh marked script, than from twelve sessions in October working from a syllabus checklist.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-umm-al-shei.subjectsIntro: For each subject, what the calendar demands rather than what the syllabus contains: when the content should be finished, when the practice has to start, and where the late-stage marks sit.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Content should be complete by the end of the winter term so the spring is pure past papers. Late marks sit in multi-step questions where working is not shown and in the recurring topics students forget annually: bearings, similar shapes, compound interest and cumulative frequency.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Equation rearrangement and unit prefixes need to be automatic before the spring, because they cost marks under time pressure rather than through misunderstanding. Cambridge candidates must also rehearse the practical paper or the Alternative to Practical format, which has its own conventions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic and the qualitative analysis tables repay drilling in the winter term. Late in the year the highest-return work is writing every calculation with units and significant figures, which recovers marks the student has already earned but not been credited for.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-volume specification in the group, so it needs the earliest start and the most spaced recall. Terminology precision is the whole game late on: a mark scheme wanting a named process will not accept a fluent paraphrase, however well written.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing rewards planning, which is a fifteen-minute skill teachable in two sessions and then usable all year. The late-stage work is reading the task for register, audience and form, because students who write well but answer the wrong task lose marks they cannot recover.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed, so the calendar risk is breadth rather than depth. Working through the specification checklist topic by topic from the winter term is the reliable approach, because unseen topics are the loss here rather than imperfectly understood ones.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy can be fixed in a fortnight at any point in the year and is the most reliably available mark in both subjects. Definition precision takes longer and should start in the autumn, since it is recall rather than technique.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Practical or programming components have internal deadlines ahead of the written papers, so they drive the calendar. Trace tables and pseudocode conventions are examinable skills distinct from writing working code, and they are late-stage drilling material.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study recall needs spacing across months, not cramming. The source-handling method in History is teachable in three or four sessions and then holds, which makes it unusually good value in a short run-up to papers.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Because it runs alongside the examined timetable all year, short regular oral practice beats an exam-term intensive here more clearly than in any other subject.

sections.heading: Where an Umm Al Sheif student should be, term by term
paragraphs: The two IGCSE years have a shape, and almost every family that feels behind is behind against this shape rather than against their child's ability. The table below sets out what should be true at each stage. It is not a counsel of perfection; it is a checklist you can run in ten minutes to find out which of four or five things is actually missing.

The pattern of failure is consistent. A gap opens in the Year 10 spring, usually in mathematics or a science, and nobody notices because Year 10 reports are not read as exam results. The gap is then carried into Year 11, where the school is teaching new content and has no time to go back. By the winter mocks the student is being examined on two years of material with one year genuinely understood.

Catching it early is dramatically cheaper. A single weekly hour from the Year 10 spring term, aimed at the specific topic that opened the gap, costs a fraction of an exam-term intensive and does not compete with coursework deadlines and mock revision for the student's remaining hours. The families who spend least on tutoring overall in Dubai are usually the ones who started earliest, not the ones who held out longest.

If you are reading this in the second half of Year 11, the checklist still works; it just tells you to skip stages. The honest answer at that point is to pick two subjects, build backwards from the paper date, and accept that the third and fourth subjects will be carried by school teaching alone.

sections.heading: The June series counted backwards in weeks
paragraphs: Working in weeks rather than months is what makes a plan usable, because a student can hold a week in their head and cannot hold a term. The table below counts backwards from the first paper. The weeks are approximate because schools set their own mock and coursework dates, so take the structure and put your school's actual dates into it.

Two things on that list are not negotiable and are easy to miss. Final entries are submitted months before the papers, and once submitted the tier and the subject list are fixed for that series. Access arrangements, where a student needs them, have to be applied for with evidence before the entry deadline and cannot be arranged retrospectively. Both are school administrative tasks, and both are things a parent can ask about in a single email.

The stage families most often misjudge is the sixteen-week mark, which is usually just after mocks. That is the moment the plan should change character: from learning content to converting it. Students who are still working through revision guides at eight weeks out are usually the ones who did not make that switch, and the switch is a decision rather than a skill.

Always check the live official timetable on the board's own site. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and they can be revised, and Cambridge timetables differ by administrative zone. A restatement of dates on any website, including this one, is a guide to structure rather than a source for dates.

sections.heading: November as a repair series, and what results day gives you
paragraphs: Families treat results day as a verdict. It is better understood as the start of a short decision window with three options in it, and the window closes faster than most parents expect. Pearson June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, which gives a sense of how little time sits between a disappointing grade and the start of a post-16 course.

The first option is a remark or an enquiry about results, which the school submits within a deadline set by the board. It is worth considering where a grade sits a mark or two below a boundary and where the paper in question was one the student felt went well. It is not a general appeal; it is a clerical and marking review with defined grounds.

The second option is the November series, which functions as a repair route. November 2025 Pearson results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November resit produces a grade in the following January rather than the same summer. That timing works for a post-16 place that can be confirmed conditionally and does not work where a firm grade is needed in September. Cambridge candidates in the UAE use June and November for the same purpose; the February and March series is India-only and unavailable here.

The third option is to accept the grade and move on, which is sometimes the right answer and is almost never discussed calmly in the week results arrive. The useful preparation is to have the conversation in advance, in the spring, so that nobody is making a decision about a resit in the twenty-four hours after a result lands.

sections.heading: Mock season is the diagnostic, not the rehearsal
paragraphs: Dubai British-curriculum schools generally run mocks in the winter term, and most families use them as a progress report. Read as a progress report, a mock tells you a grade. Read as a diagnostic, the same paper tells you precisely which of four things is wrong, and the four things have completely different remedies. The difference between those two readings is worth more than several months of tutoring.

Take the script and go through it mark by mark. Every lost mark falls into one of four categories: content not known, command term misread, working not shown, or time ran out. Tally them. A student with thirty lost marks spread evenly across the four needs a different plan from a student with twenty-five of them in the timing column, and the second student does not need more content teaching at all.

Timing is the category parents underestimate most. A student who consistently leaves the last question blank is losing a grade boundary to pacing, and the remedy is counter-intuitive: practise the final question first for a fortnight so that it stops being the question met while tired. That costs two sessions and can move a grade, which is a better return than any amount of additional content.

Umm Al Sheif has a practical advantage during mock season. Schools often release students for parts of it, and journeys here are short, so a daytime session is possible for the only time in the year. Three or four sessions in that fortnight, working from a fresh script, consistently outperform twelve sessions in October working from a syllabus checklist.

sections.heading: Coursework and practical deadlines sit before the papers
paragraphs: The most avoidable lost grade in the IGCSE years is a coursework component submitted late or submitted thin, and it happens because the deadline arrives while the household's attention is on revision. Coursework and practical assessment, where a specification includes them, are completed in the term before the written papers and are marked by the school against board criteria.

The two boards handle practical science differently, which changes the calendar. Cambridge assesses practical skills through a practical test or the Alternative to Practical paper, so the student has a dated examination to prepare for. Pearson International GCSE assesses practical skills inside its written papers instead, so there is no separate practical date but the method and analysis still have to be taught deliberately rather than absorbed.

For subjects with a practical or project component, Computer Science and ICT in particular, the internal deadline drives everything else. A student who leaves it late ends up revising for mocks and finishing a project in the same fortnight, which damages both. Put the coursework date in the plan first, before any revision schedule, and work the revision around it.

What a tutor may do here has a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the content, explain what the criteria reward, question a plan and tell a student why a section is weak. No tutor at IB Gram will write coursework, draft it or edit it to completion. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and a provider that offers otherwise is selling your child a malpractice finding.

sections.heading: Ramadan, school holidays and the real teaching weeks
paragraphs: The UAE academic year does not deliver thirty-nine usable teaching weeks, and a plan built as though it does will break. Most Dubai private schools run three terms with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break towards the end of March, and the spring break lands squarely in the period when exam-term revision should be at its most intense.

Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year and currently falls in the spring, which means it increasingly overlaps the weeks before the May and June papers. Schools shorten the day during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon, but the freed afternoon is a poor teaching window because the household is fasting and preparing. A post-Iftar slot, commonly between 20:30 and 22:00, works far better and is easy to staff on video because nobody is driving.

Some families would rather pause for the month and resume afterwards, and that is a legitimate choice we would rather you made deliberately than drift into. Paying for sessions nobody attends is the worst outcome for everyone. What matters is deciding in advance, because a month lost by accident at that point in the year is expensive and a month paused on purpose is manageable.

Count your real weeks before agreeing a plan. Take the paper date, subtract the spring break, subtract the weeks the school has reserved for study leave, subtract any travel you already know about, and look at what is left. Most families find the number is smaller than they assumed, and the plan that follows is more honest for it.

sections.heading: An eight-week build when the weeks really are short
paragraphs: Sometimes a family arrives with eight weeks and two subjects in trouble. It is not an ideal position and it is not a hopeless one, provided the eight weeks are spent on conversion rather than on coverage. The single decision that matters is to stop trying to learn the parts of the specification that were never understood and to secure marks on the parts that were.

The structure that works runs in four phases of two weeks. The first two weeks establish a baseline with timed sections and produce the error list. The next two attack the two or three highest-frequency errors on that list, which are almost always command terms or unshown working rather than topics. The next two rehearse full papers under timed conditions. The last two reduce to pacing, a short recall routine and sleep.

Two things should be dropped in an eight-week plan, and dropping them is the hard part. Topics that appear rarely and are not understood should be abandoned rather than learned badly, because the hours they consume are worth more elsewhere. And re-reading notes should stop entirely, since it produces a feeling of progress with very little measurable return at this stage.

The honest caveat: eight weeks can move a grade boundary and will not usually move three. A tutor who promises more than that is selling rather than teaching, and no provider can guarantee a grade or a score. What we can do is tell you, after one session with a marked script, what the eight weeks realistically reach.

sections.heading: What the exam term costs, by phase of the year
paragraphs: Tutoring costs more per grade point in the spring than in the autumn, which is a pricing reality rather than a moral failing. Demand concentrates in the weeks before papers, the formats families want then are intensive, and the specialists who can work on a named paper are the scarcest part of the market. Buying earlier is cheaper for the same outcome.

The Dubai market, with sources named, runs roughly as follows. University-student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik on their own pages. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase quoting around AED 270. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home visits AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in.

The table below maps those bands to the phase of the year where each makes sense. The pattern is that the cheap bands are good value early and poor value late, because what they buy, supervision and fluency, is exactly what a student eight weeks from a paper no longer needs. None of these figures is an IB Gram rate card; they are the market, published so you can judge any quote against something.

One piece of wider context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is therefore the variable line in a Dubai education budget this year, which is an argument for spending it deliberately and early on two subjects rather than late and thinly across six.
