process.title: Send the paper date and the school calendar
process.description: Tell us the series your child is entered for, the mock dates and any coursework deadline the school has published. A plan built backwards from those dates is usable; one built forwards from today is not. If you do not have the dates, ask the school office; it is a routine request answered in a day.

process.title: Send the most recent marked script
process.description: A mock paper is worth more than any description of the problem. We classify every lost mark as content, command term, unshown working or timing, and the tally decides the plan. A timing-heavy script and a content-heavy script need completely different engagements and different numbers of hours.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One per family, booked before payment and with no card details required. It is a real lesson on your child's own material. Ask the tutor at the end what the remaining weeks can realistically reach; a straight answer there is the best signal you will get about everything that follows.

process.title: Count the real weeks, then commit
process.description: Subtract the spring break, study leave and any travel you already know about from the weeks before the paper. Most families find the usable number is smaller than assumed. Agree a plan against that number rather than against the calendar, and agree what it is meant to achieve.

process.title: Review on a new timed section
process.description: At the halfway point, run a fresh timed section and compare the error list. If the recurring errors have stopped recurring, the plan is working. If they have not, we change the tutor, the focus or the diagnosis rather than adding hours. Re-matching is free and the diagnosis carries across.

whyPoints.title: Plans built backwards from a date
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from the paper, the mock or the coursework deadline and works back in weeks. That is the difference between a schedule a Year 11 student can hold in their head and a term's worth of good intentions that runs out of road in March.

whyPoints.title: Series and dates named at the source
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November with Cambridge and May, June and November with Pearson. We name series by month so the page does not go stale, cite past results dates because those are checkable, and point at the board's own live timetable rather than restating what can be revised.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts read for pattern, not grade
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark is classified as content, command term, unshown working or timing. The tally decides the plan, and it routinely contradicts what the student guessed. This is the single most useful hour in the whole engagement and it happens in session one.

whyPoints.title: The real weeks, counted honestly
whyPoints.description: Spring break, study leave and Ramadan all remove teaching weeks, and a plan that ignores them fails in March. We count the usable weeks with you before agreeing anything, and we would rather you paused deliberately than paid for sessions nobody attends.

whyPoints.title: No promises about grades
whyPoints.description: Eight weeks can move a grade boundary and will not usually move three. No provider can guarantee a grade, a score or an improvement, and anyone offering one is selling rather than teaching. What we will do is tell you after one session what the remaining weeks realistically reach.

faqs.question: Is it too late to get an IGCSE tutor near me in Umm Al Sheif this term?
faqs.answer: Rarely, but what the weeks can achieve changes sharply with how many are left. With twenty weeks you can still teach content and then convert it. With eight you should abandon coverage and spend the time on conversion: timed sections, command-term discipline, shown working and pacing. With three you work on pacing and recall only. The first session with a marked script will tell you which of those you are in, and we will say so plainly rather than sell a plan that cannot fit.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series do Umm Al Sheif students actually sit?
faqs.answer: June and November with Cambridge International, and May, June or November with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it, however many revision sites list its deadlines. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Check your own school's timetable on the board's site, because Cambridge allocates centres to six administrative zones and the timetable differs between them.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram come to a house in Umm Al Sheif for lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Umm Al Sheif families are one to one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and your child's own school material on screen. We say this directly because several providers in this market imply a visit and then connect families to tutors outside the country. If you want somebody physically in the room, you want a different provider.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE entry deadlines, and what happens if we miss one?
faqs.answer: Final entries are submitted by the school months before the papers, and once submitted the tier and subject list are fixed for that series. Missing a deadline usually means waiting for the next series, which for a UAE candidate means June or November. Access arrangements, where a student needs them, must be applied for with supporting evidence before the entry deadline and cannot be arranged retrospectively. Both are school administrative tasks; email the office and ask for the dates and the current entries in writing.

faqs.question: What should my child have finished by the winter mocks?
faqs.answer: The full specification taught once, coursework and practical assessment complete or nearly so, and at least two timed sections attempted in each examined subject so pacing has been tested. If the specification is not finished by mocks, the mock will measure teaching coverage rather than the student, which is worth knowing before anybody reacts to the grade. The most common gap at this point is not content; it is that no timed practice has happened, so nobody knows whether the student can finish a paper.

faqs.question: How do we read a mock script properly instead of just looking at the grade?
faqs.answer: Go through it mark by mark and sort every lost mark into four boxes: content not known, command term misread, working not shown, or ran out of time. Then count the boxes. A student with most losses in the timing box does not need more content teaching, and a student with most in the command-term box needs three or four sessions on question wording rather than a term of revision. The tally almost always contradicts what the student assumed was wrong.

faqs.question: Is the November series a reasonable plan if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: It is a genuine repair route with one timing caveat. November results arrive the following January, as happened when November 2025 Pearson results reached students on 22 January 2026. That works where a post-16 place can hold a conditional grade and does not work where a firm grade is needed in September. Consider it alongside an enquiry about results, which the school submits within a board deadline and which is worth pursuing when a grade sits a mark or two below a boundary.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan make exam-term tutoring harder in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It changes the shape of the week rather than removing it. Schools shorten the day, which frees the afternoon, but the freed afternoon is a weak teaching window because the household is fasting and preparing. A post-Iftar slot, commonly 20:30 to 22:00, works much better, and online delivery makes it easy because nobody is driving late at night. Families who prefer to pause for the month can do that; the important thing is to decide in advance rather than lose the weeks by accident.

faqs.question: How many usable teaching weeks are actually left before the papers?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests. Take the paper date, subtract the spring break, subtract the weeks the school has reserved for study leave, subtract Ramadan if your family reduces sessions then, and subtract any travel you already know about. Most Dubai families find the real number is four to six weeks lower than their first estimate. Doing that arithmetic before agreeing a plan is the difference between a schedule that holds and one that quietly collapses in March.

faqs.question: Should coursework or revision come first in Year 11 autumn?
faqs.answer: Coursework, without much argument. A late or thin coursework component is the most avoidable lost grade in the IGCSE years, and it happens because the deadline arrives while attention is on revision. Put the coursework date into the plan first and build revision around it. For Computer Science, ICT and any subject with a project component, that internal deadline should be driving the whole autumn schedule rather than competing with it for leftover hours.

faqs.question: Why does tutoring cost more in the spring than in the autumn?
faqs.answer: Demand concentrates in the weeks before papers, the formats families want then are intensive, and the specialists able to work on a named paper are the scarcest part of the market. Published Dubai bands run from about AED 33 to 65 for student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors and AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists. Buying the same outcome in Year 10 autumn costs materially less, which is the strongest practical argument for starting early.

faqs.question: Can daytime sessions happen during study leave in Umm Al Sheif?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the real advantages of this part of Dubai. Journeys here are short and schools in the Umm Suqeim and Al Safa cluster often release students during mock season and study leave, which opens a daytime window that does not exist during normal term. A morning session with a rested student is worth more than an evening session with a tired one, so families who can use those weeks should plan the heaviest work into them.

faqs.question: My daughter runs out of time in every paper, so what do we do?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a pacing problem, not a knowledge problem, because it usually costs a full grade boundary. The remedy that works is counter-intuitive: practise the final question first for a fortnight, so it stops being the one met while tired and short of time. Alongside that, have her write a planned time per mark at the top of the paper before starting, and practise abandoning a stuck question and returning to it. Two sessions on this often beat a month of extra content.

faqs.question: Can a tutor finish my son's IGCSE coursework if the deadline is close?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider that says yes is selling him a malpractice finding. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own. A tutor can teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, question whether a plan is answerable, and tell him why a section is weak so that he can fix it himself. Nobody at IB Gram writes, drafts or edits coursework to completion. If a deadline is genuinely unreachable, the conversation to have is with the school, not with a tutor.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for the subject and hour we need in exam term?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than fill the slot with a generalist. Exam term is the tightest part of the year for availability, especially for specific science codes at fixed weekday hours. Common subjects are usually matched within a few days; narrow combinations can take a week or more, and occasionally nobody suitable is free at all. Hearing that honestly eight weeks out leaves you time to try elsewhere, which is more useful than discovering in session three that the specification is unfamiliar.

intro.heading: Too many names, too little information: the real problem with a local IGCSE search
paragraphs: The UK curriculum is the largest curriculum group in Dubai, accounting for 37% of private-school enrolment across a market of 387,441 students in 227 schools. That has a direct consequence for anyone searching locally: there is no shortage of people in this city offering IGCSE tuition. Umm Suqeim parents who ask in a neighbourhood group get a dozen names within an hour. The scarcity problem described on IB pages does not apply here. The problem here is the opposite one, and it is harder to solve.

Every one of those dozen names will say they teach IGCSE. Very few will volunteer which board, which specification code, which tier, which paper structure, or which year they last taught it. Those are the facts that determine whether a tutor can help your child, and none of them appear in a recommendation. The result is that families in Umm Suqeim do not fail to find a tutor; they find one quickly, pay for a term, and discover in March that the work was aimed at a paper structure their child is not sitting.

So this page is not a persuasion exercise. It is a filter. It gives you a shortlisting sheet with signals you can actually verify, explains the tiering decision that quietly caps a grade before any teaching happens, shows how to use a single marked paper to run a better diagnostic than most paid first sessions, sets out the Dubai market rates with the premium separated out from the teaching, explains the November series as a route rather than as a failure, and covers what happens if a school will not enter your child for a subject.

On delivery, the position is straightforward and stated early. IB Gram teaches Umm Suqeim students one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer in India only. In an abundant local market that is a real choice rather than a necessity, so the section on rates explains exactly what the in-home premium buys and the last section names three situations in which a local in-person tutor genuinely suits a family better than we do.

Everything factual on this page can be checked. Rates are attributed to the provider that published them with the reading date given. Grade ranges and paper structures come from the boards' own specifications. Regulatory statements come from u.ae, KHDA and MoHRE. Where something is not verifiable - most IB session dates, any provider's claims about its own results - this page says so rather than filling the gap. That restraint is deliberate. In a search cluster where three of the six best-performing pages publish no price at all, two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in, and one publishes a rating it awarded itself, the cheapest way to be useful is to state only what can be checked and to name the source next to it. If a figure on this page cannot be traced back to a board document, a regulator's page or a named provider's own published rate, it should not be here, and if you find one that cannot, treat the rest with the scepticism it has earned.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Tiering here sets the ceiling: Cambridge Core papers are graded C to G and Extended A* to E, while Pearson 4MA1 Foundation gives 5 to 1 and Higher gives 9 to 4. A student aiming at a 7 or above on a Foundation entry is aiming at something the paper cannot award.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths qualification by students heading for A Level Mathematics. It is the hardest subject in this list to staff locally in Dubai, which makes it the clearest case for working with a tutor who does not need to drive anywhere.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: In Cambridge 0625 the multiple-choice paper is 30% of the grade, the theory paper 50%, and the practical test or alternative-to-practical paper 20%. Students routinely leave the practical component unrevised because it feels like the easy fifth, and it is the easiest fifth to lose.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same component pattern as Physics on the Cambridge specification. Predictable losses sit in moles calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic conditions, each of which is procedural and each of which responds quickly to drilled practice with a tutor marking to the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-word sensitive. 'Describe' wants what happens, 'explain' wants why, 'suggest' wants an inference from unfamiliar data, and 'compare' wants both sides in one sentence. A correct fact in the wrong structure earns nothing on the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: Reduced content across all three sciences, awarded as a double or single qualification. It is a sensible choice for a loaded timetable and a closing of doors for some A Level and university routes, so check the intended post-16 course before accepting it as the default.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Reading comprehension and directed writing carry the marks in Language, with a mark-per-point structure on inference questions that rewards precision over length. Literature depends on quotation accuracy and on answering the question asked rather than the one revised for.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with different implications for university applications and for MoE equivalency counting. Confirm which one your child is entered for in writing, because the two are easy to conflate and the revision material is not interchangeable.

subjects.name: Economics, Business Studies and Accounting
subjects.description: All three reward structured evaluation that most students never learn: a judgement, two sides weighed, and a stated reason for the preference. Writing more content instead is the reliable way to sit in the middle bands with full knowledge of the syllabus.

subjects.name: Geography, History and Computer Science
subjects.description: Case-study and application subjects where the specified examples are the marks. Computer Science is thinly staffed locally and combines written theory with practical programming, so a tutor who can only do one half of it is a half-useful tutor.

sections.heading: A shortlisting sheet for an abundant local market
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor near me in Umm Suqeim is easy to find and hard to choose. The table below is a filter you can apply in a ten-minute conversation, built around signals that can be checked rather than impressions that cannot. Every row has a verifiable answer; none of them requires you to know the syllabus yourself.

The strongest single signal is whether a tutor asks you for the syllabus code before they tell you what they will teach. A tutor who opens with their own credentials and closes without asking which specification your child sits has told you that the teaching will be generic. A tutor who asks for the code, the tier and the last marked paper in the first three minutes is going to build the lessons around your child rather than around a scheme they already own.

The second strongest signal is how they talk about marks. Ask where the marks in a subject are, and a specialist will give you component percentages - 30, 50 and 20 for Cambridge sciences, for instance - and then ask which of the three is losing them. A generalist will talk about topics the child finds hard. Both answers sound knowledgeable; only one of them leads to a plan.

Two rows in the table are deliberate traps. Anyone claiming to be KHDA-approved or Cambridge-approved as an individual tutor is claiming something that is not available: KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, and examination boards approve centres rather than tutors. And anyone quoting a specific grade outcome has told you they will say what closes the sale. Run these rows on us as well; the answers in the strong column are the ones we would give.

sections.heading: Tiering: the decision that caps the grade before any tutoring begins
paragraphs: This is the part of IGCSE that families in Dubai most often discover too late. Both major boards tier several subjects, and the tier a student is entered for sets a maximum achievable grade. Cambridge IGCSE Core papers are graded C to G, while Extended papers are graded A* to E. Pearson's 4MA1 Mathematics Foundation tier awards grades 5 to 1 and the Higher tier awards 9 to 4. A student entered at the lower tier cannot be awarded a top grade regardless of how well they perform or how much tuition they have had.

Entries are made by the school, to the board's deadline, and the decision is usually taken on the basis of internal assessment performance in Year 11. That makes Year 10 and the first term of Year 11 the period in which tier is decided, even though nobody announces it as a decision at the time. A parent who learns in February that their child has been entered at the lower tier has learned it after the point at which tuition could have changed it.

So the useful conversation to have with the school, early, is a simple one: which tier is my child currently heading for in each tiered subject, and what would need to change for the higher tier to be viable? Schools answer that question willingly when asked in Year 10 and defensively when asked in February. The answer also tells you exactly where tuition is worth spending, because a child on the boundary between tiers in mathematics has more to gain from a term of work than a child comfortably inside either one.

There is a second-order effect worth knowing. Tier interacts with Ministry of Education equivalency, because the published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 - a threshold the lower tier can satisfy - while university and A Level entry requirements frequently sit above the lower tier's ceiling. The equivalency floor and the progression requirement are different numbers, and planning only against the lower one is how a student ends up technically qualified and practically blocked.

sections.heading: Why one marked paper beats an hour of description
paragraphs: Parents describe the problem in terms of the child: not confident, finds it hard, loses focus. Mark schemes describe it in terms of marks. The translation between those two languages is the whole of a good first session, and it needs a marked paper to do it with. A recent mock, with the marks written on it, is the most informative document a family will handle in two years, and it is usually read for the total and then filed.

What a marked paper shows that nothing else does: whether marks are being lost on content the student never learned, on command words they misread, on questions they ran out of time for, or on arithmetic slips under pressure. Those are four different problems with four different fixes, and the grade looks identical in all four cases. A child losing eight marks to command words does not need more content teaching, and a child losing eight marks to unfinished final questions needs timing practice rather than either.

The exercise itself takes about an hour and you can do a version of it without paying anyone. Go through the paper question by question with the official mark scheme beside it. For each lost mark, categorise it: did not know, knew but answered the wrong question, ran out of time, or careless. Count the four categories. The largest category is the thing to work on, and it is frequently not the one anybody expected.

Where a tutor adds to this is in the subtler reading. Mark schemes award points for specific phrasing, and a student can write a correct explanation that earns nothing because the mark scheme wanted a named term. Spotting that pattern reliably takes someone who has marked against the scheme rather than someone who knows the subject, which is precisely the distinction the shortlisting table earlier on this page is designed to expose.

sections.heading: What the in-home premium buys in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: In an abundant market the honest question is not whether you can get someone to your door in Umm Suqeim - you can - but what the premium for it purchases. Published Dubai rates for an in-home one-to-one visit with travel included run AED 180-500 an hour, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200-500. Published rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run AED 150-300, and for IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270.

Line those up and the premium is visible: the two bands overlap across almost their entire range. The in-home figure is not a higher-quality band; it is the same band with a journey attached. What the extra money buys, concretely, is the tutor's unpaid driving time, fuel and parking, plus the convenience of a person physically present. What it does not buy is better knowledge of the mark scheme, and it costs you something real in return - the start time becomes dependent on traffic, and the pool shrinks to those who can reach your address in your one usable evening slot.

Monthly, the market shows the same shape. Advertised packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Against school fees that KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, tutoring is the uncapped part of the education budget, which is a reason to buy it by diagnosis rather than by the hour.

All of the above are other providers' published figures, read during the October 2026 research round, quoted as market context rather than as an IB Gram price list. Before you commit to anyone, local or online, get five things in writing: the rate per 60 minutes, whether VAT is included, the cancellation terms, the exact syllabus code the tutor teaches, and their position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: The November series as a route rather than a punishment
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. UAE candidates sit June and November; the February/March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting it to a Dubai family is quoting a timetable from a different country.

Families treat November as the resit series and nothing else, which undersells it. It is a resit route, and it is also an early-entry route for a strong student, a staging route for a child carrying an unusually heavy subject load, and a recovery route for a subject disrupted by illness or a mid-year school move. The only structural cost is time to results: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November entry means waiting until the following January, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026.

For planning, that date difference matters more than it sounds. A student resitting in November will have their result in January, which is in time for most A Level and sixth-form conversations but after some admissions deadlines. A student using November as an early entry banks a grade and reduces the June load, which is the single most effective thing a family can do for a child taking ten subjects. Neither option is remedial, and neither is advertised by anyone in this market.

Two cautions on dates. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which means published dates can be revised, so always work from the live official timetable rather than from any restated date. And Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Get the timetable from the school, not from a search result.

sections.heading: If the school will not enter your child: the private-candidate question
paragraphs: It happens more often than families expect. A school declines to enter a student for a subject, usually because internal performance suggests the entry would be unsuccessful, or a student wants a subject the school does not offer, or a family has moved mid-course and the new school's option blocks do not match. In each case the question becomes whether the student can sit as a private candidate, and that question has to be settled before any tuition plan makes sense.

The practical position is that both major boards operate through registered examination centres, and some centres in Dubai accept private candidates while others only enter their own students. Fees, deadlines and the availability of practical or coursework components vary by centre and by subject, and a subject with a compulsory practical component is harder to arrange privately than a written-only one. The board's own centre information is the place to start, and the centre's own administration team is the only reliable source on what they will accept this series.

This is also where tiering returns. A private candidate's tier is fixed at entry, and without a school's internal assessment history behind the decision the family is making it with less information. A diagnostic on a full past paper under timed conditions, marked properly, is the sensible evidence base for that decision, and it is one of the few situations where paying for a single session before any plan exists is clearly worth the money.

What IB Gram does and does not do here should be clear. We can teach the specification, work through past papers, and tell you honestly whether the timed evidence supports the higher tier. We are not an examination centre, we do not enter candidates, we cannot influence a school's entry decision, and we do not supply or reproduce board materials - we reference the official sources and work from the papers you hold. Entry logistics are the family's to arrange with a centre.

sections.heading: Starting from Umm Suqeim, and three cases where a local tutor suits you better
paragraphs: Starting is short. Send the subject, the year group, the syllabus code and tier if you have them, and the most recent marked paper. We confirm the specification, match a tutor who teaches it, and you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost worked on your child's own paper. Sessions then run weekly in Gulf Standard Time, set against your gate's release time, usually from 4:45pm. Ramadan timings move to post-Iftar slots and holiday weeks often work better in the morning.

Now the part that is unusual on a page like this. In an abundant local market, online delivery is not always the right answer, and three situations genuinely favour a local in-person tutor. The first is a student who will not sit down and work without somebody physically present - for them, presence is the service, and no screen substitutes for it. The second is a younger child, Year 7 or Year 8, whose attention over video is short and whose need is supervision rather than specification knowledge. The third is a family with poor or shared bandwidth, where a video lesson will be a frustrating lesson; this is uncommon in Umm Suqeim's villa streets but it is real.

Outside those three, the case for online is straightforward. The pool is everyone qualified in the exact specification rather than everyone within twenty minutes, which matters most in Further Pure Mathematics, Computer Science and the separate sciences at the top end. The start time does not depend on Al Khail Road. And the premium that pays for driving stays in your pocket. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and the comparison above is why we are comfortable saying so rather than hedging.

The fixed limits, stated once. No claimed approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB - IB Gram holds none. No reproduction or supply of syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; we link the official sources and work from your school's materials. No writing or completing of coursework. No UAE office, because there isn't one. No grade promises and no published statistics about our own results, because we cannot show you the sample, the date and the method that would make such a figure mean anything.

faqs.question: Why does a local search return so many IGCSE tutors and so few that fit?
faqs.answer: Because the UK curriculum is the largest in Dubai, accounting for 37% of private-school enrolment across 227 schools, so supply is genuinely plentiful. What is scarce is specificity. Almost nobody advertising IGCSE tuition states which board, which syllabus code, which tier and which paper structure they teach, and those are exactly the facts that determine whether they can help. Families in Umm Suqeim therefore find a tutor within an hour and discover the mismatch two terms later. The filter is not finding names; it is asking each name for the code before they describe what they teach.

faqs.question: What is tiering and why does nobody mention it until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Tiering is the entry decision that sets a ceiling on the achievable grade. Cambridge IGCSE Core papers are graded C to G and Extended A* to E; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation awards 5 to 1 and Higher awards 9 to 4. The school makes the entry to the board's deadline, usually on the basis of Year 11 internal performance, and nobody announces it as a decision at the time. Ask in Year 10 which tier your child is heading for in each tiered subject and what would change it. Asked then, schools answer helpfully; asked in February, the answer arrives too late to act on.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Dubai be KHDA-approved?
faqs.answer: Not as an individual tutor. KHDA regulates schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, which requires initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a licence for an organisation with a physical location. Examination boards approve examination centres, not tutors. The permit that applies to an individual providing private tuition in the UAE is MoHRE's private tuition work permit. A tutor claiming KHDA or board approval is making a claim that is not available to them.

faqs.question: What should the first paid session with an IGCSE tutor actually contain?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis built from your child's most recent marked paper, not a new assessment test. The tutor should work question by question against the official mark scheme and categorise every lost mark: content the student never learned, a command word misread, a question not reached in time, or a careless slip. Those four have different remedies and the grade looks identical in all four cases. The output should be a short written list ranked by marks lost. If the first session is a generic test the child has effectively already sat at school, you have paid twice for the same information.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying the in-home premium if we can afford it in Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: Only if physical presence is itself the thing you need. Published Dubai in-home rates run AED 180-500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200-450 or more for a specialist - bands that overlap almost completely. The premium buys driving time, fuel, parking and a person in the room; it does not buy better mark-scheme knowledge. It also costs you a start time dependent on traffic and a pool limited to whoever can reach your address in your one usable slot. For a child who will not work without supervision, that trade can still be worth it.

faqs.question: Should we consider the November series, or is it only for resits?
faqs.answer: It is more useful than its reputation. Cambridge runs June and November series and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and UAE candidates sit those; the February/March series is India-only. November works as a resit route, as an early entry that banks a grade and lightens a heavy June, and as a recovery route after illness or a mid-year school move. The structural cost is waiting for results: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, against June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026. Work from the live official timetable, since provisional dates can be revised.

faqs.question: Our school will not enter our child for a subject. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Establish the entry route before planning any teaching. Both major boards operate through registered examination centres, some of which accept private candidates while others only enter their own students, and fees, deadlines and the handling of practical or coursework components vary by centre and subject. A written-only subject is far easier to arrange privately than one with a compulsory practical. Start with the board's centre information and then speak to a centre's administration directly. IB Gram is not an examination centre and does not enter candidates; we can teach the specification and give you timed evidence for the tier decision.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are genuinely hard to staff around here?
faqs.answer: Further Pure Mathematics and Additional Mathematics, Computer Science with its practical programming element, Arabic as a first language, and separate sciences at grade 8-9 level. These are the cases where an abundant local market turns out to be abundant only in the common subjects. Insisting that the tutor also be able to reach Umm Suqeim by 5pm usually empties the list entirely. Over live video the request is answered from everyone qualified in that specification. If we cannot cover a combination at the time you need, we will tell you rather than place a generalist.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does an IGCSE subject actually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week per subject, consistently, from the start of Year 10 is more effective than three hours a week from February of Year 11, and it is considerably cheaper in total. The reason is that IGCSE grades are mostly determined by whether the Year 10 content was learned properly, and repair under deadline pressure requires re-teaching alongside new material. In the final twelve weeks a second weekly session on past papers is justified in one or two subjects. Beyond that, extra hours tend to displace the independent practice that actually consolidates anything.

faqs.question: Does the alternative-to-practical paper need separate preparation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is routinely skipped. In Cambridge sciences the practical test or alternative-to-practical paper carries 20% of the grade, and the marks go on controlled variables, repeats, table headings with correct units, graph conventions and conclusions that actually reference the data. Those are written skills assessed on paper and entirely teachable over video using the student's own past-paper responses. Students treat the component as the easy fifth and give away marks that require no subject insight at all. Two or three focused sessions on it usually return more than the same time spent on content.

faqs.question: Which revision resources are safe to buy for a Dubai IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Buy nothing until you have the syllabus code. Dubai bookshops stock Cambridge and Pearson material side by side and the covers do not make the distinction loud, so a family that buys before confirming the code has a reasonable chance of revising the wrong paper structure. Once you have the code, the boards' own published specifications and specimen materials are the reference point, accessed through their official sites. We do not supply, host or reproduce syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; we reference the official sources and work from the papers your school has issued.

faqs.question: What time of day works for a session if we live in Umm Suqeim 1 or 2?
faqs.answer: Aim for 4:30pm to 4:45pm. Secondary gates around Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Jumeirah release roughly between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the beach road and Al Wasl Road take the traffic in both directions at once, and a child living in the first two sections of Umm Suqeim is typically home between 3:30pm and 3:45pm. Add changing and food and the usable window opens about 4:30pm and starts closing around 6:30pm. Delivering over live video protects that window, because nothing in the arrangement depends on how a road is behaving at the time.

faqs.question: Do UAE Ministry of Education equivalency rules affect which subjects we take?
faqs.answer: They should. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A student taking eight subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education therefore has six that count. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects are required; the sourced rule is five. Verify on moe.gov.ae, and note that equivalency is run by the Ministry, not by any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: What if my child is doing well and we just want to protect the grade?
faqs.answer: Then buy less than you are being offered. A student on track rarely needs weekly tuition; they need periodic marking against the mark scheme and someone to check that technique is holding under timed conditions. A single diagnostic session each half term on a recent paper, plus a short block of timed full papers in the final weeks, covers it. Providers do not usually suggest this because it is a smaller sale, but adding weekly sessions to a working routine displaces independent practice and can make a comfortable student anxious about a subject they were handling.

faqs.question: How do we judge progress when the next real exam is months away?
faqs.answer: By recounting the four categories of lost mark on a fresh marked paper every six to eight weeks, not by asking whether lessons feel useful. If the largest category at the start was misread command words, the test is whether that category has shrunk on the next paper, regardless of whether the overall mark moved. Grades move in steps and often lag technique by a term, so a category count is a more honest early indicator. If nothing has shifted after a full block, change the focus, change the tutor, or stop - and we will say which we think it is.

intro.heading: The real cost of IGCSE tutoring for a Villanova household

School fees in Dubai are already the largest line in that budget, so when a parent searches for an IGCSE tutor near me in Villanova, the unspoken question is: what should this cost, and am I about to be overcharged?

So this page does the unglamorous thing and shows the arithmetic. What the per-hour bands are and who published them. What a term and a year actually come to. And the five specific ways money gets wasted in this belt, each of which we have watched happen.

On the 'near me' part: proximity has a price, and in Villanova it is high. Because the community sits far out, a tutor travelling here prices forty to sixty minutes each way into the hour, which is why in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor online. programmes.name: Year 11, mocks and the series
programmes.description: The most expensive year and the one where spending is least efficient, because panic buying happens here. A targeted block driven by marked mock scripts — six to twelve sessions — typically costs AED 1,000 to 4,000 and moves more marks than a full year of general weekly tuition. Families who start in September with a plan spend less than families who start in February without one.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is India-only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The second series is a resit route, and resits carry their own entry fee, so a realistic Year 11 budget includes the possibility of one subject being sat twice.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-villanova.subjectsIntro: Cost per subject does not vary much, but value does. These are the IGCSE subjects Dubailand families buy most, with the syllabus codes to quote and where the money actually does something.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most tutored subject in this market and the one with the clearest return, because method marks lost to unshown working are recoverable in weeks. Confirm the tier before booking: it sets the grade ceiling and determines which past papers are worth buying time on.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity is the reliable weak point in UAE cohorts. Good value when targeted at two or three topics plus the alternative-to-practical paper; poor value as a general weekly sweep, because most of the syllabus is already secure in a mid-grade student.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and qualitative analysis carry the grade. Organic chemistry at IGCSE is narrow and highly learnable, which makes it the fastest available gain for a Year 11 and therefore the cheapest block of sessions to justify.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy, so parents assume it needs the most hours. Usually it needs the fewest, because the commonest failure is answering 'explain' with description — a command-term habit fixable in three or four sessions of strict marking.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: The route most Dubai students take without triple science. Because a weak discipline drags the whole grade, the efficient purchase is support in the single weakest discipline rather than even coverage of all three, which costs three times as much for less movement.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: A structure problem rather than a vocabulary problem, which is good news for a budget: directed writing and composition both respond to a small number of taught frameworks. Reading marks go to students who explain effect rather than restate content.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different course from First Language and often confused with it when parents book. Listening and speaking components are examined, so sessions include work that looks unlike exam practice. Accuracy in tense and article use is where the measurable gains sit.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Evaluation questions worth six and eight marks have a recognisable structure that is rarely taught in class and takes two or three sessions to install. That is the highest-return purchase in either subject; general content revision is the lowest.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 / 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and theory, not programming fluency. Students who write confident Python still lose marks on board-standard pseudocode and hand-tracing, and binary and data-representation questions are formulaic enough to secure cheaply.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements regardless of curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Excluded from the five subjects that count towards Ministry of Education British-track equivalency, but still real timetabled work that nobody usually budgets support for.

regions.note: Amaranta, Casa Dora, La Rosa and Tulipa, off Al Qudra Road. Far enough out that any in-home quote includes a substantial travel component, which is the main reason Villanova families are quoted more than Motor City families for the same tutor.

regions.note: Adjacent and quoted at almost identical in-home rates. Households here frequently need two different specifications covered, so a single tutor arrangement often costs more than expected once a second subject is added.

regions.name: Serena
regions.note: Same travel band, near-identical school intake. Serena and Villanova families share tutors and share quotes, which makes this the most useful community to compare prices with before you commit.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: Apartment-dense with high Year 10 and Year 11 demand. Group classes at nearby centres are more common here, which makes the per-student price comparison with one-to-one worth running properly.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: Shorter travel for visiting tutors, so in-home quotes here tend to sit AED 30 to 50 lower per hour than Villanova's for the same person. Worth knowing when a neighbour reports a cheaper rate.

regions.note: Where the belt's tuition centres are. The realistic comparison point for group pricing, and the reason to count your own driving time as part of the cost of a centre-based option.

schoolClusters.city: Dubailand, Motor City and Arabian Ranches
schoolClusters.note: The nearest school cluster and a mixed-board one, so confirm board and tier in writing before paying for any sessions. This is also where group classes are sold, which is the cheapest formal option in the belt and the one whose per-student value needs checking.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-villanova.modesIntro: Format drives cost more than tutor choice does. These three are what a Villanova family realistically picks between, all delivered live online with no travel on either side.

modes.title: One-to-one weekly, single subject
modes.description: The standard arrangement and the easiest to budget: one subject, one hour or ninety minutes, one fixed slot. At the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, a full school year in one subject is roughly AED 4,500 to 9,000. The discipline that makes it worth that is a review every term asking whether the slot still earns its place.

modes.title: Short targeted block
modes.description: Six to twelve sessions aimed at a dated problem: a mock recovery, a topic that has failed twice, the run-up to an entry deadline. Costs roughly AED 1,000 to 4,000 depending on band, and for most Year 11 families it moves more marks per dirham than any weekly arrangement, because it works from a marked script rather than a worry.

modes.title: Pair sessions with a neighbour

Per-student cost falls materially and, because there is no travel, a Villanova and a Serena student can share without either family driving. It works for content and exam technique and does not work where boards or tiers differ, which in this belt is common enough to check first.

sections.heading: What a year of IGCSE tutoring actually costs, in context
paragraphs: An hourly rate on its own tells a parent almost nothing, because the number of hours is the variable that decides the bill. So here is the whole picture for a Villanova household, with tutoring set beside the other education costs it competes with. The figures for tutoring come from the published market bands; the surrounding items are included so the tutoring line can be judged against something.

Two observations fall out of the table. First, a single subject supported weekly for a school year at the qualified-tutor band costs roughly what a family might spend on one short holiday, which is a decision most households can make deliberately if they can see the number. Second, the targeted block is dramatically cheaper than the weekly year, and for a Year 11 with a specific diagnosed problem it is usually the better instrument.

The third observation is the one families miss until it arrives. Exam entry fees for private candidates, resit entries, and the cost of re-sitting in a second series are real and are not part of any tutoring quote. A family planning only for tuition and then meeting an entry fee in the same month is a family that feels overcharged by its tutor, which is not quite what happened.

The flat-fee context helps here. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are therefore a known quantity this year, which makes the tutoring line the one worth planning rather than reacting to.

sections.heading: Five ways Dubailand families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: These are not hypothetical. Each one is a pattern we see repeatedly in enquiries from this belt, and each is avoidable with a single question asked before the money is committed.

The first is paying a specialist rate for supervision. If what your child needs is somebody to make them sit down and do the homework, that is a AED 33 to 65 service at the budget online band, and buying it at AED 300 an hour wastes roughly AED 250 every week. The second is paying the travel premium by default. In Villanova that premium sits at the top of the AED 50 to 150 range, and it buys presence, not teaching. If your child works fine on a screen, it is pure cost.

The third is buying a year when a block was needed. A diagnosed problem — one topic, one paper, one habit — closes in six to twelve sessions. A standing weekly slot that nobody reviews runs for thirty and costs four times as much. The fourth is revising the wrong board's past papers, which happens whenever a family books without knowing the syllabus code and which makes every hour less effective without anyone noticing.

The fifth is the most expensive of all: starting in February of Year 11. At that point the available options are compressed and the family buys hours under time pressure, usually more of them than a planned approach would have needed. A family that spends AED 2,000 in September spends less in total than a family that spends AED 8,000 in the spring, and usually gets a better result.
bullets: Paying specialist rates for homework supervision
Paying the in-home travel premium when the child works fine on a screen
Buying a weekly year when a six-session block was the actual need
Practising the wrong board's past papers because nobody checked the code
Starting in February of Year 11 and buying hours under pressure

sections.heading: What each price band actually delivers
paragraphs: The spread from AED 33 to AED 650 is not arbitrary; each band buys something different. The problem is that advertising does not distinguish between them, so a parent comparing two quotes is often comparing a trainee with a subject specialist and reading only the number.

At the budget end, AED 33 to 65 an hour, you are buying attention and routine: someone to sit with a student, keep them on task and recap content. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For a Year 8 who will not start unsupervised, that is appropriate and good value. It is not diagnosis, and it will not find out why a Year 11 is losing marks on Paper 4.

At AED 150 to 300 you are buying a trained subject teacher who works from the specification — Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. This is where most exam-year IGCSE tuition should sit. Above it, at AED 200 to 450 or more, you are buying board-specific depth and mark-scheme-accurate marking; TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 table shows AED 200 to 450+. At AED 500 to 650, where BartyED publishes AED 650, you are buying scarcity and reputation.

The red-flag column in the table below is the useful part. Any promise of a particular grade, any offer to supply completed coursework, and any self-awarded star rating should change your view of a quote regardless of its number. Those are not premium features; they are reasons to walk away.

sections.heading: One-to-one, pair or group: price against outcome
paragraphs: Group classes are the cheapest formal option in this belt and are sold hard by centres in Motor City and Sports City, with monthly packages advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions. Whether they are good value depends entirely on what your child needs, and the honest answer differs by case rather than by format.

A group class delivers a fixed syllabus at a fixed pace to a fixed timetable. If your child is broadly on track and needs more exposure and more practice, that is a sensible purchase and the per-student economics are unbeatable. If your child has a specific diagnosed gap, a group cannot address it, and the money buys hours in a room rather than movement in a grade.

A pair sits between the two and is underused. Two students on the same board, tier and subject, taught together online, splits the cost while keeping the diagnosis individual enough to be useful. Between Villanova, Serena and Mudon this is easy to arrange because no one has to travel to make it work. It stops working the moment the two students are on different boards, which in this belt is common.

One-to-one is the most expensive per hour and the cheapest per outcome where the problem is specific. The decision rule we would give any family: if you can name the problem in one sentence, buy one-to-one and buy few hours. If you cannot name it, buy a short diagnostic block first, because buying thirty hours to find out what the problem is costs more than three hours spent finding out.

sections.heading: The extras that are not in anybody's hourly quote
paragraphs: An hourly rate is the start of the cost, not the whole of it, and the extras are where families feel caught out. Ask about every one of these before a first paid session, from any provider including us.

Session length and what counts as a session. An hour sometimes means fifty minutes. Ninety-minute sessions are sometimes billed as two hours. Ask whether the quote is per hour or per lesson, which are different questions with different answers.

Cancellation terms. How much notice avoids a charge, and what happens when a school event moves at twenty-four hours' notice, which in Dubai it regularly does. For in-home arrangements this is sharper, because a wasted journey is a real cost to the tutor and is usually charged in full. Online, a clashed session can often move within the same week, which is a quiet financial advantage over a school year.

Materials, platform fees and VAT. Ask whether any materials charge applies, and note that nobody should be selling you board past papers or mark schemes, which are published by the boards and should be linked rather than resold. On VAT, the only honest position is to ask whether a quoted price includes it and to require that in writing; we do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact here because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we are not going to invent. Get the answer in writing from whoever will be invoicing you, before the first paid session rather than after it.
bullets: Per hour or per lesson, and whether an hour is sixty minutes
Cancellation notice, and who pays when a school event moves
Materials charges — and whether anyone is reselling board documents
Whether the quoted price includes VAT, confirmed in writing

sections.heading: What money cannot buy at any price
paragraphs: Three things are for sale in this market that should not be, and knowing them protects both your budget and your child's entry. The first is a promise about the final grade. No tutor, centre or platform can control an exam outcome, and any page offering one either has unpublished refund terms or is making a claim it cannot honour. Where a refund promise exists, the exact terms should be printed on the same screen as the promise.

The second is completed coursework. At least one operator ranking for searches like yours sells finished Internal Assessments. Buying one is not a shortcut; it is passing off another person's work as your child's own, which is misconduct under board rules and risks the qualification rather than the grade. Legitimate support means teaching the skills, explaining the criteria, and giving feedback on what the student wrote. It never means supplying text or data.

The third is board material as a product. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge and Pearson and should be cited and linked, not resold or bundled as a 'resource pack'. If someone is charging for them, you are paying for something you can get free and they are redistributing material they do not own.

A fourth, smaller point: star ratings and review counts that nobody can trace. Competitor pages in this market show conflicting rating figures on the same page, and one shows a perfect score from twenty reviews against a claimed student count many times larger. A rating you cannot audit is not information you should pay a premium for.
bullets: No guaranteed grades; a refund promise means nothing without published terms
Completed IAs and coursework are misconduct, not a service
Board documents are free to access and should be linked, never resold
Untraceable ratings are not a reason to accept a higher quote

sections.heading: Entry fees, series and resits — the costs nobody budgets
paragraphs: Tutoring is the cost families plan for. Exam administration is the cost that surprises them, and it is driven by the calendar rather than by choice. Getting the series right is therefore a budget matter as well as an academic one.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate sitting in the UAE, so any advice built on a February exam window is advice for another country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exam officer which zone applies.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. As checkable reference points: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for later series that may be revised, so work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

The budget consequence is simple. Because there are two series a year, a subject that goes wrong in June can be re-sat in November — but a resit is a second entry fee, potentially a second set of tutoring hours, and a term of divided attention while the next course is starting. A Year 11 budget that allows for one resit in one subject is a realistic budget. One that assumes everything lands first time is a hopeful one.

sections.heading: Spending less by removing the journey
paragraphs: The cheapest structural change available to a Villanova family is not a cheaper tutor; it is removing travel from the arrangement. Travel appears in a budget twice and most families only count it once.

Counted once: the in-home premium. Because this community sits far out, a visiting tutor prices forty to sixty minutes each way into the hour, which is why market in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor teaching online. Over thirty sessions, paying the middle of that premium costs roughly AED 3,000 for driving.

Counted twice: your own driving to a centre. Twenty-five to forty minutes each way to Motor City, plus waiting, is around two hours of household time per session. That is not on any invoice, which is precisely why it is easy to accept. For two children on different days it is the largest uncosted item in the whole arrangement.

IB Gram removes both, because teaching is live, one-to-one and online and nobody drives — there is no IB Gram centre in the UAE and no home visits anywhere in the country, which are India-only. What that buys beyond the saving is selection: the tutor is chosen because they teach your child's specification and tier rather than because they live within range of Al Qudra Road. If presence in the room is genuinely what your child needs, the in-home market exists and the premium is the honest price of it.
bullets: In-home premium over thirty sessions: roughly AED 1,500 to 4,500 for travel
Driving to a centre: about two hours of household time per session, uninvoiced
Removing travel widens the tutor pool from 'who will drive' to 'who teaches this'
No UAE centre and no UAE home visits; delivery is live online

process.title: Send the subject, code and the problem in one sentence
process.description: The most useful enquiry names the subject, the syllabus code and tier if you have them, the year group, and the problem in a single sentence. Families who can state the problem need fewer hours, which makes the arrangement cheaper from the first week. Families who cannot should ask for a short diagnostic block instead of a year.

process.title: We quote after we have seen the work
process.description: The rate depends on the level and the type of work, so it is quoted after the free trial lesson rather than before anyone has looked at a marked paper. That is deliberate: quoting a single headline figure for every request is how families end up paying specialist prices for supervision.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: The first session is a genuine lesson with the person who would continue, with no card required. It produces a diagnosis — what your child can do, where the marks are going, and how many sessions this realistically needs. Sometimes the honest answer is fewer than you expected, and occasionally it is none.

process.title: A plan with a session count and a finish date
process.description: You get a short written plan naming the topics, the order, the number of sessions and the date it ends, set against your school's own deadlines. A plan without a finish date is a subscription. We would rather close a gap in eight sessions and stop than hold a slot nobody is reviewing.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, because there is no travel
whyPoints.description: Nobody drives to Al Qudra Road and no parent drives to Motor City, which removes both the AED 50 to 150 hourly premium a visiting tutor charges in this belt and the two hours of household time a centre visit consumes. The saving is structural rather than a discount.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: Each AED band on this page names the competitor or rate table that published it, and is presented as the market rather than our price. We publish no statistic without a source, no self-awarded rating, and no exam date we cannot point at an official page for.

whyPoints.title: Quoted after diagnosis, not before
whyPoints.description: A rate quoted before anyone has seen a marked paper is a rate set by the seller's convenience. We look at the work in a free trial lesson first, then quote the level of support the work actually needs, which sometimes means recommending fewer hours than you came for.

whyPoints.title: A finish date in writing
whyPoints.description: Plans name their session count and their end point. Most IGCSE problems are finite — a tier decision, a topic, a mark-scheme habit — and the honest arrangement closes and stops rather than renewing quietly into a second year.

whyPoints.title: Nothing sold that should not be
whyPoints.description: No promises about final grades, no completed coursework, no resold board past papers or mark schemes, no self-asserted star ratings. Each of those is on sale in this market, and each is a reason to question a quote rather than a feature to pay extra for.

faqs.question: What should I expect to pay for an IGCSE tutor around Villanova?
faqs.answer: For a qualified subject tutor teaching online, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 or more, per TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table. In-home visits to Dubailand run AED 180 to 500 including travel, and because Villanova is far out, expect the upper half. Budget online tuition starts around AED 33 to 65. Those are published market figures. IB Gram quotes per student after the free trial, because the right band depends on what the marked work shows.

faqs.question: Why am I quoted more than my friend in Arabian Ranches for the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Almost always travel. An in-home quote prices the drive into the hour, and Villanova sits twenty to thirty minutes further out than the Ranches for most of Dubai's tutoring workforce. That difference commonly shows up as AED 30 to 50 an hour on an otherwise identical arrangement, which over thirty sessions is around AED 1,500. If the quotes are for online sessions and still differ, ask both tutors which syllabus code they work from — you may be comparing a generalist with a specialist rather than two prices for the same thing.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a Motor City centre better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, unquestionably; monthly packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions. Per outcome, it depends. A group delivers a fixed syllabus at a fixed pace, which suits a child who is broadly on track and needs more exposure and practice. It cannot address an individual diagnosed gap, and it costs you the drive — twenty-five to forty minutes each way from Villanova plus waiting. If you can name your child's problem in one sentence, one-to-one for a small number of hours is usually cheaper overall.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE tutoring does a Year 11 actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families buy, if the hours are aimed properly. A marked mock script typically reveals that a third to a half of lost marks are method and reading errors rather than content gaps, and those close fast. Six to twelve focused sessions, costing roughly AED 1,000 to 4,000 at mid and specialist bands, moves more marks than thirty unfocused ones. The expensive version is starting in February without a diagnosis, because hours then get bought under time pressure. Start with the marked paper, not with a weekly commitment.

faqs.question: Does the price include VAT, and what else is not in the quote?
faqs.answer: Ask and get it in writing — we will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a general fact here, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion. The other items to confirm before a first paid session are whether the quote is per hour or per lesson, whether an hour means sixty minutes, how much cancellation notice avoids a charge, and whether any materials fee applies. On that last point, nobody should be charging you for board past papers or mark schemes, which are published by Cambridge and Pearson and should simply be linked.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest online tutoring in Dubai worth using at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. At AED 33 to 65 an hour — Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 — you are buying routine and supervision: someone to sit with a student and keep them working. For a Year 8 who will not start unprompted, that is appropriate and good value, and paying AED 300 an hour for it is the single commonest waste in this market. What it will not do is diagnose why a Year 11 is losing marks on a specific paper, which is a different service with a different price.

faqs.question: Where exactly does tutoring money get wasted in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: Five places, in order of cost. Paying a specialist rate for homework supervision. Paying the in-home travel premium for a child who works perfectly well on a screen. Buying a weekly year when a six-session block was the actual need. Practising the wrong board's past papers because nobody confirmed the syllabus code. And starting in February of Year 11, when hours have to be bought under pressure and there is no time for the cheap fixes. Each is avoidable with one question asked before the first payment.

faqs.question: Can I pay for fewer sessions and stop when the grade moves?
faqs.answer: That is how we would prefer you to buy it. Plans name a session count and a finish date, and the point of a termly review against marked work is to decide whether the slot still earns its place. Most IGCSE problems are finite: a tier decision, a topic block, a mark-scheme habit. An arrangement that renews quietly into a second year is a cost to you and no credit to anyone. If a subject no longer needs weekly support, we will say so rather than wait for you to notice.

faqs.question: What does a resit cost if my child's June result is poor?
faqs.answer: A second entry fee, quoted by the exam centre rather than by any tutor, plus whatever further tutoring you decide on and a term of divided attention while the next course begins. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates and Pearson runs May/June and November, so there is a resit route each year. A realistic Year 11 budget allows for one subject being sat twice. Entry fees and centre charges vary, so ask the school's exam office for the figure rather than estimating from anything you read online.

faqs.question: Are the tutors teaching Villanova students permitted to tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring here requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years according to u.ae. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so distrust any amount quoted at you. Note the permit itself is free, so no tutor should be passing on a licensing cost.

faqs.question: Is the premium band ever worth paying for an IGCSE tutor in this belt?
faqs.answer: Only if the claim can be evidenced, and examiner status is not a reason to expect access to marking, boundaries or paper content, which it does not provide. We do not describe tutors as examiners for anyone whose current status cannot be shown, and a premium justified by an unevidenced claim is simply a higher price. What is worth paying for at the top band is scarcity in genuinely scarce subjects. BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour; whether that band is worth it depends on whether anyone cheaper can actually teach the specific thing your child needs.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IGCSE coursework for a fee?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the task needs, explain what the criteria ask for, and give feedback on work your child has written. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, produce the data, edit it to a finished state or hand over another student's work as a model — and no price makes that acceptable, because it is passing off another person's work as your child's own and risks the entry rather than the grade. At least one operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. Ask any prospective tutor directly where their line is.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education need separate tutoring budgets in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They often go unbudgeted and sometimes should not. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with instructional time based on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. For a non-Arab student these are real timetabled periods in a language not used at home. Note that for Ministry of Education British-track equivalency, Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five subjects that count — so they matter for the school report rather than for the equivalency file.

faqs.question: How do I compare two tutoring quotes properly?
faqs.answer: Put them on the same basis before you look at the numbers. Ask each for the syllabus code they would work from, whether the quote is per hour or per lesson and what an hour means, how many sessions they expect the job to take, what the cancellation terms are, whether VAT is included, and what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable. A cheaper quote for forty sessions is more expensive than a dearer quote for eight. The comparison that matters is total cost to close the gap, not the rate on the first line.

dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-villanova.closingHeading: Decide the hours before you choose the tutor
dubai/igcse-tutor-near-me-in-villanova.closingBody: The most useful thing a Villanova family can do before hiring an IGCSE tutor is work out how many hours the problem actually needs. Get the marked mock or the last assessment, get the syllabus code from the school, and then ask any provider — including us — how many sessions they think it will take and what happens when it is done. Send us those two documents and the subject, and you will get an honest session count and a rate quoted after the free trial lesson rather than before. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online; no travel, and so no travel premium.
